When selecting, it is necessary to ensure that the highest voltage generated by the hand-cranked generator is higher than the rated working voltage of the object under test, while not damaging the object under test. When measuring equipment with a rated voltage of 500V and above, an insulation resistance tester of 1000~2500V specification should be selected; when measuring the winding of low-voltage equipment with a rated voltage of 500V and above, an insulation resistance tester of 1000~2500V should likewise be selected. When the winding insulation resistance of a marine motor is lower than 0.5MΩ, it needs to be detected with a 500V insulation resistance tester and dried; the insulation resistance between phases and to ground of a marine transformer is measured with a 500V tester and should be not less than

0.5MΩ.

The insulation resistance tester is provided with three terminal posts, namely L (line, connected to the conductor), E (earth, connected to the casing or ground) and the guard terminal post G (connected to the guard ring). When measuring the insulation resistance of a cable, the guard ring should be connected to the innermost insulation layer to eliminate errors. A marine cable contains an insulation layer, whose purpose is to electrically insulate the various conductive core wires and prevent short circuit or earthing between core wires; in the structure of a marine cable it is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer.

Before using the insulation resistance tester, an open-circuit test and a short-circuit test must be carried out. In the open-circuit test, turn the handle clockwise at a speed of 120r/min so that the instrument pointer points to infinity; in the short-circuit test the pointer should point to 0, and the speed is usually 120r/min. Before use, it is also necessary to observe whether the pointer points to infinity during the open-circuit test. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, the state of parts, the state of conductors and the operating parameters of the equipment; whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, cracked, abraded or burnt. Observation is also the preceding step of check the monitoring and indicating device; only after observation is completed does one proceed to check the monitoring and indicating device. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, whose relative positions must be checked for accuracy; in the voltage circuit a potentiometer is connected in series as a regulator, used to adjust the error of the pointer at the "∞" position. A potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the other pins changes as the shaft rotates; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component and is generally considered manually adjustable; in automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance, and automatic oil-fired boilers contain such potentiometers.

When using the insulation resistance tester, improper wiring and improper operation will affect the measurement results and even endanger personal safety. Improper operation is one of the fault causes of the marine power system, referring to equipment abnormality or system trip caused by human operating errors; common manifestations include improper closing operation, unbalanced generator load control and improper operation caused by observation errors. During parallel operation, improper grasp of the closing moment or reversing the adjustment direction of load distribution can cause the generator reverse-power protection to trip, and improper operation can lead to a single-phase earthing fault of the power system. It is strictly forbidden to use the insulation resistance tester on live equipment; before and after measuring large-capacity equipment, it must be fully discharged to prevent electric shock. It is strictly forbidden to use the insulation resistance tester to measure the insulation resistance of low-voltage electrical equipment such as electronic equipment, instruments and sensors, so as to avoid breaking down the electronic devices therein; it is likewise strictly forbidden to use the insulation resistance tester to test diodes, transistors and integrated circuits, so as to avoid high voltage breaking down the electronic devices. A diode has unidirectional conductivity, with small conduction resistance under forward voltage and cutoff under reverse voltage; according to function it can be divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148) and Schottky diodes, etc., and is commonly denoted VD in circuits; diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. A transistor internally contains two PN junctions and has current amplification capability, and is divided into NPN type and PNP type; in circuits it is commonly denoted by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17, and main models include A92, 9015 (PNP type) and A42, 9014, 9018, etc. (NPN type). An integrated circuit has the advantages of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance, and commonly comes in 14-pin or 16-pin packages; it is divided into CMOS circuits and TTL circuits, and the pins are numbered counterclockwise starting from the notch or dot; for ease of maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often welded on the circuit board for direct plugging-in, and common package forms include pins with inner hooks on four sides (PLCC), gull-wing pins on two sides (SOIC), dual in-line pins (DIP) and power integrated circuit packages.

Capacitors, diodes, transistors and integrated circuits are used in marine electrical equipment. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle; its characteristic is blocking direct current and passing alternating current, and in circuits it is generally denoted by "C" plus a number, e.g. C25 denotes the capacitor numbered 25; its hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC); main performance indicators include capacitance, withstand voltage value (maximum working voltage) and temperature withstand value; types include electrolytic capacitors, ceramic capacitors, chip capacitors, monolithic capacitors, tantalum capacitors and polyester capacitors; units include farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF) and picofarad (pF). The capacitor detection steps apply to capacitors; a capacitor may suffer a capacitor fault, and a capacitor fault belongs to the capacitor; the diode detection steps apply to diodes; a transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to the transistor. Both AC single-phase motors and electric fans contain capacitors. A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog-quantity and switching-quantity sensors; in the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the analog-quantity sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed; the control platform contains sensors.

Electrical quantities such as resistance, voltage, current and capacitance can be measured with a multimeter; a multimeter can measure the resistance value of a resistor, the voltage value of a voltage, the current value of a current, the capacitance value of a capacitor, and the relevant parameters of diodes and transistors; a clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. When measuring a resistor in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is a capacitor in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with power on. To measure current, an ammeter must be used, connected in series after breaking the circuit. Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting, failure to start, low speed under load operation, and motor overheating or smoking; it will also cause difficulty in starting marine electrical equipment, reduced speed, excessive temperature rise or poor contactor pull-in; when an electric fan starts slowly and its speed decreases, the possible cause is undervoltage of the power supply; when an electric drill rotates too slowly, the possible cause is undervoltage of the power supply, which needs to be checked and adjusted. A contactor contains a coil; the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start; the current coil of a wattmeter is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action.

The insulation resistance tester is a portable instrument composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables, and often adopts the ratio-meter structure. The meter is provided with three terminal posts, of which L is connected to the conductor, E to the casing or ground, and G is the guard terminal post connected to the guard ring. Before use, an open-circuit test must be done, with the pointer pointing to ∞, then a short-circuit test, with the pointer pointing to 0; the cranking speed is usually 120r/min. When the scale error of the insulation resistance tester is relatively large, the guide wire can be re-welded; by slightly lengthening or shortening the guide wire, the residual torque is used to change the scale characteristic. Welding is a process in which the solder is melted by heating, atomic diffusion occurs between the workpiece and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer with good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength is formed; welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products.

For the fault of broken input wiring, the corresponding treatment is welding.

Steps for measuring the insulation resistance of a coil to earth in electrical equipment: cut off the power supply -> connect the terminal posts -> measure and read; its first step must be to cut off the power supply of the electrical equipment under test, then connect the terminal posts and measure and read. When wiring, the E end of the insulation resistance tester is connected to the casing or core, and the L end to the coil conductor; when the phases of polyphase equipment are not connected, the L end needs to be connected to each phase coil conductor one by one; coils not involved in the measurement may be earthed to avoid interference from induced voltage. Then crank the generator to the rated speed, and read the insulation resistance value after the pointer stabilizes. The core is a component of marine electrical equipment; when measuring the insulation resistance of a coil to earth, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; the coil is also a component of marine electrical equipment, made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and having the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current.

Steps for measuring the insulation resistance of a line to earth: cut off the power supply -> connect the terminal posts -> crank the handle -> read the reading; its first step must be to cut off the power supply of the line to be tested; terminal post L of the insulation resistance tester should be connected to the line to be tested, and when measuring on board, terminal post E should be connected to the hull as the earthing end; then crank the generator of the insulation resistance tester until the rated speed is reached, and after the pointer stabilizes, the indicated scale value is the insulation resistance value of the line to earth. Steps for measuring the insulation resistance between lines: cut off the power supply -> connect the terminal posts -> crank the handle -> read the reading; its first step is likewise to cut off the power supply of the line under test; terminal posts L and E of the insulation resistance tester are connected to the two lines under test respectively; crank the generator of the insulation resistance tester to the rated speed, and after the pointer stabilizes, the indicated scale value is the insulation resistance value between the lines. A multimeter can be used to measure the resistance value of a resistor and also to measure the voltage value of a voltage; a voltmeter is likewise used to measure voltage values.

Structure and principle of the clamp-on ammeter The clamp-on ammeter is a measuring instrument composed of a current transformer and an ammeter, and its working principle is based on the single-turn through-type current transformer. During measurement, the conductor under test passes through the core window of the transformer, equivalent to the primary winding, while the secondary winding of the transformer itself is connected to the ammeter. The current induced in the secondary winding drives the pointer to deflect, thereby indicating the value of the current under test. Since the conductor under test directly serves as the primary winding to participate in electromagnetic induction, there is no need to break the circuit under test during measurement; this is an important feature that distinguishes the clamp-on ammeter from an ordinary ammeter.

The through-type current transformer is one type of current transformer; its primary winding has very few turns, and the conductor may even pass directly through the core to link with the magnetic circuit. When the number of primary turns is reduced to a certain extent, a dedicated primary winding need not be wound; instead, the current-carrying conductor is passed directly through the core hole. Taking the HL-25 through-type transformer as an example, when the primary current I1 is 600A, the conductor only needs to pass through once; when I1 is 100A, a flexible wire can be passed through the transformer hole six times; when I1 is 150A, the conductor passes through four times. This practice of adapting to different current ranges by changing the number of passes is precisely the flexibility of the through-type structure.

A current transformer is used in circuits to transform the current ratio, and its symbol is TA, that is, the current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA; the standard current on the secondary side is usually 5A. According to structure it can be divided into coil type, busbar type and through type, etc.; one end of the secondary side is required to be earthed; when working it is equivalent to a short-circuit transformer, and during operation the secondary winding must never be open-circuited. The current transformer contained in the clamp-on ammeter belongs to the through type; it combines the transformer and the ammeter in one unit, facilitating on-site measurement.

Method of using the clamp-on ammeter Method of using the clamp-on ammeter: wipe off oil dirt on the clamp jaw -> check the pointer zero position -> select the maximum range -> adjust to a suitable range -> clamp the conductor under test -> read the reading -> after measurement turn the range switch to the maximum. In specific operation, first wipe off oil dirt on the clamp jaw and check the pointer zero position, adjusting the mechanical zero position if necessary. Before measurement, first select the maximum range for a trial measurement, then change to a suitable range according to the actual situation. During measurement, squeeze the trigger firmly to open the core, pass the conductor under test through the core gap, then release the trigger; when the core closes, the reading can be taken. To reduce errors, the conductor under test should be placed in the center of the magnetic core window (clamp jaw). After measurement, the range should be turned to the maximum position.

The clamp-on ammeter can be used to detect the starting current of a motor, in which case the range must be greater than 7 times the rated current; it can also be used to check the balance of three-phase currents. Current is one of the basic electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, and its measuring tools include the multimeter, the ammeter and the clamp-on ammeter. An ordinary ammeter requires breaking the circuit and connecting in series for measurement, whereas the clamp-on ammeter uses the principle of the through-type current transformer to directly clamp the conductor and measure alternating current without breaking the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system, and local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is also one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating; therefore accurate measurement of current helps to understand the operating status of the equipment.

Association with fault diagnosis and the multimeter In the conventional fault diagnosis method, observation is an important part of the first step. Interview the operator is the preceding step of observation, that is, first learn from the operator about the situation before and after the fault occurred, and then proceed to observation. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, the state of parts, the state of conductors and the operating parameters of the equipment, specifically such as whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, cracked, abraded or burnt. Observation is also the preceding step of check the monitoring and indicating device; only after observation is completed is the monitoring and indicating device further checked. This process helps to carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged.

The multimeter internally contains a changeover switch and a measuring circuit. The changeover switch is used to select the measurement object and range, and the measuring circuit is responsible for converting different electrical quantities and different ranges into signals measurable by the meter head. Among the three basic components of the MF-30 and MF-47 analog multimeters is the measuring circuit; since the moving-coil meter head can only pass microampere-level current, a conversion circuit is needed to measure different electrical quantities and ranges. Both the multimeter and the clamp-on ammeter can be used to measure current, but the two are connected into the circuit in different ways. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited.

The core is one of the components of marine electrical equipment; in the through-type current transformer, the conductor carrying the large current under test links directly with the core to replace the primary winding; in the clamp-on ammeter, the core can be opened by squeezing the trigger, so as to pass the conductor under test through without breaking the circuit. A contactor also contains a core. When measuring the insulation resistance of a coil of electrical equipment to earth, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core. The primary winding of a coil-type current transformer is already wound on the core, whereas a busbar-type one has no such structure.

Basic composition and measuring principle of the wattmeter The wattmeter, also called the power meter, is an instrument used to measure electric power. It is composed of two parts, the current coil and the voltage coil, and calculates power by detecting the load current and voltage. In the measuring connection, the current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the circuit current; the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test to detect the voltage. The wattmeter internally contains a current coil and a voltage coil, which work together and neither can be dispensed with.

The role of the current coil in the wattmeter is to detect the load current, and its connection mode is series, that is, connected in series between the power supply and the load. The branch in which the voltage coil is located has an additional resistor connected in series, and is then connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test to detect the circuit voltage. The voltage range of the wattmeter is realized precisely by connecting additional resistors of different resistance values in series with the voltage coil. With different resistance values of the additional resistor, the voltage proportion divided by the voltage coil branch differs, so the same meter head can correspond to multiple voltage ranges.

Both the current coil and the voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals, usually indicated by the "*" symbol. During measurement, the current of the two coils must flow in from the corresponding terminals simultaneously or flow out from the corresponding terminals simultaneously, so that the pointer deflects in the clockwise direction. If the corresponding terminals are connected in reverse during wiring, the pointer will deflect in the reverse direction and normal reading will be impossible. Therefore, before wiring, the "*" mark on the terminal posts should be identified first, and then the connection method for the power supply side and the load side should be determined according to the corresponding-terminal rule.

Multi-range wattmeter and D34-W wattmeter The multi-range wattmeter belongs to the portable wattmeter type and usually has two current ranges and two or three voltage ranges. The two current ranges are achieved by connecting two completely identical current coils in series or in parallel: when the two coils are in series, the current range is smaller; when in parallel, the current range is larger. The voltage ranges are achieved by connecting the voltage coil in series with additional resistors of different resistance values. The terminal posts of each range, the common terminal and the corresponding terminals are all brought out and fixed on the terminal posts of the dial, so that the user can select different range combinations according to measurement needs. The scale of the multi-range wattmeter only marks the number of divisions and not the watt value, so when reading, it is necessary to multiply by the division constant to obtain the power value. The division constant C equals the rated value of the voltage range divided by the rated value of the current range, and then divided by the number of full-scale divisions.

The D34-W wattmeter is a portable multi-range wattmeter with two current ranges and three voltage ranges. Its rated currents are 0.25A and 0.5A, and its rated voltages are 25V, 50V and 100V. When the 0.25A and 100V ranges are selected, its power range is 25W; when the 0.5A and 25V ranges are selected, its power range is
1
2.5W. This meter changes the series or parallel connection of the two current coils by means of a connecting piece to achieve range switching. Because it is a portable wattmeter, the D34-W wattmeter usually has multiple ranges rather than a single range. When using it, the range should first be selected according to the approximate range of current and voltage of the circuit under test, and then the reading should be converted according to the division constant corresponding to the selected range.

Wiring rules and loss handling of the wattmeter During wiring, the current terminal of the wattmeter marked with "*" must be connected to one end of the power supply, and the other end to the load end; the voltage terminal marked with "*" must be connected to the "*" end of the current terminal. This rule ensures that the currents of the current coil and the voltage coil flow in from the corresponding terminals simultaneously, so that the pointer deflects correctly. If the "*" end of the voltage terminal is mistakenly connected to the other end of the current terminal, the pointer will deflect in the reverse direction.

The power value measured by the wattmeter includes the power loss of the current coil itself. When accurate measurement is required, this loss should be subtracted from the reading. In addition, the reading of a multi-range wattmeter needs to be multiplied by the division constant C, where C equals the rated value of the voltage range divided by the rated value of the current range, and then divided by the number of full-scale divisions. That is, first calculate the number of watts represented by each division according to the rated value of the selected voltage range and the rated value of the current range, and then multiply the number of divisions deflected by the pointer by this constant to obtain the actual power value.

Measurement methods of active power in three-phase circuits Measurement methods of active power in three-phase circuits: one-wattmeter method -> two-wattmeter method -> three-wattmeter method. These three methods are respectively applicable to different three-phase circuit conditions. For a symmetrical three-phase circuit (three-wire or four-wire system), the one-wattmeter method can be used; after measuring the single-phase power, multiply by 3 to obtain the total power.

The two-wattmeter method is applicable to three-phase three-wire loads, and measurement can be carried out regardless of whether the load is symmetrical. The wiring principle of the two-wattmeter method is: the current coils of the two meters should be connected to two different phase lines, and the "*" ends should be connected to the power supply side; the corresponding terminal of the voltage coil of each meter should be connected to the corresponding terminal of its respective current coil. In the two-wattmeter method, the other end of each voltage coil is connected to the phase line that has no current coil, so that the voltage is a line voltage. Under normal conditions, the total power of the two-wattmeter method is the sum of the readings of the two meters, that is, P=P1+P2. When the load cosφ<0.5 (φ>60°), one meter must have a negative reading; in this case, the current coil needs to be reversed and the difference value used for calculation. The three-wattmeter method is used for three-phase four-wire circuits, with one wattmeter connected to each phase, and the sum of the three readings is the total three-phase power.

The movable parts of the two units of the electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units. The shaft, as a mechanical transmission component, is used to transmit torque and rotational motion, and is commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments. The changeover switch is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a shaft and a panel, and is assembled by bolts.

Other instruments and components related to power measurement A multimeter contains a measuring circuit, and the function of the measuring circuit is to convert different electrical quantities and different ranges. A multimeter uses measured quantities such as resistance, voltage and current for detection, among which the measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measurable property of current is the current value. A clamp-on ammeter likewise uses current for measurement. Measuring current requires an ammeter, which is connected in series after the circuit is disconnected. When measuring a resistor in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. When selecting a voltage transformer, the rated voltage ratio of the transformer should be selected according to the rated voltage of the voltage coil of the instrument used. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of AC motors; the winding insulation of marine motors must undergo "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proofing, mildew-proofing and salt-oil-mist-proofing, and must be oil-resistant.

In a reverse-power relay, if the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, the relay will fail to function, that is, the reverse-power relay fails. Failure of the reverse-power relay may be caused by a burnt-out current coil, and the coil needs to be checked and replaced. Failure to wire as required can also cause the reverse-power relay to fail. In addition, in the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open circuit in the shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect. Voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis, and current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status.

In marine low-voltage power systems, the measuring circuit refers to the specific wiring and conversion circuit for voltage, current and power, and its basic function is to convert different electrical quantities and different ranges. As far as the multimeter is concerned, the measuring circuit is the internal circuit part used to convert different electrical quantities and ranges into signals measurable by the meter head; together with the changeover switch and the meter head, it constitutes the three basic components of the analog multimeter, and the MF-30 multimeter and MF-47 multimeter both belong to this category. Since a moving-coil meter head can only pass microampere-level current, a conversion circuit is necessary to measure different electrical quantities and ranges. A multimeter contains a changeover switch and also contains a measuring circuit; a multimeter uses voltage and also uses current. A clamp-on ammeter contains a current transformer and uses current. A wattmeter, also called a power meter, is composed of a current coil and a voltage coil and is used to measure electrical power, wherein the current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the circuit under test to detect voltage; the two coils are marked with corresponding terminals, and during measurement the current must flow in from or out from the corresponding terminals simultaneously.

AC voltage measuring circuit: AC single-phase voltage measuring circuit -> AC three-phase voltage direct measuring circuit. This classification indicates that AC voltage measuring circuits are divided into two types, the AC single-phase voltage measuring circuit and the AC three-phase voltage direct measuring circuit, belonging to direct voltage measuring circuits and distinguished from indirect measuring circuits. Its wiring method is that the voltmeter is connected directly across any two phases of the line through the fuse FU for measurement. In a marine low-voltage three-phase three-wire system, the "single-phase voltage" measured by this circuit is essentially a line voltage. For a 380V line rated voltage, the upper limit of the range calculated according to the specification is 456V; for a 390～400V generator rated voltage, the upper limit of the range calculated according to the specification is 480V. Based on the above parameter requirements, a voltmeter with a 0～500V range should be selected for this circuit. In the AC three-phase voltage direct measuring circuit, phase B needs to be connected to the changeover switch using two pairs of contacts. AC voltage measurement steps: select the range -> connect the circuit under test -> read, that is, first select an appropriate range, then connect the instrument to the circuit under test, and finally read the indicated value.

A fuse is used for overload and short circuit protection in marine power systems, with the symbol FU. It is a protective device that automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element when overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or electrical equipment. It belongs to distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, with a voltage of 380V and a current of 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. In the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line through FU. In circuit diagrams, FU serves as a protective element, and its graphical symbol is identified as FU; FU fuse blowing is one of the causes of the contactor KM coil being de-energized and unable to close. The fuse corresponds to the symbol FU, and the MF-30 multimeter also belongs to the category of protective elements identified by FU.

The changeover switch on the main switchboard is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set working states and issue operating commands, and has the functions of selecting measurement objects and selecting ranges. It is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a shaft and a panel, and is assembled with bolts. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The LW95-15-LH2/2 changeover switch indicates the open and closed states of contacts at different positions by means of a closing table. In a multimeter, the positions of the changeover switch are divided into five parts: the ohms region, the AC voltage region, the DC voltage region, and the DC current mA and μA regions; when measuring resistance, the actual value equals the pointer indication multiplied by the multiplier corresponding to the changeover switch, such as ×1, ×10, etc.

The symbol of the voltage transformer is TV, and its function is to transform the voltage ratio. The secondary voltage is 100V, and its characteristic is that one end of the secondary side is earthed. The voltage transformer corresponds to TV. Its working principle is the same as that of a transformer, but its internal resistance is extremely small, and the output voltage hardly changes with the load. When working, it is equivalent to a no-load transformer, and short circuit on the secondary side is strictly prohibited; a fuse must be installed on the primary side for short circuit protection. One end of the secondary side must be earthed to prevent high voltage breakdown from endangering safety, and the earthed end must correspond to the middle phase of the primary side, such as phase B. The main switchboard commonly uses voltage ratios of 380/110V and 440/110V, and the accuracy class is usually not lower than
0.5. The primary winding terminals are marked A and X, and the secondary winding is marked a and x, wherein A and a are corresponding terminals. TV has the nature of a voltage source, with extremely small internal resistance; when the load changes, the output voltage is almost unchanged and the phase shift is extremely small; when working, it is equivalent to a no-load transformer, and short circuit on the secondary side is strictly prohibited; the primary side terminals are represented by A and X, and the secondary side by a and x, with A and a being corresponding terminals; the standard secondary voltage is usually 100V, and in a 440V, 60Hz system it is 110V; the earthed end of the secondary side must correspond to the middle phase of the primary side, that is, phase B, phase V or phase L2. In a marine switchboard, the line voltage UCA is synthesized by vector addition of two TVs connected in a "V" configuration. When selecting, the rated capacity should be not less than the power consumed by all measuring instruments, and the primary rated voltage should be equal to or slightly greater than the voltage of the line under test.

The symbol of the current transformer is TA, and its function is to transform the current ratio. The secondary current is 5A, and the types include coil type, busbar type and through-type, with the characteristic that one end of the secondary side is earthed. The current transformer corresponds to TA, and the through-type current transformer belongs to the current transformer. Its primary terminals are represented by L1 and L2, and the secondary side by K1 and K2. When working, it is equivalent to a short-circuited transformer, and open circuit of the secondary winding during operation is strictly prohibited. It has the nature of a current source, with extremely large internal resistance, and the output current is almost unchanged when the load changes. One end of the secondary side must be earthed to prevent high voltage on the primary side from breaking down the insulation and endangering personal safety. When the AC current exceeds the 5A range, it needs to be measured through transformation by a current transformer. In the through-type structure, when the number of primary turns is reduced to a certain extent, the primary winding may be omitted and the conductor directly threaded through; the HL-25 type is threaded through only once at 600A, and at 100A a flexible wire can be threaded through six times. The primary side of TA carries the load current I, which is transformed into a secondary current and connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements; open circuit on the secondary side is strictly prohibited, and the terminals of the external ammeter need to have a short-circuit connecting piece, which may be removed only after wiring has been checked; when working, it is equivalent to a short-circuited transformer, and to prevent high voltage from breaking down the insulation and endangering safety, one end of the secondary side must be earthed; the primary winding is divided into coil type and busbar type, the latter being the through-type, with no independent primary winding. Inside a circuit breaker, TA is used to provide current detection sampling, and the nameplate indicates the reference current I0 and the current ratio ITA; the current ratio is selected according to the rated current, for example, when the generator rated current is 720A, the TA specification may be 800/5A.

In the AC current measuring circuit, open circuit on the secondary side of the current transformer is strictly prohibited and series connection is required. The interior of the AC ammeter is a low-resistance current element, with two non-polarized terminal posts brought out externally, so the wiring can be exchanged. A terminal post is a metal contact component used in electrical systems to connect wires to equipment or circuit nodes, commonly found in PLC interfaces, instruments and control circuits; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of terminal posts is one of the common faults of electrical components; if the terminal posts of a thermal relay have poor contact, the heat generated by contact resistance will cause an error in the operating value. The electric main engine remote control system contains terminal posts.

In the DC current measuring circuit, the shunt must be installed on the positive side of the power supply. A DC ammeter with a larger capacity needs an external shunt to expand the range, with standard output voltages of 50mV and 75mV, of which 75mV is the most commonly used; the specification requires that it must be installed at the "+" pole position of the DC circuit. A shunt is a precision resistor element used to expand the range of a DC ammeter, connected in series in the circuit under test, and is often made of shunt manganin, whose resistance maximum-point temperature is higher than that of general-purpose manganin; the resistance temperature coefficient range of shunt manganin is 0~40×10⁻⁶/℃. DC current measurement steps: select the range -> connect the circuit under test -> read, that is, first select an appropriate range, then connect the instrument to the circuit under test, and finally read the indicated value. A DC ammeter uses a moving-coil instrument, and the wiring is marked with "+" and "-" polarity; reverse connection will cause the pointer to reverse; the internal resistance of a DC ammeter is very small, and it must be connected in series in the circuit under test; the ammeter range is usually 75mV, and the dial scale directly displays the rated current value of the shunt; the specification requires that the shunt must be installed at the "+" pole position of the circuit.

A moving-coil instrument is an electrical instrument with high sensitivity, and can only pass microampere-level current. The wiring is marked with "+" and "-" polarity; if connected in reverse, the pointer will deflect in the reverse direction; DC applications with a larger capacity require an external shunt, and the commonly used shunt output voltage is 75mV; in AC current measurement, moving-coil instrument structures with transmitters are now also used. When a moving-coil instrument is at full scale, the current flowing through its meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes, and it is usually used as a high-sensitivity meter head in analog multimeters such as MF-30 and MF-47. An electromagnetic instrument is an electrical instrument used to measure AC current; it was formerly often used for AC current measurement, and now is mostly replaced by moving-coil instruments with transmitters; as an AC ammeter, its interior is a current element with very low internal resistance; two terminal posts are brought out externally, with no polarity, so the wiring can be exchanged; it is usually made into standard 1A and 5A ranges, and domestically a 5A range is generally used. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; measuring current requires an ammeter, which is connected in series after the circuit is disconnected; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system.

The control transformer is used to provide power to the control circuit, and its characteristic is isolation from the main circuit. Its capacity is expressed in VA or kVA, that is, apparent power; the secondary rated current is limited by the selected capacity and has nothing to do with the active and reactive nature of the current;

Make the insulation fault of the control circuit not affect the main circuit; it is used in the main switchboard for the main circuit to provide working power or voltage signals to the control circuit. The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electric energy in the power station; the marine power station includes the main switchboard, and the main switchboard includes the main switch and also includes the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The main circuit provides working power or voltage signals to the relevant control circuits through the control transformer, achieving electrical isolation. The transformation ratios of voltage transformers commonly used in the main switchboard have two specifications: 380/110V and 440/110V. The main switchboard has the functions of circuit making and breaking, protection and alarm, parameter detection and power adjustment; its main functions include connecting or disconnecting the circuit, actuating the protection device and giving an alarm, detecting and displaying various electrical parameters, and it can adjust the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active and reactive power of the generators running in parallel.

On the main switchboard, the changeover switch undertakes the tasks of selecting indication and measurement points, setting the working state and issuing operating commands. When working, it is equivalent to a no-load transformer, and short circuit on the secondary side is strictly prohibited. The standard current of the secondary side of the current transformer is 5A or 1A. The clamp-on ammeter contains a current transformer and uses this principle to measure current; it can directly clamp and measure AC current without disconnecting the conductor.

In the coil-type current transformer, the primary winding has been wound on the core, while the busbar type has no such structure. The core is the magnetic-conducting component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as the reference point for insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to earth, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in the through-type current transformer, the large current conductor under test is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and their relative positions must be checked for accuracy. The shaft is a mechanical transmission component used to transmit torque and rotary motion, commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments; the movable parts of the two units of the electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; during contactor maintenance, the flexibility of the operating mechanism must be checked manually at regular intervals, and a small amount of lubricating oil must be injected into the shaft (if there is a bearing). The measurable performance of photoelectric power is the power value, and the measuring tool is the wattmeter. Electrodynamic instruments, induction instruments, rectifier instruments, electrostatic instruments, thermoelectric instruments and electronic instruments all belong to the types of electrical instruments.

Audio level test steps: insert the red test lead into the "dB" jack -> select the range -> connect the circuit under test -> read the value. Resistance measurement steps: select the range -> zero the meter head -> connect the test circuit or component -> read the value. Transistor measurement steps: determine the tube type and base -> determine the emitter and collector -> performance test -> estimate the current amplification factor. Thyristor measurement steps: determine the polarity -> measure the inter-electrode resistance. Wiring rules of the wattmeter: the current coil is connected in series into the circuit -> the voltage coil is connected in parallel into the circuit -> same-name end marking.

Basic requirements for maintenance personnel: personnel engaged in the maintenance of marine electrical equipment must be very familiar with the routing and connection relationships of the whole ship's electrical equipment lines, the working principles of various types of electrical equipment, and the positions and functions of various components in the equipment. Only on this basis can they quickly determine which link the problem lies in when a fault occurs, and then take correct handling measures. At the same time, maintenance personnel should also be familiar with the performance of electrical materials such as conductive and insulating materials, and be able to select them reasonably according to specific use conditions. Whether the selection of materials is appropriate directly affects whether the equipment can operate reliably after maintenance; therefore, this requirement is as important as being familiar with the equipment structure and principles, and neither may be neglected.

These five means each have their own emphasis, and are often used in combination. Asking means inquiring of the operators or relevant personnel about the phenomena before and after the fault occurred, the changes in the operating state of the equipment and whether there was any improper operation; looking means observing whether the appearance, wiring and components of the equipment have visible abnormalities such as burning, discoloration, fracture or looseness; touching means perceiving the temperature, vibration and other conditions of the components or the enclosure by hand under the premise of ensuring safety; listening means distinguishing whether the sound emitted during the operation of the equipment is normal, and whether there is abnormal friction sound, discharge sound or impact sound; smelling means detecting whether there is abnormal odor such as burnt smell or ozone smell. Through asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, maintenance personnel can form a preliminary judgment on the fault symptom, providing direction for subsequent measurement with instruments and further locating of the fault.

Combination of maintenance materials and diagnostic methods: fault diagnosis and maintenance of marine electrical equipment require maintenance personnel not only to master knowledge of equipment principles, structures and maintenance materials, but also to skillfully use the above traditional diagnostic means. Being familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment lines, working principles and the positions of various components is the prerequisite for accurately determining the fault location; being familiar with the performance of electrical materials such as conductive and insulating materials and selecting them reasonably is the basis for ensuring maintenance quality; and asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling are common methods for obtaining fault information and narrowing the scope of troubleshooting. The three cooperate with each other and constitute the basic literacy that maintenance personnel should possess in the maintenance and repair of measuring circuits of instruments.

The service environment of marine electrical equipment on ships differs greatly from that of land-use equipment; its insulation performance and damage are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt mist, oil mist and rolling vibration. As for vibration conditions, when the equipment is installed in a general location, it should withstand vibration of 2.0~13.2Hz with displacement ±1mm or 13.2~100.0Hz with acceleration ±7m/s²; when installed on reciprocating machines and in the steering gear compartment, it should withstand
2
5.0~1
0
0.0Hz acceleration ±40m/s² vibration. These two sets of values correspond respectively to two types of installation locations: the assessment focus for general locations is on the displacement amplitude in the low-frequency band and the acceleration amplitude in the medium-high frequency band, while the assessment focus for reciprocating machines and the steering gear compartment is concentrated on the acceleration amplitude in 25.0~100.0Hz, whose value is significantly higher than that of general locations, indicating that the mechanical stress there is more severe. In addition to vibration conditions, the equipment should also ensure reliable operation under the fluctuation of the specified voltage and frequency deviating from the rated values, and the electrical clearance and creepage distance between live parts at different potentials and between live parts and the earthed enclosure must be sufficient to withstand the actual applied working voltage. Electrical clearance and creepage distance are two parallel dimensional requirements: the former targets the shortest distance through space, and the latter targets the shortest path along the insulating surface; both must be adapted to the working voltage. As for the degree of protection provided by the enclosure, marine electrical equipment should comply with the provisions of IEC Publication 29, "Classification of Degrees of Protection Provided by Enclosures", or the equivalent national standard; this requirement constrains the ability of the enclosure to block solid foreign objects and water. Under the special environmental conditions of ships, marine electrical equipment needs to meet specific requirements for insulation, vibration and voltage/frequency fluctuation, and usually uses materials of Class E or above insulation grade as insulating materials; during maintenance, insulating varnish and the corresponding solvent must be correctly selected to meet the high insulation performance requirements. Insulating varnish and solvent must be selected as a matching set; if the solvent does not match the type of varnish, it will directly affect the insulation performance after impregnation and coating.

Marine electrical equipment belongs to the category of objects served by marine cables, and its operating state is closely related to the quality of cable laying and connection. In maintenance and repair, marine electrical equipment needs attention to the use conditions of marine materials, to the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations, and also to the performance requirements of insulating materials.

In terms of composition, marine electrical equipment uses components and functional units such as resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors, integrated circuits, power supply circuits and printed circuit boards, and also involves process links such as maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links and precautions for the use of electric soldering irons. Resistors, capacitors and inductors are passive components, diodes, transistors and integrated circuits are semiconductor devices, and power supply circuits and printed circuit boards are functional units and assembly substrates; these objects correspond respectively in maintenance to operations such as resistance measurement, capacitance and withstand voltage inspection, inductance inspection, polarity and volt-ampere characteristic inspection, pin and solder joint inspection, and line continuity inspection. Maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links targets the cleaning and heat dissipation maintenance of heating components inside the equipment, and precautions for the use of electric soldering irons target the tool operation specifications during welding repair; both belong to requirements at the maintenance process level.

The environmental factors covered by the use conditions of marine materials include: the maximum ambient air temperature is +40℃ (+45℃), and the minimum ambient air temperature is -25℃; the influence of humid sea air is present, the influence of salt mist is present, the influence of oil mist is present, and the influence of mold is present; the inclination is not greater than 25°, and the rolling is not greater than 25°; vibration is present, and impact is present. Among them, the temperature item gives two upper limits: +40℃ is the general value, +45℃ is the high-temperature value in parentheses, and the minimum value -25℃ defines the low-temperature end; the four items of humid air, salt mist, oil mist and mold are all marked as present, indicating that these four types of factors exist simultaneously on ships; inclination and rolling are both limited to 25°, and vibration and impact are marked as present, indicating that the two are mechanical factors that must be considered. The insulation performance and damage of electrical equipment are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt mist and oil mist, and the rolling and vibration of ships are important factors causing damage to electrical equipment. The particularity of the marine environment determines the special requirements for marine electrical equipment, and under different specifications and rules, the requirements for equipment performance indicators are slightly different. General marine electrical equipment should be able to work normally under the conditions listed in the specified environmental condition table, while marine electronic equipment and electrical equipment of special ships have separate use condition provisions. Therefore, when checking the applicability of equipment, it should first be confirmed whether it belongs to general marine electrical equipment, marine electronic equipment or electrical equipment of special ships, and then the corresponding condition clauses should be checked respectively.

For explosive hazardous locations, the relevant requirements apply to locations with explosion hazards such as paint rooms, battery rooms and oil pump rooms of general ships. In these locations, the class, level and temperature group of the qualified explosion-proof electrical equipment allowed to be installed should not be lower than the specified limits. Class, level and temperature group are three parallel judgment contents: the class indicates the category of explosive gas atmosphere to which the equipment applies, the level indicates the test gap or minimum igniting current ratio that the equipment can withstand, and the temperature group limits the maximum surface temperature of the equipment. Electrical equipment working in an explosive gas atmosphere must meet the relevant requirements of IEC Publication 79, etc., and its explosion-proof forms include eight types such as flameproof type (d), increased safety type (e) and intrinsically safe type (i). The flameproof type (d) relies on the enclosure to withstand an internal explosion without transmitting it, the increased safety type (e) avoids sparks and dangerous temperatures through structural measures, and the intrinsically safe type (i) limits the circuit energy so that it is insufficient to ignite the explosive mixture; the other types each have their own structural principles and applicable conditions.

The above provisions target explosive hazardous locations such as ship paint rooms and battery rooms, and put forward minimum standards for the class, level and temperature group of explosion-proof electrical equipment allowed to be installed; marine electrical equipment must pay attention to them during selection and installation.

The above environmental conditions and provisions do not exist in isolation, but jointly constitute the basic basis for the selection, installation and maintenance of marine electrical equipment. As for the use conditions of marine materials, their indicators correspond respectively to different assessment objects: the maximum and minimum values of ambient air temperature are used to define the allowable ambient temperature range of the equipment, the four influences of humid sea air, salt mist, oil mist and mold are used to explain the types of corrosion and deterioration factors, the two items of inclination and rolling are used to limit the amplitude of the ship's motion attitude, and the two items of vibration and impact are used to describe the forms of mechanical stress. The insulation performance and damage of electrical equipment are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt mist and oil mist; this relationship shows that the causes of insulation deterioration are not single, but vary with the climate of the navigation area and the medium conditions of the compartment. The rolling and vibration of ships are important factors causing damage to electrical equipment; therefore, the limits for rolling and vibration must match the installation location of the equipment.

As for the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations, their applicable objects are locations with explosion hazards such as paint rooms, battery rooms and oil pump rooms of general ships.

As for the composition and maintenance objects of marine electrical equipment, it uses components and functional units such as resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors, integrated circuits, power supply circuits and printed circuit boards; these components and functional units are the direct objects of insulation inspection, parameter measurement and replacement operations. Marine electrical equipment also involves process links such as maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links and precautions for the use of electric soldering irons; the former targets the cleaning and heat dissipation maintenance of heating components inside the equipment, and the latter targets the tool operation specifications during welding repair.

The insulation performance and damage condition of marine electrical equipment are directly related to factors such as the ship's navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt mist, oil mist and rolling vibration; therefore, when selecting and repairing materials, marine electrical equipment needs attention to the use conditions of marine materials, that is, the temperature resistance, moisture resistance, salt mist resistance, oil mist resistance and vibration resistance of the materials should be able to adapt to the environment of the location. Marine electrical equipment belongs to the category of objects served by marine cables; in maintenance, marine electrical equipment needs attention to the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations. In any location where explosive gas or vapor exists, its selection, installation and maintenance should be carried out according to the hazard level of that location, and the practices for ordinary locations must not be used as a substitute. The heat resistance grade, moisture resistance and mechanical strength of insulating materials should match the working conditions of the equipment, and the grade must not be arbitrarily lowered during replacement.

In fault diagnosis and state confirmation, voltage and current are two basic measurable quantities. Voltage values can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter, that is, the multimeter is used for voltage measurement, and the voltmeter is likewise used for voltage measurement; measuring current requires an ammeter, which is connected in series after disconnecting the circuit; the clamp-on ammeter can obtain current readings without cutting off the circuit, and is suitable for quickly checking the loop current during operation. During measurement, first confirm that the instrument range matches the range of the electrical quantity to be measured, then connect it in the correct wiring mode, and the reading should be compared with the rated value for judgment. For these devices containing electronic components, attention must also be paid to the maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links and the precautions for the use of electric soldering irons, so as to avoid affecting equipment performance due to improper operation during maintenance.

Marine cables belong to marine electrical equipment and are the basic components in marine electrical equipment that undertake the task of transmitting electrical energy and signals. Their structure consists of three major parts: the conductive copper core wire, the insulation layer and the protective layer, and none of the three can be omitted. The conductive copper core wire undertakes the function of conducting current and is made of copper material, utilizing the characteristics of copper of low resistivity, high tensile strength and ease of processing and welding. To adapt to the working conditions of vibration and impact on board ship, the conductive core wire is not a single solid copper wire but is stranded from no fewer than seven round soft copper wires of 0.26～2.74mm diameter; the stranded structure enables the cable to remain intact under repeated bending and vibration. The insulation layer is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer, and its function is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires from one another and prevent short circuit between core wires or earthing to ground. The protective layer is outside the insulation layer, and its function is to protect the cable from oil, water and chemical corrosion; when the application requires further improvement of mechanical strength or interference resistance, an armour layer must also be added outside the protective layer, and the specific form of the armour may be galvanized steel wire braiding or tinned steel wire braiding. The armour layer is usually marked as armour layer in the cable structure diagram, with the number 6. Besides marine cables themselves, general-purpose insulated wires are also composed of a conductive core wire and an insulation layer and are used for control box wiring; the insulation layer of enameled wire is a lacquer film, formed by coating the conductor with insulating varnish and drying it.

The model designation of marine cables has clear code meanings. The code C indicates marine power cable, CH indicates marine telecommunication cable; HY indicates oil-resistant rubber sheath, HF indicates flame-retardant rubber sheath. Taking model CHY31 as an example, it represents a marine rubber-insulated oil-resistant rubber-sheathed galvanized steel wire braided cable, suitable for fixed installation in locations where oil may be contacted. Type CHHYP is a marine rubber-insulated core-shielded oil-resistant rubber-sheathed tinned steel wire braided telecommunication cable, used for combined telephone station lines. In fire detection loops, the communication signal is specially processed, and a general two-core unshielded marine cable may be used.

The selection of marine cables needs to follow the marine cable selection principles. These principles contain two basic bases: first, select the cable model according to the nature and purpose of the power network, and also select the cable model according to the temperature and environmental conditions of the installation location; second, select the core cross-section of the cable according to the magnitude of the conducted current. That is to say, the determination of the model depends on the nature and purpose of the power network and the temperature and environmental conditions of the installation location, while the determination of the core cross-section depends on the magnitude of the conducted current. For marine cables, attention must be paid to the marine cable selection principles: when selecting the type, first clarify the nature and purpose of the power network, then check the temperature and environmental conditions of the installation location, and finally determine the core cross-section according to the magnitude of the conducted current; the three must be implemented in sequence and must not be reversed or omitted. If the model is selected incorrectly, the insulation material may not match the installation environment; if the core cross-section is selected too small, the temperature rise will be too high when conducting current, and long-term operation will accelerate the ageing of the insulation layer. Therefore the selection work should be checked one by one in combination with the specific circuit and must not be applied merely by experience.

Besides the cable itself, conductive materials are also widely used in marine motors, and the brush is one such important part. The brush is used as the conductive element for leading current into or out of between the stationary part and the sliding part of the motor, and contacts the collector ring to transfer current. DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators all need to be equipped with brushes. Common brushes are divided into three types: graphite, electrographite and metal graphite. Graphite brushes are soft in texture and are suitable for motors with general commutation conditions and uniform load; electrographite brushes are roasted at a high temperature above 2500℃, have good wear resistance and are suitable for various motors; metal graphite brushes are made by mixing graphite and copper powder, have a large current-carrying capacity and are suitable for high-current motors, specifically for DC generators such as charging and electrolysis and for starting motors.

When the contact area between the brush and the commutator is less than 70%, grinding treatment must be carried out, and the axial clearance of the brush is
0.2～
0.5mm. If the brush position is not on the neutral line, the DC motor will produce excessive sparking, and adjustment is needed by the induction method or the trial-run method. When excessive sparking under brush occurs, the contact condition between the brush and the commutator should be checked, the brush holder condition should be checked, and the brush position should be checked. When checking the contact condition between the brush and the commutator, observe whether the contact surface is uniform and whether there are signs of uneven wear or burning; when checking the brush holder condition, confirm whether the brush holder is loose and whether the brush can move freely up and down in the brush holder; when checking the brush position, verify whether the brush holder deviates from the neutral line. The above three checks should be combined with the armature vibration condition and the commutator segment condition so as to determine the source of the excessive sparking.

In electrical measurement and maintenance, resistance and current are two basic measurable quantities. The resistance value can be measured with a multimeter; the current value can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. To measure current, an ammeter must be used, and it is connected in series after the circuit is opened. Current is one of the quantities measured by electrical instruments and is used to understand equipment status; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action. When using a multimeter to measure current, the test leads need to be connected in series into the circuit, and attention must be paid to range selection to avoid damaging the instrument due to overcurrent.

Welding is an operating step in the maintenance of the PLC control system. The mechanism of welding is to heat the workpiece to melt the solder, produce atomic diffusion between the workpiece and the solder, and after solidification form an alloy bonding layer on the interface; this alloy bonding layer has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength, and the welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products. The case of broken input wiring corresponds to welding, that is, when the input wiring is broken, the connection needs to be restored by welding. During welding operation, the heating temperature, the amount of solder and the solidification time all affect the formation quality of the alloy bonding layer; if heating is insufficient, the solder cannot fully melt and diffuse; if heating is excessive, the workpiece or adjacent components may be damaged. In addition, damaging the insulation protective layer during operation is one of the causes of short circuit faults in electrical lines; when measuring the insulation resistance of a cable, the guard ring should be connected to the innermost insulation layer to eliminate errors; when calculating the number of turns of a DC coil, the wire diameter d must include the thickness of the insulation layer. These details all show that the insulation layer and the protective layer play a dual role of isolation and protection in the electrical performance of cables and coils, and once damaged during maintenance, they should be dealt with promptly to avoid leaving hidden dangers of short circuit.

In the internal construction of marine cables, an insulation layer is provided between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer, and this layer undertakes the task of separating the conductive core wires from one another and isolating them from the external environment. The main function of the insulation layer is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires, avoid short circuit between core wires, and also avoid the core wires forming an earthing path to ground.

For general-purpose insulated wires, their basic composition is only two parts: the conductive core wire and the insulation layer. Such wires are often used for wiring inside control boxes; during wiring, the insulation layer at the end of the core wire needs to be stripped to the corresponding length required by the terminal, and the copper core must not be damaged after stripping. Enameled wire is another case: its insulation layer is a lacquer film, formed by coating the conductor surface with insulating varnish and then drying it, and whether the lacquer film thickness is uniform directly affects the inter-turn insulation performance of the coil after winding. When measuring the insulation resistance of a cable, if the error is to be eliminated, the guard ring should be connected to the innermost insulation layer, so that the surface leakage current no longer flows through the measuring circuit. When calculating the number of turns of a DC coil, the wire diameter d taken must include the thickness of the insulation layer and must not be calculated only by the diameter of the bare conductor; otherwise the number of turns estimated from the window area will be too large and cannot actually fit during winding.

The manufacturing method of enameled wire is to coat the conductor with insulating varnish and then dry it; this wire material is generally used for winding electrical appliance coils, motor windings and transformer coils. The coil is one of the component parts of marine electrical equipment, made by winding insulated wire a certain number of turns on an insulating bobbin; it has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC, which makes the coil equivalent to a path in a DC circuit and present impedance in an AC circuit.

The winding is the coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, and its function is to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force. Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of AC motors; when judging, the DC resistance of the three-phase windings can be measured separately and compared with one another; the phase with a significantly smaller resistance value often has an inter-turn short circuit, and the phase with infinite resistance is phase failure. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, once the shunt resistor is open, the voltage regulator will lose its main regulating action; at this time, focus on checking whether the shunt resistor is burnt out or its lead is desoldered.

One use of the potentiometer is for bridge balancing. When the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R′ driven by the motor M enters the balancing adjustment process; when the bridge loses balance, the output signal drives the motor M to rotate until the resistance change of the feedback potentiometer R′ makes the bridge reach balance again. The potentiometer is also called potentiometer, and the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment belongs to this type of component, which is generally considered to be manually adjustable. The potentiometer has three pins, of which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the other two pins changes with the rotation of the shaft; when measuring, first measure the total resistance across the two fixed ends, then measure the resistance between the sliding end and the two ends respectively, and the sum of the two should be close to the total resistance. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form bridge balance. The automatic oil-fired boiler contains a potentiometer, and this type of component plays the role of converting pressure changes into changes of electrical parameters in the combustion regulation loop. The sliding contact of the potentiometer needs to be made of contact conductive materials, such as silver-iron alloy, hard copper, etc.; the requirements for such materials are low resistivity and difficulty in forming high-resistance oxides, otherwise after the contact surface oxidizes, the contact resistance increases and the bridge output will deviate.

Linking the above content together, marine cables contain an insulation layer, contactors contain a coil, marine motors contain a winding, automatic oil-fired boilers contain a potentiometer, and a multimeter is used to measure resistance. The insulation layer in a marine cable is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer, and its function is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires and prevent short circuit or earthing between core wires; the coil, as a component part of marine electrical equipment, can be wound from enameled wire and is also widely found in motor windings and transformer coils;

A fault of the KM coil in the contactor will directly cause the armature to fail to close and the motor fails to start; for the two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, inside the insulation resistance tester, the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

In the maintenance and repair of marine electrical equipment, conductive materials not only undertake the task of electrical energy transmission but are also widely used in protection, measurement and commutation. The fuse is marked with the symbol FU in circuit diagrams, and its function is overload protection and short circuit protection. The protective conductive materials for making fuse and fuse must have the characteristics of low melting point and certain mechanical strength; on board ship, protective conductive materials such as lead-tin alloy and lead-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy are commonly used to make fuses. The fuse is a safety electrical appliance; when overload and short circuit occur in the power network or electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; it belongs to distribution electrical appliances and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection.
