The fuse is a component part of marine electrical equipment, and its manufacturing material is protective conductive material such as lead-tin alloy or lead-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy. The fuse is made of protective conductive material and has the characteristics of low melting point and certain mechanical strength; it is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, alongside resistors, capacitors, etc. When replacing the fuse, attention must be paid to matching the original model and specification, and the power switch must be disconnected. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components; when replacing the fuse of a digital multimeter, the power should be disconnected and a fuse matching the original model and specification should be selected. The electric main engine remote control system contains a fuse, and broken input wiring corresponds to welding treatment.

Resistance is the object whose resistance value can be measured, and the measuring tool is a multimeter. A resistor has a certain resistance value, geometric shape and technical performance, and plays a current-limiting role in a circuit. Resistors are usually divided into three major categories: fixed resistors, variable resistors and special resistors, among which fixed resistors are most widely used in electronic products. Common fixed resistors can be divided by manufacturing material into RT-type carbon film resistors, RJ-type metal film resistors, RX-type wirewound resistors and chip resistors, and their power ratings include 0.125W (1/8W), 0.25W (1/4W),
0.5W (1/2W), 1W, 2W, 3W, 5W, 7W, 10W, etc. Marine electrical equipment uses resistors; resistors include variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors; the resistor inspection procedure applies to resistors; resistors may suffer resistance faults, and resistance faults belong to the category of resistors.

The shunt is used to expand the range of an ammeter, and its standard output voltages are 50mV and 75mV, of which 75mV is the most commonly used. The shunt is often made of shunt manganin, whose resistance maximum-point temperature is higher than that of general-purpose manganin, and the resistance temperature coefficient range of shunt manganin is 0~40×10⁻⁶/℃. The shunt is a precision resistor element used to expand the range of a DC ammeter and is connected in series in the measured circuit; a DC ammeter with a larger capacity needs an external shunt to expand the range.

Welding is one of the maintenance procedures of the PLC control system.

Voltage is the object whose voltage value can be measured, and the measuring tools are a multimeter and a voltmeter. Current is the object whose current value can be measured, and the measuring tools are a multimeter, an ammeter and a clamp-on ammeter. A multimeter is used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and a clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

The S-3 model has a resistivity coefficient of 8~20Ω·mm²/m, a rated current density of 11A/cm², and a permissible peripheral speed of 25m/s; the DS-4 model has a resistivity coefficient of 6~16Ω·mm²/m, a friction coefficient ≤0.2, and a permissible peripheral speed up to 40m/s; the DS-8 model has a resistivity coefficient of 31~50Ω·mm²/m, a contact voltage drop of 1.9~2.9V, and an operating pressure of 20~40kPa; the DS-52 model has a resistivity coefficient of 12~22Ω·mm²/m, a permissible peripheral speed up to a maximum of 50m/s, and a wear amount ≤0.15mm/50h.

Electrographitic brushes are made from graphite, coke, carbon black and other raw materials, roasted at a high temperature above 2500℃, have good wear resistance and are easy to machine, and are suitable for various types of motors and motors with difficult commutation conditions. The DS-72 model has a rated current density of 12A/cm² and a permissible peripheral speed of 70m/s; the DS-74 model has a resistivity coefficient of 35~80Ω·mm²/m and an operating pressure of 20~40kPa; the DS-112 model has a 50h wear amount ≤0.1mm and a contact voltage drop of 2.5~3.7V. During the acceptance of a DC motor after overhaul, its pressure is generally controlled at about 2.45MPa. Metal-graphite brushes are made of graphite mixed with copper powder and other metal powders, have good electrical conductivity and a large current-carrying capacity, and are suitable for high-current motors such as DC generators used for charging, electrolysis and electroplating, as well as for low-voltage small traction motors and motors for starting automobiles and small diesel engines. The TS-2 model has a resistivity coefficient of 0.1~0.35Ω·mm²/m and a rated current density of 20A/cm².

During maintenance, the motor brush model is generally not easily changed, and replacement should be made according to the original model and specification. Replacing the brush is a maintenance procedure for DC motors or equipment such as electric drills, referring to replacing worn, damaged or poorly contacting brushes to restore electrical conductivity. When an electric drill fails to start due to brush wear, the repair method is to replace the brush; if the brush wire is loose, the brush should be repaired or replaced to solve the failure of the electric drill to start. During brush grinding, the contact area must be treated if it is less than 70%, and the axial clearance is 0.2～0.5mm; if the brush position is not on the neutral line, it will cause excessive commutation sparking, which needs to be adjusted by the induction method or the trial-run method. The brush and the collector ring contact to transmit current; when the contact area between the brush and the commutator is less than 70%, grinding treatment must be carried out; if the brush position is not on the neutral line, it will cause excessive sparking in the DC motor.

The commutator is a rotating sliding contact component used for leading current in and out in DC motors and wound-rotor motors, and is composed of commutator segments. When disassembling a DC motor, care should be taken to prevent damage to the winding ends, commutator or collector ring; carbon powder must not accumulate in the commutator grooves, so as to avoid short circuits between segments. A marine motor includes a commutator and brushes. When checking the contact between the brush and the commutator, the commutator and brush are used; when checking the brush holder, the brush is used; when checking the commutator segments, the commutator is used; when checking the brush position, the brush is used.

A marine cable belongs to marine electrical equipment, is composed of conductive copper core wires, an insulation layer and a protective layer, and is used to conduct current and resist environmental corrosion. The insulation layer electrically insulates the conductive core wires; the protective layer is used to protect the cable from oil, water and chemical corrosion, and when necessary, armoring is added to enhance mechanical strength and anti-interference capability. A marine cable includes conductive copper core wires, an insulation layer, a protective layer and armor, and attention must be paid to the selection principles of marine cables. The selection principles are to select the model according to the nature, purpose and environmental conditions of the power grid, and to select the core cross-section according to the magnitude of the conducted current. HY indicates oil-resistant rubber sheath, and HF indicates flame-retardant rubber sheath.

The standard model designation of the marine rubber-insulated flame-retardant rubber-sheathed cable is CHF; its two-core structure has a core cross-section specification range of 0.8 to 120mm², its main use is fixed installation, and it is required to avoid contact with oil; there is a flexible cable variant with the same name, used to connect mobile electrical equipment. The model designation of the marine rubber-insulated flame-retardant rubber-sheathed galvanized steel wire braided cable is CHF31; its core structure is three-core, with a cross-section range between 0.8 and 240mm², and its main use is the same as that of the CHF type, for fixed installation and requiring avoidance of contact with oil; the insulation material is rubber, the sheath is flame-retardant rubber sheath, and the outer protective layer is composed of galvanized steel wire braiding. The model designation of the marine rubber-insulated flame-retardant rubber-sheathed flexible cable is CHF (note: the name column in the table corresponds to this model); it belongs to the domestic marine cable series, has a core cross-section specification range of 0.8 to 70 square millimeters, and its main use is to connect mobile electrical equipment, with the use environment requiring avoidance of contact with oil; unlike the fixed-installation CHF type flame-retardant rubber-sheathed cable, this flexible cable is dedicated to mobile equipment. The model code of the marine rubber-insulated oil-resistant rubber-sheathed cable is CHY, and its main use is fixed installation, different from the flexible cable used for mobile equipment; it has oil-resistant characteristics, is allowed to work in environments where oil may be contacted, and the use conditions require avoidance of direct sunlight; its derived models CHY31 (galvanized steel wire braiding) and CHY32 (tinned steel wire braiding) have the same use as this type.

In the practical application of marine conductive materials, the brush is a conductive part that must be equipped on DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators, and its function is to complete the leading in or leading out of current between the stationary part and the sliding part of the motor. The brush and the collector ring contact to transmit current; once the contact state deteriorates, the conduction of current will be directly affected, so the inspection of the brush occupies an important position in commutator fault diagnosis.

Graphite brushes are made by mixing natural graphite with binders such as pitch and coal tar and pressing them; when not heated at high temperature, they contain more impurities and are relatively soft in texture. These parameters respectively correspond to the differences among different models of graphite brushes in resistivity coefficient, current density, peripheral speed, friction coefficient, contact voltage drop, operating pressure and wear amount, and should be checked item by item during model selection. The resistivity coefficient reflects the conductive capability of the brush itself; the smaller the value, the lower the loss when current passes through; the rated current density limits the current allowed to pass per unit contact area, and exceeding this value will aggravate heating; the permissible peripheral speed determines the upper limit of linear speed that the brush can withstand, and is directly related to the diameter and rotational speed of the commutator or collector ring; the friction coefficient and operating pressure jointly affect the mechanical wear between the brush and the commutator surface; the contact voltage drop is related to the energy loss during commutation; and the wear amount is measured by the length reduction per 50 hours to measure the service life of the brush. If any one of the above indicators does not meet the operating conditions, it will shorten the brush life and affect the commutation quality. Its application range is wider than that of graphite brushes, and it can be used for various types of motors and motors with difficult commutation conditions. Too high a pressure will increase friction and wear, while too low a pressure will make the contact unstable and easily produce sparking under the brush, so during acceptance after overhaul, the pressure must be confirmed as an independent inspection item. Because copper powder and other metal powders are mixed in, its resistivity coefficient is significantly lower than that of graphite brushes and electrographitic brushes, and the rated current density is correspondingly increased, so it is suitable for undertaking current conduction tasks in low-voltage, high-current occasions.

Abnormalities of the brush during operation often need to be judged in combination with the idea of commutator fault diagnosis. Among them, the three tasks of checking the contact between the brush and the commutator, checking the brush holder, and checking the brush position are all directly aimed at the brush itself. A loose brush holder can also cause excessive sparking under the brush; motor overload and poor contact between brush and commutator are also common causes of this phenomenon.

The conductive parts that cooperate with the brush are the coil and the winding. Enameled wire is made by coating the conductor with insulating varnish and drying it, and is generally used for winding electrical appliance coils, motor windings and transformer coils. Once a local short circuit or phase failure occurs in the winding, the current distribution will deviate from the normal state, thereby causing overcurrent and a rise in temperature rise, so when dealing with the problem of motor overheating, the winding state is an object that needs to be checked with emphasis.

In the maintenance and testing stage, the multimeter is the most frequently used instrument and can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current. Voltage measurement is likewise accomplished with a multimeter or voltmeter. When measuring resistance, voltage and current, the range selection should be adapted to the measured value, and the connection method must also be correct; otherwise the reading cannot reflect the true state of the equipment. When input wiring breakage occurs, welding treatment needs to be carried out correspondingly to restore the continuity of the line. During welding, the control of the heating degree, the amount of solder and the solidification process will all affect the quality of the bonding layer; a poor bonding layer will increase the contact resistance, thereby affecting the signal transmission and power supply reliability of the entire control system.

Marine electrical equipment cannot operate without the support of various insulating materials, and the quality of their insulation performance is directly related to whether the equipment can work safely and reliably. Marine electrical equipment usually uses materials of Class E or above insulation grade as insulating materials, and during maintenance, insulating varnish and the corresponding solvent must be correctly selected to meet the high insulation performance requirements. For insulating materials, there are a series of performance requirements that need to be grasped. Insulation withstand voltage strength refers to the voltage kV value that a 1mm-thick insulating material can withstand when broken down; insulating materials should have high insulation resistance and withstand voltage strength to avoid earth leakage breakdown; when the electric field electromotive force strength increases to the limit value, the insulating material will be broken down. In addition to withstand voltage strength, mechanical strength is measured by the tensile value; the larger the tensile value, the higher the mechanical strength; the expansion coefficient is required to be small; thermal stability formulates the component operating temperature according to the physical, chemical and electrical properties of the insulating material; and biological resistance is used to prevent mold growth. These indicators together constitute the technical requirements that marine insulating materials must meet in terms of dielectric properties, mechanical strength and thermal stability. The reason why the indicator of insulation withstand voltage strength uses 1mm thickness as the benchmark is to establish a comparable scale among different materials; the higher its value, the greater the applied voltage per unit thickness of material that can be withstood without breakdown, so during selection, calculation can be made according to the working voltage and material thickness. Mechanical strength is expressed by the tensile value; the larger the tensile value, the less likely the material is to be pulled apart or torn during operations such as wrapping, coil insertion and binding. Biological resistance targets the problem of mold growth, preventing the material from growing mold and deteriorating in a damp and warm environment.

Marine electrical equipment is closely related to marine cables; marine cables belong to the constituent parts of marine electrical equipment, and marine cables in turn include an insulation layer. The function of the insulation layer is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires and prevent short circuits or earthing between core wires; in the marine cable structure, the insulation layer is located between the conductive copper core wires and the protective layer; the conductive copper core wires are responsible for conducting current, the insulation layer covers the outside of the copper core wires to achieve electrical isolation between core wires and between core wires and earth, and the protective layer is then wrapped outside the insulation layer for protection. When selecting materials for marine electrical equipment, attention must also be paid to the conditions of use of marine materials, the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations, and the performance requirements of insulating materials. As far as the operating environment is concerned, the insulation performance and damage of marine electrical equipment are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt spray, oil mist and swaying vibration; under the special environmental conditions of ships, electrical equipment must meet specific requirements for insulation, vibration and voltage and frequency fluctuation. Marine electrical equipment should ensure reliable operation under fluctuations in which the specified voltage and frequency deviate from the rated values, and its enclosure protection degree should comply with IEC Publication 29, Classification of Degrees of Protection Provided by Enclosures, or the equivalent national standard. When installed in general locations, it should withstand vibration of 2.0~13.2Hz with a displacement of ±1mm or 13.2~100.0Hz with an acceleration of ±7m/s²; this vibration condition indicates that the equipment and its insulation fixing parts must withstand a larger displacement amplitude in the low-frequency band and a larger acceleration amplitude in the high-frequency band.

In the composition of marine electrical equipment, resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors, integrated circuits, power supply circuits, printed circuit boards, etc. are all common constituent links. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter. When using a multimeter to measure the resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is a capacitor in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with power on; otherwise the charge stored in the capacitor will discharge through the test leads, which will both affect the reading and may damage the instrument. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open circuit in the shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating function.

Among the solid insulating materials commonly used on ships, polyester film is an important variety. Its thickness range is 0.006～0.10mm, its insulation strength is >130kV/mm, and the measured breakdown voltage value is 130~230 kV/mm. Polyester film is the main insulating material of Class B heat resistance grade (permissible operating temperature 130℃), and is also a commonly used solid insulating material for ships with a heat resistance grade of Class E and an insulation strength greater than 130kV/mm. It is often made into polyester film adhesive tape, with a thickness of 0.055～0.17mm and a withstand voltage >100kV/mm; in addition, there is also a polyester film insulating paper composite foil form, whose breakdown voltage is 40 kV/mm. In the maintenance of small motors, 0.05mm-thick polyester film can be compounded with blue shell paper for slot insulation. When selecting polyester film, the thinner the thickness, the easier it is to fit in the slot and at the winding ends, but the withstand voltage level must match the working voltage; the value of insulation strength greater than 130kV/mm can be used as a basis for calculation.

Blue shell paper is commonly used in the maintenance of motors and electrical appliances; its thickness range is 0.1～0.4mm, the commonly used blue shell paper thickness is generally 0.15mm, and the insulation strength is 7kV/mm. For Class E insulation of small motors, polyester film can be compounded with blue shell paper; when used as slot insulation, a layer of 0.15mm-thick blue shell paper is commonly used, that is, the polyester film bears the higher withstand voltage, and the blue shell paper provides certain mechanical support and isolation. Pressboard is likewise commonly used in the maintenance of motors and electrical appliances; its color is mostly red, also called red pressboard, and it is used in daily maintenance for padding and making frames, etc. The standard thickness of pressboard is 0.5～2.5mm, the thickness range of light red pressboard is 0.5～3.0mm, and light red pressboard at a thickness of 0.5～0.9mm has a withstand voltage of not less than 7kV. The selection of thickness for gaskets and frames depends on the assembly clearance and the required mechanical strength, while the withstand voltage value is used to judge whether it can be used in locations of the corresponding voltage level.

Among the various insulating tapes commonly used on ships, polyester film adhesive tape is generally commonly used because of its good electrical performance, relatively thin thickness and high withstand voltage; its thickness range is 0.055～0.17mm, and its withstand voltage strength is greater than 100kV/mm. White cloth tape is divided into two structural forms, twill and plain weave; when selecting white cloth tape, its tensile strength is used as the basis. If not subjected to varnish impregnation treatment, white cloth tape has poor electrical performance and easily absorbs moisture, so white cloth tape is generally only used for reinforcing mechanical strength and binding, and is usually not used as an insulating material. The twill and plain weave structures differ in tensile strength and extensibility; when the binding part is subjected to greater force, selection should be made according to tensile strength.

For the problem that insulation materials are prone to mold growth due to ambient temperature changes, heaters are often added on board to raise the ambient temperature. The maintenance requirement for such electrical equipment with a heating link is regular maintenance and energization for operation, with the purpose of preventing condensation and driving out moisture, thereby achieving a mold-proof effect. In the use of marine electrical equipment, attention must be paid to the maintenance item of maintenance of electrical equipment with a heating link, that is, the electrical equipment with added heaters on board is maintained periodically and energized for operation, and the energization of the heater makes the internal temperature of the equipment higher than the surrounding environment, avoiding water vapor condensing into dew on the insulation surface, and at the same time driving out the moisture that has penetrated in, so that mold loses the conditions for breeding. In the use of marine electrical equipment, attention must also be paid to the precautions for use of the electric soldering iron, which involve the operating specifications during welding operations.

In the actual selection and maintenance judgment of marine insulating materials, the insulation performance is often indirectly confirmed through electrical quantities, among which voltage is the most basic measured quantity. The tool used to measure the voltage value is the multimeter, and a voltmeter can also be used to complete the same reading task. For marine electrical equipment, voltage is not only the direct basis for judging whether a circuit is energized and whether the insulation has been broken down, but also one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in fault diagnosis;

Polyester film is one of the more widely used solid insulating materials for marine use. When selecting, the thickness, insulation strength and heat resistance class should be checked in combination, avoiding looking at only one of them and ignoring the rest.

A coil is a component of marine electrical equipment; it is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating skeleton, and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. A contactor contains a coil, and the state of the coil directly affects whether the contactor can operate normally. It can thus be seen that the coil is both a functional component that performs electromagnetic action and a key component inside insulation testing instruments, and its winding quality, the state of the insulated wire and the insulation condition of the skeleton are all related to the insulation level of the entire equipment.

Linking the above contents together, the voltage measurement result can reflect whether insulating materials such as polyester film have been broken down or are close to breakdown, and the coil, as a component inside the contactor and the insulation resistance tester, has the winding of its insulated wire and the insulation treatment of its skeleton directly dependent on materials such as polyester film. When rewinding the slot insulation of a small motor, the insulation can be restored by the method of compositing 0.05mm polyester film with blue shell paper, or by using polyester film adhesive tape with a thickness of 0.055～0.17mm and a withstand voltage greater than 100kV/mm, as well as polyester film insulating paper composite foil with a breakdown voltage of 40 kV/mm. For parts with higher heat resistance requirements, attention should be paid to the limitation of the allowable working temperature of polyester film of 130℃, which is a Class B heat resistance class, while also taking into account the general statement that it is a Class E heat resistance class material with an insulation strength greater than 130kV/mm. When measuring the insulation resistance tester, it is necessary to confirm that the relative positions of the two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, are accurate, so as to avoid obtaining an incorrect voltage reading due to improper coil positions, which would then affect the judgment of the insulation state of the polyester film.

There are many types of components commonly used in electronic equipment; resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors, thyristors, integrated circuits, fuses, connectors and various sensors all belong to this category. During the maintenance and repair of marine electrical equipment, the performance of these components needs to be measured and judged, and the multimeter is the most basic testing tool.

A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; at full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. Multimeters are divided into analog and digital types; the MF-47 multimeter is a specific model of multimeter, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and the panel is provided with four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, current and capacitance, and can also be used to detect diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples. The clamp-on ammeter is specially used to measure current, and the circuit does not need to be disconnected during measurement. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit; voltage measurement uses a multimeter or a voltmeter.

Resistors are generally divided into three major categories: fixed resistors, variable resistors and special resistors, among which fixed resistors are most widely used in electronic products. Commonly used fixed resistors can be divided by manufacturing material into RT-type carbon film resistors, RJ-type metal film resistors, RX-type wirewound resistors and chip resistors. In the model naming rule, R represents resistor, T represents carbon film, J represents metal, and X represents wirewound, all taking the first letters of the pinyin. The color ring marking method is commonly used internationally; four-ring resistors are generally carbon film resistors, and five-ring resistors are generally metal film resistors. Chip resistors, i.e. SMT packaged resistors, are usually marked with three or four digits, such as 334 indicating 33×10^4Ω, i.e. 330kΩ. Rated power refers to the maximum allowable power consumption under specified ambient temperature and humidity and without air circulation, under long-term continuous load without damage; power ratings include 0.125W (1/8W), 0.25W (1/4W),
0.5W (1/2W), 1W, 2W, 3W, 5W, 7W, 10W, etc. A resistor has a certain resistance value, geometric shape and technical performance, and plays a current-limiting role in a circuit. Resistors include variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors. A variable resistor, also called a potentiometer, has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the two pins changes with the rotation of the shaft; it is generally considered that a potentiometer can be adjusted manually, while a variable resistor is smaller in size, mounted on a circuit board and not frequently adjusted. In the debugging of a regulated power supply, a variable resistor is connected in series as a load to test the overcurrent protection current value. For the master controller using a variable resistor, the contact condition between the sliding arm and the resistor needs to be checked during secondary maintenance. A potentiometer is often used as a zeroing element in a differential amplifier circuit, and in the debugging of a regulated power supply, the output voltage is made to change within a specified range such as
1.25～
7.5V by adjusting the voltage-regulating potentiometer. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure is lower than the set value, YBD drives the sliding contact of potentiometer R0 to rise, causing the bridge to become unbalanced and triggering the action of the servo motor. In the voltage circuit of the insulation resistance tester, a potentiometer is connected in series as a regulator, used to adjust the error of the pointer at the "∞" position. The volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component. When measuring the resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is a capacitor in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with power on. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage corrector to lose its main regulating action. The resistor detection steps apply to resistors; a resistor may suffer a resistance fault, and a resistance fault belongs to the resistor.

A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle, and its characteristic is to block direct current and pass alternating current. In a circuit, a capacitor is generally represented by "C" plus a number, such as C25 indicating a capacitor numbered 25. The hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC), which is related to the signal frequency and capacitance. By polarity, capacitors are divided into polarized capacitors such as electrolytic capacitors and tantalum capacitors, and non-polarized capacitors. The main performance indicators include capacitance, withstand voltage value and temperature resistance value; the withstand voltage value is the maximum working voltage. By dielectric material, they are divided into electrolytic, mica, paper, ceramic, glass glaze capacitors, etc. Common types include electrolytic capacitors, ceramic disc capacitors, chip capacitors, monolithic capacitors, etc. In the numerical marking method, the first two digits are the significant digits, and the third digit is the multiplier of 10, with the unit usually being pF.

In a filter circuit, the capacitor is connected in parallel with the load, and the AC component is filtered out by charging and discharging; the withstand voltage value of the capacitor in the filter circuit should not be less than
1.42 times the AC effective value. Common faults include pin corrosion and open circuit, desoldering and cold solder joints, and reduced capacitance or breakdown short circuit caused by leakage. When measuring earth leakage with a multimeter, if the pointer cannot return to infinity, the reading multiplied by the range is the leakage resistance; when measuring earth leakage with an analog multimeter, the leakage resistance value is tens to hundreds of megohms, except for electrolytic capacitors. The larger the capacitance, the larger the swing amplitude of the multimeter pointer to the right and the slower the return speed. An electrolytic capacitor has a small leakage current when connected with correct polarity; when the end connected to the black test lead is the positive electrode, the polarity can be judged on this basis. Slow starting and reduced speed of an electric fan may be due to insufficient capacitance, and a capacitor of the same specification needs to be replaced.

An inductor is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating skeleton, and its characteristic is to pass direct current and block alternating current; the higher the frequency, the greater the coil impedance. Inductors are mainly used for circuit functions such as filtering, trapping, oscillation and magnetic energy storage. The basic unit is the henry (H), commonly used are millihenry (mH) and microhenry (μH). Classification includes air-core inductors and magnetic-core inductors such as iron-core and copper-core inductors. Common types include fixed inductors, trimming inductors, color-code inductors, etc. An inductance coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating skeleton, and can pass direct current while blocking alternating current. A freewheeling diode is usually connected in parallel across the two ends of a solenoid valve coil, to prevent the coil from generating a high-voltage output when the transistor loses power. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. The inductor detection steps apply to inductors.

A diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity; under forward voltage it conducts with small resistance, and under reverse voltage it cuts off. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity; under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite; it is often used in circuits such as rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization and polarity protection. By function, they are divided into rectifier diodes such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, Schottky diodes such as BAT85, etc.; in addition, there are light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The circuit symbol is VD, with numbering such as VD5; the light-emitting diode symbol is VL, the photodiode is VDL, and the Zener diode is VS. The exterior of low-power diodes is often marked with a color ring to indicate the negative electrode, or the polarity is marked with a special symbol and the letters P/N. The rated current of the 1N4000 series is all 1A, and the withstand voltage value increases from 50V for 1N4001 to 1000V for 1N4007. When measuring polarity with an analog multimeter, the resistance is small when the black test lead is connected to the anode and the red test lead to the cathode, which is forward bias; when measuring a diode with a digital multimeter, the forward voltage drop is displayed when the red test lead is connected to the positive electrode and the black test lead to the negative electrode, and is less than 1V. The diode detection steps apply to diodes. Diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes.

A light-emitting diode is a semiconductor device capable of emitting light in colors such as red, green and yellow, has unidirectional conductivity, and its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode; it is commonly used as a circuit working state indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display.

The external dimensions include diameters of 3mm, 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle. The working current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model, and in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage. The conduction voltage is generally above 1.7V, so a single
1.5V battery cannot light up a light-emitting diode. The method for identifying the positive and negative electrodes is: the long pin is the positive electrode; in the visual method, the one with the smaller electrode and shorter body is the positive electrode, and the one with the larger electrode is the negative electrode. An ordinary multimeter cannot test a light-emitting diode on any range from R×1 to R×1k; the R×10k range, i.e. a higher voltage range, is needed to light it up for testing. In the fault inspection of the PLC control system, if the POWER lamp off and the fuse is not blown, it is necessary to check whether the light-emitting diode is broken down, and if so, replace the light-emitting diode. In the simulation test device of the main engine remote control system, light-emitting diodes are used to display the working state of the remote control system and the action condition of the external solenoid valves. For light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes.

A Zener diode is commonly represented in a circuit by "VS" plus a number, such as VS5 indicating a Zener diode numbered 5. Its main characteristic is that after breakdown, the voltage across it remains basically unchanged, and its forward conduction characteristic is the same as that of an ordinary diode. After being connected into a circuit, if the power supply voltage fluctuates or the voltages at various points change, the voltage across the load will remain basically unchanged. The fault manifestations are mainly three cases: open circuit, short circuit and unstable voltage stabilization value. The open-circuit fault manifests as an increase in power supply voltage; short circuit and unstable voltage stabilization value manifest as the power supply voltage dropping to 0V or unstable output. Commonly used models include the 1N4728 to 1N4761 series, corresponding to voltage stabilization values ranging from
3.3V to 75V. In the two-wire wiring of a fire detector, the terminal device can use a Zener diode to maintain the microampere-level monitoring current. During black smoke inspection, if there is no response to smoke and no alarm is ever given, it may be caused by damage to the Zener diode. A Zener diode may suffer a Zener diode fault, and a Zener diode fault belongs to the Zener diode.

A transistor internally contains two PN junctions and has current amplification capability; it is divided into NPN type and PNP type, and the working characteristics of the two can complement each other, such as the complementary pair in an OTL circuit. In a circuit it is commonly represented by "VT" plus a number, such as VT17 indicating a transistor numbered 17. Commonly used PNP models include A92, 9015, etc.; NPN models include A42, 9014, 9018, 9013, 9012, etc. The common-emitter circuit is often used in the intermediate stage of a multistage amplifier, and the emitter follower circuit is used for low-frequency input/output stages or impedance matching. The transistor type is judged by the unidirectional conductivity of the PN junction: a low resistance measured with the red test lead connected to the base indicates PNP type, and a low resistance measured with the black test lead connected to the base indicates NPN type. For a medium- and small-power silicon transistor of good performance, the forward resistance of the emitter junction and collector junction is several hundred ohms to one thousand ohms, and the reverse resistance is several hundred kilohms or more. The faster the penetration current increases with temperature, the worse the transistor performance; the larger the pointer deflection, the more unstable the performance. A transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to the transistor.

A thyristor, also called SCR, also known as a silicon controlled rectifier, allows measurement of polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode. An integrated circuit has the advantages of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration increases, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits have appeared.

Pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise; for ease of maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often soldered onto the circuit board for direct plug-in. Common package forms include the four-side inward-hook-leg PLCC, the two-side gull-wing-leg SOIC, the dual in-line DIP, and power integrated circuit packages. The 4000-series CMOS integrated circuits are numbered 4000 to 4500, the vast majority being 14- or 16-pin packages, powered by a wide 3 to 15V supply, and very sensitive to static electricity. TTL logic chips are numbered starting from 74××00, such as 74LS and 74HC, all powered by a single 5V supply. Common test methods include non-in-circuit measurement, i.e. comparing the DC resistance values of each pin, in-circuit measurement, i.e. testing pin voltage/resistance/current, and the substitution method, i.e. replacing with a known-good part of the same model. It is strictly forbidden to test integrated circuits with an insulation resistance tester, lest the high voltage break down the electronic devices within. In the main engine remote control system, a contactless electric remote control system may be constructed using integrated circuits; such electronic control systems have a constant failure rate and do not require regular preventive maintenance.

Fuse is one of the components commonly used in electronic circuits, alongside resistor and capacitance. A fuse is a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material, featuring a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength, and is made of protective conductive materials such as aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy. When replacing, note that it must match the original model and specifications, and switch off the power supply. Fuses are used for circuit overload or short circuit protection; in the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Connectors are used for circuit connection and assembly; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of connectors is a common electrical fault.

A sensor is the information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors. One function of the differential amplifier circuit in the signal conditioning circuit is to amplify and convert the small signal sent by the sensor into the required signal. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. A photoresistor is made by depositing a layer of cadmium sulfide (CdS) film on a ceramic substrate and is a semiconductor element. In complete darkness its resistance can reach several megohms or more, and under strong light it can drop to several kilohms or even below 1kΩ. A photoresistor uses the photoconductive property to convert an optical signal into an electrical signal, and is used in automatic detection, photoelectric control and alarm circuits. The resistance of a photoresistor changes with the intensity of external light: small resistance under strong light, large resistance under weak light. In marine boilers it serves as a flame monitoring element; when ignition succeeds, the resistance decreases, causing the relay to operate and stop the ignition. During troubleshooting, check whether it has aged, whether the photosensitive window is covered by accumulated oil grime affecting the light flux, or whether it is aimed at the flame. For testing, use the R×1k range of a multimeter; normally the resistance values under light and in darkness differ markedly; if the measured resistance does not change, it has failed; if both are zero, it is a short circuit; if both are infinity, it is an open circuit. In boiler automatic control, the photoresistor is used to detect the flame; when ignition succeeds, the resistance of the photoresistor decreases, energizing 1JY, which energizes 3JZ, which energizes 4JZ; 4JZ (31, 28) opens and the ignition transformer is de-energized. A rectifier is used to convert alternating current into direct current; the electrical graphic symbol for a full-wave bridge rectifier is UR. In the controllable phase compound excitation constant-voltage device, rectifier fault is one of the sub-causes of phase compound excitation device faults; if the UR rectifier has an open diode, it will cause a voltage deviation of |U0-Ufe| greater than ΔU1. The RS_0 fuse is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers and their complete sets.

In the maintenance of electronic equipment, the multimeter is the most basic testing tool. A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, and is divided into analog and digital types. The analog multimeter uses a magnetoelectric high-sensitivity meter head, with the current through the meter head at full scale being about a few microamperes to a few hundred microamperes; the MF-47 multimeter is a multimeter, and its dial has six scales, whereas common models such as the MF-30 have only four scales. The digital multimeter is likewise a multimeter and is an electronic measuring instrument; the power switch must be turned on before use, and models without an auto-power-off function must be switched off after use; it has capacitance, diode and transistor hFE test functions. When measuring DC current with a multimeter, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range and the meter head is connected in series in the broken branch; when measuring DC voltage, the test leads are connected in parallel across the component under test, and when the range is uncertain, set the maximum range first. This measurement method is equally applicable in the maintenance of the PLC control system, judging equipment faults by measuring voltage, current or resistance. A thermistor is a special semiconductor device whose resistance changes with the surface temperature; the commonly used NTC thermistor has a negative temperature coefficient, i.e. the resistance decreases as the temperature rises. Thermistors were originally used to enable electronic equipment to work normally at different ambient temperatures, called temperature compensation; the CPU temperature measurement and over-temperature alarm function of a computer motherboard utilizes the characteristics of the thermistor. On ships, thermistor sensors with a negative temperature coefficient are commonly used for temperature measurement; the R×10 or R×100 range of a multimeter can be used to measure the lead resistance of the sensor inserted into hot water to check its performance.

Resistors develop resistance faults during use. At high temperatures, especially at higher power, the resistor's own heating causing it to burn out is a common fault; some faults appear as the resistor turning black with burn marks, which can be observed directly with the naked eye. To determine whether a resistor is damaged, its resistance must be measured; if it differs from the marking, or is short-circuited or open, it is damaged. Measurement on the circuit board is susceptible to interference from other loops, so it is best to remove the resistor and measure it separately. When testing with a digital multimeter, select the appropriate ohm range according to the resistance range. The resistor test procedure applies to resistors, and its content is: for resistances below 200Ω select the 200 range, for resistances from 200Ω to 2kΩ select the R×2k range, and so on; if the measurement result differs from the marking, or shows short circuit or open circuit, the resistor is judged damaged; when using an auto-ranging multimeter, simply select the resistance measurement function.

A capacitor is usually indicated in circuit diagrams by the letter C plus a number, e.g. C25 indicates capacitor number 25. Units of capacitance include farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF) and picofarad (pF). The filter circuit is part of the power supply circuit; connecting a capacitor in parallel with the load and using charging in the positive half-cycle and discharging in the negative half-cycle achieves filtering; connecting an inductor in series with the load can more effectively filter out the AC component in the pulse current. Types of filter circuits include the L-type filter circuit, the π-type filter circuit and the RC filter circuit; the L-type filter circuit consists of one inductor and one capacitor and is named for its resemblance to an inverted L; the π-type filter circuit consists of one inductor and two capacitors and is named for its resemblance to the letter π; a resistor is commonly used to replace the inductor to form an RC filter circuit, to solve the problem of the inductor's high cost and large volume.

Capacitors develop capacitor faults; the main fault manifestations include open-circuit faults caused by pin corrosion and breakage and by desoldering or cold solder joints, and electrolyte leakage of electrolytic capacitors leads to reduced capacitance, open circuit or severe leakage and breakdown faults. Most capacitor faults can be found by visual observation of appearance, and some require removal of the instrument for measurement. The capacitor test procedure requires that before testing, the two pins of the electrolytic capacitor be touched together to discharge residual charge, to prevent affecting the measurement result; use the R×1k range of an analog multimeter or the resistance range of a digital multimeter for measurement; the resistance indicated when the pointer stops is the leakage resistance, and the larger this value the better, ideally approaching infinity; if the leakage resistance is only several tens of kilohms, the electrolytic capacitor is leaking severely; the larger the initial swing angle of the pointer to the right (the smaller the value), the larger the capacitance; for a digital meter, it is normal for it to display a smaller resistance value first and then slowly increase until infinity.

When testing a diode, the red test lead connects to the internal power supply positive pole and the black test lead is the negative pole, opposite to the polarity of an analog multimeter.

The inductor test procedure is for inductors; the first step is an appearance check, confirming that the magnetic core has no defects or cracks, the metal has no corrosion or oxidation, and the wiring has no breaks or kinks; the second step is to use a multimeter to measure the DC resistance of the coil and compare it with a known normal value to judge the fault; if the measured resistance is significantly increased or the pointer does not move, the inductor body is judged open-circuited; if the measured resistance is much smaller than the normal value, the inductor body is judged severely short-circuited; a local short circuit of the coil cannot be found by conventional resistance measurement and requires a dedicated instrument for testing. The radar antenna height should ensure that the horizontal distance from the bow line of sight to the sea surface does not exceed 500m or twice the ship's length, whichever is smaller; the radar antenna position should ensure that there is no shadow sector within the range from dead ahead to 2 to 2.5° abaft the beam on both port and starboard sides. The radar antenna installation precautions require attention to the antenna; radar installation applies to the antenna.

Among the electronic components of marine electrical equipment, the diode belongs to a class of semiconductor devices with a very wide range of applications; its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity, i.e. small conduction resistance under forward voltage and extremely large or infinite resistance under reverse voltage. With this characteristic, diodes are commonly used in rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization and polarity protection circuits. To identify its positive and negative poles, the long pin is the positive pole and the short pin is the negative pole; the light-emitting diode is a current-type device with an operating voltage of 3V but easily damaged, and must be connected in series with a current-limiting resistor, with an operating current of 1 to 30mA and a conduction voltage above 1.7V; its positive and negative poles can be identified by pin length, the long pin being positive and the short pin negative.

Testing the above devices cannot be done without a multimeter. When testing polarity with a digital multimeter, the red test lead connects to the positive pole and a displayed voltage value below 1V indicates the forward conduction state; when a digital multimeter tests electrolytic capacitor leakage, the numerical indication first shows a smaller resistance value and then slowly increases until infinity. Digital multimeter capacitance test procedure: turn the changeover switch to the capacitance measurement range -> insert the capacitor under test into the capacitance jack -> read the displayed reading. Digital multimeter diode test procedure: insert the test leads -> turn the changeover switch to the diode test range -> connect the diode under test -> read the forward voltage drop; during testing the red test lead connects to the diode positive pole and the black test lead to the negative pole, and the multimeter must be set to the diode symbol range for measurement; when forward-conducting it displays a voltage value (e.g. 0.597V), and when reverse non-conducting it displays OL or 1×××; the test lead connection is exactly opposite to that of an analog multimeter. Digital multimeter transistor test procedure: transistor type determination -> collector, emitter and current amplification factor test -> performance determination. The diode test procedure requires selecting the diode symbol range; the measurement method is to connect the red test lead to the diode positive pole and the black test lead to the diode negative pole; the judgment criterion is that the measured value is the voltage value when the diode is forward-conducting, and a reverse display of OL indicates the diode is not conducting; this test lead connection is opposite to the test connection of an analog multimeter, and the polarity of a light-emitting diode can be identified by pin length to assist testing. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, component status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, check whether components are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt.

A resistor is one of the components widely used in marine electrical equipment. Resistors include variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors.

Capacitors are likewise widely used in marine electrical equipment. The circuit symbol for a diode is VD, numbered e.g. VD5; the diode test procedure applies to diodes. The larger the pointer deflection, the more unstable the performance. The criterion for judging a transistor fault is the abnormal reading when measuring with the diode range (buzzer range) of a digital multimeter; typical phenomena include the case where two pins always show a small value, the case where no small value is displayed during measurement, and the inability to measure the transistor by the normal method (e.g. pinching the base and collector to compare the β value). This fault judgment is based on the principle that the amplification factor β is large when the emitter and collector of an NPN/PNP transistor are correctly connected.

The power supply circuit supplies energy to electronic equipment and has three types: linear rectifier power supply, switching power supply and inverter power supply; the power supply in electronic circuits is generally low-voltage direct current. The power supply circuit includes the filter circuit and the voltage stabilizing circuit. The linear rectifier power supply consists of four main parts: transformation, rectification, filtering and voltage stabilization; the switching power supply uses pulse width modulation (PWM) control to convert direct current into high-frequency alternating current. When analyzing the power supply circuit, it should be decomposed stage by stage in the order of "rectification-filtering-voltage stabilization"; in the switching regulated power supply, the inductor, capacitor and freewheeling diode are the main components. The filter circuit is used to filter out the AC component in the pulsed direct current after rectification to obtain smooth direct current; its types include the L-type filter circuit, the π-type filter circuit and the RC filter circuit. The voltage stabilizing circuit is used to stabilize the output voltage and current of the rectifier power supply, to eliminate the effects of grid fluctuations and load changes; its types include the Zener diode voltage stabilizing circuit, the series voltage stabilizing circuit, the switching voltage stabilizing circuit and the integrated voltage stabilizing circuit. The simplest form is a circuit composed of a Zener diode and a load in parallel; the series voltage stabilizing circuit samples and detects voltage changes and, after amplification, controls the regulating transistor to stabilize the output; the switching voltage stabilizing circuit has the advantages of low power consumption, high efficiency and small volume but complex circuitry; the three-terminal integrated voltage regulator integrates the high-power regulating transistor and protection circuit within the chip, with few peripheral components; the LM7800 series is a three-terminal integrated voltage regulator outputting positive voltage, and the LM7900 series outputs negative voltage. A linear regulated power supply usually adds a voltage stabilizing circuit after rectification and filtering to meet high-quality power supply requirements.

Welding is an important step in the maintenance procedure of the PLC control system. The welding mechanism is that by heating the weldment the solder melts, atomic diffusion occurs between the weldment and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer is formed at their interface. The formed alloy bonding layer has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength, and welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products. If the welding essentials are not mastered, cold solder joints are easily produced; if too much solder is added, bridging (short circuit) will result, causing product performance to fail to meet design requirements. The copper foil pattern on the PCB is often covered with a thin layer of solder to reduce oxidation and promote solderability; the effective time of this solder layer usually lasts about six months. During welding, flux (most commonly rosin) must be used to remove the oxide film on the surface of the metal being welded, ensuring the solder wets it. When soldering electronic components onto the PCB, the principle of small first then large, low first then high should be followed, otherwise large or tall components, once soldered, will affect the soldering quality of small components. When the shading coil of an AC electromagnet is broken or falls off, it can be repaired by copper welding or by replacing the shading coil.

A contactor includes a core and a coil.

In the power supply link of electronic equipment, the power supply circuit undertakes the task of supplying energy to the circuits at all levels; it is generally composed of three parts: the rectifier circuit, the filter circuit and the voltage stabilizing circuit, and by type is divided into three kinds: linear rectifier power supply, switching power supply and inverter power supply.

The function of the filter circuit is to filter out the AC component in the pulsed direct current after rectification, thereby obtaining relatively smooth direct current; common types are the L-type filter circuit, the π-type filter circuit and the RC filter circuit. A filter circuit composed of one inductor and one capacitor is named the L-type filter circuit because its shape resembles an inverted L;

When identifying the positive and negative electrodes, the long pin is the positive electrode; it has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the other pins changes as the shaft rotates. In a differential amplifier circuit, the potentiometer Rp is often used as the zero-adjusting element;

The resistor category also includes photoresistors and thermistors.

Photosensitive devices include photosensitive cells, photoresistors, photodiodes and phototransistors, etc., which can convert optical signals into electrical signals; the measurable performances include resistance change, electromotive force and current. Devices such as photoresistors utilize the photoconductive characteristics of semiconductors, and their resistance changes with the intensity of incident light: when the light intensity increases, the resistance decreases significantly, and when the light intensity decreases, the resistance increases significantly. Photosensitive cells generate an electromotive force or current when exposed to light, and can be detected with the DC mV/mA range of a multimeter. Photosensitive devices are widely used in automatic detection, photoelectric control, communication and alarm circuits.

The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel; during ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation loop and fuel enters the nozzle for injection. Its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil, to prevent high voltage from being generated when the power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel circulation loop, release residual air from the air compressor, or control the fine water mist fire-extinguishing zones; it is energized in the burner ignition program, cutting off the fuel circulation loop so that fuel enters the nozzle for injection. The PLC output interface converts digital signals into voltage or current to drive the solenoid valve. The automatic fuel boiler contains a photoresistor, a solenoid valve and a potentiometer. The control platform contains sensors. The clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

In the electronic circuits of marine electrical equipment, the transistor is a semiconductor device containing two PN junctions and having current amplification capability, and is divided into NPN type and PNP type. The operating characteristics of the NPN type and the PNP type can complement each other, and the complementary pair in an OTL circuit works by utilizing this characteristic. The measurable performances of a transistor include the tube type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor. When measuring with a multimeter, the greater the pointer deflection, the more unstable the performance.

The diode used together with the transistor has unidirectional conductivity as its main characteristic, that is, under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is very large or infinite. The circuit symbol of the diode is VD, with designations such as VD5; for resistors, a dedicated resistor testing procedure is available, and during maintenance the resistor can be judged good or bad by measuring item by item according to this procedure. The capacitor testing procedure applies to capacitors, and during maintenance the leakage and capacitance can be measured according to this procedure. The pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise; the switching power supply adopts pulse width modulation (PWM) control to convert DC into high-frequency AC, and in the switching regulated power supply the inductor, capacitor and freewheeling diode are the main components. The programmable logic controller (PLC) includes a power supply section, which is responsible for converting AC or DC power into the DC working power required by the internal circuits, wherein the first type of power supply supplies the integrated circuit and is +5V and +15V DC power.

The printed circuit board consists of a base material and traces; the base material is an insulating material, often called the substrate, and the most commonly used are phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the trace part is made of conductive copper, laid on the substrate, and the required pattern is obtained by etching. In addition to the conductive traces, the printed circuit board also includes sockets, grounding points, slots and pads (connection points). Dust, oil mist and salt mist on board easily cause the insulation performance of the printed circuit board to deteriorate or even cause a short circuit; when cleaning, an electrical cleaner can be used to spray-wash oil stains and salt crystals, and the operation must be carried out with the external power supply cut off.

The conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation; interview the operator before observation, and check the monitoring and indicating device before observation. Before switching on the power supply, it must be checked whether there is a short circuit or ground fault in the input and output sections, and only after confirmation can the power be switched on. During the debugging of the regulated power supply, after switching on the power supply, if there is no abnormality, the first step should be to adjust the potentiometer to test the output voltage range. The PLC starts the self-diagnosis process as soon as the power is switched on; if an internal error occurs in the CPU, the "CPU Error" lamp on the panel shows an abnormality; after eliminating the interference of external surge voltage, the power supply needs to be switched on again to observe whether the PLC fault disappears, otherwise the CPU board is replaced.

In the maintenance practice of marine electrical equipment, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure and working principle of the electrical equipment as well as the functions and locations of the components (assemblies), which is the basic prerequisite for carrying out fault diagnosis and repair work. Maintenance personnel should master the whole set of methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, and be very familiar with the ship-wide electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components in actual work, so as to quickly narrow the scope of fault troubleshooting.

The multimeter is the most commonly used multi-purpose instrument in the maintenance of electronic equipment, and it consists of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit. The current flowing through the meter head contained in the multimeter at full scale is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes; the changeover switch contained in the multimeter is used to switch different measurement functions and ranges; the measuring circuit contained in the multimeter completes the signal conversion. Multimeters are divided into analog and digital types, and the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter each have their own advantages. Taking the MF-47 multimeter as an example, it is a typical product in the multimeter family, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A, and the panel is provided with four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The MF-30 multimeter is an instrument commonly used in the detection of FU-related circuits. The multimeter can be used to measure various parameters and devices such as resistance, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples, and is a basic tool for judging whether components are good or bad and the state of the circuit.

In circuit diagrams, the fuse serves as a protective element and its graphical symbol is FU; the fuse corresponds to FU, and FU is the symbol of the fuse. The fuse is a safety device that, when overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or the electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. It belongs to the distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is a screw-type fuse, with a voltage of 380V and a current of 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. FU blowing is one of the causes of the contactor KM coil being unenergized and unable to close. The fuse performs the overload and short circuit protection function in the ship's power system, and its symbol FU is used uniformly in circuit diagrams.

The printed circuit board consists of two parts: the base material and the traces. The base material is often called the substrate, and the most commonly used are phenolic resin board and epoxy glass; the phenolic resin board is yellow and insulating, while the epoxy glass uses glass fiber as the base material. Marine electrical equipment widely uses printed circuit boards, and printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components, as the soldering quality directly affects the reliability of the circuit board.

A printed circuit board may suffer a circuit board fault, and the circuit board fault is a typical fault on this type of carrier, the printed circuit board. The manifestations of circuit board faults include integrated ICs or other components being burnt or cracked, and the circuit board being broken or cracked, etc. The circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards. Before repair, the user must be carefully asked about the fault symptom of the circuit board, and when conditions permit, the site should be visited to confirm the correctness of the connections and the standardization of the operation so as to eliminate misjudgment. When it is necessary to confirm a circuit board fault, the correctness of the connections, the firmness of the plug-in connections and the setting changes must be checked, and whether the steps of operating the equipment are correct must be verified, so as to avoid misjudgment caused by improper operation. Improper operation is one of the causes of a single-phase ground fault in the power system; faults caused by improper operation commonly include improper closing operation, unbalanced generator load control, and improper operation caused by observation errors; during parallel operation, improper timing of closing or reversing the adjustment direction of load sharing can cause the generator reverse power protection to trip.

If it is not confirmed before repair whether the steps of operating the equipment are correct, a misjudgment of the circuit board fault may be caused by improper operation. It is necessary to understand the recent use of the faulty circuit board and distinguish whether it is an aging phenomenon or a newly occurring symptom; if there is a repair record, the repair history and the replaced components should be confirmed to assist fault analysis. When an abnormal function of a component is found, the surrounding related components and circuits need to be further checked; when the fault cannot be confirmed, the suspected component can be removed and measured separately for judgment. The complete flow of the circuit board repair procedure includes such steps as asking about the fault symptom, observing the fault traces, preliminarily analyzing the fault location, preparation before power-on testing, and functional area division, among which the preparation before power-on testing needs to confirm the power supply type, positive and negative polarity, vulnerable components of the faulty circuit board, and whether there is a short circuit, missing parts, etc.

Contactor The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship's power system, belongs to low-voltage control apparatus, and undertakes the control task of the motor in the electric drive system. The power of various auxiliary machinery on board is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on board. This type of apparatus has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, an iron core and a coil; the arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the main contacts break, the main contacts undertake the task of making and breaking the main circuit, and the iron core and the coil together form the electromagnetic mechanism; after the coil is energized, it generates electromagnetic attraction to drive the iron core to move, thereby driving the main contacts to close or open. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and its content is developed around the above-mentioned components such as the arc chute, main contacts, iron core and coil.

Circuit breaker The circuit breaker is a switching apparatus used to protect circuits in the ship's power system, belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus, is divided into the frame type (air type) and the molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers and deals with various abnormalities occurring during the operation of the circuit breaker.

A circuit breaker may suffer various faults. The circuit breaker may suffer the fault that when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close, that is, when the circuit breaker is operated manually, its contacts cannot close normally. In addition, the circuit breaker may also suffer the situation that one phase contact cannot close. The shunt trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open, and the undervoltage trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open, both belong to faults in the trip unit. The circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, and the circuit breaker automatically opening about 1h after closing, are two types of opening abnormalities occurring during operation. In addition, noise in the undervoltage trip unit, excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, auxiliary switch faults, and malfunction of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit causing the circuit breaker to open, are also faults that the circuit breaker may suffer. For these faults, each item should be checked and handled in accordance with the requirements of circuit breaker maintenance, so that the circuit breaker resumes its normal switching and protection functions.

Basic categories of marine electrical apparatus Marine electrical equipment is of many kinds, and according to the tasks they undertake in the circuit, they can be roughly classified into two major categories: distribution apparatus and control apparatus. Distribution apparatus undertakes the distribution of electrical energy and the protection of circuits, and the fuse and the circuit breaker are typical representatives; control apparatus undertakes the on-off switching of circuits and the control of operating states, and the contactor belongs to this category. In addition, there is also a category of apparatus used for measurement and detection, such as the changeover switch, and the resistor as the basic constituent unit of the circuit. The following explains their functions, model designations and common faults by category.

Distribution apparatus The symbol of the fuse in circuit diagrams is FU; it is a safety device that, when overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or the electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element, and thus has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. As distribution apparatus, the fuse has the characteristic of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. Among the commonly used models, the RL93 series is of screw-type structure, with a voltage of 380V and a current of 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection; the fuse corresponds to the symbol FU, and drawings should be read and identified accordingly.

The circuit breaker is a switching device used in the marine power system to protect circuits; it belongs to low-voltage distribution devices and can likewise maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short-circuit faults. Circuit breakers are divided into two types, the frame type (air circuit breaker) and the molded-case type, and combine switching and protection functions.
