Air circuit breakers are mostly used as generator main switches and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid; molded-case circuit breakers are used as branch, load panel or lighting panel switches and provide overload or short-circuit protection. Circuit breakers may develop many faults during operation. If the circuit breaker is operated manually and the contacts cannot close, this is a common fault; in addition, the circuit breaker may have one phase whose contacts cannot close, the shunt trip unit may fail to trip the circuit breaker, the undervoltage trip unit may fail to trip the circuit breaker, the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker automatically trips about 1h after closing, the undervoltage trip unit may be noisy, the circuit breaker temperature rise may be too high, the auxiliary switch may fail, and the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit may malfunction and cause the circuit breaker to open. In view of these situations, circuit breaker maintenance should be a fixed part of routine servicing.

The contactor, a control device, is equipment used in the marine power system to control motors; it belongs to low-voltage control devices, is used in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor consists of parts such as the arc chute, main contacts, core and coil, and the condition of these parts directly determines whether the contactor can operate reliably. Contactor maintenance requires keeping it clean; in particular, the contactors in the deck cargo winch control box should have dust and oil dirt removed to prevent the moving system from jamming.

The function of the changeover switch, a measuring and detection device, is to select the measurement object and select the range; on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set operating states and issue operating commands, and it has many selection positions and contacts. A changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not left open. A multimeter contains a changeover switch, by means of which switching of measurement functions and ranges is achieved.

A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current. When measuring resistance, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. Current can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter; the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after opening the circuit.

Resistors and their testing: resistors are widely used in marine electrical equipment. A resistor is an electronic component with a certain resistance value, geometric shape and technical performance that limits current in a circuit; it is usually divided into three major categories: fixed resistors, variable resistors and special resistors, among which fixed resistors are most used in electronic products. Variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors all fall within the scope of resistors. Common fixed resistors can be divided by manufacturing material into RT-type carbon film resistors, RJ-type metal film resistors, RX-type wirewound resistors and chip resistors, with power ratings of 0.125W (1/8W), 0.25W (1/4W), 0.5W (1/2W), 1W, 2W, 3W, 5W, 7W, 10W, etc. The resistor testing steps apply to the inspection and judgment of resistors; resistors may develop resistance faults, and resistance faults are a common problem in the use of resistors. The resistance value of a resistor can be measured with a multimeter.

Junction box: the junction box is a component used in the marine electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical elements. The general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm light and junction box, etc. The solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box but is connected directly into the local control box; this difference should be noted when wiring.

The position of the contactor in the marine power system is determined by the drive mode of the ship's auxiliary machinery. The power of almost all auxiliary machinery on board is provided by motors, and the starting, stopping and running switching of the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on ships. As a marine low-voltage control device, the contactor is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. In the automatic transfer circuit of the lighting bus power supply, contactor interlocking is also used to achieve delayed connection and automatic transfer of the standby power supply. Contactor maintenance is routine work for marine electrical equipment management personnel, and its content covers cleaning, tightening, inspection of moving mechanisms, adjustment of contact parameters and coil inspection, among other aspects.

Keeping the contactor clean is the first step of maintenance work. Excessive accumulation of dirt will cause the moving system to jam and increase mechanical wear, so dust and oil dirt on the parts must be removed promptly. The contactors in the deck cargo winch control box are in the midst of loading and unloading dust and should be cleaned more frequently. When cleaning, first blow with compressed air, then brush with a brush, then wipe the oil dirt clean with a cleaning agent or an alcohol cloth; a spray-type electrical cleaner may also be used for cleaning. General cleaning practice is consistent with the basic content of motor maintenance work, which includes cleaning of the motor itself and of the motor installation environment, removing external dirt to ensure normal operation and heat dissipation of the motor; during general cleaning, attention should be paid to precautions for cleaning motor windings so as not to damage the winding insulation.

Regularly checking all fastening screws and fasteners of the contactor is one of the core contents of periodic maintenance work for marine contactors. During inspection, special attention should be paid to the fastening state of the stationary contacts and the fastening state of the wiring terminals. Once these parts become loose, they will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance, thereby causing local overheating and even faults such as phase failure or phase-to-phase short circuit. Poor contact, as a fault state, means that the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; under the harsh conditions on board, wiring heads and terminals are prone to rust, which also easily causes poor contact in the input and output circuits of the programmable logic controller, i.e. PLC, and poor contact will cause random output actions; the corresponding remedy is to check the terminal wiring. When the surface of the commutator of a DC motor is too dirty or the brush spring pressure is too low, poor contact between brush and commutator will likewise result.

Regularly checking by hand whether the moving mechanism of the contactor moves flexibly and injecting a small amount of lubricating oil into the rotating shaft is the third routine item of marine contactor maintenance work. During operation, check the flexibility of the moving mechanism by hand; if a bearing is fitted at the rotating shaft, a small amount of lubricating oil should be injected into the bearing, in order to prevent the moving system from jamming or increased mechanical wear due to accumulated dirt. The rotating shaft is a mechanical transmission part used to transmit torque and rotary motion, commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments; the moving parts of the two units of an electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same rotating shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch consists of a contact system, operating handle, rotating shaft and panel, assembled by bolts. One of the fault causes of a contactor failing to pick up or releasing slowly is precisely moving parts jammed, or a rusted or skewed rotating shaft. When an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and overheating of the bearing end cover. Therefore, checking bearing fault and checking lubrication conditions both need to be carried out using the bearing as the object.

Regularly checking and adjusting the contact pressure, opening distance and overtravel of the contactor contacts is another routine maintenance item. The main contact is the switching part in the contactor used to make or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor. After servicing, measuring tools such as calipers and feeler gauges are needed to measure the opening distance of the main contacts, i.e. the minimum distance between the moving and stationary contacts when fully separated; the main contact overtravel refers to the displacement of the moving contact after the stationary contact is removed when fully closed, and can be obtained by conversion from the measured gap. If copper main contacts discolor or give off a burnt smell, it indicates that the contacts have already made poor contact and generated overheating; at this time the opening distance and overtravel need to be adjusted and the oxide film removed. Silver main contacts should not be rubbed with abrasive cloth; they should be cleaned of dirt with a dry cloth or cleaning agent, and applying lubricating oil is prohibited to prevent poor contact. When the three-phase main contacts are worn unevenly, the moving contact bridge arms can be bent to adjust the gap, and after adjustment synchronous contact of the three phases must be ensured. If the contacts have been overheated for a long time or have welded together, a contactor one rating higher in rated current should be selected as a replacement; serious burning of the contact surface causing poor contact or burrs is also one of the causes of contact welding.

Regularly checking whether the contactor coil is firmly mounted on the core and whether the temperature rise is too high is likewise not to be neglected. Before use, the coil insulation resistance should be tested with an insulation resistance tester; the insulation resistance between phases and to earth is required to be greater than 1MΩ. The insulation resistance tester, also called a megohmmeter, consists of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is a portable instrument used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables; according to the highest voltage generated by the hand-cranked generator it is divided into specifications of 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V, 2500V, etc. When measuring the insulation resistance of an electrical equipment coil to earth, the E terminal post of the insulation resistance tester may be connected to the core. A coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. Coil open circuit is one of the main fault causes of a contactor failing to pick up; the test method is to measure the coil resistance with a multimeter after de-energizing to determine whether it is open. If an open circuit occurs in the surface layer of the coil, the coil can be removed, the broken turns removed, and the same enameled wire used to fill in and solder firmly; if the open circuit is in the deep layer of the coil or at the inner contact, it cannot be repaired and the coil can only be rewound. Coil open circuit also manifests in other equipment; for example, in the disc-type electromagnetic brake of deck machinery, a coil open circuit causes the spring to push the armature back and generate braking torque; a broken conductor in a motor winding or appliance coil belongs to the type of open-circuit fault existing in the equipment itself. A KM coil fault in the contactor is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start.

The core is the magnetic conducting part in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as an insulation measurement reference point. During contactor servicing, it is necessary to check whether the coil is firmly mounted on the core and to test the insulation resistance between the coil and the core. If there is oil dirt or rust on the core surface it must be removed to keep the contact surface clean; if the shading coil is broken it must be repaired or the core replaced. Oil sludge adhering to the pole face of the core will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed; oil dirt, dust or poor contact on the pole face of the core will cause loud electromagnet noise; the causes of loud AC electromagnet noise also include foreign matter on the pole face of the core, poor contact, or a broken or fallen-off shading coil. The shading coil is a copper ring-shaped part installed on the pole face of the core of an AC electromagnet, used to eliminate armature vibration noise; if it breaks or falls off, the AC electromagnet will produce relatively loud noise; when damaged it can be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil can be replaced directly; one of the causes of noise in the undervoltage trip unit is also a broken shading coil; during the second-level maintenance of the contactor it is necessary to check the non-magnetic shim, the shading coil and the copper sleeve for damage. When estimating the number of turns of an AC coil, the formula N = 45 * U / (B * A) can be used, where B is usually taken as 0.9～1.2T and A represents the cross-sectional area of the original coil core in cm²; when calculating the number of turns of a DC coil, the wire diameter d must include the thickness of the insulation layer.

The insulation layer is used to electrically insulate the conductive core wires and prevent short circuit or earthing between core wires; in the structure of a marine cable it is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer, and a marine cable contains such an insulation layer.

The arc chute is a part of contactors and circuit breakers, used to extinguish the arc generated when the contacts break. When the arc chute is cracked, damaged or seriously carbonized it should be replaced promptly; when the splitter plates are seriously burnt, deformed or loose, a new chute should be replaced; fallen objects in the chute and metal particles produced by contact arcing should also be removed. The integrity of the arc splitter plates should be checked and soot and fine metal dust on the surface removed; the outer cover should be intact, and if damaged it should be replaced. When servicing the fault of jamming of the moving part of the contactor, the arc chute must first be removed.

In the measurement stage, a multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, while a clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. When measuring resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after opening the circuit. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action.

Relay maintenance, circuit breaker maintenance and PLC maintenance all belong to the maintenance items of marine electrical equipment. Relay maintenance applies to transistor relays, circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers, and PLC maintenance applies to the programmable logic controller, that is, the programmable logic controller (PLC). As regards the scope of evidence involved, the evidence involves only contactor maintenance and does not include the specific content of circuit breaker maintenance, and PLC maintenance is also not mentioned in the evidence.

Contactors are used in large quantities on ships because the power of almost all types of auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the operation of the motors is in turn controlled by contactors. As electrical equipment used in the marine power system to control motors, the contactor internally contains the arc chute, main contacts, core, coil and other parts, among which the main contacts undertake the task of making or breaking the main circuit current, and their closed state directly determines whether the motor can run. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors; in daily maintenance the contactor should be kept clean, especially the contactors in the deck cargo winch control box, where dust and oil dirt must be removed promptly to prevent the moving system from jamming. At the same time, fastening screws and wiring terminals must be checked regularly; once they become loose, faults such as poor contact, local overheating, phase failure or phase-to-phase short circuit will result.

If the main contacts show copper discoloration or give off a burnt smell, it indicates that poor contact has already caused overheating; at this time the opening distance and overtravel need to be adjusted and the oxide film on the contact surface removed. When the main contacts have been overheated for a long time or have already welded together, a contactor one rating higher in rated current should be used as a replacement. After servicing is completed, measuring tools such as calipers and feeler gauges must be used to measure the opening distance of the main contacts, that is, the minimum distance when the moving and stationary contacts are fully separated; the overtravel of the main contacts refers to the displacement produced by the moving contact after the stationary contact is removed in the fully closed state, and this value can be obtained by conversion from the measured gap.

The contact spring is related to contact pressure. The initial contact pressure is the pressure acting on the contacts when the moving and stationary contacts just touch, and the final contact pressure is the pressure acting on the contacts when the contacts are fully closed. During measurement, the height of the spring installation space in the two states of contacts separated and contacts closed can first be measured, and then the spring pressure measured, thereby obtaining the initial pressure and final pressure. If there is no original data, the final contact pressure can be calculated by the formula F_z = 9.8 × 2.25 I_N / 100. If the contact spring pressure is too high or the overtravel is too large, the noise of the AC electromagnet will increase; and if the contact spring pressure is too low, this is one of the causes of contact welding.

Servicing of the core is likewise not to be neglected. Once the shading coil is broken, the core should be repaired or replaced. The causes of loud AC electromagnet noise include foreign matter on the pole face of the core, poor contact, and a broken or fallen-off shading coil; at this time the armature position must be checked and corrected, mechanical jamming eliminated, and the core made to attract flat and firmly. Failure or damage of the armature reaction spring is also one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed. In contactor servicing, measuring insulation resistance is a task that must be completed; it is necessary to measure the insulation resistance between contacts, between the coil and the core, and between live parts and earth; during measurement the voltage level of the insulation resistance tester should be selected according to the rated voltage of the contactor, and the commonly used measuring tool is the insulation resistance tester, for example an ohmmeter.

As a switching device protecting circuits in the ship's power system, the circuit breaker is divided into the frame type and the molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus; it can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short-circuit faults, and the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch, capable of automatically disconnecting the generator to protect the power network. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker; among its common faults, when the circuit breaker is operated manually the contacts may fail to close, when the circuit breaker is operated electrically the contacts may likewise fail to close, and in addition there is the case where one phase contact fails to close, the shunt trip unit fails to trip the circuit breaker, the undervoltage trip unit fails to trip the circuit breaker, the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker trips automatically about 1 h after closing, the undervoltage trip unit is noisy, the circuit breaker temperature rise is too high, the auxiliary switch fails, and the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctions and opens the circuit breaker.

The contactor undertakes the task of controlling motors in the ship's power system and is used in large quantities on board, because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor itself includes the arc chute, main contacts, iron core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; the maintenance work must be carried out around these components. During maintenance, the flexibility of the operating mechanism must be checked manually at regular intervals, and a small amount of lubricating oil must be injected into the rotating shaft (if a bearing is present).

The contactor fails to pick up is one of the common faults and may be caused by a broken power supply line, a coil open circuit or jamming of the moving parts. When judging, first measure the voltage across the coil: if there is no voltage across the coil, the power supply line is broken and the circuit must be checked to eliminate the break; if there is voltage, the coil has an open circuit. After de-energizing, use a multimeter to measure the coil resistance and determine whether it is open so as to decide on replacing the coil. In addition, low supply voltage (below 85% rated voltage) or large fluctuation, insufficient capacity of the operating power supply, and internal short circuit of the coil can also cause the contactor fails to pick up or insufficient holding force. If the contactor coil voltage measured with a multimeter is below 85% rated voltage, it can be judged as low supply voltage.

Failure or damage of the armature reaction spring will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly when the stop button is pressed; in this case the reaction spring must be replaced or adjusted, taking care that the reaction force is not too large. Contact welding will also cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly when the stop button is pressed; if contact welding occurs frequently, a contactor one current rating larger should be substituted. Such faults usually appear together with failure of the armature reaction spring, contact welding and the like.

There are many causes of coil overheating or burning. Too high a supply voltage (>1.1U~) or too low a supply voltage (<0.85U) will cause coil overheating or burning, and the remedy is to adjust the supply voltage to the normal range. Coil technical parameters (such as rated voltage, frequency, duty factor, etc.) not matching the actual operating conditions will cause coil overheating or burning, and the remedy is to select a coil or contactor matching the actual working conditions. Local internal short circuit of the coil will cause coil overheating or burning; this can be judged by the resistance comparison method, and after judgment the coil is replaced. Too high an operating frequency will cause contactor coil overheating or burning, and a contactor one current rating larger must be substituted. Special service environments, such as humid air, corrosive gases or too high an ambient temperature, can cause coil overheating or burning, and a contactor suited to the special conditions should be adopted. Jamming of the moving parts causing prolonged energization will also lead to contactor coil overheating or burning; its treatment refers to the measures for jamming of the moving parts given under contactor fails to pick up.

As for contact welding, too small a contact capacity is one of the main causes; a load short circuit will cause contact welding, and the contacts must be replaced after the fault is eliminated; insufficient holding force (such as voltage below 85%U_N) may lead to contact welding; too small a contact spring pressure is one of the factors causing contact welding; too frequent operation or overloaded use will likewise lead to contact welding. The remedy is to open the contacts and dress the burrs with a fine file or replace the contacts; if welding occurs frequently, a contactor one current rating larger should be substituted. In the JZF-H motor, welding of the ZDC auxiliary contact will cause the medium-speed winding to remain locked; welding of the brake contactor auxiliary contact or its jamming in the closed position will cause the winding to remain locked. Jamming of the moving parts and prolonged energization are often caused by mechanical factors such as rusted or skewed rotating shafts or oil sludge sticking to the pole faces of the iron core, and the treatment likewise refers to the measures for jamming of the moving parts given under contactor fails to pick up.

During testing, the multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument; it consists of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, and the current flowing through the meter head at full scale is about a few microamperes to several hundred microamperes. The analog multimeter is one type of multimeter, and the digital multimeter is also one type of multimeter. The MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter; it can measure a maximum voltage of 2500 V and a maximum direct current of 5 A, and its panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The multimeter can be used to measure the resistance value of a resistor, the voltage value of a voltage and the current value of a current, and can also be used to test capacitors, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples. When measuring direct current, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range and the meter head is connected in series in the opened branch; when measuring direct voltage, the test probes are connected in parallel across the component under test, and when the range is uncertain the highest range is selected first. The generator fails to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in an AC electric drive system; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in an AC electric drive system.

Structurally, the contactor includes the arc chute, main contacts, iron core and coil, and all of these must be attended to one by one during maintenance. The work of contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; routine maintenance must first keep it clean, especially the contactors in the deck crane control box, where dust and oil sludge must be removed promptly, otherwise the moving system is easily jammed. Fastening screws and wiring terminals must be checked regularly; once loose they will cause poor contact of contacts, the contact resistance will increase accordingly, and this will in turn cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure or phase-to-phase short circuit. Discoloration of copper contacts or scorching of insulating parts often indicates that the contacts have already made poor contact and generated overheating. During inspection, also check whether the coil is firmly mounted on the iron core and measure the insulation resistance between the coil and the iron core;

Large noise of the electromagnet (AC) is one of the common fault symptoms of the contactor, and its causes involve several aspects. Low supply voltage will cause large noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the supply voltage must then be adjusted to 0.85 to 1.10 times the rated voltage; too large a contact spring pressure or too large an overtravel will likewise cause large noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the corresponding remedy is to adjust the contact spring and the overtravel; a skewed armature or mechanical jamming, which prevents the iron core from seating flat and firm, will also cause large noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the armature position should be corrected and the mechanical jamming eliminated; foreign matter on the pole faces of the iron core (such as oil sludge or dust) or poor contact will cause large noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the pole faces must be cleaned and the iron core adjusted for good contact; a broken or fallen-off shading coil will cause large noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the repair method is to weld it with copper or replace the shading coil. The shading coil is a copper ring-shaped component mounted on the pole faces of the AC electromagnet iron core to eliminate armature vibration noise; once it breaks, besides causing noise of the AC electromagnet, it will also cause the undervoltage trip unit to be noisy, in which case the armature or iron core should be replaced accordingly.

Contact welding is another type of fault requiring key treatment; contact welding will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly when the stop button is pressed. There are many causes of contact welding: too small a contact capacity will cause contact welding, and a suitable contactor should be selected as the replacement; a load short circuit will cause contact welding, and the load short-circuit fault must first be eliminated before replacing the contacts; insufficient holding force will cause contact welding, and it is necessary to check whether the supply voltage is below 85% rated voltage and to eliminate the mechanical resistance; too small a contact spring pressure will cause contact welding, and the contact spring must be replaced or repaired and the contact pressure adjusted to standard; if welding occurs frequently, a contactor one current rating larger should be substituted. Opening the contacts and dressing the burrs with a fine file or replacing the contacts is a common means of dealing with welding.

Insufficient holding force is itself a type of contactor fault cause; when the contactor fails to pick up or has insufficient holding force, a buzzing sound is often present. Insufficient capacity of the operating power supply will cause insufficient holding force of the contactor, an internal short circuit of the coil will make the contactor exhibit insufficient holding force, and jamming of the moving parts, too large a spring reaction force or a rusted rotating shaft can also cause insufficient holding force of the contactor. In the electromagnetic brake, a too dirty attracting surface of the iron core will cause insufficient holding force, resulting in failure to release the brake or a half-released state.

Checking the power supply is a maintenance procedure that runs through the above fault treatments. When the AC electromagnet is noisy, the supply voltage must be adjusted to 0.85 to 1.10 times the rated value; when contact welding is caused by insufficient holding force, it should be checked whether the supply voltage is below 85%U_N. Motor fails to start, motor speed low after starting, motor temperature rise high and excessive sparking under brush all correspond to the procedure of checking the power supply. Voltage can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter. When carrying out the procedure of checking the power supply, note that the circuit terminals must be marked clearly one by one before disassembly, so as to avoid confusion when reconnecting. A power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply.

The contactor undertakes the task of controlling motors in the ship's power system; the power of the various auxiliary machinery on board comes almost entirely from motors, and the starting, stopping and running of the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities. Structurally, the contactor includes the arc chute, main contacts, iron core and coil, and the work of contactor maintenance applies precisely to the contactor itself; routine maintenance must be carried out around these parts. The primary content of maintenance work is to keep it clean, especially the contactors in the deck crane control box, where dust and oil sludge should be removed promptly to prevent the moving system from being jammed. For an AC coil, its number of turns can be estimated by N = 45 * U / (B * A), where B is usually taken as
0.9 to
1.2T.

In fault diagnosis, current is an electrical quantity that must be mastered; the performance that can be measured is the current value, and a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter can be used for the measurement. Measuring current generally requires opening the circuit and connecting the ammeter in series.

One of the common fault symptoms of the contactor is contact overheating or burning. There are several causes of this symptom. Insufficient contact spring pressure or too small an overtravel will cause contact overheating or burning, and the corresponding remedy is to adjust the spring pressure and overtravel to the specified values; this operation belongs to the maintenance procedure of adjusting the spring. Poor contact of contacts will likewise cause contact overheating or burning, and the treatment is to clean the contact surfaces, dress the surfaces and fasten the contacts and the conductive plate firmly. Severe contact wear and desoldering is also one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning; the criterion is that the contact wear reaches one third of the original thickness or desoldering appears, in which case new contacts should be replaced to eliminate the fault. Too frequent operation or too large a current, and insufficient contact capacity, will also cause contact overheating or burning; for this cause a contactor of larger capacity should be selected. In addition, too high an ambient temperature or use inside a closed control box is also one of the fault causes of contact overheating or burning; in such cases the contactor should be derated in use.

Another fault symptom is excessive contact wear, numbered 8 among the fault symptoms. Too frequent operation and too large a working current are one of the main causes of excessive contact wear; for frequent operation and excessive current, the contactor should be derated or a contactor suited to frequent operation and matching the working current should be selected; if contact overheating is caused by this reason, a contactor of larger capacity must be selected. Non-synchronism of the three-phase contacts is also one of the causes of excessive contact wear; if caused by three-phase non-synchronism, the contacts must be adjusted to be synchronous. A load-side short circuit will likewise cause excessive contact wear; after a load-side short circuit occurs, the short-circuit fault must first be eliminated before replacing the contacts.

The contact spring is an important part of the contactor. During measurement, the initial pressure and final pressure can be obtained by measuring the height of the spring installation space when the contacts are open and closed, and then measuring the spring pressure. When the reaction spring becomes smaller, the corresponding remedy is to adjust the spring.

The effects of poor contact are not limited to the contacts themselves; it will also cause random output actions, and the corresponding check measure is to check the terminal wiring.

When maintaining the contactor, cleaning is the first step, especially for the contactors in the deck crane control box, where dust and oil sludge must be removed promptly, otherwise the moving system is easily jammed. Before use, the insulation resistance of the coil should also be tested with an insulation resistance tester; the insulation resistance between phases and to ground must both be greater than 1 MΩ. If the contacts have been overheated for a long time or have already welded together, a contactor with a rated current one rating larger should be selected as the replacement. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and the above operations of cleaning, fastening, insulation testing and replacement are all carried out around the contactor.

The contactor fails to pick up is a common fault symptom, manifested as the armature being unable to pull in after the coil is energized, or pulling in but with insufficient holding force. There are many causes of this symptom; a broken power supply line, a coil open circuit or jamming of the moving parts may all make the contactor fails to pick up. If there is voltage, the coil has an open circuit. After de-energizing, measure the coil resistance with a multimeter to judge whether the coil is open, thereby deciding whether the coil needs to be replaced.

When the contactor fails to pick up or has insufficient holding force with a buzzing sound after the start button is pressed, the causes can be classified into several categories. Low supply voltage or large fluctuation will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force with a buzzing sound after the start button is pressed; an internal short circuit of the coil will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force with a buzzing sound after the start button is pressed; jamming of the moving parts, too large a spring reaction force, or a rusted or skewed rotating shaft will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force with a buzzing sound after the start button is pressed; too large a contact gap (i.e. too large an armature air gap) will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force with a buzzing sound after the start button is pressed. Among these, when the supply voltage is too low, the voltage across the coil may be below the 85% rated voltage specified by the product;

For the above faults, the treatments correspond respectively. When the supply voltage is too low or fluctuates greatly, a multimeter should be used to measure the voltage across the coil; if it is below 85% rated voltage, it is judged as low supply voltage. When the operating power supply capacity is insufficient, the remedy is to replace the operating power supply. When there is an internal short circuit of the coil or a coil open circuit, the corresponding remedy is to replace the coil; when the moving parts are jammed, the spring reaction force is too large, or the rotating shaft is rusted or skewed, the arc chute must be removed and the armature pressed to check whether it can drive the contacts flexibly; if the action is not flexible, the relevant parts should be removed for derusting, oiling or fastening and correction, and parts already deformed or damaged should be replaced directly. When the rated voltage of the coil is higher than the line rated voltage, a coil matching the coil rated voltage should be replaced. When the contact gap is too large (i.e. the armature air gap is too large), the remedy is to adjust the armature air gap. A jammed armature will likewise prevent the contactor KM from closing, causing the motor to fail to start due to no power; when checking an open-circuit fault with or without power, the armature can be pushed manually to close the contacts so as to narrow the scope of the check.

The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, divided into the analog type and the digital type, and the current flowing through the meter head at full scale is about a few microamperes to several hundred microamperes. The analog multimeter and the digital multimeter likewise belong to the category of multimeters. Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting, failure to start, low speed under load operation, and even motor overheating or smoking. A load short circuit or overload corresponds to measurement with a multimeter, while a coil short circuit corresponds to replace the coil.

In ship power systems, there are many types of electrical equipment used for control or protection, and relays are one widely used category. According to the different sensing elements, relays can be divided into electromagnetic relays, induction relays and thermal relays, etc.; according to the nature of the input signal, there are voltage relays, current relays, power relays, temperature relays, pressure relays and water level relays, etc. These relays each perform their own functions in the control and protection circuits of marine electrical systems, and their maintenance quality directly affects the reliability of equipment operation.

The structure of an electromagnetic relay is basically similar to that of a contactor; its sensing part is composed of a coil, and the coil is passed with an electrical signal, reflecting the input quantity of the relay. Voltage relays, current relays, time relays and intermediate relays all belong to specific types of electromagnetic relays. When maintaining an electromagnetic relay, it is necessary to check the contact tightness between the armature and the core and remove dust and dirt to ensure the accuracy of the operating value; parameters such as contact pressure, overtravel and gap should comply with the specifications, and no lubricating oil may be applied to the contacts. The contactor itself includes parts such as the arc chute, main contacts, core and coil; the maintenance methods for the contactor are equally applicable to the contactor itself, while the construction of the intermediate relay is the same as that of the contactor, and its function is to expand contact capacity and the number of contact pairs; fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the maintenance methods for the contactor. Time relays often appear in circuits with symbols such as KT, SJ and SL, and belong to a type of electromagnetic relay classified by function.

A voltage relay belongs to electromagnetic relays, and its coil uses voltage as the excitation input quantity. When the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced; winding it oneself will affect the operating value due to inaccurate number of turns. During periodic maintenance, it is necessary to check and adjust the coil's operating voltage and release voltage values so that they meet the technical requirements. In constant-power three-speed cargo winches, voltage relays are used for undervoltage protection; after being energized, the normally open contacts close to energize the control circuit. Current relays likewise belong to electromagnetic relays; the coil is passed with an electrical quantity, and the structure is basically similar to that of a contactor. In AC three-speed electric windlasses, the current relay picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%; in the windlass system, misoperation of the overcurrent relay GLJ will cause the fault of no high speed at startup.

A thermal relay belongs to thermal relays according to the classification of sensing elements, and its sensing part is a bimetallic strip. This type of relay is used in large quantities on ships and is generally used to accomplish the overload protection task of small motors. The setting value of the thermal relay should be set between 1.15 and 1.3 times the rated current of the motor; the rated current selection should be the same as the rated current of the motor, and the dial value must match. In daily maintenance, it is necessary to check whether the rated current value or dial value matches the rated current of the motor. The heat generated by poor contact of the terminal posts will cause an error in the operating value, so the terminal posts must be kept in good contact. If the bimetallic strip undergoes permanent deformation due to a huge short-circuit current, it must be replaced rather than corrected. In control circuits such as those of air compressors, the thermal relay disconnects the control circuit through its normally closed contacts to achieve overload shutdown; in the water supply circuit, the thermal relay FR and the fuse FU constitute overload and short circuit protection respectively.

A pressure relay belongs to non-electrical quantity relays, and its sensing part is usually an air bag, while its actuating part is the contacts. In auxiliary boilers, the pressure relay is used as a control device for automatic control of steam pressure; in the main engine system, the pressure relay is used as a protection device for monitoring the main engine lubricating oil pressure.

Daily maintenance requires that the sampling conduit comply with the specifications and be sealed to prevent leakage from affecting operation. When used as a protection device, the operating value must not be easily adjusted; after adjustment, an operating value test must be carried out; when used as a control device, the return coefficient must be reasonably adjusted to avoid too frequent start-stop of equipment or excessive output fluctuation. In the automatic control system of an air compressor, the pressure relay controls the starting and stopping of the motor through high and low pressure contacts; in the automatic control system of a fuel oil pump, the pressure relay detects the system pressure to trigger automatic switching of the pump and alarm.

A temperature relay belongs to non-electrical quantity relays and is used in large quantities on ships, having both control and protection functions. When used for cooling water temperature alarm, the temperature relay acts as a protection device; when used in scenarios such as auxiliary boilers, the temperature relay can act as a control device. Daily maintenance requires that the temperature sensing element be in good contact with the heat source of the controlled object, otherwise it will cause an operating error. The probe used for monitoring the cooling water temperature of main and auxiliary diesel engines should be in good contact with the wall of the measuring hole. In the refrigerated hold system, the temperature relay acts as a regulating switch; deviation of its setting value will cause serious deviation of the hold temperature; contact faults, that is, failure to close or open, will cause abnormality of the liquid supply solenoid valve, resulting in refrigeration failure or excessive cooling. The water level relay belongs to one of the relay types classified by the nature of the input signal, alongside voltage relays, current relays, power relays, temperature relays and pressure relays. The water level relay has a structure of two major parts, the sensing part and the actuating part; when the input quantity reaches the setting value, it causes the controlled quantity to undergo a step change, and in protection circuits it measures the controlled quantity and operates when the setting value is reached.

Failure of the thermal relay to operate is a common fault symptom of thermal relays. A setting value that is too large is one of the main causes of the thermal relay failing to operate, and it needs to be reset according to the rated current of the motor. Burning out of the heating element will cause the thermal relay to lose its temperature sensing function and fail to operate, and the thermal relay must be replaced. Jamming of the operating mechanism will cause the thermal relay to refuse to operate; during maintenance, the cover plate needs to be opened to eliminate the fault and a manual test of flexibility must be carried out. Accumulation of dust, rust, or wear and deformation of the transmission mechanism can all cause the thermal relay to fail to operate, and the dirt must be removed or the parts replaced. Damage to adjustable parts or failure to align with the scale will cause the thermal relay setting to fail and the relay to not operate, and usually the thermal relay needs to be replaced. Incorrectly raising the thermal relay setting value, for example to 2, will cause it not to operate, thereby causing fuse blowing or the motor to smoke. When the motor is overloaded and the thermal relay does not operate, the fuse will blow to cut off the circuit.

The fuse uses FU as its symbol and has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. When overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or electrical equipment, the fuse automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. The fuse belongs to distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is a screw-type fuse, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. The electric main engine remote control system includes fuses and terminal posts; poor contact or corrosion of terminal posts is one of the common faults of electrical components. If the terminal posts of the thermal relay are in poor contact, the heat generated by contact resistance will cause an error in the operating value. The terminal screws of electromagnetic relays should be tightened to ensure good contact; failure to tighten the external wiring screws of the thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be disconnected. In the case of a loose "COM" screw, tightening should be carried out accordingly. In electrical maintenance, tightening is an operating step used to ensure good contact of terminal posts, screws and fastening mechanisms or to prevent loosening; if the fastening mechanism of the main switch is loose, tightening should be carried out, and when the screws connecting the two conductive parts of the circuit breaker are loose causing excessive temperature rise, the screws also need to be tightened.

During maintenance, voltage, current and resistance are electrical quantities that often need to be measured. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; the measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter. The multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. To measure current, an ammeter must be used, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. A coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a fault in the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature being unable to close and the motor failing to start. The core is the magnetic conductive part in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as a reference point for insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of an electrical equipment coil to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in a through-type current transformer, the large current conductor under test is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic part in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil's magnetic force to pull in or release, and used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will cause contactor KM to be unable to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failing to start; failure or loss of the armature return spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed.

This type of electrical device is used in large quantities on ships, and the overload protection task of small motors is generally accomplished by it. If the terminal posts are in poor contact, the heat generated will cause an error in the operating value, so the terminals must be kept in good contact. When the bimetallic strip undergoes permanent deformation due to a huge short-circuit current, only a thermal relay of the same model can be replaced, and correction cannot be carried out.

Failure of the thermal relay to operate is one of the common fault symptoms. A setting value that is too large is one of the main causes of this symptom, and during handling it needs to be reset according to the rated current of the motor. Jamming of the operating mechanism can likewise cause refusal to operate; during maintenance, the cover plate needs to be opened to eliminate the fault, and after repair a manual test must be carried out to confirm flexible operation. Accumulation of dust or rust, and wear and deformation of the transmission mechanism can all cause the thermal relay to fail to operate; for accumulation of dust or rust and wear and deformation of the transmission mechanism, the maintenance method is to remove dust and rust or replace the thermal relay. Damage to adjustable parts or failure to align with the scale will cause the setting to fail and the relay not to operate, and usually the thermal relay also needs to be replaced. If the setting value is incorrectly raised, for example to 2, the thermal relay will not operate, thereby causing fuse blowing or the motor to smoke.

When the main circuit is disconnected after the thermal relay is connected, one fault cause is burning out of the heating element, and the second cause is that the external wiring screws are not tightened. If caused by burning out of the heating element, the maintenance method is to replace the thermal relay; if caused by the external wiring screws not being tightened, the maintenance method is to tighten the external wiring screws. If the fastening mechanism of the main switch is loose, tightening should be carried out;

There are three aspects to the fault causes of the thermal relay control circuit being disconnected. The first is that the thermal relay has not been reset, and the corresponding maintenance method is to carry out the reset operation. In the ship's main propulsion device, failure of the thermal relay to reset is one of the causes of the control circuit being disconnected; the second is burning out of the contacts or loss of elasticity of the movable contact spring, causing poor contact or inability to contact between the movable and fixed contacts, and the maintenance method is to replace the movable contact spring and the burnt contacts. The third is that the dial or adjusting screw has been turned to an unsuitable position and pushes the contacts open, and the corresponding maintenance method is to adjust the dial or adjusting screw. Poor contact of contacts will cause the contacts to overheat or burn; methods for handling poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface and tightening the contacts and conductive plates.

When the thermal relay cannot reset, too short an interval between resetting and tripping is a common cause; when caused by too short an interval, manual reset should be carried out at about 5mm; breakage of the reset leaf spring will cause the mechanical structure to be unable to reset, and when caused by breakage of the reset leaf spring, the entire thermal relay needs to be replaced. Inability of the mechanism to reset is one of the fault causes of the thermal relay being unable to reset; its causes include too short an interval between resetting and tripping and breakage of the reset leaf spring; the maintenance method for a short interval is manual reset at about 5mm, and the maintenance method for breakage of the reset leaf spring is to replace the thermal relay. Inability of the mechanism to reset will cause the contacts to be unable to close during manual operation of the circuit breaker; at this time the reset contact surface should be adjusted to the specified value so that the mechanism can reset normally.

Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact, increase contact resistance, and can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit. Poor contact will cause random output action, and the corresponding measure is to check the terminal wiring. When the COM screw is loose, the corresponding handling method is to tighten it.

Commonly used types of non-electrical quantity relays on ships include temperature relays and pressure relays, which are used in large quantities.

Transistor relays have the advantages of high precision, small size, wide delay range, resistance to impact and vibration, convenient adjustment and long life, and are composed of five major circuits: voltage conversion, rectification, amplitude monitoring, delay and execution. The voltage conversion circuit converts the input physical quantity X into a linear voltage signal, satisfying the relationship U=KX; the rectification circuit converts the weak AC voltage into DC to improve conversion accuracy and maintain the proportional relationship; the amplitude monitoring circuit determines whether the input signal reaches the setting value, and often uses a voltage regulator tube or a Schmitt circuit. Relay maintenance is applicable to transistor relays; transistor relays with non-electrical quantity input are difficult to repair on board and need to be sent to the factory for handling; those with electrical quantity input are repaired according to electronic equipment methods. The transistor relay for motor overload protection converts power into voltage, satisfying the relationship U=KP. A fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not be used as overload protection for the motor; excessive refrigerant charge in the refrigeration system causing excessively high pressure and excessive load will cause motor overload; the thermal relay FR operates when the motor is overloaded, disconnecting the control circuit and de-energizing contactor KM to stop the machine.

A transistor contains two PN junctions internally and has current amplification capability; it is divided into NPN type and PNP type, and the two types' operating characteristics can complement each other, such as the complementary pair in an OTL circuit. In circuits it is often represented by the letter VT plus a number, for example VT17 represents the transistor numbered 17. Main models include PNP type transistors such as A92 and 9015, and NPN type transistors such as A42, 9014 and 9018. When marine electrical equipment uses transistors, the transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to the category of the transistor device. The multimeter can be used to measure voltage, current and transistors, and the clamp-on ammeter can be used to measure current. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system.

When a thermal relay misoperates, the cause can be sought from multiple aspects. Deformation of the bimetallic strip is one of the fault causes of thermal relay misoperation; for faults caused by deformation of the bimetallic strip, the maintenance method is to replace the thermal relay. Too long a motor starting time is likewise one of the fault causes of thermal relay misoperation; the maintenance method for this fault cause is to reduce the motor starting time. Looseness of adjustable parts of the thermal relay is also one of the fault causes of the thermal relay misoperation symptom, and the corresponding maintenance method is to tighten the loose parts. Too large a change in ambient temperature is one of the fault causes of thermal relay misoperation; for faults caused by too large a change in ambient temperature, the maintenance method is to improve the operating environment. In thermal relays, too frequent operation is a common cause of misoperation; to handle thermal relay misoperation caused by frequent operation, the operating frequency needs to be limited and reduced. A setting value that is too small is one of the common fault causes of the thermal relay misoperation symptom, and the corresponding maintenance method is to rotate the current adjustment knob to adjust the setting current, with the adjustment goal being to set the setting current to the rated current value of the motor.

Maintenance of transistor relays falls within the scope of relay maintenance.

Transistors and printed circuit boards are used in marine electrical equipment. For a transistor, the tube type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor can be measured; a transistor develops a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to the transistor. A printed circuit board consists of an insulating base plate and conductive copper traces; the base material is commonly called the base plate, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the trace portion is made of conductive copper, laid on the base plate, and the required pattern is obtained by etching; a printed circuit board develops a circuit board fault, and a circuit board fault belongs to the printed circuit board; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards, and printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components.

A multimeter is used in maintenance to measure many objects. A multimeter is used for transistor measurement; a multimeter is used for thyristor measurement; a thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, and its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode can be measured. A time relay may be denoted in circuits by KT, SJ or SL.

In a ship power system, the circuit breaker undertakes the tasks of making and breaking circuits and implementing protection under abnormal conditions. According to structural form and application, circuit breakers can be divided into two types, air circuit breaker and molded-case, the former with model code DW, being a frame-type automatic air circuit breaker, and the latter with model code DZ. An air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and is the connecting component by which the generator is put onto the grid; when a short circuit occurs on the grid or the generator suffers undervoltage, it can automatically disconnect the generator from the grid, thereby protecting the grid; it simultaneously has the functions of a switching device and a protective device, and can also implement protection under abnormal operating conditions such as overload. Once an air circuit breaker fails, the corresponding generator set will also fail. A molded-case circuit breaker is generally used as the switch of a branch, load panel, lighting panel or box; different models respectively have overload protection, short circuit protection or both, and some models also have leakage protection; if a molded-case circuit breaker fails, the corresponding branch will lose power. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker itself, and both types of circuit breakers usually require a comprehensive maintenance and inspection every six months.

When maintaining a circuit breaker, the arc chute is one of the components to be inspected with emphasis. Both contactors and circuit breakers contain an arc chute, whose function is to extinguish the arc generated when the contacts break. During inspection, check whether the arc extinguishing grid plates are intact and remove soot and fine metal dust from the surface; the outer cover should be intact and undamaged, and should be replaced if damaged. When the arc chute is cracked, chipped or severely carbonized, it should be replaced in time; when the grid plates are severely burned and deformed or loose, a new chute should also be replaced. The main switch is a component of the main switchboard and is used in the ship power station to make and break the generator and the main busbar, having both switching and protection functions; it mainly consists of the undervoltage release, the shunt release, the overcurrent protection device and the arc extinguishing device, and additionally includes auxiliary contacts and the control and signal indication circuit. The main switch requires performance verification of undervoltage, overload, short circuit, reverse power and the like every 4 to 5 years. If a local short circuit occurs inside the undervoltage coil, the attraction force will decrease, and a period of time is required before the trip unit operates, thereby causing automatic tripping after operating for a period of time; when a mechanical assembly quality problem prevents the three-phase contacts from closing simultaneously, a grid phase failure fault may be caused. The DW14 circuit breaker adopts Japanese Terasaki technology and is provided with an additional AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, which is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker.

The trip unit is the electrical assembly in a circuit breaker used to implement protection functions such as overload, short circuit and undervoltage and to drive the contacts to break. When inspecting the trip unit, the working pole faces of the electromagnet should be clean, flat and smooth, free of rust and burrs. Malfunction of a semiconductor overcurrent trip unit is often caused by external electromagnetic interference generated by the operation of a large electromagnet nearby. The circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the cause may be that the instantaneous setting current of the overcurrent trip unit is too small. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will prevent the contactor KM from closing, causing the motor to have no power and fail to start, while failure or absence of the armature reaction spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed.

Various fault symptoms occur during operation of a circuit breaker. When the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close, which is a common fault of the circuit breaker; when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contacts likewise cannot close, which is also a fault symptom that can occur in a circuit breaker. In addition, there may occur the failure of one phase contact to close, the shunt trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker break, the undervoltage trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker break, the circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker automatically breaking about 1 h after closing, noise in the undervoltage trip unit, excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, auxiliary switch faults, and malfunction of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit causing the circuit breaker to open. For excessive temperature rise, if it is found to be caused by loose connecting screws of two conductive parts, the screws need to be tightened; if the main switch fastening mechanism is loose, tightening should also be carried out. In addition, if the "COM" screw is loose, this likewise corresponds to the operation of tightening. During diagnosis, voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked, and the voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter;

Circuit breaker maintenance occupies a considerable proportion in the maintenance of marine electrical equipment, and its fault manifestations are diverse, with treatment methods varying according to fault type. As far as the circuit breaker itself is concerned, an air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator in the event of a fault to protect the grid; a molded-case circuit breaker is used as a branch, load panel or lighting panel switch and has overload or short circuit protection functions. Common faults of circuit breakers include immediate breaking at startup, automatic tripping after closing and excessive temperature rise; circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker, and during maintenance a comprehensive inspection is required every six months, with emphasis on checking the integrity of the arc chute and the burning of the contact surfaces.

The circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor is a relatively typical fault symptom. The main cause of this symptom is that the instantaneous operating setting current of the overcurrent trip unit is too small; an instantaneous operating setting current of the overcurrent trip unit that is too small directly leads to the circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor. For this cause, the treatment method is to adjust the instantaneous setting spring of the overcurrent trip unit, that is, to restore its instantaneous operating value by adjusting the overcurrent trip unit. This adjustment falls within the scope of overcurrent trip unit maintenance and adjustment and is used to solve automatic tripping faults caused by failure of the overcurrent trip unit or an operating current value that is too low. When the main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration, the measure of adjusting the overcurrent trip unit is likewise taken. In addition, if the overcurrent trip unit is already close to the operating value at normal load current, this adjustment likewise needs to be performed.

The circuit breaker automatically breaking about 1 h after closing is another symptom whose cause needs to be distinguished. An incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit will cause the circuit breaker to automatically break about 1 h after closing, and deterioration of the thermal element or semiconductor delay circuit components will likewise cause the circuit breaker to automatically break about 1 h after closing. These two causes often appear in parallel, but the treatment methods differ: for an incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, the corresponding treatment method is readjustment, that is, readjusting the long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit; for deterioration of the thermal element or semiconductor delay circuit components, the thermal element or semiconductor delay circuit components need to be replaced. This fault symptom is distinguished from breaking caused by an incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, and the specific cause should be identified first before starting work during troubleshooting.

Noise in the undervoltage trip unit is a fault manifestation in which the circuit breaker emits an abnormal sound in the closed state. Excessive reaction spring force is one cause of noise in the undervoltage trip unit, oil contamination on the core working face will cause the undervoltage trip unit to produce noise, and a broken shading coil is a common cause of noise in the undervoltage trip unit. These three causes exist in parallel, and the treatment methods differ: for noise caused by excessive reaction spring force, the spring should be readjusted; oil contamination on the core working face corresponds to removing the oil contamination, and removing the oil contamination from the core working face will eliminate the noise caused by oil contamination; a broken shading coil corresponds to replacing the armature or core, and replacing the armature or core can deal with the noise caused by a broken shading coil. The shading coil is installed on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core and is used to eliminate armature vibration noise; a broken or detached shading coil will cause the AC electromagnet to produce relatively loud noise, and when damaged it can be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil can be replaced directly. The reaction spring is the spring component that provides release force or reset force; excessive force will cause the trip unit to produce noise, and readjustment is the means of eliminating this noise.

Excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker is a common fault in which the equipment temperature rises abnormally. Contact pressure that is too low is one cause of excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, excessive wear of the contact surface or poor contact of contacts will cause excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, and loose connecting screws of two conductive parts will likewise cause excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker. For temperature rise caused by contact pressure that is too low, the contact pressure needs to be adjusted or the spring replaced; for temperature rise caused by poor contact of contacts, the contacts need to be replaced or the contact surfaces cleaned; for temperature rise caused by loose connections of conductive parts, the screws need to be tightened. Contact pressure that is too low is usually caused by failure of the contact pressure spring or improper adjustment, while poor contact refers to a state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact of contacts, increasing the contact resistance; poor contact of contacts can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit, and can also cause random output actions, corresponding to the need to check the terminal wiring. Loose screws in marine electrical and mechanical equipment are caused by vibration, improper installation or aging, which reduce the fastening force of connecting parts, thereby causing poor contact, open circuit, overheating or mechanical faults; the vibration and swaying environment peculiar to ships very easily causes looseness of wiring clamping screws, of cable connectors relative to the base, and of fixing screws inside the PLC, creating hidden fault risks. In the PLC input/output circuit, a loose "COM" screw will cause the numbers of the relays with abnormal actions to show a regular pattern in units of 8 points, and retightening is required, that is, a loose "COM" screw corresponds to tightening treatment. If the main switch fastening mechanism is loose, tightening should also be carried out.

An auxiliary switch fault manifests as damage or jamming of the internal mechanical parts of the auxiliary switch. One fault cause is that the moving contact bridge of the auxiliary switch is jammed or detached, and another fault cause is that the auxiliary switch drive rod is broken or the roller is detached. Treatment methods include straightening or reinstalling the moving contact bridge, and replacing the drive rod and roller or replacing the entire auxiliary switch. The moving contact bridge of the auxiliary switch being jammed or detached is one of the direct causes of the auxiliary switch of the circuit breaker developing a fault, and the corresponding treatment method is to straighten or reinstall the moving contact bridge; a broken drive rod or detached roller of the auxiliary switch is one of the common causes, and the corresponding treatment method is to replace the drive rod and roller, or, if they cannot be repaired separately, to replace the entire auxiliary switch.

Malfunction of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit, causing the circuit breaker to open, falls within the scope of common fault troubleshooting of circuit breakers, and its consequence is to cause the circuit breaker to open. The prerequisite for treatment is to identify the fault and confirm that the semiconductor trip unit itself is not damaged. A local short circuit inside the undervoltage coil reduces the attraction force, and a period of time is required before the trip unit operates.

A circuit breaker may also develop the situation in which, when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close; if this is caused by excessive reaction spring force, readjustment is required. When the circuit breaker develops the situation in which, when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contacts cannot close, if it is failure of the motor-operated positioning switch, the corresponding action is readjustment. When the circuit breaker develops the failure of one phase contact to close, if it is because the reclosing contact surface is too large, the corresponding action is readjustment. When the circuit breaker develops the situation in which the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker break, loose internal screws are a possible fault cause; loose screws cause the shunt trip unit to fail to make the circuit breaker break, and the corresponding action is to tighten the screws. When the circuit breaker develops the situation in which the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker break, the possible cause is that the reaction spring has become smaller, and the spring needs to be adjusted.

In the measurement and judgment stage, current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments and is used to understand equipment status; the current value can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter; a multimeter is used for current measurement, and a clamp-on ammeter is used for current measurement. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. In a through-type current transformer, the large-current conductor under measurement is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding.
