Troubleshooting of circuit breakers cannot be separated from instrument measurement, and the multimeter is the most frequently used of these. A multimeter consists of three parts, the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, and is a multi-purpose instrument; according to the display mode it is divided into two types, analog and digital; an analog multimeter belongs to multimeters, a digital multimeter likewise belongs to multimeters, and the MF-47 multimeter is one type of analog multimeter. The current flowing through the meter head at full scale is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes; the MF-47 can measure a maximum voltage of 2500 V and a maximum direct current of 5 A, and the panel is provided with four jacks, "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". With a multimeter, various electrical quantities and device parameters can be measured, such as resistance, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples. When measuring direct current, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range and the meter head is connected in series in the broken branch; when measuring direct voltage, the test probes are connected in parallel across the component under measurement, and when the range is uncertain the maximum range is set first. Voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis, and its value can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter; the generator failing to build up voltage can be selected as the top event when constructing a fault tree, and overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system. A capacitor consists of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in between, has the function of charging and discharging, and its characteristic is to block direct current and pass alternating current; in circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25, and its obstructive effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC); a multimeter can be used to measure its leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. A transistor contains two PN junctions inside and has current amplification capability; it is divided into NPN and PNP types, is commonly denoted in circuits by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17, and its main models include PNP transistors such as A92 and 9015 and NPN transistors such as A42, 9014 and 9018; when marine electrical equipment uses transistors, transistor faults occur, and such faults belong to problems of the transistor itself and can be judged by measuring the tube type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor with a multimeter.

A contactor is an electrical device used in ship power systems to control motors, belongs to low-voltage control devices, is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation and small size. The power of various auxiliary machinery on board is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on board. A contactor includes components such as the arc chute, main contacts, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to contactors. A coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to pull in and the motor failing to start; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

A circuit breaker is a switching device used in ship power systems to protect circuits, belongs to low-voltage distribution devices, is divided into frame type (air circuit breaker) and molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during a short circuit fault. When a circuit breaker is used for generator protection, it opens after a delay of less than 2 min for an overload of 10%-50%.

A circuit breaker may develop various faults: when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close; when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contacts cannot close; one phase contact cannot close; the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker break; the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker break; the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the circuit breaker automatically breaks about 1 h after closing; noise in the undervoltage trip unit. Load short circuit or overload corresponds to judgment by the method of measurement with a multimeter.

When a circuit breaker fails, the fault cause should be carefully sought. If a large electromagnet is operating nearby, such as the breaking of a contactor or electric welding, it should be isolated or the line should be replaced. This step is used to troubleshoot circuit breaker faults caused by the operation of nearby large electromagnets such as contactor breaking and electric welding. When it is found that a large electromagnet is operating nearby, measures of isolation or line replacement should be taken. In most cases, this type of fault cause may be external electromagnetic interference.

The circuit breaker performs the function of protecting the circuit in the marine power system. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid; the work of circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker itself, and the fault symptoms that may occur in the circuit breaker are various. The following explains them separately according to the mode of operation and the category of trip unit. One of the causes of this symptom is that the undervoltage trip unit has no voltage or the coil is burnt out. This cause directly leads to the contact being unable to close during manual operation of the circuit breaker. For the cause of the undervoltage trip unit having no voltage or the coil being burnt out, the corresponding treatment is to check the line, apply voltage or replace the coil; if the coil is already damaged, replace the coil. Deformation of the energy-storing spring causes the closing force to decrease, which likewise leads to the contact being unable to close during manual operation of the circuit breaker; the treatment method is to replace the energy-storing spring. Among the above causes, the undervoltage trip unit having no voltage or the coil being burnt out, deformation of the energy-storing spring causing the closing force to decrease, the reaction spring force being too large, and the mechanism being unable to reset and re-latch all belong under the fault symptom of the contact being unable to close during manual operation of the circuit breaker. An operating power supply voltage that does not match will cause the contact to be unable to close during electric operation of the circuit breaker; the power supply should be replaced during treatment. Insufficient power supply capacity will also cause the contact to be unable to close during electric operation of the circuit breaker; the corresponding measure is to increase the operating power supply capacity. Insufficient travel of the electromagnet pull rod will likewise cause the contact to be unable to close during electric operation of the circuit breaker; the treatment method is readjustment or replacement of the pull rod. Damage to the rectifier or capacitor in the controller will also cause the contact to be unable to close during electric operation of the circuit breaker; for the cause of damage to the rectifier or capacitor in the controller, the corresponding treatment is to replace the rectifier or capacitor. Once the rectifier or capacitor inside the controller is damaged, it will affect the normal operation of the electric operating circuit. The angle between the foldable links of the current-limiting switch release mechanism becoming larger belongs to abnormal mechanical fit of the current-limiting switch release mechanism and will also cause one phase contact to be unable to close; during treatment, the angle between the links should be adjusted to the requirements specified in the original technical conditions. In the fault of excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, loosening of the connecting screws of two conductive parts is also one of the main causes, which likewise needs to be handled by tightening the screws. The reaction spring becoming smaller is one of the causes of this fault; the treatment method is to adjust the spring to restore the reaction force. Abnormal energy-storage release will also cause this fault to occur; for the refusal to operate of the undervoltage trip unit caused by energy-storage release, the treatment method is to adjust the energy-storing spring. Mechanism jamming is the mechanical cause of this fault; during treatment, the cause of mechanism jamming needs to be eliminated. If the reaction spring force of the circuit breaker undervoltage trip unit is too large, it will cause the trip unit to produce noise; this point should also be noted when checking the reaction spring. The main switch is mainly composed of the undervoltage release, the shunt release and the overcurrent protection device. The DW14 circuit breaker is additionally provided with an AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker.

Other components belonging to marine electrical equipment together with the circuit breaker also need to be maintained. Capacitor types include electrolytic capacitor, ceramic capacitor, chip capacitor, monolithic capacitor, tantalum capacitor and polyester capacitor; capacitance units are farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF) and picofarad (pF). When marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, the capacitor detection steps apply to capacitors; a capacitor may suffer a capacitor fault, and a capacitor fault belongs to the category of capacitor. The function of a capacitor is charging and discharging; the measurable performance includes earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors, and a multimeter is used during measurement. Voltage is likewise one of the meter readings that need to be checked; its measurable performance is the voltage value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter or voltmeter. A multimeter is used both for measuring voltage and for measuring capacitance.

The reaction spring is a spring component in contactors and circuit breakers, used to provide release force or reset force. Failure or absence of the contactor armature reaction spring will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed. When handling contactor release faults, the reaction spring needs to be replaced or adjusted, but care must be taken that the reaction force is not too large. The energy-storing spring, as a component of the circuit breaker, will cause the closing force of the circuit breaker to decrease when deformed. If the contact cannot close during manual operation of the circuit breaker due to deformation of the energy-storing spring, the energy-storing spring needs to be replaced; if the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker break due to energy-storage release, the energy-storing spring needs to be adjusted.

The multimeter is used to measure voltage and is a basic means of judging circuit status. During measurement, the corresponding range should be selected according to whether the circuit under test is AC or DC, and it should be confirmed that the range is higher than the voltage value under test, so as to avoid inaccurate readings or damage to the meter head.

There are many forms of faults that may occur in a circuit breaker. When the temperature rise of the circuit breaker is too high, the contact resistance, the tightness of the connecting screws and the integrity of the arc chute should be checked; when the auxiliary switch fails, its contact contact and the position of the transmission link should be checked; when the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit misoperates and causes the circuit breaker to open, the setting value of the trip unit and whether the secondary circuit wiring of the transformer is correct should be checked.

Models and uses of common fuses. A fuse is represented by the symbol FU in circuit diagrams and belongs to distribution apparatus; it is a protective apparatus. When overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or electrical equipment, it relies on melting the fuse element to automatically cut off the circuit, and therefore has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. The protective conductive material for making fuse and fuse element needs to have conditions such as a low melting point and certain mechanical strength. Common fuses in marine power systems include RL93, RS0, RSo, RS3, RLS, RM10, BX and other series, each suitable for different voltage and current ranges and protection objects.

The RL93 series belongs to marine fuses of spiral structure, with a rated voltage of 380V and a rated current range of 6 to 600A, used as an overload or short circuit protection element in circuits. The rated voltage of the RS0 series fuse is 250 to 900V, and the current specification is 30 to 480A; it is specially used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers and their complete sets, and can also provide appropriate overload protection for certain devices. The voltage specification range of RSo is 250V to 900V, and the current specification is marked as 30sim480V (as in the original text); its main use is to protect semiconductor rectifiers or complete sets composed of such elements, provide short circuit protection, and provide appropriate overload protection for certain devices. The rated voltage of the RS3 series includes three levels of 250V, 500V and 750V, and the current specification is 10 to 300A; it is used for internal short circuit protection of thyristor rectifiers and their complete sets, as well as overload protection of devices that do not allow overcurrent. The rated voltage of the RLS series fuse is 500V, and the rated current specifications include 10A and 50A; it is used for internal short circuit protection of silicon rectifier elements, thyristor rectifier elements and complete sets composed of silicon or thyristor elements, and is also used for overload protection of certain devices that do not allow overcurrent. The rated voltage of the RM10 series fuse is 500V, and the rated current range is 15 to 600A; it is used as an element for overload or short circuit protection in circuits. The rated voltage of the BX series fuse is 250V, and the rated current range is 1 to 5A; it is applied to the protection of electrical installations and radio installations and has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. A rectifier is a component that converts alternating current into direct current. The electrical graphic symbol of a full-wave bridge rectifier is UR. In a controllable phase compound excitation constant voltage device, rectifier fault is one of the sub-causes of phase compound excitation device fault; if the UR rectifier has an open-circuit diode, it will cause a voltage deviation of |U0-Ufe| greater than ΔU1. The RS0 fuse is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers and their complete sets, and the RS3 fuse is used for internal short circuit protection of thyristor rectifiers and their complete sets, precisely meeting the protection requirements of such rectifier elements.

Selection of the rated current of the fuse element. The fuse element is the main component of the fuse, and its rated current should be selected according to the specific conditions of the protected circuit. In lighting and electric heating circuits, the rated current of the fuse element should be greater than or equal to the rated current of the total load. For a circuit with a single asynchronous motor started directly, the rated current of the fuse element is taken as 1.5 to 2 times the rated current of the motor; for a motor circuit with light load and infrequent starting, 2.5 to 4 times the rated current of the motor is taken; for a motor circuit with heavy load and frequent starting, 3 to 6 times the rated current of the motor is taken. In a circuit with multiple asynchronous motors started directly, the fuse is used only as short circuit protection and should not be used as overload protection. This is because the fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not serve as overload protection for the motor; motor overload protection is usually realized by a transistor relay converting power into voltage and satisfying the relationship U=KP, and the thermal relay FR operates when the motor is overloaded, opening the control circuit so that the contactor KM loses power and stops the machine. In addition, excessive refrigerant charged in the refrigeration system causing excessive pressure and excessive load will also cause motor overload, and this type of overload should likewise not rely on the fuse for protection.

Judgment of phenomena after fuse blowing. Fuse blowing is a common cause of equipment faults, and its phenomena differ markedly with the nature of the breaking current. When blowing under overload current, the sound is not loud, the fuse element breaks at only one or two places, there is no scorch mark in the tube, and there is no large amount of vapor attached. When breaking the limiting current, that is, a short circuit, the sound is loud, accompanied by flame, the fuse element breaks into multiple sections, and there are vapor or scorch marks on the tube wall. Fuse blowing will cause the POWER lamp to go out, and will also cause the relay with abnormal action to be numbered unit 8; in a PLC system, one of the possible causes of the POWER lamp going out is fuse blowing in the input circuit, and one of the possible causes of all PLC outputs being unable to connect is fuse blowing in the power supply. The typical manifestation when a short circuit fault occurs in the control circuit is also fuse element blowing. The fuse element, subjected for a long time to the surge current of the power supply, may also blow under non-short-circuit fault conditions.

Operating requirements for replacing the fuse. After a fuse is blown, the operation corresponds to replacing the fuse; fuse blowing in the power supply likewise corresponds to replacing the fuse. When replacing a fuse, generally the fuse should be removed for replacement without power applied; if live replacement is permitted, the load must first be cut off to avoid danger. Before replacing with a new fuse element, the inner surface of the tube and the contact surfaces must be carefully wiped clean of fuse slag, soot and dust, because after the fuse element breaks the limiting current, the fuse element is often melted and welded onto the contact surfaces. This operation belongs to item 2 of the fuse replacement instructions.

When replacing the fuse element, attention must be paid to the current value of the fuse element and the number of fuse element pieces; the fuse element must be the same as the original fuse element, and it is strictly forbidden to arbitrarily replace it with fuse elements of different specifications to substitute for the original fuse element; the fuse element of a fast-acting fuse cannot be replaced with the fuse element of an ordinary fuse. When replacing the fuse element, care should be taken not to bend or twist the fuse element, because the fuse element material is relatively soft and easily broken and the risk of physical damage is high; bending or twisting will cause cracks in the fuse element, and mechanical damage will reduce the effective cross-sectional area of the fuse element, and the reduction of cross-sectional area will in turn cause the rated current value of the fuse element to decrease.

For enclosed tube fuses, the fuse tube cannot be replaced with other insulating tubes; replacing the enclosed tube fuse tube with other insulating tubes easily leads to explosion and personal injury; drilling holes in the enclosed tube fuse tube is prohibited, otherwise it will cause difficulty in arc extinction, and drilling holes in the tube may also spray high-temperature metal and gas, endangering the safety of persons and equipment.

Use of instruments in fuse fault inspection. In fault diagnosis of fuses and related circuits, voltage and current are the meter readings that need to be checked. The voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter, and the current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after opening the circuit. A multimeter can also be used to measure the polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode of a thyristor; a thyristor is also called SCR or controlled silicon. The MF-30 multimeter belongs to FU-related measuring instruments. In the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line via FU.

The programmable logic controller (PLC) is equipment that undertakes control tasks in the marine automation system; its full English name is Programmable Logical Controller, and it also appears in the form PLD in some materials. This type of equipment came out in the 1960s and, together with robot technology and CAD/CAM technology, is called one of the three pillars of industrial production automation. PLC has the advantages of simple programming, easy modification and debugging, convenient maintenance, high reliability, small size and moderate price, so it is often listed by engineers as the preferred scheme in automation scheme design. On ships, PLC is used to control equipment such as cargo winches, automatic oil separators, boilers and automated power stations, and its operating condition is directly related to whether these controlled objects can work normally.

Structurally, the programmable logic controller (PLC) belongs to a dedicated industrial computer, and its basic structure is composed of a central processing unit (CPU), memory (RAM/EPROM), input interface, output interface, programmer and power supply part. The central processing unit (CPU) is the core component of the central controller and plays the role of overall monitoring; it reads input signals into the memory, takes out the user-written program according to the program counter address and compiles it, controls each executing component to complete the operations specified by the user instructions, and finally sends the operation results to the output interface. The memory (RAM/EPROM), together with the central processing unit (CPU) and the input and output interfaces, is one of the basic structural components of the PLC. Inside the PLC, a bus-type structure is used for the transmission of data and instructions; once the bus fails, for example a CPU bus fault will cause abnormal action of input relays, and an I/O bus fault in the CPU will cause abnormal action of output relays.

The input interface accepts control information from field devices such as buttons, travel switches, contactor contacts and sensors, and converts the received field control information into digital signals that the CPU can accept and process. In the microcomputer-type engine room monitoring and alarm system, the input interface is used to input the status of switching-value sensors into the computer; in the switching-value input interface, the input voltage is 24V when the switch is closed and 0V when it is open. If all PLC inputs are abnormal and the wiring problem has been ruled out, it is usually judged as an input interface circuit fault and replacement is required. The output interface converts the digital signal output by the CPU into voltage or current to drive actuating devices such as solenoid valves and contactors; the switching-value output interface controls the display and alarm devices through an optical isolator and a driver. The power supply part provides higher voltage and large current power supply for the output interface circuit. In the final stage of PLC operation, the output interface status is refreshed according to the output register results. Vibration and bumping on board often cause poor contact of output interface terminals or circuit disconnection faults; if the output indicator lamp is on but there is no action, the fault may be in the drive circuit, the actuating device or the external wiring. The input interface and the output interface are collectively called the I/O interface, which is the channel for the CPU to exchange information with the outside and is easily damaged by faults of external devices.

The power supply part has the function of converting AC or DC power into the DC working power required by the internal circuit, and its output is divided into three categories. The first category of power supply supplies the integrated circuit, providing +5V and +15V DC power; the third category of power supply is a lithium battery, ensuring that the memory does not lose information when power is off. Different categories of power supply have different wiring and capacities, which must be noted during expansion and maintenance. When the POWER lamp is out and fuse, diode and wiring faults have been ruled out, the entire power supply part needs to be replaced. The lithium battery belongs to the third category of DC working power supply of the PLC and is dedicated to memory backup; its main function is to ensure that the PLC memory does not lose information when power is off, and it needs to be replaced periodically according to the battery manufacturer's data to prevent loss of RAM/ROM information. Before replacement, the AC power supply needs to be connected for 10s to charge the backup capacitor; during replacement, the AC power supply needs to be disconnected, and the new battery should be taken out of the battery clip and installed; when installing the new battery, attention must be paid to polarity, and the operation time should be as short as possible.

Modern PLCs use EEPROM storage technology and do not require replacement of backup lithium batteries.

The programmer is the most important peripheral device of the PLC; its main uses include inputting, editing, debugging, modifying and checking user programs and monitoring execution. In PLC fault diagnosis, the programmer can display "error" information to assist in distinguishing internal and external faults; in the troubleshooting process, the programmer must be connected to check whether the program has an END instruction or whether the program is appropriate; the programmer can also be used to input the simplest ladder diagram simulation signal to test the controllability of the output channel circuit.

The PLC input terminals together with the COM terminal form the input circuit interface; the output terminals are located between COM and the load, corresponding to the external contacts of output coils such as Y31-Y32. The harsh environment on board easily causes the wiring heads and terminals to rust, resulting in poor contact, which must be cleaned in time. Loosening of the input terminals or poor contact will cause the PLC POWER lamp to go out; poor contact of the input terminals is also one of the common causes of random input action. If the terminal voltage is still abnormal after removing the load, first check whether the output terminals and the output fuse are normal; poor contact of the output terminals is one of the causes of a certain output relay failing to pick up while the indicator lamp is lit; the treatment measure for this type of fault is to reconnect.

The PLC control system consists of the CPU, input/output interface circuits and peripheral equipment; faults in the peripheral connecting lines or components will cause the system to fail or malfunction, endangering personal safety. Its input signals originate from switches, contacts and sensors, and the goodness of contact and the deviation of analog signals must be checked regularly; the output control objects are mainly relays and solenoid valves, whose working state must be checked periodically to eliminate hidden dangers. External surge voltage noise interference can cause CPU malfunction, manifested as the "CPU Error" lamp staying lit. Abnormal phenomena that may occur in the PLC control system include the POWER lamp going out, the fuse blowing repeatedly, the RUN lamp going out, all inputs failing to pick up, all PLC inputs abnormal, a certain input relay failing to pick up, a certain input relay normally closed, random input action, the numbers of abnormally acting relays being in units of 8 points, the input relay acting correctly but the indicator lamp going out, all outputs failing to pick up, all outputs failing to turn off, a certain output relay failing to pick up while the indicator lamp goes out, a certain output relay failing to pick up while the indicator lamp is lit, a certain output relay failing to turn off while the indicator lamp goes out, a certain output relay failing to turn off while the indicator lamp is lit, etc.

PLC maintenance applies to the programmable logic controller (PLC) itself, and its periodic maintenance work includes several specific steps. One step is to check whether the connecting lines are damaged, aged, etc., and whether the solder joints are desoldered, cold-soldered, oxidized, etc.; if the above abnormal phenomena are found, the relevant components should be replaced in time; for the rusting of wiring heads and terminals caused by the harsh environment on board, timely cleaning is required to prevent poor contact. Another step is to check for loosening of wiring clamping screws caused by ship vibration and swaying. Yet another step is to open the outer cover, blow away dust with a hot-air blower, and spray-wash with electrical cleaner to wash away oil stains and salt crystals; this step is used to remove dust, oil mist and salt mist on the printed circuit boards inside the PLC; before the operation, the PLC outer cover must be opened and the external power supply cut off, a hot-air blower used to remove dust, and electrical cleaner used to spray-wash oil stains and salt crystals, aimed at preventing deterioration of the insulation performance of the circuit board or short circuits between components caused by contamination.

Regularly replacing the lithium battery inside the machine is also one of the maintenance steps; its purpose is to ensure that the RAM and ROM inside the PLC do not lose information during a short-term power failure, and replacement must be carried out regularly according to the data provided by the battery manufacturer; in addition, it is necessary to check whether the switches and contacts of the input peripheral equipment are in good contact and whether the analog signals sent by the sensors deviate too much; this step belongs to the connecting line inspection content in the periodic maintenance of the PLC control system; faults in the peripheral equipment connecting lines will cause the PLC control system to fail to work normally or even fail, and connecting line faults may cause PLC malfunction, causing equipment damage or endangering personal safety. At the same time, check whether the relays, solenoid valves, etc. of the output peripheral equipment are in good working condition.

The harsh conditions on board cause the wiring heads and terminals to rust, easily causing poor contact in the PLC input/output circuits. Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to loosening, oxidation or foreign matter; loosening of fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance and thereby causing faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit. The vibration and swaying environment peculiar to ships very easily causes loosening of wiring clamping screws, of the connections between cable heads and bases, and of the fixing screws inside the PLC, creating hidden fault dangers; in the PLC input/output circuits, loosening of the "COM" terminal screw will cause the numbers of abnormally acting relays to show a regularity in units of 8 points, and it must be tightened again. Screw loosening is a common cause in marine electrical and mechanical equipment in which the fastening force of connections decreases due to vibration, improper installation or aging, thereby causing poor contact, open circuit, overheating or mechanical faults; in the fault of excessively high temperature rise of a circuit breaker, loosening of the connecting screws of two conductive parts is one of the main causes and must be handled by tightening the screws; when an open-circuit fault occurs in a line, loosening of the screws at the wire joints or falling off of nuts is also one of the common causes.

Among the peripheral actuating devices of the PLC, the solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel oil, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit at ignition so that oil enters the nozzle to inject fuel; the PLC output interface converts digital signals into voltage or current to drive the solenoid valve to act. A solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel oil circulation circuit, release the residual air of the air compressor, or control the zones of fine water mist fire extinguishing; it is energized in the burner ignition program, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle to inject fuel; its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when the power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve. A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors; in the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. The control platform contains sensors.

A contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system, belonging to low-voltage control apparatus, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, featuring high operating frequency and long life, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The amount of contactors used on board is very large, because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor contains an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and its inspection and repair methods can likewise be used for reference for apparatus of similar construction such as intermediate relays. An intermediate relay is a type of electromagnetic relay, similar in construction to a contactor, used to expand contact capacity and number and for control logic conversion; its function is to expand contact capacity and number, its construction is the same as a contactor, and fault analysis and treatment can be carried out by referring to the inspection and repair methods of contactors. A coil is an electrical component made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, having the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start;

The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked.

In testing and maintenance, voltage is one of the measurable performance parameters, and the measuring tool is a multimeter or voltmeter; current is likewise a measurable performance parameter, and the measuring tools are a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter; a multimeter is used to measure voltage, current and capacitance, and a clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. The function of a capacitor is charging and discharging, and its measurable performance includes earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors; a capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle, its characteristic being to block direct current and pass alternating current, and in circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; its hindering effect on alternating current signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC).

Marine electrical equipment uses integrated circuits and printed circuit boards. Integrated circuits have the advantages of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration increased, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits appeared; their common package forms are 14-pin or 16-pin, and the types include CMOS circuits and TTL circuits; the pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise, and to facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often soldered on the circuit board for direct plugging in; common package forms include the four-side J-lead type (PLCC), the two-side gull-wing lead type (SOIC), the dual in-line lead type (DIP) and power integrated circuit packages. A printed circuit board consists of a base material and circuits; the base material is an insulating material, such as phenolic resin board or epoxy glass, and the circuits are conductive foil, usually copper; dust, oil mist and salt mist on board easily cause deterioration of the insulation performance of the printed circuit board or even short circuits, and when cleaning, electrical cleaner can be used to spray-wash oil stains and salt crystals, and the operation must be carried out with the external power supply cut off. A printed circuit board consists of an insulating base plate and conductive copper circuits, and is the carrier for mounting and interconnecting electronic components, with patterns formed by etching processes; the base material is often called the base plate, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the circuit part is made of conductive copper, laid on the base plate, and the required patterns are obtained by etching. Printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards; printed circuit boards will suffer circuit board faults, and circuit board faults fall within the scope of printed circuit boards.

The power supply section of the PLC undertakes the task of converting AC or DC power into the DC working power required by the internal circuits, and according to the different objects supplied, it can be divided into three types of DC working power.

Power supply faults are a common type of fault in PLC control systems. Switching inverter power supplies are prone to faults and difficult to repair, so on board the strategy of overall replacement is usually adopted. The inspection process for power supply faults starts with the state of the POWER lamp; if the POWER lamp is out, then the power supply, fuse and light-emitting diode are checked in sequence. The fault symptom of the POWER lamp being out may be caused by a fuse blown, poor contact of the input terminals, or a broken input power line. During troubleshooting, first confirm whether there is power input; if the power supply is normal, check whether the fuse is blown; if the fuse is intact, check whether the light-emitting diode is broken down, and if so, replace the light-emitting diode; if the above components are normal, measure the terminal output voltage; if there is no voltage output at the terminals, check the terminal wiring.

Power supply faults correspond to the maintenance procedure of checking the power supply; in the overall inspection of the PLC, if the POWER lamp is out, the step of checking power supply faults must be carried out.

The RUN lamp being out is another type of fault symptom of the PLC. When the RUN lamp is out, first check whether the PC switch is set to the run position; if the switch is normal, confirm whether the RAM/ROM is inserted correctly; connect the programmer to check whether there is an END instruction in the program; if the program is appropriate, check whether the input and output terminals are in good contact; after eliminating external factors, it may be an internal circuit fault, and the circuit board must be replaced; if accompanied by the CPU Error lamp flashing, check whether the battery voltage has dropped. The absence of an END indication in the program, power supply faults, and duplication of I/O port addresses will all cause the RUN lamp to go out. Poor input contact corresponds to the maintenance procedure of checking the terminal wiring; no load power supply corresponds to the maintenance procedure of switching on the power supply. The PLC starts its self-diagnosis process as soon as the power supply is switched on; if an internal CPU error occurs, the panel "CPU Error" lamp shows an abnormality; after eliminating external surge voltage interference, the power supply must be switched on again to observe whether the PLC fault disappears, otherwise replace the CPU board. Before switching on the power supply, the input and output sections must be tested for short circuit or earthing faults, and power may be applied only after confirmation that there is no problem.

The PLC control system consists of the CPU, input/output interface circuits and peripheral equipment, and is susceptible to surge interference causing malfunction. The input interface receives on-site information such as from pushbuttons and sensors and converts it into digital signals that the CPU can process; the PLC input interface receives sensor information from field devices and converts it into digital signals that the CPU can accept and process. The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve. The control platform contains sensors.

The PLC input/output interfaces exchange information with the controlled objects through wiring terminals and connecting wires, and are susceptible to vibration causing poor contact. Severe vibration and jolting on board often cause poor contact of the wiring terminals, thereby causing faults such as open circuits in the loops. A wiring terminal is a metal contact component used in electrical systems to connect wires to equipment or circuit nodes, commonly found in PLC interfaces, instruments and control circuits; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals is one of the common faults of electrical components. The electric main engine remote control system contains fuses and wiring terminals. A fuse is made of protective conductive material and has the characteristics of a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength; its material is aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, etc.; in the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components.

A diode has unidirectional conductivity, is commonly denoted by VD in circuits, and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite. According to function, it is divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), etc. Diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. A light-emitting diode can emit red, green and yellow light, has unidirectional conductivity, and its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode; it is commonly used as a circuit working state indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display screen; its external dimensions include diameters of 3mm, 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle; the working current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model, and in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage; the conduction voltage is above 1.7V.

For light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the precautions for using light-emitting diodes. The diode testing procedure applies to diodes. The multimeter is used to measure voltage and diodes; marine electrical equipment uses diodes. Voltage is one of the meter readings to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems.

The conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation. Observation is a sub-step of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged"; the content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status, and equipment operating parameters, specifically including whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device.

The input interface, together with the CPU and memory, constitutes the basic structure of the PLC; the input/output interface circuit is the channel through which the CPU exchanges information with the outside, and is easily damaged by external equipment faults. When the X400/X401 indicator lamps are off and the voltage across the two ends is normal, it is judged to be an input interface processing circuit fault and replacement is required; if the voltage measured after removing the wiring is still abnormal, it indicates an input interface processing circuit fault, and the input interface circuit must be replaced. If all PLC inputs are abnormal and wiring problems have been ruled out, it is usually judged to be an input interface circuit fault and replacement is required; this step is at the end of the troubleshooting flow of first checking the external wiring and load, then checking the PLC internal circuit.

One of the common fault symptoms of the PLC control system is that a certain input relay fails to pick up; its possible fault causes include input signal source (device) fault, input wiring break, input terminal loose or input terminal poor contact, input on-time too short, and input circuit fault. When the fault cause is an input signal source (device) fault, the corresponding handling method is to replace the input device, that is, to perform the maintenance procedure of replacing the input device. The PLC control system may also exhibit random output actions; PLC supply voltage too low is one of the common fault causes of this phenomenon, and the corresponding handling method is to adjust the power supply output. In addition, the PLC control system may suffer faults such as POWER lamp off, fuse blown repeatedly, RUN lamp off, all inputs failing to pick up, and all PLC inputs abnormal. When the POWER lamp is off and the fuse is not blown, check whether the light-emitting diode is broken down; if so, replace the light-emitting diode.

The testing and replacement of semiconductor devices is common content in PLC maintenance. A transistor contains two PN junctions internally and has current amplification capability; it is divided into NPN type and PNP type, and is commonly denoted in circuits by "VT" plus a number, e.g. VT17 denotes transistor No. 17; main models include PNP types such as A92 and 9015, and NPN types such as A42, 9014 and 9018; a transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault falls within the device category of the transistor. The thyristor is also called SCR, or silicon controlled rectifier; its measurable characteristics include polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode. Marine electrical equipment widely uses diodes and transistors. The fuse corresponds to the symbol FU and has overload protection and short circuit protection functions; it is a protective electrical device that, when the power grid or electrical equipment suffers overload or short circuit, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; it belongs to distribution electrical devices and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs; the RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection.

Contactor-type faults are likewise closely related to the PLC control circuit. Supply voltage too low or fluctuating greatly, insufficient capacity of the operating power supply, short circuit inside the coil, jamming of moving parts, excessive spring reaction force, rusted or skewed shaft, coil rated voltage higher than the line rated voltage, and too large contact gap, i.e. too large armature air gap, will all cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force with a buzzing sound when the start button is pressed. Failure or damage of the armature reaction spring, contact welding, jamming of moving parts, rusted or skewed shaft, and oil sludge adhering to the core pole face will all cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly when the stop button is pressed.

The interior of the PLC uses a bus-type structure to complete the transmission of data and instructions; once the bus fails, the impact often spreads to the entire input/output channel. On the input side, a CPU bus fault is one of the causes of abnormal actions with relay numbers in units of 8 points; when such regular abnormalities occur, the handling measure for the CPU bus fault is to replace the CPU unit. A parallel clue is the loose "COM" screw, which likewise causes abnormal actions with relay numbers in units of 8 points; the handling method is to tighten the loose "COM" screw. Over a wider range, a loose screw also causes the shunt trip unit to fail to trip the circuit breaker, and the corresponding handling is likewise to tighten the screw.

Random input actions are a relatively common type of abnormality in the PLC control system, with three parallel causes. Input signal level too low is the primary fault cause of random input actions; during troubleshooting, check the power supply and input devices; input poor contact is one of the main causes of random input actions, and the terminal wiring needs to be checked; input noise too high is one of the three major causes of random input actions, and the elimination measure is to add shielding or filtering measures. These three items are arranged in sequence in the fault list, with input poor contact located after input signal level too low and before input noise too high. Input poor contact means the input signal fails to be transmitted stably due to a contact problem; together with input signal level too low and input noise too high, it constitutes the complete set of causes of random input actions. A similar situation exists on the output side: poor contact causes random output actions, and the terminal wiring must likewise be checked during handling; input noise too high requires shielding or filtering measures, and when the output circuit noise is too high, shielding or filtering measures are also adopted.

A certain input relay normally closed is another type of fault symptom occurring in the PLC control system; its direct cause is judged to be an input circuit fault, and the handling method is to check the circuit or replace the relevant components. In the troubleshooting table, this phenomenon is listed alongside items such as input wiring break and terminal loose, with input circuit fault listed as item 5. An input circuit fault is a problem at the input circuit level, distinct from wiring break or terminal loose; it may both cause a certain input relay to be normally closed and cause random input actions, and the corresponding maintenance procedure is to check the circuit or replace, that is, to check the faulty circuit or directly replace the damaged components.

On the input side there are also several fault causes that cause a certain input relay to fail to pick up, each corresponding to a different handling means. An input wiring break causes a certain input relay to fail to pick up, and the handling measure is welding; welding is the process of heating to melt the solder so that atomic diffusion occurs between the weldment and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer is formed at their interface; this bonding layer has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength. Input terminal loose or input terminal poor contact likewise causes a certain input relay to fail to pick up, and the corresponding elimination method is to perform the reconnect operation; it is listed alongside input wiring break and input on-time too short as common input-side faults. Input on-time too short also causes a certain input relay to fail to pick up, and the corresponding handling measure is to adjust the relevant parameters; this belongs to the parameter correction step in input circuit troubleshooting. When an input circuit fault causes a certain input relay to fail to pick up, perform check the circuit or replace. In addition, input terminal poor contact causes the POWER lamp off, and the handling method is reconnect; it is listed alongside input terminal loose, and both belong to input-side connection faults. Power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply. When the PLC power supply terminal has no output voltage, the operation of checking the terminal wiring should be performed.

When the indicator lamp state is inconsistent with the actual relay action, the problem mostly lies in the indicating element itself. When the PLC control system exhibits the phenomenon that the input relay operates correctly but the indicator lamp is off, the direct cause is LED damage, and the handling method is to replace the LED. The same applies on the output side: LED damage causes the output relay to operate normally but the indicator lamp to be off, and the LED likewise needs to be replaced; this step is the direct measure to solve the failure of relay status indication.

On the output circuit side, poor contact (terminal block) corresponds to reconnect, output terminal poor contact corresponds to reconnect, and terminal connection block poor contact also corresponds to reconnect. Output terminal block poor contact causes all outputs to fail to pick up, and the handling method is reconnect; output terminal poor contact causes a certain output relay to fail to pick up, and the handling method is likewise reconnect. An I/O bus fault in the CPU causes poor terminal connection contact, and the handling method is reconnect; when all inputs fail to pick up and the cause is terminal contact loose, reconnect is also adopted, and terminal contact loose corresponds to reconnect.

In the automatic control of the diesel generator set, output terminal 20 energizes the coil of the running signal intermediate relay K₂ to operate; during automatic starting, output terminal 18 outputs the start command to energize the coil of the start output intermediate relay K₃.

Diagnosing output faults cannot be separated from checking voltage and current. The voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter, and the current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter, among which the clamp-on ammeter is used for current measurement. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. A fuse blown causes the PLC POWER lamp off, and the handling method at this time is to replace the fuse. The causes of fuse blown repeatedly include load short circuit, overload, input voltage setting error or capacity too small. From the manifestation at fusing: under overload current the fusing sound is not loud, the fuse element breaks at only one or two places, and there is no charring or large amount of vapor attached inside the tube; at breaking limit current, i.e. short circuit, the sound is loud, there is firelight, the fuse element breaks into multiple sections, and the tube wall has vapor or charring. Replacing the fuse should generally be done with the fuse removed under de-energized conditions; if live replacement is permitted, the load must first be disconnected to prevent danger; before installing a new fuse element, the slag, soot and dust on the inner surface of the tube and on the contact surfaces must be carefully wiped clean.

When all outputs of the PLC control system fail to pick up, no load power supply is one cause, and the corresponding handling is to switch on the power supply; a faulty load power supply or voltage too low also causes this phenomenon, and the power supply needs to be adjusted or repaired; poor contact (terminal block) likewise causes all outputs to fail to pick up, and the handling method for this cause is reconnect; power supply fuse blown is one of the causes of this fault, and the fuse needs to be replaced; an output circuit fault also causes this phenomenon, and the handling measure is to replace the output interface circuit. When all outputs of the PLC control system fail to turn off, the direct cause is an output interface circuit fault, and the handling method is likewise to replace the output interface circuit; this phenomenon is distinct from the local fault of a certain output relay failing to turn off.

For faults of a single output relay, distinction must be made according to the indicator lamp state. When a certain output relay of the PLC control system fails to pick up and the indicator lamp is off, the possible cause is output on-time too short, or an output circuit fault; if due to short on-time, the handling measure is to modify the output program; if due to an output circuit fault, replace the output interface circuit. When a certain output relay of the PLC control system fails to pick up and the indicator lamp is on, it may be caused by output relay damage, and the relay needs to be replaced; it may be caused by output wiring break, and the wire needs to be welded or the wiring replaced; it may be caused by output terminal poor contact, and the handling measure is reconnect; it may also be caused by an output drive circuit fault, and the output interface circuit needs to be replaced. Output wiring break is distinct from poor contact and drive circuit fault: the former requires welding the wire or replacing the wiring, poor contact requires reconnect, and drive circuit fault requires replacing the interface circuit. It may also be caused by excessive leakage current of the output drive transistor, and the output transistor needs to be replaced; this situation is distinct from the drive circuit fault or program address duplication fault when the indicator lamp is on. It may also be caused by duplicated port addresses in the output instruction, and the program needs to be modified;

this situation is distinct from the case of failing to turn off but with the indicator lamp off, the latter being mostly relay damage or drive transistor leakage.

At the maintenance operation level, reconnect is used to handle various terminal-type faults: when input terminal loose or input terminal poor contact, the handling method is reconnect; when the POWER lamp is off and the cause is input terminal poor contact, the handling method is reconnect; when all inputs fail to pick up and the cause is terminal contact loose, the handling method is reconnect. Modifying the program is used to solve faults caused by program logic errors, address conflicts or missing instructions: when the RUN lamp is off and the cause is no END instruction in the program, the handling method is to modify the program; when a certain output relay fails to turn off and the indicator lamp is on and the cause is duplicated port addresses in the output instruction, the handling method is to modify the program; when a certain output relay fails to pick up and the indicator lamp is off and the cause is output on-time too short, the handling method is to modify the output program.

The transmission of data and instructions inside the PLC relies on the bus-type structure; once the bus fails, both input relays and output relays may exhibit abnormal actions. On the output side, an I/O bus fault in the CPU is one of the causes of abnormal output relay actions; its manifestation is listed alongside loose "COM" screw, fuse blown and poor terminal connection contact, all of which make the abnormal-action relay numbers show the regularity of units of 8; for an I/O bus fault in the CPU, the corresponding maintenance measure is to replace the CPU module. Terminal connection block poor contact likewise causes abnormal actions with relay numbers in units of 8, and the handling method is reconnect. When the abnormal-action relay numbers are in units of 8, if it is found to be caused by a loose "COM" screw, retighten should be performed; if it is found to be caused by a fuse blown, the fuse should be replaced.

Random output actions are a relatively common fault symptom in the PLC control system; PLC supply voltage too low, poor contact, and input noise too high all cause random output actions. PLC supply voltage too low corresponds to the handling method of adjusting the power supply output, and this step is also one of the preferred troubleshooting measures for handling the random output action problem. Poor contact corresponds to the handling method of checking the terminal wiring. Input noise too high corresponds to the measure of adding shielding or filtering measures; this measure is used both to solve random input actions caused by excessive input signal noise and to solve random output actions caused by excessive output circuit noise. In addition, a loose "COM" screw causes abnormal actions with relay numbers in units of 8, and a fuse blown may also cause random output actions; the former requires retightening, and the latter requires replacing the fuse.

When all outputs fail to pick up, one cause is the power supply fuse blown; at this time, replace the fuse should be performed to restore the circuit; if the cause is output terminal block poor contact, the handling method is reconnect. When a certain output relay fails to pick up and it is caused by output terminal poor contact, reconnect is likewise adopted. A similar situation exists on the input side: when the input relay operates correctly but the indicator lamp is off, it is judged to be LED damage, and the LED likewise needs to be replaced; this step is the direct measure to solve the failure of relay status indication.

One possible cause of the POWER lamp off is the input circuit fuse blown, and the handling method at this time is to replace the fuse; when all inputs fail to pick up and it is caused by terminal contact loose, the handling method is likewise reconnect. Input terminal loose or input terminal poor contact corresponds to reconnect, while input poor contact corresponds to checking the terminal wiring. Input noise too high corresponds to adding shielding or filtering measures. When a loose "COM" screw of the input/output module causes abnormal actions, tightening should be performed. A loose screw also causes the shunt trip unit to fail to trip the circuit breaker, and the corresponding handling method is to tighten the screw.

PLC input-side faults are often first reflected by the indicator light status. When the POWER light is off, the three causes of fuse blown, poor contact of the input terminal, and broken input power supply wiring can be considered in turn; all of them will cause the POWER light to go out. Among them, the treatment corresponding to fuse blown is to replace the fuse, the treatment corresponding to poor contact of the input terminal is to reconnect, and the treatment corresponding to broken input power supply wiring is to replace the wiring. Broken input power supply wiring will also cause the contactor fails to pick up; at this time there is no voltage across the coil, and the circuit must be checked to eliminate the broken wire. The environmental conditions on board are harsh, and wiring heads and terminals are prone to rust, thereby causing poor contact in the PLC input and output circuits; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals will likewise cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance and thereby possibly causing local overheating, phase failure, short circuit between phases and other faults.

Troubleshooting the POWER light being off also involves the link of power supply fault. In a microcomputer monitoring system, a power supply fault of the integrated circuit chip on the circuit board can cause the system to shut down completely with no fault information output.

The RUN light being off is another typical manifestation. For the fault caused by no END instruction in the program, the treatment is to modify the program and add the END instruction; for the RUN light being off caused by power supply fault, the treatment is to check the power supply; for the fault caused by duplicate I/O port addresses, the treatment is to modify the port addresses.

For the phenomenon that none of the inputs can be connected, the fault causes include no power supplied to the input signal source, input signal source power supply voltage too low, loose terminal contact, and poor contact of the terminal board. When no power is supplied to the input signal source, the relevant power supply should be connected; when the input signal source power supply voltage is too low, the power supply voltage should be adjusted to meet the requirements; when the terminal contact is loose, the terminal should be reconnected; when the terminal board has poor contact, it should be treated and then reconnected. Input signal source power supply voltage too low, together with no power supplied to the input signal source and loose terminal contact, constitutes the cause of input failure; it means the power supply voltage of the input signal source is lower than the specified value. Power supply voltage too low also manifests in other situations: in a circuit breaker, power supply voltage too low makes the electromagnetic force generated by the shunt trip unit coil insufficient, and the circuit breaker cannot open; when a DC motor starts, power supply voltage too low makes the starting torque less than the load torque, causing the motor to stall and fail to start.

All PLC inputs abnormal is listed separately among common faults; its root cause is a fault in the PLC input interface circuit, and the treatment is to directly replace the input interface circuit. The input terminal cooperates with the COM terminal to form the interface of the input circuit; the diesel engine unit controller receives fault signals through input terminals of specific numbers, and the overspeed fault signal is input from terminal 10 of the controller to execute immediate shutdown. In addition, loose COM screws, input circuit fault, poor contact (terminal block), broken input wiring, bad load power supply or voltage too low, poor contact of the terminal connection block, etc. are also fault causes on the input side that need to be checked. Among them, input circuit fault and broken input wiring both belong to faults in the input circuit and wiring, and should be checked together with the terminal wiring and circuit continuity during inspection.

Fuse blowing repeatedly is another fault manifestation of the PLC control system. Load short circuit or overload, incorrect input voltage setting, and fuse capacity too small will all cause fuse blowing repeatedly. For load short circuit or overload, a multimeter must be used for measurement and troubleshooting; for incorrect input voltage setting, it should be reconnected correctly; for fuse capacity too small, a larger-capacity fuse should be used. Besides causing fuse blowing repeatedly, load short circuit will also cause welding of the contactor contact; when treating welded contacts, the load short circuit fault must be eliminated first and then the contact replaced. Fuse blown itself is one of the possible causes of the POWER light being off in the PLC system, and also one of the possible causes of none of the PLC outputs being connectable; when the PLC operates abnormally and the relay number is 8 units, the possible cause is likewise fuse blown.

Troubleshooting the above faults cannot be done without a multimeter. A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument; it contains three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, and at full scale the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. Distinguished by display mode, the analog multimeter belongs to multimeters, and the digital multimeter also belongs to multimeters. The MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter; it can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A, and its panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, current, capacitance, diode, transistor, thyristor, photosensitive device, thermocouple, etc. In PLC maintenance, troubleshooting of load short circuit or overload requires measurement with a multimeter, and treatment of fuse blowing repeatedly likewise requires measurement with a multimeter to find the cause.

Fault treatment on the output side also has corresponding steps. When the output is abnormal, the output interface circuit can be replaced, and the output program modified if necessary; where a relay is damaged, the relay should be replaced; where an output tube is damaged, the output tube should be replaced; where the output port circuit is damaged, the output port circuit should be replaced; where wiring is broken or loosely connected, it should be soldered or replaced. When the thermal relay malfunctions, it can be adjusted or repaired. These treatment steps, together with the steps on the input side such as replacing the wiring, reconnecting correctly, using a larger-capacity fuse, modifying the port addresses, connecting the relevant power supply, adjusting the power supply voltage to meet the requirements, and reconnecting after treatment, constitute the specific operations for different fault symptoms in PLC maintenance.

Composition and operating environment of marine motors Marine motors are the core power equipment in the ship's electric drive system, and their scope is relatively wide; divided by function and structure, they include main types such as marine asynchronous motors, marine DC motors and AC single-phase motors. Besides these complete machines, marine motors structurally also include key components such as bearings, windings, commutators, brushes and shafts, and the condition of these components directly determines whether the motor can operate reliably.

The ship environment features high humidity, salt spray, vibration and narrow installation space; marine motors operate under exactly such harsh conditions, and thus special requirements are placed on insulation performance, mechanical structure and electrical performance. China's standards specify that the ambient temperature for marine motors is 45℃, and require them to work normally under an air relative humidity of 95%. To adapt to this environment, the winding insulation must undergo "three-proof" treatment against moisture, mildew and salt-oil mist, and must also have oil resistance.

Supporting relationship of marine transformers Also belonging to the category of marine electrical equipment together with marine motors are marine transformers. Transformers commonly used on ships include three-phase, single-phase and special-purpose types, and their structural forms are mostly dry-type, air-cooled and waterproof. Among them, transformers used to supply loads such as lighting and electric heating are mostly three-phase transformers with relatively large capacity. Marine transformers and marine motors cooperate with each other in the ship's power network to jointly ensure the power supply and drive requirements of various loads.

Daily maintenance items of marine motors The maintenance work of marine motors includes several aspects, which can be summarized as general cleaning, working environment inspection, bearing maintenance, power supply voltage monitoring, armature current monitoring, temperature rise monitoring, running sound listening and commutation spark monitoring.

General cleaning aims to keep the inside and outside of the motor clean and prevent the accumulation of dust, oil dirt and salt spray from affecting heat dissipation and insulation. Working environment inspection focuses on whether there is abnormal dampness, corrosive gas or debris hindering ventilation around the motor. Bearing maintenance regularly deals with the lubrication and wear condition of the bearings to ensure smooth operation of the shaft. Power supply voltage monitoring requires attention to whether the supply voltage is within the allowable range, avoiding damage to the winding caused by abnormal voltage. Armature current monitoring is used to grasp the current magnitude of the armature circuit and prevent overload operation. Temperature rise monitoring judges whether the temperature of each part of the motor exceeds the allowable limit by detecting it. Running sound listening uses hearing to distinguish whether there is abnormal sound during motor operation, so as to discover mechanical or electromagnetic hidden troubles early. Commutation spark monitoring targets the working state of the commutator and brushes of DC motors, observing whether the spark grade is within the normal range.

The above maintenance items are interrelated and together constitute the basic content of daily inspection and repair of marine motors. Marine asynchronous motors, marine DC motors and AC single-phase motors all need to cover these items during maintenance, and the inspection and upkeep of components such as bearings, windings, commutators, brushes and shafts runs through all the monitoring and maintenance work.

Basic requirements for marine motors Marine motors are a class of equipment in ship power equipment that operate under harsh environments such as high marine humidity, salt spray, vibration and narrow space, and have special requirements on insulation, mechanical structure and electrical performance. According to China's standards, the ambient temperature of marine motors is considered as 45℃, and they must maintain normal operation under an air relative humidity of 95%. This humidity condition places requirements on the motor insulation system far higher than those for land products; therefore the winding insulation of marine motors must undergo "three-proof" treatment against moisture, mildew and salt-oil mist, and must also have oil resistance. A winding is the coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, undertaking the function of generating a magnetic field or inducing an electromotive force, and its insulation state directly determines whether the motor can operate at sea for a long time. According to the assessment index of insulation resistance, the cold-state insulation resistance of the marine motor winding should be not less than 5MΩ, and the hot-state insulation resistance should be not less than 2MΩ. Marine motors mostly use class E and class B insulation, with drying temperatures not exceeding 110℃ and 120℃ respectively; if the insulation resistance of the winding is low due to salt content, it needs to be desalinated by washing with high-temperature high-pressure water or boiling in fresh water.

In terms of mechanical structure, marine motors must ensure normal operation under long-term conditions of 15° list, 7.5° trim and 22.5° roll. This inclination and rolling condition places higher requirements on the bearing structure; the bearing, as the mechanical component supporting the rotation of the rotor, has a working state whose reliability directly relates to whether the motor can continue to operate while rolling. Likewise, the brush must not jam in the brush holder under long-term list and rolling; the brush holder, as the device fixing the brush, must have its connecting parts guaranteed not to loosen. Besides the above requirements, marine motors should also be impact-resistant, vibration-resistant and bump-resistant, and be small in size, light in weight and easy to disassemble and assemble. For windlass motors there is an additional special requirement, namely to meet 25 starts within 30min and allow stalling for 1min.

Composition and running monitoring of marine motors This major category of equipment, marine motors, includes varieties such as marine asynchronous motors, marine DC motors and AC single-phase motors. As for a specific marine motor, its composition includes parts such as bearings, windings, commutators, brushes and shafts. Around these parts, the daily maintenance of marine motors involves general cleaning, working environment inspection, bearing maintenance, power supply voltage monitoring, armature current monitoring, temperature rise monitoring, running sound listening and commutation spark monitoring.

When the phenomenon of excessive sparking under brush occurs, it is necessary to check the contact condition between the brush and the commutator, check the condition of the brush holder, check the brush position, and also check the armature vibration condition and the commutator segment condition. If the clearance fit between the brush and the brush holder is too tight, it will cause jamming and cause excessive brush sparking; once the brush holder is loose, the brushes are not arranged in a straight line, which will also affect commutation and increase sparking. When grinding the contact surface between the brush and the commutator, the brush must be placed in the brush holder for the operation. Regarding the bearing, checking the bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition both belong to the scope of bearing maintenance; bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by loud uneven noise and the characteristic of an overheated bearing end cover.
