Poor contact, as a fault state, means that the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation, or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact, increase contact resistance, and then cause local overheating, phase failure, interphase short circuit, and other faults, and may cause random output action, corresponding to the need to check terminal wiring.

Loose brush holder is another common cause of excessive sparking under the brush. The brush holder is the device that fixes the brush; a loose brush holder will cause the brushes to be out of line during motor operation. The greater the brush position deviation, the greater the spark caused; it causes excessive brush sparking by affecting the commutation process. If the brush holder clearance fit is too tight, it will cause brush sticking, and the tightness must be adjusted by grinding the side of the brush. For marine motors under long-term 15° list, 7.5° trim, and 22.5° roll, the brush holder connecting parts must be ensured not to loosen; when grinding the contact surface between the brush and the commutator, the brush must be placed in the brush holder for the operation; when checking the contact surface of a motor in operation, the brush can be taken out of the brush holder for observation.

Armature vibration can also cause excessive sparking under the brush. Armature vibration is generated because the uneven gap between the armature and each magnetic pole causes an uneven magnetic field, resulting in different voltages in the branches of the armature winding and producing equalizing currents that cause excessive brush sparking. Causes of uneven gap include improper installation of magnetic poles (such as missing or loose shims), bearing wear or damage, and failure to align the motor and load axes; in addition, poor armature balance, incorrect fan blade installation, or movement of balance weights may also cause armature vibration.

Short circuit between commutator segments is one of the causes of excessive sparking under the brush. Brush powder or commutator copper powder filling the grooves will cause short circuit between commutator segments; falling off or mildew corrosion of the insulating mica between commutator segments will cause short circuit between segments; burrs formed by undercutting the commutator during maintenance and not being smoothed in time will also cause short circuit between segments. The commutator should be maintained frequently, and the commutator segments should be kept clean and smooth to prevent this fault. The commutator is the rotating sliding contact component used for current lead-in and lead-out in DC motors and wound-rotor motors, and it is composed of commutator segments; a dirty commutator surface or brush sticking will cause poor contact between brush and commutator and produce sparks; desoldering between the armature winding and the commutator can be judged by measuring the resistance between adjacent commutator segments. Graphite brushes are soft and easily damage the commutator, and are suitable for motors with general commutation conditions and uniform load; when disassembling a DC motor, prevent damage to the winding ends, commutator, or slip rings.

The brush position not being on the neutral line can also cause excessive sparking under the brush. This fault is caused by moving the brush holder during repair or by loose brush holder bolts, which makes the brush position deviate from the neutral line; the brush deviating from the neutral line makes the commutation process not occur on the zero-potential element, thereby producing excessive sparks. There are two adjustment methods: the induction method is to connect a millivoltmeter to adjacent brushes when stationary, and press the excitation button until the pointer stops, at which point it is the neutral line; the trial-run method is to use separate excitation, and when the speeds in both directions are equal, the brush position is on the neutral line.

Bearing wear or damage will cause an uneven gap between the armature and each magnetic pole, causing excessive brush sparking; it is also one of the main causes of large armature vibration in DC motors. Bearing wear manifests as excessive bearing clearance or surface damage, causing vibration, overheating, and performance degradation of the motor or mechanical components; when rolling bearing wear causes excessive clearance, it manifests as loud rotational noise, wobbling of the outer ring, or impact noise between the balls and the outer ring. For rolling bearings with an inner diameter of 20~59mm, the allowable wear value is about 10 times the original clearance; the clearance of a new bearing is 0.01~0.02mm, and the maximum allowable wear value can reach
0.15~
0.25mm. As a mechanical component of the motor, the bearing is used to support rotor rotation; its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration, and abnormal noise, and it is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and overheating of the bearing end cover. For bearing maintenance, on the one hand, check the bearing fault itself; this step takes the bearing as the object and checks whether its surface damage and fit clearance exceed the standard; on the other hand, check the lubrication condition, also taking the bearing as the object, to confirm whether its lubrication state is normal.

For excessive sparking under the brush, a series of inspection steps need to be carried out. When the contact surface between the brush and the commutator is less than 70%, it is necessary to check the contact condition between the brush and the commutator; the inspection content includes the cleanliness of the commutator surface and whether the brush spring pressure is too small. If the brush is found to be sticking in the brush holder, the clearance fit should be adjusted by grinding the side; this inspection is intended to solve the problem of difficult commutation of DC motors caused by poor contact, and the commutator and brush are needed during inspection, and power supply voltage monitoring must be noted. Checking the brush holder condition is used to eliminate the faults of poor commutation and excessive sparking caused by brushes not being arranged in a straight line; the brush is needed during inspection. Checking the armature vibration condition requires troubleshooting uneven gaps caused by improper installation of magnetic poles (such as missing or loose shims), troubleshooting armature vibration caused by bearing wear or damage, and troubleshooting vibration caused by failure to align the motor and load axes. Checking the commutator segment condition requires the use of the commutator. When checking the brush position, the greater the brush position deviation, the greater the spark generated by the DC motor; a loose brush holder causes the brushes to be out of line, affecting commutation and causing sparks; after commutation sparks appear during no-load operation of a DC motor, this inspection step should be carried out, and during inspection it is necessary to confirm whether the brush jumps and its contact condition with the commutator, and to note armature current monitoring. In addition, excessive sparking under the brush also corresponds to checking the power supply voltage; for faults such as slow starting of an electric fan, motor failure to start, or excessive temperature rise, it is necessary to verify whether the supply voltage is within the allowable range; when an electric fan starts slowly and its speed decreases, the power supply voltage should be checked to eliminate the undervoltage fault; when a traction motor fails to start due to undervoltage, the power supply voltage needs to be checked and appropriately increased.

During inspection, voltage, current, and resistance are three basic measurable properties. A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, and current, while a clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

A winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force. Partial short circuit or phase failure of a winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating in AC motors. The winding insulation of marine motors must undergo "three-proof" treatment against moisture, mildew, and salt-oil mist and be oil-resistant. A coil is a component of marine electrical equipment, made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a contactor contains a coil, and a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and their relative position accuracy needs to be checked.

For DC generators, the possible causes of a DC generator failing to build up voltage include absence of residual magnetism, the excitation winding being connected in reverse after repair, open-circuit faults in the excitation winding and the voltage regulator, and the generator rotating in the opposite direction; these all belong to the fault symptom in which a self-excited DC generator fails to build up voltage due to residual magnetism, wiring, or direction of rotation. Low voltage of a DC generator is related to the commutating-pole coil being connected in reverse; the commutating-pole coil being connected in reverse causes loss of the commutation-improving effect, making commutation more difficult during operation and producing larger sparks under the brush; the polarity of the commutating pole can be judged by a small magnetic needle test, and the polarity of the generator commutating pole is the same as that of the preceding main pole in the direction of rotation; the faults of voltage build-up and low voltage of the generator involve improper compensation of the commutating-pole magnetic field, and a commutating-pole magnetic field that is too strong or too weak will both produce sparks, affecting the operation of the DC generator.

When a DC motor fails to start, if the supply voltage is too low, the starting torque will be less than the load torque, and the motor will therefore stall and fail to start. This phenomenon overlaps in cause with the fault symptom of failure to start: the power supply not being connected, incorrect wiring of the control equipment, undervoltage, short circuit to earth between phases of the stator winding, incorrect wiring, stator winding short circuit, as well as excessive load or the brake not being released and a fault in the reducer, will all cause failure to start. For failure to start, the switch, fuse, and each pair of contacts should be checked to find the fault point; the wiring diagram should be checked and corrected; the supply voltage should be checked and, if indeed too low, appropriately raised; the short-circuit and open-circuit locations should be found and repaired, and if the wiring is incorrect, the wiring should be corrected; the load should be reduced and the motor separated from the reducer, and if the motor can run normally, the reducer should be checked. The causes of failure to start of the motor matched with a self-excited DC generator include no power supply, low voltage, brush sticking, and open excitation circuit; the main causes of failure to start of a DC motor are absence of power supply, low voltage, brush sticking, and open excitation circuit. From the perspective of the fault tree, power supply problems, mechanical problems, excessive load, and motor internal fault will all cause the motor to fail to start, and motor fails to start is often selected as the top event of fault tree analysis, whose analysis boundary conditions are usually set as the power supply being normal and the control circuit being normal.

One of the main causes of low speed of a DC motor is that the applied supply voltage is lower than the rated value; the applied supply voltage being lower than the rated value is one of the causes of motor speed low. The brush not being on the neutral line will cause the motor speed to decrease; short circuit or earthing of the armature winding is a fault cause of motor speed low. In contrast to low speed, when the motor speed is high, according to the electromotive force balance equation, at the applied rated voltage the main cause is a decrease in effective magnetic flux. An increase in the resistance of the excitation circuit is one of the causes of the decrease in effective magnetic flux and hence high speed; a separately excited motor under light-load starting conditions may cause a decrease in effective magnetic flux and high speed; reverse connection of the series winding of a cumulative compound motor will cause a decrease in effective magnetic flux and high speed; an open circuit in one branch of the shunt excitation winding will cause a decrease in effective magnetic flux and hence high speed. The brush position not being on the neutral line will cause excessive commutation sparking and must be adjusted by the induction method or the trial-rotation method; the brush position not being on the neutral line will cause excessive sparking in the DC machine. Armature vibration is caused by uneven gap due to improper mounting of the magnetic poles (such as loss or loosening of shims), by uneven gap due to bearing wear or damage, by uneven gap due to the axes of the motor and the load not being aligned, and may also be caused by the armature balance not being properly calibrated, the fan blade being installed incorrectly, or the balance weight having moved.

The fault symptom of large armature vibration has causes including the armature balance not being properly calibrated, bearing wear or damage, the fan blade being installed in the wrong position or the balance weight having moved during repair, mutual rubbing between stator and rotor, loosening of the foot screws, and uneven armature gap. Bearing wear causes an uneven gap between the armature and the magnetic poles, inducing equalizing currents and brush sparks. For bearings with an inner diameter of 20–59 mm, the allowable wear value is about 10 times the original clearance, up to a maximum of 0.15–0.25 mm;

AC single-phase motors occupy a certain position among marine motors, and their common types include the power machines used in electric fans, electric drills, refrigerators, and washing machines. Such motors are particularly common on small and old ships, because such ships often do not have a central air-conditioning system and the number of electric fans used is correspondingly large; the cabin of each senior crew member on board is usually also equipped with a refrigerator, whose power machine is likewise mostly an AC single-phase motor. As far as the refrigerator is concerned, its faults are mainly divided into three categories: motor, electrical control circuit, and refrigeration system; frost-free refrigerators are also provided with a cold-air circulation fan and an air-door adjusting knob. The faults of a washing machine can be divided into three categories: motor fault, electrical control circuit fault, and mechanical fault; failure to work after power-on may be caused by poor contact of contacts of the timer or slipping of the knob; slow rotation of the pulsator and poor washing may be caused by a decrease in capacitance or deterioration of the capacitor; the pulsator rotating intermittently is mainly caused by a timer fault; the pulsator of a套-cylinder washing machine failing to reverse may be caused by damage to the clutch torsion spring. When an electric drill fails to start, the possible causes include no voltage at the power supply, a damaged switch, or poor contact of the brush; if the brush holder insulation is cracked and, being damp, breaks down to earth, the brush holder must be remade. The possible causes of an electric drill rotating too slowly include low supply voltage, too little lubricating grease in the gearbox, or worn meshing gears; if the connection between the rotor winding and the commutator segment is loose, it must be checked with a multimeter and soldered firmly. The possible causes of abnormal operating sound of an electric drill include damaged meshing gears, insufficient lubricating grease, or bearing wear.

Slow starting and reduced speed of an electric fan is a relatively typical fault symptom in the maintenance of AC single-phase motors, and it has many possible causes. Low supply voltage will cause the electric fan to start slowly and its speed to decrease, and at this time the supply voltage should be checked; incorrect wiring of the main and auxiliary windings will also cause this phenomenon, and the wiring must be corrected; desoldering of the shading coil group is likewise one of the possible causes, and the shading coil should be re-soldered. Insufficient capacitance will cause the electric fan to start slowly and its speed to decrease, and the corresponding remedy is to replace the capacitor with one of the same specification. Sinking of the ceiling fan rotor will cause the electric fan to start slowly and its speed to decrease, and it must be reassembled to eliminate this. Drying and hardening of the bearing lubricating grease, wear, or excessive load caused by deformation of the fan blade with too large a twist angle can also cause this fault, and the bearing should be cleaned or replaced. Inter-turn short circuit of the winding, specifically inter-turn short circuit of the main winding, is one of the causes of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan, and the corresponding repair method is to rewind the winding, that is, to restore its performance by repairing the main winding. Taken together, the repair methods for this fault include checking the voltage, correcting the wiring, re-soldering the shading coil, and replacing the capacitor, and it is also necessary to reassemble to eliminate rotor sinking and to clean or replace the bearing to restore performance.

The capacitor is an important component of an AC single-phase motor, and the electric fan contains a capacitor. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material; its characteristic is that it blocks direct current and passes alternating current; in circuits it is generally denoted by the letter C plus a number, for example C25 denotes the capacitor numbered 25. The obstructive effect of a capacitor on an AC signal is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC). Its types include electrolytic capacitors, ceramic capacitors, chip capacitors, monolithic capacitors, tantalum capacitors, and polyester capacitors, and its units include the farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF), and picofarad (pF). The measurable properties of a capacitor include earth leakage, capacitance, and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. When marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, the capacitor must be tested according to the capacitor inspection procedure; a capacitor will develop a capacitor fault, and a capacitor fault belongs to the component category of the capacitor. Insufficient capacitance of the capacitor is one of the possible causes of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan; in the context of AC single-phase motor maintenance, it often refers to insufficient capacitance of the running capacitor, and the corresponding repair method is to replace the capacitor with one of the same specification. A multimeter can be used when measuring capacitance, and a multimeter can likewise be used when measuring voltage, or a voltmeter can be used.

Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting; motor fails to start, motor speed low after starting, high temperature rise of the motor, and excessive sparking under brush all correspond to the troubleshooting step of checking the supply voltage. When carrying out check the power supply voltage, note that the circuit terminals should be marked before disconnection. A power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply. When the electric fan starts slowly, the repair methods include checking whether the supply voltage is too low; when the electric drill fails to start and there is no voltage at the power supply, the power supply line should be checked; when the washing machine does not work after power-on, it is necessary to check whether the power supply lead is live and whether the plug and socket are intact. It will cause the electric drill to rotate too slowly, and the supply voltage must be checked and adjusted; when it is lower than 15% of the rated voltage, it will cause the refrigerator motor not to start and to make no sound after power-on, and will also cause the refrigerator motor to make a sound but fail to start after power-on, the latter requiring the installation of an AC voltage stabilizer.

The shading coil is a component of marine electrical equipment, mounted on the pole face of the core of an AC electromagnet; it is a copper ring-shaped component used to eliminate vibration noise of the armature; breakage or detachment of the shading coil will cause the AC electromagnet to produce relatively loud noise, and when the shading coil is damaged it can be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil can be directly replaced. In an electric fan, desoldering of the shading coil group is one of the possible causes of slow starting and reduced speed.

The bearing is a component included in the marine motor, used to support the rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause the motor to overheat and to have abnormal vibration and noise. Bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in an AC electric drive system and belongs to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and the feature of overheating of the bearing end cover. Wear of a rolling bearing causes an excessive clearance, manifested as loud rotation noise, wobbling of the outer ring, or the sound of balls striking the outer ring; for rolling bearings with an inner diameter of 20–59 mm, the allowable wear value is about 10 times the original clearance; the clearance of a new bearing is 0.01–0.02 mm, and the maximum allowable wear value can reach
0.15–
0.25 mm. Bearing wear of an electric fan will cause slow starting, reduced speed, and sinking of the rotor, and the bearing must be cleaned or replaced; bearing wear of an electric drill may cause failure to start, abnormal operating sound, or overheating. Checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition both need to be carried out on the bearing. Replacing the bearing is used to repair the slow starting and reduced speed of an electric fan caused by bearing wear, to eliminate the noise produced during operation of an electric fan due to bearing damage, to solve the failure to start of an electric fan caused by bearing damage, and also to repair the failure to start of an electric drill caused by bearing wear; when dealing with bearing wear of an electric drill, an appropriate amount of good-quality lubricating grease must be added at the same time.

The electric fan includes a capacitor, fan blade, timer, and speed control switch. Deformation of the fan blade with too large a twist angle will cause the load of the electric fan to increase, making it operate in an overloaded state, and is one of the possible causes of the fault of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan. When correcting the fan blade, for a ceiling fan the blades can be removed and overlapped for comparison and correction; for a desk fan, repeated correction should be made according to the deformation condition; the objects of correction include the highest and lowest points and the twist angle of the fan blade; when the deformation is severe, the fan blade must be replaced if necessary rather than merely corrected; this step is used to solve the slow-starting fault caused by increased load due to fan blade deformation. When the electric fan has noise during operation, it may be due to foreign matter in the air gap between stator and rotor or loosening of the silicon steel sheets of the speed-regulating reactor; when it sometimes rotates and sometimes does not, it may be caused by an open circuit in the shading winding of a shaded-pole motor or soft breakdown of the capacitor; when the oscillating mechanism does not work properly, it may be because the clutch tooth on the clutch cannot slide down along the meshing shaft to mesh with the lower clutch tooth; when it fails to start, if the stator winding in the slot is broken, the winding should be removed and replaced rather than merely soldering the lead.

AC single-phase motors often appear in the form of electric fans on ships, and are used in large quantities in small or aging ships, as a supplement to or replacement for central air-conditioning systems. Electric fans belong to the power load equipment of AC single-phase motors, and are used for ship ventilation and cooling; their common faults include slow starting, noise and heating. Marine electrical equipment generally uses capacitors, and a multimeter is used to test capacitors; the capacitor testing procedure applies to capacitors. In an electric fan, if starting is slow and the speed decreases, it may be due to insufficient capacitance, and a capacitor of the same specification needs to be replaced.

The fault symptom that an electric fan sometimes rotates and sometimes does not may be caused by various reasons. The fault cause of poor line contact is specifically manifested as poor contact of the fan speed control switch causing it to sometimes rotate and sometimes not; the existence of a desoldered point in the connecting wire is a manifestation of poor line contact. For the fault of poor switch contact, the treatment method is to repair or replace the switch; for poor contact caused by desoldering of the connecting wire, the desoldered point needs to be found and resoldered. Unstable power supply voltage is also a related cause of the fan sometimes rotating and sometimes not; checking the stability of the power supply voltage and checking the line contact condition are the corresponding troubleshooting steps. Poor contact will cause random output actions, and correspondingly check the terminal wiring. Poor contact, as a cause of equipment failure, refers to a fault state in which the contact resistance increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter at an electrical connection; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance; poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults. When the fan is running, it emits abnormal sound, caused by mechanical friction, loose parts or deformation. Bearing damage refers to the failure of bearing components, often leading to excessive temperature rise, noise and vibration, and starting difficulty; in the fault tree of motor temperature rise, bearing damage is classified as one of the specific causes under the mechanical fault branch. Bearing damage will cause the speed to be low during load operation, will cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and will also cause bearing overheating. When the traction motor has abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, bearing damage is a possible cause, and the damaged bearing needs to be replaced. Marine motors include bearings, windings and shafts. A winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of AC motors; the winding insulation of marine motors must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proof, mildew-proof and salt-oil-mist-proof, and be oil-resistant. The shaft is a mechanical transmission component used to transmit torque and rotational motion, commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments; the movable parts of the two units of an electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a shaft and a panel, assembled by bolts. When measuring the insulation resistance of a coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the iron core; in a through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor to be measured is directly linked with the iron core to replace the primary winding.

The fault symptom of fan heating may be caused by rubbing between the motor stator and rotor; partial winding short circuit will also cause fan heating; lack of oil or inflexible oscillating mechanism will likewise cause fan heating. When heating is due to stator-rotor rubbing, the shaft bearing needs to be checked and the air gap ensured to be uniform; when heating is due to winding short circuit, the treatment method is to rewind the winding; when heating is due to lack of oil or inflexible oscillation, the oil should be cleaned and replaced or the oscillating mechanism repaired. Lack of oil will cause moving parts jammed; lack of oil is a common cause of jamming of the piston of the fuel cutoff cylinder of the main engine remote control system. Fan heating is manifested as an abnormal rise in body temperature. Bearing damage is a possible mechanical cause, and the treatment method is to replace the bearing; damage to the speed control switch is also one of the possible causes of failure to start of the electric fan.

For the above faults, the maintenance involves steps such as replacing the capacitor, replacing the bearing, replacing the switch and inspection and repair. Replacing the capacitor is used to repair the sometimes-rotating-sometimes-not fault of a capacitor-type electric fan caused by soft breakdown of the capacitor, is also used to solve the problem of slow speed of a pulsator washing machine caused by reduced capacitance, deterioration or loose wiring of the capacitor, is used to handle abnormal operation of a spin-dry motor caused by capacitor damage, is used to repair the fault of no start and no sound after power-on of a refrigerator motor caused by damage to the starting capacitor, and is also used to eliminate the fault caused by short circuit of the resonance capacitor in the failure of generator voltage to build up normally. Replacing the switch is used to repair the fault of a fan sometimes rotating and sometimes not caused by poor contact of the speed control switch, is used to repair the failure to start of an electric drill caused by poor contact or damage of the hand-pressed switch, and in electric drill maintenance, if the switch is damaged, the replacement operation is performed to eliminate the starting obstacle. Inspection and repair is suitable for the post-disassembly treatment of a fan when the oscillating parts fit too tightly or the shading coil winding is open, is also used to solve the automatic tripping fault caused by the free tripping mechanism of the main switch failing to hold, and is a necessary measure when severe heating and three-phase current imbalance are caused by inter-turn short circuit of the transformer winding; the main switch easily tripping automatically due to hull vibration corresponds to inspection and repair. In addition, when the timer fails, the treatment method is to replace the timer; in troubleshooting the washing machine not working after power-on, it is necessary to check whether the timer wiring is loose or disconnected, whether the timer knob slips, and whether the contacts are in good contact; the main cause of the pulsator of the washing machine rotating and stopping intermittently is timer failure, and the pulsator failing to reverse may be caused by partial damage of the timer; possible causes of washing machine earth leakage include dampness of the timer or program switch, and the maintenance method can use a hair dryer to dry it. As a digital logic circuit application component used in household appliances, the timer is often used in ship living equipment to control fan start/stop, washing machine washing and spin-dry programs, and cold storage defrosting cycles; in the cold storage defrosting control system, the defrosting timer DT₁ is used to control the automatic changeover of the defrosting cycle, and when the defrosting time ends, its two sets of switches automatically return to the non-defrosting state; when the cold storage selector switch is placed in the "REF" position for manual refrigeration, the defrosting timer motor is cut off, so that defrosting heating does not work. The speed control switch is used to adjust the fan speed or the active power distribution of parallel generator sets; in the ship power station, this switch is manually operated to adjust the servo motor of the diesel engine governor, and adjusting this switch can change the diesel engine throttle opening, thereby realizing active power distribution among parallel operating units. Different inclination angles of the fan blades will cause vibration and noise during fan operation; ceiling fan blade faults can be corrected by removing the blades and overlapping them for comparison to correct the highest and lowest points and the twist angle; table fan blades should be repeatedly corrected according to the deformation, and the blades should be directly replaced if necessary; noise caused by blade problems requires inspection and correction of the blades, and replacement if necessary. If the fan blade of the electric drill does not fit tightly with the shaft, abnormal operating sound will result, and copper sheet needs to be wrapped around the shaft so that it fits tightly on the shaft.

In marine electrical equipment, capacitors are relatively commonly used components; marine electrical equipment uses capacitors to achieve the function of blocking direct current and passing alternating current. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle; in circuit diagrams it is generally represented by the letter C plus a number, for example C25 means capacitor number 25. The capacitor testing procedure applies to capacitors; during testing, a multimeter can be used to measure the capacitor, and by using the capacitance function of the multimeter, it is possible to judge whether its leakage, capacitance and electrolytic capacitor polarity are normal. Capacitors will have capacitor faults, and capacitor faults belong to the problems under the component category of capacitor. It may also be caused by the ceiling fan rotor sinking or desoldering of the shading coil set. Insufficient capacitor capacitance is a type of fault cause of abnormal starting of the fan, manifested as slow starting and reduced speed, and the treatment is to replace the capacitor with one of the same specification.

The fault symptom that the motor can only start after being given a push may be caused by an open circuit in the motor auxiliary winding, or by short circuit, open circuit or poor contact of the capacitor. For an open-circuit starting winding, the maintenance method is to find the break point and reconnect it or replace the winding, that is, restore by repairing the starting winding; for capacitor faults, the maintenance method is to check the capacitor and replace the damaged part with one of the same specification. An open-circuit starting winding will cause an open circuit in the motor auxiliary winding, thereby making the motor require a push to start.

Abnormal operation of the fan oscillating mechanism is another common fault symptom. This phenomenon may be caused by looseness or damage of the steel wire pull cable, and the cable needs to be fixed securely or replaced with one of the same specification. Failure of the clutch-type oscillating mechanism is often due to insufficient spring force of the upper clutch tooth compression spring or burrs on the meshing shaft pin; clutch failure causes torque to fail to be transmitted to the crank, and the burrs need to be filed off and lubricating grease added or the spring replaced. Failure of the sliding-plate-type oscillating mechanism may be due to the catch rod slipping at the recess of the oscillating disk, causing the oscillating disk to fail to position well; this can be repaired by adjusting the position of the steel wire pull cable so that the catch rod engages tightly with the recess of the oscillating disk. Severe wear or poor meshing of the helical gear will cause abnormal oscillation, and the helical gear needs to be replaced. Looseness of oscillating mechanism parts covers various situations: loosening of the screws on the gearbox cover causes displacement of the cover plate, resulting in poor meshing of the helical gear; the retaining ring connecting the oscillating connecting rod and the crank falls off or the connecting rod is too loose; in the clutch-type mechanism, the spring force of the upper clutch tooth compression spring is insufficient; in the sliding-plate-type mechanism, the catch rod slips at the recess of the oscillating disk, causing positioning failure; looseness or damage of the steel wire pull cable affects the operation of the oscillating mechanism. Lack of oil in the oscillating mechanism will likewise affect its normal operation.

For the above mechanical faults, tightening the oscillating mechanism parts is the main maintenance procedure. If there are burrs on the meshing shaft pin, the burrs should be filed off and a little lubricating grease added to repair the clutch mechanism; this operation also falls within the scope of adding oil to the oscillating mechanism. When the sliding-plate-type mechanism fails due to slipping of the catch rod, the steel wire pull cable should be adjusted so that the catch rod engages tightly with the recess. When loosening of the gearbox cover screws causes displacement of the cover plate, the cover plate screws should be tightened to restore gear meshing. When the retaining ring falls off, a new retaining ring needs to be replaced; when the connecting rod is too loose, washers should be appropriately added.

In terms of electrical connections, poor contact is one of the causes of equipment failure; looseness, oxidation or foreign matter at an electrical connection will cause an increase in contact resistance. Poor contact of the input terminal corresponds to reconnection; looseness of the terminal contact corresponds to reconnection; looseness of the input terminal or poor contact of the input terminal corresponds to reconnection; poor contact (terminal block) corresponds to reconnection; poor contact of the output terminal corresponds to reconnection; poor contact of the terminal connecting bar likewise corresponds to reconnection. Reconnection is one of the maintenance procedures of the PLC control system, used for rewiring operations to handle terminal poor contact, looseness or disconnection faults; for the fault of looseness or poor contact of the input terminal, the treatment method is reconnection; for the situation where poor contact of the output terminal block causes all outputs to fail to connect, the treatment method is also reconnection.

AC single-phase motors are often used on ships as the power source for equipment such as electric drills, electric fans and refrigerators, among which the fault diagnosis and maintenance of electric drills occupy a relatively large proportion. The electric drill fails to start is one of the common fault symptoms, and its possible causes involve multiple aspects such as the power supply, switch, brush, winding and mechanical transmission. No voltage at the power supply or an open power supply line will directly cause the electric drill to fail to start; at this time the power supply line should be checked to eliminate the power supply problem. Poor contact or damage of the hand-pressed switch will likewise cause the electric drill to fail to start; for this situation the switch replacement operation should be performed. Severe brush wear, insufficient spring pressure or a dirty commutator will all cause poor contact between brush and commutator, thereby causing the electric drill to fail to start; if poor contact is caused by brush wear, the brush should be directly replaced; if the brush wire is loose, the brush needs to be repaired or replaced.

An open circuit in the armature winding or stator winding is one of the common causes of failure to start of the electric drill; for an open-circuit stator winding, it is necessary to check and determine whether to repair or rewind.

Too slow speed of the electric drill is another common fault symptom. Too little lubricating grease in the gearbox will cause the electric drill speed to be too slow. Wear of the meshing gears is a mechanical fault cause of too slow speed of the electric drill; for wear of the meshing gears, the worn gears should be replaced, and this operation is gear replacement. Excessive pressure of the brush spring may cause the electric drill speed to be too slow. The brush not being on the neutral line will also cause the electric drill speed to be too slow. Damage to the meshing gears will cause abnormal sound during operation of the electric drill, and the damaged gears need to be replaced. When the electric drill has large sparks during operation and this is caused by poor contact between brush and commutator, the brush needs to be ground or replaced. An uneven or unclean commutator surface needs to be cleaned and re-treated.

In the maintenance process of the electric drill, the multimeter is a commonly used testing instrument. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, and is divided into analog and digital types; the analog multimeter belongs to the multimeter, the digital multimeter likewise belongs to the multimeter, and the MF-47 multimeter also belongs to the multimeter; it can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and the panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The multimeter includes three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; at full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. Using the resistance measurement function of the multimeter, the continuity and resistance of windings can be checked; using the voltage measurement function, the power supply voltage and the potentials at various points can be checked; using the current measurement function, whether the loop current is normal can be judged; using the capacitance measurement function, the capacitor capacitance can be checked; using the diode measurement function, the polarity and quality of a diode can be judged; using the transistor measurement function, the amplification capability of a transistor can be checked; using the thyristor measurement function, the trigger and conduction state of a thyristor can be judged; using the photosensitive device measurement function, the light response of a photosensitive element can be checked; using the thermocouple measurement function, the thermoelectric potential corresponding to temperature can be measured. In an electric fan, it causes slow starting and reduced speed; checking the bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition both take the bearing as the object. The commutator is a rotating sliding contact component used for current introduction and extraction in DC motors and wound-rotor motors, composed of commutator segments; graphite brushes are soft in texture and easily damage the commutator, and are suitable for motors with general commutation conditions and uniform load; when disassembling a DC motor, care should be taken to prevent damage to the winding ends, commutator or slip rings. The brush is an important conductive component used for introducing or extracting current between the stationary part and the sliding part of a motor; DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators all need to be equipped with brushes. Checking the contact condition between brush and commutator takes the commutator and brush as the object; checking the brush holder condition takes the brush as the object; checking the commutator segment condition takes the commutator as the object; checking the brush position takes the brush as the object. For brushed motors, excessive brush wear is one of the common faults, on a par with stator winding open circuit and short circuit; during daily maintenance of DC motors, a hand blower or hair dryer should be used to remove brush powder and dust near the winding ends and the commutator; after replacing the brush, if the contact area is less than 70%, the contact surface between the brush and the commutator must be ground; when grinding a newly replaced brush, the brush must be placed in the brush holder, and 00# abrasive cloth wrapped around the commutator surface and pulled back and forth. Reduction gears are also used in marine radar equipment; the antenna base includes a reduction gearbox structure, and the antenna base needs to be painted once every six months to prevent corrosion.

AC single-phase motors are often used on ships as the power source for equipment such as electric fans, refrigerators and electric drills, among which the electric drill is a hand-held electric tool, and its operating condition is directly related to work efficiency and operational safety. The common faults of the electric drill can be summarized into several categories: failure to start, too slow speed, abnormal sound during operation, large sparks between brush and commutator, and electric drill overheating; in addition, there is also the special phenomenon that the electric drill cannot start at a certain position. These fault symptoms are often caused by multiple reasons, and each item should be checked one by one during maintenance. Damage to the reduction gears will likewise cause the electric drill to fail to start; at this time the damaged gears should be replaced, that is, the maintenance procedure of gear replacement should be performed. When the electric drill fails to start due to brush wear, the maintenance method is to replace the brush; if the brush wire is loose, the brush should be repaired or replaced to eliminate the fault.

The phenomenon that an electric drill fails to start at a certain position likewise requires troubleshooting in combination with the above electrical and mechanical factors. The failure-to-start fault of an electric drill caused by bearing wear is likewise solved by replacing the bearing, and after replacement an appropriate amount of good-performance grease must be added. For damage to the meshing gears, the maintenance method is to replace the damaged gears; this operation is gear replacement, applicable to the case where the electric drill makes an abnormal noise during operation and the cause is damage to the meshing gears, and the specific operation is to replace the already-damaged gears; for insufficient or unclean grease, the gearbox should be cleaned and filled with sufficient good-performance grease; for bearing wear, the bearing must be replaced and an appropriate amount of good-performance grease added; for the heating fault of an electric fan, the shaft and bearing must be checked, symmetrical repair or replacement carried out, and attention paid to the uniformity of the air gap.

When the sparking between brush and commutator is relatively large, possible causes include the brush not being on the neutral line, short circuit or poor contact of the stator and rotor windings, and poor contact between brush and commutator. Poor contact between brush and commutator will lead to excessive sparking under brush, and its causes include the commutator surface being too dirty, the brush spring being too weak, or brush sticking. For the brush not being on the neutral line, the maintenance method is to correct the brush position; for short circuit or poor contact of the stator and rotor windings, the fault point must be checked and repair or rewinding determined; for poor contact between brush and commutator, the maintenance method is to adjust the brush pressure and to grind or replace the brush. When checking the contact condition between brush and commutator, the commutator and brush must be used together; when checking the condition of the brush holder, the brush is used; when checking the condition of the commutator segments, the commutator is used; when checking the brush position, the brush is used. If the commutator surface is uneven or unclean, it must be cleaned and re-treated. When adjusting the brush, mark with paint before disassembling the brush rocker seat of the DC motor, so as to adjust the brush position quickly and accurately.

When an electric drill overheats, overload of the electric drill, bearing heating, heating of the gearbox exterior surface, and heating of the stator and rotor windings may all be possible causes of the overheating. For overheating caused by overload of the electric drill, the maintenance method is to reduce the load; for overheating caused by bearing heating, the fault of poor mechanical assembly must be eliminated and the bearing cleaned and oil changed. When checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition, the bearing must be used. Bearing overheating of a generator corresponds to the maintenance procedure of replacing the bearing, used to eliminate the case of severe bearing wear in the generator bearing overheating fault, and also used to repair the overheating fault caused by bearing damage of a motor. Poor ventilation and open circuit of the armature winding are also possible fault causes of an electric drill, and the corresponding maintenance procedures include grinding the commutator, improving ventilation, repairing the stator winding and repairing the armature winding.

AC single-phase motors are widely used in marine equipment, and appliances such as washing machines, electric fans, refrigerators and electric drills mostly use this type of motor as the prime mover. As far as the washing machine is concerned, its faults can be classified into three categories: motor faults, electrical control circuit faults and mechanical faults, and when troubleshooting one should first distinguish which category the fault belongs to, then check item by item.

When the washing machine does not work after being energized, possible causes include an open circuit in the power supply, low voltage, timer fault, poor contact of the program switch or damage to the capacitor, and mechanical causes cover blockage at the bottom of the impeller, excessive or tangled clothing, damage to the transmission pulley or belt, and jamming of the main shaft. During maintenance, the power supply lead, plug and socket, and fuse condition must be checked, and electrical path faults eliminated one by one, that is, check whether the power supply lead is live and whether the plug and socket are intact, and check whether the fuse has blown.

Slipping of the timer knob is mostly caused by a loose positioning pin, which can be repaired by bonding with 502 glue; when the contacts of the program selection switch have poor contact of contacts, they should be polished with fine sandpaper and the metal parts serviced; if the break point of the motor winding is external it can be reconnected, and if the damage is internal the winding must be replaced. Poor contact of contacts of the timer will cause the washing machine not to work after being energized, and the timer must be serviced or replaced. Damage to the capacitor will cause the whole machine not to work after being energized, and when dealing with the washing motor fault of a washing machine the capacitor of the same specification must be replaced. A transmission belt that is too loose, slipping or fallen off will also cause no operation after being energized, and the maintenance method is to adjust the transmission belt or replace it with a new one. Debris blocking the clearance at the bottom of the impeller, or excessive or tangled laundry wrapping the impeller, will likewise cause no operation after being energized. When the supply voltage is low, the maintenance method is to install an AC voltage stabilizer.

For the fault symptom of slow impeller speed and unclean washing, mechanical causes include loose connection between the impeller and the shaft and a transmission belt that is too loose or slipping, electrical causes involve reduced capacitance or deterioration of the capacitor and local short circuit of the motor winding, and low supply voltage or open circuit of the motor rotor cage bars can also cause this fault; loosening of the small pulley fastening screw and timer fault are potential causes, and too much laundry or laundry wrapping the impeller are non-equipment fault causes. Maintenance methods include tightening the fixing screws and adjusting or replacing the transmission belt or capacitor. When slow speed is caused by a loose connection between the impeller and the shaft, the fixing screw should be tightened; when slow impeller speed is caused by loosening of the small pulley fastening screw, it should be repaired by tightening the screw. Slow impeller speed with unclean washing may be caused by reduced capacitance or deterioration of the capacitor, and a capacitor of the same specification must be replaced; the main cause of the impeller turning intermittently is timer fault, and the maintenance method refers to the treatment of the no-operation-after-energization fault; when the washing machine vibrates and is noisy during operation, one cause is friction between the impeller and the washing tub, and loose fastening screws at the pulley, base plate and other places must be tightened; if the impeller is out of round or deformed it can be carefully trimmed with a knife, and replaced if necessary. Damage to the capacitor of an electric fan will cause failure to start, and a part of the same specification must be replaced during maintenance; if it sometimes turns and sometimes does not, one possible cause is timer failure, and the treatment is to replace the timer; soft breakdown of the capacitor can also cause intermittent turning, and the capacitor must be replaced. When the refrigerator motor does not start and there is no sound, the possible cause may be a blown power fuse, or damage to the motor starting capacitor, the latter requiring replacement of the capacitor; poor contact of contacts of the automatic control contacts of the refrigerator thermostat will cause frequent starting of the motor. Damage to the capacitor of the spin-dryer motor is one cause of abnormal operation of the spin tub, and the capacitor must be replaced during treatment. If no capacitor of the same capacitance is available, one of close capacitance may be substituted, but one that is too small or too large is strictly prohibited. Failure of the generator voltage to build up normally corresponds to replacing the capacitor, and a power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply. Loose screws correspond to tightening the screws, loose connecting screws of two conductive parts correspond to tightening the screws, and a loose COM screw corresponds to tightening. The operation of tightening is used in electrical maintenance to ensure good contact of wiring terminals, screws and fastening mechanisms or to prevent loosening; the wiring screws of an electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact, and failure to tighten the external wiring screws of a thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be disconnected. Low supply voltage will cause loud noise in an AC electromagnet, and at this time the supply must be adjusted to 0.85~1.10 times the rated voltage; when insufficient holding force of the contactor causes welding of contacts, it should be checked whether the supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage. Poor contact of contacts will cause contact overheating or burning, and the methods for dealing with poor contact of contacts of a contactor include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface and tightening the contacts and conductive plates. The electric-type main engine remote control system contains fuses, and fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Voltage can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter; voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; failure of the generator to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in an AC electric drive system.

In the maintenance of AC single-phase motors, capacitors are an unavoidable inspection object. The main performance indicators of a capacitor include capacitance, withstand voltage value, i.e. maximum working voltage, and temperature resistance value. When marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, a multimeter can be used to test the capacitor; the capacitor testing procedure applies to the capacitor, determining by measurement whether its earth leakage and capacitance are normal. Once a capacitor fault occurs, the fault still belongs to the component category of capacitor, and usually manifests as soft breakdown, reduced capacitance, deterioration or damage.

Capacitor damage will cause obvious abnormalities in various marine and household appliances. Damage to the starting capacitor of a refrigerator motor will cause no sound and failure to start after being energized. In addition, the fault of failure of the generator voltage to build up normally corresponds to replacing the capacitor, so as to eliminate failure of voltage build-up caused by short circuit of the resonant capacitor.

AC single-phase motors include those of washing machines and also include capacitors, and electric fans likewise include capacitors and timers. The washing machine is generally used as the prime mover of electric fans, electric drills, refrigerators and washing machines, etc., and its faults can be divided into three categories: motor faults, electrical control circuit faults and mechanical faults. Debris blocking the clearance at the bottom of the impeller, or excessive laundry or laundry wrapping the impeller, will also cause the washing machine not to work after being energized. Possible causes of the heating fault of an electric fan include lack of oil or stiffness of the oscillating mechanism. Loosening of the bearing bracket screws of an electric fan will cause uneven rotor clearance, resulting in rubbing between stator and rotor and thus failure to start.

Among the lubrication problems of the washing machine transmission mechanism, lack of oil in the bearing is a specific case of poor lubrication of the transmission mechanism of an impeller washing machine; for this fault the motor must be removed and lubricating oil added for repair, and it is listed alongside lack of oil in the seal ring, V-belt friction and poor lubrication of the shaft hole, all belonging to transmission lubrication problems. At the impeller shaft of a washing machine, a seal ring that does not fit tightly with the shaft will cause water leakage; if there is a lack of lubrication between the impeller shaft and the seal ring, an appropriate amount of lubricating oil can be applied to the seal ring. Lack of lubrication between the impeller shaft and the seal ring of a washing machine will cause poor lubrication of the transmission mechanism. Lack of oil in the refrigerator compressor may cause sound but failure to start after being energized.

Abnormal operation of the spin tub is also related to the brake drum. The brake drum is the braking device component of the washing machine spin-dryer motor; looseness between the spin-dryer motor shaft and the brake drum will cause abnormal noise during operation of the spin tub, and deformation of the brake drum or too small a clearance will also cause abnormal noise during operation of the spin tub; the method for servicing looseness between the spin-dryer motor shaft and the brake drum is to tighten the lock nut, and for the fault of deformation of the brake drum or too small a clearance the brake drum must be serviced and the clearance adjusted.

Faults in the drainage link also require attention. In a washing machine, a drain valve blocked by debris will cause poor drainage or inability to drain, and the maintenance method is to open the drain valve and remove the debris; a drain valve pull strap that is too tight or debris in the valve may cause the washing machine to leak water, and the strap should be appropriately loosened and the debris removed. If the drain hose of a washing machine is folded into a dead corner or has creases, it is easily blocked by debris causing poor drainage; an aged and cracked drain hose will cause water leakage, and it must be replaced and the pipe mouth firmly bonded with glue; when clearing a blocked drain hose, a thin iron wire can be bent into a hook to pull out the debris inside.

Poor contact and loose screws are common fault causes running through the above equipment. Loose screws are a common cause in ship electrical and mechanical equipment of reduced fastening force of connections due to vibration, improper installation or aging, thereby causing poor contact, open circuit, overheating or mechanical faults; in the fault of excessive temperature rise of a circuit breaker, loose connecting screws of two conductive parts is one of the main causes and must be dealt with by tightening the screws, and loose connecting screws of two conductive parts correspond to tightening the screws; loose screws will cause the shunt trip unit to fail to trip the circuit breaker, corresponding to tightening the screws; a loose "COM" screw corresponds to tightening. The vibration and swaying environment peculiar to ships can easily cause loosening of wiring clamping screws, of the connections between cable connectors and the base, and of the internal fixing screws of the PLC, creating hidden fault risks.

The cabins of senior crew members on ships are usually equipped with a refrigerator, whose prime mover is mostly an AC single-phase motor, so the maintenance of AC single-phase motors occupies a certain place in the maintenance of marine motors. The faults of a refrigerator can be broadly classified into three categories: motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system, and maintenance personnel should master the troubleshooting of common faults of the refrigerator motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system. Personnel undertaking such work need to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of components (assemblies) of electrical equipment, and master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, so as to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary diagnosis through inquiry, observation, touching, listening and smelling.

Failure of the refrigerator motor to start with no sound after being energized is one of the common faults. There are many causes of this phenomenon: a blown power fuse, poor contact of the plug, and a thermal relay that has not reset will all prevent the motor from starting; the thermostat being open or in the "stop point" position will likewise prevent the motor from starting; damage to the coil of the starting relay or poor contact of contacts will also cause the motor not to start with no sound after being energized; damage to the defroster and damage to the starting capacitor of the refrigerator motor are both possible causes of this fault. In addition, when the supply voltage is lower than the rated value by 15%, it will also cause the motor not to start with no sound after being energized. If the motor makes a sound but fails to start after being energized, it may be caused by undervoltage, and at this time an AC voltage stabilizer must be installed;

For the above faults, troubleshooting should be carried out item by item. If the power fuse is blown, check whether the power supply lead and fuse are blown and replace them; if the plug has poor contact, check the plug and socket; if the thermal relay has not reset, perform the reset operation; if the thermostat is open or in the "stop point" position, readjustment is required; loss of the temperature-sensing agent of the thermostat will cause an open circuit, preventing the refrigerator motor from starting, and the temperature-sensing agent must be reset or the thermostat replaced. For a WSF-type thermostat, turning the differential adjustment screw counterclockwise can increase the on-off differential, and one turn of the screw changes the differential by about 4°C; for a WDF-type thermostat, turning the cut-in point adjustment screw clockwise can raise the cut-in temperature and vice versa lower it, while the cut-out point adjustment is the opposite. Sticking of the thermostat contacts will cause the refrigerator to run continuously; the knob can be turned repeatedly to try to restore it, otherwise it must be serviced or replaced. If the starting relay coil is damaged, the coil must be repaired or replaced; if the contacts have poor contact, they must be repaired or replaced; sticking of contacts may cause the refrigerator motor to stop suddenly during starting or running, and the stuck contacts likewise must be repaired or replaced. If the defroster is damaged, the component must be repaired or replaced. If the starting capacitor is damaged, the capacitor must be replaced. If the refrigerant leaks seriously or the refrigeration system is blocked, the phenomenon of continuous running without cooling will occur. Frost-free refrigerators are provided with a cold-air circulation fan and an air door adjustment knob, which should also be noted during maintenance. The performance of a capacitor that needs to be tested includes earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors; a multimeter can be used for testing, and the capacitor testing procedure applies to the capacitor.

Capacitor damage is the cause of abnormal operation of various equipment. If intermittent turning or intermittent stopping is caused by soft breakdown of the capacitor, the capacitor should also be replaced. In addition, failure of the generator voltage to build up normally may be caused by short circuit of the resonant capacitor, and the corresponding measure is to replace the capacitor. It may also be undervoltage, and the supply voltage should be checked. When the electric drill speed is too slow, the possible cause is undervoltage, and the supply voltage must be checked and adjusted. Failure of an electric drill to start may be caused by switch damage, poor contact of the brush, open circuit of the winding or bearing wear.

Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting, will also cause low speed under load operation, and will also cause the motor temperature to be too high or smoking. A contactor contains a coil; if the contactor fails to pick up or has insufficient holding force accompanied by a humming sound, it may be due to undervoltage or large fluctuation of the supply voltage, and a voltage across the coil lower than 85% of the rated voltage specified by the product is regarded as undervoltage. The thermal relay uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and is mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors; it is used in large quantities on ships, and generally the overload protection of small motors is accomplished by it.

The fault symptom of failure to start corresponds to several treatment methods during maintenance: check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the supply voltage and, if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find the short circuit and open circuit parts and repair them, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer, and if the motor runs normally, the reducer part should be checked. Failure of the power supply to be connected, incorrect wiring of the control equipment, undervoltage, short circuit to earth between phases of the stator winding, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will all cause failure to start.

When measuring voltage, a multimeter or a voltmeter may be used; the multimeter is also used to measure capacitance. Marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, and capacitors are widely used in marine electrical equipment.

Senior crew members' cabins on board are usually each equipped with a refrigerator, whose prime mover is mostly an AC single-phase motor; therefore the refrigerator is one of the typical loads of the AC single-phase motor. Refrigerator faults can be broadly classified into three categories: the motor, the electrical control circuit and the refrigeration system; troubleshooting often requires the use of a multimeter or a voltmeter to measure voltage, judging from the voltage value whether the power supply is normal. That is to say, the multimeter is used to measure voltage, and the voltmeter is likewise used to measure voltage; the voltage values read by the two are the direct basis for judging whether the power supply circuit is normal. If the supply voltage is lower than 15% of the rated value, the motor neither starts nor makes any sound after being energized; the indirect-cooling refrigerator is additionally provided with a cold-air circulation fan and an air-door adjusting knob; when its air door fails, although the compressor can still start and stop automatically, the temperature inside the cabinet is on the high side; at this time the air door should be removed to check whether the mechanism has failed and to adjust it.

The temperature controller performs the electrical control function in the refrigeration system of refrigerators and refrigerated containers; it relies on a temperature-sensing element to monitor temperature and control starting and stopping of the compressor. After being energized, the motor does not start and makes no sound; one of the causes is that the temperature controller is open or the knob is in the "stop" position. Loss of the temperature-sensing agent will open the temperature controller circuit, and the refrigerator motor then fails to start; the remedy is to reset the temperature-sensing agent or replace the temperature controller. If the contacts of the temperature controller stick, the refrigerator will run continuously; the knob may be rotated repeatedly to try to restore it, and if this is ineffective, the controller should be repaired or replaced. When terminals 10 and 11 of electronic temperature controller 23A1 are conducting, the liquid-supply solenoid valve is energized and opens, and the compressor begins refrigerating; when the temperature inside the cabinet reaches the set lower limit, terminals 10 and 11 of 23A1 open and the compressor stops running. Once the contacts stick, the motor may suddenly stop during starting or running. The corresponding repair method is to repair or replace the coil, and to repair or replace the contacts that have stuck. Poor contact of contacts is essentially a decrease in conductivity caused by contamination, oxidation or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface; in a contactor it is one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning, and handling requires cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface and tightening the contact and the conductive plate. Poor contact is mostly caused by looseness, oxidation or foreign matter at electrical connections increasing the contact resistance; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs can cause it; it can result in local overheating, phase failure, short circuit between phases, and can also make the output operate randomly; the corresponding remedy is to check the terminal wiring. When the temperature rise of a circuit breaker is too high, looseness of the screws connecting the two conductive parts is one of the main causes, and the screws must be tightened; failure of the shunt trip unit to trip the circuit breaker may also originate from loose screws, and the remedy is likewise to tighten the screws.

The thermal relay is a protective relay using a bimetallic strip as the sensing element; classified by sensing element it belongs to the bimetallic strip type, is used in large quantities on board, and is generally used to accomplish overload protection of small motors. When the motor is overloaded, the thermal relay FR operates, opening the control circuit so that contactor KM is de-energized and the machine stops; the fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not act as overload protection. The transistor relay for motor overload protection converts power into voltage, satisfying the relation U=KP. Charging too much refrigerant into the refrigeration system will cause excessively high pressure and too heavy a load, thereby causing motor overload. Motor internal fault will cause the motor to fail to start, automatic start failure, motor overheating or even burning out; it is also one of the potential causes of noise or vibration when the refrigerator compressor is running; faults in the motor stator winding, bearings, etc. will also produce the phenomenon of excessive temperature rise.

Noise and vibration during refrigerator operation have several other sources. The damping rubber pad is used to fix the refrigerator compressor; if pressed too tightly, too loosely or aged, it will make the motor produce noise during operation; adjustment of its tightness or replacement with a new pad is sufficient during maintenance. Breakage of the vibration-damping suspension spring will increase noise inside the compressor; the remedy is to replace the compressor or repair the vibration-damping suspension spring. Noise may be emitted when the capillary tube and the high- and low-pressure lines collide due to compressor operation; gently moving the lines by hand to avoid collision will eliminate it;

Wax deposition in the capillary tube is one of the fault causes for high temperature inside the cabinet; the wax deposit can be flushed out or the capillary tube replaced. A poor door seal will cause serious cold leakage and cause frequent starting of the motor; serious door-seal leakage or too many door openings will prevent the refrigerator from cooling down. For a poor door seal, the door gap should be patched or the magnetic door seal strip replaced; for serious door-seal leakage, the door seal strip should be repaired or replaced. A damaged lamp switch will make the lighting lamp stay on or fail to light; repairing the lamp switch or directly replacing it is sufficient. As for the electric fan, a damaged speed-control switch is a possible cause of the motor failing to start, and the switch should be repaired; sinking of the ceiling-fan rotor manifests as slow starting and reduced speed, and it is necessary to reassemble and eliminate the cause so as to restore the rotor to its original position.

AC single-phase motors appear on ships mostly in the form of equipment such as electric fans, electric drills and washing machines, and the prime movers of these devices are all single-phase motors. Electric drills and washing machines likewise use AC single-phase motors as the prime mover; among them the washing machine washes clothes by rotation of the pulsator, and its faults can be classified into three categories: motor faults, electrical control circuit faults and mechanical faults.

Failure of the electric fan to start is a common fault symptom, and its causes involve both electrical and mechanical aspects. The power supply not being connected is the first possible cause, and the corresponding repair method is to check the power supply circuit. An open-circuit in the stator winding will also cause the electric fan to fail to start; if the lead portion is broken it should be re-soldered, and if the wire is broken inside the slot the winding should be removed and replaced rather than merely soldering the lead; this handling process is finding the open-circuit point and repairing it. Detachment of the end ring (shading winding) will likewise cause failure to start, and the remedy is to re-solder the end ring. Mechanically, bearing damage, burrs or foreign matter in the bore of the oil-impregnated bearing, or lack of lubricating oil all cause excessive mechanical resistance, and the bearing must be replaced; serious wear of the rotating shaft or looseness of the bearing bracket screws causing rubbing between stator and rotor requires replacement of the rotating shaft or adjustment of the clearance, wherein looseness of the bearing bracket screws causes uneven rotor clearance, leading to rubbing between stator and rotor and thus failure to start; poor assembly of the motor affects concentricity, and reassembly is required to ensure smooth operation. Repair methods also include checking whether the supply voltage is too low, and replacing bearings that have failed due to bearing wear. If the fan blade does not fit tightly on the rotating shaft, copper sheet should be wrapped on the shaft so that it fits tightly on the shaft; after replacing the bearing, an appropriate amount of good-quality lubricating grease must be added. The pulsator turning intermittently is mainly caused by a timer fault. When a capacitor fault occurs, that fault is a problem of the capacitor itself. The marine motor comprises bearings, windings and a rotating shaft. The rotating shaft is used to transmit torque and rotary motion.

Bearing overheating of the generator corresponds to the remedy of replacing the bearing. Abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation corresponds to replacing the rotating shaft, and bearing overheating corresponds to replacing the bearing. A power supply fault corresponds to checking the power supply. The wiring diagram should be checked and corrections made; the supply voltage should be checked and, if it is indeed too low, appropriately raised;

For repair of the refrigerator, faults need to be treated separately according to the three categories of motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system, because the manifestations and troubleshooting directions of different categories of faults are not the same.

As far as the motor category is concerned, when the supply voltage is lower than 15% of the rated value, the motor will exhibit the phenomenon of not starting and making no sound after being energized; this is a direct basis for judging whether there is an undervoltage problem on the supply side. In such a case, it should first be checked whether the supply voltage meets the rated value requirement, and then it is decided whether to dismantle and inspect the motor itself.
