Faults in the electrical control circuit will likewise manifest as the motor failing to start normally or running abnormally; therefore, during troubleshooting the control circuit must be distinguished from the motor proper, and the continuity and contact condition of the circuit confirmed section by section, so as to avoid misjudging a circuit problem as motor damage.

Faults in the refrigeration system manifest as another sign: when the refrigerant leaks seriously or the refrigeration system is blocked, the refrigerator will run continuously without cooling down. At this time the motor is still running continuously, but the temperature inside the cabinet cannot be brought down, indicating that the problem is not whether the motor can start, but whether the refrigerant is sufficient and whether the piping is unobstructed.

For the indirect-cooling refrigerator, its structure is additionally provided with a cold-air circulation fan and an air-door adjusting knob. The cold-air circulation fan is responsible for delivering the cooling capacity from the evaporator side into the cabinet, and the air-door adjusting knob is used to adjust the distribution of cold air.

When servicing an indirect-cooling refrigerator, besides checking the motor, the electrical control circuit and the refrigeration system separately according to the above three categories of faults, attention must also be paid to whether the cold-air circulation fan rotates normally and whether the position of the air-door adjusting knob is appropriate, because once these two are out of order they will likewise cause the temperature inside the cabinet to fail to meet requirements, and their symptoms are similar to refrigerant leakage or system blockage and need to be distinguished in conjunction with the motor's running condition and the state of the control circuit.

In summary, fault judgment for the refrigerator can be carried out along the three lines of motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system: a supply voltage lower than 15% of the rated value corresponds to the motor not starting and making no sound after being energized; for the indirect-cooling refrigerator, the cold-air circulation fan and the air-door adjusting knob must also be included in the scope of inspection.

Key points of routine maintenance of marine transformers. Transformers commonly used on ships include three categories: three-phase transformers, single-phase transformers and special-purpose transformers. Among them, three-phase transformers are mainly used to supply loads such as lighting and electric heating, and are mostly of the larger-capacity type; single-phase transformers, together with three-phase transformers and special-purpose transformers, belong to the types of transformers commonly used on ships; special-purpose transformers are designed for specific operating conditions. The structural forms of these transformers include dry-type, air-cooled and waterproof types.

Avoiding dampness of the transformer is the first matter to be attended to in routine maintenance. The purpose of strictly preventing dampness is to prevent the transformer windings from becoming damp and thus lowering the insulation resistance. Routine maintenance should regularly check whether the transformer is well sealed and whether the screws are loose. The insulation resistance between phases and to earth of a marine transformer is measured with a 500V insulation resistance tester and should be not less than 0.5MΩ; when the insulation resistance is lower than 0.2MΩ, measures must be taken to raise the insulation resistance value. The insulation resistance tester used here, also known as a megohmmeter, consists of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is a portable instrument used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables; when measuring the insulation resistance of a coil to earth, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester may be connected to the iron core.

Keeping the lead-out terminals clean is likewise not to be neglected. Dirt and oil fouling on the terminals must be removed to ensure good contact of the terminals; if traces of overheating are found on the terminals, the oxides should be removed and the terminals retightened, preventing short circuit or earthing faults by reducing the contact resistance. In the maintenance of marine transformers, when the lead-out terminals show traces of overheating, removing the oxides and retightening is this type of operation.

Monitoring transformer heating is a routine requirement during operation. The heating condition of the transformer should be monitored frequently, and its temperature rise must not exceed the maximum temperature rise permitted by the insulation. This precaution applies to the three-phase, single-phase and special-purpose transformers commonly used on ships. When installing a single-phase load of larger capacity, it is necessary to monitor heating and ensure three-phase current balance: the degree of three-phase current unbalance must not exceed ±5% of the rated current, and the maximum phase current must not exceed the rated value.

Attention to transformer wiring mainly concerns the use scenarios of various small transformers. When using a small transformer, it is strictly forbidden to connect the secondary winding to the power supply, so as to avoid burning out the transformer; incorrect wiring will cause the transformer to burn out.

Winding faults and insulation treatment. A winding is the coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to produce a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force. The marine motor comprises windings, and the winding insulation of a marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proofing, mould-proofing and salt-oil-mist-proofing and be oil-resistant. Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes leading to overcurrent and overheating of AC motors. When inter-turn short circuit of the transformer winding causes serious heating and three-phase current unbalance, inspection and repair is a necessary measure. Inspection and repair means detection and restoration carried out for faults of electrical equipment and components, covering mechanical mechanisms, winding insulation and contact parts, etc., and is also used to solve the automatic tripping fault caused by the free tripping mechanism of the main switch failing to latch, and the post-removal treatment when the oscillating parts of the electric fan fit too tightly or the shading winding is open. The phenomenon that the main switch is liable to trip automatically due to hull vibration corresponds to the handling measure of inspection and repair.

Use and maintenance of AC arc welding machines. The AC arc welding machine belongs to the category of special transformers, and structurally all are movable equipment. Precautions for use of the welding machine: when used in the open air, seawater or rainwater must be prevented from entering the interior of the equipment; after use it should be placed in a dry, rain-sheltered place and secured, the securing measure being intended to prevent movement as the ship rolls; during operation the current and temperature rise must be observed to ensure they do not exceed the maximum values permitted by the insulation. The observation covers abnormal phenomena, condition of parts, condition of conductors and operating parameters of the equipment, specifically such as whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, cracked, chafed or burnt.

Selection of related instruments and transformers. Resistance, voltage and current are the basic quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment condition. The multimeter is used for measurement of resistance, voltage and current; the clamp-on ammeter is used for measurement of current, contains a current transformer inside, and by the principle of the through-type current transformer can directly clamp on and measure AC current without disconnecting the conductor; the through-type current transformer is a kind of current transformer, in which the large-current conductor under measurement is directly linked with the iron core to replace the primary winding. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after the circuit is opened. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system; local short circuit or phase failure of the winding, overvoltage, etc. are all related causes.

The wattmeter contains a current coil and a voltage coil. The current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load, and is used to detect the current of the circuit under measurement; the branch in which the voltage coil is located has an additional resistor connected in series, and is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under measurement, and is used to detect voltage. The voltage range of the wattmeter is realized by connecting additional resistors of different resistance values in series with the voltage coil; the current coil and the voltage coil are each marked with a corresponding terminal (such as "*"), and during measurement the current must flow in or out from that terminal at the same time.

The voltage transformer corresponds to the symbol TV, is used to transform the voltage ratio, the secondary voltage is 100V, and one end of the secondary side is earthed. When selecting a voltage transformer, the rated voltage ratio of the transformer should be selected according to the rated voltage of the voltage coil of the instrument used; its rated capacity should be not less than the power consumed by all measuring instruments, and the primary rated voltage should be equal to or slightly greater than the voltage of the line under measurement. The voltage transformer has the nature of a voltage source, and the secondary standard voltage is usually 100V or 110V; its operating principle is the same as that of a transformer, but its internal resistance is extremely small and the output voltage hardly varies with the load; during operation it is equivalent to a no-load transformer, the secondary side must strictly not be short-circuited, and a fuse must be installed on the primary side for short circuit protection.

The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA, is used to transform the current ratio, the secondary current is 5A, the types include the coil type, the busbar type and the through type, and one end of the secondary side is earthed. During selection the secondary rated current should be slightly greater than or equal to the current of the line under measurement. The current transformer has the nature of a current source, and the secondary standard current is usually 5A; the primary terminals are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary by K1 and K2; during operation it is equivalent to a short-circuited transformer, the secondary winding must strictly not be open-circuited during operation, and no fuse may be installed in the primary winding of the current transformer.

The fuse corresponds to the symbol FU, has overload protection and short circuit protection functions, and is a safety device that, when overload or short circuit occurs in the power network or the power-consuming equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; it belongs to the distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. The automatic transfer circuit of the lighting busbar power supply contains fuses such as FU1, FU2 and FU3. In the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line through FU. The MF-30 multimeter is a related instrument under the symbol system of FU. A fuse must be installed on the primary side of the voltage transformer to provide short circuit protection for the power network and the transformer.

The contactor is a low-voltage control apparatus on ships, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, featuring high operating frequency, long service life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size; it is used in large quantities on ships because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil; contactor maintenance applies to the contactor. The core is the magnetic-conducting component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as an insulation measurement reference point; the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked. Welding is a process in which heating melts the solder, atomic diffusion occurs between the workpiece and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer with good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength is formed; its mechanism is to heat the workpiece to melt the solder, produce atomic diffusion between the workpiece and the solder, and after solidification form an alloy bonding layer at their interface, which has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength; welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products. The treatment measure corresponding to a broken input wiring is welding, and the treatment measure corresponding to a loose "COM" screw is tightening. In addition, overheating of the magnetic field coil, oiling the bearing, etc. are also situations requiring attention and treatment in maintenance and repair.

Marine transformers and their automatic power supply changeover circuits In the ship electrical system, three-phase transformers undertake the power supply task for loads such as lighting and electric heating, usually with large capacity, and their structural forms include dry-type, air-cooled and waterproof types. Such transformers are often configured in pairs on ships, with the two able to serve as mutual standby, and a selector switch sets which one is in the main state and which one is in the standby state. When the main transformer loses power, the secondary circuit needs to automatically switch the load to the standby transformer; this changeover is usually realized by contactor interlocking: the secondary sides of the two transformers are each connected by one contactor, and the coil circuits of the two contactors are connected in series with each other's normally closed contacts, thereby ensuring that only one contactor can pick up at any time and avoiding parallel connection of the secondary sides of the two transformers. The standby contactor does not act instantaneously but is put in after a delay; the delay is accomplished by a time relay, so as to avoid false changeover caused by instantaneous fluctuation of the main power supply.

Basic requirements and diagnostic methods for maintenance personnel Personnel engaged in the maintenance of marine transformers and auxiliary machinery electrical systems must be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions of each component and assembly, and their installation positions on the equipment, and must also be very familiar with the routing of the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, the working principle and the positions of each component. In conventional fault diagnosis, maintenance personnel rely on the method of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary judgment: asking is to learn from the operator about the operating conditions before and after the fault, looking is to observe the appearance, indications and action states, touching is to check the temperature rise and tightness, listening is to distinguish whether the operating sound is abnormal, and smelling is to detect any burnt odor. This method is equally applicable to the inspection of transformers and their changeover circuits.

Contactor and its maintenance The contactor is an electrical apparatus used to control motors in the ship power system, belonging to low-voltage control apparatus, mainly used in electric drive systems, and featuring accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long service life and small size. The power of various auxiliary machinery on ships is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on ships. The contactor includes an arc chute, which is used to extinguish the arc generated when the main contacts break; the contactor includes main contacts, which undertake the task of making and breaking the main circuit; the contactor includes a core, and the contactor also includes a coil; the core and the coil together form the electromagnetic mechanism, and when the coil is energized it attracts the core, thereby driving the main contacts to act. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor as equipment, and the maintenance content centers on the above components, including the contact condition of the contacts, the inspection of the core and coil, and the cleaning of the arc chute.

Time relay and thermal relay The time relay is an electrical apparatus used for control or protection in the ship power system, used to set the action time in occasions such as delayed putting-in of transformer standby power supply, with common designations KT, SJ, SL. The thermal relay is also an electrical apparatus used for control or protection in the ship power system; it uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and belongs to thermal relays classified by sensing element, its sensing part being the bimetallic strip. The thermal relay is mainly used for overload protection of small motors on ships and is used in large quantities on ships; generally the overload protection task of small motors is accomplished by it. Common fault symptoms of the thermal relay include the thermal relay not acting, the main circuit not being connected after the thermal relay is connected, the thermal relay control circuit not being connected, and the thermal relay failing to reset; fault diagnosis of the thermal relay body does not involve internal winding faults of the motor, nor does it involve problems of external actuating elements such as a burnt contactor coil.

Circuit breaker and its maintenance The circuit breaker is a switching apparatus used to protect circuits in the ship power system, belonging to low-voltage distribution apparatus, divided into the frame type (air circuit breaker) and the molded-case type, having both switching and protection functions, and being able to maintain thermal stability and dynamic stability under short circuit faults. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker as equipment, and during maintenance the following fault symptoms need to be checked and treated: the circuit breaker may have the situation that when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close, that is, the contacts cannot close during manual operation; the circuit breaker may have the situation that when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contacts cannot close, that is, the contacts likewise cannot close during electrical operation; in addition there is the case where the contacts of one phase cannot close; the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker break; the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker break; the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the circuit breaker automatically breaks about 1h after closing; the undervoltage trip unit has noise; the circuit breaker temperature rise is too high; the auxiliary switch fails; the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit misoperates, causing the circuit breaker to open. These symptoms cover several aspects such as the circuit breaker operating mechanism, trip unit, auxiliary switch and the electronic parts of the trip unit, and inspection should be carried out item by item in combination with the specific symptoms.

The maintenance work of the ship auxiliary machinery electrical system starts from the accurate reading of electrical control circuit diagrams. Reading diagrams is a key skill that maintenance personnel must master, among which the wire-tracing diagram-reading method is used to analyze faults of auxiliary machinery control systems and is the basic means of tracing the continuity of circuits one by one and determining the fault section. The wire-tracing diagram-reading method requires checking section by section along the control circuit, starting from the power supply end, passing through the protective apparatus and control apparatus up to the actuating apparatus, comparing the make/break state of each contact with the drawing markings, thereby narrowing the fault range to a certain circuit or a certain element. At the same time, proficiently mastering the general fault checking methods for the three situations of short circuit, open circuit and earthing is also a basic skill that maintenance personnel should possess. A short circuit manifests as instantaneous fuse blowing or tripping, an open circuit manifests as the circuit not being connected and the apparatus not acting, and earthing manifests as a decrease in insulation resistance to earth or contact with the casing; the three have different checking means and different bases for judgment. These two capabilities together determine whether fault troubleshooting can quickly locate the specific circuit and specific element.

When the conventional fault diagnosis method is used, the first step is observation. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part conditions, wire conditions and equipment operating parameters. Specifically for parts, check whether there is jamming or damage; specifically for wires, check whether there is looseness, breakage, abrasion or burning; specifically for operating parameters, compare the deviation between instrument readings and rated values to judge whether the equipment deviates from the normal working state. In this process, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions of components (assemblies) and their positions of the electrical equipment, and understand the phenomena and make a preliminary diagnosis by means of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. Maintenance personnel must also be very familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, working principle and the positions of each component, otherwise neither diagram reading nor wire tracing can be carried out.

In the ship power system, the contactor is an electrical apparatus used to control motors. It belongs to low-voltage control apparatus, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, and features accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long service life and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor itself includes parts such as the arc chute, main contacts, core and coil. The arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the main contacts break, the main contacts undertake the task of making and breaking the main circuit, and the core and coil form the electromagnetic mechanism; when the coil is energized it generates electromagnetic attraction to make the armature act. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; during inspection the voltage across the coil and the coil resistance can be measured to determine whether the coil is open or the power supply circuit has lost power. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor as an electrical apparatus, and its content centers on the condition inspection and upkeep of the above components, including whether the arc chute is damaged or has carbon deposits, whether the main contacts are eroded or welded, whether the core is jammed or rusted, and whether the coil is overheated and discolored.

The thermal relay likewise belongs to electrical apparatus used for control or protection in the ship power system. It uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, is mainly used for overload protection of small motors on ships, and is used in large quantities on ships; generally the overload protection task of small motors is accomplished by it. In control circuits such as air compressors, the thermal relay realizes overload shutdown by opening the control circuit through its normally closed contact; in the air compressor control circuit, its normally closed contact is connected in series in the control circuit to realize overload shutdown. In the water supply circuit, the thermal relay FR and the fuse FU respectively form overload and short circuit protection; the former acts according to the thermal effect of current, the latter fuses according to the thermal effect of current, and the division of labor between the two is clear. The thermal relay not acting, the main circuit not being connected after the thermal relay is connected, the thermal relay control circuit not being connected, and the thermal relay failing to reset are common fault manifestations of this type of protective apparatus, among which the difference between not acting and failing to reset is that the former manifests as the contacts not closing or the mechanism being stuck during overload, while the latter manifests as being unable to restore the initial state by manual reset after tripping; the difference between the main circuit not being connected and the control circuit not being connected is that the former affects the motor power supply circuit, while the latter only affects control signal transmission. During inspection, first confirm whether the setting current matches the motor rated current, then check whether the normally closed contact is in good contact and whether the reset mechanism is flexible.

The time relay is also an electrical apparatus used for control or protection in the ship power system, often appearing in control circuits with letter symbols such as KT, SJ, SL, used to realize delayed action and, together with contactors and thermal relays, complete the control logic of acting in time sequence. When encountering KT, SJ, SL during diagram reading, one should distinguish the circuit where its coil is located from the circuit where the delayed contacts are located, clarify whether it is on-delay or off-delay, and then judge the influence of the delay length on the subsequent action sequence.

The fuse undertakes overload and short circuit protection functions in the ship power system, and its letter symbol is FU. The fuse is a safety apparatus; when the power grid or electrical equipment has overload or short circuit, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. It belongs to distribution apparatus and has the characteristic of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability under short circuit faults. The RL93 series is the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. A line short circuit fault manifests as instantaneous fuse blowing or tripping, and live checking is needed to distinguish whether it is an external line short circuit or an internal element breakdown.

The fuse and the fuse element are closely related; the state of the fuse element directly reflects whether the fuse has already acted, and when replacing the fuse element it must be selected according to the original specification, and the capacity must not be arbitrarily increased nor copper wire used as a substitute.

The functions of the changeover switch include selecting the measurement object and selecting the range. It is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has relatively many selection positions and contacts. On the main switchboard, the changeover switch is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not opened. The multimeter includes a changeover switch; during measurement the measurement object and range are selected through the changeover switch, so the contact condition of the changeover switch directly affects the credibility of the multimeter reading; if the contacts are oxidized or in poor contact, the false appearance of jumping readings or zero indication will occur.

When an open circuit fault occurs in the line, it manifests as being unable to switch on the power supply after closing the switch or pressing the button, and neither the apparatus nor the motor acts. Switching on the power supply is a key link in the maintenance procedure of the PLC control system, referring to the process of connecting the power supply to carry out functional testing or self-diagnosis after confirming that there is no short circuit or earthing fault. Before switching on the power supply, it must be detected whether there is a short circuit or earthing fault in the input and output parts, and only after confirmation can power be applied. When the PLC is switched on, the self-diagnosis process begins; if there is an internal error in the CPU, the panel "CPU Error" lamp shows an abnormality. Not applying the load power supply corresponds to the link of switching on the power supply, that is, first energizing under the condition of no load, observing the action of the control circuit itself, and then gradually putting in the load, so that even if there is incorrect wiring in the circuit, the fault range will not be expanded by putting in the load.

After observation, the monitoring and indicating device should be further checked, and the current state of the equipment judged by means of instrument readings. Maintenance personnel, as the executors of fault diagnosis and repair, must be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions of components (assemblies) and their positions of the electrical equipment, and their method can be summarized as asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. Reading diagrams is a key skill of maintenance personnel, and they need to master the wire-tracing diagram-reading method to analyze faults of auxiliary machinery control systems; maintenance personnel must also be very familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, working principle and the positions of each component, need to be familiar with equipment principles, structure and maintenance materials, and in conventional fault diagnosis understand the phenomena and make a preliminary diagnosis by asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling.

Measuring instruments are important tools for fault checking. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, and is divided into the analog type and the digital type; the MF-47 multimeter belongs to one type of multimeter, and the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter also respectively belong to the category of multimeters. The multimeter includes a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, wherein the current flowing through the meter head at full scale is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes, and the measuring circuit is used to convert different quantities and different ranges, because the magnetoelectric meter head can only pass microampere-level current and a conversion circuit is needed to measure different quantities and ranges. The MF-47 multimeter can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A, and the panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The multimeter can be used to measure various objects such as resistance, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples.

When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together with an insulating material separating them; its characteristic is to block direct current and pass alternating current, and in circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; its opposition to alternating current signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC). The insulation resistance tester, also called a megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, includes a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, has terminal posts L, E, and G, and is used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines, and cables; according to the highest voltage generated by the hand-cranked generator, it is divided into specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V, and 2500V. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked. A contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, a core, and a coil. The main contact is the switching component in a contactor used to connect or disconnect the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor. If the motor does not turn and the power supply is normal, a multimeter can be used to push the armature so that the main contacts close, in order to troubleshoot an open-circuit fault in the main circuit. Discoloration of copper main contacts or a burnt smell indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel must be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the main contacts have been overheated for a long time or have welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected as a replacement. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch, used for auxiliary control, and also used for self-locking of the control circuit, signal indication, and interlock protection; it is one of the main components of the generator main switch, and as a series system element, its failure will cause the indicator light not to light. In motor forward-rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to achieve self-locking of the contactor coil; through its on-off state it controls the lighting and extinguishing of the running indicator light to display the working state of the equipment; the normally closed auxiliary contact can control the action of the solenoid valve, used to release residual air when the air compressor stops; the coordinated action of the normally open and normally closed auxiliary contacts can switch the signal display of the water pump pumping state. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. A circuit breaker is a switching device used in ship power systems to protect circuits, belongs to low-voltage distribution devices, is divided into frame type (air circuit breaker) and molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults, and the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch, capable of automatically disconnecting the generator to protect the power grid. The shunt trip unit failing to open the circuit breaker is a fault manifestation of the circuit breaker, meaning that when the shunt trip unit operates it fails to drive the circuit breaker contacts to open; a coil short circuit is one of the causes of the shunt trip unit failing to open the circuit breaker, and too low a power supply voltage will also cause the shunt trip unit to fail to open the circuit breaker. The fuse element is a component of the fuse; long-term exposure to power supply surge currents may cause it to blow under non-short-circuit faults, and a typical manifestation of a short circuit fault in the control line is the fuse element blowing. In lighting and electric heating circuits, the rated current of the fuse element is greater than or equal to the total load rated current; for direct starting of a single asynchronous motor, the rated current is taken as 1.5 to 2 times the motor rated current; in circuits for motors with light load and infrequent starting, the rated current is taken as 2.5 to 4 times the motor rated current.

A line short circuit fault is a common fault in ship electrical systems; a very large current flows through the short circuit point, causing the fuse to blow or the protective device to operate automatically, accompanied by abnormal indications of monitoring instruments and system alarm signals, and in severe cases the line insulation may burn and smoke. Its causes include insulation soaked in water or damp, damaged padding causing insulation to be worn through, and dirty terminal posts discharging; metal parts falling onto wire ends or exposed conductors can cause a short circuit, and non-continuous short circuits also exist, such as after oil dirt discharges the dirt is burned away or the conductive object falls off by itself. Poor maintenance management and improper operation will cause line short circuit faults, and are one of the main causes of electrical line short circuit faults; specific manifestations include the insulation of electrical lines being soaked in water or seriously damp, the padding being damaged and not replaced in time when cables pass through metal holes or sharp edges, causing insulation damage, and damaging the insulation protective layer during operation belongs to this type of cause, and terminal posts between lines being too dirty causing discharge between posts when power is applied, and metal parts falling onto wire ends or exposed conductors during operation or maintenance.

Improper operation is also one of the causes of short circuits; during operation, damaging the insulation protective layer or metal parts falling onto wire ends can cause electrical line short circuit faults; common manifestations include improper closing operation, unbalanced generator load control, and improper operation caused by observation errors, and during parallel operation, improper grasp of the closing moment or adjusting the load distribution in the reverse direction can cause the generator reverse power protection to trip. Defects in the equipment itself will likewise cause line short circuit faults; the equipment has hidden dangers such as poor insulation and local insulation damage before leaving the factory, and a short circuit occurs after long-term operation; motor or electrical appliance coils have weak insulation due to winding not meeting requirements, thereby causing a short circuit; aging of equipment or line insulation and deterioration of materials belong to short circuit causes due to defects in the equipment itself. Marine cable includes a protective layer; the protective layer is used to protect the cable from oil, water, and chemical corrosion, and is one of the three main components of the marine cable structure, alongside the conductive copper core wire and the insulation layer; damaging the insulation protective layer during operation is one of the causes of electrical line short circuit faults.

A line short circuit fault corresponds to the short circuit fault inspection steps. When detecting a line short circuit, the power supply should first be cut off and the blown fuse found; use the resistance range of a multimeter to measure the resistance between the two ends of the circuit; if the resistance value is zero, it is a short circuit; to ensure measurement accuracy, the multimeter should be set to the R×1 range for measurement; when the line under test contains large-capacity capacitance, it must be disconnected before inspection to avoid misjudging it as a short circuit; for a single-loop short circuit, all terminal posts, series electrical appliance coils, or components along the line can be checked one by one; when multiple parallel lines are short-circuited, the "disconnect one by one method" can be used to find the branch where the short circuit occurs. The short circuit fault inspection steps require attention to the short circuit fault detection precautions: during measurement the multimeter should be set to the R×1 range, and the normal resistance value of the line under test should be referenced to ensure accuracy; if the line contains large-capacity capacitance, it must be disconnected before inspection to prevent the charging current from being misjudged as a short circuit; when the circuit is seemingly connected but not connected, an insulation resistance tester can be used as an auxiliary judgment, and an indication of zero means a short circuit exists; lines containing electronic equipment must strictly not use an insulation resistance tester, to avoid high voltage damaging components; when multiple parallel lines are short-circuited, the disconnect one by one method should be used to locate the branch where the short circuit occurs.

A line open circuit fault manifests as, when the power supply voltage is normal and the switch is good, after closing, the electrical appliances and motors do not operate and the lamps do not light; its causes include the fuse element of the fuse blowing or screws at wire joints being loose and nuts falling off, poor contact of contactor contacts, damage to the changeover switch or the contacts of protective devices not resetting, conductors being broken, being broken by foreign objects, or internal equipment such as a burnt filament or a coil open circuit. The fuse element of a line fuse blowing will cause a line open circuit fault; screws at wire joints being loose or nuts falling off will cause a line open circuit fault; poor contact of line contactor contacts will cause a line open circuit fault; conductors in the wire being broken will cause a line open circuit fault; damage to the changeover switch or poor contact will cause a line open circuit fault; the line being broken by foreign objects will cause a line open circuit fault; poor contact or non-reset of the contacts of protective devices will cause a line open circuit fault. In the AC boat davit control circuit, the forward contactor KMF not operating indicates an open circuit fault; during live inspection, if a multimeter connected across the two ends of a component displays the power supply voltage, then the interior of that component is open-circuited.

There are many causes of line open circuit faults, which can be summarized into several categories.

The first category is the fuse element of a line fuse blowing. The fuse element, under long-term action of power supply surge currents, may blow under non-short-circuit fault conditions; after the fuse element blows, loads such as electrical appliances and motors in the line will stop operating, and various lamps will not light. In the air compressor control line, FU plays a protective role during a short circuit; in the water supply circuit, the motor obtains power through FU, and FU constitutes short circuit protection. On ships, the cross method is commonly used to check FU open circuits, using the lighting and extinguishing of a test lamp to determine the open circuit point.

The second category is screws at wire joints being loose or nuts falling off. Loose screws are a common cause in ship electrical and mechanical equipment of reduced fastening force of connecting parts due to vibration, improper installation, or aging, thereby causing poor contact, open circuit, overheating, or mechanical faults; in the fault of excessive temperature rise of a circuit breaker, loose connecting screws of two conductive parts is one of the main causes, and must be handled by tightening the screws. The vibration and swaying environment unique to ships can easily cause loosening of wiring compression screws, between cable connectors and bases, and of fixing screws inside PLCs, creating hidden fault dangers. In the open circuit fault of the AC boat davit control line, loose screws are one of the more common specific causes than poor contact of contacts. Loose fastening screws and terminal ends will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance; poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults, and can also cause random output actions; the corresponding treatment is to check the terminal wiring. In addition, loose screws will also cause the shunt trip unit to fail to open the circuit breaker.

The third category is poor contact of line contactor contacts. Poor contact of contacts refers to an electrical fault state in which the conductive performance is reduced due to contamination, oxidation, or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface; it is one of the causes of ship electrical line open circuit faults, and is also one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning; methods for handling poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface, and tightening the contact and conductive plate.

The fourth category is conductors in the wire being broken, and the fifth category is the line being broken by foreign objects; both belong to physical disconnection of the line itself, and their consequence is likewise that when the power supply voltage is normal, after closing the power supply cannot be connected, and electrical appliances, motors, etc. in the line do not operate, and various lamps do not light.

The sixth category is some changeover switches being damaged or having poor contact. In distribution lines, damage to the changeover switch or poor contact is one of the causes of open circuit faults; in a refrigerator, damage to the lamp switch will cause the lighting lamp to stay on or not light; for lighting lamp faults, the maintenance method is to repair the lamp switch or directly replace it. The consequence caused by damage to the changeover switch or poor contact manifests as, after closing or pressing the power-on button, the power supply cannot be connected, loads such as electrical appliances and motors in the line do not operate, and various lamps do not light, and this fault occurs under the premise that the power supply voltage is normal and the power switch opens and closes well.

The seventh category is poor contact or non-reset of the contacts of protective devices in some lines. Poor contact or non-reset of the contacts of protective devices will cause a line open circuit fault; its specific manifestation is that the contacts of the protective device have poor contact, or the protective device has not reset after operating; all the above situations will make the circuit open.

The eighth category is open circuit faults in the equipment itself. Open circuit faults in the equipment itself will cause line open circuit faults; it refers to broken conductors in motor windings and electrical appliance coils, burnt filaments of some lamps, or open circuit of ballast coils, etc. Broken conductors in motor windings and electrical appliance coils belong to the type of open circuit fault existing in the equipment itself. Coil open circuit refers to a fault in which the internal conductor of an electrical coil is broken, causing the circuit not to conduct, commonly found in equipment such as contactors and electromagnetic brakes; in a contactor, coil open circuit is one of the main fault causes of the contactor failing to pick up; the method for detecting coil open circuit is to measure the coil resistance with a multimeter after power off, to determine whether it is open. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil magnetic force to pull in or release, used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, causing the motor to have no power and failure to start; failure or defect of the armature return spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after pressing the stop button.

For line open circuit faults, the corresponding inspection methods are divided into live inspection of line open circuit faults and dead inspection of line open circuit faults. Live inspection of open circuit faults can use the voltage range of a multimeter, but its range should not be lower than the power supply voltage; a test lamp can also be used for inspection. Before inspection, confirm that the power supply voltage is normal and that the power switch has no open circuit or poor contact; close the power switch, and after measuring that the voltage is normal, inspection can begin. Its principle basis is: due to the line open circuit, there is no current in the circuit, and the resistors, electrical appliance coils, or motor windings connected in the circuit have no voltage drop. If the voltmeter indication is the power supply voltage, it indicates that the line or component between the two test pens is open-circuited. In complex interlock lines, the electrical appliance armature can be manually pushed to close the contacts, to narrow the inspection scope; on ships, the cross method is commonly used together with a test lamp to check fuse open circuits. During live or dead inspection of open circuit faults, the armature can be manually pushed to close the contacts to narrow the inspection scope.

A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch, and a measuring circuit, divided into pointer type and digital type; at full scale the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes; the MF-30 multimeter belongs to FU-related measuring instruments. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit, and a clamp-on ammeter can also be used to measure current; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of AC electric drive systems. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open circuit of the shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect.

Inspection of open circuit faults is divided into two approaches, live and dead; the former corresponds to live inspection of line open circuit faults, and the latter corresponds to dead inspection of line open circuit faults. During dead inspection of line open circuit faults, use the resistance range of a multimeter for measurement, and the range should be selected at R×1k or R×10k, because the resistance of some components is very large, and too small a range will make the judgment inaccurate. During measurement, move the two test pens along the line to measure the resistance across components or terminal posts in sequence; if the resistance measured between the two test pens is infinite, then it is determined that an open circuit exists in that interval. During operation, it is forbidden to touch the metal parts of the two test pens with both hands at the same time, to avoid affecting measurement accuracy.

Dead inspection of line open circuit faults requires attention to several matters, which constitute the open circuit fault inspection precautions. The circuit under inspection or the components in the circuit must not have parallel paths, otherwise R=∞ cannot be measured at the break point; in this case one end of the component should be disconnected from the circuit before measuring. When the circuit under test has electrical appliance contacts, the armature must be manually pushed to close them, to avoid measurement errors. The range of the multimeter should be set at R×1k or R×10k, to avoid inaccurate judgment due to the very large resistance of some components. When using a multimeter, do not touch the metal parts of the two test pens with both hands at the same time, to avoid affecting measurement accuracy. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are a multimeter and a voltmeter. In addition, broken conductors, being broken by foreign objects, or internal equipment such as a burnt filament or a coil open circuit are all among the causes.

The AC boat davit control circuit is composed of two parts, the raising and lowering circuits, connected in parallel. The raising circuit goes from the fuse through the normally closed contact of FR to point C, then through the KMF coil and two series-connected limit switches SQ to point D, and finally through SBP and ST back to power supply point B; the lowering circuit goes from the fuse through the KMR coil, the lowering interlock switch S, and ST back to power supply point B. Both circuits return to power supply point B through the emergency stop button ST. In the AC boat davit control circuit, when the raising start button SBTF is pressed the motor does not start, and its phenomenon is that when the raising start button SBTF is pressed the motor does not start. If it is observed that the forward contactor KMF does not operate, it indicates that an open circuit fault exists in the control circuit. The AC boat davit control circuit fault inspection steps apply to the scenario where pressing the raising start button SBTF the motor does not start and the forward contactor KMF does not operate: preliminary inspection requires confirming that the power supply is normal and that the motor drive system is not jammed, that is, check whether the power supply is normal and whether the motor drive system is jammed; first use a test lamp to cross-check the fuses; if both fuses are normal, then the open circuit fault occurs in the subsequent line, and then check whether contacts such as FR, SQ, and ST have reset or are in good contact. During live inspection, the SBTF button must be pressed and somehow fixed to prevent automatic disconnection; when using a test lamp or voltmeter for live inspection, if a multimeter connected across the two ends of the KMF coil displays the power supply voltage value, it indicates that the internal conductor of the coil is open-circuited; if KMF is normal, the open circuit point is between the two terminals where the multimeter indicates the power supply voltage value. Common open circuit faults include loose screws, poor contact of contacts, or open circuit of winding lead wires, among which loose screws are one of the more common specific causes than poor contact of contacts.

In a three-phase three-wire marine power network, when an earth fault occurs at one point, the electrical equipment can still operate normally; if another point is earthed, a multi-point earthing indirect short circuit fault is formed. The marine power network is a component of the marine electrical power system and usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system. After one point is earthed, the electrical equipment can still operate normally, but it must be eliminated promptly to improve reliability. The earth fault check procedure is: the earthed line can be easily found through the earth lamps on the switchboard, then this line is disconnected from the power supply, and the "section-by-section narrowing method" is used to find the earthing point; divide the line into two parts, use the insulation resistance tester to determine which part is earthed, then divide the earthed part into two parts and find the earthed portion, and so on, to find the earth fault point; the earth lamps on the switchboard can also be used directly to check and find the fault point, switching off each equipment or lighting switch in turn; if the brightness of the earth lamps returns to normal, the equipment is judged to be earthed.

The conventional fault diagnosis method lists observation as the first step. Before starting to look, first ask the operator to clarify the operation process and abnormal manifestations before and after the fault; only after asking does one move on to observation. In the observation step, attention should be paid to abnormal phenomena, the state of parts, the state of wires and the operating parameters of the equipment; specifically, whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. After observation is completed, the next step is to check the monitoring and indicating device. Maintenance personnel should be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of the electrical components of the equipment; the means can be summarized as asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. Reading drawings is a key skill; the method of checking wires while reading drawings must be mastered to analyze faults of auxiliary machine control systems; the general fault check methods for the three cases of short circuit, open circuit and earthing are basic skills and must be proficient. The working principles of various electrical components must also be understood; otherwise the electrical drawings cannot be read or analyzed. The MF-30 multimeter is listed among instruments for uses of the FU type. Both the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter belong to multimeters. To measure resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistance must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must also be cut off; if there is a capacitor in the circuit, discharge it before measuring resistance; live measurement is absolutely not allowed. Voltage can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter; current can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter; the clamp-on ammeter is also for measuring current. To measure current with an ammeter, the circuit must be opened and the ammeter connected in series. Measuring with a multimeter belongs to the maintenance procedure of the PLC control system, judging equipment faults by measuring voltage, current or resistance; when measuring DC current, turn the changeover switch to the milliampere range and connect the meter in series into the opened branch; when measuring DC voltage, place the test probes across the two ends of the measured component, and if the range is uncertain, first set it to the maximum range. The changeover switch handles two things: selecting the measurement object and selecting the range; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, the purpose being to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited.

The wattmeter contains a current coil, which is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the current of the measured circuit. The current coil and the voltage coil each mark a corresponding terminal (such as "*"), and during measurement the current must flow in or out from that terminal at the same time. In the main circuit fault check, the state of the current coil of electrical components such as the contactor coil can be detected with a multimeter.

The fuse symbol is written as FU, and it has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions; when the power network or electrical equipment is overloaded or short-circuited, the fuse element melts and automatically cuts off the circuit. It belongs to distribution apparatus and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during a short circuit fault. On ships, the cross method is mostly used to check FU open circuits, judging the open-circuit point by whether the test lamp lights. In the air compressor control circuit, FU plays a protective role during a short circuit; in the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line through FU. If the fuse element is subjected to power supply surge current for a long time, it may also blow under non-short-circuit faults; the typical manifestation of a short circuit fault in the control circuit is that the fuse element blows.

The contactor is responsible for controlling the motor in the marine electrical power system; it is a low-voltage control apparatus used in electric drive systems, with high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size. The contactor consists of an arc chute, main contacts, an iron core and a coil. The main contacts connect or break the main circuit current, and their closed state directly determines whether the motor can run; contactor maintenance is aimed at the contactor, and circuit breaker maintenance is aimed at the circuit breaker. When the motor is overloaded, the thermal relay FR operates, disconnecting the control circuit, and the contactor KM loses power and stops the machine. The transistor relay for motor overload protection converts power into voltage, satisfying the relationship U=KP; the fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not be used for overload protection; in a refrigeration system, charging too much refrigerant causes excessively high pressure and too heavy a load, which can also cause motor overload.

The marine motor contains a winding, which is made by winding enameled wire and is installed in the motor or transformer to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of AC motors; the winding insulation of the marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proofing, mildew-proofing and salt-oil-mist-proofing, and must be oil-resistant. In the main circuit of a DC drive system there are many resistors and electrical components and many wiring joints, so checking is relatively complicated; electrical component fault is one of the common faults of the electrical parts of the main engine remote control system.

The manifestation of a control circuit short circuit is that the fuse element blows; the check procedure is: first disconnect the control circuit from the power supply, then carefully inspect the line for abnormal conditions. A short circuit point generally has a large current flowing through it and may leave burn marks; during the check, first determine which parallel branch the short circuit is on, then use a multimeter to check the contactor coil, and at the same time check whether there is dirt or fallen metal parts between the terminal posts. A control circuit short circuit can occur in the AC boat davit control circuit, and a control circuit short circuit corresponds to the control circuit short circuit check procedure.

When the start button SBT is pressed, the contactor KMF operates but the motor does not start; this phenomenon corresponds to the main circuit fault check procedure. When the power supply voltage and the main circuit fuse or circuit breaker are normal, this phenomenon indicates that there may be an open circuit fault in the main circuit line. For the check, first cut off the power supply, and use a multimeter to test whether the thermal element of the thermal relay connected in series in the main circuit is open-circuited; if the thermal element is normal, measure at the power supply knife switch which phase is not conducting, and push the contactor armature by hand to close the main contacts so as to locate the open-circuit point. This procedure applies to the scenario where the contactor operates when the start button is pressed but the motor does not start and the power supply voltage is normal; before the check, confirm that the motor winding has no fault and that the main circuit fuse or circuit breaker is normal; if the thermal element is normal, measure at the power supply knife switch which phase is not conducting to determine the open-circuit phase; during measurement, push the contactor armature by hand to close the main contacts to simulate the working state; after finding the open-circuit phase, use the aforementioned method (sectional measurement) to find the specific open-circuit point.

The air compressor control circuit is divided into the main circuit and the control circuit; the main circuit includes the contactor KM, thermal relay FR, transformer T and fuse FU; the control circuit includes the changeover switch SC, buttons SBT1, SBT2, SBP1, SBP2, pressure relays KP1, KP2, solenoid valve YV and indicator lamp HL. When the changeover switch SC is turned to the manual position, the air compressor is controlled by button operation; when turned to the automatic position, the air compressor is controlled by the pressure relay. The contactor KM is the power contactor; when it is connected, the motor starts, and when it is disconnected, the motor stops; the thermal relay FR operates when the motor is overloaded, cutting off the control circuit and stopping the main contactor KM; the transformer T isolates the main circuit from the control circuit; the fuse FU plays a protective role when the circuit is short-circuited. The air compressor control circuit belongs to the AC boat davit control circuit, includes starting box maintenance, and may suffer faults such as the system failing to start, the motor stopping immediately after the start button SBT resets, the motor suddenly stopping during operation, loud noise from the starting box after starting, the indicator lamp not lighting, and premature rewiring. The pressure relay takes pressure as its input signal, and its sensing element is a bellows; it is used for automatic control and protection of marine boilers, air compressors and pump sets, controls the starting and stopping of the motor through high and low pressure contacts in the air compressor automatic control system, and serves as a control apparatus in auxiliary boilers to automatically control steam pressure.

Drawing-reading ability is the basis for maintenance personnel to carry out fault analysis of auxiliary machine control systems, and the method of checking wires while reading drawings especially needs to be mastered proficiently. At the same time, the general check methods for the three common faults of short circuit, open circuit and earthing are also basic skills that electrical maintenance personnel must master. Maintenance personnel should be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of the electrical components of the equipment, and use means such as asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary judgment. The prerequisite for understanding and analyzing electrical drawings is to understand the working principles of various electrical components, so knowledge of the electrical components themselves is indispensable. In a DC drive system, there are a relatively large number of resistors and electrical components in the main circuit and also many wiring joints, so checking is relatively complicated.

The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch, used for auxiliary control, and is also one of the main component parts of the contactor, undertaking functions such as control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection. The main switch is one of the carriers of auxiliary contacts, and the main components of the generator main switch also include auxiliary contacts.

The thermal relay is a protective relay with a bimetallic strip as its sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors; it belongs to thermal relays classified by sensing element, and its sensing part is the bimetallic strip. Thermal relays are used in large quantities on ships, and generally the overload protection task of small motors is completed by them. The symbol of the fuse is FU; the fuse corresponds to FU and serves as a protective element in circuit diagrams, with the graphical symbol marked FU. In the air compressor control circuit, FU plays a protective role during a short circuit;

The automatic water supply control circuit consists of the main circuit, the water level control circuit, the motor start-stop control circuit, the single-phase bridge rectifier circuit and the sound-light signal circuit; it belongs to the category of AC boat davit control circuits and is a marine auxiliary machinery control circuit with functions of automatic water level control, motor protection and sound-light display. In its main circuit, the motor M obtains power through the thermal relay FR, contactor KM, fuse FU and switch QS; when QS is closed, the contactor KM closes to make the motor run, and KM opens to make the motor stop. Besides automatic water level control, this circuit also has complete motor protection and sound and light display functions. The water level control circuit is composed of transistor VT1 and others and is a typical transistor switching circuit; when the base of VT1 obtains bias voltage and saturates and conducts, relay K1 is energized and operates, and when the base of VT1 loses bias voltage and cuts off, relay K1 is de-energized and released to play a control role. In the automatic water tank water level control circuit, potentiometer RP1 provides base bias current for transistor VT1. A potentiometer has three pins, of which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes with shaft rotation; it is generally considered manually adjustable, and the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, potentiometer R1 driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance, used for bridge balancing; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by potentiometer R driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R′ driven by motor M changes accordingly.

The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve and a potentiometer. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel oil circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control the water mist fire extinguishing zone. In the air compressor system, the solenoid valve is controlled by the normally closed contact of the contactor and opens when the machine stops to release residual air. In the burner ignition procedure, the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that oil enters the oil nozzle and is sprayed; its purpose is to control the on-off of the fuel oil, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit at ignition so that it enters the oil nozzle and is sprayed.

The solenoid valve drive circuit connects a freewheeling diode in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge.

A diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity, commonly represented by VD in circuits, used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite. By function, diodes can be divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), etc.; diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The diode test procedure applies to diodes. A transistor contains two PN junctions internally and has current amplification capability; it is divided into NPN type and PNP type, and is commonly represented in circuits by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17 representing transistor number 17; main models include A92, 9015 (PNP type) and A42, 9014, 9018, etc. (NPN type). Transistors are divided into two types, NPN type and PNP type, and their operating characteristics can complement each other, such as the paired transistors in an OTL circuit. A transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault is a problem under the category of transistors. Marine electrical equipment uses diodes and also uses transistors. The function of a capacitor is charging and discharging; its earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors can be measured. The measurable property of a resistor is its resistance value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter.

A multimeter can measure resistance, voltage, capacitance, diodes and transistors during use.

In the marine auxiliary machinery electrical system, the maintenance work of the single-speed drive control system first needs to face the measurement and judgment of various electrical parameters. Voltage, as a basic measurable property, can be obtained with a multimeter or a voltmeter; current is likewise a measurable electrical quantity, and the measuring tools include a multimeter, an ammeter and a clamp-on ammeter, among which the clamp-on ammeter is used for measuring current without cutting off power. The detection results of these electrical quantities are an important basis for understanding the operating state of the equipment and judging the fault location.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control the motor in the marine electrical power system; it belongs to low-voltage control apparatus and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The power of various auxiliary machines on ships is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities. The contactor is composed of multiple parts, including an arc chute, main contacts, an iron core and a coil. The arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the contacts break; it should be installed firmly, and the number of arc chute plates must not be insufficient; if it is cracked, damaged or severely carbonized, it should be replaced promptly, and when the chute plates are severely burnt, deformed or loose, a new chute should also be replaced. The main contacts are used to connect or break the main circuit current, and their closed state directly controls the operation of the motor. Silver main contacts should not be rubbed with emery cloth; they should be cleaned with a dry cloth or cleaning agent, and applying lubricating oil is prohibited to prevent poor contact; if copper main contacts change color or emit a burnt smell, it indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel need to be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the three-phase main contacts wear unevenly, the clearance can be adjusted by bending the moving contact bridge arm, and after adjustment, synchronous contact of the three phases must be ensured; in a forward-reverse drive system, poorly maintained main contacts are likely to become rough, overheat or even weld together and fail to open due to frequent commutation; when the main contacts are overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected as a replacement. The iron core is the magnetic conducting part in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil, and can serve as a reference point during insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to earth, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the iron core; in a through-type current transformer, the measured large-current conductor is directly linked with the iron core to replace the primary winding. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic part in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil's magnetic force to pull in or release, used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will prevent contactor KM from closing, causing the motor to have no power and fail to start, while failure or loss of the armature reaction spring is one of the main reasons why the contactor does not release or releases slowly after the stop button is pressed. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct reasons why the contactor armature cannot close and the motor fails to start; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

The contactor maintenance item applies to contactors; its content covers the inspection and upkeep of the above-mentioned components and is the basis for ensuring reliable operation of the contactor.

Starting box maintenance is a periodic maintenance item for the starting box covering rust removal, contact maintenance and safety inspection; the air compressor control circuit includes the starting box maintenance step. Before sailing, the starting boxes of out-of-service or standby equipment should be inspected; when in port, the starting box of the main engine service pump shaft should be inspected. During maintenance the power supply must be cut off and a "Do Not Switch On" warning sign hung at the remote switch. For rust removal use emery cloth or a scraper; scraping should remove oxides as far as possible without removing metal; after scraping, non-conductive surfaces not subject to friction may be coated with petroleum jelly or grease; where the anti-rust layer on painted parts peels off, anti-rust paint may be applied after rust removal, but painting is forbidden on terminal posts, smooth friction contact surfaces, threads and springs. Contact surfaces must be clean and show a metallic luster; initial and final pressure and overtravel must conform to specifications; oxides on contacts may be rubbed off with a fine file or glass emery cloth, and emery cloth with金刚砂 (corundum) is forbidden. At acceptance of the starting box, if the factory setting of protective devices deviates too much, readjustment should be made.

In single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control systems, common faults fall into two major categories, namely control system faults and motor internal faults.
