Motor internal faults refer to faults in internal parts of the motor such as the stator winding and bearings, which cause the motor to fail to start, automatic start failure, motor overheating or even burnout, and also excessive temperature rise; their repair methods are usually referred to elsewhere and are not repeated here. Control system fault symptoms include the system failing to start, the motor stopping immediately after the start button SBT resets, sudden stopping of the motor during operation, loud noise from the starting box after starting, and the indicator lamp not lighting.

Failure of the system to start is one of the common faults of single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control systems; its repair method is referred to elsewhere. When thermal relay FR has not operated and the motor suddenly stops, troubleshoot according to this fault. Causes of failure to start are various: an unconnected power supply causes failure to start, incorrect wiring of control equipment causes failure to start, undervoltage causes failure to start, stator winding phase-to-phase short circuit to earth, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit cause failure to start, and excessive load or brakes not released, or a faulty reduction gearbox, also cause failure to start. The corresponding remedies are: check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage and, if indeed too low, raise it appropriately; locate the short-circuit or open-circuit part and repair it, and if wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reduction gearbox; if the motor runs normally, inspect the reduction gearbox. In addition, poor contact causes random output action, in which case the terminal wiring should be checked; excessive reaction spring force, failure of the motor operating positioning switch, too large a reclosing contact surface, incorrect long-time-delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, and excessive reaction spring force must all be handled by readjustment.

The phenomenon in which the motor stops immediately after the start button SBT resets is manifested as the motor running when the start button SBT is pressed and stopping immediately when released and reset; this fault is classified as a control system fault, not a motor internal fault, and requires dedicated troubleshooting in ship electrical maintenance. The cause of this fault is loss of function of the self-holding auxiliary contact KM connected in parallel across button SBT, specifically the self-holding brush contact KM1 connected in parallel across button SBT; during repair, check whether the KM1 contact is intact, whether its leads are loose and whether contact is good. If FR has not operated and the motor suddenly stops, the troubleshooting method is the same as for the system failure-to-start fault.

Sudden stopping of the motor during operation is a common motor fault symptom in single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control systems, manifested as the motor suddenly stopping during operation after starting; operation of thermal relay FR is the cause of this phenomenon. When the motor heats up and FR operates on overload, this is normal; the load should be reduced, FR reset and the motor restarted; if the motor is not hot and shows no sign of overload yet FR operates, this is abnormal operation, and the FR setting must be readjusted, or FR itself is damaged and must be replaced and the setting readjusted.

Loud noise from the starting box after starting is one of the common control system faults of single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control systems; the noise inside the starting box is produced by the contactor, and its repair method is referred to elsewhere.

The indicator lamp not lighting is likewise one of the common faults of single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control systems; it is a series functional logic event composed of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact, and failure of any one of these four components will inevitably cause the indicator-lamp-not-lighting event, that is, failure of one element in the functional logic event composed of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact will cause the indicator lamp not to light, so during repair the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact must each be checked. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch used for auxiliary control; as a series system element, its failure causes the indicator-lamp-not-lighting fault; in motor forward-rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to achieve self-locking of the contactor coil. In single-speed reversible drive systems, the fault-checking steps and methods for the indicator lamp not lighting are the same as for the non-reversible starting box; if the fault exists in both forward and reverse states, the common parts such as the power supply and thermal relay should be checked.

In the electrical maintenance of refrigeration and cold-storage equipment, phenomena such as relatively large temperature variation, failure to defrost automatically and large temperature variation inside the box are also encountered. Relatively large temperature variation is manifested as large or high room temperature fluctuations and may be caused by the external environment, the refrigeration system or electrical control; external high temperature such as high seawater temperature affects refrigeration effect and raises room temperature, and this fault is easily triggered when a ship passes through high-temperature sea areas such as the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf in summer. Failure to defrost automatically specifically means that the evaporator of the LAKEN5BD refrigerated container cannot execute the automatic defrosting program; normal defrosting is initiated by the frost-thickness microswitch 63DA on the evaporator. Large temperature variation inside the box is mainly caused by abnormal operation of the electronic temperature controller; during repair, check whether the temperature-sensing element is intact.

Changeover-type faults occurring during operation of single-speed drive control systems are concentrated in three forms: early changeover, late changeover and failure to change over, all of which are closely related to the operating conditions of time relay KT, contactor KM2 and their coil circuits. As for early changeover, its direct consequence is excessive second inrush current when the motor starts; this current acts on the motor itself and further impacts the power grid. There are two causes of early changeover: first, the delay time of time relay KT is too short; second, the motor is difficult to start and the starting time is too long. When troubleshooting, one should not rush to adjust but should first turn the motor shaft by hand to check whether the resisting torque is too large, thereby determining whether the problem lies on the load side or the control parameter side. Only when inspection confirms that the delay is too short may the time relay knob be adjusted to increase the delay; if it is confirmed that the cause is difficulty in starting the motor, it is forbidden to directly adjust the time relay delay knob, otherwise the true mechanical or load defect will only be concealed. The above early changeover phenomenon occurs in the air compressor control circuit, that is, the air compressor control circuit may exhibit early changeover.

Late changeover is another timing deviation. Although it reduces the impact on the power grid, it prolongs the starting time of the motor, causing the motor to run in an undervoltage state and thus to heat up. For this phenomenon, the remedy is to adjust the time relay delay and reduce the delay time. Compared with early changeover, the adjustment direction for late changeover is exactly opposite, so determining which category the fault belongs to is a necessary prerequisite before taking action. Late changeover likewise occurs in the air compressor control circuit, that is, the air compressor control circuit may exhibit late changeover.

The consequences of failure to change over are more serious than the previous two. It first causes the machinery driven by the motor to fail to work normally, and at the same time causes the motor to overheat, whereupon the thermal protection relay operates; if the system uses autotransformer reduced-voltage starting, failure to change over will also burn out the autotransformer coil. This fault is mostly caused by faults in time relay KT and contactor KM2 themselves and faults in their coil circuits, that is, faults in time relay KT and contactor KM2 themselves and faults in their coil circuits are the direct causes of failure to change over. Whether the starting control has successfully changed over can be indicated by the indicator lamp not lighting or an audible signal sounding continuously. During troubleshooting, focus on checking time relay KT, contactor KM2 proper and their coil circuits, and do not focus only on the main circuit. The failure-to-change-over phenomenon also occurs in the air compressor control circuit, that is, the air compressor control circuit may exhibit failure to change over.

The indicator lamp not lighting is itself also one of the common faults of single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control systems; the air compressor control circuit may exhibit the indicator lamp not lighting.

The motor failing to start is another type of fault requiring systematic troubleshooting. Power supply problems, mechanical problems, excessive load and motor internal faults can all cause the motor to fail to start. Specifically for the failure-to-start phenomenon, its causes include an unconnected power supply, incorrect wiring of control equipment, undervoltage, stator winding phase-to-phase short circuit to earth, incorrect wiring, stator winding short circuit, and excessive load or brakes not released, or a faulty reduction gearbox. The corresponding remedies are: check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage and, if indeed too low, raise it appropriately; for the motor-fails-to-start fault, the motor internal fault should also be checked, that is, motor fails to start corresponds to the troubleshooting direction of checking motor internal fault. In this troubleshooting process, current, voltage and resistance are three basic measurable quantities: current values can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter and a clamp-on ammeter respectively, voltage values with a multimeter and a voltmeter, and resistance values with a multimeter. To measure current an ammeter is needed, connected in series after breaking the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems, and partial winding short circuit or phase failure is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating in AC motors, so the measurement results of the above electrical quantities have direct reference value for determining the fault location. A contactor comprises an arc chute, main contacts, iron core and coil. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; its coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start.

Time relays often appear in circuits with symbols such as KT, SJ and SL and belong to the electrical equipment used for control or protection in ship power systems. A current relay is an electromagnetic relay classified by the nature of the input signal; its coil carries electrical quantities and its structure is basically similar to that of a contactor; in AC three-speed electric windlasses it picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%. The symbol of the fuse is FU; it has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions, and when overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; the thermal relay uses a bimetallic strip as its sensing element and is mainly used for overload protection of small ship motors, with very large usage on board. When abnormal operation of the thermal relay causes the motor to suddenly stop, its setting must be readjusted.

The air compressor control circuit includes the acceptance check after overhaul of the starting box. Acceptance after overhaul of the starting box applies to reversible or non-reversible starting boxes after overhaul and before new installation. The appearance check requires that the shell and surface paint quality of the starting box meet requirements, all fixing screws be tight, the earthing screw bear a red mark, and watertightness conform to regulations; the electrical wiring inside the box must fully agree with the schematic and wiring diagrams, and all electrical apparatus and components must be intact and correctly installed; moving parts pushed by hand should be flexible without jamming, and the three-phase contacts should make good contact simultaneously; the insulation resistance to earth measured with a 500V insulation resistance tester shall be not less than 2MΩ; when the settings of thermal relays, overcurrent relays and time relays deviate too much, readjustment is required. The insulation resistance tester, also called a megohmmeter, consists of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is classified by the highest voltage generated by the hand-cranked generator into specifications of 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V, 2500V, etc.

The multimeter contains a changeover switch; the changeover switch is used to select the measurement object and the range, and on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set operating states and issue operating commands; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits to ensure that the secondary side of the current transformer is not opened. The rotating shaft is used to transmit torque and rotary motion; the moving parts of the two units of an electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same rotating shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch is also assembled from the contact system, operating handle, rotating shaft and panel by bolts.

In maintenance of single-speed drive control systems, the conventional fault diagnosis method takes observation as the starting step. The objects of observation cover abnormal phenomena, component condition, conductor condition and equipment operating parameters, that is, seeing whether components are jammed or damaged and whether conductors are loose, broken, chafed or burnt.

In instrument measurement, the insulation resistance tester, also called a megohmmeter, has as its main body a hand-cranked generator together with a moving-coil ratio meter, and three terminal posts L, E and G are provided on the panel. The insulation resistance tester contains a hand-cranked generator and also a moving-coil ratio meter, whose internal voltage circuit and current circuit each have a measuring coil, and whether the relative positions of these two coils are accurate needs to be checked. Classified by the highest voltage the hand-cranked generator can produce, insulation resistance testers have specifications of 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V, 2500V, etc. When measuring the insulation resistance to earth of an electrical equipment coil, terminal post E may be connected to the iron core. If there is a capacitor in the circuit, discharge it before measuring resistance; live measurement is absolutely not permitted. Current values can likewise be measured with a multimeter, or with an ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. When measuring current with an ammeter, break the circuit and then connect the ammeter in series. The clamp-on ammeter consists of a current transformer and an ammeter and works on the principle of the single-turn through-type current transformer; the conductor under test is equivalent to the primary winding, and its structure is a current transformer with an openable iron core plus an ammeter connected to it, so the circuit need not be broken during measurement. The electrical quantity measured by the clamp-on ammeter is current; it is used to check the starting current and three-phase balance of the motor, and the range selected should be greater than 7 times the rated current.

The symbol corresponding to the fuse is FU; it undertakes the two functions of overload protection and short circuit protection, and when overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or electrical equipment, the fuse element melts and the circuit is automatically cut off. The fuse belongs to distribution apparatus and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of spiral structure, 380V, 6~600A, used for overload or short circuit protection of circuits. The fuse element is a component of the fuse; in lighting and electric heating circuits, the rated current of the fuse element must be greater than or equal to the total load rated current; for direct starting of a single asynchronous motor, the fuse element rated current is taken as 1.5 to 2 times the motor rated current; for motor circuits with light load and infrequent starting, the fuse element rated current is taken as 2.5 to 4 times the motor rated current.

Contactors are responsible for controlling motors in ship power systems and are low-voltage control apparatus, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, with high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation and small size. A contactor comprises an arc chute, main contacts, iron core and coil. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin; it passes direct current and blocks alternating current; a fault in the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic part of the electromagnetic mechanism, pulled in or released by the coil's magnetic force to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature prevents contactor KM from closing, so the motor receives no power and cannot start; the shading coil is mounted on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core and is a copper ring-shaped component whose function is to eliminate armature vibration noise; once the shading coil breaks or falls off, the AC electromagnet emits relatively loud noise; after damage it can be repaired by copper welding, or the shading coil can be replaced directly.

The object targeted by contactor maintenance is the contactor.

The pressure relay takes pressure as its input signal and belongs to the non-electrical quantity relays; its sensing element is the air bag, and it is used for the automatic control and protection of marine boilers, air compressors and pump units; its actuating part is the contact, and in auxiliary boilers it is used as a control appliance to automatically control steam pressure. The temperature relay is likewise a non-electrical quantity relay and can serve both as a control appliance and as a protective appliance; it is commonly used in marine cooling water temperature alarms and cargo hold temperature regulation, and is used in large quantities on ships; when used for cooling water temperature alarm it performs a protective function, and when used in auxiliary boilers and similar applications it can serve as a control appliance.

The starting box commissioning steps apply to the air compressor control circuit. Before formally energizing, check whether the starting box meets the requirements; the model and capacity of the starting box should match the associated motor; the interior and exterior of the starting box should be intact and free of oil stains and dirt, and the internal wiring should conform to the drawings; the external wiring should also be checked, and whether the contactor operates flexibly must be carefully checked; if the contactor armature is obstructed and does not pull in properly, the coil current will be too large and burn out. Use a 500V insulation resistance tester to measure the insulation resistance. When the driven machinery is not allowed to reverse, the coupling must be disengaged to start the motor in order to confirm the direction of rotation. Use a clamp-on ammeter to detect the starting current, and the range should be selected at more than 7 times the rated current. Reduced-voltage starting commissioning must verify whether the changeover is accurate and detect the balance of the three-phase currents. If the contactor noise is too loud, check the cleanliness of the iron core mating surface and the condition of the shading coil. In the load test, measure the motor current under rated load and adjust the setting values of the protective appliances if necessary. After 2 hours of rated operation, measure the hot-state insulation resistance of the starting box and record the data.

The pump automatic control system consists of the control circuit, the motor and the main power supply, and undertakes such tasks as remote-control starting and stopping, automatic starting and automatic changeover, sequential starting and alarming in marine auxiliary machinery. It is generally required that the system can perform remote-control starting and stopping of each group of pumps in the centralized control room; when in the automatic control state, the pump shafts of the same group can perform automatic changeover; after the power grid loses power and power supply is restored, the pump shafts of each group automatically restart one by one in sequence according to the primary-secondary relationship. The system should also be provided with alarms and support local control of the pumps. In daily maintenance, the setting values of the time relay and the pressure relay need to be checked periodically, and before sailing it should be checked whether the automatic changeover operation is normal and whether the remote-control function is available. The automatic control system of the marine pump box likewise has the functions of remote-control starting and stopping, automatic changeover, sequential starting and alarming.

The time relay, pressure relay, voltage relay and contactor all belong to the electrical equipment used for control or protection in the marine power system. The time relay often appears in circuits with text symbols such as KT, SJ and SL. The pressure relay is a non-electrical quantity relay that takes pressure as its input signal, with the air bag as the sensing element and the contact as the actuating part, and is used for the automatic control and protection of marine boilers, air compressors and pump units; in auxiliary boilers it serves as a control appliance for automatically controlling steam pressure; in the fuel pump automatic control system, the pressure relay detects the system pressure to trigger automatic changeover and alarming of the pumps. The voltage relay is classified by the nature of its input signal and belongs to the electromagnetic relay; it realizes control or protection functions through the coil sensing voltage changes, and its coil takes the electrical quantity, namely voltage, as the excitation input quantity;

When the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced; winding it oneself will affect the operating value due to inaccurate turns. The contactor is a low-voltage control appliance, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size; it is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors; the contactor consists of parts such as the arc chute, main contact, iron core and coil, and contactor maintenance is carried out on these parts. The circuit breaker is a low-voltage distribution appliance, divided into the frame type and the molded-case type, and has both switching and protective functions; it can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid; circuit breaker maintenance is carried out according to the above characteristics.

The changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has relatively many selection positions and contacts; its functions include selecting the measurement object and selecting the range; on the main switchboard, the changeover switch is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not opened. The multimeter contains a changeover switch internally, and with it uses measurement functions such as resistance, voltage, current, capacitance and diode. The clamp-on ammeter is used with current as the measurement object, and the conductor need not be disconnected during measurement. The voltage transformer corresponds to the symbol TV and is used to transform the voltage ratio; the secondary side voltage is 100V, and one end of its secondary side is earthed; it belongs to the instrument transformers and has the nature of a voltage source; the secondary side standard voltage is usually 100V or 110V, and its working principle is consistent with that of the transformer, but its internal resistance is extremely small, and the output voltage hardly changes with the load; when working it is equivalent to a no-load transformer, the secondary side must strictly not be short-circuited, and a fuse must be installed on the primary side for short circuit protection. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA and has the nature of a current source, with extremely large internal resistance; the secondary side standard current is 5A or 1A; its primary side carries the load current I, which is transformed into the secondary current and then connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements; the secondary side must strictly not be open-circuited, the external ammeter terminals must have short-circuiting links, and these may be removed only after the wiring has been checked.

A capacitor consists of two metal films placed close together and separated in the middle by insulating material; its characteristic is that it blocks direct current and passes alternating current; in circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; its obstructive effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC); its measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. The measurable property of a resistor is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; in the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating function; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and the voltmeter; voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree, and overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems. The measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; the diode has unidirectional conductivity, with small conduction resistance under forward voltage and cutoff under reverse voltage; its measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance; in circuits it is often denoted by VD and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; by function it can be divided into rectifier diodes such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, Schottky diodes such as BAT85, as well as light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes, etc.; when marine electrical equipment uses diodes, the above categories are involved, and the diode detection steps apply to diodes. The potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the other pins changes as the shaft rotates; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component, and it is generally considered manually adjustable; in the auxiliary boiler control circuit, potentiometers W1 and W2 are used to adjust the delay or sensitivity of the time relay; in automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by the potentiometer R driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R′ driven by the motor M changes accordingly; the automatic fuel boiler contains such potentiometers. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; the insulation resistance tester contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. If the coil of the starting relay is damaged or the contact makes poor contact, the motor will not start and there will be no sound after the refrigerator is energized; if the contact sticks, the refrigerator motor may suddenly stop during starting or running; its troubleshooting methods include repairing or replacing the coil, and repairing or replacing the stuck contact.

The pump automatic control system will experience automatic start failure, that is, the pump auxiliary cannot start automatically. Main power supply faults, motor internal faults and control system component failures will all lead to automatic start failure. The causes of main power supply faults include RD fuse blowing, K not closing and the line not being supplied with power; when analyzing automatic start failure, the main power supply fault is considered in parallel with the motor and control system component faults; the main power supply fault is also one of the top-level events in the fault tree of the fuel pump failing to change over automatically, is one of the causes of the fuel pump unit failing to start automatically, and belongs to one of the top-level branches of automatic start failure in the fault tree. A main power supply fault will also cause both ahead and astern starting to fail when the master controller handle is moved, that is, once problems such as RD fuse blowing, K not closing or the line not being supplied with power occur on the main power supply side, neither the ahead nor the astern direction can establish a starting process after the master controller handle is operated. During troubleshooting it is assumed that the wire connections are intact and there is no short circuit or open circuit, and the fault analysis covers three aspects: the main power supply, the motor and the control system components. The motor internal fault is a cause of the pump auxiliary unit failing to start automatically and should be checked after eliminating main power supply and control element faults; in the fault tree of failure to change over and run automatically, it appears as a branch cause of "motor has no power" and is also one of the basic events in the fault tree causing the unit to fail to change over and run automatically. The motor internal fault refers to faults in internal parts of the motor such as the stator winding and bearings, which will cause the motor to fail to start, have low speed or have excessive temperature rise; it is one of the eight causes in the fault tree of the three-phase asynchronous motor failing to start, and also one of the eight possible causes of motor speed low after starting; in the marine single-speed non-reversible direct-on-line starting control system it belongs to one of the two major categories of common faults, and is one of the direct causes of the single-speed non-reversible AC electric drive system failing to start; the motor internal fault will cause the motor to fail to start, and will also cause the motor to overheat or even burn out. The specific causes of control system component failure include C not operating, J0 not operating, the WH changeover switch not being placed in the automatic start position, the run/standby selector switch KK not closing, J2 not operating, the contact not closing, ZL having no DC voltage output, and open-circuit faults in J2 itself and the components related to the J2 coil circuit. C not operating will prevent the pump auxiliary from starting automatically, and its causes are C itself being faulty or J0 not operating; the causes of J0 not operating include J0 itself being faulty, the WH switch not being set to the automatic position or the KK switch not closing; the causes of the J2 contact not closing include J2 itself being faulty, the coil circuit being open or the control power supply being faulty; the J2 contact not closing or J2 itself being faulty can lead to start failure; the J3 normally closed contact being open is one of the possible fault sources, and M1 being open or SJ being open can cause automatic start failure. This fault analysis excludes main power supply and motor internal faults and focuses on the logic elements of the control system.

The pump automatic control system will also experience fault symptoms such as failure to change over automatically, failure to start automatically in sequence, and failure of the unit to start and run during manual operation. Power supply not connected, incorrect wiring of control equipment, undervoltage, short circuit and earthing between stator winding phases, incorrect wiring, stator winding short circuit, as well as excessive load or the brake not being released and a faulty reducer, will all cause failure to start; for failure to start, check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point. In the main engine remote control system, a power supply fault is one of the main causes on the main power supply side of the unit failing to start automatically; a power supply fault will also cause motor overheating, PLC control system faults and main engine remote control failure; in the AC electric drive system, a power supply fault is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent leading to overheating; in the PLC control system, the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, so on ships the strategy of overall replacement is usually adopted.

Fault tree analysis uses the fault tree. The fault tree is a connected logic tree that does not contain closed loops, and uses graphical symbols to represent the logical combinations among the various events that cause an undesired event of the system; its structure is a logic tree, developing downward from the tree root of the top event, with branches representing accident events and nodes representing logical relationships; the most commonly used logical relationships are the AND relationship and the OR relationship. The fault tree contains the top event, intermediate events and basic events. When constructing a fault tree, electrical equipment faults such as motor fails to start are often selected as the top event, and the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as the power supply being normal and the control circuit being normal.

Automatic start failure manifests as the pump auxiliary failing to start automatically, and its fault analysis covers three aspects: the main power supply, the motor and the control system components. The main power supply fault is one of the causes of the fuel pump unit failing to start automatically, and its specific manifestations include RD fuse blowing, K not closing and the line not being supplied with power; in the fault tree it is one of the top-level branches of automatic start failure. The motor internal fault likewise leads to automatic start failure, and control system component failure is also one of the parallel causes. During troubleshooting it is assumed that the wire connections are intact and there is no short circuit or open circuit, and on this basis the above links are checked one by one.

Failure to change over automatically manifests as the standby pump auxiliary failing to start automatically and be put into operation. Normal changeover relies on the normally closed contact of the running pump J1 closing after power loss to control the starting of the standby pump, so the fault causes include two aspects: the standby pump failing to start automatically, and the J1 normally closed contact failing to close under power-loss conditions. For judgment, the standby unit KK can be placed in the run position; if it can start, it is determined to be a fault of the running unit J1; if it still cannot start when placed in the run position, it should be checked according to the automatic start failure fault. The cause of the standby pump auxiliary failing to start automatically needs to form a complete fault tree together with the J1 normally closed contact fault; its inspection method is the same as the automatic start failure fault inspection, involving the detection of the same components, and is distinguished from the changeover failure caused by the normally closed contact of the running pump auxiliary J1 not closing after power loss. The J1 normally closed contact failing to close under power-loss conditions is one of the causes of the pump auxiliary control system failing to change over automatically; under normal logic, after J1 loses power the normally closed contact should close to control the automatic starting of the standby pump auxiliary; during troubleshooting it is necessary to check whether J1 and its normally closed contact in the running pump auxiliary control system are faulty. This fault tree covers causes such as the main power supply, RD fuse blowing, WH, J2, J3 contacts and coil open circuits. In another system, when b1 is placed in the "0" position the system is in manual mode and automatic changeover is prohibited.

Failure to start automatically in sequence manifests as the unit failing to start and be put into operation with the set delay according to the primary-secondary sequence. The sequential starting function is realized under the control of the delay relay SJ2 or SJ3; after the power grid is energized the unit should start with the set delay according to the primary-secondary sequence and be put into operation, and a fault of the delay relay SJ2 or SJ3 will cause the system to fail to start automatically in sequence. During troubleshooting, first check whether the delay relay SJ2 operates normally; after confirming that SJ2 is normal, continue troubleshooting according to the method for the automatic start failure fault. A power supply fault will also cause the RUN lamp to go out, and at this time the power supply should be checked. The corresponding handling methods are: check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find the short circuit or open circuit location and repair it, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer, and if the motor can run normally, check the reducer part.

When troubleshooting the above faults, the multimeter is a commonly used tool, and it can be used to measure voltage and detect diodes. The diode has unidirectional conductivity, with small conduction resistance under forward voltage and cutoff under reverse voltage; its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity, and it is commonly used in circuits such as rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization and polarity protection, and is often denoted by VD in circuits. Diodes include categories such as light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes; the diode detection steps apply to diodes, and during detection its polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance can be measured. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment.

The contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil; contactor maintenance applies to the contactor. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil's magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will prevent contactor KM from closing, causing the motor to have no power and fail to start; failure or loss of the armature return spring is one of the main reasons why the contactor does not release or releases slowly after the stop button is pressed. The main contact is the switching component in the contactor used to make or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor; discoloration of the copper main contact or a burnt smell indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel must be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the main contact has been overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected as a replacement. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch and the contactor, used for control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection, and is also one of the main components of the generator main switch; in the motor forward-rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize self-locking of the contactor coil. In the automatic switching logic of the main and standby pumps, the auxiliary contact is used to cut off the circuit of the originally running unit and provide self-holding for the new unit. In the automatic switching system of the pump group, the intermediate relay, after pressure is established, is energized and self-holds and prevents erroneous switching after the start delay ends; it is an electromagnetic relay, similar in construction to the contactor, and is used to expand contact capacity and number and for control logic conversion, and its fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the contactor inspection method. The thermal relay is a protective relay with a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors, and is used in large quantities on ships. The time relay undertakes the delay task in the control circuit, and its setting value needs to be checked regularly.

The pump automatic control system consists of the control line, motor, main power supply, etc., and has the functions of remote start and stop, automatic start and automatic switching, sequential starting and alarm.

Troubleshooting of the pump automatic control system usually starts with the conventional fault diagnosis method, and the first step of this method is to use observation. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, check whether parts are jammed or damaged, whether wires are loose, broken, chafed or burnt, and note whether operating parameters deviate from the normal range. For more complex control logic, fault tree analysis is used, with the fault tree as a tool for analysis. The time relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship's power system, with common designations KT, SJ and SL. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker, and is the inspection work carried out on the circuit breaker body.

The contactor includes two components: the main contact and the coil. As far as the motor itself is concerned, faults in the stator winding, bearings, etc. will cause excessive temperature rise; such internal faults include stator winding and bearing damage, and are one of the direct causes of failure to start of the single-speed non-reversible AC electric drive system, and belong to one of the two common categories of faults in the single-speed non-reversible direct-on-line starting control system on ships.

The pump automatic control system may also exhibit the phenomenon that the unit cannot be started and run during manual operation, that is, in manual operation mode the pump unit cannot be started and run. During inspection, first press the start button 1b2 and observe whether contactor 1c1 operates. If 1c1 operates and the motor hums, it indicates phase failure of the power supply or mechanical jamming of the pump shaft; when the humming is heard, the stop button should be pressed immediately to prevent the motor from being locked-rotor for a long time and burning out. Power supply phase failure is a fault state in which one phase is missing from the three-phase power supply, often causing the motor to fail to start or to have abnormal speed; it will cause motor speed low after starting, and will also cause the motor temperature rise to be high; when locked rotor occurs due to phase failure, it should be stopped immediately to prevent the motor from burning out after long operation.

If 1c1 operates but there is no sound, check the closing of the main circuit contacts, motor faults and the state of thermal relay 1e. If 1c1 does not operate but intermediate relay 1d1 operates, it indicates that 1c1 itself is faulty or the 1d1 contact is not closed; this is one case in which 1c1 does not operate; if 1c1 does not operate and 1d1 does not operate, check the control power supply and the components of the 1d1 coil circuit; at this time it is judged that 1d1 does not operate, and it should be checked whether there is control power supply and whether the components in the 1d1 coil circuit are intact. The case where 1d1 does not operate is different from the case where 1d1 operates but 1c1 does not operate; the latter points to a fault in 1c1 itself or an unclosed 1d1 contact. Both the case where 1c1 does not operate and the case where 1d1 does not operate will cause the unit to fail to start and run during manual operation; this phenomenon appears after pressing the start button 1b2 and serves as a basis for judging a main circuit or control circuit fault. Check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately;

If the main circuit is not connected after the thermal relay is connected, one of the causes is that the external wiring screws are not tightened, and the corresponding inspection method is to tighten the external wiring screws. The circuit breaker may exhibit various fault symptoms during operation: when the circuit breaker is manually operated, the contacts cannot close, that is, when the circuit breaker is manually operated, the contacts cannot close; in addition, one phase contact cannot close, the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1 h after closing, the undervoltage trip unit has noise, and the circuit breaker temperature rise is too high.

According to the type of power supply, the electrical system of a ship's cargo winch can be divided into two major categories: AC electric cargo winch and DC electric cargo winch, among which the AC electric cargo winch is more commonly used on ships. The AC electric cargo winch is generally driven by a cage-type pole-changing variable-speed motor with three speeds; according to the speed regulation range from medium speed to high speed, it can be divided into constant-power speed regulation and constant-torque speed regulation. Domestic systems mostly use constant-power speed regulation or derived forms, such as PHKJ-1A-H with JZF-H type motor; foreign systems mostly use constant-torque speed regulation systems. Some AC electric cargo winches use three-phase wound-rotor asynchronous motors, with speed regulation by rotor series resistance or thyristor. The constant-power speed regulation system requires reliable overload protection and two-boom same-speed interlock control. There are many types of drive control for DC electric cargo winches, including the generator-motor set drive system, relay-contactor control system, magnetic amplifier control system and AEC control system, etc. Because DC motors have good speed regulation performance, they are often used in ship G-M systems. At present, ships generally use AC power systems, and DC electric cargo winches with relay-contactor control are no longer common.

From the perspective of mechanical structure, the AC electric cargo winch includes three types: the double-boom cargo winch, the single-boom cargo winch and the deck crane. The double-boom cargo winch drives the cargo winches separately through two motors; the starting, speed regulation, forward and reverse rotation and braking control of the motors are realized by the electrical control system, and it has the characteristics of smooth operation, low noise, compact design, and convenient operation and daily maintenance; its disadvantages are that cargo positioning and luffing are difficult, and it is convenient for remote control and automation. In the application of DC electric cargo winches, one AC motor can drive one DC generator to supply power to the two DC motors of the double-boom cargo winch at the same time, that is, the two-shaft output system. The single-boom cargo winch drives the hoisting winch, luffing winch and slewing winch separately through three motors, and the starting, speed regulation, forward and reverse rotation and braking of each motor are completed by their respective electrical control lines; it is one classification form of the electric cargo winch.

The hoisting mechanism, slewing mechanism and luffing mechanism of the deck crane and their control equipment are all on the same working platform, and the winch, platform and boom can all rotate together about its central axis; operation is relatively flexible, cargo handling speed is fast and production efficiency is high, but the structure is complex and compact, and maintenance is inconvenient. The deck crane often adopts a three-shaft output system in which an AC motor drives a DC generator to supply power to three DC motors; during maintenance, check whether various limit protection and alarm devices are normal.

Maintenance of the electrical system of the cargo winch involves many aspects; the AC electric cargo winch includes maintenance of the electromagnetic control panel and control box, maintenance of the master controller and cam controller, the electromagnetic brake and its maintenance, and daily maintenance of the electrical system of the AC electric cargo winch. The first-level maintenance cycle of the electromagnetic control panel and control box is generally once every 2~3 months, including removing accumulated dust and dirt from each component, checking the completeness of buttons, indicator lights, switches, instruments and other parts, ensuring fasteners are not loose, checking and maintaining relays and contactors, ensuring mechanical and electrical interlocks are reliable, ensuring mechanical moving parts are flexible, and adding lubricating oil when necessary. The first-level maintenance of the master controller and cam controller should be carried out once per voyage or before use, checking external devices such as handles, handwheels, indicator lights, switches and buttons, checking whether the actual position of the controller pointer matches and the positioning accuracy, cleaning the contacts and cam surfaces, checking whether the internal springs are damaged or displaced, and cleaning the arc chute; if damaged or with poor insulation, it must be repaired or replaced. For master controllers using a variable resistor, the contact between the sliding arm and the resistor needs to be checked during second-level maintenance. The resistor includes the variable resistor; the variable resistor, also called a potentiometer, has three pins and can change the resistance value by rotating the shaft to adjust the voltage or current in the circuit, wherein the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the two pins changes with shaft rotation.

The electromagnetic brake is composed of an electromagnetic armature disc, spring, moving plate, friction plate or friction block, end cover, etc., and often adopts a disc-type structure integrated with the motor to improve watertightness and braking stability. When the coil is energized, the electromagnet pulls in and compresses the spring so that the moving plate rotates freely; when power is off, the spring pushes the armature back to generate braking torque. The power supply of the DC electromagnetic brake must be supplied after rectification from the same power supply. When the coil current is less than the holding current, the medium- and high-speed windings should be de-energized in time to prevent the load from falling. When friction plate wear causes excessive clearance, the braking torque decreases and the slip distance is large; if the clearance is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply. Besides the disc type, there is also the open-type electromagnet shoe brake, which uses a lever mechanism to brake by spring tension when power is off. Maintenance of the electromagnetic brake is divided into multiple levels: first-level maintenance is carried out per voyage or before use, mainly measuring the clearance and adjusting it; second-level maintenance has a cycle of 3~6 months, requiring partial disassembly and cleaning of the core pull-in surface to prevent insufficient holding force or failure to release the brake caused by a too-dirty core; third-level maintenance is carried out every 3~4 years or during ship repair, and is handled simultaneously when the motor is disassembled. The electromagnetic brake corresponds to operational contents such as the electromagnetic brake clearance measurement method, electromagnetic brake clearance adjustment and electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment.

During maintenance and testing, the multimeter is used to measure parameters such as resistance, voltage, current and the polarity and inter-electrode resistance of the thyristor, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. The thyristor, also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, has measurable properties including polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode. The measuring tool for resistance is the multimeter; when measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect. Current measuring tools include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit; motor overcurrent is a direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. Voltage measuring tools include the multimeter and voltmeter; voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship's power system, belongs to low-voltage control appliances, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size; it is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes components such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil. The arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the contacts break; if damaged or with poor insulation, it must be repaired or replaced; if cracked, damaged or severely carbonized, it should be replaced in time; if the grid plates are severely burnt, deformed or loose, a new chute should be replaced. During second-level maintenance of the contactor, check whether the non-magnetic shim, shading coil and copper sleeve are damaged; during regular inspection, confirm that the shading coil on the contactor armature is not loose or higher than the contact surface. The shading coil is installed on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core; it is a copper ring-shaped component used to eliminate armature vibration noise; breakage or falling off of the shading coil will cause the AC electromagnet to produce greater noise; when damaged, it can be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil can be directly replaced. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to pull in and the motor failing to start. The above inspection and maintenance contents all belong to the scope of contactor maintenance, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor body and its components such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil.

The time relay is used for control or protection in the ship's power system, with designations such as KT, SJ and SL. The thermal relay uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and is mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors; it is used in large quantities on ships, and generally the overload protection of small motors is completed by it. The AC electric cargo winch may exhibit various fault symptoms during operation, including high temperature rise of the electromagnetic brake and excessively fast wear of the friction plate, as well as failure of the electromagnetic brake to pull in and locked rotor of the motor. In addition, there may also be motor overheating or even burning out, loss of control of the control system, failure to start when the master controller handle is moved to either forward or reverse, starting only in forward or only in reverse when the master controller handle is moved, no high speed and medium speed in either forward or reverse, excessive cargo slip distance during braking, single-phase operation of the motor, failure of the constant-power cargo winch to run at high speed under light load, failure of the electromagnetic brake to release, immediate release of the electromagnetic brake after pulling in, heating of the electromagnetic brake, and excessively fast wear of the friction plate, etc.

The AC electric cargo winch is widely used on ships, and its electrical system covers different models such as the double-boom cargo winch, single-boom cargo winch and deck crane. The DC electric cargo winch is also a member of the electric cargo winch family, and its drive control scheme is often the same as that of the ship's AC electric cargo winch. Foreign systems mostly use constant-torque speed regulation systems; the mooring winch has basically the same drive control scheme as the cargo winch; mooring winches are divided into DC and AC types, and at present most use AC three-speed windlass and mooring winch or G-M system windlass and mooring winch; the drive control systems of the two are basically the same, and they belong to short-time duty equipment, allowing 25 starts within 30 min.

Daily maintenance is divided into three parts: inspection patrol, general servicing each voyage, and periodic maintenance. The inspection patrol system should be formulated according to the type of cargo loaded and unloaded and the technical condition of the equipment, monitoring the temperature rise of the motor and electromagnetic brake, which should not exceed the allowable temperature rise during operation; if the motor overheats, check whether the motor ventilation and cooling system is normal, and at the same time check whether the motor stall and the action and release of the electromagnetic brake meet the technical requirements. If the AC electric cargo winch is improperly maintained, the motor will overheat or even burn out, and the electromagnetic brake will also have consequences such as high temperature rise and excessively fast wear of the friction plate.

The electromagnetic brake is an important braking component of the drive motor of deck machinery such as cargo winches and windlasses, realizing brake release or braking through electromagnetic attraction and spring return. When power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. If the gap is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply. In the disc-type electromagnetic brake of deck machinery, a coil open circuit will cause the spring to push the armature back, producing braking torque. In the disc-type brake, the armature disc is pushed back by the spring and jammed between the end cover and the friction plate to produce braking torque; adjusting the manual release screw can limit the return stroke of the armature disc being pushed back, thereby adjusting the tightness of the brake; if the measured gap between the armature disc and the electromagnet core is too large, the friction plate or block should be adjusted or replaced with a new one. When the shoe-type brake is energized, the armature is attracted and pushes the lever to open the brake shoe to release the brake; when power is cut off, braking relies on spring tension. In the electromagnet shoe-type brake, when power is cut off, the spring tension forces the brake shoe to grip the brake wheel tightly for braking. The surface roughness of the brake wheel is required to be not less than 3.2, the steady-state working temperature should be less than 180℃, and it is necessary to prevent erosion by oil, rain and ice and snow. The wear amount of the brake shoe must be less than 2mm, and the wear amount of the brake shoe tightness of each model of traction machine should be less than 2mm; if it exceeds the standard, the brake shoe or brake arm must be replaced; in the brake-release state, the gap between the two arc surfaces of the brake shoe and the brake wheel should be kept at
0.1～
0.3mm.

The maintenance of the electromagnetic brake is divided into three levels. The first-level maintenance is carried out every voyage or before use, mainly measuring the gap and adjusting it if necessary. The second-level maintenance cycle is 3~6 months, including partial disassembly and cleaning to prevent the core attraction surface from being too dirty, causing insufficient holding force and resulting in failure to release the brake or a seemingly released but not released fault; check whether the armature, copper sleeve and spring are deformed, and if deformed, repair or replace them; when replacing the brake plate spring, attention should be paid to the relevant assembly requirements. In the electromagnetic brake, a too dirty core attraction surface will cause insufficient holding force, resulting in failure to release the brake or a seemingly released but not released condition. Insufficient holding force is also a fault cause leading to welding of contactor contacts or failure of the electromagnetic brake to release the brake, usually caused by low voltage, mechanical resistance or dirty core; to deal with insufficient holding force of the contactor, check whether the power supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage and eliminate mechanical resistance.

For the electromagnetic brake, there are three corresponding maintenance procedures, namely the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, electromagnetic brake gap adjustment and electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment. The electromagnetic brake gap adjustment stipulates that when the friction plate or block is seriously worn, the gap will be too large, and at this time the friction plate or block can only be replaced; after replacing with a new friction plate or block, if the gap is still too large, it may be that the end cover is not screwed in place or the armature disc and the end cover have been worn by long-term friction, causing the gap to be too large. When the brake is too tight and causes the end cover temperature to rise sharply, the spring return stroke can be changed by adjusting the manual release screw; when the gap is large due to wear of the armature disc and end cover, causing insufficient braking, shims need to be inserted into the spring holes; the thickness of the shims placed in each spring hole must be the same to prevent local stress and serious heating during braking. When after replacing with a new friction plate or friction block, the slip is too large and the braking torque is insufficient, the manual release screw should be unscrewed; if the slip is still too large at this time, it indicates that the working length of the spring has increased, causing insufficient spring force; at this time, take out end cover 3, remove the spring from the rotating shaft and check it. When the spring force is insufficient due to long-term working fatigue of the spring, a new spring should be replaced; it is recommended to replace all of them or place old and new ones alternately and evenly.

The contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contacts, core and coil. Coil open circuit is one of the main fault causes leading to the contactor fails to pick up; the method for detecting coil open circuit is to measure the coil resistance with a multimeter after power is cut off to determine whether it is open. A jammed armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start; failure or damage of the armature reaction spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and its fault analysis and handling can be carried out with reference to the relevant maintenance methods. The intermediate relay is a type of electromagnetic relay, similar in construction to the contactor, used to expand contact capacity and number and for control logic conversion; its fault analysis and handling can be carried out with reference to the maintenance methods of the contactor; in the constant-power three-speed cargo winch, when the load exceeds half load, the intermediate relay operates to cut off the high-speed winding circuit.

The marine motor includes the rotating shaft, a mechanical transmission component; the rotating shaft is used to transmit torque and rotational motion, and is commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments; the movable parts of the two units of the electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same rotating shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a rotating shaft and a panel, assembled by bolts. The core is the magnetic conductive component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as the insulation measurement reference point; when measuring the insulation resistance to ground of the coil of electrical equipment, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in the through-type current transformer, the large current conductor under test is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and their relative position accuracy needs to be checked. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil magnetic force to attract or release, used to control contact action or braking. The observation contents include abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status, and equipment operating parameters; specifically check whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, scratched or burnt. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, divided into analog and digital types, mainly composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; at full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. The MF-47 multimeter is a type of multimeter, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A, and its panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The analog multimeter and the digital multimeter also belong to multimeters. The multimeter can be used to measure various electrical quantities and device parameters such as resistance, voltage, current, capacitance, diode, transistor, thyristor, photosensitive device and thermocouple.

Overheating or even burning out of the motor of the AC electric cargo winch is often not caused by a single reason. Failure of the load relay ZJ is the main cause of heavy-load overspeed operation; the domestic constant-power motor cargo winch precisely uses the load relay to prevent the load from exceeding half load and raising the speed. The original load relay ZJ has poor reliability and cannot play a good protective role; through continuous improvement, a transistor-type load relay is now available, which has high sensitivity and is little affected by grid voltage fluctuations. If not discovered, adjusted and repaired in time, motor overheating will occur, and over time or with other faults the motor may burn out. Long-term overload and excessively high operating frequency are another cause of motor overheating: when using the cargo winch, because the loading and unloading personnel find it difficult to accurately estimate the cargo weight, it operates overloaded, and at the same time they hope to increase the loading and unloading speed, so the operating frequency often exceeds 240/480/480 closing times/hour; once this limit is exceeded, it is regarded as excessively high operating frequency. In pursuit of speed and because it is difficult to accurately estimate the cargo weight, the loading and unloading personnel easily cause the cargo winch operating frequency to be too high, and excessively high operating frequency is one of the main causes of motor overheating or even burning out in cargo winch motors.

The cause of long-term overload and excessively high operating frequency will likewise cause the motor to overheat or even burn out. In addition, motor stall and motor internal fault will likewise cause the motor to overheat or even burn out. As far as the protection links are concerned, the thermocouple in the stator slot is easily damaged before leaving the factory and cannot be repaired, resulting in poor protection reliability; the setting value of the thermal relay RJ in the main circuit is difficult to set accurately, and the protection for large currents is rough; the transistor-type load relay has high sensitivity and can replace ZJ to prevent heavy-load overspeed.

The thermocouple is often buried in the winding end in the motor stator slot for overheating protection, but it is easily damaged before leaving the factory and cannot be repaired. Normally, the resistance between the two terminal posts is zero; if infinity is measured, it indicates that the hot end is open and has been damaged. The voltage relay is used for undervoltage protection in the constant-power three-speed cargo winch; after being energized, the normally open contact closes to energize the control circuit; poor contact of contacts is one of the fault causes leading to the AC electric cargo winch not turning in either forward or reverse. Periodic maintenance requires checking and adjusting the operating voltage and release voltage values of the voltage relay coil to meet the technical requirements; when the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced, and self-winding will affect the operating value due to inaccurate number of turns. The contactor includes the arc chute, main contacts, core and coil. Excessively high operating frequency will cause the coil to overheat or burn out; when dealing with contactor coil faults caused by excessively high operating frequency, a contactor one current rating larger should be selected as the replacement. When power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. If the gap is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply.

The marine motor includes bearings and windings. The bearing is used to support the rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause the motor to overheat, vibrate and have abnormal noise; bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when the upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and the characteristic of overheating of the bearing end cover. Checking the bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition are both carried out for the bearing. Generator bearing overheating and bearing overheating both correspond to replacing the bearing; replacing the bearing is aimed at bearing wear, damage or overheating faults in equipment such as electric fans, electric drills and generators, used to repair the fault of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan caused by bearing wear, and also used to eliminate the operating noise of the electric fan caused by bearing damage. The winding is the coil component wound with enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes leading to overcurrent and overheating of the AC motor; the winding insulation of the marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proof, mildew-proof and salt-oil-mist-proof and be oil-resistant.

The insulation resistance tester, also known as the megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, and is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G; it is a portable instrument composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand the equipment status; the multimeter is used for the measurement of resistance, voltage, current, transistor and thermocouple; the clamp-on ammeter is used for the measurement of current.

The transistor internally contains two PN junctions and has current amplification capability, and is divided into NPN type and PNP type, commonly represented in circuits by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17. The main models include A92, 9015 (PNP type) and A42, 9014, 9018, etc. (NPN type). The measurable properties of the transistor include transistor type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor; marine electrical equipment uses transistors, and the transistor has a transistor fault, and the transistor fault belongs to the transistor.

In the AC electric cargo winch, the electromagnetic brake is a key component related to hoisting safety, and its common faults are manifested as high temperature rise and excessively fast wear of the friction plate. The causes of this phenomenon can be found from two aspects: the control circuit and the brake body. In terms of the control circuit, if the setting of time relay 2SJ is too short, the regenerative braking of the motor cannot take effect in time, and before the speed has decreased, the electromagnetic brake brakes at high speed, thereby causing high temperature rise of the brake and accelerated wear of the friction plate. If the discharge resistor of the electromagnetic brake coil circuit is too large and discharges too fast, high-speed braking will likewise occur, with consequences similar to too short a setting of 2SJ. If the resistance of the economy resistor is too large or it is connected in too early, the brake will be in a state of seemingly open but not open, directly causing accelerated wear of the friction plate. After the diode in the discharge circuit of the brake coil breaks down, the discharge resistor becomes a shunt circuit in the circuit, which will also cause excessively fast wear of the friction plate. The above-mentioned too short setting of time relay 2SJ, too large discharge resistor of the electromagnetic brake coil circuit, too large resistance of the economy resistor or too early connection, and breakdown of the diode in the discharge circuit of the brake coil all belong to the control circuit side causes of the fault of high temperature rise of the electromagnetic brake and excessively fast wear of the friction plate.

From the perspective of the brake body, too small friction plate gap, uneven gap and deformation of the friction plate will all cause heating and serious wear of the brake. Too strong spring force inside the brake, internal short circuit of the coil, too small holding force, the spring falling off so that the armature is obstructed, and uneven or reduced gap are also causes of excessively fast wear of the friction plate. These factors are parallel to the aforementioned control circuit causes and together constitute the fault sources of high temperature rise of the electromagnetic brake and excessively fast wear of the friction plate. When power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. If the gap is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply.
