For the electromagnetic brake, maintenance correspondingly includes the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, used to determine the size of the gap between the armature disc and the electromagnet core; it also correspondingly includes electromagnetic brake gap adjustment, so as to restore the appropriate distance between plates when the gap is too large or too small; it also correspondingly includes electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment, to obtain the required braking effect by changing the spring compression amount or the position of the manual release screw.

Motor stall is another type of fault in the cargo winch electrical system that needs attention. When the motor stalls, the stator current increases greatly, and the temperature rise is fast and high. The stall currents of the 28-pole, 8-pole and 4-pole of the domestic constant-power JZF-H type three-speed asynchronous motor are 2Ie, 4Ie and 4Ie respectively. If the master controller handle is quickly thrown to the medium-speed or high-speed position during starting, the acceleration contactor 2C of the medium-speed winding and the ZDQ coil are energized at the same time; if 2C acts faster than ZDQ, short-time stall of the medium-speed winding may occur. In the JZF-H type motor, welding of the ZDC auxiliary contact will cause long-term stall of the medium-speed winding; welding or jamming in the closed state of the auxiliary contact of the braking contactor will also cause long-term stall of the winding. When the brake itself fails and cannot release, it will directly cause the motor to stall. The braking contactor ZDC fails to pick up and its auxiliary contact is welded or jammed closed, causing long-term stall of the medium-speed winding. During braking, if the 2SJ delay is too long and the ZDQ discharge resistor is relatively large, low-speed winding stall will occur; failure of time relay 5SJ will cause stall of the low-speed winding. Motor stall will cause the motor to overheat or even burn out.

In the control of the JZF-H type three-speed asynchronous motor, quickly throwing the master controller handle makes the operation too frequent, which will cause serious heating of the motor. Too frequent operation belongs to the electrical fault cause, referring to the equipment acting too many times per unit time or the operation interval being too short, resulting in contact overheating, wear or misoperation of the thermal relay. In the contactor, too frequent operation will cause the contacts to overheat or burn, and is also one of the main causes of excessive contact wear.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system, belonging to ship low-voltage control appliances, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, with the characteristics of high operating frequency and long life, and also with the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation and small size. The contactor includes the arc chute, main contacts, core and coil.

Contact welding is a fault symptom in which the contacts of a contactor cannot release due to welding, often caused by insufficient capacity, short circuit or too little pressure. Contact welding directly causes the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed; that is, the contactor not releasing for a long time or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed is precisely the consequence of contact welding. Too small a contact capacity is one of the main causes of contact welding; a load short circuit will cause contact welding, and the contacts must be replaced after the fault is cleared; insufficient holding force, poor contact of contacts caused by severe burning of the contact surface or the presence of burrs, metal particles, etc., too little pressure of the contact spring, and too frequent operation or overload use will all cause contact welding. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. A circuit breaker is a switching device used in the ship's power system to protect the circuit; it belongs to marine power distribution equipment and is divided into the frame type and the molded-case type, having both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during a short circuit fault; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid.

A motor internal fault will cause the motor to fail to start and automatic start failure, and will also cause the motor to overheat or even burn out. Faults in the stator winding and bearing will cause the motor to show excessive temperature rise. A marine motor includes a bearing and a winding;

When measuring electrical quantities and device performance such as resistance, current and diodes, the multimeter is a common tool. The measurable property of a resistor is its resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; a diode has unidirectional conductivity and is commonly denoted VD in circuits, and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity, with a small conduction resistance under forward voltage and a very large or infinite resistance under reverse voltage. Diodes are divided by function into rectifier diodes, isolation diodes, Schottky diodes, etc., for example 1N4004, 1N4148, BAT85; diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The diode test procedure applies to diodes, and marine electrical equipment also uses diodes.

Once the control system of an AC electric cargo winch loses control, cargo handling cannot proceed as intended by the operation. So-called loss of control of the control system refers to the phenomenon in which the cargo winch does not work as required by the master controller handle, causing control failure. When the cargo winch loses control, maintenance personnel must quickly clear the fault to ensure normal operation. The maintenance personnel undertaking this work should be familiar with the structure of the electrical equipment, the working principle, the functions of the components (assemblies) and their locations, and should master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, so as to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary diagnosis through these means. Maintenance personnel must also be very familiar with the circuits of the whole ship's electrical equipment, the working principles and the locations of all components, so as to quickly determine on site in which link the fault occurs.

Moving the master controller handle, neither forward nor reverse can start, is one of the more common loss-of-control faults. The fault cause of this symptom lies in the common part of the forward and reverse control circuits. A main power supply fault, a blown fuse in the control circuit, the brake contactor not operating or poor contact of contacts, poor closing of the master controller contacts or damage to the master controller, the damper switch not being connected, the temperature relay not reset or poor contact of contacts, poor contact of contacts of the undervoltage relay, and poor contact of the emergency switch will all cause neither forward nor reverse to start when the master controller handle is moved. During troubleshooting, if the fan does not turn, check the main power supply, the fuse and whether the thermal relay RJ has reset; if the fan turns, check the auxiliary contact of the fan contactor FSC and the pull-in condition of the zero-voltage relay. In addition, check whether the internal contacts of the master controller are in good contact, whether any have fallen off or are damaged, confirm whether the brake has been released, and check whether the motor itself has a fault.

As far as the power supply not being connected is concerned, it likewise leads to the result of failure to start.

Moving the master controller handle and having only forward or only reverse is another manifestation of loss of control. One of the directional contactors being faulty, poor contact of contacts of a directional contactor, or a fault in the master controller will all cause this symptom. Specifically, poor contact of contacts of the cargo winch directional contactor (ZC or FC) will cause only forward or only reverse when the handle is moved; during troubleshooting, check the contact condition of the main and auxiliary contacts of the two contactors ZC or FC, and also check the contact state of the master controller to clear the fault.

No high speed and no medium speed in either forward or reverse has many causes. Long-term overload operation of the cargo winch fan will cause the thermal relay to operate, so that high and medium speeds cannot run, among which long-term overload of the fan causing operation of thermal relay 2RJ and release of contactor FSC is one of the main causes. Poor contact of contacts of the auxiliary contact of fan contactor FSC can cause this fault, poor contact of contacts of the auxiliary contact of the brake contactor is also a possible cause, and a fault in the internal contacts of the master controller can likewise lead to the absence of high and medium speeds. When this fault occurs, the cargo can only be lowered using the low speed position. Long-term overload will not only prevent high and medium speeds from running, but will also cause a high temperature rise of the motor, and in severe cases even cause the generator to overheat; long-term overload operation of an asynchronous motor will cause reduced insulation performance, aging or mechanical damage; when checking excessive motor temperature rise, it is necessary to check whether there is long-term overload in the mechanical aspect.

Excessive cargo slip during braking is a typical fault in the braking link of the cargo winch. Generally, for an electric cargo winch at a rated speed of 40 m/min, the slip should not exceed 0.4 m. The main causes include poor coordination of the three-stage braking or a fault in the electromagnetic brake. If the delay setting of time relay 2SJ is too short, the regenerative braking time of the motor is short, and braking at high speed will increase the slip; if the 2SJ delay is too long, the electromagnetic brake will brake too late, which will also make the slip too long; to avoid excessive slip, the 2SJ delay is generally set at 0.7 s. When the core of the electromagnetic brake has residual magnetism, under the action of the residual magnetic holding force, the armature will be released too late, causing the cargo to be in free fall and producing a large slip. Friction plates that are too smooth, too large a gap, and insufficient reaction spring force will all affect the slip; the above factors are one of the manifestations of a fault in the electromagnetic brake.

Single-phase operation of the motor also often accompanies cargo winch faults. When the three-phase contacts of a certain position contactor in the main circuit cannot make contact at the same time, or a contact of a certain phase is damaged or has fallen off, single-phase operation often occurs, and the motor cannot start when energized; but after starting at medium or high speed, when the handle is moved back to the low speed position, the low speed can still turn, but the load torque is small, and the same phenomenon also occurs in the medium and high speed positions. When single-phase operation is caused by damage to or falling off of the contacts of the main circuit contactor, the motor shows failure to start at the instant of energization. Failure of the motor to start may also be caused by a power supply problem, a mechanical problem, excessive load or a motor internal fault; when checking, follow the principle from simple to complex: first check the power supply, then check whether the shaft is seized or the load is excessive, and finally check the interior of the motor, and correspondingly check the power supply voltage and check the motor internal fault.

At the device level, the fuse symbol is FU, which has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions; when the power grid or electrical equipment is overloaded or short-circuited, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; the designations of the time relay are KT, SJ, SL. For the electromagnetic brake, maintenance requires mastering the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, on this basis carrying out electromagnetic brake gap adjustment, and on this basis completing electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment, so that the brake recovers normal braking performance.

Poor contact of contacts is a common cause of many cargo winch faults. Contamination or oxidation of the contact surface or insufficient mechanical pressure will cause a decrease in conductivity; in a contactor, poor contact of contacts is one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning; methods for dealing with poor contact of contacts of a contactor include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface, and tightening the contacts and the conductive plate. Electrical connections with increased contact resistance due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter form poor contact; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance; poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults. After the fault is identified, when it is confirmed that the semiconductor trip unit itself is not damaged, in most cases the cause may be external electromagnetic interference.

The AC electric cargo winch is widely used in ship deck machinery; its drive motor is generally a squirrel-cage pole-changing variable-speed motor with three speeds. According to the speed regulation range from medium speed to high speed, this type of cargo winch can be divided into two forms: constant power speed regulation and constant torque speed regulation. Foreign products mostly use constant torque speed regulation systems. The constant power speed regulation system has higher requirements for overload protection and for the same-speed interlock control of two derricks. Although the DC electric cargo winch differs from the AC type in drive and control mode, in terms of fault analysis thinking it can still be considered together within the category of the AC electric cargo winch.

In troubleshooting the electrical system of a cargo winch, resistance measurement is a basic task. Poor contact of contacts is a common fault state in a contactor; contamination or oxidation of the contact surface or insufficient mechanical pressure will cause a decrease in conductivity; poor contact of contacts will cause contact overheating or burning; when dealing with it, it is necessary to clean the contact surface, dress the surface and tighten the contacts and the conductive plate.

Poor contact of contacts of the cargo winch directional contactor ZC or FC will cause only forward or only reverse when the handle is moved; that is, the AC electric cargo winch will have the fault of only forward or only reverse when the master controller handle is moved. Poor contact of the internal contacts of the cargo winch master controller may cause no high speed and no medium speed operation in either forward or reverse. Poor contact of contacts of the AC electric cargo winch brake contactor will cause the brake not to be released, so that neither forward nor reverse turns. These symptoms all belong to faults that may occur during operation of the AC electric cargo winch; alongside them are also motor overheating or even burning out, loss of control of the control system, neither forward nor reverse starting when the master controller handle is moved, excessive cargo slip during braking, and single-phase operation of the motor. The AC electric cargo winch will also have the faults of excessive temperature rise of the electromagnetic brake and too fast wear of the friction plates; this symptom is directly related to the various causes of brake heating and abnormal wear of the friction plates.

Failure of a constant power cargo winch to run at high speed under light load is one of the common faults of the AC electric cargo winch, and is listed as a separate item in the fault and cause comparison data. One direct cause of this fault is failure of the load relay, and the second direct cause is an incorrect setting value of the load relay; that is, failure of the load relay or an incorrect setting value will cause the constant power cargo winch to fail to run at high speed under light load. The load relay ZJ is a component that frequently causes faults, mainly manifesting as overheating of the motor when running at high speed under heavy load; therefore, in cargo winch management, the load relay should be carefully adjusted and monitored. Causes of this symptom include an open circuit or short circuit in the electromagnetic brake circuit, and failure of time relay KT. An open circuit or short circuit in the electromagnetic brake circuit is one of the direct causes of the electromagnetic brake not pulling in, will cause the AC electric cargo winch to have motor stalling, and together with failure of time relay KT constitutes the cause of the brake not pulling in; failure of time relay KT will cause the electromagnetic brake not to pull in, and further cause the motor to stall.

The electromagnetic brake not releasing is another fault symptom, manifesting as the electromagnetic brake being unable to release the braking state. Fracture and jamming of the friction plates is one of the causes of the electromagnetic brake not releasing; the auxiliary contact of the accelerating contactor not opening so that the electromagnetic brake is not de-energized will likewise cause the electromagnetic brake not to release; a fault in the brake contactor is also one of the causes of the electromagnetic brake not releasing. The mechanism of the fault of the auxiliary contact of the accelerating contactor not opening lies in the auxiliary contact not opening, so that the electromagnetic brake is not de-energized; in the AC electric cargo winch it is one of the three main causes of the electromagnetic brake not releasing, and usually together with a brake contactor fault causes the brake not to be de-energized. Fracture and jamming of the friction plates is somewhat different from excessive slip or small braking torque caused by too large a friction plate gap.

The phenomenon of the electromagnetic brake releasing immediately after pulling in may be caused by an interruption produced by improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting; too short a delay setting of time relay KT2 may also cause this fault; too large a value of the economy resistor of the brake coil is a potential fault cause; and too strong a reaction spring force of the brake will likewise cause immediate release after pulling in.

The cause of improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting with an interruption is an item in the fault and cause comparison data of the AC electric cargo winch, and together with too short a KT2 delay and too large a coil economy resistance, etc., constitutes the causes of the same fault symptom; too short a KT delay, i.e. too short a KT2 delay, is one of the fault causes of the electromagnetic brake releasing immediately after pulling in, and is usually listed alongside factors such as improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting, the coil resistance or the spring force; too large a resistance value of the economy resistor of the brake coil is listed alongside factors such as improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting and too short a KT2 delay, and belongs to the common fault causes of the electromagnetic braking system of the AC electric cargo winch; too strong a reaction spring force of the brake is listed alongside improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting, too short a KT2 delay, and too large a value of the coil economy resistance.

The fault causes of electromagnetic brake heating include an inter-turn short circuit in the brake coil, deformation of the friction plates or too small a gap between plates, and too small a value of the economy resistor or too late insertion. An inter-turn short circuit in the brake coil is one of the main fault causes of heating of the electromagnetic brake of the AC electric cargo winch, and often occurs together with deformation of the friction plates, too small a gap or an improper economy resistance value to cause brake heating. Deformation of the friction plates or too small a gap between plates is one of the fault causes of electromagnetic brake heating; too small a gap between plates will cause too fast wear of the friction plates, and deformation of the friction plates caused by long-term high-speed friction will cause brake heating. Too small a resistance value of the economy resistor or too late insertion is one of the main fault sources of electromagnetic brake heating, specifically manifesting as the resistance value of the economy resistor in the brake coil being set too small, or the economy resistor being inserted into the circuit too late, failing to limit the current in time; the opposite fault symptom is the brake releasing immediately after pulling in, whose cause lies in too large an economy resistance value.

Too fast wear of the friction plates is a type of fault symptom of the electromagnetic brake, manifesting as abnormally fast wear of the friction plates accompanied by excessive temperature rise. Too short a setting of time relay 2SJ causes regenerative braking to fail, causing high-speed braking and thus too fast wear; too large a discharge resistor in the coil circuit causes too fast discharge, causing high-speed braking and thus accelerating friction plate wear; too large an economy resistance value or too early insertion prevents the brake from opening fully, causing accelerated friction plate wear; too small, uneven or deformed friction plate gaps directly cause brake heating and severe wear; too strong a spring force in the brake, small holding force due to a coil short circuit, or obstruction of the armature will all cause too fast wear. Too small a gap between plates is one of the main causes of heating of the electromagnetic brake of the AC electric cargo winch, will cause too fast wear of the friction plates of the electromagnetic brake, and in the fault and cause comparison data is listed both as a specific fault cause of electromagnetic brake heating and as a specific fault cause of too fast wear of the friction plates. Poor quality and low wear resistance of the friction plates is one of the causes of the fault of too fast wear of the friction plates of the AC electric cargo winch, and together with too small a gap between plates and too short a regenerative braking time, etc., constitutes the cause of too fast wear of the friction plates; it belongs to the causes of electromagnetic brake-related faults and is distinguished from fracture jamming or heating causes. Too short a regenerative braking time of the motor and the occurrence of high-speed braking is one of the fault causes of too fast wear of the friction plates of the electromagnetic brake of the AC electric cargo winch, manifesting as too short a regenerative braking time of the motor and further occurrence of high-speed braking; this fault cause is listed alongside too small a friction plate gap, poor quality and uneven gap. If the gap is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply. For the electromagnetic brake, maintenance work correspondingly includes the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, electromagnetic brake gap adjustment and electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment; that is, the electromagnetic brake corresponds to the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, corresponds to the electromagnetic brake gap adjustment, and also corresponds to the electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment, and the three together constitute the basic work content of brake maintenance.

Foreign countries mostly use constant torque speed regulation systems; the DC electric cargo winch also belongs to the major category of electric cargo winches.

The symptom of neither forward nor reverse starting when the master controller handle is moved can be caused by many reasons. A blown fuse in the control circuit will cause this symptom; the brake contactor not operating or poor contact of contacts will cause this symptom, whose direct consequence is that the brake is not released; poor closing of the master controller contacts or damage to the master controller will cause this symptom; the damper switch not being connected will cause this symptom; poor contact of contacts of the undervoltage relay will cause this symptom; poor contact of the emergency switch will likewise cause this symptom. The above causes are listed alongside the power supply voltage not being connected, etc., and constitute possible factors for the cargo winch being completely unable to start. One of the directional contactors being faulty belongs to a fault at the directional contactor assembly level, and is distinguished from detailed problems such as poor contact of contacts;

A fault in the master controller may cause either forward running without reverse running, or reverse running without forward running. A voltage relay is a relay classified by the nature of its input signal; it realizes control or protection functions through the voltage change induced in its coil, belongs to the electromagnetic relay, and its coil uses the electrical quantity, i.e. voltage, as the excitation input. If the temperature relay in an AC electric cargo winch is not reset or its contacts have poor contact, the motor will also fail to rotate in either forward or reverse.

Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; a multimeter is used when measuring voltage, the multimeter is used to measure voltage, and a voltmeter may also be used to measure its voltage value; it belongs to the switchgear, and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series fuse is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection.

In the electrical system of ship auxiliary machinery, the windlass and the mooring winch both belong to deck machinery, and their drive control schemes are generally the same as the AC electric cargo winch on the same ship. The electric windlass is divided into DC and AC types, and the mooring winch is likewise divided into DC and AC types; at present most adopt AC three-speed windlasses, mooring winches, or windlasses and mooring winches of the G-M system, and the drive control systems of the two are basically the same. As regards equipment attribution, the mooring winch belongs to the major category of deck machinery, the electric windlass, and the maintenance of the electrical systems of the windlass and mooring winch is included within the maintenance scope of the electric windlass. The mooring winch is usually listed as the first-level non-essential load to be shed with priority.

The AC three-speed electric windlass adopts a three-speed cage-type asynchronous motor as the drive motor, and the cage-type asynchronous motor is the main form of marine asynchronous motor; the three-phase asynchronous motor used on most ships is the cage-type asynchronous motor. The stator core of the three-speed cage-type asynchronous motor has two sets of windings, one for high speed and one shared by medium and low speed; the high-speed winding of this motor is 4-pole, the medium speed is double-star connection (8-pole), and the low speed is single-delta connection (16-pole). Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes leading to overcurrent and overheating of AC motors. In the AC three-speed windlass, the two sets of stator windings are respectively the high-speed 4-pole and the medium/low-speed shared pole-changing type; this type of windlass has undervoltage and high-speed overload protection, and automatically switches to medium-speed operation on high-speed overcurrent.

The motor of the electric windlass should be able to withstand the locked-rotor current for 1min, with a locked-rotor torque twice the rated torque; during emergency heaving of the anchor, the motor is allowed to start 25 times within 30min; during deep-water anchoring, the control system makes the motor operate in the regenerative braking or dynamic braking state. At an anchoring depth of 45m, the average speed of heaving both anchors shall be not less than 6m/min; the electric drive device shall be able to satisfy heaving both anchors after a single anchor breaks ground within the given voyage area.

The maintenance content of the electrical systems of the windlass and mooring winch includes: the number of starts should not be too frequent, generally 25 starts within 30min are allowed; the locked-rotor time must not be too long, generally 1min is allowed, and when the ammeter reading exceeds the rated current of the motor for a relatively long time, the machine should be stopped. For the maintenance of the electrical control panel of the windlass and mooring winch, refer to the maintenance requirements for the control panel of the cargo winch; the maintenance requirements for the electromagnetic brake and the master controller are the same as those for the cargo winch. The equipment belongs to the short-time duty system, and operation should be carried out according to the state of the anchor chain and mooring rope and the current reading.

The electromagnetic brake is composed of an electromagnetic armature disc, springs, a moving plate, a friction plate or friction block, an end cover, etc., and is used as the braking component for the drive motors of deck machinery such as cargo winches and windlasses; it realizes brake release or brake application through electromagnetic attraction and spring return, and often adopts a disc-type structure integrated with the motor to improve watertightness and braking stability. When the coil is energized, the electromagnet attracts and compresses the spring so that the moving plate rotates freely; when the power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. The AC electric cargo winch includes the electromagnetic brake, and the electromagnetic brake corresponds to the electromagnetic brake clearance measurement method, electromagnetic brake clearance adjustment, and electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment. The contactor includes a core; the core is a component of ship electrical equipment, serving as the magnetic-conducting component in electromagnetic devices, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil, and serve as a reference point for insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester may be connected to the core; in the through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor under measurement is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding.

The debugging of the electrical control system of the windlass and mooring winch applies to the electric windlass. Electrical and mechanical braking are combined to meet the requirement of rapid stopping; the electric drive device shall satisfy heaving both anchors after a single anchor breaks ground; the equipment belongs to the short-time duty system, and starting should not exceed 25 times within 30min. During debugging, first carry out the no-load test and roughly set the various protective devices: the zero-voltage relay LYJ may be set to 80%U; the overcurrent relay GLJ is set to 110%Ie for AC and to slightly greater than 2Ie for DC. Switch on the power supply, place the master controller handle in the zero position, and observe the action of each device; the zero-voltage relay LYJ and the three time relays 1SJ~3SJ should operate, and other devices should not operate.

Among the protective devices, the current relay in the AC three-speed electric windlass picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%; in the windlass system, misoperation of the overcurrent relay GLJ will cause the fault of no high speed at starting; during debugging of auxiliary machinery, the AC overcurrent relay is set to 110%I_e, and for DC slightly greater than 2I_e. The current relay is an electromagnetic relay classified by the nature of its input signal, used for control and protection of the ship electrical system; its coil carries the electrical quantity, and its structure is basically similar to that of the contactor; after the generator trips during parallel operation, the overcurrent relay needs to be reset to restore closing of the main switch. Time relays are often denoted in circuits by KT, SJ, SL. The thermal relay is a protective relay using a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors; it belongs to the thermal relay classified by sensing element, its sensing part is the bimetallic strip, it is used in large quantities on ships, and is generally used to accomplish the overload protection task of small motors.

Current is one of the measurable performances, and its measuring tools include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; voltage is likewise a measurable performance, and its measuring tools include the multimeter and voltmeter. The multimeter can be used to measure both voltage and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system.

During operation of the electric windlass, the fault symptom of serious motor heating may occur, and its main causes include frequent operation, harsh working conditions, and motor internal fault. From the control circuit point of view, the control circuit allows direct starting at medium speed, and the relatively large starting current after repeated starts easily leads to overheating; the windlass often needs high-speed braking, causing serious heating of the brake and aggravating the overall temperature rise; when heating is serious, thermal relays 1RJ and 2RJ operate to cut off the circuit; during emergency heaving of the anchor, the emergency button AN may be pressed to force operation to cope with the overload protection action. Frequent operation and harsh working conditions are, apart from motor internal fault, the main causes of serious heating of the windlass motor, because the control circuit allows direct starting at medium speed and repeated starting with large current leads to overheating, and the working characteristics of the windlass require frequent high-speed braking, causing serious heating of the brake.

The contactor is the electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system, belongs to low-voltage control apparatus, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size; it is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. Time relays are often marked in diagrams as KT, SJ, SL. The voltage relay realizes control or protection functions through the voltage change induced in its coil; when the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced, since self-winding will affect the operating value due to inaccurate turns.

The multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current, and the ammeter is also used to measure current. If capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action.

The electric hydraulic steering gear is an important part of the ship auxiliary machinery electrical system; its electrical control system is equipped with an autopilot or automatic track keeper, which controls the course error according to certain requirements by proportional, proportional-derivative or proportional-derivative-integral law, or keeps the ship sailing on a given course. The steering gear used on large ocean-going or offshore passenger and cargo ships has an electrical control system equipped with an autopilot or autopilot selector. The electric hydraulic steering gear should be supplied by two power sources, the emergency switchboard and the main switchboard, and the lines should be routed far apart and separately. The electric oil pump unit adopts the cold-standby bypass scheme and can operate alone, switch over automatically with each other, or operate two units in parallel. At maximum draft and maximum speed, the time for the rudder to turn from 35° on one side to 30° on the other side shall not exceed 28s. The error of the rudder angle indicator indicating the rudder blade position shall not be greater than ±1°. The system is provided with a rudder blade deflection limit switch, and audible and visual alarm devices for power supply undervoltage and overload.

The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy of the ship power station; the ship power station includes the main switchboard, and the main switchboard includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The main switchboard has the functions of circuit making and breaking, protection and alarm, parameter detection and power regulation; its main functions include making or breaking circuits, protective device operation and alarm, and detection and display of various electrical parameters, and it can regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station and the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel.

In the fault diagnosis of the steering gear electrical system, the conventional fault diagnosis method uses the step of observation. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status and equipment operating parameters, specifically involving whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Observation belongs to a sub-step of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carrying out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged". The multimeter is used to measure resistance and voltage; voltage is one of the measurable performances, and its measuring tools include the multimeter and voltmeter. Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under measurement must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on.

The electro-hydraulic steering gear includes three maintenance items: rudder alignment during pre-departure preparation, patrol inspection during navigation, and maintenance of the steering gear electrical system. During pre-departure preparation, rudder alignment requires checking whether the control switches, buttons, indicator lamps, and devices such as undervoltage and overload alarms on the steering console are complete and effective; the power supply changeover on both sides should be observed, and trial operation should be performed separately on the bridge and in the steering gear room using the emergency power supply; trial operation should be carried out using various steering modes to check the effectiveness of the emergency steering, the reliability of automatic unit changeover, and the flexibility of mechanical transmission. During trial operation of the autopilot and electro-hydraulic steering gear system, there should be no rudder drift, rudder overshoot, failure to return to midships, or oscillation. At midships, the deviation between the steering gear and the indicator and the actual position should be 0°, and at large rudder angles the deviation should not exceed 2°. It is also necessary to recheck whether the time for the rudder to turn from 35° on one side to 30° on the other side meets the specified requirement, and to check whether there is any abnormal noise during rudder turning.

Patrol inspection during navigation requires checking the operating condition of the units, the running noise and temperature rise of the motor, confirming whether the solenoid valve, servo motor, limit switch, etc. operate reliably, and observing whether the readings of the instruments, the unit operation indications, and the rudder angle indication device work normally. For ships whose steering gear is controlled by two sets of drag control systems, they should be changed over for use periodically. Regarding maintenance of the steering gear electrical system, the transmission part of the main steering gear of the autopilot console should be lubricated once every 6 months, and the oil quality of the transmission parts such as gears and miniature bearings should be checked once every 1 year; if deteriorated, they should be cleaned and relubricated, and at the same time the dust and dirt inside the steering gear should be removed, and wearing parts replaced if necessary. For the follow-up control system, the resistance, brushes, and conductive rings of the transmitter and receiver of the AEG-type steering gear should be checked every voyage, and corresponding checks should also be made for slip-ring structures.

In steering gear maintenance, the solenoid valve needs to be disassembled, cleaned, and inspected to ensure that the movable part of the valve body is free from jamming and that the stroke meets the requirements. A solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control the water mist fire-extinguishing zone; in the burner ignition program it is energized, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle and is sprayed, and its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve and a servo motor. The servo motor is part of the patrol inspection content of the steering gear electrical system, and its reliable operation needs to be confirmed. A servo motor is a motor controlled by a bridge or regulator signal, which drives a feedback potentiometer or fuel control actuator by rotation to achieve automatic balance and position control; in boiler combustion regulation, its winding is energized under the control of a differential amplifier and thyristor to adjust the air-fuel ratio, and when rotating it drives the sliding contact of feedback potentiometer R10 to move, so that the bridge reaches balance again and then stops.

A resistor is ship equipment whose resistance can be measured, and the measuring tool is a multimeter. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating action. A printed circuit board consists of a base material and circuits; the base material is an insulating material, including phenolic resin board and epoxy glass, and the circuits are conductive foil, usually copper. The base material is often called the substrate, most commonly phenolic resin board and epoxy glass; the circuit part is made of conductive copper, laid on the substrate, and the required pattern is obtained by etching. Marine electrical equipment uses printed circuit boards; printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards; circuit board faults occur on printed circuit boards, and circuit board faults fall within the scope of printed circuit boards. Printed circuit boards of dual-channel systems with mutual standby should be frequently interchanged to ensure working performance, and spare printed circuit boards and components should be stored sealed or dry.

A coil is a component of marine electrical equipment, made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. A contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in marine power systems, belonging to low-voltage control apparatus, used in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life, and small size; it is used in large quantities on ships because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor includes an arc chute, main contact, iron core, and coil; contactor maintenance applies to contactors.

The brush contacts the collector ring to transfer current, serving as an important conductive element for leading current in or out between the stationary part and the sliding part of a motor; DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors, and synchronous generators all need to be equipped with brushes. Motor overload, poor contact between brush and commutator, and loose brush holder will all lead to excessive sparking under brush.

A fuse is used for overload and short circuit protection in marine power systems, with the symbol FU; it is a protective device that, when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. A fuse belongs to distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. Fuse blown corresponds to replace the fuse, and power supply fuse blown also corresponds to replace the fuse. When replacing the fuse, it should generally be removed and replaced without power; if live replacement is permitted, the load must first be cut off to prevent danger. Before replacing with a new fuse element, the slag, soot, and dust on the inner surface of the tube and on the contact surfaces must be carefully wiped clean. In troubleshooting the steering gear system, if the main power supply has no fault but emergency steering fails, the fuse needs to be replaced after inspection.

The electro-hydraulic steering gear may exhibit three types of fault symptoms: autopilot not working, autopilot not sensitive (sluggish operation), and autopilot error too large. Autopilot not working is one of the four main summarized types of general autopilot faults, namely not working, not sensitive, unstable, and inaccurate. Autopilot not working is generally caused by obvious faults, such as open power supply, blown fuse, open circuit (broken wire), short circuit, various electronic component faults, etc.; in the general troubleshooting process of the PR4507 autopilot it appears as the primary troubleshooting category, and may occur concurrently with other faults or occur intermittently. Autopilot not sensitive (sluggish operation) may be due to improper amplifier gain setting, phase mismatch, component failure within the system, etc.; in complex systems such as the PR4507 autopilot, troubleshooting this fault is relatively difficult. Autopilot error too large may be caused by inflexible operation of the autopilot actuator and other reasons, and is listed as a main inspection item in the troubleshooting process of equipment such as the PR4507 autopilot.

Commissioning after repair of the steering gear drag electrical control system applies to the electro-hydraulic steering gear. Different faults of the steering gear drag electrical control system have different specific commissioning methods; although the specific methods differ, the commissioning content of the steering gear drag electrical control system is the same; it is impossible to describe the specific commissioning method of the steering gear drag electrical control system for a single circuit. Before initial power-on, the entire system needs to be cleaned, including cleaning the control box, motor and junction box, feedback device, solenoid valve, and actuator motor, etc., and at the same time the autopilot should be checked; the drawings and the working principle of the steering gear system should be familiarized, and the wiring and installation should be checked to see whether they conform to the circuit diagram; all fuses in the system should be checked or installed according to the capacities required by the drawings, and the indicator bulbs should be installed in the specified number; the insulation resistance should be checked.

A junction box is a component used in marine electrical systems to connect cables, protect wiring points, and accommodate electrical components; the general alarm device includes a junction box, and the general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp, and junction box, etc. The maintenance cycle of the rudder angle indicator is 3 months, and the content includes removing dust and check the power supply. During autopilot commissioning, it is necessary to measure whether the output voltages of the power transformer are correct. Power supply faults correspond to check the power supply; in the overall PLC inspection, if the POWER lamp off, the step of checking power supply faults needs to be carried out; when the electric fan starts slowly, the repair method includes checking whether the power supply voltage is too low; when the electric drill fails to start and there is no voltage at the power supply, the power supply circuit should be checked.

Maintenance of the steering gear electrical control system, in addition to control logic and hydraulic actuators, also involves inspection of a large number of general electrical devices and motor components. The error of the rudder angle indicator in indicating the rudder blade position should not be greater than ±1°. During operation, the electro-hydraulic steering gear may experience autopilot not working, autopilot not sensitive, i.e., sluggish operation, or autopilot error too large; these phenomena are often related to the power supply, wiring connections, and the state of control devices. During maintenance of the steering gear follow-up control system, the linkage parts in the system need to be checked to confirm whether the linkages are deformed, loose, or jammed. These practices all show that check the power supply is a common link in handling many types of electrical faults.

Measuring circuit parameters is inseparable from the multimeter. A multimeter includes a changeover switch; the changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measuring points, or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts; on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measuring points, set the working state, and issue operating commands; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, and the polarity and inter-electrode resistance of a thyristor. A thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier; measuring its control electrode and inter-electrode resistance is a basic means of judging whether it is good or bad. If a line short circuit fault occurs in the steering gear system, it often manifests as the fuse blowing instantaneously or tripping, and a live check is needed to distinguish whether it is an external line short circuit or an internal component breakdown. The corresponding treatment measure for broken input wiring is soldering. Soldering is a process in which solder is melted by heating, atomic diffusion occurs between the workpiece and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer with good conductivity and mechanical strength is formed; soldering quality directly affects the performance of electronic products.

Marine electrical equipment widely uses printed circuit boards.

A marine motor includes components such as bearings and brushes. The bearing is used to support the rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration, and abnormal noise, and is one of the direct causes of the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and overheating of the bearing end cover. Checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition are both maintenance contents for the bearing. Fracture of one phase connecting rod of a circuit breaker will cause the contact of that phase to fail to close, and the treatment method is to replace the connecting rod; an increase in the angle between the detachable connecting rods of the current-limiting switch release mechanism will cause the contact to fail to close, so the state of the connecting rods also needs to be included in the inspection scope.

Ships whose main engine is a diesel engine are usually equipped with an auxiliary fuel oil boiler to undertake the heating task; the automatic fuel oil boiler with an evaporation capacity of 1.8t/h is more commonly used on Chinese ships, and its air pressure range is 294～686kPa. The control system of this automatic fuel oil boiler consists of an automatic regulating system, program controller, automatic protection, and audible and visual alarm, etc.; the control box should be installed centrally near the boiler, has manual and automatic control functions, and can be switched between the two. During boiler operation, water level control is achieved by automatic feed water at low water level and stopping feed water at high water level; once the water level drops to the dangerous water level, the system immediately gives an audible and visual alarm and stops all systems from working; pressure control is manifested as automatic ignition at low pressure and automatic extinguishing at high pressure; when the steam pressure reaches the maximum value, an audible and visual alarm is given and the safety valve is automatically opened to release steam and reduce pressure.

In addition, the system is also provided with an automatic fuel temperature regulating link to keep the fuel at a suitable temperature. The ignition program follows the principle of "fire waits for oil", completing pre-purge, fuel pump start, ignition transformer energization, and fuel injection in sequence; if ignition fails, the system performs automatic extinguishing, post-purge, and alarm actions.

During operation, the automatic fuel oil boiler will exhibit various typical faults, including failure to ignite, failure to feed water automatically, failure to ignite and raise combustion pressure automatically, automatic extinguishing after flame is produced during ignition, failure to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature, and automatic flameout and too frequent ignition, etc. That is to say, the automatic fuel oil boiler may exhibit the phenomenon of failure to ignite automatically and raise combustion pressure, and may also exhibit automatic flameout and too frequent ignition. For these faults, there are respectively the repair method for failure to ignite, the repair method for failure to feed water automatically, the repair method for failure to ignite and raise combustion pressure automatically, the repair method for automatic extinguishing after flame is produced during ignition, the repair method for failure to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature, and the repair method for automatic flameout and too frequent ignition. Among them, the repair method for failure to ignite automatically and raise combustion pressure applies to the automatic fuel oil boiler, and the repair method for automatic flameout and too frequent ignition also applies to the automatic fuel oil boiler. Along with repair, there are also commissioning of the alarm subsystem, commissioning of the automatic feed water system, and commissioning of the ignition control system; these commissioning items also apply to the automatic fuel oil boiler. Maintenance work of the automatic fuel oil boiler covers control system maintenance, ignition system maintenance, feed water system maintenance, air-fuel regulating device maintenance, and exhaust gas boiler mechanical transmission maintenance, etc., and attention needs to be paid to the various requirements in the precautions for daily maintenance of the boiler control system. In terms of component composition, the automatic fuel oil boiler includes an ignition rod, photoresistor, solenoid valve, water level sensor, proportional pressure regulator, and electric proportional actuator, and the servo motor is also one of its components.

Flame monitoring is accomplished by means of a photoresistor. A photoresistor is a semiconductor element whose resistance value changes with the strength of external light; the resistance is small when light is strong and large when light is weak, and it is made by depositing a layer of cadmium sulfide (CdS) film on a ceramic base. In complete darkness its resistance can reach several megohms or more, and under relatively strong light it can drop to several kilohms or even below 1kΩ. In marine auxiliary boilers, the photoresistor is used to detect the flame; when ignition succeeds, its resistance value decreases, energizing 1JY, which in turn energizes 3JZ and 4JZ; the 31 and 28 contacts of 4JZ open, the ignition transformer is de-energized, thereby stopping ignition. During commissioning, the photoresistor can be taken out of the furnace chamber and illuminated with a flashlight to verify whether its resistance decreases and whether the subsequent relay actions are normal. Common faults of the photoresistor include aging, the photosensitive window being covered by accumulated oil soot affecting the luminous flux, or the photosensitive tube not being aligned with the flame; during repair it is necessary to check whether it is aged, whether the photosensitive window is covered by accumulated oil soot affecting the luminous flux, or whether it is aligned with the flame. From the perspective of component classification, a photoresistor belongs to a type of resistor, and its resistance can be measured with a multimeter; during measurement, at least one end of the resistor under test should be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is a capacitor in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with power on.

The ignition rod is used to generate the ignition spark and ignite the fuel. When maintaining the ignition rod, it is necessary to check its gap, the insulation performance of the rod electrode, and the carbon deposit at the tip; if it fails to ignite, it is necessary to check whether the insulation of the ignition rod to ground or between each other is good. During commissioning, pressing the manual button can make it generate an ignition spark; when there is no spark in the test, it needs to be taken out of the furnace chamber to check its state; if ignition fails and there is an ignition spark and oil traces, it may be caused by the ignition rod being too far from the fuel nozzle. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of the fuel; during ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle and is sprayed; in the burner ignition program the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle and is sprayed. If ignition fails, it should be checked whether the solenoid valve coil is open and whether the valve core is jammed.

The automatic regulation of the combustion process is accomplished jointly by the proportional pressure regulator and the electric proportional actuator. The model code of the proportional pressure regulator is YBD, and together with the electric proportional actuator (DBC) it realizes the automatic regulation of the combustion process. The electric proportional actuator internally contains core components such as the differential amplifier, thyristor and servo motor, and uses the bridge balance state formed by potentiometer R10 and R0 to control the start and stop of the servo motor. When the boiler steam pressure reaches the set value of the pressure regulator, the bridge is balanced and the servo motor stops; when the boiler steam pressure is lower than the set value, the bridge loses balance and the servo motor rotates in the direction of increasing the oil and air dampers. Specifically, when the steam pressure is lower than the set value, YBD drives the sliding contact of potentiometer R0 upward, causing the bridge to become unbalanced and triggering the servo motor to act, triggering the thyristor to make the motor rotate in the direction of increasing the oil and air dampers; when the servo motor rotates, it drives the sliding contact of feedback potentiometer R10 to move until a new bridge balance is formed with the setting potentiometer and then it stops. The maintenance cycle of the proportional pressure regulator is once every 2 months, and it is necessary to check whether the upper and lower pressure limit set values meet the requirements. In the automatic regulation of boiler combustion, the potentiometer forms a bridge balance through potentiometer R1 driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R10; during daily maintenance, the contacts of each potentiometer must be cleaned frequently to prevent oil and water from entering the control box and affecting contact performance; during troubleshooting, it is necessary to check whether the sliding contact of the potentiometer driven by the pressure regulator is in good contact, and whether the moving parts are jammed. The servo motor is used to regulate the opening of the air damper and oil damper, rotates according to the bridge output signal, and drives the feedback potentiometer to adjust so that the bridge is rebalanced; in boiler combustion regulation, the differential amplifier and thyristor control the winding to be energized so as to adjust the air-oil ratio.

The daily maintenance of the boiler control system has several specific requirements: regularly clean the control box to prevent oil and water from entering the interior of the control box; clean the contacts of the multi-circuit time relay and other relays and contactors; frequently clean the contacts of each potentiometer to maintain good contact; frequently check the insulation of the ignition system, especially the insulation condition of the ignition rod; clean the carbon deposit on the tip of the ignition rod to maintain ignition performance; regularly check the insulation resistance of each motor and monitor the heating condition during operation; clean the water level observer to prevent scale accumulation. The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system, belongs to low-voltage control electrical appliances, has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size, and is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself. The time relay is also an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship power system, and its codes include KT, SJ and SL. The pressure relay is a non-electrical relay with pressure as the input signal, its sensing element is the air bag, and its actuating part is the contact; it is used for the automatic control and protection of ship boilers, air compressors and pump sets, and in auxiliary boilers it is used as a control appliance for automatically controlling steam pressure. The thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, and its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode can be measured with a multimeter.

During diagnosis and maintenance, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of electrical equipment and components, must be very familiar with the whole-ship electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of each component, and master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, it is necessary to see whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. In the maintenance and debugging of PLC and electrical control systems, switching on the power supply is a key step, referring to the process of connecting the power supply for functional testing or self-diagnosis after confirming that there is no short circuit or earthing fault; before switching on the power supply, it is necessary to detect whether there is a short circuit or earthing fault in the input and output parts, and only after confirming that there is no error may the power be switched on; when the PLC is switched on, the self-diagnosis process begins, and if there is an internal error in the CPU, the "CPU Error" lamp on the panel shows an abnormality.

For troubleshooting of the electrical control system of a marine auxiliary boiler, one usually starts with the conventional fault diagnosis method, and the first step of this method is to use observation. After observation, it is also necessary to further check the monitoring and indicating device so as to judge the scope of the fault.

When testing components and devices, the multimeter is a common tool for measuring resistance and can be used to measure their resistance values. The category of resistors includes the photoresistor; the photoresistor is a semiconductor element whose resistance value changes with the strength of external light, being small when the light is strong and large when the light is weak. In ship boilers, the photoresistor is used as a flame monitoring element; when ignition succeeds, its resistance decreases, causing the relay to act and stop the ignition. During debugging, the photoresistor can be taken out of the furnace chamber and illuminated with a flashlight to observe the action of the relay so as to verify whether its performance is normal. The contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, among which the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature being unable to close and the motor failing to start. There are many causes of failure to ignite; ignition gap problems, ignition rod insulation problems, ignition transformer problems, solenoid valve faults, nozzle blockage, oil circuit system pressure problems and 2JZ faults will all cause failure to ignite. The troubleshooting method for failure to ignite applies to automatic oil-fired boilers and requires investigation from both the electrical and oil circuit aspects. On the electrical side, first check whether an ignition spark is produced at the ignition gap; if there is no spark, check the insulation of the ignition rod and lead to earth or their insulation to each other, check the insulation of the ignition transformer to earth, and see whether the ignition gap is too large or too small, and finally check the ignition transformer and ignition button 4LA. If there is a spark, check whether DF acts; if it does not act, check whether it is open-circuited. On the oil circuit side, if the nozzle does not spray oil, check whether the nozzle is blocked and whether pressure is established in the oil circuit system. If the 2JZ normally open contact is not closed, the combustion proportional regulator will put the air damper open very wide during ignition, causing ignition failure; at this time, check 2JZ itself, the coil circuit and the contact closing condition. During debugging, if there is a spark and oil traces but ignition still fails, it may be that the ignition rod is too far from the nozzle or the oil pressure is insufficient causing poor atomization; the air damper and oil damper are linked, and if the air damper is closed too small it is not easy to ignite, so it is necessary to check whether the air damper opening is appropriate. During debugging, pressing the manual button can make it produce an ignition spark; when testing and there is no spark, it needs to be taken out of the furnace chamber to check its condition.

Failure to feed water automatically is another type of fault symptom of the automatic oil-fired boiler and belongs to a specific fault type of the automatic feed water system. Faults in the circuit or relay controlling 7JZ or 8JZ, as well as faults in contactor 1CJ or the pump auxiliary unit, will cause failure to feed water automatically. The troubleshooting method for failure to feed water automatically also applies to automatic oil-fired boilers: first carry out manual feed water; if manual feed water is normal, it indicates that the fault lies in the circuit or relay itself controlling 7JZ or 8JZ, and at this time it is only necessary to check 7JZ itself and the normally closed contact of 2JY; if manual feed water is also abnormal, it indicates a fault in contactor 1CJ or the pump shaft unit itself, and contactor 1CJ or the pump shaft unit should be checked.

The step of interviewing the operator is the preceding step of observation; after observation, the step of checking the monitoring and indicating device is entered, that is, observation is the preceding step of checking the monitoring and indicating device. In the measurement step, the multimeter is a common tool; it contains a changeover switch and can be used to measure resistance and thyristors. The function of the changeover switch is to select the measurement object and select the range; it is used to set the working state, select the measurement point or issue operating instructions, and has many selection positions and contacts; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, and its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode can be measured.

The automatic oil-fired boiler will have several typical faults during operation. It will have failure to ignite automatically and combustion pressure build-up, will have the flame extinguish automatically after being produced during ignition, will have failure to automatically maintain normal steam pressure and steam temperature, and will also have automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition. As for the former fault, the automatic changeover switches K1~K7 not being in place can cause failure to ignite automatically and combustion pressure build-up, misoperation of the minimum water level and ignition failure relays 6JZ and 5JZ can cause this phenomenon, faults in pressure relays YD and 1JZ can cause this phenomenon, and a fault in the sequence controller 1JS can likewise cause this phenomenon. During maintenance, first switch to manual operation; if the furnace also cannot be lit, troubleshoot according to the failure to ignite fault; if manual operation is normal, it indicates that the automatic control system has a problem, and at this time press the start button to see whether the fan and oil pump run. If the fan and oil pump do not run, the first step is to confirm whether the automatic changeover switches K1~K4 are in place, whether the two relays 6JZ and 5JZ for minimum water level and ignition failure have misoperated, and whether pressure relays YD and 1JZ are normal. If the fan and oil pump run normally, it is judged to be a fault of the sequence controller 1JS, and it is necessary to check whether each contact of relay 1JS acts according to the delay table, and at the same time check whether the normally closed contact of 4JZ (31, 28) is closed.

The flame extinguishing automatically after being produced during ignition belongs to a fault in the flame monitoring link. Aging of photoresistor Rg can cause the flame to extinguish automatically after being produced during ignition, and a fault in relay 1JT or its circuit can also cause this phenomenon. The troubleshooting method for the flame extinguishing automatically after being produced during ignition also applies to automatic oil-fired boilers; it is necessary to focus on checking whether photoresistor Rg is aged, whether the photosensitive window is covered by accumulated oil ash affecting the luminous flux, and check whether relay 1JT itself or its circuit has an open-circuit fault, as well as whether its working power supply rectifier bridge 1ZX has an open-circuit fault. The above component faults will cause the system not to detect the flame, thereby triggering the ignition failure automatic protection action.

Failure to automatically maintain normal steam pressure and steam temperature manifests as relatively large fluctuations in steam pressure and steam temperature when the boiler is burning, indicating that the air-oil proportional regulator is not working normally. A change in the set value of pressure regulator YBD can cause failure to automatically maintain normal steam pressure and steam temperature, and a fault in electric proportional regulator DBC can also cause this phenomenon. During maintenance, it is necessary to confirm whether the set value of pressure regulator YBD has changed, whether its own working state is good, whether the moving parts are jammed, and whether the sliding contact of the potentiometer driven by it is in reliable contact; it is also necessary to check whether the differential amplifier parameters of electric proportional regulator DBC are symmetrical, whether components are damaged, whether the AC electronic switch thyristors VTH1~VTH4 are normal, whether servo motor M works normally, and whether the contact of the feedback potentiometer driven by it is in good contact. The troubleshooting method for failure to automatically maintain normal steam pressure and steam temperature applies to automatic oil-fired boilers. The automatic oil-fired boiler includes a photoresistor, a servo motor and a potentiometer. In boiler combustion regulation, the differential amplifier and thyristor control the winding to be energized so as to adjust the air-oil ratio; when rotating, it drives the sliding contact of feedback potentiometer R10 to move so that the bridge reaches balance again and then stops. The potentiometer is used for bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by potentiometer R1 driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R10 driven by motor M is balanced;

Automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition are another fault symptom. Too small a deviation between the upper and lower limit values of pressure relay YD can cause automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition, and improper adjustment of the air damper mechanical pull rod can also cause this phenomenon. The troubleshooting method for automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition applies to automatic oil-fired boilers; it is necessary to check whether the deviation between the upper and lower limit values of pressure relay YD is too small, so as to prevent frequent ignition, furnace lighting and furnace shutdown caused by a small deviation; it is necessary to check whether the electric proportional regulator can automatically regulate the air-oil ratio with changes in steam pressure, so as to prevent loss of control leading to pressure rise and flameout; if the electric proportional regulator still maintains large air damper and large oil damper combustion when the deviation between steam pressure and the given value is small, it will quickly cause automatic flameout; it is also necessary to check whether the air damper mechanical pull rod is properly adjusted, because improper adjustment often causes the boiler to flame out.

When the electrical control system of a marine auxiliary boiler fails to ignite, troubleshooting can be started according to the conventional fault diagnosis method, and the starting point of this method is to use the maintenance procedure of observation. After observation is completed, the step of checking the monitoring and indicating device is entered, and there is likewise a sequence between the two.

The automatic oil-fired boiler will have the phenomenon of failure to ignite during operation, and its causes involve multiple aspects. During maintenance, first check whether there is a spark at the ignition gap; if there is no spark, check the insulation, the transformer and button 4LA. If there is a spark but ignition still fails, check whether solenoid valve DF acts; if it does not act, check whether the coil is open-circuited or the valve core is jammed. On the oil circuit side, it is necessary to check whether the nozzle is blocked, whether oil circuit pressure is established, and whether the 2JZ normally open contact is closed.
