If 2JZ does not act, the combustion proportional regulator will open the air damper too wide, causing ignition failure. When testing and there is no spark, it needs to be taken out of the furnace chamber to check its condition; during debugging, pressing the manual button can make it produce an ignition spark;

The debugging of the alarm subsystem applies to automatic oil-fired boilers. Before debugging, only close DZ1 and remove 1RD so that only the alarm and water level detection parts are energized. At this time, if there is no water in the boiler, the alarm bell will be heard immediately; if the armature of 3JY or 5JY is pushed with a screwdriver, the alarm can be stopped; if the armature of ignition failure relay 5JZ is pushed, an alarm will also be given immediately, indicating that the alarm subsystem works normally. In the same way, it is necessary to push the armatures of contactors 1C to 5C and observe whether the indications of each operation indicator lamp are normal. If the simulated action does not conform to the circuit principle, the fault should be found and eliminated to restore the correct logic. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic part in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will cause contactor KM to be unable to close, causing the motor to have no power and fail to start; failure or loss of the armature return spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed.

The debugging of the automatic feed water system also applies to automatic oil-fired boilers. Before debugging, it is necessary to close DZ1 and DZ2 to supply power to the control circuit, and close the water level detection part K8 to the 71 side. Debugging follows the principle of manual first and automatic second; first place K1 in the manual position to make the feed water pump run and inject water into the boiler; when the boiler is full of water, close K1 in the automatic position and open the drain valve to drain the boiler water to the low water level to test automatic starting. If the feed water pump can start automatically, disconnect DZ2 to stop feed water so that the water level continues to reach the lowest limit position; at the lowest limit water level, an alarm should be triggered; if it cannot alarm, check relay 6JZ and its circuit. The function of the drain valve in this process is to drain the boiler water to the low water level after opening so as to observe whether the feed water pump can start automatically.

The debugging of the ignition control system applies to automatic oil-fired boilers. Before debugging, it is necessary to ensure that the boiler water level is normal and close DZ1~DZ4 to energize the ignition control subsystem; close K3 in the manual position to energize 1JZ and energize the ignition control subsystem; close K in the manual position to energize 3C, the fan runs and pre-purge is carried out; if it is the first pre-purge, the time should be longer; after pre-purge, close the air damper a little smaller and make a mark. Start the oil pump by closing K5 in the manual position to establish oil pressure in the pipeline. When manual ignition button 3LA is pressed, the ignition rod produces a spark and the oil valve opens to spray oil. If ignition fails, it is necessary to disconnect DZ5 to stop the oil pump or close the oil valve, and take out the ignition rod for inspection. If there is a spark and oil traces but ignition fails, it may be because the ignition rod is too far away or the oil pressure is insufficient causing poor atomization.

The automatic fuel oil boiler includes regular maintenance items such as ignition system maintenance, feed water system maintenance, air-oil regulating device maintenance and exhaust gas boiler mechanical transmission maintenance. The maintenance period of the ignition system is once every 2 months; the maintenance content and requirements are to check the gap of the ignition rod, the insulation performance of the rod electrode, and the working condition of the photosensitive element and the solenoid valve, to maintain good light transmittance of the photosensitive element, and the photosensitive element must be rotated for use regularly. The maintenance period of the feed water system is once every 2 months; it is necessary to check whether the action of the automatic feed water controller and the water level sensor is sensitive and reliable, and whether the watertightness is good. The maintenance period of the exhaust gas boiler mechanical transmission is once every 2 months; the core content is to check whether the electrical and mechanical parts of the three-way changeover valve are flexible and reliable. The water level sensor is used to detect the boiler water level; when the water level reaches the high water level, the feed water is automatically stopped, and when the water level drops to the dangerous water level, it can send out an audible and visual alarm signal and stop all systems from working; its maintenance period is once every 2 months, and it is necessary to check whether its action is sensitive and reliable and whether its watertightness is good. When the boiler steam pressure reaches the set value, the potentiometer R1 driven by it balances the bridge, and the servo motor stops rotating; the sensor is placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, and its function is to send out an error signal, and the control platform contains the sensor.

The composition and control modes of the general alarm device The general alarm device is an alarm device that issues emergency general mobilization and assembly signals to all crew members and passengers when a ship encounters an emergency such as a major marine casualty or fire. In terms of composition, the general alarm device includes four parts: the shutter, the alarm bell, the alarm lamp and the junction box. The shutter is used to switch the alarm signal on and off, the alarm bell is responsible for emitting the audible signal, the alarm lamp is responsible for emitting the light signal, and the junction box serves as the connection and distribution link between the components and between the device and the ship's power grid. The above four together constitute the on-site execution part of the general alarm device, and none of them can be omitted.

In terms of control mode, the general alarm device includes two modes: the direct control mode and the indirect control mode. In the direct control mode, the emission of the alarm signal is directly driven by the operating component to drive loads such as the alarm bell and the alarm lamp, with few control links and direct action; in the indirect control mode, the operating component does not directly drive the load, but instead connects or disconnects the load circuits such as the alarm bell and the alarm lamp through an intermediate control link. The coexistence of the two control modes enables the general alarm device to adapt to the requirements of different ships and different installation occasions for the structure of the alarm circuit. Regardless of which control mode is adopted, the general alarm device includes the general alarm device control system, which uniformly controls and coordinates the execution part composed of the shutter, the alarm bell, the alarm lamp and the junction box, so that the audible alarm and the light alarm act according to the predetermined requirements.

Inspection points of the general alarm device in the maintenance of the auxiliary boiler electrical control system In the maintenance work of the marine auxiliary boiler electrical control system, the general alarm device is an important link of the alarm branch. Since the general alarm device includes the shutter, the alarm bell, the alarm lamp and the junction box, each of these four parts should be inspected item by item during maintenance. For the shutter, it should be confirmed whether its on-off action is reliable and whether the contacts are in good contact; for the alarm bell, it should be confirmed whether its sound is normal and whether there is abnormal sound caused by moisture or vibration; for the alarm lamp, it should be confirmed whether its filament, lamp holder and light-transmitting cover are intact; for the junction box, it should be confirmed whether its internal wiring is firm, whether the markings are clear, and whether there are hidden dangers of looseness and short circuit. These inspections should all be carried out with the cooperation of the general alarm device control system, that is, alarm commands are applied separately through the control system to observe whether the responses of the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box are consistent with the commands.

In the inspection of the control mode, it should be distinguished whether the general alarm device of the ship adopts the direct control mode or the indirect control mode. If it is the direct control mode, the focus should be on inspecting the direct circuit from the operating component to the alarm bell and the alarm lamp; if it is the indirect control mode, the focus should be on inspecting the intermediate control link and its connection relationship with the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box. The circuit structures of the two control modes are different, and the distribution of fault points is also different, so they cannot be treated the same during maintenance.

The general alarm device includes the general alarm device control system, so the inspection of the control system should also include whether its control logic for the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box is normal, and whether the control system itself can correctly drive the above execution components after the alarm command is issued.

Coordination relationships to be noted in maintenance The general alarm device includes the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, and also includes the direct control mode, the indirect control mode and the general alarm device control system. These components are not isolated from each other. The action result of the shutter must be sent to the alarm bell and alarm lamp through the junction box; whether the alarm bell and alarm lamp act simultaneously and in what order depends on the control mode adopted by the general alarm device control system. During maintenance, if only the alarm bell is replaced or only the alarm lamp is adjusted without checking the shutter and junction box, the fault of the alarm branch often cannot be completely eliminated. Similarly, if only the circuit under the direct control mode is checked while the role of the intermediate link under the indirect control mode is ignored, missed inspection will also result. Therefore, in the maintenance of the marine auxiliary boiler electrical control system, the general alarm device should be regarded as a whole, and inspection and repair should be implemented item by item around the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp, junction box, direct control mode, indirect control mode and general alarm device control system, so that the general alarm device can reliably issue emergency general mobilization and assembly signals to all crew members and passengers in an emergency such as a major marine casualty or fire.

The composition and control modes of the general alarm device The general alarm device undertakes the task of issuing emergency general mobilization and assembly signals to all crew members and passengers when a ship encounters an emergency such as a major marine casualty or fire, so it is also called the emergency assembly alarm. The device is composed of the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp, junction box and other parts, among which the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box each undertake different functional links and together constitute a complete alarm circuit. According to the different ways of connecting the emergency power supply, the control modes of the general alarm device are divided into two categories: the direct control mode and the indirect control mode.

The direct control mode is suitable for ships with a small number of alarm bells and a small current capacity of the feed main line. In this mode, when the shutter is pressed on the bridge, its contact directly connects the emergency power supply, and the alarm bells and alarm lamps of the whole ship immediately emit audible and light signals simultaneously. That is to say, in the direct control mode, the shutter undertakes the role of directly connecting the emergency power supply, and the alarm bell and alarm lamp rely on this power supply to sound and light respectively. The fundamental difference between the direct control mode and the indirect control mode is that no contactor is used, and the power is supplied directly by the shutter contact.

The indirect control mode is suitable for ships with many alarm bells and a large current capacity of the feed main line, also suitable for ships with a relatively thick total feed line cross-section, and for ships where it is difficult to connect the alarm bell power supply to the bridge and then feed it. In this mode, a contactor is installed on the battery charge-discharge board and controlled by the shutter or button on the bridge; the alarm bells and alarm lamps of the whole ship connect the emergency power supply through the closing of the normally open contact of the contactor. It can be seen that in the indirect control mode, the alarm bell and alarm lamp are no longer directly supplied by the shutter contact, but obtain the emergency power supply through the normally open contact of the contactor.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship's power system. It belongs to low-voltage control electrical appliances and is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems. It has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The amount of contactors used on ships is very large, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor itself includes the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance is carried out for these parts.

Functions and interfaces of the general alarm device control system The general alarm device control system is provided with two buttons, "general alarm" and "manual alarm", and is provided with an audible and visual alarm device for main power supply failure. The general alarm signal is output in a cycle of seven short and one long, repeated every 2s; the manual alarm signal is output in the on/off rhythm of the button switch. When the system is connected to the public address system, sounds of different rhythm frequencies can be played from the loudspeaker to distinguish the alarm modes. Its external input terminals include the emergency alarm button, fire alarm equipment (connected after a delay of 2min) and the remote control box beside the lifeboat; when output to the alarm bell control terminal, a closed contact is output under the alarm state to control the electric bell. In addition, the system is also provided with a general alarm remote control box, and can output to the engine room alarm indicator terminal, the fog horn control terminal and the public address system.

Diagnosis and treatment of common faults The general alarm device control system of a certain bulk carrier will show several typical faults during use, which can be checked one by one according to the phenomena.

When only one of the remote start/stop buttons works, the cause lies in the incorrect connection of the common line of the remote buttons. The phenomenon that only one of the remote start/stop buttons works corresponds to the treatment measure of checking whether the common line connection of the remote buttons is correct, and by restoring the correct connection of the common line, both buttons can function normally.

When there is no response to the start operation from the remote button and the control board, the common cause is that the remote start/stop button is connected to the normally closed contact. The phenomenon that there is no response to the start operation from the remote button and the control board corresponds to the treatment step of checking whether the remote start/stop button is connected to the normally closed contact, and if so, changing it to the normally open contact; if it is confirmed to be connected to the normally closed contact, change it to be connected to the normally open contact, and the operation can resume response.

When, after the start operation, the remote start/stop button indicator lamp is on but the control board indicator lamp is not on, the root cause is that the power supply polarity is reversed. Reversed power supply polarity will cause the remote start/stop button indicator lamp to be on but the control board indicator lamp not to be on after the start operation; and the phenomenon that after the start operation the remote start/stop button indicator lamp is on but the control board indicator lamp is not on corresponds to the treatment measure of checking whether the power supply polarity is reversed, and if so, correcting it. If it is confirmed that the power supply polarity is reversed, correcting the polarity can eliminate the fault; its manifestation is that the remote start/stop button indicator lamp is still on while the control board indicator lamp is not on, and the treatment method is to correct the power supply polarity connection.

When the control board indicator lamp is not on after the general alarm device is started, it is likewise necessary to check whether the power supply polarity is reversed. The phenomenon of the indicator lamp not being on may also be caused by failure of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer or KM auxiliary contact in single-speed non-reversible and reversible drive control systems; if one of the functional logic events composed of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact fails, the indicator lamp will not be on, and the phenomenon of the indicator lamp not being on can also occur in the air compressor control circuit. In the overall PLC inspection, if the POWER lamp off, the step of checking the power supply fault needs to be performed, and the power supply fault corresponds to the treatment measure of check the power supply; when the electric fan starts slowly, the troubleshooting method includes checking whether the power supply voltage is too low; when the electric drill fails to start and there is no voltage in the power supply, the power supply line should be checked. These practices of check the power supply are consistent with the idea of checking whether the power supply polarity is reversed when the control board indicator lamp of the general alarm device is not on.

Inspection and measurement of related electrical appliances When troubleshooting the above faults, it is often necessary to use instruments to measure circuit parameters. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand the equipment status; the measurable performance is the current value, and the measuring tools used include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. Using the multimeter to measure current and using the clamp-on ammeter to measure current are both commonly used on-site means. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system, so when checking the power supply circuit of the alarm device, attention to the current value helps to judge whether the circuit is in a normal state.

The fuse is used for overload and short circuit protection in the ship's power system, and the fuse corresponds to the symbol FU. The fuse is a safety electrical appliance; when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; it belongs to distribution electrical appliances and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. In the power supply circuit of the general alarm device, the fuse likewise undertakes the role of overload and short circuit protection.

The junction box is a component used in the ship's electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical elements. In the general alarm device, the junction box is one of the components; the solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box, but directly connected to the local control box; when testing the thermal resistance sensor, it is necessary to disconnect the wiring of the temperature sensor in the junction box. These practices show that the connection methods of the junction box in different circuits are different, and during maintenance it should be handled according to the actual connection of each circuit.

The alarm lamp is used in the general alarm device to emit a light signal. In the direct control mode, the alarm lamp is lit by connecting the emergency power supply through the shutter contact; in the indirect control mode, the alarm lamp is lit by connecting the emergency power supply through the normally open contact of the contactor. During a fault alarm, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room will flash; after the fault alarm is silenced, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room goes out. The alarm bell cooperates with the alarm lamp to emit audible and light signals by connecting the emergency power supply: in the direct control mode, the alarm bell is directly connected to the emergency power supply by the bridge shutter contact; in the indirect control mode, the alarm bell connects the emergency power supply through the closing of the normally open contact of the contactor.

The ship's automatic fire monitoring and alarm device is mainly divided into three categories according to the installation area and detection medium: the automatic fire monitoring and alarm device used for cabins, the automatic fire monitoring and alarm device used for dry cargo holds, and the combustible gas detection device. The whole device is composed of two major parts, the alarm controller and the fire detector, and its basic function is to receive the signal sent by the detector, give audible and visual alarms after processing, and display the specific location where the fire occurs, thereby helping the crew to take fire-fighting measures as early as possible.

The alarm controller is the core component of this device. At present, the main types used on ships are relay-contactor control type, PLC control type and microcomputer control type. Its task is to receive the fire signal sent by the fire detector from the monitoring site, give audible and visual fire alarm signals after processing, and display the location of the fire. In the bus coded transmission system, the fire judgment function is undertaken by the controller, that is, the controller realizes the fire judgment of analog signals. This type of controller can be used in conjunction with intelligent ion smoke detectors, etc., and improve the moisture resistance through the adjustment of circuit parameters. As the core component of the bus coded transmission type centralized alarm system, the alarm controller represents the development direction of the marine fire monitoring system. There is a typical phenomenon in the installation link: if the two wires on the detector base are connected in reverse, after the detector is installed on the ceiling base, the alarm controller will display an alarm in that area; at this time, the multimeter can be used to check the polarity and then reconnect.

The fire detector is composed of a fire parameter sensor or measuring element, a detection signal processing unit and a fire judgment circuit, in which the sensor is responsible for converting physical and chemical effects into measured values. Fire detectors include four major types: smoke-sensing fire detectors, heat-sensing fire detectors, light-sensing fire detectors and combustible gas fire detectors, and the detector is mainly composed of these four. The interior of the smoke-sensing detector includes an ionization chamber or a photosensitive element, and detection is realized through the influence of smoke on the ion current or light flux. In actual systems on ships, detectors are usually connected in parallel, divided into two-wire and four-wire systems; in the two-wire system, the power supply and signal lines coincide, and when a fault occurs, the disconnection of the internal terminal post will cause an open-circuit alarm of the loop. The heat-sensing detector is suitable for places with more dust and oil mist, and its fixed-temperature action temperature is generally 60℃, 70℃ and 90℃. The light-sensing detector needs to be used in conjunction with the smoke-sensing or heat-sensing type, and there must be no light interference of the same wavelength in the detection area.

According to statistics, the smoke-sensing fire detector can detect more than 70% of fires and is widely used in ships. Its main types include the ion type and the photoelectric type. The ion type uses the principle of air ionization to detect fires; the photoelectric type uses smoke to change the light intensity received by the photosensitive element to send an alarm signal, and is divided into the laser type and the scattering type according to the absorption and scattering of light by smoke. The moisture-resistant adaptive performance of the single-source ion smoke detector is better than that of the dual-source type. According to the structural form of the internal ionization chamber, it is further divided into the dual-source smoke-sensing fire detector and the single-source smoke-sensing fire detector. The dual-source smoke-sensing detector uses the adsorption of smoke particles on charged ions to change the characteristic curve of the ionization chamber used for detection, and then processes the voltage difference ΔV formed by the change of the characteristic curve through an electronic circuit to confirm the fire and give an alarm; the dual-source design can reduce the influence of changes in ambient temperature, humidity and air pressure on the ion current. Compared with the single-source type, its environmental adaptability and working stability are higher, and it is currently used more in ships. When the single-source smoke-sensing fire detector detects a fire, both its smoke detection ionization chamber and its compensation ionization chamber work in the sensitive region of their characteristic curves, and the detection and alarm function of the fire is realized by using the change amount of the electrode potential;

It improves the adaptability to slow changes of tiny particles in the operating environment; in terms of the moisture resistance required in humid areas, its adaptive performance is much better than that of dual-source ion smoke fire detectors.

The photoelectric smoke fire detector is a type of point-type fire detector; according to the absorption and scattering of light by smoke particles, it is divided into two types: laser type and scattering type. In the laser-type detector, smoke particles reduce the luminous flux passing through the optical path, causing the photocurrent of the light-receiving element to decrease, and the magnitude of the change of the photocurrent relative to the initial calibrated value reflects the smoke concentration. The photoelectric smoke fire detector includes two types: the light-attenuation photoelectric smoke fire detector and the scattered-light photoelectric smoke fire detector. The working principle of the light-attenuation photoelectric smoke fire detector is: when smoke appears around the detector, the smoke particles entering the photoelectric detection dark chamber absorb and scatter the light emitted by the light source, reducing the luminous flux passing through the optical path, thereby lowering the photocurrent generated on the light-receiving element; the magnitude of the change of this photocurrent relative to the initial calibrated value reflects the smoke concentration.

The photosensitive fire detector includes two categories: the ultraviolet detector and the infrared detector. The ultraviolet detector responds to the ultraviolet spectrum emitted by flames; its sensitive element may use solid substances such as zinc sulfide and lead selenate, or may use a light-sensitive tube; the detection angle is 90°, and during installation it is necessary to ensure that the protected area is within the coverage area; it is suitable for areas with visible flames such as the oil treatment area of drilling platforms, wellheads and the explosion-proof area of chemical tankers; due to its high sensitivity and susceptibility to interference, there must be no light of the same wavelength as the detector in the detection area, and in the same area it must be used together with a smoke or heat detector as an auxiliary detector. The basic structure of the infrared detector includes a filtering device and a lens system; it works by screening out unwanted wavelengths such as the spectra of sunlight and fluorescent lamps, and concentrates the incoming light energy on an infrared-sensitive phototube or photoresistor; it has the advantages of a wide field of view, high sensitivity and strong anti-interference, and its general detection angle is 140°; it likewise belongs to the photosensitive detector in the classification of fire detectors commonly used on ships.

The combustible gas fire detector, also called the flammable gas detection system, is one of the four major types of fire detectors commonly used on ships, alongside the smoke, heat and photosensitive types.

In the maintenance and testing process, resistor, voltage and current are commonly measured objects. The measurable property of resistor is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; when measuring a resistor in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistor, and never measure with power on. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter or voltmeter. The measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. The multimeter can be used to measure resistor, voltage and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control the motor in the ship power system; it belongs to low-voltage control apparatus, is mainly used to control the motor in the electric drive system, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The amount of contactors used on ships is very large, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes components such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the control platform includes sensors. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals, and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The core component of the automatic fire monitoring and alarm device is the fire detector. The fire detector is composed of a fire parameter sensor or measuring element, a detection signal processing unit and a fire judgment circuit; its function is to convert the fire phenomenon into a signal that can be recognized by the alarm controller. In terms of wiring form, the actual systems on ships usually adopt the parallel wiring method, which is specifically divided into two-wire and four-wire types. The smoke fire detector includes two main types: the ion smoke fire detector and the photoelectric smoke fire detector. The photoelectric smoke fire detector uses smoke to change the light intensity received by the photosensitive element to issue an alarm signal; it contains a photosensitive element inside and realizes detection through the influence of smoke on the luminous flux. The photoelectric smoke fire detector can further be divided, according to the absorption and scattering of light by smoke, into laser type and scattering type, among which is included the scattered-light photoelectric smoke fire detector.

The working process of the scattered-light photoelectric smoke fire detector can be described as follows: when smoke appears around the detector, the smoke particles entering the light-shielding dark chamber scatter the light of a certain wavelength emitted by the light-emitting element, i.e. the light source, causing the impedance of the light-receiving element located at a certain angle to change and generating a photocurrent. The magnitude of this photocurrent is related to the intensity of the scattered light, and further reflects the concentration of smoke particles. When the scattered light energy is sufficient to generate a photocurrent of a certain magnitude, the excitation signal processing circuit issues a fire signal, and then the fire information is amplified, compared or subjected to parameter calculation through electronic circuits before the fire signal is transmitted.

The heat fire detector is suitable for places where large amounts of dust, oil mist and water vapor often exist, where the smoke detector cannot be used. In important places, the heat detector can be used simultaneously with the smoke detector to improve monitoring reliability or ensure accurate fire-extinguishing action. According to the principle of action, heat fire detectors are divided into three major categories: fixed-temperature type, rate-of-rise type and rate-of-rise/fixed-temperature type.

The action principle of the fixed-temperature fire detector is: within a specified time, an alarm is started when the temperature rise caused by fire exceeds a certain fixed value. It has the characteristics of simple structure, high reliability and few false actions but poor sensitivity; common action temperature set values are 60℃, 70℃ and 90℃; the main forms include bimetallic type, fusible alloy type and thermistor type, and it is generally suitable for places with high temperature or large environmental changes such as kitchens, boiler rooms and clothes-drying rooms. Environmental temperature changes in winter or summer will have a certain influence on the response time of the probe. The thermistor is a common form of the fixed-temperature fire detector, suitable for environments such as kitchens and boiler rooms; the thermistor is a special semiconductor device whose resistance value changes with the surface temperature; the commonly used NTC thermistor has a negative temperature coefficient, that is, the resistance value decreases as the temperature rises, and it can be used for temperature compensation.

The action condition of the rate-of-rise fire detector is: within a specified time, the temperature rise rate caused by fire exceeds a certain specified value. The rate-of-rise detector of point-type structure acts according to the local thermal effect, and its main temperature-sensing elements include an air diaphragm box and a thermal semiconductor resistor.

The rate-of-rise/fixed-temperature fire detector is formed by combining the functions of the fixed-temperature and rate-of-rise detectors. If one of the functions fails, the other function still works; because of this redundant function, the reliability of fire monitoring is greatly improved, and it is used relatively often in actual ships. The rate-of-rise/fixed-temperature fire detector is generally of point-type structure of the diaphragm box type or thermal semiconductor resistor type.

The photosensitive fire detector, also called the flame detector, is divided into the ultraviolet detector sensitive to short wavelengths and the infrared detector sensitive to long wavelengths. The photosensitive fire detector is suitable for high-risk areas where visible flames may occur and smoke is relatively small; in the same area it must be used together with a smoke or heat detector as an auxiliary, and because of its high sensitivity and susceptibility to false alarms, light of the same wavelength is prohibited in the detection area. In the infrared fire detector, the photoresistor serves as the photosensitive element and receives the light energy concentrated by the lens system.

The photoresistor is a semiconductor element whose resistance value changes with the intensity of external light; the resistance is small when the light is strong and large when the light is weak; it is made by depositing a layer of cadmium sulfide (CdS) film on a ceramic base, and belongs to semiconductor elements. In complete darkness its resistance can reach several megohms or more, and under relatively strong light it can drop to several thousand ohms or even below 1kΩ. In automatic oil-fired boilers, the photoresistor is used to detect the flame; when ignition succeeds, the resistance value of the photoresistor decreases, energizing 1JY, which energizes 3JZ, which energizes 4JZ; 4JZ (31, 28) opens, and the ignition transformer is de-energized. Among the large category of resistor components, besides the photoresistor, the thermistor is also included.

The flammable gas detection system is suitable for ro-ro ships, ferries, firefighting ships and oil tankers, and is used to detect whether the flammable gas in cargo holds or certain cabins on board reaches a dangerous concentration. Since combustible gas density is usually greater than that of air and is not easily dispersed, it is necessary to detect whether its volume exceeds the lower explosion limit to prevent explosion. Among its detection methods, the chemical reagent method measures concentration through the length of color change from the reaction of gas with the reagent; it is accurate but cannot be reused; infrared, spectrophotometer and chromatographic separation methods can measure continuously and accurately, but because of their high price they are only suitable for specialized industrial analysis; the catalytic filament method uses the principle that the resistance of a metal wire changes with gas concentration, but it is affected by inert gases, making readings unreliable. In the fire alarm system, the combustible gas fire detector refers to the flammable gas detection system.

Water vapor is one type of fault cause that leads to false alarms of fire detectors. Water vapor can enter the detector and interfere with its normal operation; water vapor condensed on the relevant components will affect the emission and reception of light. The presence of water sources and vapor sources such as kitchens, laundry rooms or water leaks indoors is one of the main causes; in summer, especially during the plum rain season, the indoor humidity is likely to be very high due to seasonal influence. Most detectors are suitable for environments with relative humidity below 85%, and the smoke fire detector cannot be used in places where large amounts of water vapor often exist.

In the two-wire wiring method, the power line and the signal line coincide. In the normal state, terminal posts ⑥ and ⑦ inside the detector are closed to transmit power; the terminal probe is provided with terminal equipment such as a resistor or Zener diode, and in the normal monitoring state the system has a monitoring current of the microampere level. When a fire occurs, the detector acts, causing the resistance to drop sharply and generating an action current of the milliampere level. If a probe fault causes the internal terminal posts to fail to close, the system will display an open circuit of the loop or a probe fault. In the two-wire wiring of fire detectors, the terminal equipment may use a Zener diode to maintain the microampere-level monitoring current. In the four-wire wiring method, the power line and the signal line are separated from each other; its working principle is similar to that of the two-wire wiring method, and it is suitable for the wiring scenarios of ship fire detectors, requiring the ability to detect states such as detector detachment, faults and line open circuits, and requiring the ability to realize terminal resistor failure detection and the fire alarm function.

The Zener diode is a semiconductor diode whose voltage across the two ends remains basically unchanged after breakdown; its circuit symbol is VS, and in circuits it is often represented by "VS" plus a number, for example VS5 represents the Zener diode numbered 5; its forward conduction characteristics are the same as those of an ordinary diode. Zener diode faults manifest as open circuit, short circuit and unstable voltage regulation value. If there is no response to smoke and no alarm is ever given during black smoke inspection, it may be caused by damage to the Zener diode. The diode has unidirectional conductivity and is often represented by VD in circuits; it is used for rectification, isolation, voltage regulation, etc., and according to its function is divided into rectifier diode (such as 1N4004), isolation diode (such as 1N4148), Schottky diode (such as BAT85), etc.; this large category of diodes includes the light-emitting diode and the Zener diode. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment, and the diode testing steps apply to diodes.

The marine fire alarm system adopts bus-coded transmission technology to form a centralized alarm system; this technical route constitutes the bus-coded transmission type centralized alarm system. The system is composed of parts such as the fire alarm controller, regional display, sound and light alarm device and control module; the intelligent heat or smoke detector must carry an address module to be connected to the system, the control module is used to control fire-fighting linked equipment, and the regional display can be set in the central control room or the accommodation area. A typical system adopts single-chip microcomputer technology, has the characteristics of few wires and convenient installation and commissioning, and is the development direction of marine fire monitoring systems. During maintenance it is necessary to confirm that the detector bus has no short circuit and to measure the voltage at the detection bus output end of the controller; if the voltage at the detection bus output end of the controller is still 8～12V after the detector bus is disconnected, then the bus is faulty. The first two digits of the physical number represent the detection bus position where the detector or module is located. Reversed wiring of the base will cause the area alarm to be displayed on the alarm controller immediately after installation.

The display belongs to radar equipment and is used to display radar images; radar equipment includes the display; the display involves cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface; radar display installation precautions require attention to the display; radar installation applies to the display; the display should be installed in the wheelhouse where there is no strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources and in a dry place, fixed with a hardwood base, with the main radar display oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge.

In testing and maintenance, the multimeter includes a measuring circuit; the multimeter uses resistors; the multimeter uses diodes. The function of the measuring circuit is to convert different electrical quantities and convert different ranges; in the gas detection alarm device it cooperates with the gas-sensitive semiconductor element to realize the continuous detection function; it is also one of the three basic components of the MF-30 and MF-47 analog multimeters, because the magnetoelectric meter head can only pass microampere-level current, so different electrical quantities and ranges need to be measured through the conversion circuit. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating function. The light-emitting diode is a semiconductor device capable of emitting red, green and yellow light, has unidirectional conductivity, and its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode; it is commonly used as a circuit working status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display; its external dimensions include 3mm diameter, 5mm and 2mm×5mm rectangular; its working current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model; in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage; light-emitting diode precautions require attention to the light-emitting diode. RS is used for overload and short circuit protection in the ship power system and belongs to the fuse series used in the ship power system for short circuit and overload protection of devices such as semiconductor rectifiers or thyristor rectifiers; the RS_0 type has a rated voltage of 250 to 900V and current specifications of 30 to 480A; the RS_0 type is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers or their complete sets.

The flammable gas detection system is suitable for ro-ro ships, ferries, firefighting ships and oil tankers, to monitor cargo holds or compartments where flammable gas may accumulate. Its detection methods include the chemical reagent method, the infrared/spectrophotometer/chromatography method, the catalytic filament method and the gas-sensitive semiconductor method. The chemical reagent method passes the gas through a glass tube containing a chemical reagent and uses the color change caused by a chemical reaction for detection, using the length of the faded reagent in the tube as the measurement scale for gas concentration; this method is relatively accurate but the display tube cannot be reused, is suitable for fixed-point measurement scenarios, and cannot perform continuous monitoring. The infrared/spectrophotometer/chromatography method can perform continuous and accurate concentration measurement, but the equipment is expensive and is only suitable for specialized industrial analysis scenarios. The principle of the catalytic filament method is that the gas reacts and burns on a catalytic metal wire, causing the temperature to rise, and detection is performed through the change of the metal wire resistance with the combustible gas concentration; its disadvantage is that it is affected by the inert gas in inert compartments, and because of the influence of the inert gas it cannot provide reliable readings. The gas-sensitive semiconductor method coats a metal oxide on a platinum wire and sinters it at high temperature; the resulting gas-sensitive semiconductor elements are divided by nature into two major categories, N-type and P-type; the resistance of an N-type gas-sensitive semiconductor element decreases when it encounters a sensitive gas, and the resistance of a P-type gas-sensitive semiconductor element increases when it encounters a sensitive gas; at present it is used more in practical applications of flammable gas detection. The explosion-proof safety probe is specially designed for continuous detection and alarming of flammable gas in dangerous areas such as oil tanker cargo pump rooms and pipelines; it belongs to the flameproof structure, so that even if an internal explosion occurs it will not ignite the flammable gas in the external environment; its housing is made of nylon material; its core detection component is the gas-sensitive semiconductor element; the gas-sensitive element is placed in a stainless steel cavity and protected and isolated by sintered metal particles; the flame-arresting effect produced by the sintered metal particles and metal mesh forms the explosion-proof structure.

In the ship automatic fire monitoring and alarm device, the fire detector and the alarm controller are two basic components; the former is responsible for converting the fire phenomenon into an alarm signal, and the latter is responsible for receiving and processing these signals and giving audible and visual alarms and displaying the fire location. Among them, the alarm processing board is the core part, receiving detection information through the internal serial port and communicating with the operating unit through the external serial port; the communication interface board has two RS-232 and two RS-485 serial communication ports built in, used for communication with external computers and printers.

In gas detection, the intrinsically safe pump-suction detection device meets the intrinsic safety requirements through the pump-suction design; its pump box is placed in a safe area to avoid electrical sparks causing ignition of flammable gas; during measurement, the gas at the monitoring points in the dangerous area is drawn through pipes into the pump box, measured by the gas-sensitive semiconductor, and then this dangerous gas is returned to its original place or discharged into the atmosphere at a safe place; the pipe is installed with a flame arrester where it passes through the wall from the safe area to the dangerous area; the flame arrester adopts a stainless steel housing with an embedded sintered metal structure, which can effectively prevent the spread of flame explosion; the pump box is also provided with a pipe blockage monitoring circuit, which clearly indicates and reminds when blockage occurs. Used in conjunction with it is the alarm device for multi-point cyclic monitoring, which performs cyclic monitoring of multiple points (dozens of points) and can complete the suction and measurement of gas at each monitoring point within a set time period; each monitoring point undergoes pre-suction before the measurement suction to obtain the latest sample gas at the monitoring point; the purpose of pre-suction is to ensure that the quality within the average allocated measurement time is not affected by differences in pipe length; the pipe of each monitoring point waiting for measurement is protected by a back-pressure device to prevent water from being sucked in or blockage by debris; the central measuring device is equipped with standard concentration sample gas, so the equipment can be calibrated at any time.

Fire detector faults are mainly divided into two categories: missed alarms and false alarms. A fire detector missed alarm means that the fire has developed to a scale at which an alarm should be given but no alarm is given; it is parallel to false alarm and is one of the main types of fire detector faults; contact-type detectors such as heat-sensitive, smoke-sensitive and gas-sensitive semiconductor detectors may all have missed alarms. When the detector and lines are fault-free, a missed alarm is often caused by the detector not detecting enough smoke; this situation belongs to the missed alarm situation of contact-type detectors such as heat-sensitive, smoke-sensitive and gas-sensitive semiconductor detectors, on the premise that the detector itself and the lines are fault-free, and is commonly seen in scenarios where a fire starts near the floor and the monitored compartment ceiling height exceeds 10m, because it can only be detected when smoke of sufficient concentration or sufficient heat reaches the position; the ceiling height of compartments monitored by commonly used smoke detectors generally does not exceed 10m. The detector being too close to the ceiling causing smoke thermal drop can also cause a missed alarm: when the ambient temperature is high in summer, the air temperature under the indoor ceiling rises, and the high-temperature ceiling air causes the smoke produced by combustion to be unable to reach the ceiling; this phenomenon is usually called the thermal drop of smoke; if the detector is too close to the ceiling, a missed alarm may also be caused by thermal drop; to avoid thermal drop, the smoke detector should keep a certain distance from the ceiling. Forced air flow formed by indoor ventilation devices causing smoke deflection is likewise one of the causes of missed alarms of smoke detectors; it is caused by the forced air flow formed by indoor ventilation devices, resulting in the smoke deflection phenomenon, so that the smoke cannot reach the position of the smoke detector.

A fire detector false alarm means that an alarm signal is issued when no fire has occurred; it is one of the common faults of fire detectors and is parallel to missed alarm; in the automatic fire alarm system, faults occur most often in the detectors and peripheral wiring. There are many causes of false alarms. Too high detector sensitivity is one of the structural causes; too high sensitivity easily causes false alarms, while too low sensitivity causes alarm delay; when the room ceiling is low and the sensitivity is high, smoking easily triggers a false alarm; three people smoking at the same time is enough to make a high-sensitivity smoke detector issue a fire alarm signal. The smoking process is mostly smoldering, and the generated smoke particles are relatively large, which easily causes false alarms of smoke detectors; when the room ceiling is low and the detector sensitivity is high, smoking more easily causes false alarms; the smoke produced by three people smoking at the same time is enough to trigger a smoke detector to issue a fire alarm signal; a single person smoking can interfere with the normal operation of a high-sensitivity smoke detector. The large amount of smoke produced during electric welding operations easily makes fire detectors issue fire alarm signals; when electric welding operations are carried out in the engine room workshop, ship management personnel should pay special attention to prevent false alarms; when electric welding operations are carried out during ship repair at a repair yard, vigilance is needed against their interference with fire detectors. The commonly used smoke inlet mesh aperture is 1.25mm, which can block large insects but cannot block small insects and small spiders; the purpose of providing smoke inlet holes and mesh is to block insects while allowing smoke to enter, and the aperture size needs to be balanced; small insects and spider webs are one of the electrical fault causes that lead to false alarms or interference with the operation of fire detectors. Cooking often produces a large amount of smoke, especially when stir-frying, steaming and boiling, when the amount of smoke is greater; cooking smoke is often mixed with oil vapor, which has a serious impact on the detector; the presence of vapor sources in the kitchen leads to excessive indoor moisture, and water vapor can enter the detector and interfere with its operation. The influence of the lack of cleaning on the detector accumulates gradually; after long-term use of the detector, pollutants will always accumulate inside it; ship management personnel often do not maintain fire detectors for several years, so false alarms inevitably occur frequently. Faults of the detector itself are manifested as the system displaying an alarm in a certain area but there is actually no fire in that area; specific causes include reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor, low dose of the Am-241 piece (or tin-241 piece), thyristor breakdown, etc.; the treatment measure is to replace the faulty detector.

After the detector is installed on the ceiling base, the alarm controller immediately displays an alarm in that area; this is generally caused by the two wires on the base being connected in reverse (except for detectors without polarity requirements), belongs to the base wiring error category in the common fault handling of detectors, and the treatment method is to check the polarity with a multimeter and then swap the wiring. The phenomenon that after the detector is installed on the ceiling base the alarm controller immediately displays an alarm in that area corresponds to the treatment method of checking the polarity with a multimeter and then swapping the wiring. The maintenance procedure of checking the polarity with a multimeter and then swapping the wiring applies to the case except for detectors without polarity requirements, that is, base wiring error of detectors with polarity requirements; this step is used to solve the fault in which the alarm controller immediately displays an area alarm after the detector is installed; the root cause of the fault is usually that the two wires on the base are connected in reverse; before operation, a multimeter must be used to check the line polarity to confirm the reverse connection state. In addition to the manifestation that the two wires of the fire detector base are connected in reverse (except for no polarity requirements), which causes an area alarm to be displayed immediately after installation, incorrect wiring on equipment such as motors can also cause the current direction to reverse due to winding wiring error, causing severe motor vibration, abnormal noise and serious three-phase current imbalance; if the power supply is not cut off in time, winding wiring error may cause the motor winding to burn out; incorrect wiring can also cause the generator voltage to fail to build up normally.

The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument, composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, and is divided into analog and digital types; the analog multimeter belongs to the multimeter, the digital multimeter also belongs to the multimeter, and the MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A, with four jacks "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A" on the panel. The multimeter can be used to measure resistors, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples. A transistor is a semiconductor device containing two PN junctions internally and having current amplification capability, divided into NPN and PNP types, commonly represented in circuits by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17; main models include A92, 9015 (PNP type) and A42, 9014, 9018, etc. (NPN type); when marine electrical equipment uses transistors, transistor faults may occur, and transistor faults belong to transistor-related faults. The thyristor, also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, allows measurement of its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode.

In the maintenance of the automatic fire monitoring and alarm device, the multimeter is one of the most frequently used instruments. The multimeter is composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; it is a multi-purpose instrument and is divided by display mode into analog and digital types; the MF-47 multimeter is one type of analog multimeter, and the digital multimeter likewise belongs to the broad category of multimeters. Diodes and transistors are used in large quantities in marine electrical equipment, so it is very necessary to master the detection methods of these two types of devices.

A diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity, commonly represented in circuits by VD; under forward voltage its conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage its resistance is very large or infinite. Divided by function, diodes include rectifier diodes, isolation diodes, Schottky diodes, light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes, among which rectifier diodes include 1N4004, isolation diodes include 1N4148, and Schottky diodes include BAT85. The diode detection procedure applies to the above various types of diodes, and the measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance. Transistors may suffer transistor faults, which belong to the failure of the transistor itself.

Faults of the detector itself will cause false alarms of the fire detector. When the fire alarm displays an alarm in a certain area but there is no fire in that area, it belongs to a false alarm fault in a certain area; the cause lies in faults of the detector itself, such as reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor, low dose of the Am-241 piece, thyristor breakdown, etc. Specifically, reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor is a manifestation of a fault of the detector itself; a low dose of the Am-241 piece (or tin-241 piece) is likewise a cause of a fault of the detector itself; thyristor breakdown is one of the specific situations causing a fault of the detector itself. Such faults will cause a false alarm in a certain area when there is no fire. For the phenomenon that the fire alarm displays an alarm in a certain area but there is no fire in that area, the corresponding treatment measure is to replace the detector. When there is no fire in a certain area but the alarm displays an alarm and it is confirmed to be a detector fault, replace the detector; this measure applies to false alarms caused by reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor, applies to false alarms caused by low dose of the Am-241 piece, and also applies to false alarms caused by thyristor breakdown.

No response to smoke during a smoke test is another typical fault symptom. Damage to the field-effect transistor will cause the fire detector to have no response to smoke during a black smoke test and never give an alarm; damage to the thyristor or Zener diode will likewise cause no response to smoke during a black smoke test and never give an alarm; this fault is one possible cause of internal component failure of the fire detector, among which thyristor breakdown may also cause the fire alarm to show a false alarm in a certain area. Damage to the field-effect transistor and damage to the thyristor or Zener diode have similar symptoms, and such faults can be troubleshooted by blowing cigarette smoke through a plastic tube or using a special tester for the black smoke test. The black smoke test can be performed by blowing cigarette smoke through a plastic tube, and using a special tester for the black smoke test gives better results. If there is no response to smoke during the black smoke test and no alarm is ever given, and it is component damage, replacement is required; this replacement step applies to the no-response situation in the black smoke test caused by field-effect transistor damage.

The bus control fire monitoring system adopts bus-coded transmission technology to form a centralized alarm system; its fault maintenance focuses on checking peripheral equipment, lines, detectors, input/output modules and the detector bus. When a fault occurs in the fire monitoring system, generally the main check is on peripheral equipment and lines, and the check focuses on all fire detectors, input/output modules and the detector bus; it is necessary to confirm that the detectors have no short circuit and that the connections between the input/output modules and the controlled equipment are not shorted. Under normal conditions all fire detectors and input/output modules should be fully registered in the controller. During maintenance, the step of connecting the detection bus to the detection bus output terminal of the controller, turning on the controller power, and checking whether the fire detectors and input/output modules are all registered must be performed. If all detectors and input/output modules of a loop are registered, it is determined that the loop has no fault. If not a single detector or input/output module of a loop is registered, the voltage at the detection bus output terminal of the controller needs to be measured; under normal conditions this voltage should be 8～12V; if only some detectors and input/output modules of a loop are registered, it indicates that the unregistered detectors and input/output modules have open-circuit faults, and there are also duplicate number faults, that is, the unregistered detectors and input/output modules have faults such as broken wires and duplicate numbers. In addition, if the registered detectors and input/output modules report a fire alarm or fault, but there is no fire alarm or fault at the location of the detector or input/output module, this phenomenon likewise indicates that the detectors and input/output modules have duplicate numbers, and it is a typical fault that needs to be troubleshooted in the maintenance and debugging of the bus control fire monitoring system.

Program the fire detectors and input/output modules on the fire alarm controller; before execution it is necessary to confirm that all fire detectors and input/output modules have been registered in the system. The second step of the programming operation is to select the detector or input/output module type; the selectable types include ion smoke detector, photoelectric smoke detector, input module, photoelectric combined detector, ion smoke-temperature combined detector, area display, heat detector, manual alarm button, output module and fire hydrant alarm button; before a type is selected, all detectors or input/output modules default to the ion smoke detector; the core purpose of this step is to keep the types registered in the system consistent with the actually installed hardware types. After completing the above two steps, perform display address programming; for the output module, the display address is generally programmed as the name and location of the equipment it controls; for the input module, the display address is generally programmed as the name and location of the detector or equipment it displays; the display address of other equipment is programmed as the location of the detector, so as to quickly find it after an alarm. After completing the display address programming, the output module still needs subsequent programming work, while the detectors and manual alarm buttons are fully programmed after the display address programming. Module location programming applies only to input/output modules and does not apply to other equipment such as detectors or manual alarm buttons; the module location is defined as the specific position number of the input/output module on the linkage panel, with a numerical range of 0 to 599; this step is located after the display address programming and before the linkage logic relationship programming. After repair, it is necessary to confirm that all equipment has been registered, and then program the physical number and type.

The marine fire alarm system adopts bus-based coded transmission technology to form a centralized alarm system, in which the bus is both a bus-type structure for transmitting data and instructions inside the programmable logic controller and a coded transmission line connecting the detectors and the controller in the fire monitoring system. Among the faults of the programmable logic controller, a CPU bus fault will cause the input relay to act abnormally.

The automatic fire monitoring and alarm device includes an alarm controller and a fire detector.

When the detectors and input/output modules have duplicate numbers, the symptom is that only part of the detectors and input/output modules of a certain loop are registered on the controller, and also that registered equipment reports a fire alarm or fault but there is actually no fire or fault at the actual location; this is one of the common fault types of the detectors and modules of a bus-controlled fire monitoring system. The second step of the programming operation is to select the type of detector or input/output module; before the type is selected, the equipment defaults to an ion-type smoke detector.

The linkage logic relationship programming is likewise only applicable to input/output modules, and its logic relationships include: when any fire hydrant button alarms, the fire pump control module is automatically started; when any water flow indicator alarms, the sprinkler pump control module is automatically started; when there is a fire alarm in any area, the fire alarm broadcast control module of the adjacent area is started.

Whether the input/output module works normally should be checked before programming the logic relationships. The checking method is: on the linkage panel, use the mouse to start the selected input/output module, and the indicator lamp on the module should light; when the two ends of the module input signal are short-circuited, the lamp at the corresponding position of this block on the alarm controller panel should light. If the lamps do not light in the above two cases, it indicates that there is a fault in the module or the wiring. During commissioning, the control output end is not connected to the controlled equipment and is connected only during joint commissioning; the feedback signal input can remain connected to the controlled equipment throughout commissioning. During commissioning, the control output end of the input/output module is not connected to the controlled equipment, that is, during system commissioning the control output end of the input/output module must not be connected to the controlled equipment; only when system commissioning is completed and joint commissioning is required is the control output end connected to the controlled equipment, while during commissioning the feedback signal input end can remain connected to the controlled equipment all the time.

The marine water mist fire extinguishing system mainly consists of three major parts: the local control part, the cargo control room part and the bridge display part. The local control part is one of the three main parts, and its composition includes the local control box, fresh water tank, inlet valve, fresh water feed pump, filter, check valve, fresh water cabinet, drain valve, high-pressure fresh water pump, pressure gauge, main isolation valve, safety valve, solenoid valves of each zone and nozzles of each zone, and also includes a liquid level indicator with four indication functions: high level, low level, low-low level and lowest level. Fresh water enters the fresh water tank through the inlet valve, feed pump, filter and check valve; when the water level is above the low level and any zone acts, the high-pressure fresh water pump is started. The local control part is responsible for the water mist release execution of seven zones in total: the main engine area, No.1-3 generators, the incinerator, the oil separator and the boiler. The cargo control room part mainly consists of one control box; on the cargo control room control box, remote release of each sub-zone can be realized, and the signal of the ship fire system can enter the water mist fire extinguishing system from the cargo control room part. The bridge display panel part corresponds to component No.16 in the system diagram, and its main function is to display the release situation of each area of the engine room; together with the local control part and the cargo control room part, it constitutes the whole system.

The solenoid valves of each zone are components of the local control part of the water mist fire extinguishing system, numbered 17 in the system, located after the main isolation valve and before the nozzles of each zone, and usually powered by DC24V. After high-pressure fresh water passes through this solenoid valve, it is released through the nozzles for fire extinguishing; when it acts, the cargo control room control box and the bridge display show the release zone and give an alarm, and it is remotely controlled by the cargo control room control box to realize release control of each sub-zone. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel oil; at ignition it cuts off the fuel oil circulation loop and oil enters the nozzle to be injected, and the automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve. The display is used to display radar images and, as a component of the fire monitoring system, displays area fire alarm information in the centralized control room or the accommodation area; the display also includes two maintenance items: cleaning of the display air filter and cleaning of the display surface.

Faults occurring during commissioning and operation of the water mist fire extinguishing system can often be traced separately in the links of fresh water supply, pressure build-up, zone release and communication. After the fresh water feed pump is started, if no water flow or insufficient water flow is found in the fresh water tank, the emergency stop button should be pressed immediately; this operation corresponds to preventing the centrifugal pump from rotating in reverse and dragging down the motor, thereby burning out the fuse. There is more than one cause of this phenomenon: the water valve from the fresh water tank to the fresh water pump not being opened or not being fully opened will directly cause no water flow or insufficient water flow in the fresh water tank; the incorrect rotation direction of the motor connected to the fresh water feed pump will likewise cause no water flow or insufficient water flow in the fresh water tank; the filter or check valve being installed in the reverse direction will also cause no water flow or insufficient water flow in the fresh water tank. For the first cause, the corresponding treatment is to check whether the water valve from the fresh water tank to the fresh water pump is opened or fully opened; if it is not opened or not fully opened, this valve should be fully opened immediately at this time; for the second cause, the corresponding treatment is to check whether the rotation direction of the motor connected to the fresh water feed pump is correct; if the rotation direction is reversed, it must be adjusted immediately. The fresh water feed pump consists of six ordinary centrifugal pumps connected in series and its rotation is directional; once the motor rotates in reverse, the centrifugal pumps deliver no water or only a small amount of water flow, while the motor is in an overload state with excessive current, and the fuse of the motor in the local control box may be burned out. Therefore, after the system is energized, the rotation direction of the motor connected to the fresh water feed pump should first be checked, and if reverse rotation is found, the motor wiring or rotation direction should be adjusted immediately. As for the filter or check valve, each has a specific installation direction requirement; if either one or both are installed in reverse, no water flow or insufficient water flow in the fresh water tank will result, and they need to be reinstalled according to the direction requirements.

In order to confirm the fresh water feed pump link before energizing, the step "before the system is energized, the drain cock of the fresh water feed pump should be opened; if a large amount of water flows out, it means this link is normal" should be performed; the purpose of this pre-check is precisely to avoid the fault of no water flow or insufficient water flow in the fresh water tank after startup. Current value is a measurable electrical quantity; the multimeter is used for current measurement, the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement, and in addition an ammeter is also used to measure current, through which the equipment state is understood, wherein the ammeter needs to be connected in series after the circuit is disconnected. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system, and the overload caused by the aforementioned reverse rotation belongs to this category; the fuse, as a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material with a low melting point and certain mechanical strength, together with the resistor and capacitance, is a commonly used component in electronic circuits, and its material is mostly aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy; it burns out first under overload to cut off the circuit.

Faults regarding the main isolation valve manifest as main isolation valve fault and incorrect wiring of the main isolation valve limit switch. During commissioning of the local control box, this valve should first be closed, but the limit switch should be artificially put in the open state; the purpose of doing so is to prevent high-pressure fresh water from directly spraying into each sub-zone before it is truly confirmed whether the solenoid valves of each sub-zone work well, causing damage to unprotected equipment. The main isolation valve limit switch of this system should be connected at the closed contact; if the main isolation valve limit switch is connected at the normally open contact, incorrect wiring of the main isolation valve limit switch will result, and the corresponding treatment is to connect the main isolation valve limit switch at the closed contact.

The cause of damage to the pressure gauge at the high-pressure pump outlet is: there is a small amount of air in the small pipeline from the high-pressure pump outlet to the pressure gauge; when the high-pressure pump is started directly after the bypass valve is closed, the pressure gauge is very easily damaged under the impact of the small amount of high-pressure air. The corresponding treatment is that before the test the bypass valve must first be put in the open state, and the high-pressure pump is manually started on the local control box so that it runs for 2~3min in the bypass state of the bypass valve, ensuring that the air in the small pipeline connected to the pressure gauge is driven out; then the bypass valve is closed, the high-pressure pump is manually started, and the high-pressure pump outlet pressure is checked. The normal range of the high-pressure pump outlet pressure of this system is 70~130kg, and under normal circumstances the high-pressure pump outlet pressure is adjusted to 100kg.

Abnormality of the sound and light alarm and solenoid valve of each zone is another common fault type, involving the sound and light alarms and solenoid valves of each zone of the water mist fire extinguishing system. The sound and light alarm of each zone gives alarm indication on the cargo control room control box and the bridge display. One cause of the abnormality is that the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarm and solenoid valve are connected in reverse; the corresponding treatment is to swap the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarm and solenoid valve, and under normal circumstances swapping the positive and negative poles of the power supply can solve this fault.
