The second cause is that the wiring mode of the solenoid valve of the paint room zone differs from that of the other six zones; the solenoid valve of this zone is not connected inside the external junction box but is connected directly from the solenoid valve to the local control box, and this part of the wiring is very easily misconnected to the solenoid valve of the fresh water feed pump. The third cause is that the valve core of the solenoid valve is stuck with impurities such as iron filings; at this time the solenoid valve function fails and high-pressure fresh water is mistakenly sprayed, manifesting as high-pressure fresh water directly spraying into each area; the corresponding treatment is that before formal spraying the manual release switch should be manually opened and closed several times, this operation being performed on the manual release switch below the solenoid valve of each area, with the purpose of preventing impurities such as iron filings in the pipelines of a new ship from sticking at the valve core of the solenoid valve. In the water mist fire extinguishing system it serves as the release device of each zone, usually powered by DC24V, and its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated at power-off and to accelerate discharge.

Abnormal communication between the local control box and the cargo control room (ECR) has causes including incorrect connection of the communication line and incorrect connection of the power line. For incorrect connection of the communication line, it is only necessary to ensure that the color and number of the line are correct when connecting the communication line; for incorrect connection of the power line, a multimeter can be used to check the line, and before energizing the power line in the cargo control room should be disconnected, and after energizing the positive and negative poles are distinguished with the multimeter before connection.

The sound and light alarms and solenoid valves of each zone of the water mist fire extinguishing system are all powered by the DC24V power supply; reverse connection of the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarm and solenoid valve will cause abnormality of the sound and light alarm and solenoid valve of each zone. To eliminate this fault, under normal circumstances it is only necessary to swap the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarm and solenoid valve, that is, to restore normal operation of the alarm and solenoid valve by exchanging the positive and negative pole wiring of the power supply. The junction box is used in the marine electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical components; the general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc.; when testing the thermal resistance type sensor, the wiring of the temperature sensor needs to be disconnected in the junction box. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel oil circulation loop, release residual air from the air compressor or control the water mist fire extinguishing zone; the automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve, and in the burner ignition program the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation loop so that oil enters the nozzle to be injected; its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated at power-off and to accelerate discharge;

Impurities such as iron filings stuck at the valve core of the solenoid valve will also cause abnormality of the sound and light alarm and solenoid valve of each zone. If impurities stick the valve core, the solenoid valve function fails and high-pressure fresh water is mistakenly sprayed; this fault manifests as high-pressure fresh water directly spraying into each area.

When communication between the local control box and the cargo control room (ECR) is abnormal, three measures can be taken. Second, use a multimeter to check the line, which is used to distinguish the lines when the models of the power lines in the cargo control room are mixed, and to distinguish the positive and negative poles of the power line after energizing; before operation the power line in the cargo control room needs to be disconnected. Third, before energizing the power line in the cargo control room should be disconnected, and after energizing the positive and negative poles are distinguished with the multimeter before connection; this step is applicable to the connection of the communication power line between the local control box and the cargo control room of the water mist fire extinguishing system, and in view of the situation that multiple power lines of different models may appear in the cargo control room and cause wiring confusion, the operation requires that the power line in the cargo control room must be disconnected before the system is energized, and after energizing the positive and negative poles of the power line must be distinguished with a multimeter before connection can be made.

The object targeted by this step is the main isolation valve of the water mist fire extinguishing system; the operation requires first closing the main isolation valve while artificially putting the limit switch in the open state, with the purpose of preventing high-pressure fresh water from directly spraying into each sub-zone before it is truly confirmed whether the solenoid valves of each sub-zone work well, causing damage to unprotected equipment; the main isolation valve limit switch of this system should be connected at the closed contact.

No water flow or insufficient water flow in the fresh water tank is a common fault symptom of the water mist fire extinguishing system, referring to no water flow or insufficient flow in the tank after the fresh water feed pump is started. For no water flow or insufficient water flow in the fresh water tank, it should be checked whether the water valve from the fresh water tank to the fresh water pump is opened or fully opened; if it is not opened or not fully opened, this valve should be fully opened immediately at this time. Motor reverse rotation will cause the centrifugal pump to deliver no water and the motor to be overloaded and burn out the fuse. When this fault occurs, the emergency stop button should be pressed immediately; the preventive checking method is to open the drain cock before energizing and observe whether there is a large amount of water flow. During commissioning, the bypass valve must first be opened and the pump run for 2~3min to drive out the air, and then the bypass valve is closed to check this pressure; if the high-pressure pump is started directly without driving out the air in the pipeline, the impact of a small amount of high-pressure air easily damages the pressure gauge.

Nozzle blockage mostly occurs at the small nozzles on the second layer counted from the main engine side; this location is the lowest point of the system, and dirt in the piping system gathers at the lowest point of the system, namely the position on the second layer counted from the main engine side, due to gravity; this gathering phenomenon makes the seven small nozzles on the second layer counted from the main engine side the most easily blocked points of the system. The treatment measure is that before each water discharge of the system, these seven small nozzles are first removed and flushed with high-pressure fresh water for about 1min, and then reinstalled; the execution timing is to perform the removal and flushing operation before each water discharge of the system, and the specific operation is to remove the seven nozzles, flush them with high-pressure fresh water for about 1 minute, and reinstall the nozzles after flushing is completed to ensure that blockage no longer occurs subsequently.

The cold storage call alarm device consists of a call switch, a call lamp installed in this store, and call bells installed at two places, the kitchen and the dining room. When a crew member is mistakenly locked in the store and cannot get out, the alarm is triggered as soon as the call switch K3 in the store is pressed. Switch K3 has one set of contacts inside; when this set of contacts closes, the call lamp HL3 of this store lights up, thereby sending out the call signal; switch K3 also has another set of contacts, and when this set of contacts acts, the call bells HA1 and HA2 in the kitchen and the dining room sound, forming the rescue alarm sound. At the same moment the alarm acts, the call lamps HL1 and HL2 corresponding to the kitchen and the dining room respectively are also lit. To cancel the alarm, the method adopted is to directly turn off the call switch. The whole device relies on the call switch to link the lamp in the store with the bells and lamps of the kitchen and the dining room, constituting the cold storage safety alarm device, so that a mistakenly locked person can promptly send a help signal to the outside. From the circuit relationship, call switch K3 is the signal initiating element of this device, and the call lamp HL3 of this store as well as the call lamps HL1 and HL2 of the kitchen and the dining room and the call bells HA1 and HA2 are all its controlled objects; therefore, to judge whether the device is normal, it should be separately confirmed whether the on-off of the two sets of contacts of K3 is reliable, whether HL3 can light up, whether HA1 and HA2 can sound, whether HL1 and HL2 can light up synchronously, and whether all signals disappear after the call switch is turned off.

The patient call alarm system mainly consists of a call board, a call button, and a responder installed at the chief officer's room and other places; its purpose is for the patient to call when medical staff are needed at the sickbed in the ward. After the patient presses the call button SB provided beside the sickbed, the relay KM in the bridge call board is energized and acts, one set of its contacts performs the self-holding function so that the relay continues to remain in the actuated state; another set of contacts lights up HL1 on the ward alarm board, and at the same time connects the call bells at three places: the dining room, the chief officer's room and the bridge. Pressing the answer button SB2, SB3 or SB4 at any one place can cause the relay to be de-energized and released, thereby completing silencing. At the same time as silencing, the call lamp HL1 on the ward call board goes out accordingly, from which the patient knows that the alarm signal has been received.

This system belongs to the ship's medical cabin alarm device and consists of a call panel and buttons, for patients to call medical staff from their beds. When checking this system, confirm item by item around the call button SB, the self-holding contact of relay KM, HL1 on the ward alarm panel, and the three call bells in the dining room, the chief officer's room and the wheelhouse, and verify that the three answer buttons SB2, SB3 and SB4 can all cause KM to de-energize and release, with HL1 going out accordingly.

The general alarm device includes the alarm lamp as a component; the function of the alarm lamp is to give a light signal in an emergency, and it is also one of the components of the general alarm device, namely the emergency assembly alarm. When the direct control mode is adopted, the alarm lamp lights up by connecting to the emergency power supply via the shutter contact. As a component of the general alarm device, whether the alarm lamp lights depends on whether the shutter contact connects to the emergency power supply; therefore, when checking the alarm lamp in the direct control mode, the connected state of the shutter contact and the power supply condition of the emergency power supply should be confirmed together.

The engineer safety alarm system is applicable to unattended engine rooms or one-man engine rooms, and its function is to ensure that the engineer works safely. Before the engineer goes down into the engine room to work, this system needs to be switched on first. If personal injury occurs during work and the system cannot be reset within the fixed time, the system will give an alarm, and the alarm signal is sent to the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the engine room monitoring and alarm system; the engine room monitoring and alarm system will again send this alarm signal to the extension alarm system, and then forward it to the wheelhouse, crew rooms and public places, to remind the relevant personnel to go to the rescue. If it can be reset within the fixed time, the system restarts the alarm timing until the engineer leaves safely and switches off the system. The control circuit of this system consists of three parts, namely the control circuit in the centralized control console, the start/stop button box at the engine room entrance and the reset button box at the stairway entrance. In the control circuit, the rotary switch K2 is connected in parallel with the start/stop button at the engine room entrance, and both can control the start and stop of the system. The working process of this system can be understood in time order as follows: the engineer switches on the system before entering the engine room, and the system immediately starts timing; if personal injury occurs during work and no reset is made within the fixed time, the alarm is sent step by step via the engine room extension alarm lamp column, the engine room monitoring and alarm system and the extension alarm system to the wheelhouse, crew rooms and public places; if the reset is completed within the fixed time, the timing restarts until the engineer leaves safely and switches off the system.

The control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system consists of the control circuit, the start/stop button box and the reset button box. Among them, the control circuit is arranged in the centralized control console, the start/stop button box is located at each engine room entrance, and the reset button box is set at the stairway entrance of the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the engine room monitoring and alarm system. If injury occurs during work and no reset is made within the fixed time, the system will send an alarm to the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the like; the alarm signal is sent via the engine room monitoring and alarm system to the wheelhouse and the relevant crew rooms, to remind personnel to rescue. If the reset is successfully completed within the fixed time, the system will restart the alarm timing until the engineer leaves safely. This control circuit is used in unattended engine rooms to ensure the personal safety of the engineer, and consists of the control circuit in the centralized control console, the entrance start/stop box and the stairway reset box. As for the installation positions, the control circuit is in the centralized control console, the start/stop button boxes are distributed at each engine room entrance, and the reset button box is set at the stairway entrance of the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the engine room monitoring and alarm system; the three are located in different positions in space, and they should be checked one by one according to this distribution during inspection.

When checking and maintaining the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system, one requirement is to check that the wiring of all components is correct and firm, and another requirement is to measure that there is no short circuit on the power supply side and that the polarity is correct. Both requirements apply to the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system.

Checking that the wiring of all components is correct and firm covers each component and its connection points in the control circuit, the start/stop button box and the reset button box, with the purpose of eliminating incorrect wiring and looseness; measuring that there is no short circuit on the power supply side and that the polarity is correct is to confirm the power supply inlet before energizing, avoiding damage to components caused by short circuit or reversed polarity. In addition, for the convenience of debugging, the delay of time relay KT1 can be adjusted from 27min to 2min, and KT2 to 1min; this adjustment also applies to the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system. The time relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship's power system, commonly marked KT, SJ, SL. The contactor contains a coil, which is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. The insulation resistance tester contains two measuring coils inside, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

Before energizing the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system, a series of preparatory work must be done, and one of the first items is to check that the wiring of all components is correct and firm. According to the acceptance standard, components should be installed correctly and fixed firmly, the system should be kept clean, the structure complete without missing parts, and the electrical insulation performance good. This maintenance procedure applies to the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system and is the basic work that must be carried out before energizing.

After the wiring check is done, next measure that there is no short circuit on the power supply side and that the polarity is correct. This step also applies to the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system; it is necessary to measure and confirm that there is no short circuit on the power supply side and that the power supply polarity is connected correctly. It is located after checking the component wiring and before adjusting the time relays; only when there is no short circuit on the power supply side and the polarity is correct are the conditions in place for subsequent energizing and debugging.

Further on, for the convenience of debugging, the delay of time relay KT1 is adjusted from 27min to 2min, and KT2 to 1min. This step also applies to the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system and belongs to the preparatory work before energizing, with the purpose of facilitating subsequent debugging. The specific method is to adjust the delay of time relay KT1 from 27min to 2min, and adjust the delay of time relay KT2 to 1min. The time relay performs control or protection functions in the ship's power system and is commonly marked with symbols such as KT, SJ, SL on circuit diagrams. The above settings are only for the debugging stage: KT1 is changed from 27min to 2min, and KT2 to 1min.

In fault diagnosis, the conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation. The objects of observation include abnormal phenomena, part conditions, wire conditions and equipment operating parameters, that is, checking whether parts are jammed or damaged, whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt, and noting whether operating parameters deviate from the normal range. Observation is a sub-step of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged". In the diagnosis order, interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation: first learn the situation from the operator, then go to the site for observation; observation is in turn the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device: after obtaining a preliminary impression, go to check the various monitoring and indicating devices.

Voltage is a measurable performance; the measuring tool is the multimeter, or a voltmeter. In ship electrical fault diagnosis, voltage is one of the meter readings that need to be checked.

There is a co-occurrence association between the engineer safety alarm system and the alarm lamp, and there is likewise a co-occurrence association between the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system and the alarm lamp; when troubleshooting alarm system faults, the alarm lamp and its power supply circuit should be checked together.

For the engine room monitoring and alarm system to monitor equipment operating states and display parameters, it must first rely on various sensors to convert changes in the measured quantity into signals convenient for transmission and processing. According to the form of the output signal, the information acquisition devices in the ship monitoring and control system are divided into two major categories: analog and switching-value sensors. An analog sensor converts the parameter into a continuously varying electrical signal and can both monitor the equipment state and display the specific value of the parameter, being suitable for occasions where it is necessary both to judge whether the equipment is normal and to read the actual values of temperature, pressure, level, etc. This type of sensor outputs an electrical quantity that varies continuously with the measured quantity; after the computer reads this quantity, it can both compare it with the set value to judge whether the equipment exceeds the limit and send the value directly to the display screen for the duty personnel to read, so it simultaneously undertakes the two tasks of state monitoring and parameter display. A switching-value sensor converts the parameter limit-exceeding condition into switching-value information of contact opening or closing; it gives only the two states of on and off, so it is only used to monitor whether the equipment is normal and does not undertake the task of continuously displaying parameter values. This type of sensor is usually composed of elements such as pressure relays, temperature switches and level switches; when the measured quantity reaches the actuating value the contact flips, and the computer only needs to identify whether the contact is closed or open to judge whether the corresponding equipment is in a normal or abnormal state. The two types of sensors have a clear division of labor in the engine room monitoring and alarm system: the former is oriented to continuous measurement of quantities, the latter to out-of-limit judgment of limit values; when configuring measuring points, parameters whose specific values need to be read should use analog sensors, while parameters for which only normality needs to be judged may use switching-value sensors.

The signal sent out by the sensor cannot enter the computer directly; in between it must pass through the corresponding input interface and alarm control unit. The measuring circuit of the analog alarm control unit undertakes the task of converting the information sent by the analog sensor into a voltage signal; for example, the resistance change of the thermistor is converted by the measuring circuit into a corresponding voltage signal and then further processed. The reason the measuring circuit first turns quantities such as resistance into voltage is that the subsequent links of comparison, judgment and feeding into the computer all use the voltage quantity as a unified intermediate quantity; only by normalizing the outputs of different types of sensors to the voltage form can the same set of circuits be used to process different parameters such as temperature, pressure and level. This measuring circuit also has a self-check capability: when the sensor is open-circuited or short-circuited, it sends a fault signal, enabling the system to distinguish an abnormality of the sensor itself from a parameter limit excess. This distinction is crucial for maintenance judgment: if a measuring point shows a fault signal rather than a limit alarm, the problem lies in the sensor and its connecting circuit, and the wiring should be checked for looseness and the sensor for damage; if it shows a limit alarm, the sensor itself is working normally and the operating parameter of the measured equipment has indeed exceeded the set range. The function of the analog input interface is to convert the analog signal sent by the analog sensor via the A/D converter into a digital quantity and send it into the computer, and the computer completes the comparison, judgment, display and alarm. The A/D converter is the key link in the analog channel; only the converted digital quantity is convenient for the computer to store, calculate and send via the communication network to other display terminals. The switching-value input interface realizes electrical isolation between the sensor circuit and the I/O interface and CPU by means of an optical isolator, separating the field circuit from the interface board in this way to protect the interface board from damage by abnormal voltages on the field side. The optical isolator transmits signals by means of light, and there is no direct electrical connection between the field side and the interface board side; therefore, when surges, induced overvoltage or earthing potential differences occur in the field circuit, the components on the interface board side are not subjected to impact, and the interface board is effectively protected.

The installation positions and uses of sensors on ships are not limited to the interior of the engine room. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively; when the ship pitches and rolls, the sensors in these two directions send out error signals to control the compensating motion so as to keep the antenna platform stable. The sensor in the X-axis direction detects the tilt deviation in that direction, and the sensor in the Y-axis direction detects the tilt deviation in the other direction; the error signals of the two directions are sent together to the control link, which drives the actuator to perform the corresponding compensating action, thereby offsetting the influence of hull sway on antenna pointing. It can thus be seen that the control platform contains sensors, and the sensors are the sensing link by which the control platform realizes error detection and compensating action; without the error signals sent by the sensors in these two directions, the compensating motion would lose its basis for action. Also belonging to the sensing link is the field of fire detection: the fire detector consists of a fire parameter sensor or measuring element, a detection signal processing unit and a fire judgment circuit, in which the sensor is responsible for converting the physical and chemical effects produced during combustion into measured values for the subsequent circuits to judge whether a fire has occurred. The detection signal processing unit amplifies and shapes the measured values sent by the sensor, and the fire judgment circuit then determines, based on the processed signals, whether the fire condition is reached; the three work together in the order of sensing, processing and judgment.

Once an alarm is established, in addition to giving a prompt on the display screen, the system must also attract the attention of the duty personnel through audible and visual devices. The general alarm device includes the alarm lamp; the alarm lamp is one of the components of the general alarm device and gives a light signal in an emergency. The general alarm device is used on occasions such as emergency assembly; the alarm lamp works together with the audible device so that personnel can learn of the alarm through the visual channel even in a noisy environment. In the direct control mode, the alarm lamp lights up by connecting to the emergency power supply through the shutter contact, so that a visible alarm indication can still be given under emergency power supply conditions. The significance of this power supply mode is that when the main power supply is lost, the alarm lamp can still be lit by the emergency power supply, and the alarm indication will not disappear together with the main power supply. As far as the engine room monitoring and alarm system is concerned, when a fault alarm occurs, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room flashes, prompting the occurrence of a fault with flashing light; when the duty personnel press the silence button and the fault alarm is silenced, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room goes out and the light signal stops accordingly. The rotating alarm lamp expands the visible range of the light by rotating, and flashing makes the light different from steady lighting, making it easier for the duty personnel to notice. These two states of the alarm lamp, flashing and going out, correspond to the two stages of alarm establishment and silencing, and constitute the basic visual manifestation of the engine room alarm. When checking the alarm function, the state of the alarm lamp can be used to judge whether the system works normally: if an alarm occurs but the alarm lamp does not flash, the alarm lamp itself and its power supply circuit should be checked; if the alarm lamp still does not go out after silencing, the coordination between the silencing link and the alarm lamp control circuit should be checked.

Viewing the above links in series: the engine room monitoring and alarm system obtains information from sensors; analog sensors provide continuously varying electrical signals, and switching-value sensors provide switching-value information of contact on/off; the measuring circuit of the analog alarm control unit converts the analog information into a voltage signal and sends a fault signal when the sensor is open-circuited or short-circuited; the switching-value input interface separates the sensor circuit from the I/O interface and CPU by means of an optical isolator, protecting the interface board; after an alarm is established, the alarm lamp in the general alarm device gives flashing light, and after silencing the alarm lamp goes out. The sensors send error signals in the X-axis and Y-axis directions of the ship station antenna control platform to control the compensating motion, and convert physical and chemical effects into measured values in the fire detector; all this shows that, as information acquisition devices, the specific form and installation position of sensors vary with the monitored object, but the basic function of converting the measured quantity into a processable signal is the same.

For maintenance purposes, mastering this signal flow helps locate faults by stage: first confirm whether the sensor output is normal, then check the conversion and isolation stages of the measuring circuit and input interface, and finally verify the alarm lamp action at the alarm output end; by troubleshooting section by section, the fault scope can be narrowed down to a specific component or wiring.

In the engine room monitoring and alarm system, analog sensors undertake the task of converting the monitored parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, and the thermistor is one commonly used type. The thermistor belongs to the broad category of resistors; it is a special semiconductor device whose resistance value changes with the surface temperature, and its resistance value changes with the surface temperature. The commonly used NTC type has a negative temperature coefficient, that is, the resistance value decreases as the temperature rises, and this characteristic makes it suitable for temperature compensation. In the monitoring system, the thermistor is used as an analog sensor, and its resistance value is converted into a voltage signal for use by the comparison stage. Unlike analog sensors, switching sensors convert parameter limit-exceeding conditions into switching information of contact opening or closing, and are only used to monitor whether the equipment is normal; analog sensors are suitable for occasions where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. The measuring circuit must not only complete normal signal conversion but also give a fault indication when an abnormality such as an open circuit or short circuit occurs in the sensor circuit, so that operating personnel can distinguish whether the parameter has exceeded the limit or the measuring circuit itself has a problem. For an analog sensor such as a thermistor, to judge whether it works normally, on the one hand one should see whether the displayed reading changes continuously with the monitored parameter, and on the other hand one should see whether the measuring circuit issues an open-circuit or short-circuit fault signal; once a fault signal appears, one should first check whether the sensor wiring is loose, broken or shorted, and then check the conversion stage of the measuring circuit, and must not conclude that the sensor is damaged merely because the displayed value is high or low.

The comparison stage in the analog alarm control unit usually consists of the alarm value setting potentiometer and the upper/lower limit alarm jumper wires. A potentiometer is a manually adjustable component with three pins, in which the resistance between two pins is fixed and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes with the rotation of the shaft; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment belongs to this type. In automatic fuel oil boilers, the potentiometer has a specific application: the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 driven by the motor M form a bridge for achieving bridge balance, and when the boiler steam pressure changes, the balance state of this bridge changes accordingly. When adjusting the alarm value, a screwdriver can be inserted into the small hole on the panel to adjust the alarm value setting potentiometer Rp, thereby changing the setting value UL. After replacing the analog alarm plug-in board, if the displayed reading differs from the original alarm value, the alarm value setting potentiometer needs to be adjusted accordingly. This adjustment is necessary because after the plug-in board is replaced, the setting state of each channel may be inconsistent with the original board; only by readjusting the displayed reading to match the original alarm value can the alarm action point be consistent with the original setting requirements. In terms of operating sequence, one should first confirm that the plug-in board is inserted in place and the channel correspondence is correct, and then adjust channel by channel against the original alarm values; during adjustment, use the displayed reading as the basis and check while adjusting, avoiding turning too much at one time and overshooting the setting point. The upper/lower limit alarm jumper wire determines whether the channel is upper-limit alarm, lower-limit alarm, or both upper and lower limit alarm; with different jumper wire positions, the action direction corresponding to the same setting value is also different, so before adjusting the setting value, one should first check whether the jumper wire is consistent with the required alarm direction.

In the microcomputer-based engine room monitoring and alarm system, the input interface is used to input the status of switching sensors into the computer. In the switching input interface, when the switch is closed the input voltage is 24V, and when open it is 0V. As for the output interface, the switching output interface controls the display and alarm devices through an optical isolator and a driver. The programmable logic controller (PLC) includes an input interface and an output interface; the input interface accepts control information from field devices such as pushbuttons, limit switches, contactor contacts and sensors, and converts it into digital signals that the CPU can process; the output interface converts the digital signals output by the CPU into voltage or current to drive actuators such as solenoid valves and contactors. In the basic structure of the PLC, the input interface and output interface together with the CPU and memory constitute its components; the former is responsible for bringing in field control information, and the latter is responsible for sending out processing results, and together they complete the information transfer between the monitoring and alarm system and the field devices. When checking the switching input interface, one can judge whether the input state is correct according to the quantitative relationship that the switch is closed at 24V and open at 0V: if the field contact is already closed but 24V cannot be measured at the interface end, or the contact is already open but it is still 24V, then the input circuit is abnormal, and the optical isolator and its peripheral wiring should be checked. The function of the optical isolator is to electrically separate the sensor circuit from the I/O interface and CPU, so that overvoltage, interference or earthing problems occurring on the field side do not act directly on the interface board and CPU; therefore, when replacing the interface board or troubleshooting, one should not arbitrarily short-circuit or bypass the optical isolator.

Resistance and voltage are two basic quantities that need to be measured in fault diagnosis. Resistance is measured with a multimeter, and voltage is measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. The essence of these two precautions is to avoid bypass effects on the reading from other components or residual charge in the branch under test, and also to avoid instrument damage or personal injury caused by live measurement. In specific operation, one should first cut off the power supply of the circuit under test, then disconnect one end of the resistor under test from the circuit so that the measuring current flows only through the resistor itself; if a capacitor is connected in parallel in this branch, the capacitor must also be discharged first, and the meter can be connected for measurement only after confirming there is no residual charge. Voltage, as one of the instrument readings, is an object to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis; when checking such faults, one can first measure the resistance of the shunt resistor to judge whether it is open, and then analyze the cause of high no-load voltage in combination with the operation of the voltage regulator. Although the specific tasks undertaken by sensors differ in different occasions, the common point is that they convert the measured quantity into a signal form that subsequent circuits can process; analog sensors output continuously varying electrical signals, and switching sensors output switching information of contact opening or closing, corresponding respectively to the two types of requirements of parameter display and status monitoring. As far as the engine room monitoring and alarm system is concerned, which type of sensor to select depends on the monitoring purpose: where continuous display of parameter values and judgment of change trends based on them are required, analog sensors are used; where only judgment of whether the equipment exceeds limits and whether it is normal is required, switching sensors are used. The signals sent by the sensors ultimately enter the computer through the input interface; analog signals are first converted into digital quantities by the A/D converter, and switching signals are acquired as voltage states of 24V or 0V; the two paths each complete the corresponding signal conversion and isolation, constituting the basic links of information acquisition and transmission in the monitoring and alarm system.

The electrical characteristics of the switching input interface are as follows: when the switch is in the closed state the input voltage is 24V, and when the switch is open the input voltage is 0V. In order not to create a direct electrical connection between the field sensor circuit and the I/O interface and CPU, the input interface achieves electrical isolation between the two through an optical isolator, thereby protecting the interface board. Switching signals are read into the CPU via the data bus, and this reading process is controlled by the state of the three-state gate. As a component of the programmable logic controller (PLC), the input interface together with the output interface, CPU and memory constitutes the basic structure of the PLC; it accepts control information sent from field devices such as pushbuttons, limit switches, contactor contacts and sensors, and converts this information into digital signals that the CPU can process. In the switching output interface, the display and alarm devices are controlled through an optical isolator and a driver. The input interface and output interface have a clear division of labor in the PLC: the former is oriented to the acquisition and conversion of field control information, and the latter is oriented to the output and driving of processing results; both are separated from the CPU and field circuits by means of optical isolation, avoiding external interference or faults directly affecting the interface board and CPU.

The sensors used in the engine room monitoring and alarm system are divided into two major categories: analog and switching. The measuring circuit of the analog alarm control unit converts the information sent by the analog sensor (for example, the resistance of the thermistor) into a voltage signal, and sends a fault signal when the sensor is open-circuited or short-circuited. As for the checking sequence, for analog channels one should first confirm whether the sensor output signal changes continuously with the monitored parameter, then check whether the measuring circuit can convert this signal into a voltage signal, and finally verify whether the digital quantity sent by the A/D converter to the computer corresponds to the parameter change; for switching channels one should first confirm whether the contact can reliably open or close when the parameter exceeds the limit, and then check whether the electrical isolation on both sides of the optical isolator is intact.

The thermocouple is a temperature sensor with a simple structure and small thermal inertia; it detects the temperature of the measured object by outputting a thermal electromotive force, and its electromotive force increases as the temperature rises. As for specific models, the platinum-rhodium 10-platinum type (LB-3) has a measuring range of 0~+1300℃, and when the temperature does not exceed 600℃ the allowable error is ±3℃; the tungsten-rhenium 5-tungsten-rhenium 20 type (WR) has a measuring range of 10~+2800℃, and when the temperature is higher than 1000℃ the allowable error is 1t; the copper-constantan type (CK) has an allowable error of ±0.6% in the range of -40~+80℃; the nickel-chromium-constantan type (NK) has an allowable error of ±1% when the temperature is higher than 400℃. Under normal conditions the resistance between the two terminal posts of the thermocouple is zero; if the measured resistance is infinite, it indicates that the hot end is open and the thermocouple is damaged. The measuring range and allowable error of the above models are the quantitative basis for judging whether the thermocouple is qualified: when the measured temperature falls within the corresponding range, the measured deviation should not exceed the allowable error given for that model; if it exceeds the range or the deviation is too large, one should further judge whether the thermocouple itself has failed in combination with the measurement result of the resistance between the terminal posts.

The diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity, commonly denoted VD in circuits, and used in rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization and other occasions. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: when a forward voltage is applied the conduction resistance is small, and when a reverse voltage is applied the resistance is very large or infinite. Classified by function, diodes include rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85) and other types, and also include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The light-emitting diode can emit red, green, yellow and other colors of light and has unidirectional conductivity; its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit working status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display; its external dimensions include 3mm diameter, 5mm diameter and 2mm×5mm rectangular, its working current is generally 1~30mA depending on the model, and its conduction voltage is above 1.7V. For the light-emitting diode, attention should be paid to the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes: in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage, the working current should be controlled within the range of 1~30mA, and when selecting, the external dimensions such as 3mm diameter, 5mm diameter or 2mm×5mm rectangular should match the installation position. In the optical isolation circuit, when the input Q=0, the light-emitting diode inside the optical isolator emits light, causing the light-emitting transistor to conduct; when the input Q=1, the light-emitting diode does not emit light, and the light-emitting transistor is cut off. Diodes and transistors are widely used in marine electrical equipment; testing a diode requires following the corresponding diode testing procedure, and this testing procedure applies to diodes. During testing, one should focus on the measurable properties of polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance: first determine the polarity, then measure the forward voltage drop and reverse resistance, so as to confirm whether the unidirectional conductivity is normal.

The transistor is a semiconductor device containing two PN junctions internally and having current amplification capability; it is divided into NPN type and PNP type, and is commonly denoted in circuits by the letter "VT" plus a number, for example VT17 means the transistor numbered 17. Its main models include PNP type transistors such as A92 and 9015, and NPN type transistors such as A42, 9014 and 9018. The working characteristics of the NPN type and the PNP type can complement each other; for example, the complementary pair in an OTL circuit makes use of this feature.

A transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault is a common problem under the device category of transistor. When testing a transistor, the measurable properties include the tube type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor; the checking sequence is usually to first determine the tube type and base, then distinguish the collector and emitter, and finally measure the current amplification factor, so as to judge whether its amplification capability has decreased, whether its switching characteristics have deteriorated, or whether there is an open circuit between electrodes.

In the fault diagnosis process, the multimeter is used to measure voltage and current, and also to test diodes, transistors and thermocouples; the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. Voltage, as a measurable property quantity, its value can be measured by a multimeter or a voltmeter; to measure current an ammeter is needed, connected in series after breaking the circuit. Voltage and current are both electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; the measurable properties of a diode include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance; the measurable properties of a thermocouple include resistance and electromotive force, and its electromotive force increases as the temperature rises.

In the composition of marine electrical equipment, integrated circuits and printed circuit boards are two types of widely used basic devices. Marine electrical equipment uses integrated circuits and also uses printed circuit boards. Integrated circuits have the characteristics of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration continues to increase, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits have also appeared. Their common package forms include PLCC with inward-hooking pins on four sides, SOIC with gull-wing pins on two sides, DIP with dual in-line pins, and power integrated circuit packages; the common pin counts are 14 pins or 16 pins. Pin numbering starts from the notch or dot and proceeds counterclockwise. To facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often soldered on the circuit board for direct insertion of the integrated circuit. Integrated circuits can be divided by type into CMOS circuits and TTL circuits. The printed circuit board consists of two parts: the base material and the circuit; the base material is the insulating substrate, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the circuit part is made of conductive copper laid on the substrate, with the required pattern obtained by etching, usually using copper foil. For printed circuit boards, attention should be paid to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards; a printed circuit board may suffer a circuit board fault, and a circuit board fault is a problem to be faced within the scope of printed circuit boards.

Once the microcomputer monitoring and alarm system experiences a program interruption or shutdown during operation, the state of the power supply fuse needs to be checked. The fuse is a component of marine electrical equipment, made of low-melting-point protective conductive material, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection; its manufacturing material is aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, etc., and it has the characteristics of low melting point and certain mechanical strength, and is listed together with resistors and capacitors as commonly used components in electronic circuits. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Power supply faults also deserve attention: in the microcomputer monitoring system, a power supply fault of the integrated circuit chip on the circuit board can cause the system to shut down completely with no fault information output; a power supply fault can also cause motor overheating, PLC system faults and main engine remote control failure; in AC electric drive systems, it is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent and thus overheating; in PLC control systems, the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, so the ship usually adopts the strategy of overall replacement.

The main engine remote control system is used for remote operation of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge; when operating away from the engine side, this system needs to be installed between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. By type, the main engine remote control system includes pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and fieldbus-type main engine remote control system, and also includes the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system and the main engine remote control system simulation test device. There are several points to note in the maintenance of the main engine remote control system: do not arbitrarily adjust the parameters in the system or disassemble components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer; when disassembling the pneumatic pipeline, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; drain residual water every day, check the filter every month, and replace dirty filter screens; before using the keyboard to modify system working parameters or modifying system working parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record the original data or original position; when performing electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance; when plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, the power supply should be turned off; also remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.

In terms of preventive measures, the links of the main engine remote control system that can be prevented include keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean, internal inspection of the control box, inspection of input and output components, the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing, and the periodic effectiveness test of all system functions.

Various fault symptoms will appear during the operation of the main engine remote control system. The main engine remote control system may exhibit the situation where microcomputer remote control starting must be performed twice each time, with the first attempt failing and the second succeeding; that is to say, microcomputer remote control starting must be performed twice each time, the first attempt fails and the second succeeds, and this phenomenon is precisely one of the faults occurring in the main engine remote control system. The main engine remote control system may exhibit the phenomenon that after the main engine is started it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; the main engine remote control system may exhibit serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; the main engine remote control system may exhibit air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; the main engine remote control system may exhibit moving parts jammed; the main engine remote control system may exhibit fuse blowing or power supply fault; the main engine remote control system may exhibit poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; the main engine remote control system may exhibit electrical component fault; the main engine remote control system may exhibit incorrect wiring after maintenance; in addition, the main engine remote control system may also exhibit main engine cannot be started by remote control.

Maintenance personnel are responsible for fault diagnosis and repair of marine electrical equipment, and need to be familiar with equipment principles, structures and repair materials; they must be very familiar with the whole-ship electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the positions of all components, and be familiar with the structure, working principles, functions of components (assemblies) and their locations of electrical equipment. In conventional fault diagnosis, maintenance personnel need to understand the phenomenon and make a preliminary diagnosis through asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling; the conventional fault diagnosis method uses system detection, and determining the system structure and test method is the precondition for system detection. System detection adopts the measurement method most suitable for the system structure, and its purpose is to check out the fault location; during operation, measurement must be carried out at suitable test points, and the fault location is checked by comparing the input feedback with the normal value. When dealing with difficult faults of the microcomputer system that have no fault information, the module segmentation method is often used to narrow the scope.

Some systems' external test programs (such as memory and CPU detection) are often stored on floppy disks and temporarily loaded for running. As a magnetic medium, the storage requirements for floppy disks are to keep away from magnetic objects, with an ambient temperature of 10~40℃, and the usage requirement is to use a dedicated floppy disk and not to run it on other computers. In the C ship station, the floppy disk is used for operation; a dedicated floppy disk should be used to prevent virus infection, the storage ambient temperature should preferably be 10~40℃, and it must be kept away from magnetic objects.

The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of the ship's radar and monitoring system, used to present images, data and alarm information; it should be installed in the wheelhouse where there is no strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources and in a dry place, fixed with a hardwood base, and the main radar display should be oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge. The electrical control system of refrigerated containers has developed from the relay type to the microcomputer control type, featuring a wide temperature adjustment range (generally ±30℃), high constant-temperature accuracy, and functions such as electric heating, automatic unloading and automatic control of the number of condenser fans; its technical requirements include that the temperature adjustment range inside the container is generally within ±30℃, and the adjustment accuracy needs to be improved through controlling intermittent operation of the compressor, hot bypass of refrigerant, refrigerant flow and evaporator fan speed; when the temperature inside the container is lower than the set value, the electrical control system of the refrigerated container can perform electric heating, and can automatically perform unloading operation according to the size of the heat load, and automatically control the number of condenser fans according to the external environment and condenser pressure.

In the fault diagnosis of the engine room monitoring and alarm system, the conventional fault diagnosis method takes observation as the primary means. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, it is necessary to see whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, scratched or burnt. Only after observation is completed does it turn to checking the monitoring and indicating device, that is, observation is the preceding step of check the monitoring and indicating device. This sequence reflects the requirement of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site", and observation is precisely a sub-link under this step. As far as applicable objects are concerned, observation applies both to the alarm device itself and to the associated sensor circuits, interface boards and various actuators;

As far as the basis for judgment is concerned, abnormal phenomena reflect that the current working state of the equipment deviates from normal, part status reflects the intactness of the mechanical part, wire status reflects the reliability of the electrical connection, and equipment operating parameters reflect the actual value of the monitored object. As far as the basis for judgment is concerned, the signal sent out by an analog sensor is a continuously changing electrical signal, whose value changes synchronously with the monitored parameter, so it can be used both for out-of-limit alarm and for parameter display; a switch-type sensor sends out only two states, contact on and off, and can only judge whether the equipment is normal, and cannot give the specific numerical value of the parameter. As far as the order of checking and operation is concerned, it should first be confirmed whether the sensor is analog or switch-type, and then the corresponding input interface and measuring circuit should be selected accordingly; during checking, attention should be paid to whether electrical isolation has been achieved between the sensor circuit and the I/O interface and CPU through an optical isolator, so as to avoid damage to the interface board due to circuit abnormality. In the automatic fuel oil boiler, the potentiometer is used for bridge balancing: when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 driven by the motor M loses balance, thereby reflecting the pressure deviation. The control platform contains sensors, which echoes the situation in the aforementioned antenna control platform where sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions. As far as the components involved are concerned, the alarm value setting potentiometer and the upper and lower limit alarm jumpers together form the comparison link; the level of the set value UL is determined by the resistance of the potentiometer Rp, and the jumpers determine whether the alarm takes the upper limit or the lower limit. As far as the order of operation is concerned, adjustment of the alarm value should be carried out after confirming that the plug-in board works normally; insert a screwdriver into the small hole on the panel and turn slowly, watching the display reading while adjusting, until the set value UL meets the requirement; if after replacing the plug-in board the reading is inconsistent with the original alarm value, readjust in the same way, and the jumpers must not be changed directly to accommodate the reading.

The multimeter contains a measuring circuit, and the function of the measuring circuit is to convert different electrical quantities and different ranges. Since the magnetoelectric meter head can only pass microampere-level current, a conversion circuit must be used to measure different electrical quantities and ranges; the measuring circuit therefore becomes one of the three basic components of the MF-30 and MF-47 analog multimeters. The multimeter uses the resistance range to measure the resistance value of a resistor. As far as applicable objects are concerned, the measuring circuit is suitable for uniformly converting different electrical quantities and different ranges into microampere-level signals measurable by the meter head, and the resistor is one of the objects it frequently measures. As far as the basis for judgment is concerned, whether the resistance value of the resistor matches the nominal value is the basic basis for judging whether the component is good or bad; once the shunt resistor is open-circuited, the voltage corrector loses its main regulating effect, and the no-load voltage of the generator rises accordingly. As far as precautions are concerned, the power supply must be cut off before measurement, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and if there is a capacitor in the circuit it should be discharged first; measuring with power on is strictly prohibited, so as to avoid damage to the meter head or distortion of the reading.

Readjustment is a maintenance operation for parameter deviation or abnormal mechanical state of electrical components such as circuit breakers and relays, restoring them to the specified values by adjusting springs, setting values or travel. When the reaction spring force is too large, readjustment is required; when the reaction spring force is too large and causes noise of the undervoltage trip unit, it is likewise eliminated by readjustment. Failure of the motor-operated positioning switch corresponds to readjustment; too large a reclosing contact surface also corresponds to readjustment; an incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit causing automatic breaking of the circuit breaker is still solved by readjustment. In the liquid level monitoring alarm unit, after interchange the delayed alarm time needs to be readjusted to meet the requirement. It can be seen that readjustment is used both for correcting the mechanical and electrical parameters of components such as circuit breakers and relays, and for setting the time parameters after interchange of alarm units. As far as applicable objects are concerned, readjustment covers electrical components such as circuit breakers and relays, and also covers alarm devices such as the liquid level monitoring alarm unit. After interchange of the liquid level monitoring alarm unit, the delayed alarm time not meeting the requirement is likewise a case requiring readjustment. As far as the order of operation is concerned, it should first be ascertained whether it is an abnormal mechanical state or a setting value deviation, and then respectively restore it to the specified value by adjusting the spring, changing the setting value or correcting the travel; after adjustment, it is necessary to recheck whether the action has returned to normal and whether the delayed alarm time meets the requirement.

During observation, instruments need to be used to verify electrical quantity parameters; the multimeter is a commonly used tool and can be used to measure objects such as resistors, voltage and thermocouples. In the ship station antenna control platform, the control platform contains sensors, with sensors placed respectively in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, used to send out error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. When a thermocouple is normal, the resistance between its two terminal posts is zero; if infinity is measured, it indicates that the hot end is open-circuited and the thermocouple is already damaged; this resistance criterion is the simplest method for judging on site whether a thermocouple is good or bad. When testing a thermocouple-type sensor, it is necessary to disconnect the wiring of the temperature sensor in the junction box; when testing a thermal resistance-type sensor, it is likewise necessary to disconnect the wiring of the temperature sensor in the junction box, and after disconnection measure its resistance or electromotive force respectively, so as to prevent other components in the circuit from affecting the reading. Thermocouples of different graduation numbers each have their own measuring range and permissible error: the platinum-rhodium 10-platinum type (LB-3) has a measuring range of 0~+1300℃, and a permissible error of ±3℃ at ≤600℃; the nickel-chromium-constantan type (NK) has a permissible error of ±1% at >400℃. These values are the basis for judging whether a thermocouple is out of tolerance and whether it needs to be replaced; when selecting, the temperature to be measured should also fall within the measuring range of the corresponding graduation number.

The junction box plays the role of connecting cables, protecting wiring points and accommodating electrical components in the alarm device. The general alarm device contains a junction box; the general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc., and the junction box is one of its components; the wiring among the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box is all transferred through the junction box. The solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box, but directly connected into the local control box; this point needs to be distinguished when troubleshooting wiring faults, so as to avoid taking a detour by checking according to the routing of a conventional junction box. In addition, incorrect connection of the power supply line is also a type of cause of abnormality in the alarm and monitoring circuits; during troubleshooting, it should be checked whether the connection of the power supply line is consistent with the drawing requirements, with emphasis on checking whether the phase sequence, polarity and earthing terminal are connected wrongly, and power-on test should be carried out only after confirmation that there is no error.

Composition and types of the main engine remote control system: when leaving local operation, a main engine remote control system needs to be provided between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. The main engine remote control system is used for remote manipulation of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge; according to the implementation mode and the components used, it includes types such as the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and fieldbus-type main engine remote control system. At the specific device level, the main engine remote control system includes the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, and also includes the digital electronic governor system, and is equipped with a main engine remote control system simulation test device for commissioning and function verification. As far as functions are concerned, the main engine remote control system has logic program functions such as reversing, starting, repeated starting, restarting and slow turning starting.

Precautions for daily use and maintenance: for the maintenance of the main engine remote control system, first of all, it is required not to adjust the parameters in the system at will or to disassemble components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer. When disassembling the air circuit piping, prevent external debris and dust from falling in. Residual water should be drained daily, the filter should be checked monthly, and dirty filter screens should be replaced. Before using the keyboard to modify system working parameters or modifying system working parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record the original data or original position. When carrying out electrical measurement, the test plan should be designed in advance. When plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, the power supply should be switched off, and the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot should be remembered.

Preventive maintenance and inspection items: the preventive work of the main engine remote control system includes: keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean; carrying out internal inspection of the control box; carrying out inspection of input and output components; the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing; and the periodic effectiveness test of all system functions.

Common fault symptoms: various fault symptoms will appear during the operation of the main engine remote control system, including: microcomputer remote control starting must be performed twice each time, with the first attempt failing and the second succeeding; after the main engine is started it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit;

moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after maintenance; main engine cannot be started by remote control; cannot restart; cannot reverse by remote control. The above faults involve specific components contained in the main engine remote control system, such as the reversing solenoid valve and orifice 3, and checking should be carried out item by item in combination with the working states of these components.

Classification of the main engine remote control system: the role of the main engine remote control system is to remotely manipulate the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge. Once the operating position is moved away from the local position, this system must be configured between the operating position and the main engine for remote control to be realized. If classified according to the difference in the components used by the remote control device and the driving mechanism, the main engine remote control system includes types such as the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and fieldbus-type main engine remote control system; the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system and the main engine remote control system simulation test device also fall into this category.

The pneumatic main engine remote control system consists of a pneumatic remote control device plus a pneumatic driving mechanism, and is additionally equipped with a small number of electric components such as solenoid valves and speed measuring circuits. Its advantages lie in large driving power, reliable operation, simple and intuitive structure, and ease of mastering and management; its disadvantages are that pressure transmission has lag, so the control distance is thus limited, and it has high requirements on air supply quality, and pneumatic components are prone to air leakage, dirt blockage and wear. The pressure reducing valve is a constituent component inside this system.

The remote control device and driving mechanism of the electric main engine remote control system are all composed of electric components. It has a compact structure, unlimited remote control distance, good control performance, and relatively flexible realization of various functions; its shortcoming is that the driving power of the actuator is small, and it has higher requirements on the technical level of management personnel. Distinguished by component form, it has two types: the contact relay type and the contactless integrated circuit type. The contactless electric remote control system can build the electronic control part with the help of integrated circuits. The advantages of integrated circuits are small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; the package forms are commonly 14-pin or 16-pin, and by type they are divided into CMOS circuits and TTL circuits; after the increase of integration level, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits have also appeared. The pin numbers are numbered counterclockwise starting from the notch or dot; to facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is usually soldered on the circuit board for direct plugging in. There are four common package forms: PLCC with inward-hook pins on four sides, SOIC with gull-wing pins on two sides, DIP with dual in-line pins, and power integrated circuit packages. The failure rate of this type of electronic control system is constant, and periodic preventive maintenance is not required. In marine electrical equipment, the application of integrated circuits is very common.

The remote control device of the electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system is mainly electric components, while the driving mechanism adopts pneumatic components, combining the advantages of both the electric type and the pneumatic type, and is regarded as a relatively perfect main engine remote control system. The electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system consists of an electric remote control device and a hydraulic actuator; large driving power, good controllability and ease of remote control are its advantages; complex structure, the need to provide a hydraulic oil recovery system, and susceptibility to oil leakage and air seepage are its disadvantages.

For the microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system, the hardware part is mainly PLC or microcomputer and its interface circuits, and only the driving mechanism uses pneumatic or electric components, with most system functions realized by software. It is flexible in application, powerful in function, highly applicable and highly reliable; in recent years, almost all ships launched have selected it, and it is currently evolving toward distributed and networked directions.

The data and instructions inside the PLC are transmitted using a bus-type structure, and the bus is one of the PLC's constituent parts; once a CPU bus fault occurs, the input relay will act abnormally.

The fieldbus-type main engine remote control system is a product of the widespread application of computer network technology on ships. Its constituent parts adopt distributed computer node control, and the control nodes are interconnected via the fieldbus. Compared with the traditional method, the connecting cables are greatly reduced, the wiring cost is accordingly lowered, installation and maintenance are extremely convenient, and the reliability of the system is also improved by the fieldbus interconnection.

The technical requirements of the main engine remote control system include the logic program functions of commutation, starting, repeated starting, restarting, slow-turning starting, etc., all of which the main engine remote control system possesses; it can also automatically avoid operating in the critical speed range, and executes the load program when the load reaches 70%-75%. The safety protection program is also part of the system; when conditions such as low lubricating oil pressure occur, it can automatically decelerate or stop the engine and give an alarm. The microcomputer control system is additionally provided with a self-diagnosis program, so that the fault point can be displayed and the fault type can be printed.

For daily maintenance, the air source pressure must be kept normal and clean, valve parts must be overhauled regularly, and the contact condition of plug-in units must be checked. There are several items of work that the main engine remote control system can prevent: keep the starting and control air source pressure normal and clean; check the interior of the control box; check the input and output components; the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing; and regularly carry out the effectiveness test contents of all functions of the system.

During maintenance, the precautions for the main engine remote control system are as follows. Do not adjust the parameters in the system at will, and do not dismantle components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer. When dismantling the air circuit piping, prevent external debris and dust from falling in. Drain residual water every day, check the filter every month, and replace dirty filter screens in time. Before using the keyboard to modify the system operating parameters, or modifying the system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record their original data or original positions. When carrying out electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance. When plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, the power supply must be switched off. Also remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.
