The fault symptoms that may occur in the main engine remote control system include: microcomputer remote starting requires two attempts each time, the first fails and the second succeeds; after the main engine starts it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after maintenance; main engine cannot be started by remote control; failure to repeat starting; failure to remotely reverse.

In the maintenance of related equipment, the solenoid valve undertakes the control task of fuel on-off; at ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation circuit so that the oil enters the nozzle for injection. This kind of valve controlled by an electrical signal can also be used to release residual air from the air compressor, or to control a water mist fire-extinguishing zone; the automatic fuel boiler also has solenoid valves. Its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil, the purpose being to prevent high voltage from being generated when the power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The marine motor contains bearings; the function of the bearing is to support the rotor in rotation, and once a fault occurs, the motor will exhibit overheating, vibration and abnormal noise; one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems is bearing fault, and when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is often accompanied by very loud uneven noise and the characteristic of the bearing end cover overheating. Checking the bearing fault itself and checking the lubrication condition must both be carried out around the bearing.

According to the implementation method, the main engine remote control system can be divided into types such as the pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electric main engine remote control system, the electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, the microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and the fieldbus-type main engine remote control system; the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system and the main engine remote control system simulation test device all belong to this category. This system is used for remote manipulation of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge; when the operating position is away from the engine side, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. The goal of daily maintenance is to keep the starting and control air source pressure normal and clean; around this goal a number of maintenance items for preventing faults have been formed, including checking the interior of the control box, checking the input and output components, the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing, and regularly carrying out the effectiveness test contents of all functions of the system.

For the main engine remote control system, it should be noted that the maintenance item of keeping the starting and control air source pressure normal and clean requires draining residual water every day, checking the filter every month, and replacing dirty filter screens; for the main engine remote control system, it should be noted that when dismantling the air circuit piping, external debris and dust must be prevented from falling in. Under the condition that the air source is dry and clean, valve parts with a working pressure of 1MPa are overhauled once every four years, and valve parts with a working pressure of 3MPa are overhauled once every two years; during regular overhaul, aged sealing rings, sealing washers and worn moving parts must also be replaced in time. The air source pressure and cleanliness directly affect the working state of the sealing elements in the pneumatic valve parts; the sealing washer is used to prevent air leakage in the circuit, and once the sealing washer in the two-position three-way valve is damaged or lost, it will cause air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit, thereby making the actuating air pressure at the control end of the valve part too low and the valve position unable to switch. During daily maintenance, aged sealing rings and sealing washers must be replaced in time; aging of the sealing ring is one of the problems that must be dealt with in regular overhaul.

The internal inspection of the control box is applicable to electrical control devices in plug-in form. The inspection contents include: whether the plug-in units are loose and whether the contact is good, whether there is corrosion between the plug-in unit and the socket and its timely removal, whether the control box and external signal lines are fastened and in good contact, whether the shielding earthing is reliable, and regular checking of the contact condition of relay contacts and sliding-contact electrical appliances such as potentiometers. The potentiometer plays an important role in the microcomputer remote control system; the telegraph handle controls only a potentiometer, and different positions send different voltage signals to the microcomputer; in automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance, and when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by the potentiometer driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer driven by the motor M changes accordingly. A potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the other pins changes with the rotation of the shaft; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component, and it is generally considered to be manually adjustable.

The inspection objects of the input and output components include components such as transmitters, sensors and actuators, and generally each item must be checked once every three months. During inspection it is necessary to check the electrical contacts and parallel high-resistance resistors of temperature, pressure and other sensors, to verify the upper and lower limit set values of the sensing and detection components and readjust the deviation, to confirm that the error between the display device of the control station and the actual value is within the required range, and also to check whether actuator components such as actuating motors and solenoid valves are in good condition. The sensor is the information acquisition device of the ship's monitoring and control system, and is divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors; in the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals, and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control a water mist fire-extinguishing zone; the automatic fuel boiler contains a solenoid valve and a potentiometer, and the solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of the fuel, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit at ignition so that it enters the nozzle for injection.

Before sailing, the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation include: checking whether the working power supply, emergency power supply and alarm power supply of the device are normal; carrying out the transfer and interlock tests of the control stations on the bridge, in the centralized control room and at the engine side; carrying out closed-loop manipulation tests and simulation tests on each remote control station according to function; observing and judging whether components such as the telegraph transmitter and program controller work correctly and reliably; and checking the state of the auxiliary power and automatic control devices related to the main engine remote control system. Any auxiliary or automatic regulating device that does not meet the technical requirements must not be put into use.

The regular effectiveness test contents of all functions of the system cover: verification of program control functions such as commutation, starting, braking, speed regulation and stopping; testing of the safety interlock logic among the turning gear, starting device and remote control station; verifying the effectiveness of functions such as stopping, deceleration and emergency manipulation by simulating faults; testing the limiting functions of the device using simulated signals such as scavenging air pressure, torque and fuel rack; checking the alarm functions under conditions such as power supply fault, emergency manipulation, and commutation or starting failure; and testing the accuracy indicators of the speed detection system and the governor.

For the main engine remote control system, it should be noted that the parameters in the system should not be adjusted at will and components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer should not be dismantled; this precaution applies to the daily maintenance of the electrical main engine remote control system and comes after the regular overhaul requirement of keeping the air source pressure normal and clean. For the main engine remote control system, it should be noted that before using the keyboard to modify the system operating parameters or modifying the system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record their original data or original positions. For the main engine remote control system, it should be noted that when carrying out electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance. For the main engine remote control system, it should be noted that when simulating the closed state of an external relay contact (short-circuiting two electrical wiring terminals), it must be confirmed that there is no voltage between the two terminals, or that although there is voltage, there is a current-limiting resistor so that no short circuit will occur and the fault will not be expanded. For the main engine remote control system, it should be noted that when plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, the power supply must be switched off, and the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot must be remembered.

Various faults will occur during the operation of the main engine remote control system, including: microcomputer remote starting requires two attempts each time, the first fails and the second succeeds; after the main engine starts it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after maintenance; main engine cannot be started by remote control; failure to repeat starting. Among them, serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve can be caused by blockage of the orifice, aging of the rubber diaphragm, or incorrect positioning of some parts during disassembly and assembly; when dealing with it, a cleaning needle can be used to clear the blocked orifice, clean the dirt and replace the rubber diaphragm; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit can be caused by air leakage at pipe joints or damage or loss of the sealing washer in the two-position three-way valve, and a pressure gauge can be used to quantitatively measure from the air source to the end to locate the leaking part; jamming of moving parts is often caused by lack of oil; the main engine cannot be started by remote control can be caused by incorrect setting of working parameters, the manipulation mode selection switch not being at the selected control station, the working air source of the main engine remote control pneumatic system not being opened, or the starting conditions not being met; failure to repeat starting can be caused by a fault in the timing circuit or time relay (according to the time principle) or a fault in the speed detection and judgment circuit (according to the speed principle); failure to remotely reverse can be caused by a fault in the logic circuit or logic relay circuit, or a fault in the mechanical and control detection circuits and devices that cannot switch to a certain direction. Power supply fault is an electrical supply abnormality that causes motor overheating, PLC system faults and main engine remote control failure; in AC electric drive systems, power supply fault is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent and thus overheating; in the PLC control system, because the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, the ship usually adopts the strategy of overall replacement.

Fault diagnosis and repair work place clear requirements on maintenance personnel. Maintenance personnel must be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of the electrical equipment and components (assemblies), must be very familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the positions of all components, and must master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. Observation is also the preceding link to checking the monitoring and indicating device; after completing the observation, the monitoring and indicating device is then checked. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, part condition, conductor condition and equipment operating parameters; specifically, it is necessary to check whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Observation belongs to the sub-link of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, "carrying out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged". When a motor or drive system cannot establish rotational motion after being energized, the fault symptom of failure to start occurs; when constructing a fault tree, this is often selected as the top event of electrical equipment, such as motor fails to start, and the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as the power supply being normal and the control circuit being normal.

Marine electrical equipment uses integrated circuits. Integrated circuits have the advantages of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration increases, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits have appeared. Their common package forms are 14-pin or 16-pin, and the types are divided into CMOS circuits and TTL circuits; the pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise, and to facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often welded on the circuit board for direct plugging. Common package forms also include the four-side J-lead type (PLCC), the two-side gull-wing lead type (SOIC), the dual in-line lead type (DIP) and the power integrated circuit package. If there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with the power on. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open circuit in the shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action.

In daily maintenance, keeping the starting and control air source pressure normal and clean is a basic task for preventing faults; at the same time, the internal inspection of the control box and the inspection of input and output components should be done well, and the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing should be implemented one by one, and the effectiveness test contents of all functions of the system should be carried out regularly. During system operation, the phenomenon may occur that microcomputer remote starting requires two attempts each time, the first failing and the second succeeding; such abnormalities are often related to parameter settings or component conditions.

There are several precautions that must be observed in maintenance work. When dismantling the air circuit piping, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; drain residual water every day, check the filter every month, and replace dirty filter screens. When carrying out electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance.

The daily maintenance of the main engine remote control system also requires regular checking of the contact condition of relay contacts and sliding-contact electrical appliances (potentiometers). In the microcomputer remote control system, the telegraph handle controls only a potentiometer, and different positions send different voltage signals to the microcomputer; therefore, whether the potentiometer contact is reliable directly affects the accuracy of command transmission.

As for pneumatic valve parts, when the pressure regulating valve is in normal use, the output air pressure is stable at the set value, and when the working condition is unchanged, no air leaks from the vent hole. Its fault manifestation is serious air leakage from the vent hole, and the causes include blockage of the orifice, aging of the rubber diaphragm or incorrect assembly of parts; the repair method is to clear the blocked orifice with a cleaning needle, clean the dirt and replace the aged rubber diaphragm. In the engine-side manipulation system of the Sulzer RTA84c diesel engine, the pressure regulating valve is used to manually adjust the speed-regulating air pressure signal.

Serious air leakage from the vent hole of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; electrical component faults; incorrect wiring after maintenance; main engine cannot be started by remote control; cannot repeat starting. These all fall within the scope of common faults, among which air leakage and jamming of pneumatic valves, poor contact of electrical components and incorrect parameter settings are relatively typical.

When handling faults, changes to parameters must be made with particular care. This precaution applies to the electrical measurement process of the main engine remote control system; its operating scenario is short-circuiting two electrical wiring terminals to simulate the closed state of an external relay contact. Before execution it must be confirmed that there is no voltage between the two terminals; if there is voltage between the two terminals, it must be confirmed that a current-limiting resistor exists to prevent a short circuit from expanding the fault. This precaution applies to the fault analysis and handling procedure of the main engine remote control system; when performing the operation of inserting and removing printed circuit boards, the power must first be switched off, and at the same time the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot must be recorded; this step must be performed in conjunction with the power-off operation. A printed circuit board consists of a base material and circuitry; the base material is an insulating material, such as phenolic resin board and epoxy glass, and the circuitry is conductive foil, usually copper.

Resistance is measured with a multimeter, while voltage is measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter. The property that resistance can measure is the resistance value, and the property that voltage can measure is the voltage value. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power must be cut off;

The pneumatic main engine remote control system contains a pressure reducing valve, a pressure regulating valve and a sealing ring; these three are all components of its pneumatic valves. Once a fault occurs, relatively serious air leakage can be found at the vent hole. The causes of this phenomenon are usually of three types: blocked throttle orifice, aged rubber diaphragm, or some components installed in the wrong position during disassembly and assembly. The corresponding repair method for this type of fault is to clear the blocked throttle orifice with a cleaning needle, clean off the dirt, and replace the rubber diaphragm; the specific operation is to clear the blocked throttle orifice with a cleaning needle, clean off the dirt and replace the aged rubber diaphragm. For that caused by a blocked throttle orifice, simply clear the blockage with a cleaning needle and clean off the dirt; for that caused by an aged rubber diaphragm, directly replace the rubber diaphragm; some components installed in the wrong position during disassembly and assembly will likewise cause the above-mentioned air leakage fault of the valve, and this must be corrected during disassembly and assembly. The sealing ring is a sealing element in pneumatic valves, used to prevent air leakage in the air circuit; damage to or loss of the sealing ring in a two-position three-way valve will make the actuating air pressure at the control end of the valve too low and the valve position cannot be switched, so aged sealing washers and sealing rings must be replaced promptly in daily maintenance. When locating such leakage points, it is best to use a pressure gauge to make quantitative measurements from the air source toward the end; compared with judging by listening to the sound, quantitative point-by-point measurement from the air source toward the end with a pressure gauge is a better locating method, and this method is suitable for solving the problem of too-low control-end air pressure caused by damage to pipe joints or sealing rings. A fuse is a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material, characterized by a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength; it is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, alongside resistors, capacitors, etc., and is made of protective conductive materials such as aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy. Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance; poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults, and will cause random output actions; the corresponding remedy is to check the terminal wiring. In addition, a circuit breaker may have a mechanical fault in which one phase contact cannot close, generally caused by breakage of one phase connecting rod of the circuit breaker, that is, the fault cause is generally breakage of one phase connecting rod of the circuit breaker, and the remedy is to replace the broken connecting rod.

The control mode selection switch not being at the selected control station, the working air supply of the pneumatic system of the main engine remote control not being opened, etc., will cause the main engine cannot be started by remote control; for the control mode selection switch not being at the selected control station, the working air supply of the pneumatic system of the main engine remote control not being opened, etc., correspondingly check whether the control mode selection switch is at the selected control station, whether the working air supply of the pneumatic system of the main engine remote control is opened, etc.; during troubleshooting, first check whether the control mode selection switch is at the selected control station and confirm that the working air supply of the pneumatic system of the main engine remote control has been opened; if the above routine checks show no abnormality, then further verify whether the main engine starting conditions are met. The starting conditions include the turning gear disengaged signal and the main engine starting position signal, and also include the starting air pressure signal and the control air pressure signal. Incorrect working parameter settings are one of the common fault causes of the main engine remote control system; setting the ignition speed preset value, starting fuel quantity or main starting air valve opening time limit to zero will cause main engine starting failure; even if the system components have no hardware fault, incorrect parameter settings will also cause main engine starting failure, and system aging causing the original working parameters to no longer match is the cause of incorrect parameter settings. If the starting conditions are not met, each starting condition or sensing/detecting element should be checked one by one for faults, on the basis that the main engine is permitted to start only when all starting conditions are met and detection is normal; if this step confirms that the conditions and elements are normal, the logic discrimination circuit of the control box should be checked next. If repeated starting is by the time principle, a fault in the timing circuit or time relay (by the time principle) will cause inability to repeat starting; for a fault in the timing circuit or time relay (by the time principle), correspondingly check the timing circuit or time relay (by the time principle), and the timing circuit or time relay should be checked with emphasis; if repeated starting is by the speed principle, a fault in the speed detection and judgment circuit (by the speed principle) will cause inability to repeat starting; for a fault in the speed detection and judgment circuit (by the speed principle), correspondingly check the speed detection and judgment circuit (by the speed principle), and the speed detection and judgment circuit should be checked with emphasis; if by the combined speed and time principle, both the speed detection and conversion circuit and the time circuit must be checked.

Inability to reverse by remote control may be caused by a fault in its own logic circuit or logic relay circuit; a fault in the logic circuit or logic relay circuit will cause inability to reverse by remote control; it may also be caused by a fault in the machinery and control detection circuits or devices that prevent reversing to a certain direction; a fault in the machinery and control detection circuits or devices that prevent reversing to a certain direction will cause inability to reverse by remote control; a fault in the reversing solenoid valve will also cause inability to reverse by remote control. When the fault prevents correct response, emphasis should be placed on checking the components and circuits of the two parts, machinery and control detection.

The maintenance items that the main engine remote control system can prevent include keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean, including inspection inside the control box, including inspection of input and output components, and also including the items that must be checked before sailing in conjunction with main engine preparation. When disconnecting the air circuit piping, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; its pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise; the automatic fuel oil boiler contains a potentiometer. Starting conditions not being met will likewise cause the main engine cannot be started by remote control. A time relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship's power system, with common designations KT, SJ, SL. A fault in the logic circuit or logic relay circuit is one of the possible fault causes of the main engine being unable to reverse by remote control; if a relay logic circuit is used, the relays of that part and their related contacts must be checked; if an electronic integrated circuit is used, it can be checked by the waveform test method or the substitution method; if it is a microcomputer control system, the fault point can be found by the self-test program or the simulation board.

During inspection, if the safety interlock is normal and local control is normal, the possibility of actuator failure can be ruled out, and the starting link including the starting fuel quantity setting and holding links must be analyzed with emphasis. One of the fault causes is that orifice 3 is dirty and blocked; orifice 3 is located at the one-way variable orifice valve 3 between regulating valve 2 and air reservoir 4. When the main engine is started, through the action of orifice 3 the solenoid valve is made to operate in the upper position to supply the starting fuel quantity; after the starting signal disappears, the air in the air reservoir is released through this orifice, and its release time determines the holding duration of the starting fuel quantity. Dirty blocking will cause the two speed signals not to switch in time after starting, so that the main engine cannot accelerate; because the orifice becomes smaller, the switching process between the two states is too long, causing the valve spool to remain in the critical state for too long and resulting in shutdown. The maintenance procedure corresponding to dirty blocking of orifice 3 is to clean and adjust the orifice valve; the operating object is the one-way variable orifice valve (No. 3) in the main engine governor system. After performing this step, the above governor fault can be eliminated, allowing valve 1 to reset and normal speed regulation to proceed.

The reversing solenoid valve fault is one of the fault causes listed in the fault handling examples of the main engine remote control system, and will cause inability to reverse by remote control; the maintenance procedure corresponding to the reversing solenoid valve fault is to inspect the reversing solenoid valve. In the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the reversing solenoid valve fault is one of the potential causes of abnormal main engine starting. In troubleshooting burner ignition faults, if there is an ignition spark but no fuel injection, check whether solenoid valve DF operates; if solenoid valve DF does not operate, further check whether its coil is open and whether the valve core is stuck. The drive circuit of the solenoid valve has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge.

Among the common faults of the PLC control system, the possible fault causes for a certain input relay failing to pick up include an input signal source (device) fault; the direct cause of a certain input relay being normally closed is judged to be an input circuit (circuit) fault, and the handling method is to check the circuit or replace the relevant components. On the output side, the manifestations are: a certain output relay cannot pick up while the indicator lamp is off, the possible cause being that the output on-time is too short or an output circuit fault; a certain output relay cannot pick up while the indicator lamp is on, possibly caused by damage to the output relay or broken output wiring; a certain output relay does not drop out while the indicator lamp is off, possibly caused by damage to the output relay, requiring replacement of the relay, or possibly caused by excessive leakage current of the output drive transistor, requiring replacement of the output transistor; a certain output relay does not drop out while the indicator lamp is on, possibly caused by an output drive circuit fault, requiring replacement of the output port circuit, or possibly caused by duplicate port addresses in the output instructions, requiring program modification.

Technical requirements and general maintenance principles of the digital electronic governor system. The main engine remote control system is used for remote operation of the main diesel engine from the centralized control room or the bridge. When the operator leaves the local operating position, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine in order to achieve remote control. According to different implementation methods, the main engine remote control system includes the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system, and fieldbus-type main engine remote control system, among which the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system is one specific product. The main engine remote control system also includes a main engine remote control system simulation test device, used for simulated verification of system functions before mooring or navigation.

The digital electronic governor system is a component of the main engine remote control system; it directly operates the fuel lever through an electric actuator, changing the fuel lever opening and thereby regulating the main engine fuel supply.

The basic technical requirements for the digital electronic governor system include the following aspects. The regulating link should adopt a PI control law with no steady-state error and have good performance in tracking telegraph commands. The output characteristic curve of the governor system should conform as closely as possible to the propeller operating characteristics in order to achieve optimum regulating performance. The system should be able to accept various limits, such as maximum speed limit, minimum speed limit, maximum fuel limit, etc., but under emergency operation these limits can be automatically cancelled. The system should be able to immediately execute fault slowdown or shutdown commands sent from the main engine safety system.

In maintenance work, there are several precautions requiring special attention in the main engine remote control system. Do not arbitrarily adjust parameters in the system or disassemble components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer. When disconnecting pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in. Drain residual water daily, inspect the filter monthly, and replace dirty filter screens. Before using the keyboard to modify system operating parameters or modifying system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record the original data or original positions. When performing electrical measurements, a test plan should be designed in advance. When simulating the closed state of an external relay contact (short-circuiting two electrical terminal posts), confirm that there is no voltage between the two terminals, or that although there is voltage, there is a current-limiting resistor so that no short circuit will occur and expand the fault. When inserting or removing printed circuit boards, turn off the power and remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.

The preventable faults of the main engine remote control system are realized through a series of preventive maintenance measures. Keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean is a basic requirement for preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Internal inspection of the control box is likewise an important part of preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Inspection of input and output components also falls within the scope of preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Before navigation, the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation are routine work for preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Periodic effectiveness tests of all system functions ensure, from the standpoint of overall function, that preventable faults of the main engine remote control system are avoided. In addition, the main engine remote control system may exhibit the phenomenon that microcomputer remote starting requires two attempts each time, that is, the first start fails and only the second start succeeds; attention should be paid to this phenomenon in maintenance.

Composition and maintenance items of the DGS-8800e digital electronic governor system. The DGS-8800e digital electronic governor system is a product of NOR-CONTROL company and is a specific implementation of the digital electronic governor system. It consists of two major parts, the regulator and the actuator, controlled respectively by two microcomputer systems. This system can serve as the speed regulation control circuit in the main engine remote control system and can also directly receive telegraph commands. The regulator performs rate-limiting control and critical speed avoidance processing on the telegraph commands, and after comparing the current telegraph command with the current main engine speed, issues a fuel supply signal. The actuator drives the servo motor to act according to the command in order to adjust the fuel lever position.

The preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system are implemented item by item through the following maintenance items. Testing the relevant indicator lamps and promptly replacing damaged bulbs or light-emitting diodes is one aspect of preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Tightening plug-in boards and plug-in board sockets can keep the circuit board plug-ins secure and in good contact, and is a measure for preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Tightening fuses and terminal posts is likewise for keeping the circuit board plug-ins secure and in good contact, and is also a measure for preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system.

Checking whether the electrical (hydraulic) converter valve works normally, that is, checking the operating state of the electro-pneumatic (hydraulic) converter valve, is an inspection item for preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Checking whether the AC and DC operating power supply voltages are normal, with the inspection objects including the AC operating power supply voltage and the DC operating power supply voltage, is likewise an inspection item for preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Carefully checking whether each lead cable has an open-circuit fault and whether the shield end is reliably earthed also falls within the scope of preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. If the actuator is a servo motor, the motor should be serviced regularly. The relay, servo motor, and brake in the control circuit should also be checked.

In the DGS-8800e system, the actuator causes the servo motor to act according to the regulator command, pulling the fuel lever to the fuel supply position corresponding to the regulator command. When disassembling and inspecting the servo motor, special attention must be paid to its position feedback and the corresponding positional relationship between the synchro and the fuel lever opening; the corresponding relationship between the position feedback, the synchro, and the fuel lever opening should be verified. This maintenance item falls within the scope of control circuit inspection and requires checking the relay and brake at the same time. A multimeter can be used to measure voltage and can also be used to test diodes. When measuring voltage, a multimeter or voltmeter may be used.

A diode is a semiconductor device widely used in marine electrical equipment, having unidirectional conductivity, and is commonly denoted VD in circuits. A diode has a small conduction resistance under forward voltage and an extremely large or infinite resistance under reverse voltage, and is commonly used in rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, and polarity protection circuits. Diodes include many types and, by function, can be divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), light-emitting diodes, Zener diodes, etc. The diode testing procedure is applicable to the testing of devices of the diode category. The measurable performance of a diode includes polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop, and reverse resistance.

A light-emitting diode is one type of diode, has unidirectional conductivity, and can emit red, green, yellow, and other colors of light. Its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit operating status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display. The external dimensions of light-emitting diodes include 3 mm diameter, 5 mm diameter, and 2 mm×5 mm rectangular. The operating current, depending on the model, is generally 1–30 mA, and the conduction voltage is above 1.7 V. For light-emitting diodes, the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes must be observed; in actual use, a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage.

A fuse is a component of marine electrical equipment and is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, alongside resistors, capacitors, etc. A fuse is made of protective conductive material and has the characteristics of a low melting point and certain mechanical strength; the material is aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, etc. A fuse is used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. The maintenance content of the electronic governor system includes tightening fuses and terminal posts.

A servo motor is used to adjust the opening of the air damper and fuel lever, rotating according to the bridge output signal and driving the feedback potentiometer to adjust so that the bridge is rebalanced. An automatic fuel oil boiler contains a servo motor; in boiler combustion regulation, the servo motor is energized by the differential amplifier and thyristor control winding to adjust the air-fuel ratio, and when rotating it drives the sliding contact of feedback potentiometer R10 to move, so that the bridge is rebalanced and then stops. In the DGS-8800e governor system, the servo motor receives the power amplifier signal and rotates to pull the fuel lever to the specified position.

A display is used in the main engine remote control system to display the actual speed, and in the event of a fault displays error information of core components such as the CPU. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed respectively in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. Analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The main engine remote control system is used for remote operation of the main diesel engine from the centralized control room or the bridge. When the operator leaves the local operating position, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine in order to achieve remote control. According to different implementation methods, the main engine remote control system can be divided into the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system, and fieldbus-type main engine remote control system, etc.; the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system and the digital electronic governor system also fall within this category. The main engine remote control system includes a main engine remote control system simulation test device, which is used to check the functions and operating conditions of the main engine remote control system.

The basic design purpose of the main engine remote control system simulation test device is to provide simulated signals in order to check remote control system functions, diagnose faults, and adjust parameters. It utilizes the characteristic that the remote control system cannot distinguish actual speed from simulated speed, and performs functional testing while the main engine is stopped. Structurally, the device consists of two parts: the main engine simulated speed setting board and the system function simulation test board. The main engine simulated speed setting board includes a selector switch, a potentiometer, and an indicating voltmeter, used to replace the speed sensor signal; the system function simulation test board is equipped with LED display of operating status, as well as digital display and keyboard for querying and modifying parameters. In a microcomputer control system, this device shares the same microcomputer with the control system to process simulated input signals. In the main engine remote control system simulation test device, light-emitting diodes are used to display the operating status of the remote control system and the action of external solenoid valves.

A light-emitting diode is a semiconductor device capable of emitting red, green, yellow, and other colors of light, has unidirectional conductivity, and its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode; it is commonly used as a circuit operating status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display. Its external dimensions include 3 mm diameter, 5 mm diameter, and 2 mm×5 mm rectangular; the operating current, depending on the model, is generally 1–30 mA, and the conduction voltage is above 1.7 V; in actual use, a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage. Light-emitting diodes fall within the category of diodes, and diodes also include Zener diodes. A diode has unidirectional conductivity, is commonly denoted VD in circuits, and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: small conduction resistance under forward voltage, and extremely large or infinite resistance under reverse voltage. By function, it is divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), etc. The measurable performance of a diode includes polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop, and reverse resistance. Marine electrical equipment uses diodes, and the diode testing procedure is applicable to diodes. For light-emitting diodes, the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes must be observed.

A multimeter is used to measure voltage and is also used to test diodes. Voltage values can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter.

A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed respectively in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. Analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve and a potentiometer. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel oil; during ignition it cuts off the fuel oil circulation circuit and allows oil to enter the nozzle for injection. A solenoid valve is a valve controlled by electrical signals, used to cut off the fuel oil circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control water mist fire extinguishing zones. In the burner ignition procedure, the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle for injection. The solenoid valve drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The potentiometer is used for bridge balancing; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by potentiometer R1 driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R10 driven by motor M is balanced. A potentiometer is also called a potentiometer; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is this type of component, and it is generally considered manually adjustable. A potentiometer has three pins, of which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the other pins changes as the shaft rotates. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the bridge formed by potentiometer R1 driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R10 is balanced.

The conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, the condition of parts, the condition of conductors, and the operating parameters of the equipment. In the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, the maintenance procedure of visually inspecting abnormal phenomena of the equipment, the condition of parts and the operating parameters belongs to a sub-step of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carrying out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged". The content of observation includes whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt.

The main engine remote control system requires the following precautions: do not arbitrarily adjust the parameters in the system or dismantle components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer; when dismantling pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; drain residual water daily, check the filter monthly, and replace dirty filter screens; before using the keyboard to modify system operating parameters or modifying system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record their original data or original positions; when carrying out electrical measurements, a test plan should be designed in advance; when simulating the closed state of an external relay contact (short-circuiting two electrical terminal posts), confirm that there is no voltage between the two terminal posts, or that although there is voltage, there is a current-limiting resistor so that no short circuit will occur and expand the fault; when plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, turn off the power; remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.

Problems that the main engine remote control system can prevent include: keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean; internal inspection of the control box; inspection of input and output components; items to be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing; and regularly carrying out effectiveness tests of all system functions. Fault symptoms occurring in the main engine remote control system include: microcomputer remote control starting requires two attempts each time, the first fails and the second succeeds; after the main engine starts it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault. Failure to start refers to the fault symptom in which the motor or drive system cannot establish rotational motion after being energized, and is often used as the top event of fault tree analysis. When constructing a fault tree, it is often selected as the top event of electrical equipment, such as motor fails to start. The boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as normal power supply and normal control circuit.

In the maintenance management of the main engine remote control system, the conventional fault diagnosis method often starts with observation. When marine electrical equipment uses diodes, diodes include types such as light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The diode testing procedure is applicable to diodes, and their quality can be judged item by item according to the above measurable performance. The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of the ship's radar and monitoring system, used to present images, data and alarm information; it should be installed in the wheelhouse in a dry place free from strong electromagnetic radiation and away from heat sources, fixed with a hardwood base, with the main radar display oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge. The main engine remote control system includes the pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electric main engine remote control system, the electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, the microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system, and the field bus type main engine remote control system, and also includes the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system and the main engine remote control system simulation test device. When dismantling pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; drain residual water daily, check the filter monthly, and replace dirty filter screens; when carrying out electrical measurements, a test plan should be designed in advance; when plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, turn off the power; remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.

After the main engine starts it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault.

The main engine remote control system is used to carry out remote control of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge. When the operator leaves the local operating position beside the engine, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine in order to achieve remote control. According to differences in the implementation method and the components used, the main engine remote control system includes types such as the pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electric main engine remote control system, the electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, the microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and the field bus type main engine remote control system. At the specific product level, the main engine remote control system also includes the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system and the main engine remote control system simulation test device. These different implementation forms have different emphases in maintenance and testing, but all require maintenance personnel to be familiar with their composition and adjustment points.

When maintaining the main engine remote control system, there are a series of precautions requiring special attention. For the main engine remote control system, note that the parameters in the system should not be arbitrarily adjusted and components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer should not be dismantled. The parameters in the system often correspond to setting values, delays and action thresholds, and arbitrary changes will shift the original control relationships; components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer have usually been calibrated at the factory, and once dismantled it is difficult to restore the original position and the seal is easily invalidated. For the main engine remote control system, note that when dismantling pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in. The bore of pneumatic pipelines is generally small, and once debris or dust enters, it may remain on the pipe wall or at throttling points and change the original flow area, so after dismantling the pipe openings should be promptly plugged, kept facing upward or fitted with temporary plugs. For the main engine remote control system, note that residual water should be drained daily, the filter checked monthly, and dirty filter screens replaced. Residual water accumulates at the lower part of the air supply processing components, and daily draining can prevent moisture from entering valves and pipelines with the air flow; the filter is checked once a month, and dirty filter screens should be replaced in time to ensure the flow capacity and cleanliness of the air supply. For the main engine remote control system, note that before using the keyboard to modify system operating parameters or modifying system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record their original data or original positions. Parameters modified by keyboard are usually stored in digital form, while the trimming potentiometer reflects the setting value as a mechanical rotation angle; before changing either, a record should be left for comparison so that the original values can be restored if the adjustment result is unsatisfactory. For the main engine remote control system, note that when carrying out electrical measurements, a test plan should be designed in advance. Before measurement, the test point positions, ranges used, probe connections and measurement sequence should be clarified, to avoid affecting the measurement result or even affecting adjacent circuits due to improper selection of test points or slipping of probes. For the main engine remote control system, note that when simulating the closed state of an external relay contact (short-circuiting two electrical terminal posts), confirm that there is no voltage between the two terminal posts, or that although there is voltage, there is a current-limiting resistor so that no short circuit will occur and expand the fault. The short-circuiting operation is equivalent to manually giving a contact closure signal; if voltage exists between the two terminal posts and there is no current-limiting resistor in the circuit, a short circuit will be formed at the instant of short-circuiting, expanding the fault range from the original local area to the power supply or related boards. For the main engine remote control system, note that when plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, turn off the power. Plugging or unplugging while energized will subject the components on the board to the current surge and potential difference at the instant of plugging or unplugging, and can easily damage the slot and pins. For the main engine remote control system, note that the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot should be remembered. There are often multiple boards of similar appearance in the same system; once the model and slot position are confused, at best the function will be abnormal and at worst the board will be damaged, so before plugging or unplugging each board should be checked one by one and marked.

The above precautions are aimed at daily maintenance and adjustment, while in terms of preventive maintenance, the main engine remote control system can prevent the starting and control air supply pressure from departing from normal and clean conditions. Normal and clean air supply pressure is the prerequisite for pneumatic and electro-pneumatic circuits to act according to the setting values; low pressure will make actuators act slowly or incompletely, while high pressure may make valves act too violently, and moisture and impurities in the air supply will likewise change the flow state, so keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean belongs to the range of faults that the system can prevent. The main engine remote control system can prevent faults through internal inspection of the control box, which mainly covers the wiring, terminals, board fixing and traces of abnormal heating, dust accumulation and dampness inside the box. The main engine remote control system can prevent faults through inspection of input and output components, which covers command input components and execution output components, confirming whether their action and signal transmission are normal. The main engine remote control system can prevent faults through the items to be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing; these items should be implemented one by one so that the system is in a usable state before departure. The main engine remote control system can prevent faults through regularly carrying out effectiveness tests of all system functions, which is the work of verifying each function one by one on the basis of the above inspections. These tasks constitute the routine preparation that should be completed before the simulation test.

Various typical fault symptoms occur during operation of the main engine remote control system. These include: microcomputer remote control starting requires two attempts each time, the first fails and the second succeeds; after the main engine starts it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of terminal posts or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after repair; main engine cannot be started by remote control; cannot restart; cannot reverse by remote control. These symptoms involve many aspects such as the pneumatic circuit, electrical circuit, machinery and wiring, and need to be reproduced and judged one by one in the simulation test. Jamming of moving parts will prevent valves or actuators from reaching position. Electrical component fault will make the corresponding function fail;

In the pneumatic and mechanical links, the main engine remote control system includes specific components such as the reversing solenoid valve and orifice 3. Whether the reversing solenoid valve acts normally directly affects the execution of the reversing command; the flow state of orifice 3 relates to the changes of pressure and flow in the pneumatic circuit.

In electrical measurement and fault diagnosis, voltage is an instrument reading that needs to be checked. The voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter, and the multimeter is used to measure voltage during use. During measurement, the range should be selected according to the expected voltage at the measured point, and attention should be paid to the polarity of the probes and the earthing relationship. These measurement and judgment methods are equally applicable to the inspection of the electrical part of the main engine remote control system.

The marine motor includes a bearing, and the bearing is the mechanical component of the motor, used to support the rotation of the rotor. A bearing fault will cause the motor to overheat, vibrate and produce abnormal noise; it is also one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance. When an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and overheating of the bearing end cover. During inspection, first observe the temperature of the bearing end cover and the running noise, then judge in conjunction with the lubrication condition whether the lubricant needs to be replenished or replaced. If the motor-related part of the main engine remote control system is abnormal, it should also be considered together with the bearing condition.

The main engine remote control system simulation test device provides the conditions for reproducing and troubleshooting the above fault symptoms.

During the test, attention should be paid to the working state of the reversing solenoid valve and orifice 3, the sealing condition of the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve, the tightness of the pneumatic logic circuit and the flexibility of moving parts. Measuring voltage with a multimeter or voltmeter can provide a basis for judgment.

The simulation test of the main engine high-temperature alarm device needs to be designed around the operating characteristics of the thermocouple. The thermocouple is a temperature sensor with a simple structure and small thermal inertia; it reflects the temperature of the measured object by outputting a thermal electromotive force, and its electromotive force increases as the temperature rises, so the measurable performance includes two items: resistance and electromotive force. Under normal conditions, the resistance between the two terminal posts of the thermocouple is zero; once the resistance is measured as infinity, it indicates that the hot end is open and the component itself is damaged. Based on this characteristic, the simulation test of the main engine high-temperature alarm device can be carried out by the resistance method, voltage method or current method, that is, simulating the temperature signal respectively according to the resistance change, electromotive force change and current change of the thermocouple, to check whether the alarm device acts correctly.

In the simulation test and the subsequent troubleshooting, observation is the first step of the conventional fault diagnosis method and also the most frequently used link. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, the condition of parts, the condition of conductors and the operating parameters of the equipment; specifically, it is necessary to see whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Only after observation does the inspection of the monitoring and indicating device follow, further judging the fault location through instrument readings. This sequence shows that interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device.

Measuring resistance, voltage and current is the main means of obtaining equipment operating parameters during observation. A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and can also be used to test whether a thermocouple is good or bad; when measuring current, an ammeter or clamp-on ammeter can also be used, and the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor should be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure while energized.

A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship's monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching. An analog sensor converts a parameter into a continuously varying electrical signal, and is suitable for occasions where both the equipment state is monitored and the parameter value is displayed. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls, which shows that the control platform includes sensors as a constituent relationship. The simulation test of the main engine remote control system likewise cannot do without the signals sent by various sensors; during the test, it is necessary to combine observation, measurement and instrument readings to confirm the state of actuating components including the stop-oil cylinder piston, and judge whether they are jammed or damaged, so as to ensure that the simulation test results truly reflect the working condition of the system.

The maintenance and upkeep of the ship's gyrocompass first involves grasping the starting conditions of the equipment. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass consists of the master compass, repeater compasses and course recorder, etc., and usually needs to be started 4 to 5 hours before sailing; if berthed at the dock and the course has not changed, it can be started 2 to 3 hours before sailing. The starting procedure is: after connecting the ship's power and the transformer power supply, connect the follow-up switch 20 minutes later.

Inside the small door on the left side of the master gyrocompass there are a switchboard and a follow-up switch; before use, the headings of all repeater compasses must be checked to be consistent with the master gyrocompass.

For the pre-start check and preparation of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass, it is necessary to confirm that the ship power switch and the power switch on the transformer box are set to the "OFF" position, to check whether the follow-up switch on the switchboard inside the small door on the left side of the master gyrocompass is in the "OFF" position, to check that the headings of all repeater compasses are consistent with the heading of the master gyrocompass, to check that the heading of the heading recorder is consistent with the master gyrocompass and that the time mark on the recording paper is consistent with ship time, and also to check that all instruments of the master gyrocompass are clean and dry, that the mechanical transmission is flexible, and that the cable connections are firm and normal. These checks cover confirmation of the power supply, the state of the master gyrocompass, the follow-up switch, and the heading consistency of the repeater compasses, and are the concrete embodiment of the pre-start check and preparation of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass as applicable to this type of compass.

The starting process of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass is applicable to the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass and includes steps such as switching on the ship power switch, switching on the power switch of the transformer box, and switching on the follow-up switch. The first step is to switch the ship power switch and the power switch of the transformer box to the ON position; 20 minutes after the main power supply is switched on, turn the follow-up switch from position 0 to position 1. Before starting, it must be checked that the ship power and transformer box switches are in the OFF position, and before starting it must be confirmed that the follow-up switch on the switchboard on the left side of the master gyrocompass is in the OFF position. The pre-start check and preparation of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass is the preceding link of the starting process of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass, and the starting process of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass is in turn the preceding link of the daily use check of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass.

As a type of marine navigation equipment, the gyrocompass is used to provide bow heading information and to control the antenna azimuth axis (AZ axis) to compensate for heading changes; one of its functions is to provide the control signal for the AZ axis so that the antenna rotates in the reverse direction by the same angle as the bow heading changes, that is, the AZ axis uses the gyrocompass. When starting the Sperry MK37, the changeover switch must be turned to the "SLEW" position, and the heading is adjusted to deviate 30° from the true heading. After starting the Arma-Brown 10, it is necessary to wait 5 min for the gyro motor to reach rated speed, and the follow-up system automatically comes into operation. After the Anschutz 22 is switched on for about 3 h, the pointing accuracy is ≤2°, and after 5 h the static accuracy is less than
0.1×1/cosφ. The fast settling function of the Anschutz 22 is available only when the ship's position has not changed between the previous shutdown and the current startup. The supporting liquid of the Anschutz 22 should be replaced every 18 months as specified, with a filling volume of 840cm³.

The use of the recording paper in the gyrocompass heading recorder requires checking whether it is sufficient and whether the time mark is consistent with ship time. The remaining-length warning mark of the recording paper is <1m; when the remaining length of the recording paper is less than 1m, there will be an obvious mark reminding the user that it is about to run out. The recording paper belongs to the weather facsimile receiver and is used as the medium for marine weather facsimile receivers and refrigerated container temperature recorders, recording weather charts or temperature curves; when a paper jam occurs, the equipment power supply should be switched off and the recording paper reinstalled. The observation content includes abnormal phenomena, component status, wire status, and equipment operating parameters, specifically involving whether components are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded, or burnt. Observation is a sub-link of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged."

The daily use check of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass is applicable to the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass and includes checking the liquid level of the supporting liquid, the height of the gyro sphere, and the composition and function of the supporting liquid. The distance from the supporting liquid level to the top of the filling hole should be kept at 4–5cm, which can be measured with a small wooden stick. Insufficient liquid level exposes the top electrode and prevents conduction, so the liquid quantity must be checked frequently to maintain the conductive path of the follow-up sphere. Normally, the red equator line of the gyro sphere is 2mm above the reference horizontal line, with an allowable deviation of ±1mm. An abnormal gyro sphere height will cause friction with the follow-up sphere, resulting in indeterminate error. Checking the gyro sphere height requires the compass to be stable, the liquid temperature normal, and the unit level, and is observed through the small door at the rear.

The supporting liquid consists of 10L distilled water, 1L glycerin (specific gravity
1.23), and 10g benzoic acid. Glycerin is used to increase the specific gravity of the liquid, and benzoic acid is used for conduction. The distance from the liquid level to the top of the filling hole should be kept at 4–5cm. Adding 20mL of glycerin can raise the liquid level by 1mm, and adding 125mL of distilled water can lower it by 1mm. The Anschutz 22 compass specifies replacement of the supporting liquid every 18 months; during replacement, 840cm³ of new liquid is added through the supporting liquid screw hole. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass contains supporting liquid, and the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass also contains supporting liquid.

The gyro sphere is the core component of the gyrocompass, supported by the follow-up sphere, suspended by the supporting liquid, and forming a conductive path with the follow-up sphere. Insufficient liquid level exposes the top electrode and prevents conduction, so the distance to the top of the filling hole must be kept at 4–5cm. Abnormal height will cause friction with the follow-up sphere and induce indeterminate error; normally the red equator line is 2mm±1mm above. In the Anschutz 22 compass, the friction of the liquid with the follow-up sphere drives it to reduce the initial azimuth. During maintenance, it must be taken out from the lower hemisphere and its outer surface and conductive electrode parts cleaned with a clean cotton cloth and distilled water.

The follow-up sphere is used to support and control the motion of the gyro sphere, supporting the gyro sphere through the internal supporting liquid and forming the follow-up conductive path of the gyro sphere. By means of the friction of the liquid with the gyro sphere, it drives the gyro sphere to reduce the initial azimuth for fast settling. The follow-up sphere consists of upper and lower hemispheres connected by six screws, with a distilled water reservoir and a vent screw inside. A vent screw is provided at the top center, and a distilled water filling hole and a supporting liquid filling hole are provided on the side. It is equipped with four disassembly locking screws, which must be turned 90° and loosened in two stages before removal.

The function of the changeover switch is to select the measurement object and select the range; it is a device used to set the working state, select measurement points, or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts. On the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set working states, and issue operating commands. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The multimeter contains a changeover switch. The primary side carries the load current I, which is converted into a secondary current fed to an AC ammeter or other series current element. The secondary side must never be open-circuited; the external ammeter terminals must have a short-circuit connecting piece, which may be removed only after wiring has been checked.

The Sperry MK37 gyrocompass contains components such as the electronic control box, transmitter box, and compensator. Normal starting of the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass is applicable to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass; before starting, it must be confirmed that all switches on the transmitter box and the changeover switch on the electronic control box are in the "OFF" position. The equipment power supply is started by switching on the power switch located on the electronic control box. Turn the changeover switch to the "SLEW" position, and adjust the heading deviation by 30° according to the positive or negative indication of the altitude angle indicator. If the altitude angle indication is (+), use the slew switch to reduce the heading by 30° relative to the true heading; if it is (-), increase it by 30°. After completing the preset, turn the changeover switch to the "START" position. After starting, wait 10 minutes to ensure that the gyro motor speed reaches the rated value.
