The operation of this compass involves the altitude angle indicator on the electronic control box being used to determine the adjustment direction. Shutdown of the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass is applicable to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass: place the changeover switch on the electronic control box in the "OFF" position, place the power switch on the electronic control box in the "OFF" position, and place all switches on the transmitter box in the "OFF" position. Radar range error correction is applicable to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass, and radar bearing error correction is also applicable to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass.

The Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass contains components such as the power box, master compass control panel, and repeater instruments. After switching on the power box switch, all repeater instruments also enter the working state. Turning the slew rate knob clockwise increases the compass heading reading, and counterclockwise decreases it. The speed error correction knob should be set to the position corresponding to the ship's speed, and set to zero when the ship is stationary. The latitude error correction knob should be set to the latitude of the ship's voyage, with an allowable error of no more than 5°. Daily checks require confirming that the latitude knob on the compensator is at the latitude value of the ship's location. During startup, press the slew button and turn the rate knob so that the master compass azimuth dial indicates close to the true heading. Turning the slew rate knob clockwise increases the compass reading, and counterclockwise decreases it; upon reaching the true heading, the knob must be returned to center before releasing. Before starting, check that the ship power is normal; after switching on the power supply, confirm that the power indicator lamp on the master compass control panel is lit. Startup of the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass is the preceding link of shutdown of the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass; shutdown of the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass is applicable to the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass and includes steps such as switching off the power box switch, switching off the power failure alarm switch, and switching off the ship power switch.

Regarding power failure, when starting the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass, the power failure alarm switch must be switched on before subsequent operations can be carried out. A power failure causes the RUN lamp to go out; power failure corresponds to check the power supply, and no-load power supply corresponds to switch on the power supply. Before switching on the power supply, the input and output sections must be tested for short circuit or earthing faults, and power may be applied only after confirmation that there is no problem. The PLC begins its self-diagnosis process as soon as the power supply is switched on; if an internal CPU error occurs, the "CPU Error" lamp on the panel indicates an abnormality. Startup of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass is applicable to the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass; after closing the ship power switch, the entire set of equipment automatically completes the startup process. The digital display on the panel can display heading, working state, and alarm information. After switching on the power supply for 5 h, it is fully stable and points north, with static accuracy less than 0.1×1/cosφ and dynamic accuracy index less than
0.4×1/cosφ. An optional fast settling function is supported to shorten the compass settling time, using the heading value retained from the previous shutdown to calculate the initial azimuth. It is only necessary to close the ship power switch, and the entire set of compass equipment will automatically complete the whole startup process. The content of the digital display on the master compass panel must be observed to judge whether operation is normal. The compass is usually not switched off while in port; after shutdown under special circumstances, it must be restarted. For the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of the fast settling function of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass, and these precautions also require attention for the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass.

The display is used to display radar images; the Anschutz compass digital display shows heading, working state, and heating stage temperature codes. Radar equipment contains a display, and the display belongs to radar equipment. The display includes cleaning of the display air filter and cleaning of the display surface. The radar display installation precautions require attention to the display, and radar installation is applicable to the display. The display should be installed in the wheelhouse in a place free from strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources, and dry, fixed with a hardwood base. The main radar display is oriented so that the observer faces the bow, and is installed on the starboard side of the bridge.

The supporting liquid of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass performs the dual function of supporting the gyro sphere and forming the conductive path between the gyro sphere and the follow-up sphere, and its composition is prepared from distilled water, glycerin, and benzoic acid. An abnormal height of the gyro sphere will cause friction with the follow-up sphere, thereby causing indeterminate error; under normal conditions the red equator line of the gyro sphere should be 2mm above the horizontal line of the transparent glass block, with an allowable deviation of ±1mm. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass also contains the core component, the gyro sphere. When replacing the supporting liquid of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass, the gyro sphere, follow-up sphere, and supporting liquid must be used together in the operation.

The startup process of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass is characterized by automation; the operation of starting the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass is applicable to the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass itself. After switching on the power supply for about 3 h, the pointing accuracy is ≤2°; after 5 h the static accuracy is less than 0.1×1/cosφ, and the dynamic accuracy index is less than
0.4×1/cosφ. The operating unit in the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass can control the fast settling function to shorten the startup time; by pressing the Dim Up/Down and Contr. Up/Down keys, the display brightness and contrast are adjusted, and the Up/Down keys are used to change the latitude value and the Set key is pressed to confirm, on the basis of which the system calculates the speed error. This function can be used only when the ship's position has not changed between the previous shutdown and the current startup, because the driving capability of the liquid friction is limited. After startup, if it can be activated, the fast settling button flashes continuously for 2 minutes; pressing the flashing button to light it activates the function, otherwise start according to the normal procedure. If it is not activated within 3 minutes, start normally, and the settling time is about 3 hours.

As equipment providing the AZ axis control signal, the gyrocompass has multiple models and starting methods in ship navigation. The operation of switching on the power supply is likewise a key step in the maintenance and commissioning of PLC and electrical control systems, referring to the process of connecting the power supply after confirming that there is no short circuit or earthing fault, in order to carry out functional testing or self-diagnosis. No-load power supply corresponds to the operation link of switching on the power supply.

In the testing and maintenance of marine electrical equipment, both the multimeter and marine electrical equipment use diodes. A diode has unidirectional conductivity, is commonly denoted VD in circuits, and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is very large or infinite. According to function, it can be divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), etc. Diodes include types such as light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. A light-emitting diode has unidirectional conductivity and can emit red, green, yellow, and other colored light; its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit working state indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display. Its external dimensions include diameters of 3mm and 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle; the operating current is generally 1–30mA depending on the model, and in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage; the conduction voltage is
above 1.7V. For the light-emitting diode, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of the light-emitting diode. The diode testing steps are applicable to judging the performance of devices such as diodes.

Radar equipment contains a display, and the display belongs to radar equipment. The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of the ship radar and monitoring system, used to present images, data, and alarm information.

The control platform contains sensors; in the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system and is divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass, which belongs to the same series as the Anschutz 22, requires checking before startup whether the follow-up switch on the switchboard inside the small door on the left side of the master gyrocompass is set to the "OFF" position. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass likewise contains components such as the supporting liquid and the gyro sphere. As marine navigation equipment, one of the functions of the gyrocompass is to provide the control signal for the AZ axis; the AZ axis uses the bow heading information output by the gyrocompass so that the satellite communication antenna rotates in the reverse direction by the same angle as the bow heading changes, in order to compensate for heading changes.

During maintenance, the sealing ring between the upper and lower hemispheres must also be checked to ensure good sealing performance. Marine electrical equipment generally uses printed circuit boards; a printed circuit board consists of an insulating base plate and conductive copper traces, the base material is often called the base plate, the most commonly used being phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber), and the trace portion is made of conductive copper laid on the base plate and etched to obtain the required pattern. Printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components, and welding quality directly affects the working reliability of the circuit board. The circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards. When a circuit board fault occurs on a printed circuit board, the fault falls within the scope of printed circuit boards. When the "COM" screw is loose, tighten it accordingly to restore normal connection of the circuit.

Radar equipment is the detection system for ship navigation safety, composed of the antenna, transceiver, display and other parts, wherein the antenna undertakes radiation and reception of targets, the transceiver is responsible for transmitting and receiving signals, and the display is used to present radar images. The complete set of equipment also includes the waveguide, magnetron and air filter and other components; the waveguide is used to transmit radar microwave signals, the magnetron is a device inside the transceiver, and the air filter serves the heat dissipation and ventilation of each unit. As regards maintenance and correction work, radar installation, radar acceptance, radar regular maintenance, radar range error correction and radar bearing error correction all apply to radar equipment; the antenna, transceiver, display and waveguide all belong to radar equipment, and the magnetron and air filter are also included among the components of radar equipment. Among the maintenance items included in radar equipment, one is cleaning the power supply air filter, that is, cleaning the air filter of the power supply unit.

Radar equipment installation is usually completed by technical personnel designated by the shipyard, manufacturer or supplier during construction, repair or while in port; the electro-technical officer bears a certain responsibility for determining equipment positions and is responsible for acceptance after installation. Before installation, a configuration proportion diagram must be prepared, marking on the diagram the antenna position, surrounding building obstructions and the range of rotating objects. The antenna should be installed on the wheelhouse top or an independent radar mast, away from the funnel to avoid high heat and corrosive environments. Each unit cabinet must be well earthed, cable shielding should be reliably earthed and wiring should be as short as possible. After installation, initialization settings are required, including tuning, reference point setting and error calibration. During acceptance, check whether the shadow sector meets the specification requirements and record the results in the radar log. Outdoor wiring requires attention to waterproofing, and sensor connections should conform to product standards and be connected to the specified interfaces.

Radar installation covers the steps of pre-installation preparation, antenna installation, transceiver installation, display installation, wiring and enabling initialization, and its applicable objects include the antenna, transceiver, display and waveguide. The installation and initialization setting process is completed by designated technical personnel, and the electro-technical officer is responsible for supervision and acceptance. Enabling initialization includes parameter setting, error calibration and shadow sector measurement, and the relevant results must be recorded in the installation report. Radar installation is the preceding stage of radar acceptance; only after the installation work is completed and initialization has been carried out can the acceptance process begin.

Antenna installation has several specific constraints. The radar antenna height should ensure that the horizontal distance from the bow line of sight to the sea surface does not exceed 500 m or twice the ship's length, whichever is smaller. The antenna position should ensure that there is no shadow sector area within the range from dead ahead to 2 to 2.5° abaft the beam on both sides. The antenna rotation plane should be parallel to the main deck, and protective railings not lower than 0.9 m must be provided around it. When two radars are installed on board, the elevation angle between the two radar antennas should be greater than 20°, and the vertical distance should not be less than 1 m, to avoid electromagnetic interference. The lowest edge of the antenna radiation window should be more than 0.5 m above the safety railing of the installation platform. In daily maintenance, the metal gear transmission system of the antenna must be cleaned of oil sludge and re-greased once a year; the maintenance links included in the antenna also include greasing the bearing of the antenna rotation link, cleaning and greasing the antenna metal gear transmission system, and checking the oil level of the antenna worm gear reduction gearbox.

The precautions for radar antenna installation require that when installing the antenna base, the antenna rotation plane must be parallel to the main deck. If there is a forward mark, the mark line should be within ±5° on both sides of the bow line. In addition to sufficient space for antenna rotation, there should also be a platform necessary for installation and maintenance work around the antenna, and protective railings not lower than 0.9 m must be provided. These precautions directly concern the antenna itself and are links that must be grasped in radar equipment installation.

The transceiver is usually installed in a well-ventilated equipment room near the bridge, the chart room or inside the bridge, as far as possible directly below the antenna. For mast-below type radar, the transceiver is connected to the antenna through a waveguide; the effective length of the waveguide must not exceed 25 m, and there should preferably be no more than five bent waveguides. For mast-above type radar, the transceiver and antenna are connected by cables provided by the manufacturer, with a standard length of about 25 m, which must not be arbitrarily shortened or lengthened. When maintaining the transceiver, open the cover plate to clean the air filter intake pipe and outlet filter; when the intake filter has much dust, the filter element can be removed and washed. When maintaining high-voltage devices, shut down and remove the protective cover against high-voltage electric shock, clean dust with a brush and clean oil stains with alcohol. The maintenance items included in the transceiver are cleaning the transmitter air filter and electrostatic dust removal for transmitter high-voltage devices, and the magnetron is also contained inside.

In mast-below type radar, the effective length of the waveguide must not exceed 25 m, and the number of bent waveguides should preferably not exceed five. The waveguide should run in a straight line and be as short as possible, and its direction should always keep the choke flange facing the transceiver. In mast-below type radar installation, the use of flexible waveguide should be avoided as far as possible. Special water-blocking films should be added to the waveguide surfaces at the transceiver outlet and the antenna inlet.

The display should be installed in the wheelhouse in a place free from strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources and dry, and fixed with a hardwood base. The main radar display should be oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge, and does not affect lookout. The base height should take into account convenient cable entry and bending, leave sufficient maintenance space around, and accommodate two observers standing. Display maintenance includes cleaning the air filter once a quarter, electrostatic dust removal cleaning of high-voltage devices once every half year, and wiping the surface with a damp cotton cloth every day before departure and during navigation; cleaning agents are prohibited. The maintenance items included in the display are cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface.

The precautions for radar wiring require that each unit cabinet of the radar be well earthed and the cable shielding layer be reliably earthed. Wiring should be as short as possible to avoid signal attenuation and kept away from high-frequency radiation cables. Cables should cross other equipment cables perpendicularly to avoid magnetic field coupling interference. Enabling initialization includes parameter configuration such as tuning, common reference point setting and transmission sector suppression; initialization error calibration involves bow line bearing error, ranging error and shadow sector measurement.

Radar acceptance includes the steps of appearance inspection, power-on acceptance and performance testing. New radar acceptance is implemented by the competent department of the shipowner or the electro-technical officer; the acceptance process must be truthfully recorded and the acceptance checklist provided by the manufacturer must be filled in, the installation engineering report must be signed and the documents generated during installation must be archived. Appearance inspection includes the installation positions and workmanship of the antenna, transceiver and display, with particular attention to whether the radar shadow sector meets the specification requirements, and also checks cable connection tightness, protection of vibration-prone parts and anti-corrosion treatment of corroded locations. Radar acceptance applies to radar equipment, and its results must be recorded in the radar log. Radar equipment also requires attention to the precautions for radar repair acceptance, that is, the repair and acceptance links should follow the corresponding technical specifications and recording requirements to ensure that acceptance work has a basis. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, check whether parts are stuck or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, chafed or burnt. Observation is a sub-link of fault analysis carried out while maintaining the site, which is the first step of traditional fault diagnosis.

The sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively on the antenna control platform of the ship station, and are used to send error signals to control compensation motion when the ship pitches and rolls; their function is to send error signals. The equipment to which the receiving antenna belongs is the weather facsimile receiver, and its installation position should maintain a safe distance from the radar antenna to avoid electromagnetic interference; in the marine weather facsimile receiver, the receiving antenna is used to receive radio signals, its performance is equivalent to that of an MF/HF single-sideband receiver, and it together with the recording device constitutes the complete machine.

Radar equipment is composed of the antenna, transceiver, display and power supply and other parts, wherein the antenna undertakes the task of radiating and receiving detection targets, the transceiver is responsible for transmitting and receiving radar signals, the display is used to present radar images, and the magnetron is the core component inside the transmitter. Carrying out radar installation, radar acceptance and radar regular maintenance on radar equipment are all basic work contents in the whole life cycle of the equipment; radar range error correction and radar bearing error correction are likewise carried out for radar equipment. During installation and use of radar equipment, attention must be paid to the precautions for radar antenna installation, the precautions for radar display installation, the precautions for radar wiring and the precautions for radar repair acceptance, wherein the precautions for radar antenna installation put forward requirements for the antenna, the precautions for radar display installation put forward requirements for the display, the precautions for radar wiring put forward requirements for the radar equipment itself, and the precautions for radar repair acceptance put forward requirements for the magnetron. Wiring requires that the cabinet be well earthed, the cable shielding be reliably earthed, and the wiring be as short as possible to avoid signal attenuation. Radar installation takes radar acceptance as its preceding link, and its applicable scope covers the antenna, transceiver, display and waveguide. The antenna base contains a reduction gearbox structure, and the reduction gearbox therein must be painted once every half year to prevent corrosion. During radar acceptance, the installation positions of the antenna and others, the shadow sector, cable binding and anti-corrosion and fire-prevention measures should also be checked.

Radar regular maintenance belongs to the regular category in the classification of radar maintenance and is parallel to unscheduled maintenance; a corresponding plan must be formulated, recording personnel, time, content and material consumption, etc., and it is one of the contents of the shift handover work of the electro-technical officer or the second officer; the shipowner should provide the spare parts and spare components required by the plan, and the ship management company is responsible for supervising and reviewing the completion status and putting forward suggestions for improvement. For greasing the bearing of the antenna rotation link, grease the bearing grease nipple of the antenna rotation link with a grease gun once every half year; the execution frequency is greasing once a year; before operation, shut down and place the antenna safety switch in the "OFF" position, and clean the dirt at the grease nipple hole before greasing. The execution cycle of cleaning and greasing the antenna metal gear transmission system is once a year, and the main work content is cleaning oil sludge and re-greasing; before operation, likewise shut down and place the antenna safety switch in the "OFF" position. The frequency of checking the oil level of the antenna worm gear reduction gearbox is once a year, and oil must be replenished when necessary; before operation, shut down and place the antenna safety switch in the "OFF" position; check the liquid level through the oil level observation window, and when it is below the lower limit scale, replenish special gearbox oil from the oil filling hole, and the replenished amount should reach an appropriate position between the lower and upper limit scales; if the gearbox oil has deteriorated, the oil change procedure must be carried out rather than merely replenishing, and during oil change both the oil filling hole and the oil drain hole must be opened at the same time, and the waste oil must be collected in a container.

The transmitter air filter is cleaned once a quarter; before operation, shut down and open the transceiver cover plate; the air filter intake pipe and outlet filter must be cleaned; the intake filter usually has much dust and is the key cleaning object; filters with filter elements can be removed, washed clean with clean water and reinstalled. The cleaning cycle of electrostatic dust removal for transmitter high-voltage devices is once every half year; before operation, shut down and open the transceiver cover plate; remove the transmitter and the protective cover against high-voltage electric shock; use a brush to gently clean dust on the high-voltage devices and alcohol to gently clean oil stains; after cleaning, install the protective cover and reinstall the transmitter.

The display part includes cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface. The display air filter is cleaned once a quarter, and the cleaning method is similar to that for the transmitter air filter. The frequency of display surface cleaning is once a day before departure and during navigation; no cleaning agent may be used during cleaning, and a damp cotton cloth should be used for wiping and cleaning. Radar equipment also includes cleaning the power supply air filter, whose cleaning frequency is once a quarter, and the cleaning process is similar to that for the transmitter and display air filters. The air filter is used to filter the air entering the equipment and prevent dust from entering; the air filters in the transmitter, display and power supply systems all need to be cleaned every quarter.

The precautions for radar repair acceptance require that each acceptance confirm that the radar responds correctly to the operation of each button, with clear echoes and stable images; after replacing the magnetron, the original working time should be cleared and effective preheating carried out according to technical requirements; verify the magnetron current and the working condition of the magnetron under various pulse widths; after repairing the bearing sweep system or replacing the magnetron, verify the bearing accuracy; after repairing the range sweep system or changing the signal cable length, verify the ranging accuracy; when system initialization or circuit adjustment is involved, carefully verify the sensor information and radar image quality. As the core component of the radar transmitter, the magnetron has a service life limit; the service life of magnetrons below 10 kW is about 20000 hours, and that of magnetrons above 25 kW is about 4000 hours; after replacement, the original working time must be cleared and preheating carried out according to technical requirements; after replacement, the radar bearing accuracy must be verified, the current and working condition under various pulse widths must be verified, and spare magnetrons should be used alternately on a regular basis. After the radar has worked for 0.5 h, the magnetron current must be detected and compared with the rated value. A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and a clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. The measurable performance of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter or voltmeter; the measurable performance of current is the current value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter; the measurable performance of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter. When measuring a resistor in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistor, and never measure with power on. Poor contact is one of the causes of equipment faults; increased contact resistance at electrical connections due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter, and loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance; poor contact can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit.

A marine motor contains a bearing; both checking the bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition are carried out for the bearing. The bearing is used to support the rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause overheating, vibration and abnormal noise of the motor; bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems and belongs to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and overheating of the bearing end cover.

Radar equipment is composed of two major parts, the antenna and the display; the antenna undertakes the target detection task, and the display is responsible for presenting radar images. As regards the installation link, the requirements of radar installation apply to both the antenna and the display. The precautions for radar antenna installation require attention to the antenna, that is, the antenna installation position, rotation plane, protective railings, spacing between two antennas and radiation window height are all points that should be checked item by item during antenna installation; the precautions for radar display installation require attention to the display, that is, the display placement environment, base fixing method, orientation and installation position are all points that should be checked item by item during display installation. The reason why checking at the installation stage is important is that once the antenna and display are fixed, subsequent error correction and daily maintenance can only be carried out under the established installation conditions, and installation deviations are often difficult to compensate for by adjusting menus or replacing parts.

The antenna is a key component of radar equipment, and its installation position must satisfy multiple conditions.

For the bearing lubrication of the antenna rotation link and the oil quantity check of the antenna worm gear reduction gearbox, check the oil quantity and oil quality at the corresponding intervals; when insufficiency or deterioration is found, replenish or replace in time. The oil quantity can be checked by means of the oil sight glass or dipstick, and the oil quality is observed by its color, viscosity and whether water or metal chips are mixed in. The above three operations respectively correspond to bearing lubrication of the antenna rotation link, cleaning and lubrication of the antenna metal gear transmission system, and oil quantity check of the antenna worm gear reduction gearbox, constituting the routine maintenance content of the mechanical part of the antenna.

The display is used to display radar images; its installation position should be selected in the wheelhouse where there is no strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources and dry, and it should be equipped with a hardwood base for fixing, so as to reduce the influence of vibration and moisture on the display components. The air filter is cleaned once every quarter; during cleaning, take out the filter element, remove the accumulated dust and then reinstall it. High-voltage components are cleaned once every half year by electrostatic dust absorption; before cleaning the high-voltage components, power should be cut off first and they should be fully discharged, to avoid residual charge damaging the components or endangering the operator. The display surface is wiped with a damp cotton cloth every day before sailing and during navigation; cleaning agents are prohibited to avoid damaging the screen coating, and during wiping the cotton cloth should be wrung until it does not drip.

Radar range error correction applies to radar equipment, and its correction objects include timing error, common reference point error and variable range marker error. Pixel error and pulse width error are not within the scope that the electro-technical officer needs to maintain and correct; these two types of deviation should be handled separately. Timing error correction needs to be carried out when the weather and sea conditions are calm and the berthing or anchorage environment is suitable; usually the north-up relative motion display mode is selected, with a range not greater than 0.25 nautical miles, so as to distinguish the echo position of a fixed target at close range. For traditional PPI radar, correcting the timing error requires adjusting the delay line of the display system; modern radar can complete it by operating the display menu, and during operation each item is set according to the menu prompts until the echo leading edge of the fixed target aligns with the range ring scale. Radar range error correction also applies to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass.

Radar bearing error correction also applies to radar equipment, and its correction scope only covers the heading line error, compass indication error and common reference point error that the electro-technical officer needs to pay attention to. Beam width error, pixel error, antenna main lobe deviation angle and beam asymmetry error are not the correction content of this step. The common reference point is the CCRP, and its deviation compensation setting should be completed during installation and must be carried out after calibrating the radar timing error; reversing the order will make the compensation amount lose its reference. An inaccurate CCRP deviation compensation amount will cause a range error relative to the CCRP when measuring the target range on the radar display, so the compensation amount must be set according to the measured value. The CCRP position adjustment steps are similar to the radar timing error adjustment, and need to be set according to the steps specified in the technical manual, with each item input and rechecked. In terms of operation order, radar range error correction comes first, that is, complete the range error correction first, and then carry out the radar bearing error correction; the two must not be reversed, otherwise the result of the bearing correction will lose meaning because the range reference is not determined.

As for the installation position, the height of the radar antenna should ensure that the horizontal distance from the bow line of sight to the sea surface does not exceed the smaller of 500 m or twice the ship length; the antenna position should also ensure that no shadow sector appears within the range from dead ahead to 2 to 2.5° abaft the port and starboard beams. Radar installation also applies to the antenna, and the antenna is a component of the radar equipment.

As for the ship station antenna, the Inmarsat-B/M/Mini-M/F ship stations use a parabolic directional antenna with a diameter of about 0.8 m, while the Inmarsat-C/E ship stations use an omnidirectional helical antenna, which does not require a satellite tracking system but has higher requirements for the satellite's transmission energy. The ship station directional antenna control system usually includes two motion axes, azimuth (AZ) and elevation (EL), to compensate for the pointing deviation caused by ship rolling.

A directional antenna is a ship station satellite antenna that radiates electromagnetic waves in a certain direction and needs to cooperate with the control system to always point at the satellite. Inmarsat-B/M/Mini-M/F ship stations all use directional antennas, mostly parabolic antennas with a diameter of about 0.8 m, using geometric characteristics to form strong directional radiation; in recent years, phased array antennas have begun to be used, which are small in size and fast in scanning, but high in cost and complex in control. During navigation, the directional antenna must always point at the satellite, and a four-axis control system is needed to compensate for ship rolling and heading change errors. During maintenance, it is necessary to regularly check whether the antenna base is desoldered and loose due to ship vibration. When the directional antenna is working, personnel are prohibited from staying within 5 m of the antenna to prevent microwave radiation injury, unless the radome is 2 m above the deck.

The directional antenna belongs to the parabolic antenna and also belongs to the phased array antenna; the maintenance and upkeep of the Inmarsat ship station antenna applies to the directional antenna, and the directional antenna also requires attention to the antenna safety distance precautions.

The omnidirectional antenna, also called the non-directional antenna, radiates electromagnetic waves uniformly in all directions, is used in Inmarsat-C/E ship stations, does not require a satellite tracking system, and has relatively high requirements for the satellite's transmission energy. The omnidirectional antenna shares transmission and reception; due to reversibility, its transmission and reception performance are the same; during maintenance, it is necessary to check whether the fixing is firm and the cable connection is good. The omnidirectional antenna belongs to the helical antenna, and the maintenance and upkeep of the Inmarsat ship station antenna also applies to the omnidirectional antenna.

The parabolic antenna belongs to the directional antenna and is mainly used in Inmarsat-B, M, Mini-M and F ship stations, with a typical diameter of about 0.8 meters. Its working principle is that the weak directional radiation generated by the illuminator is reflected by the parabolic surface to form strong directional radiation, radiating electromagnetic waves in a specific direction. The parabolic antenna usually uses a mechanical tracking method to drive the antenna movement to align with the satellite; in ship station applications, the step tracking method (hill-climbing method) is mostly used for control. The parabolic antenna uses mechanical tracking.

The phased array antenna belongs to the directional antenna and uses an electronic tracking method, controlling the beam direction by changing the phase shift value of the phase shifter to track the satellite. It has the advantages of flexible control, fast scanning speed, small antenna volume and the ability to conform to the carrier platform, while having the disadvantages of high antenna cost and complex control. The phased array antenna is one of the types of directional antennas used in Inmarsat ship stations, and the phased array antenna uses electronic tracking.

The helical antenna belongs to the omnidirectional antenna and is mainly used in Inmarsat-C and Inmarsat-E ship stations, radiating electromagnetic waves uniformly in all directions. When using a helical antenna, it is not necessary to equip a satellite tracking system, but the requirements for the satellite's transmission energy are relatively high. Among the omnidirectional antennas of Inmarsat-C/E ship stations, helical antennas are the majority.

The receiving antenna belongs to the weather facsimile receiver and is a component of the marine weather facsimile receiver, forming the complete machine together with the recording device, and its performance is equivalent to that of an MF/HF single sideband receiver. The receiving antenna belongs to the weather facsimile receiver.

The function of the antenna control system is to compensate for the pointing error of the ship antenna caused by various factors; it obtains error signals through sensors monitoring ship motion and controls the antenna pointing through a feedback system to compensate for the error. The antenna control system is usually established as a four-axis control system, including the X/Y axes that maintain level and the AZ/EL axes that compensate for heading position; the control platform formed by the X axis and Y axis maintains level in any weather, so that the AZ/EL axes specifically compensate for heading changes. Since the four axes are controlled independently and do not need mutual transformation, their control circuit structure is relatively simple. The antenna needs two motion degrees of freedom, azimuth and elevation, to track the satellite. The antenna control system includes a four-axis control system, and the antenna control system also requires attention to the ship station power-on precautions.

The four-axis control system consists of the AZ axis, EL axis, X axis and Y axis, and the four axes are controlled separately, with a relatively simple control circuit. Its control platform is formed by the X axis and Y axis, responsible for keeping the platform in a horizontal position under any weather conditions; the AZ axis and EL axis installed on the horizontal platform are specifically used to compensate for changes in the ship's heading and position. The four axes are controlled independently, and no coordinate transformation is required between them, so the control circuit structure is relatively simple. This system is intended to compensate for the problem of the antenna deviating from the satellite caused by ship rolling and pointing errors.

The four-axis control system includes the AZ axis, EL axis and control platform.

The AZ axis, namely the azimuth axis, is one of the two motion degrees of freedom of the ship station antenna control system, corresponding to the azimuth motion in the horizontal plane. Its control signal is provided by the ship's gyrocompass to obtain heading error information; when the ship's heading changes, the AZ axis is driven to rotate in the opposite direction by the same angle to compensate for the pointing deviation. The AZ axis is installed on the horizontal control platform formed by the X axis and Y axis, specifically used to compensate for changes in the ship's heading and position, and together with the EL axis forms part of the four-axis control system, controlled independently without transformation, simplifying the circuit. The AZ axis uses the gyrocompass.

The EL axis, namely the elevation axis, is responsible for elevation motion in the vertical plane and, together with the AZ axis, forms the two motion degrees of freedom of the antenna relative to the hull. The EL axis is installed on the horizontal control platform formed by the X axis and Y axis, used to compensate for the antenna pointing error caused by changes in the ship's heading and position, and maintains continuous tracking of the satellite by automatically tracking the strongest received signal state. The control principle of the EL axis is the same as that of the AZ axis, both based on a feedback system for error compensation.

The control platform is formed by the X axis and Y axis, maintains the platform in a horizontal position under any weather conditions, and serves as the installation base for the AZ axis (azimuth) and EL axis (elevation), specifically compensating for changes in the ship's heading and position. Sensors are placed in the two axis directions respectively to detect the ship's pitching and rolling and send out error signals, which after processing control the X axis or Y axis to perform compensating motion, so that the platform is kept in a horizontal position as much as possible. In the four-axis control system based on this platform, the four axes are controlled separately, and no transformation is required between them. The control platform includes sensors.

In the ship station antenna control platform, the sensors are placed in the X axis and Y axis directions respectively, used to send out error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. In the engine room monitoring and alarm system, analog sensors convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed; switch sensors convert parameter out-of-limit conditions into switch quantity information of contact opening or closing, only used to monitor whether the equipment is normal.

The gyrocompass provides the AZ axis control signal for the satellite communication antenna, so that the antenna rotates in the opposite direction by the same angle as the ship's heading changes. Before starting the Anschutz 4 type, it is necessary to check whether the follow-up switch of the switchboard inside the small door on the left side of the master compass is set to the "cut off" position; when starting the Sperry MK37 type, it is necessary to turn the changeover switch to the "rotate" position and adjust the heading to deviate 30° from the true heading.

The content of the ship station power-on precautions is that after the ship station is powered on, the initial positioning of the antenna pointing requires satellite information and also ship position information.

Mechanical tracking is one of the two basic categories of antenna automatic tracking, and the other is electronic tracking. To realize mechanical tracking, a servo drive system must be equipped; the parabolic antenna generally adopts the mechanical tracking method. In ship station applications, the step tracking method is mostly used to meet the needs of simple circuits and light equipment; its control principle is based on the principle of maximum received level, deciding the antenna movement direction by comparing the levels before and after movement. Each step of step tracking has a fixed angular displacement, generally 0.5°. Mechanical tracking includes the step tracking method.

Electronic tracking also belongs to one of the two overall divisions of antenna automatic tracking, usually controlling the antenna beam direction by changing the phase shift value of the phase shifter; the phased array antenna adopts the electronic tracking method. Unlike mechanical tracking, which requires a servo drive system, electronic tracking relies on electronic control rather than mechanical motion.

The step tracking method, also called the hill-climbing method, belongs to the mechanical tracking method and is suitable for ship station antennas that do not require high precision and need simple circuits. Its control principle is to enable the antenna to obtain the maximum received level; when deviating from the satellite, the received level decreases as the angle increases; if the level rises after movement, continue moving in the same direction; if it decreases, move in the opposite direction, finally jumping back and forth near the peak value. Because changes in ship position cause changes in azimuth and elevation, the tracking process alternates between azimuth stepping and elevation stepping.

The C ship station belongs to the Inmarsat-C system and supports link testing (PV test) through menus. Some models are operated with floppy disks, requiring the use of dedicated floppy disks and prevention of virus infection; some models have a remote alarm function, and the button needs to be tested regularly to ensure reliability. Maintenance requires ensuring registration in an ocean region with a relatively strong signal throughout the voyage; after the GPS is shut down and restarted, it must be checked and ensured that the ship station has an accurate ship position output; after long periods of non-use, a link test should be carried out, and this test is also part of the PSC inspection. The C ship station requires attention to the link test precautions and also to the new ship station commissioning precautions.

The routine inspection and maintenance of the C ship station applies to the C ship station, and its content includes: ensuring that the ship station is registered in an ocean region with a relatively strong signal, checking or updating the ship position at any time, correct use and protection of the floppy disk, regular testing of the remote control button, regular internal testing, frequent checking of the ship position update function, and link testing after long periods of non-use. Specifically, during navigation it is necessary to ensure that the C ship station completes registration in an ocean region with a relatively strong signal; the ship position should be checked or updated at any time to ensure the accuracy of the ship position information; for C ship stations operated with floppy disks, the floppy disks should be stored away from magnetic objects, and the ambient temperature should preferably be 10–40°C; to prevent virus infection, the C ship station floppy disks should be dedicated, and it is prohibited to run them on other computers or use floppy disks from other computers; for C ship stations with a remote alarm function, the remote control button should be tested regularly to ensure reliable function; using the menu provided by the C ship station, regular internal testing should be carried out.

The floppy disk belongs to the C ship station and also belongs to the NBDP terminal. In the C ship station, the floppy disk is used for operation, and a dedicated floppy disk should be used to prevent virus infection; the storage ambient temperature is preferably 10–40°C, and it must be kept away from magnetic objects; it is prohibited to run the floppy disk on other computers, to prevent failures caused by virus infection. In the NBDP terminal, the floppy disk is often used as a dedicated drive medium; damage will cause the equipment to fail to start, and it should be stored away from radiation sources and heat sources.

The routine inspection and maintenance of the B/F ship station covers six aspects. During navigation, it is necessary to ensure that the ship station is synchronized to a satellite in an ocean region with a relatively strong signal, regularly check the distress confirmation ground station settings, ensure that the parameters have been set and are known clearly, use the menu to regularly carry out internal testing of the B/F ship station regardless of whether it is used or not, frequently check the ship position update function, ensure there is a ship position output after GPS restart, regularly clean the attached facsimile machine and printer to ensure smooth communication, and the telephone distress test requires RCC cooperation, cannot be carried out frequently and must be strictly carried out as required. The attached equipment of the B/F ship station includes a facsimile machine and a printer; during navigation it is necessary to ensure synchronization to a satellite in an ocean region with a relatively strong signal, regularly check the setting status of the distress confirmation ground station, use the built-in menu to regularly carry out internal testing, regardless of whether it is used, the attached facsimile machine, printer, etc. should be regularly cleaned to ensure smooth communication, after GPS restart the ship position update function and output status need to be checked, and the telephone distress test requires RCC cooperation and cannot be carried out frequently.

The telephone distress test usually requires the cooperation of RCC personnel, so it cannot be carried out frequently. The Beijing ground station stipulates: to test equipment sending distress and urgency information, it must be reported to the China Maritime Search and Rescue Center in advance. Attention should be paid to understanding the specific requirements of the relevant ground station or RCC for distress testing, and it should be carried out strictly as required. The operation manual should be referred to for regularly carrying out the telephone distress test of the B/F ship station. The B/F ship station requires attention to the telephone distress test precautions, and its operating specifications require RCC cooperation and prior reporting to the China Maritime Search and Rescue Center.

Within 24 h after the new ship station passes the commissioning test, only the coast station used for the commissioning test can be selected for connection communication; during the 24 h restriction period, the ship should sail in the ocean region served by the commissioning test coast station; after 24 h, communication can be carried out via coast stations of other Inmarsat systems; distress calls are not subject to the restriction of only specific coast stations within 24 h after the commissioning test. Both the C ship station and the B/F ship station require attention to the new ship station commissioning precautions.

Regarding link testing, after the 2min time limit is exceeded, the ship station operator does not need to manually send a distress alert test message again. If it is still manually sent after the timeout, two consecutive distress alert test messages will be sent, and the Inmarsat system will treat the retransmitted distress alert test message as a genuine distress telegram; misoperation will cause the message to be sent to the Rescue Coordination Center (RCC) and initiate distress rescue procedures, and this operational error will cause a serious false alert accident. Some ship stations require the operator to send a distress alert test message according to the screen prompt during link testing. The C ship station needs to pay attention to the link test precautions, that is, the operating time limit and risk precautions for preventing retransmission of distress alert test messages in Inmarsat ship station link testing.

The antenna is used for radar target detection; radar equipment includes the antenna, and the antenna belongs to radar equipment. Radar installation applies to the antenna, and radar antenna installation precautions require attention to the antenna. An omnidirectional antenna belongs to the helical antenna; the omnidirectional antenna is also called a non-directional antenna and radiates electromagnetic waves uniformly in all directions, mostly being helical antennas.

The satellite radome is used to protect the antenna. Compared with ground system equipment, a ship station antenna equipped with a radome does not require excessive maintenance; the satellite radome should be kept clean, and spraying paint on the radome is strictly prohibited. When entering the radome for maintenance, the ship station power supply and the power switch inside the radome should be cut off. When the radome is more than 2m above the deck, personnel approaching it are not subject to the 5m distance limit; when the RF transmitter is not turned off, the time personnel approach the antenna shall not exceed 1h per day. The satellite radome requires attention to radome precautions; spraying paint on the satellite radome of an Inmarsat ship station is strictly prohibited, and the satellite radome of an Inmarsat ship station should be kept clean.

Maintenance and upkeep of the Inmarsat ship station antenna applies to directional antennas and omnidirectional antennas, and its contents include keeping the satellite radome clean, regularly checking the antenna base, cutting off the power supply when entering the radome for maintenance, and regularly performing functional tests. The satellite radome should be kept clean, and spraying paint on the radome is strictly prohibited. For directional antennas, the base needs to be regularly checked for desoldering and loosening due to ship vibration. For omnidirectional antennas, the fastening firmness and the connection between the cable and the antenna need to be checked. When entering the radome for maintenance, the ship station power supply and internal switch must be cut off. In the working state, personnel are prohibited from staying within 5m of the antenna to prevent microwave radiation. If the radome is more than 2m above the deck, the 5m safety distance limit may not apply.

Daily maintenance of the MF/HF transceiver The MF/HF transceiver is important shipborne equipment in the ground communication system, and whether its communication performance is normal is directly related to whether the ship can smoothly pass the PSC inspection. Ventilation and heat dissipation holes are provided on the casing of this equipment; while meeting heat dissipation needs, this structure also becomes a passage for dust to enter the interior of the equipment. Once dust accumulates on the circuit board, it is very easy to cause faults such as discharge and short circuit under humid conditions. Therefore, in daily maintenance, tools such as a hand bellows (leather bellows) need to be used regularly for internal cleaning and dust removal, to remove dust accumulated on the circuit board and prevent discharge or short circuit faults in a humid environment. This is one of the basic maintenance measures to ensure normal communication performance of the equipment and smooth passage of PSC inspection. The daily maintenance of the MF/HF transceiver implemented for the MF/HF transceiver includes timely internal cleaning and dust removal of the equipment, attention to moisture protection, attention to lightning protection, familiarity with the external power supply situation, prohibition of operating the equipment with faults, reminding the operator not to press keys too hard, timely detection of equipment performance, and proper cleaning of the equipment panel and microphone. The hand bellows is a cleaning tool used in MF/HF transceiver maintenance; its other name is leather bellows, and its purpose is cleaning and dust removal, used for internal cleaning and dust removal of communication equipment such as the MF/HF transceiver.

In terms of electrical connections, loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance. Poor contact is one of the causes of equipment faults, referring to a fault state in which contact resistance increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter at an electrical connection; it can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure, and interphase short circuit, and lead to random output actions. The corresponding measure is to check the terminal wiring.

Daily maintenance of the DSC terminal The DSC terminal is the digital selective calling terminal, an independent terminal with automatic ship position update function and internal self-test function. The ship position parameter in distress alert information is automatically extracted from the ship position memory; in addition to being used for alerts, the ship position parameter is also used for receiving area calls. If the ship position cannot be automatically updated, manual updating should be performed frequently. Internal self-test includes watchkeeping receiver, DSC Modem, alarm and display detection. Certified officers should perform a DSC self-test once a day during navigation. An independent DSC terminal needs frequent checking of its connections with other equipment to prevent looseness and detachment.

The contents of daily maintenance of the DSC terminal include frequently checking the connection with other equipment, frequently observing the automatic ship position update function, performing performance detection through the internal self-test function, and conducting test calls as required. The equipment panel and microphone should be kept clean, ensuring that function key markings are clear and the microphone is not covered with dust. For an independent DSC terminal, the connection with other equipment should be frequently checked to prevent loose or false connections caused by ship swaying and vibration. The ship position parameter is not only used for distress alerts but also for receiving area calls; its memory content is usually located in the initial settings. In addition, the normal DSC communication function can be verified by mutual calling between two devices on the ship.

The DSC terminal requires attention to test call precautions. Transmission testing is required once a week and is an important part of PSC inspection. In the message, the priority level should be selected as "Safety", and the communication instruction should be selected as "Test". Because the intermediate frequency band has only one distress and safety frequency, 2187.5kHz, it should be avoided as much as possible. The message should be sent on the DSC distress and safety frequency, but it is necessary to ensure no interference with ongoing communication. During operation, the shore station MMSI needs to be entered and an appropriate transmission frequency selected to start transmission. The shore station's reply must be received to confirm that the terminal reception, transmission and connection with the SSB are normal. In SSB communication, test calls are needed to confirm whether the terminal equipment and the SSB transceiver are normal in reception, transmission and connection.

Daily maintenance of the NBDP terminal The NBDP terminal is the narrow-band direct-printing telegraph terminal, with ARQ as the working mode and a dedicated floppy disk drive as the drive mode. As terminal equipment of the combined radio station, reliable communication performance must be ensured. The working state can be judged by conducting a telex test with a shore station through the "TEST+" command. Some equipment uses a dedicated floppy disk drive, and damage to the floppy disk will cause failure to start. Daily maintenance includes checking connections, timely self-testing and protecting the floppy disk. The floppy disk should be stored away from radiation sources and heat sources, and is prohibited from being used in other computers to prevent viruses.

The contents of daily maintenance of the NBDP terminal include frequently checking the connection with other equipment, timely self-testing, conducting telex tests through the "TEST+" command, and properly protecting the floppy disk.

Perform self-testing in a timely manner to confirm the equipment status. Through the ARQ mode in cooperation with the shore station, use the "TEST+" command to conduct a telex test to judge the working state. If the floppy disk is damaged, the NBDP equipment will fail to start.

The floppy disk belongs to the C ship station and also belongs to the NBDP terminal. In the NBDP terminal it is often used as a dedicated drive medium, and damage will cause the equipment to fail to start. The NBDP terminal floppy disk should be stored away from radiation sources and heat sources. The magnetic medium used to store inspection programs or data of the C ship station and NBDP terminal must be dedicated and kept away from magnetic fields and heat sources. For operation in the C ship station, a dedicated floppy disk should be used to prevent virus infection. The storage environment temperature is best 10～40℃, and it must be kept away from magnetic objects.

Maintenance of the combined radio station antenna The contents of combined radio station antenna maintenance include being familiar with the antenna configuration and installation position, checking the stressed parts, insulation performance and corrosion of the antenna, checking the insulation and stability of the bottom of the mast-type vertical antenna, and checking the cable feeder connection of the automatic antenna tuner unit. It is necessary to be familiar with the antenna configuration and installation position of the ship's combined radio station, conduct regular external inspections and promptly solve discovered problems. Focus on checking the stressed parts, insulation performance and corrosion of T-shaped and inverted-L-shaped multi-strand copper stranded wire antennas. Fasten, clean and rust-proof antennas that are prone to rust damage and breakage, ensuring their insulated installation state. Check the insulation and stability of the bottom of the mast-type vertical antenna to prevent looseness or failure due to strong wind. Check the cable feeder connection between the outdoor automatic antenna tuner unit and the antenna to prevent lightning damage caused by corroded connectors.

Combined radio station antenna maintenance applies to T-shaped antennas, inverted-L-shaped antennas, mast-type vertical antennas and automatic antenna tuner units. T-shaped antennas and inverted-L-shaped antennas mostly use multi-strand copper stranded wire as material; due to strong sea winds and material reasons, they are prone to rust damage and may break due to wind. Insulated installation is required during installation, and daily maintenance needs to focus on checking each stressed part, insulation performance and corrosion; for corrosion and looseness problems, fastening, cleaning and rust-proof treatment should be carried out in a timely manner. The mast-type vertical antenna is relatively firm, but the insulation at the bottom needs to be checked, and the stability at the bottom also needs to be checked. The transmitter automatic antenna tuner unit of some equipment is installed outdoors, and the cable connection between the antenna and the automatic antenna tuner unit needs to be checked daily. There was once a case where corroded feeder connectors led to lightning strikes, causing damage to the automatic antenna tuner unit. The automatic antenna tuner unit belongs to MF/HF equipment components and is threatened by the frequency band below 20MHz which is concentratedly affected by lightning; there has been a fault in which the automatic antenna tuner unit of MF/HF equipment was damaged due to lightning strike.

Correspondence of radar equipment-related maintenance Radar equipment includes the antenna, transceiver and display; the antenna, transceiver and display all belong to radar equipment. Radar installation applies to the antenna, transceiver and display. Radar antenna installation precautions require attention to the antenna, and radar display installation precautions require attention to the display. The transceiver includes transmitter air filter cleaning, electrostatic dust attraction of transmitter high-voltage components, and the magnetron. The display includes display air filter cleaning and display surface cleaning.

The antenna is the component in ship radar and communication equipment used to radiate or receive electromagnetic waves, and it needs to meet specific installation height, field of view and anti-interference requirements. The radar antenna height should ensure that the horizontal distance from the bow line of sight touching the sea surface does not exceed 500m or twice the ship length, whichever is smaller. The radar antenna position should ensure that there is no shadow sector area within the range from dead ahead to 2
2.5° abaft the beam on both port and starboard sides. The transceiver is the core equipment unit of the radar system, responsible for signal transmission and reception, usually installed near the bridge or directly below the antenna, usually installed in a well-ventilated equipment room near the bridge, the chart room or the bridge, and located directly below the antenna as much as possible. The mast-mounted radar transceiver connects to the antenna through a waveguide; the effective length of the waveguide should not exceed 25m, and there should preferably be no more than five bent waveguides. The display is the display terminal of ship radar and monitoring systems, used to present images, data and alarm information; it should be installed in the wheelhouse in a place without strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources and dry, fixed with a hardwood base, with the main radar display oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge.

Basic requirements for daily maintenance of VHF communication equipment The bridge is equipped with two VHF communication devices, and these two devices have both communication and DSC terminal functions. In daily maintenance, these two devices should be used alternately to avoid long-term use of only one of them, which would cause performance degradation or moisture and dust accumulation in the other. Daily maintenance of VHF communication equipment applies to the VHF communication equipment itself, and its contents cover equipment rotation, cleaning, power supply inspection and DSC function verification. Maintenance personnel need to regularly clean the microphone and panel to keep the transmission channel and operating surface clean; at the same time, they should frequently check the working condition of the equipment indicator lights and the regulated power supply to confirm that the power supply is normal and the indication state is consistent with the actual working state. The equipment's connection joints should also be frequently checked and tightened to prevent poor contact caused by vibration.

DSC terminal and communication function check The DSC terminal is fully called the digital selective calling terminal, belongs to an independent terminal, and has automatic ship position update and internal self-test functions. Daily maintenance of the DSC terminal applies to the DSC terminal; daily maintenance requires checking whether the DSC terminal ship position data is automatically updated, and frequently checking the working state of the DSC watchkeeping receiver. DSC self-testing should be performed daily, and at the same time the normal DSC communication function can be verified by mutual calling between two devices on the ship. The ship position parameter in distress alert information is automatically extracted from the ship position memory; in addition to being used for alerts, the ship position parameter is also used for receiving area calls, so the automatic update of ship position data is directly related to the accuracy of alert and call information. When conducting test calls on the DSC terminal, attention should be paid to test call precautions to avoid mistakenly sending distress alerts or interfering with normal watchkeeping. The antenna is used for radar target detection; in ship radar and communication equipment it is used to radiate or receive electromagnetic waves, and it needs to meet specific installation height, field of view and anti-interference requirements. Radar antenna installation precautions require attention to the installation conditions of the antenna itself, and radar installation applies to the antenna. The radar antenna height should ensure that the horizontal distance from the bow line of sight touching the sea surface does not exceed 500m or twice the ship length, whichever is smaller; the radar antenna position should ensure that there is no shadow sector area within the range from dead ahead to 2
2.5° abaft the beam on both port and starboard sides. For VHF communication equipment, the outdoor antenna connection and waterproof performance need to be regularly checked to prevent contact corrosion or rainwater infiltration into cable joints; this is an important link to ensure VHF communication distance and call quality.

VHF通信设备日常维护的基本要求驾驶台配置两台VHF通信设备，这两台设备兼具通信与DSC终端功能。日常维护中应当轮换使用这两台设备，避免长期只用其中一台而造成另一台性能下降或受潮积尘。VHF通信设备日常维护适用于VHF通信设备本身，其内容涵盖设备轮换、清洁、电源检查以及DSC功能验证等方面。维护人员需定期对麦克风和面板进行清洁，保持送话通道与操作面整洁；同时应经常检查设备指示灯及稳压电源的工作情况，确认供电正常、指示状态与实际工作状态一致。设备的连线接头也应经常检查并紧固，防止因振动造成接触不良。

DSC终端与通信功能检查DSC终端全称为数据选择性呼叫终端，属于独立终端，具备船位自动更新和内部自检功能。DSC终端日常维护适用于DSC终端，日常维护需检查DSC终端船位数据是否自动更新，并经常检查DSC值守机的工作状态。每日应进行DSC自检测，同时可通过本船两台设备相互呼叫来证实DSC通信功能正常。遇险报警信息中的船位参数自动从船位存储器中提取，船位参数除用于报警外，还用于接收区域性呼叫，因此船位数据的自动更新情况直接关系到报警与呼叫信息的准确性。对DSC终端进行测试呼叫时，需注意测试呼叫注意事项，避免误发遇险报警或干扰正常值守。天线用于雷达探测目标，在船舶雷达及通信设备中用于辐射或接收电磁波，需满足特定安装高度、视野及防干扰要求。雷达天线安装注意事项需注意天线本身的安装条件，雷达安装适用于天线。雷达天线高度应保证从船首视线触及海面的水平距离不超过500m或两倍船长较小者；雷达天线位置应使正前方至左右舷正横后

Composition and maintenance focus of the weather facsimile receiver. Most models of marine weather facsimile receivers consist of two parts: an independent receiver and a recording device. The receiver is functionally equivalent to an MF/HF single-sideband receiver, while the recording device is mostly composed of precision mechanical components. Daily maintenance focuses precisely on these two parts, the receiver and the recording device, so that through maintenance the equipment can still receive charts promptly and clearly under severe weather conditions such as typhoons.

The receiving antenna is a component of the weather facsimile receiver; together with the recording device it forms the complete unit, and functionally it is equivalent to an MF/HF single-sideband receiver. Daily maintenance of the receiving antenna requires guarding against contact corrosion, loosening of fixing devices and deterioration of insulation performance; during installation, protection against lightning damage is also required, and its installation position should maintain a safe distance from the radar antenna to avoid electromagnetic interference. The content of daily maintenance of the weather facsimile receiver includes: performing maintenance work on the receiving antenna, taking care to prevent lightning strikes, carrying out thermal head testing and inspection, handling recording paper jams, replacing recording paper in time, checking the automatic reception function, and visually inspecting the weather chart. The height of the radar antenna should ensure that the horizontal distance from the bow line of sight to the sea surface does not exceed the smaller of 500 m or twice the ship's length; the position of the radar antenna should ensure that there is no shadow sector within the range from dead ahead to 2 to 2.5° abaft the beam on both port and starboard sides. Precautions for radar antenna installation require attention to the antenna installation requirements; radar installation likewise applies to the antenna.

Maintenance of recording device components. The thermal head is part of the recording device of the marine weather facsimile receiver, and its function is to record the weather chart. The heat-sensitive recording head is a precision component in the recording device of the marine weather facsimile receiver; the thermal head and the heat-sensitive recording head are different names for the same component. When the received weather chart is unclear, the state of the thermal head needs to be tested and the heat-sensitive recording head checked for damage; if damage is detected, it should be replaced in time. Closing the paper compartment cover too forcefully may cause damage to the thermal head and may also cause damage to the heat-sensitive recording head.

The recording paper is part of the weather facsimile receiver and is used to record the weather chart. When the remaining length of the recording paper is less than 1 m, there will be an obvious mark reminding the user that it is about to run out. When a paper jam occurs, the equipment power should be switched off and the recording paper reinstalled. The weather facsimile receiver requires attention to the precautions for installing recording paper, namely that after installing the recording paper, the paper compartment cover should not be closed too forcefully, otherwise the paper compartment cover may be deformed or the heat-sensitive recording head damaged.

Lightning protection and other related equipment. During daily maintenance, attention should be paid to preventing the influence of lightning strikes on the equipment. In thunderstorm weather, it is best not to use the weather facsimile receiver unless necessary; after use, the antenna should be disconnected and earthed.

The ship power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its prescribed tasks; its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. The ship power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 type circuit breaker, ship's power network and shore power box. The ship's power network belongs to the ship power station; precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the relevant requirements of the ship power station.

Composition and basic requirements of the ship power station. The ship power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its prescribed tasks. Its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. Around this responsibility, the equipment and systems contained in the ship power station form a complete system for the generation, distribution and conversion of electrical energy.

In the electrical energy distribution link, the main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the ship power station; the ship power station includes the main switchboard, which feeds electrical energy to all power-consuming equipment throughout the ship. In the electrical energy generation link, the ship power station includes two types of generating devices, the brushed synchronous generator and the brushless synchronous generator, which respectively suit different excitation and maintenance conditions. In the voltage regulation link matched with the generators, the ship power station includes the uncontrolled phase compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system and brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system; these voltage regulation systems respectively correspond to different types of generators and operating requirements. In the protection and switching link, the ship power station includes the DW14 type circuit breaker, used for closing and opening the generator main circuit and for fault clearing.
