In the electrical energy output and external connection link, the ship power station includes the ship's power network and the shore power box, wherein the ship's power network is a component of the ship power station and undertakes the function of transmitting power to the ship's loads; the shore power box is used to supply power to the ship from the shore power source during berthing. Precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the relevant states and operating conditions of the ship power station, so as to ensure the safety of the ship power station when shore power is connected.

For AC generators operating in parallel, a reverse power protection with a 3 to 10 s operating delay should be provided to prevent the generator from continuing to operate in the reverse power state.

Key points of daily maintenance of the marine weather facsimile receiver. The daily maintenance of the marine weather facsimile receiver should be arranged in an overall manner in combination with the power supply conditions of the ship power station and the signal environment. The receiver is usually powered by the ship's power network, so its operating state is directly related to the power supply reliability of the ship power station. In daily inspection, it should first be confirmed that the power supply of the ship power station is normal, that the DW14 type circuit breaker of the corresponding branch of the main switchboard is in the closed position, and that the voltage and frequency of the ship's power network are stable, so as to avoid distortion of the recorded image or shutdown of the receiver caused by power supply fluctuations.

If the power supply part of the receiver is switched from the ship power station via the shore power box, when connecting shore power during berthing, the phase sequence and voltage should be checked in accordance with the precautions for connecting shore power, and it should be confirmed that the switching relationship between the ship power station and the shore power box is correct, so as to prevent the normal operation of the motor and recording mechanism in the receiver from being affected by a phase sequence mismatch. For ships supplied by a brushed synchronous generator or a brushless synchronous generator, attention should also be paid to the voltage regulation characteristics of the uncontrolled phase compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system and brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system when the load changes, so as to avoid excessive voltage deviation affecting the recording quality of the receiver.

Daily maintenance should also include inspection of the receiver antenna. The antenna should be kept away from strong electromagnetic interference sources in the ship power station such as the main switchboard, the DW14 type circuit breaker and high-power cables, so as to reduce the influence of interference on the received signal. The connecting cable between the receiver and the ship's power network should be reliably fixed, and the shielding layer should be well earthed. If the AC generators operating in parallel in the ship power station are provided with reverse power protection with a 3 to 10 s operating delay, during generator changeover or paralleling operations, important recording work of the receiver should be avoided at this time, and the receiver should be put into operation after the power supply of the ship power station has returned to stability. For ships supplied by the brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, because the voltage regulation link responds relatively quickly, the power supply part of the receiver generally does not need additional voltage stabilization, but the power supply voltage should still be regularly measured to see whether it is within the permitted range. When the receiver is re-enabled after long-term disuse, it should first be checked whether the power supply of the ship power station is normal, and then the states of the main switchboard, the ship's power network, the shore power box and the DW14 type circuit breaker should be confirmed item by item; only after confirmation without error may the unit be switched on.

Maintenance records should state the inspection date, the operating state of the ship power station, the reception effect of the receiver and the handling situation, so as to facilitate subsequent comparative analysis. By combining the daily maintenance of the receiver with the power supply management of the ship power station, reception faults caused by power supply and interference factors can be reduced, and the clarity and completeness of the weather facsimile chart can be maintained.

The ship power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its prescribed tasks. This equipment bears the basic responsibilities of ensuring reliable power supply and safe operation, and of rapidly eliminating faults after they occur. In terms of composition, the ship power station includes the main switchboard, the ship's power network and the shore power box, and also includes the brushed synchronous generator and the brushless synchronous generator, as well as different forms of voltage regulation devices such as the uncontrolled phase compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system and brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, and also includes the DW14 type circuit breaker. Among these, the ship's power network is a component of the ship power station, and the main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy of the power station, having functions such as circuit switching, protection alarming, parameter detection and power regulation; it can connect or disconnect circuits, issue an alarm when a protection device operates, detect and display various electrical parameters, and regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel. The interior of the main switchboard includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The main switch is used in the power station to connect and disconnect the generator and the main busbar; it is an air circuit breaker having both switching and protection functions, and its components include the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device, arc extinguishing device, auxiliary contact and control and signal indication circuit. The DW14 type circuit breaker adopts Japanese Terasaki technology and is fitted with an AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, which is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker. The trip unit is the electrical component in a circuit breaker used to realize protection functions such as overload, short circuit and undervoltage and to drive the contact to open; the main switch is mainly composed of the undervoltage release, the shunt release and the overcurrent protection device. The circuit breaker, as a switching appliance used in the ship's electrical power system to protect circuits, belongs to the low-voltage distribution appliances and is divided into two types, the frame type (air type) and the molded-case type, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short-circuit faults; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power network. When used as generator protection, the circuit breaker opens after an overload of 10%-50% with a delay of less than 2 min; when the overcurrent is greater than 50%, the short-delay trip unit is set to 200%-250% of the rated current with a delay of ≤0.6 s; the undervoltage trip unit operates instantaneously when the voltage drops to 35% of rated value, and operates with a delay at 35%-70%.

Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the equipment, the circuit breaker.

Both the brushed synchronous generator and the brushless synchronous generator include the generator prime mover, the generator stator winding and the excitation system. The generator prime mover is the power source of the generator; the generator stator winding is the stator part of the generator, used to generate the induced electromotive force; in the brushless synchronous generator, three-phase AC is induced in the main generator stator winding and output; the excitation system provides the excitation current for the generator and belongs to the voltage regulation system of the synchronous generator, including brushed, brushless and thyristor forms, with common forms being the uncontrolled phase compounding, controlled phase compounding, thyristor excitation and brushless excitation voltage regulation systems. Maintenance of the excitation system applies to the excitation system; its maintenance cycle is once every half year, and the insulation resistance value is required to be not less than 1 MΩ. The insulation of marine motor windings must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture proofing, mould proofing and salt-oil-mist proofing, and must be oil resistant. The general alarm device is composed of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, that is, the general alarm device includes the junction box. The junction box is a component in the ship's electrical system used to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical elements; the solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to an external junction box but is connected directly into the local control box.

In terms of fault symptoms, a single-phase earthing fault of the power system manifests as the insulation indicator lamp of one phase going out while the insulation indicator lamps of the other two phases are abnormally bright; its typical appearance feature is precisely that the insulation indicator lamp of one phase goes out and the insulation indicator lamps of the remaining two phases are abnormally bright. The causes of this fault include an earthing fault caused by single-phase insulation breakdown of a power-consuming load, including loosening or shell contact of the wiring in the junction box of a load motor, including breakdown faults of power distribution switches or other electrical equipment in the main switchboard, and also including earthing occurring inside the generator. This fault belongs to the category of faults caused by severe environmental conditions reducing electrical insulation capability. The low insulation resistance fault of the power system manifests as low insulation resistance that has already reached the alarm value, and is divided into two categories, 400 V and 220 V. 400 V system faults mostly occur at the load end, on open deck equipment or inside the main switchboard; 220 V system faults mostly occur in the lighting distribution systems of each deck, kitchen electrical equipment or deck lighting. If such a fault is not solved in time, a further fault in the other phase will form a short-circuit current, and the consequence of the short circuit may cause some load switches to trip or even the main switchboard to trip. Severe environmental conditions reducing electrical insulation capability is one of the main causes.

As for fault causes, common faults of the equipment itself include: damage to the generator prime mover, such as failure of the prime mover governor or overheating of the cylinder block; burning out or open circuit of the generator stator winding; damage to the excitation system; insulation damage of the cable junction box. That is to say, damage to the generator prime mover is one of the common causes belonging to the equipment itself that cause faults of the ship's electrical power system, and both failure of the prime mover governor and overheating of the cylinder block are specific manifestations of damage to the generator prime mover; insulation damage of the cable junction box is one of the common equipment-itself faults that cause faults of the ship's electrical power system. When an excitation system fault causes underexcitation or loss of excitation, reactive circulating current is produced between units operating in parallel, which may cause tripping. Common faults caused by improper operation include: improper closing operation; unbalanced generator load control; improper operation caused by erroneous observation. Improper paralleling operation may cause the overcurrent protection of the generator main switch to operate and trip or the reverse power protection to operate and trip; during paralleling operation, improper grasp of the closing moment or reversing the direction of load sharing adjustment may cause the generator reverse power protection to trip; during operation, damaging the insulation protective layer or metal parts falling onto wire ends may cause a short-circuit fault of the electrical circuit. Accidents refer to various accidents that occur unexpectedly such as sudden short circuit and open circuit; common forms of accidents include sudden short circuit and open circuit;

In the ship's electrical power system, a short circuit is classified as a severe overload; the heat and electrodynamic force produced by the short-circuit current are the main causes of generator damage, and a short circuit means that two points in a circuit are connected artificially or accidentally through an extremely small impedance. Maladjustment of synchronous generator operating parameters means that the operating parameters of the generator exceed the permitted values, which may damage the generator set or power-consuming equipment, and protective measures need to be taken to avoid accidents; its specific manifestations include overcurrent, overload, short circuit, reverse power, undervoltage, overvoltage, low frequency and high frequency. In the ship's electrical power system, a relatively small overcurrent is called overload, and only a relatively large overcurrent such as a short circuit is called overcurrent; 1.1 times the rated current is called a small overload, 1.5 times the rated current is called a relatively large overload, and a short circuit is called a severe overload. The heat produced by long-time overcurrent operation will age the insulation; the range of current in which the generator is permitted to operate is mainly determined by the current flowing through the stator (armature) winding. The influence of severe environmental conditions refers to various faults caused by severe environmental conditions reducing the electrical insulation capability of equipment; it mainly leads to two types of problems, the single-phase earthing fault of the power system and the low insulation resistance fault of the power system: the low insulation resistance fault of the 400 V system mostly occurs in open deck electrical equipment or inside the main switchboard, the low insulation resistance fault of the 220 V system often occurs in the lighting of each deck, kitchen electrical equipment or deck lighting systems, and the single-phase earthing fault manifests as the insulation indicator lamp of one phase going out while the other two phases are abnormally bright; a low insulation resistance fault not handled in time may form a short-circuit current and cause a switch to trip or the breaker to trip. Faults of the equipment itself, improper operation, accidents and maladjustment of synchronous generator operating parameters may all lead to a single-phase earthing fault of the power system.

AC generators operating in parallel in the ship power station should be provided with reverse power protection with a 3 to 10 s operating delay. For generators with a diesel engine prime mover, the reverse power protection setting value is 8%-15% of the rated power, and for generators with a turbine prime mover, the reverse power protection setting value is 2%-8% of the rated power. Undervoltage protection is mainly for the protection of generators operating in parallel, and also protects consumers such as asynchronous motors. Precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the relevant requirements of the ship power station.

In terms of the instruments and electrical quantities used for maintenance and testing, the measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. The multimeter is used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand the state of equipment; measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with the power on. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open circuit in the shunt resistor will cause the voltage corrector to have no main regulating effect. Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes leading to overcurrent and overheating of the AC motor.

The ship power station is composed of parts such as the main switchboard and the ship's power network; the main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy of the power station, undertaking tasks such as circuit switching, protection alarming, parameter detection and power regulation, and can regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel. The ship's power network usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system, in which single-phase earthing at any point is an abnormal state, and if another phase is earthed, a short circuit will be formed; therefore, a power network insulation detection device is installed on the lighting distribution panel of the main switchboard to monitor the insulation condition of the power network.

In the operation of the power station, voltage and current are two basic electrical quantities that need to be measured frequently.

The circuit breaker may suffer the fault that the contacts cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated manually, that is, the contacts cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated manually; at this time there is an obstruction in the manual closing circuit itself, and during inspection it should first be confirmed whether the operating mechanism is in position and whether the trip unit is in the reset state, and then it should be checked whether the contacts and transmission parts are jammed. The circuit breaker may also suffer the fault that the contacts cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, that is, the contacts cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically; at this time the electric closing circuit fails to act normally, and during inspection the operating power supply, the closing coil and its control circuit should be examined, confirming level by level whether the signal is delivered. The circuit breaker may also exhibit the failure of one phase contact not closing, indicating that the three-phase contacts do not act consistently, and the cause must be sought separately for that phase contact and its transmission link. If the shunt trip unit cannot cause the circuit breaker to open, it indicates that the shunt trip circuit fails to effectively drive the tripping mechanism, and the shunt trip unit coil and its control circuit should be checked; if the undervoltage trip unit cannot cause the circuit breaker to open, it indicates that the undervoltage tripping link has lost its due breaking capability, and the undervoltage trip unit and its setting state should be checked. If the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, it indicates that the circuit breaker trips under the impact of the motor starting current, and the setting value of the overcurrent trip unit should be checked against it; if the circuit breaker opens automatically about 1h after closing, it indicates that the opening occurs after a period of operation, and the cause should be sought in combination with the temperature rise and the state of the trip unit. If the undervoltage trip unit is noisy, it indicates that its electromagnetic system is not working normally, and its core and coil should be checked; if the temperature rise of the circuit breaker is too high, it indicates that there is abnormal heating in the conductive circuit or connection parts, and the contact condition of the contacts and the tightness of the connections should be checked; if the auxiliary switch fails, it will affect the correct action of the control and signal indication circuit, and the contacts and transmission of the auxiliary switch should be checked; if the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctions and causes the circuit breaker to open, it indicates that the trip unit issues a tripping command before the setting conditions are reached, and its detection and setting links should be checked.

The current relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship power system, belonging to the electromagnetic relay classified by the nature of the input signal; its coil carries electrical quantity, its structure is basically similar to that of the contactor, and in the AC three-speed electric windlass it picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%. After the generator parallel operation trips, the overcurrent relay needs to be reset to restore the main switch closing. The reverse power relay is used to detect and protect against reverse power and is one of the control and protection devices commonly used on the ship main switchboard; it is used to detect the reverse power of the AC generator and trigger the protection action, and the setting value for the diesel engine prime mover is 8% to 15% of rated power, with an operating delay of 3 to 10s. When improper operation of parallel connection causes the reverse power relay to trip, some panels require manual reset.

Motor overload refers to the fault state in which the motor operating current or power exceeds the rated value; when the generator output power or current exceeds its rated value it is defined as overload, which in DC motors will cause commutation difficulty and excessive sparking; when a DC motor is overloaded, the current per unit area of the brush is large, causing commutation difficulty and resulting in excessive sparking under brush, while in a generator it triggers overload protection. Systematic fault escalation may cause abnormal grid frequency and voltage, which in turn causes generator overload. Improper operation can also cause a single-phase earthing fault in the power system.

The main generator undertaking the power generation task in the ship power station is currently mainly divided into two forms: the brushed synchronous generator and the brushless synchronous generator. Both types of generator include the generator prime mover, generator stator winding, excitation system, generator bearing and generator shaft and other components, and their daily maintenance and upkeep requirements are basically the same.

As far as the excitation system is concerned, it is the voltage regulation system that provides excitation current for the generator, and common forms include uncontrollable phase compounding, controllable phase compounding, thyristor excitation and brushless excitation voltage regulation systems. The maintenance cycle of the excitation system is once every half year, and the insulation resistance value is required to be not less than 1MΩ; during maintenance it is necessary to check whether the wiring of each terminal post of the excitation system is good, and any loose wire end found must be tightened, and to check the gap size of the linear reactor and whether there is abnormal sound; when the gap is unsuitable it should be adjusted to the required value, and when there is abnormal sound the cause should be found and eliminated, and at the same time check whether the insulation between phases and between phase and earth of the excitation system is good.

The uncontrollable phase compounding voltage regulation system is one of the common forms of the excitation voltage regulation system of marine synchronous generators, and its structural feature is a small number of components and simple line connections. When carrying out fault repair on this system, it is necessary to find the fault point against the schematic diagram according to its working process and phenomena; common faults include failure to build up voltage at rated speed or abnormal terminal voltage; when voltage build-up fails, it is necessary to check the residual magnetism voltage and the state of the phase-shifting reactor and the resonant capacitor. The controllable phase compounding voltage regulation system is likewise one of the four main forms of the excitation voltage regulation system of marine synchronous generators, and in classification it is parallel with the uncontrollable phase compounding voltage regulation system and the thyristor excitation voltage regulation system. The thyristor excitation voltage regulation system is also one of these four main forms; during fault repair, the thyristor main circuit is checked first, and then the trigger circuit; common faults include failure to build up voltage at rated speed and sudden loss of power during operation; if voltage still cannot be built up after magnetization, it may be due to breakdown of the thyristor or rectifier diode in the magnetization circuit, and a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases is one of the typical fault symptoms of this system. The brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system is likewise among these four main forms, parallel with the uncontrollable phase compounding, controllable phase compounding and thyristor excitation voltage regulation systems, and is suitable for the brushless synchronous generator form currently used on ships.

The brushless synchronous generator internally contains the coaxially rotating main generator excitation winding, the exciter armature winding and the rotating rectifier device; the static excitation system supplies power to the exciter stator and, after rotating rectification, provides DC current to the main generator excitation winding. Its common faults include breakdown or open circuit of the rotating commutator and short circuit or open circuit of the rotating-armature type excitation winding; during maintenance special attention must be paid to the fact that centrifugal force easily causes the rotating rectifier armature to loosen and open. In the brushless system, breakdown of the rotating rectifier module will cause the voltage to drop, and when one diode is damaged the voltage can drop to above 200V. In the thyristor system, if a rectifier element is open or the trigger half-wave fails, the terminal voltage will drop greatly when the load increases. Damage to components of the static excitation system will cause insufficient DC current, and the exciter stator winding current must be detected to judge the fault. When an excitation system fault causes underexcitation or loss of excitation, reactive circulating current arises between units operating in parallel, which may cause tripping; in parallel operation, the brushless synchronous generator usually adopts a current stabilizing device to achieve even distribution of reactive power.

Common fault types of the brushed synchronous generator include open circuit of the stator winding, interphase short circuit, turn-to-turn short circuit, as well as poor brush contact and brush wear. Poor brush contact is a common fault type of brushed motors and is often mentioned alongside faults such as open circuit of the stator winding and short circuit of the rotor excitation winding; it is distinguished from the rotating commutator breakdown or rotating-armature type winding fault of the brushless synchronous generator. For brushed motors, excessive brush wear is also one of the common faults, parallel with open circuit and short circuit of the stator winding. The commutator is the rotating sliding contact component used for leading current in and out in DC motors and wound-rotor motors, and is composed of commutator segments; the graphite brush is soft in texture and easily damages the commutator, and is suitable for motors with general rectification conditions and uniform load. When dismantling a DC motor, care should be taken to prevent damage to the winding ends, the commutator or the slip rings. When excessive sparking under brush occurs, it is necessary to check the contact condition between the brush and the commutator, check the brush holder condition, check the armature vibration condition, check the commutator segment condition and check the brush position.

Regarding the maintenance and upkeep of generator bearings, in oil-ring lubricated sliding bearings the oil quantity of the bearing should be kept constant, and generally oil is not added during operation; with the oil quantity below the specified liquid level, the bearing should not throw oil, so as to avoid splashing onto the winding. The lubricating oil must be sampled periodically for inspection, and if the oil color darkens, becomes turbid, or contains water or dirt, it should be replaced; when the bearing heats up, new oil should be replaced in all cases, generally the oil should be changed every 250 to 400 working hours, but at least once every half year. Causes of generator bearing overheating include severe bearing wear; the lubricating oil quantity of the generator bearing must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space; improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover will cause generator bearing overheating; poor assembly of the generator set is also one of the causes of generator bearing overheating; bending of the generator shaft will cause generator bearing overheating; when the stator and rotor rub against each other, it is necessary to check whether the motor bearing is loose. Marine motors include components such as bearings, windings, commutators and brushes, among which the bearing is the mechanical component of the motor used to support the rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration and abnormal noise; bearing fault is one of the direct causes of overheating of the motor in the AC electric drive system, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very large non-uniform noise and the feature of bearing end cover overheating.

Regarding the daily maintenance and upkeep requirements of the generator, to ensure normal operation of the generator, water, oil and dirt should not accumulate near it, and there must be no corrosive gas, so as to avoid damaging the generator winding insulation; while guarding against moisture and dust, care must be taken not to affect the normal ventilation and cooling of the generator; the dust and dirt in the ventilation ducts should be cleaned frequently to keep them unobstructed, and the temperature of the cooling air must not be too low, so as to avoid condensation on the winding and other conductive components. These requirements apply to both brushed synchronous generators and brushless synchronous generators.

Regarding detection and repair means, the multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, current as well as the polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode of the thyristor, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistance must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is a capacitor in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. The thyristor, also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, has its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode all detectable with the aid of a multimeter. Printed circuit boards are widely used in marine electrical equipment; they are composed of an insulating material base material and conductive foil lines, the base material is often called the substrate, with phenolic resin board and epoxy glass being the most commonly used, and the line part is made of conductive copper laid on the substrate, with the required pattern obtained by etching. During maintenance it is necessary to check whether the contact of the plug-in printed circuit board is good; for discrete components the solder joints and copper film corrosion should be checked; for printed circuit boards attention should be paid to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards; printed circuit boards will suffer circuit board faults, and circuit board faults belong to the category of printed circuit boards. Electrical connections due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter will cause increased contact resistance, that is, poor contact; loose fastening screws and wire terminals will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance; poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, interphase short circuit and other faults, therefore the wiring screws of the electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact, and failure to tighten the external wiring screws of the thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be disconnected. The rectifier is used to convert AC into DC, and the electrical graphic symbol of the full-wave bridge rectifier is UR; the rotating rectifier of the brushless synchronous generator is prone to loosening and opening of the armature due to centrifugal force; rectifier breakdown is one of the fault causes of a large voltage drop when the generator load increases; an open circuit in one phase of the phase-shifting reactor, rectifier or phase compounding transformer will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; the generator residual magnetism voltage being opposite in polarity to the rectifier output voltage will cause the voltage to fail to build up normally; in the controllable phase compounding constant voltage device, rectifier fault is one of the sub-causes of phase compounding device fault, and if the UR rectifier has an open-circuit diode, it will cause a voltage deviation of |U0-Ufe| greater than ΔU1. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage corrector to have no main regulating action.

When carrying out fault repair on such systems, it is necessary, according to their working process, to compare the observed phenomena with the schematic diagram and find the fault location point by point. Common faults include failure to build up voltage at rated speed, terminal voltage deviating from the rated value, sudden failure to generate during operation, a large voltage drop when the load increases, and generator overheating; generator bearing overheating is also included among the common faults of such systems.

Failure of the generator voltage to build up normally refers to the voltage still failing to build up when the speed has reached the rated value. This phenomenon is relatively common in the uncontrollable phase compounding voltage regulation system.

In preliminary troubleshooting, it should first be checked whether there is residual magnetism voltage; if not, magnetization should be carried out; if residual magnetism exists but voltage still does not build up, the state of the voltage regulator and the phase-shifting reactor should be checked. There are many causes of this fault: no residual magnetism or insufficient residual magnetism will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; an open circuit of the excitation winding will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; rusting and blackening of the generator slip rings making them non-conductive will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; the brush being stuck in the brush holder or the brush braid being broken will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; the linear reactor having no air gap or too small an air gap will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; breakdown or open circuit of the rectifier element of the voltage regulator will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; incorrect wiring will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; disconnection of the connections among the reactor, resonant capacitor and phase compounding transformer will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; in addition, an open circuit of the phase-shifting reactor will likewise prevent the generator from building up voltage, and short circuit or breakdown of the resonant capacitor is also a possible fault cause.

Generator voltage lower than the rated value manifests as terminal voltage lower than the rated voltage. Too small an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor will cause generator voltage lower than the rated value; too small a setting resistance will cause generator voltage lower than the rated value; too low a speed will cause generator voltage lower than the rated value; an open circuit in the generator excitation winding will cause generator voltage lower than the rated value; a change in the tap of the reactor or phase compounding transformer will cause generator voltage lower than the rated value; an error in the voltmeter will cause generator voltage lower than the rated value, and among the various fault causes of voltage lower than the rated value this item is listed as item 7, with the corresponding troubleshooting method being to calibrate the voltmeter. For voltage on the low side caused by too small a setting resistance, the setting resistance needs to be adjusted. Too large an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor is one of the causes, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to reduce the air gap as required, the object of operation being the air gap structure of the phase-shifting reactor, and this measure is listed as the first item among the various troubleshooting methods for generator voltage higher than the rated value. Burning, rusting or poor contact of the sliding contact of the setting resistance, or burning out of the resistance, is one of the main causes, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and repair or renew the resistance, that is, to check and repair or renew the damaged resistance element. A change in the tap of the reactor or phase compounding transformer will also cause voltage on the high side, and readjustment as required is needed, the specific operation being to readjust the tap of the reactor or phase compounding transformer that has changed. An error in the voltmeter will likewise cause a high reading, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to calibrate the voltmeter, and this item is listed as the fourth among the various troubleshooting measures.

Sudden failure of the generator to generate during operation is also one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase compounding voltage regulation system. If it still cannot generate after magnetization, it indicates that the excitation coil of the generator itself has an open-circuit fault, and such excitation coil open circuit should be handled by the method for rated speed but failure to build up voltage; if it can generate after magnetization, it may be breakdown of the main circuit thyristor or stoppage of the trigger circuit, and the rectifier main circuit and the trigger circuit power output need to be checked. Causes of this fault include: rectifier breakdown will cause sudden failure of the generator to generate during operation; no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit will cause sudden failure of the generator to generate during operation; loosening of the reactor core, resulting in a reduced air gap, will cause sudden failure of the generator to generate during operation; short circuit of the reactor or phase compounding transformer coil will cause sudden failure of the generator to generate during operation; breakdown of the resonant capacitor will cause sudden failure of the generator to generate during operation. When one phase of the phase-shifting reactor, rectifier or phase compounding transformer is open, the generator will also suddenly fail to generate during operation.

A large drop in generator voltage when the load increases is characterized by a large drop in terminal voltage when the generator load increases. An open circuit in the rectifier will cause a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases; inconsistency in polarity between the current winding and the voltage winding of the phase compounding transformer will also cause a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases. To deal with this fault, it is necessary to find the fault point against the working principle diagram according to the specific phenomena, and during repair fault analysis and diagnosis must be carried out in combination with the working process.

Generator overheating is one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase compounding voltage regulation system, and its fault causes and troubleshooting methods must be analyzed item by item in combination with the specific working process of the system. Generator bearing overheating manifests as abnormal rise in bearing temperature and likewise belongs to the common faults of this system. If overheating is caused by too much lubricating oil, the oil quantity must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space; too little or deteriorated lubricating oil can also cause bearing overheating. When caused by severe bearing wear, the bearing needs to be replaced; when caused by improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover, it needs to be reinstalled; when caused by poor assembly of the generator set, it needs to be realigned and installed; when caused by bending of the generator shaft, the shaft needs to be straightened;

Mutual friction between the stator and rotor, such as bearing looseness, may also cause bearing overheating, so the bearing, shaft and rotor core need to be checked. From the perspective of cause classification, bearing fault causes bearing overheating, lubrication fault causes bearing overheating, and installation fault causes bearing overheating; therefore, bearing overheating corresponds to the three tasks of checking bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition, and checking the installation condition. Both checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition require the use of the bearing, and the marine motor contains the bearing. If the noise disappears during no-load operation, it indicates poor coupling installation; if the noise still exists and is accompanied by vibration, it points to a fault of the shaft or the bearing itself.

When diagnosing the above faults, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions of components (assemblies) and their locations of the electrical equipment, must be very familiar with the circuits, working principles and positions of all components of the whole ship's electrical equipment, and master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, so as to understand the phenomena and make a preliminary diagnosis through these five approaches. A multimeter or voltmeter can be used to measure voltage values, and a multimeter is also used to measure resistance and capacitance. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle; its characteristic is that it blocks direct current and passes alternating current. In circuit diagrams it is usually represented by the letter C plus a number, such as C25. Its hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC). Its measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. The measurable property of a resistor is its resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; poor contact is one of the causes of equipment faults, referring to a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter. Loose fastening screws and terminal ends will cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance, and further causing local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults. As the heart of the ship's power system, the reliability and survivability of the ship's power station are important signs of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks; its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur.

When the load increases, a large drop in generator voltage is a relatively common type of abnormality in the operation of the ship's power station. There is more than one cause of this phenomenon, among which no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit is a typical case. The so-called no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit means that no current flows through the circuit where the excitation winding is located; at this time the excitation magnetic field of the generator cannot be established or maintained, and once the load increases, the terminal voltage drops significantly accordingly. For this fault cause, the troubleshooting method is to check whether the wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding is loose or broken, that is, to lock the inspection object onto this section of wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding, and confirm point by point whether its connection is reliable and whether the conductor is intact. This maintenance procedure corresponds to no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit in the fault troubleshooting table, and is one of the troubleshooting methods for the fault of a large drop in generator voltage caused by increased load.

Parallel to the above cause is rectifier breakdown. The rectifier undertakes the function of converting alternating current into direct current; once its internal elements break down, the supply of excitation current loses its normal channel, and the generator voltage will likewise drop significantly when the load increases. For rectifier breakdown, the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and replace the broken-down rectifier elements, and the core of the operation is to find the rectifier elements that have broken down and replace them. This step is used to troubleshoot the fault of a large drop in generator voltage caused by rectifier breakdown; in the fault troubleshooting table, this method corresponds to the fault cause rectifier breakdown. The electrical graphical symbol of the full-wave bridge rectifier is UR.

The loosening of the reactor core, resulting in a reduced air gap, is yet another fault cause that can cause a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases.

Its mechanism lies in the loosening of the reactor core, which reduces the air gap of the magnetic circuit, and the working state of the magnetic circuit changes accordingly. When dealing with this fault, the air gap should be adjusted to the required value and the core tightened, that is, after adjusting the air gap the action of tightening the core must be performed. This step is used to solve the fault of a reduced air gap caused by loosening of the reactor core, and is one of the troubleshooting methods for the fault of a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases. As a component of marine electrical equipment, the core is the magnetic-conducting part in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as a reference point for insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of a coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in the through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor under test is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. The contactor also contains the core as a component.

Breakdown of the resonant capacitor will likewise cause abnormal generator voltage. The resonant capacitor is used in a resonant circuit; after breakdown its original resonant function is lost, excitation regulation becomes abnormal accordingly, and the generator voltage drops significantly when the load increases. For the fault of resonant capacitor breakdown, the treatment method is to replace the broken-down capacitor, and the operation is simply to directly replace the broken-down capacitor element. Resonant capacitor breakdown is one of the troubleshooting items for the fault of short circuit of the reactor or the phase compound excitation transformer winding, and is one of the troubleshooting methods for the fault of a large drop in generator voltage. Besides breakdown, a short circuit of the resonant capacitor will also cause the generator voltage to fail to build up normally; in this case the troubleshooting method is to replace the capacitor; correspondingly, the phenomenon that the generator suddenly stops generating during operation corresponds respectively to the four treatment measures of checking and replacing the broken-down rectifier elements, checking whether the wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding is loose or broken, adjusting the air gap to the required value and tightening the core, and replacing the broken-down capacitor.

In the testing stage, electrical quantities and parameters such as voltage, current and capacitance can all be measured with instruments. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools include the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. The function of a capacitor is charging and discharging, and its measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. Its hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC), which is related to the signal frequency and capacitance. Types of capacitors include electrolytic capacitors, ceramic capacitors, chip capacitors, monolithic capacitors, tantalum capacitors and polyester capacitors; the units are farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF) and picofarad (pF); the main performance indicators include capacitance, withstand voltage value (maximum working voltage) and temperature resistance value. Marine electrical equipment uses capacitors; the capacitor testing step applies to capacitors; capacitors will develop capacitor faults; capacitor faults belong to the category of capacitors. AC single-phase motors and electric fans both contain capacitors.

Several typical faults occur during the operation of the uncontrollable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, and generator overheating is one of them. Generator overheating is also related to factors such as long-term overload, short circuit of the excitation winding or stator winding, unbalanced three-phase load, and mutual friction between stator and rotor; all these causes will make the motor temperature exceed the normal range. For generator overheating, the output current and power of the generator should be observed during troubleshooting and controlled below the rated values; at the same time, the stator and rotor windings of the motor should be checked and the short-circuited windings repaired; generator overheating also corresponds to checking whether there is a single-phase high-power load or single-phase operation of the motor, that is, it is necessary to check whether there is a single-phase high-power load or single-phase operation of the motor; in addition, it is necessary to check whether the motor bearing, shaft and rotor core are loose. The fault causes and troubleshooting methods of generator overheating are listed item by item in the relevant fault troubleshooting table.

When the load increases, a large drop in generator voltage often corresponds to a variety of fault causes. Poor performance of the prime mover's governor will cause a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases; displacement of the stator core will also cause a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases.

For bearing overheating, the corresponding troubleshooting directions are checking bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition and checking the installation condition, and the inspection must all be carried out around the bearing. If the noise disappears during no-load operation, it indicates poor coupling installation; long-term overload will cause the motor temperature rise to be high and will also cause generator overheating; long-term overload operation of an asynchronous motor will also cause insulation performance degradation, aging or mechanical damage; therefore, when checking excessive motor temperature rise, it is necessary to troubleshoot whether there is a long-term overload condition on the mechanical side. In traction motors, a stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start and will also cause the motor temperature to be too high or smoking. For unbalanced three-phase load, it should be checked whether there is a single-phase high-power load or single-phase operation of the motor, that is, check whether there is a single-phase high-power load in the system and whether any motor is in single-phase operation. The thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, and its measurable properties include polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode.

A diode has unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is very large or infinite. In circuits it is usually represented by VD, and by function it can be divided into rectifier diode, isolation diode, Schottky diode, light-emitting diode and Zener diode, etc., for example rectifier diode 1N4004, isolation diode 1N4148, Schottky diode BAT85. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment; the diode testing step applies to various diodes, and its measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance.

In the troubleshooting of the ship's power station, the conventional fault diagnosis method often takes observation as the starting step, that is, first interviewing the operator about the operating conditions before and after the fault, and then carrying out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged. Only after this step is completed is the inspection of the monitoring and indicating device entered.

During observation, instruments are needed to measure electrical quantities and components, and the multimeter is one of the commonly used tools. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; the current flowing through the meter head at full scale is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. Distinguished by display mode, multimeters fall into two types: the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter; the MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter, and its panel is provided with four jacks "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A", capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A. A multimeter can be used to measure various objects such as resistors, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples; a clamp-on ammeter can also be used when measuring current, and the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement. When measuring direct current, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range and the meter head is connected in series in the broken branch; when measuring direct voltage, the test probes are connected in parallel across the component under test, and when the range is uncertain the maximum range is set first. A diode has unidirectional conductivity and is usually represented by VD in circuits; its measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance; by function, diodes include rectifier diodes, isolation diodes, Schottky diodes, light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes, among which rectifier diodes are such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, and Schottky diodes such as BAT85. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment; the diode testing step applies to diodes, and breakdown can be judged by testing their continuity.

The brush contacts the collector ring to transfer current, and the device that fixes the brush is the brush holder. For marine motors under long-term 15° list, 7.5° trim and 22.5° roll, the brush holder connecting parts must be guaranteed not to loosen; too tight a clearance fit between the brush and the brush holder will cause sticking, causing excessive brush sparking; a loose brush holder will cause the brushes to be arranged out of line, affecting commutation and increasing sparking. Checking the contact between the brush and the commutator, checking the condition of the brush holder, and checking the brush position all revolve around the brush. When the generator voltage cannot be established normally, the brushes, brush holders and brush pigtails need to be checked and repaired; troubleshooting the generator excitation circuit fault also includes checking whether the brush is stuck in the brush holder.

A potentiometer is also called a potentiometer; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is this type of component, generally considered manually adjustable, it has three pins, of which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes as the shaft rotates. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by the potentiometer R& driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R' driven by the motor M changes accordingly. The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a potentiometer, and this is the purpose of the potentiometer. There are many causes of this phenomenon: breakdown of the rectifier will cause the generator to suddenly stop generating during operation; the fault of the generator suddenly stopping generation during operation corresponds to several handling methods: for that caused by rectifier breakdown, the broken-down rectifier element should be checked and replaced; for that caused by no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit, check whether the wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding is loose or broken; for that caused by loosening of the reactor core and reduction of the air gap, the air gap should be adjusted to the required value and the core tightened; for that caused by short circuit of the reactor or phase compound excitation transformer coil, the coil should be checked and repaired or replaced with a new one; for that caused by breakdown of the resonant capacitor, the broken-down capacitor should be replaced. When using a multimeter to test a faulty rotating rectifier module, the breakdown condition is judged by detecting the continuity of the diode.

The generator voltage cannot be established normally means that the generator speed has reached the rated speed but the voltage cannot be established. This phenomenon is one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system. During troubleshooting, first confirm whether there is residual magnetism voltage; if there is no residual magnetism voltage, use an external power source (DC) for magnetization to build up voltage; if there is already residual magnetism voltage but the voltage still does not rise, then turn to check the state of the voltage regulator and the phase-shifting reactor.

No residual magnetism or insufficient residual magnetism manifests as the generator lacking an initial magnetic field or insufficient residual magnetism strength, and the corresponding handling method is to use an external power source (DC) for magnetization to build up voltage. Open circuit of the excitation winding is one of the main fault causes; during troubleshooting it is necessary to check whether there is looseness or breakage from the rectifier to the excitation winding, and the inspection scope covers the entire line from the rectifier to the excitation winding, specifically checking whether the line is loose or broken. The brush being stuck in the brush holder or the brush pigtail being broken manifests specifically as the brush being stuck in the brush holder or the brush pigtail being broken, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and repair the brush, brush holder and brush pigtail, and the operating objects include the three components of brush, brush holder and brush pigtail. The linear reactor having no air gap or too small an air gap corresponds to the troubleshooting method of adjusting the air gap to an appropriate size, and the core of the operation is to adjust the air gap to an appropriate size. The voltage regulator rectifier element being broken down or open-circuited is listed as cause item 6 (⑥) in the fault troubleshooting table; this fault involves an abnormal state of the rectifier element in the voltage regulator assembly, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and replace the broken-down rectifier element. Incorrect wiring, that is, incorrect wiring of the generator excitation circuit, corresponds to the step of carefully checking the wiring and correcting the wrongly connected places, and this step corresponds to fault cause number ⑦ (incorrect wiring). The generator residual magnetism voltage and the rectifier output voltage having opposite polarity manifests as the residual magnetism voltage and the rectifier output voltage having opposite polarity, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to swap the connections of the excitation winding.

Short circuit of the resonant capacitor is one of the fault causes of the generator voltage not being able to be established normally; for the resonant capacitor short circuit fault, the troubleshooting method is to replace the capacitor. The main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration, and the corresponding handling method is inspection and repair; inspection and repair performs detection and repair for faults of electrical equipment and components, covering mechanical mechanisms, winding insulation and contact components, etc., and is also used to solve the automatic tripping fault caused by the free tripping mechanism of the main switch failing to hold. The maintenance operation for faults such as soft breakdown, capacitance reduction, deterioration or damage of the capacitor is to replace the capacitor; this operation is also used to repair the intermittent rotation fault of the capacitor-type electric fan caused by soft breakdown of the capacitor, and to solve the slow speed problem of the pulsator washing machine caused by capacitance reduction, deterioration or loose wiring of the capacitor. Marine motors contain windings and brushes.

Similarly, an open circuit in one phase of the reactor, rectifier and phase compound excitation transformer will also cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; at this time it should be checked whether the wiring among the three is loose or broken, and after finding it, connect and tighten it to restore the circuit connection to normal. Too low generator speed is another possible cause; during handling the speed needs to be raised to the rated value and the frequency checked to confirm whether the frequency meets the requirements after the speed is raised. If the generator excitation winding has an open circuit, the terminal voltage will likewise be lower than the rated value; at this time the excitation winding should be checked, and after confirming the open circuit, repair or replace it. Changes in the taps of the reactor or phase compound excitation transformer will also cause low voltage; during troubleshooting the voltage needs to be checked and verified, and then the tap wiring redone. In addition, an error in the voltmeter will also make the reading low, thus manifesting as the generator voltage being lower than the rated value; this cause is listed as item 7 in the voltage-lower-than-rated-value fault table, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to calibrate the voltmeter.

There is a clear correspondence between the above causes and handling measures. Generator voltage lower than rated value corresponds to increasing the setting resistance, used to eliminate the influence of too small a setting resistance; generator voltage lower than rated value corresponds to raising the speed to the rated value and checking the frequency, used to solve the problem of too low speed; generator voltage lower than rated value corresponds to checking the excitation winding and repairing or replacing it, used to handle open circuit of the excitation winding; generator voltage lower than rated value corresponds to checking and verifying the voltage and redoing the tap wiring, used to eliminate tap changes; generator voltage lower than rated value corresponds to calibrating the voltmeter, used to eliminate the reading deviation caused by voltmeter error.

In contrast to low voltage, generator voltage higher than the rated value is also one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system. Too large an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor is the cause of the terminal voltage being higher than the rated value; during handling the air gap is reduced as required. The sliding contact of the setting resistance being burned out, rusted, in poor contact, or the resistance being burned through will likewise cause the generator voltage to be higher than the rated value; at this time the resistance should be checked and repaired or renewed. An error in the voltmeter may make the reading high, and the voltmeter should be calibrated. These correspondences show that generator voltage higher than the rated value corresponds respectively to reducing the air gap as required, checking and repairing or renewing the resistance, readjustment as required, and calibrating the voltmeter.

Besides voltage abnormality, generator overheating is also one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, and its fault causes and troubleshooting methods can refer to the relevant fault comparison data. Check the motor stator and rotor windings and repair the short-circuited windings; check whether the motor bearing, rotating shaft and rotor core are loose.

In the troubleshooting process, resistance and voltage are two basic parameters that need to be measured. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; if its air gap is too small, it will cause the generator terminal voltage to be lower than the rated value;

As far as the bearing itself is concerned, bearing damage will cause bearing overheating, and severe bearing wear will directly cause generator bearing overheating; as far as lubrication is concerned, insufficient lubricating oil, impurities, and too much, too little or deteriorated lubricating oil (grease) will all cause generator bearing overheating; as far as installation is concerned, improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover, poor assembly of the generator set, and bending of the generator rotating shaft will likewise cause generator bearing overheating. Marine motors contain bearings and rotating shafts, and both brushed synchronous generators and brushless synchronous generators also contain generator bearings and generator rotating shafts; the generator bearing undertakes the task of supporting the generator rotating shaft, and the maintenance and upkeep of the generator bearing is carried out precisely on the component of the generator bearing.

For bearing overheating, the troubleshooting work corresponds to three directions: checking the bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition and checking the installation condition. Checking the lubrication condition also uses the bearing, checking the amount and quality of the lubricating grease from the bearing; checking the installation condition focuses on the assembly state of the end cover, bearing cover and the unit as a whole. When severe bearing wear causes generator bearing overheating, the corresponding handling method is to replace the bearing; when improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover causes generator bearing overheating, the corresponding handling method is to reinstall it properly; when bending of the generator rotating shaft causes generator bearing overheating, the corresponding handling method is to straighten the rotating shaft. Among the above troubleshooting methods, replacing the bearing is used to eliminate the cause of severe bearing wear, while checking and adding oil or changing oil, reinstalling properly, realigning the installation, and straightening the rotating shaft correspond respectively to the situations of abnormal lubrication, improper assembly of the end cover or bearing cover, poor assembly of the unit, and bending of the rotating shaft.

Too much, too little or deteriorated lubricating oil is a common cause of bearing overheating; when adding oil, it must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space. Improper assembly of the motor end cover, poor assembly of the generator set or bending of the rotating shaft may all cause bearing overheating. Mutual friction between stator and rotor is also one of the potential causes of bearing overheating; at this time the looseness of the bearing and rotating shaft needs to be checked, and the rotor core checked as well. Severe wear of the generator bearing will cause bearing overheating and needs to be handled by replacing the bearing. Bending of the generator rotating shaft is one of the fault causes of bearing overheating, and the handling method is to straighten the rotating shaft.

From the perspective of judging the amount of wear, when the inner diameter of the rolling bearing is 20–59 mm, the allowable wear value is about 10 times the original clearance; the clearance of a new bearing is 0.01–0.02 mm, and the maximum allowable wear value can reach 0.15–0.25 mm. When wear of the rolling bearing causes too large a clearance, it manifests as loud rotation noise, wobbling of the outer ring, or the balls striking the outer ring and making noise. If the noise disappears during no-load operation, it indicates poor installation of the coupling; if the noise still exists and is accompanied by vibration, it points to a shaft or bearing fault. The maintenance procedure of replacing the bearing, besides being used for the overheating problem of the generator caused by severe bearing wear, is also applicable to bearing wear or damage faults in equipment such as electric fans, electric drills and generators, and can be used to repair the slow starting and reduced speed of electric fans caused by bearing wear, and to eliminate the noise generated during operation of electric fans due to bearing damage.

As the heart of the ship's power system, the reliability and survivability of the ship's power station are important signs of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks. The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the ship's power station; its functions include connecting or disconnecting circuits, issuing alarms when protective devices operate, detecting and displaying various electrical parameters, and being able to regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active power and reactive power of parallel-operating generator sets. The main switchboard is equipped with common electrical apparatus such as circuit breakers, changeover switches, excitation rheostats, reverse power relays and various measuring instruments. The lighting distribution panel is also equipped with a network insulation detection device, such as earth lamps and a switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The operation of switching to shore power is also carried out on the main switchboard, which is provided with a shore power switch and an indicator lamp indicating that the shore power box has been closed.

In the measurement and detection link, the multimeter contains a changeover switch; the function of the changeover switch is to select the measurement object and select the range, it is used to set the working state, select the measurement point or issue operating commands, it has relatively many selection positions and contacts, and on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. If there is a capacitor in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on.

The clamp-on ammeter contains a current transformer; the current transformer is used to transform the current ratio, has the nature of a current source, the standard secondary current is usually 5 A, its symbol is TA, the primary terminals are denoted by L1 and L2, the secondary by K1 and K2, and when working it is equivalent to a short-circuit transformer; during operation the secondary winding must never be open-circuited, and one end of the secondary side is earthed. The through-type current transformer is one type of current transformer; current transformers also include coil-type and busbar-type types. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA, is used inside the circuit breaker to provide current detection sampling, and the nameplate indicates the reference current I0 and the current ratio ITA; the current ratio is selected according to the rated current, for example, when the generator rated current is 720 A, the TA specification may be 800/5 A. The load current I flowing through the primary side of the current transformer is transformed into a secondary current connected to an AC ammeter or other series current element; its secondary side must never be open-circuited, the external ammeter terminals need a short-circuit connecting piece, and it can only be removed after the wiring has been checked.

The insulation resistance tester, also called the megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is a portable instrument used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables, often adopts the ratio meter structure, and is divided according to the highest voltage emitted by the hand-cranked generator into specifications such as 100 V, 200 V, 500 V, 1000 V and 2500 V, with terminal posts L, E and G. The wattmeter, also called the watt meter, is composed of a current coil and a voltage coil, is used to measure electrical power, and calculates power by detecting the load current and voltage. The current coil of the wattmeter is connected in series between the power source and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test to detect the voltage; the current coil and voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals (such as "*"), and during measurement the currents of the two coils must flow in from these terminals or out from them at the same time.

The circuit breaker is a switching apparatus used in the ship's power system to protect circuits, belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus, is divided into frame type (air type) and molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the network. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker itself. The main switch is used to control the connection between the generator and the network; it is the air circuit breaker in the ship's power station that connects and disconnects the generator and the main busbar, has both switching and protection functions, can automatically disconnect the generator from the network when the network has a short circuit or the generator has undervoltage, and needs performance verification of undervoltage, overload, short circuit, reverse power, etc. every 4–5 years. The main switch is mainly composed of the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device and arc extinguishing device, etc., and also includes auxiliary contacts and the control and signal indication circuit. The undervoltage release is one of the main components of the generator main switch, together with the shunt release, overcurrent protection device, etc. constitutes the main switch, exists as a standard configuration component in the DW14 type circuit breaker, and is used to realize the undervoltage protection function. The shunt release is one of the main components of the generator main switch, together with the undervoltage release, overcurrent protection device, etc. belongs to the main switch components, and is used for shunt control.
