The overcurrent protection device is one of the main components of the generator main switch; in the DW14 type circuit breaker it specifically appears as the AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, is set with the generator rated current as the reference value, is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker, has long-time delay, short-time delay and instantaneous tripping functions, and is provided with three operating current setting knobs and two delay time setting knobs. The arc extinguishing device is one of the main components of the generator main switch, together with the undervoltage release, shunt release, etc. constitutes the main switch, serves the coordinated work of completing the connection and disconnection between the generator and the main busbar, and is used to extinguish the arc when the switch is connected and disconnected. The auxiliary contact is one of the main components of the generator main switch, used for control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection; in motor forward rotation control the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize the self-locking of the contactor coil, and through the on-off state controls the lighting and extinguishing of the operation indicator lamp to display the equipment working state.

The control and signal indication circuit is one of the main component parts of the generator main switch, and together with the undervoltage, shunt, overcurrent protection and arc extinguishing device it forms the main switch, existing as a component part in main switches commonly used on ships such as the DW14-type circuit breaker.

The trip unit is a component part of ship electrical equipment; in a circuit breaker it is used to realize protection functions such as overload, short circuit and undervoltage and to drive the contacts to open. The undervoltage protection of a ship generator is realized by the undervoltage trip unit in the circuit breaker, and the generator external short circuit protection is also realized by the overcurrent trip unit in the circuit breaker. The AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, as an overcurrent protection device, is one of the component parts of the generator main switch and is usually additionally installed on the DW14-type circuit breaker; its operation setting takes the generator rated current as the reference value, and its physical installation position is on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker. The DW14-type circuit breaker is produced by introducing the technology of the AH-type and AS-type circuit breakers of Japan's Terasaki company and is widely used in domestic ships; when used as a generator main switch it is additionally fitted with the AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, whose overcurrent trip unit takes the generator rated current as the reference value and is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker.

The reverse power relay is one of the control and protection apparatuses commonly used on the ship main switchboard, used to detect the reverse power of the AC generator and trigger protection action; the setting value for the diesel engine prime mover is 8%~15% of rated power, with a delay of 3~10s before action, and the starting value of the moving contact of the GG-21-type induction relay differs from the actual contact value. Failure of the reverse power relay will cause the AC generator to produce a reverse power phenomenon; one of its causes is that wiring was not carried out as required, and the troubleshooting method for incorrect wiring is to change to correct wiring; the second cause is that the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out; once the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, the reverse power relay ceases to function, and it is precisely because the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out and the reverse power relay ceases to function that the reverse power relay fails; the troubleshooting method for a burnt-out coil is to check and replace the coil.

The generator main switch failing to close (excluding electric closing) is one of the common faults. Failure of the undervoltage release to pull in normally will cause the generator main switch to fail to close, specifically manifested as the undervoltage release coil being open-circuited, wiring being loose, or abnormal tension of the reaction spring causing failure to pull in; serious wear of the tripping mechanism so that it cannot catch will also cause the generator main switch to fail to close, and the bolt must be adjusted or the part replaced; maladjustment of the overcurrent or electromagnetic trip unit (i.e. the action value being too small) will hinder closing, and it must be corrected and adjusted to the required value; the thermal trip unit not being reset after action will likewise cause failure to close, in which case one should wait 1~2s for the thermal element to reset, and this handling measure is precisely the corresponding treatment method for the fault of the generator main switch failing to close. During troubleshooting, first detect whether the voltage across the undervoltage coil is normal; if normal, check whether the coil is open-circuited, whether the terminal posts are loose, whether the tension of the trip unit reaction spring is normal, and whether the mechanical mechanism is jammed; if the coil voltage is abnormal, the undervoltage coil circuit should be detected and the series resistor checked. If the voltage across the undervoltage coil is normal but it cannot pull in, check whether the mechanical mechanism is jammed; if the voltage across the undervoltage coil is abnormal, detect the circuit and check the series resistor. For problems of the tripping mechanism, check the tripping mechanism and adjust the corresponding bolt or renew it.

No voltage on the network after the main switch closes is also a common fault. A burnt-out main contact or non-contact between moving and fixed contacts will cause no voltage on the network after the main switch closes, and the troubleshooting method for a burnt-out main contact is to check, repair or replace the main contact; the moving contact being loose or the wire being broken will also cause no voltage on the network after the main switch closes, and the troubleshooting method for a loose moving contact is to check the wiring and connections and connect them properly or tighten the screws.

Tripping during use after the main switch closes likewise belongs to the common faults. If the armature of the undervoltage trip unit cannot catch the tripping shaft, tripping will occur, and the tripping mechanism must be checked; if the tripping mechanism is aged and cannot catch, tripping will occur, and the tripping mechanism must be checked and the corresponding bolt adjusted or renewed; if the series resistance of the undervoltage coil is too large, tripping will occur, and it is necessary to check whether the resistor and wiring are in good condition; if the reaction spring force of the undervoltage release is too large, tripping will occur, and the spring tension must be checked; if the load suddenly increases so that undervoltage acts, tripping will occur, and the voltage regulator or governor must be checked, or the spring tension reduced; if the delay of the overload relay is too small or there is no delay action, tripping will also occur.

In the fault where the main switch is liable to trip automatically due to hull vibration, a resistance value of the undervoltage coil that is too large causing weak electromagnetic attraction, or a core reaction spring force that is too large so that the core does not pull in firmly, will cause this phenomenon, and troubleshooting should be carried out by increasing the electromagnetic attraction or reducing the spring reaction force; if the free tripping mechanism cannot catch, this phenomenon will occur, and it must be checked and repaired; if the overcurrent trip unit is maladjusted, the action current value is too low, and it is already close to the action value at normal load current, this phenomenon will occur, and the overcurrent trip unit should be adjusted to correct the action current value.

Motor overload refers to the fault state in which the motor running current or power exceeds the rated value; in a DC motor it causes difficult commutation and excessive sparking, and in a generator it triggers overload protection; when a DC motor is overloaded the current per unit area of the brush is large, causing difficult commutation and resulting in excessive sparking under brush; when the output power or current of a generator exceeds its rated value it is defined as overload. During single-unit operation, starting a large load such as an air compressor, or starting a large load without observing the power, easily causes the generator to trip due to overload; during parallel operation, if one unit trips due to a fault and stepped unloading fails, the remaining units may trip due to overload. Generator overload protection action often occurs during single-unit operation with a large load, when large equipment such as an air compressor or ballast pump is started without observing the power; during parallel operation, if stepped unloading fails or overload still exists after unloading, the protection of the running unit will trip; it may also be caused by another unit tripping immediately due to a motor fault, causing the remaining unit to overload. Generator undervoltage protection action mainly occurs in cases where the governor and fuel system or the voltage regulator is faulty; when caused by a governor and fuel system fault, the speed first drops and then tripping occurs, and whether the speed has dropped can be judged from the sound of the diesel engine to confirm tripping caused by a governor fault; when caused by a voltage regulator fault, the voltage first drops and then tripping occurs, and whether the voltage has dropped can be judged from the change in brightness of the lighting lamps to confirm tripping caused by a voltage regulator fault.

The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy of the ship's power station; the ship's power station includes the main switchboard, the ship's network and the shore power box, and also includes brushed synchronous generators, brushless synchronous generators as well as uncontrollable phase-compounding voltage regulation systems, controllable phase-compounding voltage regulation systems, thyristor excitation voltage regulation systems, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation systems and DW14-type circuit breakers. The main switchboard includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter; its main functions include connecting or disconnecting circuits, protection device action and alarming, detecting and displaying various electrical parameters, and it can also regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station and the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel. When changing over to shore power, the shore power switch must be closed immediately after disconnecting the generator main switch.

The fuse corresponds to the symbol FU in circuit diagrams and is a safety apparatus; when overload or short circuit occurs in the network or electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; it belongs to distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs, and has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. The RL93 series is of the screw type, with a voltage of 380V and a current of 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection.

The ship's network belongs to the ship's power station and usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system; single-phase earthing at any one point is an abnormal state, and if another phase is earthed a short circuit is formed; after one-point earthing occurs, electrical equipment can still operate normally, but it must be eliminated in time to improve reliability, and the earthed line and fault point can be found by means of the earth lamps on the switchboard or the section-by-section narrowing method. A network insulation detection device is installed on the lighting distribution panel of the main switchboard; insulation measurement must be carried out with the network energized, and a portable insulation resistance tester must not be used. Earthing faults of the ship's network mostly occur in the lighting network, and the search order is from the accommodation area to the navigation and communication equipment of the wheelhouse.

The switchboard-type insulation resistance meter is used to measure the insulation resistance of the network, is installed on the lighting panel of the main switchboard, consists of a meter head and a rectifier power supply, and is used for live measurement of the insulation resistance to earth of the power and lighting networks.

Structurally it consists of two parts, the measuring mechanism (meter head) and the auxiliary device (rectifier power supply), and through the changeover switch it can separately measure the insulation resistance of the 380V/440V power network and the 220V/110V lighting network. Its working principle is based on the magnitude of the leakage current: the lower the insulation resistance, the larger the leakage current and the larger the deflection angle of the meter head pointer; when a one-phase earthing fault occurs, the meter head pointer deflects the most, indicating an insulation resistance value of "0". Measurement must be carried out with the ship's network energized, and it is strictly forbidden to use a portable insulation resistance tester as a substitute. It is often used to find earthing faults in the lighting network, locating the fault point by pulling off the distribution switches one by one and observing whether the reading recovers. The meter head serves as the measuring mechanism in the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter; the larger the leakage current, the larger the pointer deflection; its type is a high-sensitivity moving-coil instrument, and the number of scales is 4-6.

The multimeter includes a meter head and a changeover switch, and the multimeter uses resistance, voltage, current and capacitance. The meter head is the core measuring component of the multimeter, adopting a high-sensitivity moving-coil instrument with a full-scale current in the microampere range; it is one of the three major component parts of the basic structure of the multimeter (the other two parts being the changeover switch and the measuring circuit), and a high-sensitivity moving-coil instrument is usually adopted as the measuring mechanism. The function of capacitance is charging and discharging; the measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and polarity (electrolytic capacitors); it is a component formed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in between, with the characteristic of blocking direct current and passing alternating current, and is usually represented in circuit diagrams by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; the hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC).

Generator reverse power protection action is manifested as generator reverse power protection tripping: improper grasp of the closing moment during paralleling operation causes the main switch of the incoming set to trip after closing; during parallel operation, adjusting the load distribution in the reverse direction causes reverse power protection tripping; during paralleling, damage to the governor or interruption of fuel of one of the diesel engines causes reverse power tripping; improper paralleling operation causing the generator current to reach 250A can be misjudged as an external short circuit fault, and the generator main switch trips because reverse power triggers protection. Generator external short circuit fault refers to the main switch tripping when the generator current is greater than or equal to 2IN; the criterion is the generator external short circuit protection action threshold required by the regulations: the main switch trips when current ≥2I_N; in an automatic power station management system, if the main switch trips and there is no other reaction in the engine room and only a short circuit fault is reported, this fault can be determined; in a conventional power station, excluding large load starting, cargo handling operations and the case of tripping after speed/voltage reduction first, this fault can be concluded to have occurred; improper paralleling operation causing the generator current to reach 250 (unit not explicitly stated, suspected to be amperes or multiples) may also cause similar tripping.

Improper operation refers to faults caused by improper operation; the common ones are: ① improper closing operation; ② unbalanced generator load control; ③ improper operation caused by observation errors. During paralleling operation, improper grasp of the closing moment or adjusting the load distribution in the reverse direction can cause generator reverse power protection tripping.

Lighting network earthing fault refers to low insulation resistance or earthing of the lighting network; earthing faults of the ship's network mostly occur in the lighting network; the switchboard insulation resistance meter indicating "0" is the direct basis for judging a lighting network earthing fault; the search order by pulling area switches is: crew accommodation area—deck lighting area—engine room lighting area—wheelhouse navigation and communication equipment; in front of the main switchboard, pull off the lighting distribution switches one by one and observe whether the insulation resistance meter returns to normal to locate the faulty circuit; in front of the distribution box, use a portable insulation resistance tester to measure the insulation to earth of the branch circuits of the secondary distribution network; when finding the specific earthing point, disconnect from the intermediate junction box to determine which small area (such as a room) is earthed. The lighting network earthing fault corresponds to the search procedure for lighting network earthing faults, whose steps are: first turn on the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter to measure the lighting network, and the insulation resistance meter indicates an insulation resistance value of "0" at this time; after finding the distribution switch where the earthing fault occurs, cut off the power supply of that circuit and check the insulation resistance meter indication again to verify the fault point; after determining the earthed branch, pull off the distribution switch of that circuit and close the remaining switches, and restore the power supply of that circuit at the main switchboard. When searching for a lighting network earthing fault, disconnect from the intermediate junction box to determine the small earthed area; if the earthing point still cannot be found after checking the lamp holders etc., the cable between the junction box and the electrical appliance should be checked.

The junction box is a component used in ship electrical systems to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical elements; the general alarm device includes a junction box, and the general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box etc.; the solenoid valve of the paint store zone is not connected to the external junction box but is connected directly into the local control box.

The shore power box is used to connect shore power and is usually located on the main deck level, receiving power supply from the onshore power source through a cable; it is generally equipped with a shore power indicator lamp, a circuit breaker (or a switch plus fuse) and shore power terminal posts, is provided with a phase sequence indicator lamp (or negative sequence relay) to detect the consistency of the phase sequence of shore power and ship power, and is marked with a nameplate indicating the rated voltage and rated frequency of the ship power; when the shore power is a three-phase four-wire system, the neutral line must be connected to the terminal post on the shore power box that is connected to the hull; if a negative sequence relay is used, when the phase sequence is inconsistent the shore power box switch will trip as soon as it is closed. Precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the ship's power station: when connecting shore power, the type of current of the shore power and the ship power must be kept consistent, and the rated frequency and rated voltage of the shore power should be consistent with the ship power parameters; for three-phase four-wire shore power, the neutral line must first be connected to the hull terminal post before connection can be made; only when the phase sequence of the shore power is consistent with that of the ship power can changeover be carried out at the main switchboard; during the period of connecting shore power, it is strictly forbidden to close the ship's generator, and the two must not supply power at the same time.

The generator main switch failing to close refers to a type of fault in which, after excluding the electric closing function, the switch still cannot complete the closing action. There are many causes of this phenomenon, among which failure of the undervoltage release to pull in normally is one of the common causes. If the coil voltage is normal, it is necessary to check whether the coil is open-circuited and whether the terminal posts are loose, and at the same time check whether the tension of the trip unit reaction spring is normal and whether the mechanical mechanism is jammed. If the voltage across the undervoltage coil is abnormal, the undervoltage coil circuit should be detected and the resistor connected in series in that circuit should be checked.

Besides failure of the undervoltage release to pull in normally, serious wear of the tripping mechanism so that it cannot catch will likewise cause the generator main switch to fail to close. At this time the tripping mechanism cannot catch reliably due to wear, and the maintenance procedure corresponding to the generator main switch failing to close is to check the tripping mechanism and adjust the corresponding bolt or renew it, that is, check the tripping mechanism and adjust the corresponding bolt or replace it with a new part. The thermal trip unit not being reset after action is also one of the causes of the generator main switch failing to close, and during handling one must wait 1~2s for the thermal element to reset. Among the above causes, serious wear of the tripping mechanism so that it cannot catch corresponds to checking the tripping mechanism and adjusting the corresponding bolt or renewing it; the moving contact being loose or the wire being broken will likewise cause no voltage on the network after the main switch closes, and during troubleshooting the wiring and connections should be checked and the wiring connected properly or the screws tightened. That is to say, no voltage on the network after the main switch closes corresponds to two maintenance procedures: first, check, repair or replace the main contact; second, check the wiring and connections and connect them properly or tighten the screws.

Tripping during use after the main switch closes is also related to the state of the trip unit. At the same time, this fault also corresponds to the maintenance procedure of checking the tripping mechanism. The main switch is a combination of the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device, arc extinguishing device, auxiliary contacts and the control and signal indication circuit. The main switchboard includes the main switch. The DW14-type circuit breaker introduces Japanese Terasaki technology and is additionally fitted with the AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit; this trip unit is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker and has long-time delay, short-time delay, instantaneous tripping and trip pre-alarm functions.

If the voltage coil in the reverse power relay is burnt out, the relay will cease to function. The wattmeter includes a voltage coil, which is used to detect the voltage across the measured circuit, and a series additional resistor is connected in its branch, which is connected in parallel across the measured circuit; the voltage range of the wattmeter is realized precisely by connecting additional resistors of different resistance values in series with the voltage coil. A coil is an electrical component made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. The contactor includes a coil and main contacts; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; failure or deficiency of the contactor armature reaction spring will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed, and during handling the reaction spring must be replaced or adjusted, but care must be taken that the reaction force is not too large. The main contact is the switching component in the contactor used to connect or disconnect the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor; a copper main contact that has discolored or gives off a burnt smell indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel must be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the main contact has been overheated for a long time or has welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected as a replacement.

The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and their relative positions must be checked for accuracy.

Resistance is a quantity whose value can be measured, and the measuring tool is the multimeter. When measuring resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the measured resistance must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; in the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open circuit in the shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action. Voltage is a quantity whose value can be measured, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; current is a quantity whose value can be measured, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; the multimeter is used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

Tripping of the main switch during closing and use is a common type of fault in the distribution equipment of a ship's power station, and its causes involve multiple links such as the tripping mechanism, the coil circuit and the protection settings. Aging of the tripping mechanism, which fails to hold, will likewise cause tripping of the main switch during closing and use; the troubleshooting method is to check the specific condition of the tripping mechanism, and the corrective measures include adjusting the corresponding bolts or replacing with new parts. Tripping of the main switch during closing and use also corresponds to the corrective approach of checking the tripping mechanism and adjusting the corresponding bolts or replacing with new parts, that is, inspecting the mechanical tripping part item by item, adjusting the bolts as the wear and fit conditions require, and replacing with new parts when necessary. When the main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration and the cause is that the free tripping mechanism fails to hold, inspection and repair are also required. The above two causes relating to the tripping mechanism are listed in the fault table respectively as cause item ① and another cause, and their common feature is failure of holding, the difference being that the former occurs between the armature of the undervoltage trip unit and the tripping shaft, while the latter is caused by aging of the tripping mechanism itself.

Improper setting of the protective devices will also cause tripping. In the troubleshooting table, this corresponds to the troubleshooting method of adjusting the overcurrent trip unit, but the wording "correct and adjust to the required value" is not directly used. Too small a delay or no delay action of the overload relay will likewise cause tripping of the main switch during closing and use; the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and adjust to the specified delay value, and the core of the operation is to correct the delay parameter of the overload relay to the specified value. In addition, when the operating value of the overcurrent or electromagnetic trip unit is too small, this also needs to be handled by correcting and adjusting to the required value in the generator main switch failure to close fault.

Abnormality of the circuit related to the undervoltage trip unit is another important type of cause. Too large a series resistance of the undervoltage coil will cause tripping of the main switch during closing and use; the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check whether the series resistor and the wiring are in good condition, and the objects involved are the undervoltage coil and its series resistor. Tripping of the main switch during closing and use also corresponds to the corrective measure of checking and reducing the spring tension, that is, by checking the spring tension condition and appropriately reducing it so that the trip unit operating value returns to the normal range. A sudden increase in load, causing undervoltage operation, will likewise cause tripping of the main switch during closing and use; the troubleshooting method includes checking whether the characteristics of the voltage regulator and the governor are normal, and the alternative or auxiliary measure is to reduce the reaction spring tension of the undervoltage trip unit; by checking the characteristics of the voltage regulator and the governor, or reducing the spring tension of the undervoltage trip unit, the problem of nuisance tripping caused by voltage sag due to load fluctuation can be solved. When the generator main switch fails to close, it is necessary to check whether the reaction spring tension of the undervoltage trip unit is normal; the main switch is a component of the main switchboard, used to control the connection between the generator and the power grid, and can automatically disconnect the generator from the power grid when the power grid has a short circuit or the generator is undervoltage, and every 4 to 5 years the undervoltage, overload, short circuit, reverse power and other functions need to be verified.

Measurement and component inspection related to troubleshooting of tripping faults must likewise not be neglected. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil's magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; a stuck armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start; failure or deficiency of the armature reaction spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed. The reaction spring is the spring component in contactors and circuit breakers, used to provide release force or reset force; when handling a contactor release fault, the reaction spring needs to be replaced or adjusted, but care must be taken that the reaction force is not too large.

The fault symptom that the main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration is not uncommon in the operation of ship power stations.

The cause of this phenomenon is not single; too large a resistance value of the undervoltage coil, resulting in weak electromagnetic attraction, or too large a reaction spring force of the core, so that the core does not pull in firmly, is one of the direct causes. Specifically, too large a resistance value of the undervoltage coil will make the electromagnetic attraction weaker; or too large a reaction spring force of the core, both of which will make the core not pull in firmly, so that the main switch loses its hold under hull vibration and trips. For this cause, troubleshooting should increase the electromagnetic attraction or reduce the spring reaction force. Another cause is that the free tripping mechanism fails to hold, that is, the free tripping mechanism cannot maintain the locked state, and for this inspection and repair should be carried out. The third cause is misadjustment of the overcurrent trip unit, with too low an operating current value, already close to the operating value at normal load current, manifested as failure of the overcurrent trip unit, whose feature is that the operating current value is too low and already close to the operating value at normal load current, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to adjust the overcurrent trip unit. All three causes above will cause the main switch to be prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration, and the handling respectively corresponds to increasing the electromagnetic attraction or reducing the spring reaction force, inspection and repair, and adjusting the overcurrent trip unit.

Among the components of the main switch, the trip unit is one of the key parts. The wattmeter contains a voltage coil, which is used to detect the voltage across the measured circuit, and its branch is connected in series with an additional resistor and connected in parallel into the circuit. The core in electromagnetic equipment is the magnetic conductive component, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as the reference point for insulation measurement. The contactor contains a core and a coil. When measuring the insulation resistance of an electrical equipment coil to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core. In the through-type current transformer, the measured large-current conductor is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding.

Resistance, voltage and current are the basic electrical quantities that need to be measured in fault diagnosis. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter. Voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis. The generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree. Overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems. The measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems.

When the generator voltage cannot be built up normally, the corresponding troubleshooting and maintenance procedures include several items. An external power source (DC) can be used for magnetization to build up voltage; check whether there is looseness or a broken wire from the rectifier to the excitation winding, this step being aimed at the cause of excitation winding open circuit; polish the surface of the collector ring with fine sandpaper, used to solve the faults of generator voltage not adjustable and generator not conducting; check and repair the brush, brush holder and brush braid, aimed at the fault of the brush sticking in the brush holder or the brush braid being broken; adjust the air gap to an appropriate size, aimed at the fault of the linear reactor having no air gap or too small an air gap; check and replace the broken-down rectifier element, aimed at the fault of the voltage regulator rectifier element being broken down or open-circuited; carefully check the wiring and correct the wrongly connected places, aimed at the cause of incorrect wiring; swap the connections of the excitation winding, aimed at the fault of the generator residual magnetism voltage being opposite in polarity to the rectifier output voltage; check the wiring and reconnect it properly, aimed at the fault of broken connections among the reactor, the resonance capacitor and the phase compound excitation transformer; replace the capacitor, aimed at faults such as soft breakdown, reduced capacitance, deterioration or short circuit of the capacitor, and also used to repair the fault of a capacitive electric fan turning sometimes and not turning sometimes caused by soft breakdown of the capacitor, as well as to solve the problem of slow speed of a pulsator washing machine caused by reduced capacitance, deterioration or loose wiring of the capacitor.

When the generator voltage is lower than the rated value, the corresponding handling steps include: adjust to increase the air gap, aimed at the fault of the generator voltage being lower than the rated value caused by too small an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor; check whether the wiring among the three is loose or broken, and after finding it, connect and fasten it, aimed at the fault of one phase of the reactor, rectifier and phase compound excitation transformer being open-circuited; increase the setting resistance; raise the speed to the rated value and check the frequency, aimed at the cause of too low a speed; check the excitation winding, repair or replace it, aimed at the fault of the generator excitation winding being open-circuited; check and verify the voltage, and reconnect the taps, aimed at the cause of tap changes of the reactor or phase compound excitation transformer; calibrate the voltmeter, performed when the voltmeter has an error causing the displayed voltage to be low. When the generator voltage is higher than the rated value, the corresponding handling steps include: reduce the air gap as required, aimed at the fault of the generator voltage being higher than the rated value caused by too large an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor; check and repair or renew the resistor, aimed at the fault of the sliding contact of the setting resistor being burnt, rusted, in poor contact, or the resistor being burnt out.

When an AC generator produces a reverse power phenomenon, it is often directly related to the fault symptom of the reverse power relay failing. There are two causes of the reverse power relay failing: first, the wiring is not as required; second, the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, so that the reverse power relay does not act. Wiring not as required means the wiring mode does not meet the specification requirements, which will directly cause the reverse power relay to fail; for this cause, the troubleshooting method is to change to correct wiring, that is, to correct the wiring that does not meet the requirements. Burning out of the voltage coil or current coil is manifested as the reverse power relay not acting, and its root cause is that the voltage coil or current coil inside the relay is burnt out; for this cause, the troubleshooting method is to check and replace the coil, that is, first check the coil and replace it after confirming it is burnt out.

During the inspection process, instruments are needed to measure voltage and current. Voltage is a measurable quantity, and its value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter; current is likewise a measurable quantity, and can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. The clamp-on ammeter is used to detect current without breaking the circuit. The multimeter is used both to measure voltage and to measure current, and is a common tool for judging whether a coil is burnt out.

The wattmeter internally contains a current coil and a voltage coil. The function of the current coil is to detect current; it is connected in series between the power source and the load, and is used to detect the current of the measured circuit; the current coil and the voltage coil are respectively marked with corresponding terminals, for example the end marked with "*", and during measurement the current must flow in or out from that end at the same time. Failure of the reverse power relay may be caused by burning out of the current coil, in which case the coil needs to be checked and replaced; when the contactor fails to pick up and the coil is open-circuited, the resistance is measured with the power off to determine the open circuit, and then the coil needs to be replaced; when the contactor coil overheats due to internal partial short circuit, it is judged by the resistance comparison method and then the coil also needs to be replaced. Coil short circuit corresponds to the maintenance procedure of replacing the coil. When the reverse power relay fails due to burning out of the voltage coil or current coil, the step of replacing the coil needs to be carried out after inspection.

The content of observation covers abnormal phenomena, part condition, conductor condition and equipment operating parameters, specifically including whether parts are stuck or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. After observation, the monitoring and indicating device should be further checked, and the nature and scope of the fault judged from the instrument readings.

In the monitoring and indicating device, voltage and current are the two most basic measurable properties. The voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter, and the current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. The multimeter is used both to measure voltage and to measure current; the clamp-on ammeter is specially used to measure current without breaking the circuit. When measuring current, if an ammeter is used, the circuit must be broken and the ammeter connected in series. As far as parallel operation is concerned, the voltage difference and current distribution between two units are often precisely the important basis for judging whether the synchronization conditions are met and whether the load is balanced, so when reading these values, they should be recorded together with the parallel state at that time.

Power measurement relies on the wattmeter, also called the watt meter, whose function is to measure electric power. The wattmeter consists of a current coil and a voltage coil; the current coil is connected in series between the power source and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the measured circuit to detect the voltage, and the power is calculated by detecting the load current and voltage. The current coil and the voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals, for example marked with "*", and during measurement the currents of the two coils must flow in or out from that end at the same time. If the corresponding terminals are connected in reverse during wiring, the reading direction of the wattmeter will deviate, so in the active power measurement of parallel operating units, the marking of the corresponding terminals should be checked before wiring to confirm that the connection directions of the current coil and the voltage coil are consistent.

The ship power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks; its basic duties include ensuring reliable power supply and safe operation, and promptly eliminating faults after they occur. The ship power station includes the main switchboard, the ship power grid and the shore power box, and also includes brushed synchronous generators and brushless synchronous generators, as well as different types of excitation and voltage regulation devices such as the uncontrolled phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, the controlled phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, the thyristor excitation voltage regulation system and the brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system. The ship power station also includes the DW14 circuit breaker, which was introduced from Japanese Terasaki technology and is provided with an AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit. The ship power grid is a component of the ship power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the relevant operating requirements of the ship power station. Fault handling for parallel operation is carried out around the above parts; whether it is the generator proper, the excitation and voltage regulation system, or the circuit breaker and power grid links, all may become sources of abnormal phenomena.

The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the power station, with the functions of circuit making and breaking, protection and alarm, parameter detection and power regulation; its main functions include connecting or disconnecting circuits, protection device action and alarm, detection and display of various electrical parameters, and it can regulate the voltage, frequency and the active and reactive power of parallel operating generator sets. The main switchboard includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The main switch is used to control the connection between the generator and the power grid; in the ship power station it is the air circuit breaker used to connect and disconnect the generator and the main busbar, having both switching and protection functions, and is mainly composed of the undervoltage release, the shunt release, the overcurrent protection device and the arc extinguishing device, etc., and is additionally provided with auxiliary contacts and a control and signal indication circuit. The main switch belongs to the undervoltage release, belongs to the shunt release, belongs to the overcurrent protection device, belongs to the arc extinguishing device, belongs to the auxiliary contacts, and also belongs to the control and signal indication circuit. In parallel operation, the closing and opening timing of the main switch is directly related to whether the unit can be smoothly connected to the power grid; its undervoltage release acts when the power grid loses voltage, the shunt release is used for remote disconnection, the overcurrent protection device cuts off the circuit when the current exceeds the setting value, the arc extinguishing device is responsible for extinguishing the arc generated during the breaking process, and the auxiliary contacts and the control and signal indication circuit feed back the position status of the main switch to the control panel for the operator to judge.

In terms of active power distribution during parallel operation, the manual speed control switch on the generator control panel is used to adjust the diesel engine servo motor. In the ship power station, the speed control switch adjusts the diesel engine governor servo motor through manual operation; adjusting this switch can change the diesel engine throttle opening, thereby realizing active power distribution among parallel operating units. The servo motor is used for active power distribution of parallel operating generator sets, realizing load transfer by changing the diesel engine throttle opening; the automatic oil-fired boiler also contains a servo motor, which is controlled by a bridge or regulator signal and drives a feedback potentiometer or throttle actuator by rotation to achieve automatic balance and position control; the speed control switch is also found in electric fans, and an electric fan contains a speed control switch used to adjust the fan speed; poor contact of the speed control switch will cause the fault of the electric fan turning sometimes and not turning sometimes, and damage to the speed control switch is one of the possible causes of the electric fan's failure to start. It can thus be seen that once a manual adjusting component such as the speed control switch has poor contact or is damaged, it will likewise cause failure of active power distribution in parallel operation, manifested as no response of load transfer during adjustment or uneven power distribution between the two units.

The selection of the parallel operation mode is related to the specific conditions of the marine power station. The manual synchronization method is suitable for small marine power stations where parallel operation is infrequent, or as a backup for the automatic method; the automatic quasi-synchronization method is suitable for marine power stations with a large number of parallel generator sets, high power and high requirements. A generator running on the grid should carry more than 50% of the rated load before another generator can be connected in parallel. When a generator is being disconnected from parallel operation, the speed control switches of the two sets must be adjusted in the same direction to transfer the active power. During the disconnection process, if the adjustment directions of the speed control switches of the two sets are inconsistent, the transfer of active power cannot be completed smoothly; therefore, during operation the same-direction adjustment should be maintained, and the wattmeter should be used to monitor the changes in active power of the two sets until the active power of the set to be disconnected drops to a level at which it can be broken, and then the main switch completes the disconnection from the grid.

In parallel operation, the even distribution of reactive power is usually achieved by means of a current stabilizing device, and the brushless synchronous generator adopts this method. The AC voltage equalizing connection method, also called the phase-shifting reactor voltage equalizing connection method, is suitable for parallel operation of generators of different capacities; through the phase-shifting reactors of the voltage regulators of the generators in parallel operation, better distribution of reactive load can be achieved with a smaller equalizing current. The phase-shifting reactor is a key element in the phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, used to regulate voltage and to achieve reactive load distribution of generators in parallel operation; in the uncontrollable phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, an open circuit of the phase-shifting reactor will cause the generator to fail to build up voltage, and if its air gap is too large, the terminal voltage of the generator will be higher than the rated value.

The DC equalizing line connecting contactor is controlled by the normally open auxiliary contact of the generator main switch. If the normally open auxiliary contact of the main switch has poor contact, it may cause parallel connection failure or grid tripping. When the generator is being connected in parallel, poor contact of the contacts of the equalizing line contactor will open the equalizing line, likewise causing parallel connection failure or grid tripping. Poor contact of contacts refers to an electrical fault state in which the conductive performance is degraded due to contamination, oxidation or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface; in a contactor, it is one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning; methods for dealing with poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface and tightening the contacts and the conductive plate. Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter at an electrical connection; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance, and further causing local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults.

A contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the marine power system, belonging to low-voltage control appliances, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, featuring high operating frequency and long life, and having the advantages of accurate and reliable operation and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, an iron core and a coil; the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. Auxiliary contacts are a component of the main switch, used for auxiliary control, and also for control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection; in the forward rotation control of a motor, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize self-locking of the contactor coil.

The marine power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrollable phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, controllable phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 circuit breaker, marine power grid and shore power box; the marine power grid belongs to the marine power station, and the main switchboard includes the main switch. The brushed synchronous generator includes an excitation system; the brushless synchronous generator is one of the main generator types used on ships, with its own rotating-armature exciter and rotating rectifier, without a brush and slip ring structure, and is listed together with the brushed synchronous generator as one of the two main generator forms currently used on ships, and internally includes the coaxially rotating main generator excitation winding, exciter armature winding and rotating rectifier device. The daily maintenance and upkeep of the generator applies to the brushless synchronous generator; the maintenance of the excitation system applies to the excitation system. The excitation system provides excitation current for the synchronous generator, including brushed, brushless and thyristor forms, and common forms include uncontrollable phase-compound excitation, controllable phase-compound excitation, thyristor excitation and brushless excitation voltage regulation systems; its maintenance cycle is once every half year, and the insulation resistance value is required to be not less than 1MΩ.

The wattmeter, also called the power meter, is used to measure electric power, is composed of a current coil and a voltage coil, and calculates power by detecting the load current and voltage. The wattmeter includes a current coil and a voltage coil; the multimeter uses voltage and current, and the clamp-on ammeter uses current. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. The measurable performance of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools include the multimeter and the voltmeter;

The text symbol corresponding to the fuse in circuit diagrams is FU, and its function is overload protection and short circuit protection; it is a protective appliance that, when overload or short circuit occurs in the grid or electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. The fuse belongs to distribution appliances and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs; the RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. A circuit breaker is a switching appliance used to protect circuits in the marine power system, belongs to low-voltage distribution appliances, is divided into frame type (air type) and molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and dynamic stability during a short circuit fault; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the grid.

The marine motor includes windings;

Setting principles of generator overload protection: when the output power or current of the generator exceeds its rated value, it is defined as motor overload. In the marine power station, motor overload is the direct cause that triggers the overload protection action, and its setting value must match the allowable heating characteristics of the generator. For a generator not equipped with an automatic step unloading device, when the current reaches 125%~135% of the rated current, the protection device should trip after a delay of 15~30s; for a generator equipped with an automatic step unloading device, since some non-important loads can be cut off first, its overload capacity is correspondingly increased, and when the current reaches 150% of the rated current, the protection device trips after a delay of 10~20s. The above two sets of values are the basic basis for adjusting the overload protection delay and operating current, and must not be changed arbitrarily during setting.

The actuating element of overload protection is the trip unit in the circuit breaker. The undervoltage protection of the marine generator is realized by the undervoltage release in the circuit breaker, and the external short circuit protection of the generator is realized by the overcurrent release in the circuit breaker. The main switch, as the air circuit breaker controlling the connection between the generator and the grid, is mainly composed of an undervoltage release, a shunt release, an overcurrent protection device, an arc extinguishing device, auxiliary contacts and a control and signal indication circuit. The DW14 circuit breaker introduces Japanese Terasaki technology, and its additional AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker; during adjustment, the installation position and adjustable parts of the trip unit should first be confirmed, and then the setting value should be determined according to the long-time delay trip current of the generator.

Setting of the priority trip overcurrent relay: the setting value of the operating current of the priority trip overcurrent relay is based on the long-time delay setting current of the generator overload protection. Its delay is usually set to less than 15s, for example 5~10s. This delay is shorter than the long-time delay of the generator overload protection, the purpose being to cut off some non-important loads before the generator reaches the tripping condition, avoiding the generator tripping due to overload.

The grading sequence of priority trip load shedding is clearly specified. The mooring winch is usually listed as the first-stage non-important load for priority trip shedding. The mooring winch belongs to the category of electric windlass deck machinery, is divided into DC and AC types, and its drive control scheme is generally the same as the control scheme of the ship's electric cargo winch; at present, AC three-speed windlasses, mooring winches or windlasses and mooring winches of the G-M system are mostly used, and the drive control systems of the two are basically the same. In the load shedding grading of priority trip on container ships, the refrigerated container power supply is usually listed as the second-stage load to be cut off, and the first stage is non-important loads such as machine repair tools and galley equipment. The electrical control system of refrigerated containers has developed from the relay type to the microcomputer control type; the temperature adjustment range inside the container is generally within ±30℃, with high constant-temperature accuracy, and it has functions such as electric heating, automatic unloading and automatic control of the number of condenser fans; when the temperature inside the container is lower than the setting value, electric heating can be carried out, and unloading operation can be carried out automatically according to the size of the heat load, and the number of condenser fans can be automatically controlled according to the external environment and the condenser pressure. The refrigerated container includes the work content of refrigerated container electrical control system maintenance, and its power supply is included in the second stage of priority trip, meaning that when the generator is overloaded, this load will be cut off before the loads after the first stage.

Setting of reverse power protection: the reverse power relay is used to detect and protect against reverse power and is one of the commonly used control and protection appliances on the marine main switchboard. The setting value for a diesel engine prime mover is 8%~15% of the rated power, with a delay of 3~10s before action. For the GG-21 induction type relay, the starting value of the moving contact differs from the actual contact value, and adjustment should be based on the actual contact value. The electronic relay has an action indicator lamp and a delayed output trip indication function, and the action state can be judged by means of the indicator lamp. One cause of reverse power relay failure is that the wiring is not carried out as required, and another cause is that the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, in which case the relay does not work. Therefore, before setting, it should be checked whether the wiring is correct and whether the voltage coil and current coil are intact.

Coordination of measuring instruments and transformers: voltage is a measurable performance, and its measuring tool is the multimeter or voltmeter. Current is likewise a measurable performance, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. The clamp-on ammeter includes a current transformer and can measure current without cutting off the circuit. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA, and its function is to transform the current ratio; the secondary side current is 5A, and the types include the coil type, busbar type and through-type; the through-type current transformer is one type of current transformer, characterized in that one end of the secondary side is earthed. The primary side terminals of the current transformer are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary side by K1 and K2; when working it is equivalent to a short-circuit transformer, and during operation the secondary winding must strictly not be open-circuited.

The wattmeter, also called the power meter, is composed of a current coil and a voltage coil, and its function is to measure electric power. The wattmeter includes a current coil and also includes a voltage coil. The current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test to detect the voltage, with an additional resistor connected in series in its branch. The function of the voltage coil is to detect voltage, and its connection mode is parallel. The current coil and voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals, and during measurement the currents of the two coils must flow in or out from these terminals at the same time. The voltage range of the wattmeter is realized by connecting additional resistors of different resistance values in series with the voltage coil. In the on-site adjustment of generator protection parameters, it is often necessary to use the above instruments to check the voltage and current readings to judge whether the setting values are appropriate.

Basic steps of fault diagnosis and circuit breaker maintenance: the conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, it should be checked whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. This step belongs to the sub-link of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged".

Circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. A circuit breaker is a switching appliance used to protect circuits in the marine power system, belongs to low-voltage distribution appliances, is divided into frame type and molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and dynamic stability during a short circuit fault. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the grid. A circuit breaker may have faults such as the contacts of the manually operated circuit breaker failing to close, the contacts of the electrically operated circuit breaker failing to close, one phase contact failing to close, and the shunt trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open. The trip unit is an electrical component in the circuit breaker used to realize protection functions such as overload, short circuit and undervoltage and to drive the contacts to open, and there is a close coordination relationship between the circuit breaker and the trip unit.

Inspection of related elements: the contactor includes a coil. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. The insulation resistance tester internally includes two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

The potentiometer is also called the potentiometer; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component, and it is generally considered to be manually adjustable. The potentiometer has three pins, of which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the other pins changes as the shaft rotates. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; the automatic fuel boiler includes a potentiometer, whose purpose is for bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R' driven by the motor M is balanced.

The marine power station is the heart of the marine power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving the specified tasks; its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply and safe operation, and promptly eliminating faults after they occur. The marine power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrollable phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, controllable phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 circuit breaker, marine power grid and shore power box. The main switchboard includes the main switch, and the main switch belongs to the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device, arc extinguishing device, auxiliary contacts and control and signal indication circuit. The marine power grid belongs to the marine power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the marine power station. When a DC motor is overloaded, the current per unit area of the brush is large, causing difficulty in commutation and resulting in excessive sparking under brush, that is, motor overload leads to excessive sparking under brush. During single-unit operation, starting a large load such as an air compressor, or starting a large load without observing the power, can easily cause the generator to trip due to overload. In the AC three-speed electric windlass, when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%, the current relay picks up. These phenomena are interrelated with the checking of setting values, and when adjusting protection parameters, the instrument readings and element status should be checked together.

Signal input and command output of the automatic control system of the main diesel generator set: the automatic control system of the main diesel generator set takes the controller as the core, and on its exterior there are input terminals numbered 1~17 and output terminals 18~32; these wiring terminals are metal contact parts connecting wires with equipment or circuit nodes, commonly found in PLC interfaces, instruments and control circuits. The electric main engine remote control system includes wiring terminals; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals is one of the common faults of electrical components, so the inspection of such terminals should be a fixed item of daily maintenance. The diesel generator set controller receives fault signals through input terminals of specific numbers, among which the overspeed fault signal is input from terminal 10 of the controller to execute immediate shutdown, the low lubricating oil pressure and high cooling water temperature faults correspond to input from terminals 13 and 14 respectively, and the automatic start command is input from terminal 2 of the controller, with the contact closed to connect to the negative pole of the power supply.

The input terminal is the electrical connection component in the PLC and controller used to receive external signals or power supply input. In the PLC equivalent circuit, the input terminal works together with the COM terminal to form the input circuit interface.

As for the output terminal, in the automatic control of the diesel generator set, output terminal 20 energizes and actuates the coil of the running-signal intermediate relay K₂; during automatic starting, output terminal 18 outputs the start command to energize the coil of the start-output intermediate relay K₃. The output terminal is the electrical interface component in the PLC and controller used to connect external loads or receive input signals; in the PLC equivalent circuit it is located between COM and the load, corresponding to the external contacts of output coils such as Y31-Y32. The harsh environment on board is likewise liable to cause the wiring heads and terminals to rust, resulting in poor contact, which requires timely cleaning. To judge whether the output terminal is normal, the continuity state between the terminal and COM can be measured after the corresponding command is issued; if the command has been issued but the load does not operate, the terminal contact problem should be ruled out first, and then the load itself should be checked.

The intermediate relay is used for control or protection in the ship's power system and is a type of electromagnetic relay; its construction is similar to that of the contactor, and it is used to expand contact capacity and the number of contact pairs and for control logic conversion; its fault analysis and treatment can be carried out by referring to the maintenance method of the contactor. In the automatic control of the diesel generator set, the K3 coil is energized and actuates to connect the starting solenoid valve, and the K4 coil is energized and actuates to connect the stopping solenoid valve. When checking the intermediate relay, it should be confirmed whether the specified voltage is present across the coil and whether the contacts can close and open reliably; burning of the coil or erosion of the contacts will prevent the start and stop commands from being transmitted to the solenoid valve. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel oil; at ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation circuit and fuel enters the nozzle for injection; the automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve, whose drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge; when servicing the solenoid valve, in addition to checking the coil, it should also be checked whether the freewheeling diode is broken down or open-circuited and whether the valve core moves flexibly.

Measuring instruments and fault detection: in the troubleshooting process, the multimeter is a commonly used tool; the multimeter contains a changeover switch and uses resistance and current for measurement. The changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measuring points or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts; on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measuring points, set the working state and issue operating commands, and its functions include selecting the measured object and selecting the range. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits to ensure that the secondary side of the current transformer is not left open; during operation it must not be left in the intermediate position, nor may the range be switched at will under load. The AC ammeter internally is a low-resistance current element, with two non-polarized terminals brought out externally; the connections may be interchanged, so polarity need not be distinguished when wiring, but reliable contact should be ensured.

The sensor is the information acquisition device of the ship's monitoring and control system and is divided into two major categories: analog and switching-value sensors. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the control platform contains sensors. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. The check of the sensor should be combined with its output signal: for analog sensors, the key is to verify whether the output electrical signal corresponds to the measured parameter; for switching-value sensors, the key is to verify whether the actuating value is within the specified range.

Monitoring and treatment of power supply faults: the overspeed controller is powered by the battery; when K6 detects a power failure, it sends a power supply fault signal to the system. A power supply fault will cause the RUN lamp to go out, and correspondingly the power supply should be checked. A power supply fault is an electrical supply abnormality that causes motor overheating, PLC system faults and failure of the main engine remote control; in the AC electric drive system, a power supply fault is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent and hence overheating; in the PLC control system, since the switching-type inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to service, the ship usually adopts the strategy of overall replacement. When treating a power supply fault, it should first be confirmed whether the battery voltage and the supply circuit are normal, and then K6 and the related monitoring links should be checked; when the RUN lamp goes out, one should switch to checking the power supply, avoiding repeated starting of the generator set under abnormal supply conditions.

Composition of the ship's power station and precautions for connecting shore power: the ship's power station is the heart of the ship's power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are an important sign of the effectiveness of the system in accomplishing its specified tasks; its basic duties include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. The ship's power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 type circuit breaker, ship's power network and shore power box, among which the ship's power network belongs to the ship's power station. The precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the relevant requirements of the ship's power station; when switching between the shore power box and the ship's power network, the voltage, frequency and phase sequence should be checked, and it should be confirmed that the DW14 type circuit breaker and the related protection links are in normal state before operating, so as to prevent the safe operation of the various voltage regulation systems and generators in the ship's power station from being affected by inconsistent supply parameters.

The ship's power station is the heart of the ship's power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are an important sign of the effectiveness of the system in accomplishing its specified tasks. From the perspective of basic duties, the ship's power station must ensure reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur; therefore it includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 type circuit breaker, ship's power network and shore power box and other components. Among them, the ship's power network belongs to the ship's power station in terms of attribution, that is, the ship's power network is a component inside the ship's power station, undertaking the tasks of power transmission and distribution. The precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the ship's power station, that is, in the operation link of connecting shore power, what needs attention and concern is precisely the ship's power station itself, including its voltage, frequency, phase sequence and the connection relationship between the shore power box and the ship's power network; only by focusing attention on the ship's power station can it be ensured that no abnormality occurs on the power station side during the shore power connection process.
