The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the power station; it includes subsystems such as the busbar system, generator measurement and monitoring unit, paralleling circuit and load transfer circuit, and the main switchboard also contains the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. In terms of function, the main switchboard can connect or disconnect circuits, issue alarms when protection devices operate, detect and display various electrical parameters, and regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active and reactive power of the generator sets operating in parallel. The main switchboard occupies a core position in the composition of the ship's power station; the ship's power station contains the main switchboard, and the main switchboard in turn contains the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter, forming a clearly layered control and protection system.

When reading drawings, the main switch is the component in the main switchboard that undertakes the connection and disconnection and protection of the generator main circuit, while the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter is used to directly monitor the insulation condition of the power network on the switchboard; the two respectively correspond to the on-off control of electrical energy and the detection of insulation state, and are the two types of components that must be located first when reading main switchboard circuit diagrams.

As for protective apparatus, RS is the electrical equipment used for overload and short circuit protection in the ship's power system; specifically, RS is a series of fuses used for short circuit and overload protection of devices such as semiconductor rectifiers or thyristor rectifiers, among which the RS_0 type has a rated voltage of 250 to 900V and current specifications of 30 to 480A, and the RS_0 type is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers or their complete sets. The generator paralleling circuit of the main switchboard contains the protective element FU; in the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line via FU.

Voltage is one of the measurable performance quantities; its measuring tools include the multimeter and the voltmeter, and the multimeter uses voltage as the measured quantity. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system.

The multimeter contains a measuring circuit, whose function is to convert different electrical quantities and convert different ranges. The measuring circuit is the circuit part inside the multimeter used to convert different electrical quantities and ranges into signals measurable by the meter head, and is also one of the three basic components of the MF-30 and MF-47 analog multimeters. Since the magnetoelectric meter head can only pass microampere-level current, a conversion circuit is needed to measure different electrical quantities and ranges, and this is precisely the significance of the existence of the measuring circuit. When reading circuits related to the multimeter, the measuring circuit should be regarded as the intermediate link connecting the meter head and the measured quantity; its conversion objects include both the type of electrical quantity and the range position.

The contactor is the electrical equipment used to control motors in the ship's power system and belongs to the ship's low-voltage control apparatus; it is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems and has the characteristics of high operating frequency and long life, as well as accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The amount of contactors used on board is very large, because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor contains an arc chute, main contacts, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the object of the contactor. The circuit breaker is the switching apparatus used to protect circuits in the ship's power system and belongs to the ship's distribution apparatus; it is divided into the frame type (air type) and the molded-case type, and has both switching and protection functions; the circuit breaker belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power network. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the object of the circuit breaker. In switchboard circuit diagrams, the contactor's arc chute, main contacts, core and coil respectively correspond to different graphic symbols and wiring terminals; the main contacts are connected in series in the motor main circuit, the coil is connected in the control circuit, and the core and arc chute are structural components; the circuit breaker appears in different forms, frame type or molded-case type, in the generator main circuit or distribution branches, and when reading drawings one should distinguish its operating function as a switch from its tripping function as a protective apparatus.

The wiring terminal is the metal contact component used in electrical systems to connect conductors with equipment or circuit nodes, commonly found in PLC interfaces, instruments and control circuits. In the synchronizing screen of the main switchboard, the SYNS module contains multiple wiring terminals used to connect synchronizing, control and feedback signals. The electric main engine remote control system contains wiring terminals; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals is one of the common faults of electrical components. The AC ammeter internally is a low-resistance current element, with two non-polarized wiring terminals brought out externally, and the connections may be interchanged. When reading drawings, wiring terminals often appear in the form of numbers or terminal blocks; the synchronizing, control and feedback signals of the SYNS module all enter and leave through these terminals, so the correspondence of the terminals is an important basis for verifying whether the circuit connections are correct.

The circuit breaker exhibits various fault symptoms during operation. The circuit breaker may exhibit the symptom that when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close; this symptom occurs on occasions when the circuit breaker is operated manually, and when judging it one should first confirm whether the operating mechanism is in place, and then check the contacts and related transmission components. The circuit breaker may exhibit the symptom that when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contacts cannot close; this symptom occurs on occasions when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, and when judging it one should first confirm whether the operating power supply and the control circuit are normal, and then check the electric operating mechanism and the contacts. In addition, the circuit breaker may also exhibit the symptoms that one phase contact cannot close; the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open; the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open; the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1h after closing; the undervoltage trip unit has noise; the circuit breaker temperature rise is too high; the auxiliary switch fails; the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctions and causes the circuit breaker to open. These fault symptoms cover the abnormal manifestations of the circuit breaker in many aspects, including manual and electric operation, single-phase contacts, shunt tripping, undervoltage tripping, motor starting, delayed opening after closing, noise, temperature rise, auxiliary switch and semiconductor overcurrent trip unit, and are content that needs to be identified in combination with the circuit structure in the drawing-reading training of actual ship switchboard circuit diagrams. When reading circuits related to the circuit breaker, the shunt trip unit, undervoltage trip unit, auxiliary switch and semiconductor overcurrent trip unit should be respectively corresponded to the control circuit, protection circuit and signal circuit in the diagram, so that when the above symptoms occur, the order of checking and the components involved can be determined according to the circuit routing.

The drawing-reading training of actual ship switchboard circuit diagrams must ultimately land on the identification of specific circuits and components. The SYNS module in the synchronizing screen of the main switchboard is provided internally with multiple wiring terminals, through which the synchronizing signals, control signals and feedback signals are all connected in or led out.

When reading the current measuring circuit, one will inevitably encounter the current transformer. The text symbol corresponding to the current transformer is TA; its function is to transform the current ratio, the secondary side standard current is 5A, the primary side terminals are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary side by K1 and K2. Distinguished by structure, current transformers include the coil type, busbar type and through type, and the through-type current transformer is one type of current transformer. The current transformer has the nature of a current source and in operation is equivalent to a short-circuited transformer; one end of the secondary side is earthed, and during operation the secondary winding must never be open-circuited. The clamp-on ammeter internally contains a current transformer; the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current, and the circuit need not be broken during measurement.

Resistance, voltage and current are the three electrical quantities most frequently read in switchboard commissioning and fault finding. The multimeter is used to measure resistance and can measure the resistance value; the multimeter is also used to measure voltage and can measure the voltage value, and the voltmeter can likewise measure voltage; the multimeter is also used to measure current and can measure the current value, and the ammeter and clamp-on ammeter are also tools for measuring current. When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistance must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on.

Insulation detection occupies an independent position in switchboard circuit diagrams. Measuring insulation resistance is used to verify the insulation performance of electrical equipment, often after major overhaul of the equipment or after shutdown during operation, and is also one of the mandatory checks and test items for acceptance of a motor after new installation or major overhaul. In contactor servicing, it is necessary to measure the insulation resistance between contacts, between the coil and the core, and between live parts and earth. The E23 type ohmmeter is connected via wiring to F440 PNL and F220 PNL to achieve insulation detection of systems of different voltage levels.

The marine power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 circuit breaker, ship power network and shore power box, wherein the ship power network is a component of the marine power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the relevant states of the marine power station.

When reading the diagrams, several faults and handling measures related to the generator and circuit breaker will also be encountered. Corrosion of the generator slip rings, blackening and non-conduction is one of the common fault causes; the generator slip rings are used to transmit current, the brush braid is the conductor connecting the brush, and the linear reactor is used to regulate current. For the above situations, the coil can be checked and repaired or replaced with a new one; for the tripping mechanism, the tripping mechanism can be checked, the corresponding bolt adjusted or replaced; for the wiring, the wiring and connections can be checked, and the screws connected or tightened; for the spring and electromagnetic mechanism, the spring tension can be checked and reduced, or the electromagnetic attraction increased or the spring reaction force reduced.

Maintenance personnel are the personnel responsible for fault diagnosis and repair of marine electrical equipment, and must be very familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components, and at the same time be familiar with the structure, working principles of electrical equipment as well as the functions and installation positions of components (assemblies). In traditional fault diagnosis, maintenance personnel need to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary judgment through the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling; this method requires maintenance personnel to have sufficient perceptual knowledge of the normal state and abnormal state of the equipment. The elevator, as commonly used living equipment on ships, is composed of the traction machine, car, landing door and electrical control system, and its regular maintenance is a necessary condition for ensuring safe operation. Maintenance personnel should check the main safety facilities and electrical control part of the elevator every week, and organize a technical inspection after the elevator has been used for one year; generally a comprehensive disassembly, cleaning and inspection should be carried out once every 3 to 5 years, with the specific period depending on the degree of newness of the equipment. The floor illumination at the landing should be at least 50 lx, so that users can see the area clearly when the car lighting fails. Passenger elevators are not allowed to be frequently used as freight elevators, and it is strictly forbidden to carry flammable and explosive dangerous goods. If the elevator is out of use for more than one week, it must be carefully inspected and trial-run before use.

The elevator includes components such as the traction sheave, brake wheel, brake shoe, speed governor, safety gear, guide rail, buffer, traction steel wire rope, traveling cable and counterweight device, and its maintenance work covers traction machine maintenance, traction machine lubrication, brake system maintenance, speed governor inspection, car door and automatic door mechanism inspection and adjustment, safety gear inspection, guide rail and guide shoe inspection, buffer inspection and landing door mechanical-electrical interlock device inspection, etc. During elevator maintenance, attention should be paid to the regulations to be observed during elevator repair and maintenance, the regulations on the use of the insulation resistance tester during elevator repair and maintenance, the safety measures before adjusting the brake system, the safety measures before measuring the thickness of the brake lining, and the safety measures during inspection and repair.

The regulations to be observed during elevator repair and maintenance require: no passengers or cargo during repair, and inspection/out-of-service signs must be hung at each landing door; the switch at the corresponding position should be disconnected; when working in the machine room, the main power switch should be disconnected; when working on the car top, the inspection switch should be closed; when working in the pit, the emergency stop switch of the pit inspection button box should be disconnected, or at the same time the safety switch of the speed governor tensioning device should be disconnected; the operation should be carried out cooperatively by the person in charge and an assistant, and the cooperating personnel must strictly obey instructions; it is strictly forbidden to stand outside the hoistway and lean into it, or to stand with one foot inside and one foot outside the car sill for a long time during repair. These regulations are aimed at the safety protection of personnel and equipment during repair and maintenance operations, and their applicable objects include both the person in charge of the operation and the assistant cooperating in the operation; the two must act in coordination, and neither party may change the operating steps without authorization. The purpose of hanging the inspection/out-of-service sign is to make users at each landing clearly know that the elevator is in a non-use state, avoiding mistaken entry or misoperation;

The regulations on the use of the insulation resistance tester during elevator repair and maintenance clearly stipulate: the hand-cranked insulation resistance tester is prohibited; a battery-type high-voltage insulation resistance tester should be used, with a voltage of 500 V and an internal resistance of more than 200 kΩ. The insulation resistance tester, also called a megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is divided according to the highest voltage emitted by the hand-cranked generator into specifications such as 100 V, 200 V, 500 V, 1000 V and 2500 V, and is used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, circuits and cables. In elevator repair and maintenance, the battery-type high-voltage insulation resistance tester is selected to avoid the inconvenience and safety hazards brought by the hand-cranked instrument during operation. During measurement, the three terminal posts L, E and G are connected respectively according to the measurement object, wherein the G terminal post is used to eliminate the influence of surface leakage current; the specified 500 V voltage level and internal resistance of more than 200 kΩ are the basic conditions for ensuring that the measurement results can reflect the insulation condition of the elevator electrical part, and selecting an instrument with an internal resistance lower than this or a non-battery type does not meet the specified requirements.

The gap between the wedge block of the safety gear and the working surface of the guide rail is generally 3 mm, and the gaps should be similar. The fitting rotating parts of the safety gear transmission rod should be coated with mechanical lubricating oil once every two months, and the rolling or sliding parts of the clamp jaw need to be coated with lithium-based grease for lubrication and rust prevention. After shutdown, the actuating rod needs to be manually moved to check whether the action is normal. When the elevator is out of control and the safety gear has not yet acted, passengers must not attempt to jump out of the car. Misoperation of the safety gear is a fault that requires immediately notifying maintenance personnel and stopping use for repair. When inspecting the safety gear, the gap between the wedge block and the working surface of the guide rail is the key value for judging whether it can normally clamp the guide rail; 3 mm is the general value, and the requirement that the gaps should be similar means that the gaps on the left and right sides and at different positions should be kept consistent, avoiding one side contacting first and asynchronous action caused by uneven gaps. Once misoperation of the safety gear occurs, maintenance personnel must be notified immediately and use stopped for repair, and operation must not continue.

The action of the speed governor should be flexible and reliable, and its movement needs to be observed to see whether it is good. The rolling bearings of the speed governor should be inspected every year; the wear of the speed governor wheel, wheel groove, shaft sleeve and shaft needs to be checked, and whether the centrifugal throw-out head can rotate freely needs to be checked. When the rope wheel elongates beyond the specified range and cuts off the control circuit, the rope wheel should be shortened; when the speed governor steel wire rope is seriously worn, it should be replaced, with the same requirement as the traction steel wire rope. The inspection period and items of the speed governor each have their emphasis: the rolling bearings are inspected once a year, and the inspection content includes the wear of the speed governor wheel, wheel groove, shaft sleeve and shaft, as well as whether the centrifugal throw-out head can rotate freely; these parts respectively undertake the functions of supporting the rope wheel, guiding the steel wire rope, rotating fit and overspeed triggering, and wear or jamming at any one place will affect the flexible and reliable action of the speed governor.

In electrical measurement, the multimeter can be used to measure resistance and voltage. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage corrector to have no main regulating effect.

The marine power station is the heart of the ship power system, and the reliability and survivability of its work are important signs of the effectiveness of the system in achieving the specified tasks; its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination after a fault. The marine power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 circuit breaker, ship power network and shore power box. The ship power network is a component of the marine power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the relevant requirements of the marine power station.

Traction machine maintenance work must be carried out by professional, trained personnel; some inspection items need to be carried out while the elevator is running, and maintenance personnel must pay attention to personal safety. The outer surface of the traction machine should be kept clean to prevent the accumulation of dust and dirt, and the working surfaces of the brake wheel and traction sheave should be regularly wiped with clean cotton waste. The brake should be regularly inspected, adjusted and replaced in time if necessary, and attention should be paid that the temperature rise of the electromagnetic coil must not exceed 90 K. The wear of the traction sheave should also be regularly inspected; when the height difference of the steel wire ropes due to uneven wear of the grooves of the traction sheave is greater than 1/10 of the diameter, the rope grooves need to be repaired to a consistent depth; when the wear of the rope grooves makes the gap between the steel wire rope and the groove bottom less than 1 mm, the traction sheave should be re-machined or replaced. When re-machining the traction sheave, attention should be paid that the rim thickness below the cut is not less than the steel wire rope diameter. The traction sheave is a component of the traction machine, and its working surface needs to be regularly wiped with clean cotton waste to prevent dust and dirt.

For traction machine lubrication, it is recommended to use elevator-specific gear oil of corresponding viscosity such as Shell Omala 460 or Lanzhou Refining Kunlun 34# (460). Lubricating oil should be added to the center position of the oil sight glass; too little will cause lubrication difficulty, and too much will cause oil leakage. When using mineral oil, the first oil change is carried out after the new machine has accumulated about 400 h of operation; when using synthetic oil, the first oil change is carried out after the new machine has accumulated about 700 h of operation. For mineral oil, subsequent changes are every 2000 to 3000 h, and the longest should not exceed 12 to 18 months; for synthetic oil, subsequent changes are every 3000 to 4000 h, and the longest should not exceed 24 to 36 months.

The surface roughness of the brake wheel is required to be not less than 3.2, and it needs to be protected from oil contamination, rain and ice and snow erosion. The steady-state working temperature of the brake wheel should be less than 180 °C, but in actual operation the surface temperature may exceed 100 °C. The opening and closing gap between the brake wheel and the arc surface of the brake shoe should be kept at 0.1 to 0.3 mm to avoid friction. The daily inspection benchmark is that the surface has no oil contamination or other debris; if it does not meet this, the adhered matter needs to be removed. When measuring the thickness of the brake lining, the steel ruler is perpendicular to the arc surface of the brake wheel, and the distance is the brake lining thickness.

Unevenness of the guide rail joints will cause running vibration, which is easily confused with electrical system faults. The automatic lubrication device is filled with lubricating oil once a week, using No. 100 refined mineral oil. When the wear amount of the working surface of the sliding guide rail liner reaches 1 mm, it should be replaced. When the guide rail surface is rough or the surface is damaged by safety gear braking, it must be smoothed before use. Every year, check whether the guide rail is deformed or loose, and tighten the pressure plate, joint and bracket bolts. Interviewing the operator is the preceding step of observation, and observation is the preceding step of checking the monitoring and indicating device. A multimeter can be used when measuring resistance and current, and an ammeter or clamp-on ammeter can also be used to measure current. The contactor includes the coil as a component.

Bearing fault, lubrication fault and installation fault will all cause bearing overheating. Bearing overheating corresponds to three troubleshooting directions: checking bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition and checking the installation condition; both checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition require the use of bearings. Bearing damage will cause low speed during load operation, abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and bearing overheating. Insufficient lubricating oil and impurities will also cause bearing overheating. If the bearing is damaged or there are impurities in the lubricating oil, the measure of replacing the bearing is usually taken. Generator bearing overheating corresponds to replacing the bearing. When the traction motor has abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, bearing damage is a possible cause, and the damaged bearing needs to be replaced. The disappearance of noise during no-load operation indicates poor coupling installation; if the noise still exists and is accompanied by vibration, it points to a shaft or bearing fault. When an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and the characteristic of the bearing end cover overheating.

Poor earthing will cause the motor casing to become live; damp windings, damaged insulation or dirt on the terminal board will also cause the motor casing to become live, and worn insulation of the lead-out wires will likewise cause the motor casing to become live. For the fault of the motor casing becoming live, the handling direction is to find the cause and take corresponding measures to correct it; it also corresponds to the group of maintenance procedures of drying the stator winding, repairing when the insulation is damaged, and cleaning the dirt on the terminal board. For damp windings, drying treatment of the stator winding is required; for damaged insulation, repair is required; for dirt on the terminal board, the dirt on the terminal board needs to be cleaned. When applicable to handling the fault caused by damaged insulation adhesive of the motor lead-out wires, the lead-out wires need to be repaired or replaced. The ship power network is a component of the marine power station. The precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the relevant requirements of the marine power station. In marine power station equipment, replacing the bearing is used to deal with overheating caused by bearing damage or impurities in the lubricating oil. The measurable property of a resistor is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. The terminal screws of the electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact; failure to tighten the external terminal screws of the thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be disconnected. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. Welding is a process in which the solder is melted by heating, atomic diffusion occurs between the weldment and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer with good conductivity and mechanical strength is formed; welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products.

The brake wheel is the friction pair component in the elevator traction machine brake; the brake shoe clamping its circumferential surface can generate braking torque. In the electromagnet brake-shoe type brake, when power is off, the spring tension forces the brake shoe to clamp the brake wheel and brake.

The brake shoe is the component in the brake that realizes braking or release through friction against the brake wheel, and its wear amount must be less than 2 mm. The wear amount of the brake shoe tightness of various models of traction machines should be less than 2 mm; if it exceeds the standard, the brake shoe or brake arm needs to be replaced. In the open-brake state, the gap between the two arc surfaces of the brake shoe and the brake wheel should be kept at 0.1 to 0.3 mm. The surface of the brake shoe must not have oil contamination or other debris; otherwise the contamination needs to be removed or the brake shoe replaced. When adjusting the brake shoe, adjust the lower screw so that it just presses against the brake shoe plane and then turn it counterclockwise 30° to leave a gap. Before measuring the thickness of the brake lining, the main power supply must be cut off and it must be confirmed that the brake has been de-energized and closed, to prevent a runaway car accident. The brake lining is a component of the brake shoe.

Brake system maintenance includes several specific items. When checking the open-brake gap, the gap should be less than 0.5 mm; when checking the brake wheel, the surface of the brake wheel must not have any oil contamination or other debris; when checking the brake shoe, the surface of the brake lining must not have any oil contamination or other debris; when checking the brake shoe, the cumulative wear amount of the brake lining of various models of traction machines should be less than 2 mm; when checking the brake, in the closed state of the brake the specified state of the brake should be ensured. The daily maintenance items of the brake require the customer to carry out, and all friction surfaces of the brake must not be contaminated with oil.

Before adjusting the braking system, the corresponding safety measures must be carried out. The elevator must be driven at slow speed to the upper terminal station and be in an unloaded state, and the car must be placed symmetrically on the buffers and be in an unloaded state; after completing the above operations, the main power supply must be cut off. If this measure is not carried out, a car slipping accident may occur.

The safety measures during inspection and maintenance include: all maintenance work must be carried out with the elevator powered off, and it must be ensured that the elevator cannot start unexpectedly; during the braking system adjustment process, it must be ensured that no load torque is applied to the brake wheel or the motor; after maintenance is completed, it is necessary to check whether the interconnected locking components are locked, and operation may be resumed only after adjusting to sufficient braking torque; because the brake surface temperature may exceed 100°C, temperature-sensitive devices are prohibited from passing over or being fixed on the brake device.

The buffer is a safety component of the elevator, used to absorb the impact energy of the car or counterweight, including oil-pressure buffers and hydraulic buffers. The oil level of the oil-pressure buffer should be below 10°C, and the oil level height should be kept above the minimum oil level. Every two months, check the oil level and leakage of the oil-pressure buffer, replenish oil and tighten all bolts. The exposed surface of the plunger outer circle should be cleaned with gasoline and coated with anti-rust oil or buffer oil. Perform a plunger reset test once a year; the time required from release to returning to the free height should be less than 90s. Before adjusting the braking system, the unloaded elevator must be driven at slow speed to the upper terminal station and placed symmetrically on the buffers; before measuring the brake shoe thickness, the unloaded elevator must be placed symmetrically on the buffers and the main power supply must be cut off. The rolling bearings of the speed governor should be inspected every year. The maintenance item of speed governor inspection requires: the speed governor action should be flexible and reliable, and its rolling bearings need to be inspected every year; the speed governor tensioning device must be kept working normally, and the reliability of the rope-break safety switch must be checked; check whether the rope-clamping brake iron is located exactly in the center position.

The maintenance content of car door and automatic door mechanism inspection and adjustment includes: bearings such as the swing rod part should be regularly filled with lithium-based grease and cleaned once a year; for adjustment of drive belt tension, if during use the drive belt elongates causing tension reduction and slipping, the motor base adjusting screw can be adjusted to bring the belt to proper tension; the action of the safety touch panel and light curtain should be sensitive and reliable, and the collision force of the safety touch panel should not be greater than 5N.

When disassembling the brake, first remove the screws on the junction box, then remove the power wires and microswitch wires. The junction box is a component used in ship electrical systems to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical components. The general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc. The solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box, but directly connected to the local control box.

The conventional fault diagnosis method uses the step of observation. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status, and equipment operating parameters. Observation belongs to a sub-step of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged", and its content includes whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt.

The contactor contains a core. The core is a component of ship electrical equipment and a magnetic conductive component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form a magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as an insulation measurement reference point. When measuring the insulation resistance to earth of the coil of electrical equipment, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core. In a through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor under measurement is directly interlinked with the core to replace the primary winding.

The marine motor contains a bearing. The bearing is a mechanical component of the motor, used to support the rotation of the rotor; its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration and abnormal noise. Bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance. The bearing is used when checking bearing fault itself, and the bearing is also used when checking the lubrication condition. The ship power grid belongs to the ship power station. Precautions for shore power connection require attention to the ship power station.

The maintenance work of the elevator has clear periodic requirements. The regulations to be observed during elevator repair and maintenance cover weekly inspection, annual technical inspection, the cycle of complete disassembly, cleaning and inspection, and inspection and trial operation before re-commissioning after being out of service.

Guide rail and guide shoe inspection belongs to the annual maintenance item. The guide rail device should be inspected once a year, mainly checking for deformation and looseness; the inspector needs to stand on the car top and proceed from top to bottom at slow speed; during inspection, all pressure plates, joints and bracket bolts must be tightened in sequence, and the welded parts must be checked for weld separation. Check whether each movable part is loose; after stopping the machine, move the action rod by hand to check whether the action is normal; after inspection, all structures should be restored to normal and the gaps at each part measured.

Buffer inspection is carried out for the oil-pressure buffer.

The landing door mechanical and electrical interlock device inspection is carried out once a month, checking whether the conductive plate and contact have false connection or poor connection, whether the spring pressure of the contact can reset automatically, and whether there is looseness at riveted, welded and glued joints; the lock hook, arm and each roller should rotate flexibly, lithium-based grease should be applied to the bearings, and cleaning should be carried out once a year. Check the door suspension rollers once a month, and replace them immediately if wear and damage are found; when the outer circle diameter of the door suspension roller is severely worn, it should be replaced. Clean the electrical contacts to make good contact, and check and adjust the door ball, rotating parts and lock catch positioning. It is strictly prohibited to pry the landing door open by hand from outside the landing door.

The traction steel wire rope inspection requires frequent inspection and adjustment so that the tension of each traction rope is uniform, with an error less than 0.5% of the average value. The traction rope should be replaced when one of the following conditions occurs: when broken wires are evenly distributed among the rope strands, the maximum number of broken wires in one lay length exceeds 32; when broken wires are concentrated in one or two rope strands, the maximum number of broken wires in one lay length exceeds 16; the steel wires on the surface of the traction rope have significant wear or rust; after severe wear, the diameter of the traction rope is less than 90% of the original diameter. In addition, the length of the traction steel wire rope must be checked; the distance from the bottom of the counterweight beam to the surface of the hydraulic buffer must not be less than 150mm.

The traveling cable inspection content includes: check whether there are foreign objects in contact with the cable in the hoistway, and whether the cable sheath is worn; check whether the cable is twisted or biased to one side, and whether there is swaying or dragging on the ground during movement; when the car stops at the lowest floor, the cable is required to be more than 60mm from the hoistway floor.

The counterweight device inspection requires cleaning the counterweight device and checking whether the bolts at each part are loose, checking the wear condition of the counterweight wheel rope grooves and adding an appropriate amount of lubricating grease, confirming whether the counterweight pressure plate fixing buckle is fastened, and checking whether the counterweight frame bottom adjusting block bolts are fastened. Hoistway cleaning requires removing garbage on the door head cover, garbage at the hoistway bottom, oil stains, accumulated water and other garbage at various parts that affect machine operation performance, and removing protruding obstacles in the hoistway that may collide with the car and counterweight.

The inspection of various conduits, trunking, junction boxes and wiring conditions includes: checking whether the wiring at the terminal bases of the car button box, car cable junction box, intermediate junction box and various control boxes is loose, confirming the contact tightness of the power wires, power switch contacts and motor wiring, and cleaning the terminal bases, checking whether each terminal base is rusted and missing wire number plates; checking whether the conduits, trunking and boxes in the equipment room, car top, car bottom and hoistway are loose or missing covers.

The drive belt also needs attention in elevator maintenance; when the drive belt elongates causing tension reduction and slipping, the motor base screws need to be adjusted to tension it.

Maintenance personnel should be familiar with the structure, working principle, component (assembly) functions and locations of electrical equipment, master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, and must be very familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of each component.

The maintenance work of the elevator is carried out in layers according to cycle.

From the perspective of equipment composition, the elevator includes components such as the traction wheel, brake wheel, brake shoe, speed governor, safety gear, guide rail, buffer, traction steel wire rope, traveling cable and counterweight device; the status of these components directly determines operation safety. During operation, the elevator needs to observe the regulations to be followed during elevator repair and maintenance; whenever entering the hoistway, car top or pit for work, power outage, tagging and assigning a person for supervision must be confirmed according to the specified procedures, and after the work is completed, restoration must be carried out item by item. The elevator needs to observe the regulations on using the insulation resistance tester during elevator repair and maintenance; a battery-type high-voltage insulation resistance tester should be selected for measuring insulation resistance, with a range of 500V and internal resistance above 200kΩ; hand-cranked types are prohibited to avoid unstable output voltage affecting reading judgment. The elevator needs to observe the safety measures before braking system adjustment; before adjustment, the car should be in the specified position and reliably braked to prevent the car from slipping during adjustment. The elevator needs to observe the safety measures before measuring brake shoe thickness; before measurement, braking and anti-slip measures must likewise be implemented first, and then the brake shoe part is measured. The elevator needs to observe the safety measures during inspection and repair; the entire inspection and repair process should comply with the sequence requirements of power outage, voltage verification, supervision and restoration of power supply.

Specific maintenance items cover multiple aspects. The elevator includes traction machine maintenance and traction machine lubrication, requiring periodic inspection of the traction machine and ensuring proper lubrication; the elevator includes braking system maintenance, involving the matching state of the brake wheel and brake shoe; the elevator includes speed governor inspection and safety gear inspection, which need to be linked to confirm reliable action; the elevator includes car door and automatic door mechanism inspection and adjustment to ensure smooth door opening and closing; the elevator includes guide rail and guide shoe inspection, as well as buffer inspection, so that operation guidance and terminal protection are effective; the elevator includes landing door mechanical and electrical interlock device inspection to prevent the car from running when the landing door is not closed; the elevator includes traction steel wire rope inspection and traveling cable inspection, focusing on wear and connection conditions; the elevator includes counterweight device inspection to confirm its balance relationship with the car; the elevator also includes hoistway cleaning and inspection of various conduits, trunking, junction boxes and wiring conditions, to keep the hoistway clean and wiring connections reliable.

The traction motor failing to start is a fault symptom that needs to be checked item by item in control system maintenance. There are many causes of this phenomenon, and troubleshooting should be carried out in order from simple to complex. The power supply not being connected is one possible cause; for the phenomenon of failure to start, the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts should be checked to find the fault point, and the specific electrical connection fault point should be located through the above inspection means. Incorrect wiring of control equipment can also cause failure to start; for the phenomenon of failure to start, the wiring diagram should be checked and corrected. Undervoltage can also cause failure to start; the power supply voltage should be checked, and if it is indeed too low, appropriately increased. Electrical faults such as short circuit to earth between stator winding phases, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit can also prevent the motor from starting; for the phenomenon of failure to start, the short circuit and open circuit parts should be found and repaired, and if the wiring is incorrect, the wiring should be corrected. Excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer, are likewise causes of failure to start; during troubleshooting, reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer; if the motor can run normally, the reducer part should be checked. In addition, excessive load or the brake not being released can cause this fault; when the traction motor fails to start, if the load is excessive or the brake is not released, it belongs to this category; stator winding short circuit in the traction motor will cause the motor to fail to start; incorrect wiring of the traction motor control equipment will cause the motor to fail to start; incorrect stator winding wiring is a possible cause of the traction motor failing to start and the wiring diagram needs to be checked and corrected.

When the traction motor operates under load, various abnormalities may also occur. Excessive load will cause abnormal stator current; at this time, the operation of reducing the load should be carried out. Undervoltage or excessively low power supply voltage will cause abnormalities during loaded operation of the traction motor and excessive temperature or smoking; the troubleshooting method is to directly check the power supply voltage and appropriately increase it after confirmation. If the power supply voltage is too low during loaded operation of the traction motor, troubleshooting should be carried out through the step of checking the power supply voltage. If an abnormality occurs during loaded operation of the traction motor and the cause is excessively low power supply voltage, the voltage needs to be checked. Weld separation between the guide bars and end rings of the traction motor can also cause faults during loaded operation; the end ring is the annular conductive component at the end of the squirrel-cage rotor, which together with the cage bars forms the short-circuit winding; ring breakage refers to one or several cracks in the end ring, and cracking of the cast aluminum rotor end ring can generally be found by visual inspection. Undervoltage can also cause low speed during loaded operation; excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer, can likewise cause low speed during loaded operation.

When the traction motor operates with abnormal noise or excessive vibration, the causes and treatments differ. Mechanical friction is one possible cause; for the phenomenon of abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, the air gap between rotor and stator and the gap between brake wheel and brake band should be checked, the cause of rubbing should be found and correction carried out. Two-phase operation can also cause this phenomenon; at this time, power should be cut off, and if it cannot start after switching on again, one phase may be open-circuited; check the power supply and motor and repair them. Bearing damage is another cause, and the treatment method is to replace the damaged bearing. Shaft extension bending can also cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration, and the treatment method is to replace the shaft. Loose coupling connection can likewise cause this phenomenon; the loose part needs to be checked and the coupling tightened. Excessive load may also cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration; the stator current needs to be checked and the load reduced when overload is found. When abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation is caused by excessive load, the load needs to be reduced; after reducing the load, the motor and reducer can be separated to determine whether the fault originates from the reducer.

Excessive temperature or smoking of the traction motor may be caused by multiple reasons. Undervoltage will lead to this result; short circuit to earth between stator winding phases, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will lead to this result; mechanical friction will also lead to this result. In the traction motor, stator winding short circuit will cause the motor temperature to be too high or smoking, and during treatment the short circuit part needs to be found and repaired. If excessive temperature or smoking of the traction motor is caused by undervoltage, the voltage needs to be checked and appropriately increased; when the temperature rise of the traction motor is too high or smoking occurs, if the cause is undervoltage, the step of checking the power supply voltage should be carried out.

In the measurement and inspection stage, voltage is a measurable performance, and its voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter; current is likewise a measurable performance, and its current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. For the maintenance procedure of checking the power supply voltage, attention should be paid during implementation to marking the circuit terminals before disassembly. Motor fails to start corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, motor speed low after starting corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, motor temperature rise high corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, and excessive sparking under brush also corresponds to checking the power supply voltage. The winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce electromotive force; the shaft is a mechanical transmission component, used to transmit torque and rotational motion. Incorrect wiring will cause the generator voltage to fail to build up normally.

In the elevator braking device, the brake wheel and brake shoe form a friction pair; the brake shoe tightly grips the circumferential surface of the brake wheel to generate braking torque.

If the brake release gap does not meet the requirements, for example reaching 0.5mm or more, the gap needs readjustment. Readjustment is a maintenance operation for electrical components such as circuit breakers and relays with parameter deviation or abnormal mechanical state, restoring them to specified values by adjusting springs, setting values or travel. Cases such as excessive reaction spring force, failure of the motor operating positioning switch, too large re-latching contact surface, incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, and excessive reaction spring force all correspond to treatment by readjustment. Among them, readjustment can be used to handle the circuit breaker automatic tripping fault caused by incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, and can also be used to eliminate the noise of the undervoltage trip unit caused by excessive reaction spring force. The elevator contains a brake wheel and also contains a brake shoe, which cooperate to complete the braking and release actions.

The electrical control circuits of ship refrigeration and air-conditioning installations drive the refrigeration compressor motor, and the starting and stopping of the motor depend on the pressure changes sensed by the suction-side pressure relay. The electrical circuits of refrigeration equipment are relatively simple; the starting and stopping of the refrigeration compressor motor are directly controlled by the suction-side pressure relay. Air-conditioning equipment is generally used on ocean-going transport ships, adopting centralized cooling or centralized heating, and is equipped with two refrigeration compressor units and fans; the motors driving the refrigeration compressors are likewise controlled to start and stop by the pressure relay at the compressor suction side, stopping when the suction-side pressure is low and starting to run when the suction-side pressure is high. The air-conditioning compressor also has a reduced-load starting function and can automatically unload or reload with changes in the external heat load, that is, adapt to the load by cutting in or cutting out cylinders. Whether refrigeration equipment or air-conditioning equipment, its control system should be provided with protection for insufficient cooling water pressure, excessively low lubricating oil pressure, low refrigerant suction pressure, etc., and be equipped with corresponding audible and visual alarms. For high-power compressors, unloading should be carried out first at starting to avoid a large starting current impacting the ship's power network; at the same time, unloading or reloading control should be possible according to the heat load, both achieving energy saving and avoiding the impact of a large starting current on the power network.

In the specific circuits, for the RKS10F type provision refrigeration installation in automatic mode, when the cargo hold temperature rises causing the suction-side pressure to rise, the contactor is energized and the compressor runs accordingly. In the cold store defrost control, the defrost timer DT₁ is used to control the automatic changeover of the defrost cycle; when the defrost time ends, its two sets of switches automatically return to the non-defrost state. When the cold store selector switch is placed in the "REF" position for manual refrigeration, the defrost timer motor is cut off, so that defrost heating does not operate. One of the fault causes of the cold store failing to defrost automatically is that the two sets of switches of the defrost timer cannot change over automatically. In the refrigeration installation control circuit, the defrost timer (code 2DX) is energized when the frost ice on the evaporator thickens and touches the defrost start switch and the defrost termination thermostat closes, and its normally open contact closes and self-locks. In the cold store defrost control, de-energization of the intermediate relay causes the fan contactor and the liquid supply solenoid valve circuit to open. In the cold store system, the drain pipe is located below the drain pan and is used to discharge the water produced by defrosting; when the cold store control is placed in the "DRAIN" position, the heating element heats the drain pipe to assist drainage. When manual defrosting fails, it is necessary to check the operation of the defrost contactors MC31 and MC32; if they operate normally, then check the heater and fuse. When multiple cold stores and compressors are controlled in combination, the circuits are complicated, and it is necessary to be familiar with the unit to which each relay and contactor belongs and the lead numbers, so as to quickly troubleshoot.

In the air-conditioning installation, the operation of intermediate relay 4/2 is a prerequisite interlock condition for compressor starting. Important contactors and solenoid valves should have indicator lights when working, so that operators can understand the system's working condition. A contactor is an electrical device used in the ship's power system to control motors; it belongs to low-voltage control apparatus and is mainly used in electric drive systems to control motors, featuring high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships, because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil; contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself. An intermediate relay is a type of electromagnetic relay, similar in construction to a contactor, used to expand contact capacity and number and to perform control logic conversion; its function is to expand contact capacity and number, and fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the contactor's inspection method. A pressure relay is a non-electrical relay with pressure as the input signal, whose sensing element is a bellows and whose actuating part is a contact; it is used for automatic control and protection of ship boilers, air compressors and pump units, and in auxiliary boilers it is used as a control apparatus for automatically controlling steam pressure. A thermal relay is a protective relay with a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small ship motors; it belongs to thermal relays classified by sensing element, its sensing part is a bimetallic strip, and it is used in large quantities on ships, with overload protection of general small motors being accomplished by it. A solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to control the on-off of fuel oil; at ignition it cuts off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle and is injected; it can also be used to release residual air from air compressors or to control fine water mist fire-extinguishing zones. In the burner ignition program, the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle and is injected; its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve.

A timer is a digital logic circuit application component used in household appliances; in ship living equipment it is often used to control the start and stop of electric fans, the washing and spinning programs of washing machines, and the defrost cycle of cold stores; an electric fan includes a timer. In troubleshooting an electric fan, if it sometimes turns and sometimes does not, one possible cause is timer failure, and the handling method is to replace the timer. In troubleshooting a washing machine that does not work after being energized, it is necessary to check whether the timer wiring is loose or disconnected, whether the timer knob slips, and whether the contact is in good contact. The drain pipe is the drainage component of a washing machine and a cold store defrost system, used to discharge washing waste water or defrost water; in a washing machine, if it is folded into a dead corner or has creases, it is easily blocked by debris causing poor drainage; aging and cracking of the washing machine drain pipe will cause water leakage, and it needs to be replaced and the pipe mouth firmly glued.

The ship's power station is the heart of the ship's power system; the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks, and its basic duties include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. The ship's power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrollable phase-compounding voltage regulation system, controllable phase-compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 type circuit breaker, ship's power network and shore power box. The ship's power network belongs to the ship's power station and usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system; single-phase earthing at any point is an abnormal state, and if another phase is earthed, a short circuit is formed; an insulation detection device for the power network is installed on the lighting distribution panel of the main switchboard. Precautions for connecting shore power need attention to the ship's power station. A multimeter is used for current measurement, and a clamp-on ammeter is used for current measurement. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after opening the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. When the motor is overloaded, the motor overload protection transistor relay converts power into voltage, satisfying the relationship U=KP; a fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not be used as overload protection for the motor; excessive refrigerant charged in the refrigeration system causing excessively high pressure and excessive load will cause motor overload.

When compressor control fails, in automatic operation the starting and stopping of the compressor are controlled by the suction-side low-pressure switch 63HL(L); if it can start normally after switching to manual, it is determined that the low-pressure switch 63HL(L) is damaged or its contact is not closed; if manual operation is also abnormal, it is necessary to check the high-pressure protection switch 63HL(H) and the oil pressure switch 63QL. Troubleshooting involves the motor overload protection thermal relay 51-1 and the auxiliary relay AX12; if all components of the protection interlock circuit are normal and 88-1 operates, the fault originates from the compressor motor itself failing to start. When compressor control fails, it is also necessary to check whether the motor overload protection thermal relay 51-1 is normal. Before starting the refrigeration installation, it is necessary to confirm that motor overload has not occurred and the relevant contact 51C is closed. Failure to start is a fault symptom in which the motor or drive system cannot establish rotational motion after being energized, and is often used as the top event of fault tree analysis; when constructing a fault tree, it is often selected as the top event of electrical equipment, such as motor fails to start, and the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as normal power supply and normal control circuit. Power supply not connected will cause failure to start, incorrect wiring of control equipment will cause failure to start, undervoltage will cause failure to start, stator winding phase-to-phase short circuit to earth, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start; excessive load or the brake not released, and a faulty reducer, will likewise cause failure to start. For failure to start, the corresponding handling is: check the switch, fuse, and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find the short circuit and open circuit locations and repair them, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer, and if the motor can run normally, the reducer part should be checked.

Refrigeration equipment includes refrigeration and air-conditioning control system maintenance. Excessive cold store temperature deviation is a fault symptom requiring attention in refrigeration and air-conditioning control circuits.

The content of observation covers abnormal phenomena, part condition, conductor condition and equipment operating parameters, specifically including whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, chafed or burnt. High-power compressors should be able to perform unloading or reloading control according to the heat load, so as to achieve energy saving and avoid a large starting current impacting the power network. Taking the RKS10F type provision refrigeration installation as an example, in automatic mode, when the high cargo hold temperature causes high suction-side pressure, the contactor is energized and the compressor runs.

A temperature relay is used as a regulating switch in cold store systems; deviation of its setting value will cause the store temperature to deviate seriously; if the contact cannot close or open, it will cause the liquid supply solenoid valve to be abnormal, causing refrigeration failure or overcooling. A temperature relay is a non-electrical relay, used in large quantities on ships, with both control and protection functions; it can be used for cooling water temperature alarm as a protective apparatus, and can also be used in scenarios such as auxiliary boilers as a control apparatus. A contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil. The main contact is used to make or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor; discoloration of the copper main contact or a burnt smell indicates poor contact and overheating, and it is necessary to adjust the gap and overtravel and remove the oxide film; when the main contact has been overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected for replacement. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch and the contactor, used for control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection, and is also one of the main components of the generator main switch; in motor forward rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize self-locking of the contactor coil. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature being unable to close and the motor failing to start. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and its fault analysis and handling can refer to the contactor's inspection method.

A fuse is a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material, featuring a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength; its material is aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, etc., and it is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, listed alongside resistors and capacitors. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Alarm code AL20 indicates control circuit fuse blown (24V), and AL21 indicates computer controller fuse blown (18V). The electric main engine remote control system includes a fuse. In the starting control of multi-cylinder high-power compressors, when timed cylinder sealing is adopted to limit the starting current and starting time, the cylinder loading solenoid is controlled by the timer.

A changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts. On the main switchboard, the changeover switch is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. A multimeter includes a changeover switch and uses voltage and current for measurement; a clamp-on ammeter also uses current. Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree, and overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system.

Regarding fan faults, the fan operating state is controlled by the defrost timing relay; the fan should run when not defrosting; if in the defrost state, the fan stopping is a normal phenomenon rather than a fault; the fan stopping when not in the defrost state is judged as a fault and requires inspection and repair. To troubleshoot, first check the selector switch position and the operation of intermediate relay AX31; if contactor MC33 does not operate normally, check the coil circuit for an open circuit according to the schematic diagram; if both AX31 and MC33 operate normally, it is determined that the fan motor itself is faulty.

For troubleshooting the failure to defrost automatically, first place CS in the "DEFROST" position for manual defrosting to determine the scope of the fault. If manual defrosting succeeds, it indicates that the two sets of switches of the defrost timer cannot change over automatically, or it may be that selector switch CS is not properly closed in the automatic position; with aged changeover switches, poor contact of CS in the automatic position often causes this fault. If MC31 and MC32 operate normally but there is no heat, the defrost heater and fuse should be checked.

For troubleshooting the compressor failing to start, if the condenser fan does not turn, the fan fault should be eliminated first or the power circuit breakers 52C1/52C2 and the running switch 3-88 should be checked. If the fan turns but the compressor does not start, it is necessary to measure whether there is voltage in the compressor control circuit to judge the closing condition of 88/F. When there is voltage in the control circuit, it should be checked whether intermediate relay 4/2 operates; if it does not operate, measure the voltage across its coil. If relay 4/2 operates, further check relay 4/1 and the closed state of its normally open contact and the 52C auxiliary contact. If relay 88/CX does not operate, check the start button 3C/C, the 4/1 normally open contact and the temperature regulating relay 23LH. In the defrost control logic, the 88C contact not being closed may cause the compressor to have no power and fail to start.

For the fault of relatively large temperature changes, external high temperature (such as high seawater temperature) will affect the refrigeration effect, causing the room temperature to rise; this fault is easily triggered when the ship passes through high-temperature sea areas such as the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf in summer. Insufficient refrigerant due to leakage or low efficiency due to poor compressor maintenance are common causes. Placing the unloading selector switch in the unloading position for artificial unloading operation will cause insufficient refrigerating capacity, and misoperation of the automatic unloading switches 63CU1/63CU2 will form unexpected unloading operation.

The failure to start may be caused by power supply not connected, incorrect wiring of control equipment, undervoltage, stator winding phase-to-phase short circuit to earth, incorrect wiring, stator winding short circuit, excessive load or the brake not released, and a faulty reducer. The corresponding handling measures include: check the switch, fuse, and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately;

Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance, and poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults.

The technical requirements of the refrigerated container electrical control system include: the temperature regulation range inside the container is generally within ±30℃, and the regulation accuracy needs to be improved by controlling intermittent operation of the compressor, hot gas bypass of refrigerant, refrigerant flow and evaporator fan speed. When the temperature inside the container is lower than the set value, the refrigerated container electrical control system can perform electric heating; it can automatically perform unloading operation according to the size of the heat load, and automatically control the number of condenser fans according to the external environment and condenser pressure. Refrigerated container electrical control system maintenance is usually carried out before loading, and the maintenance content includes checking whether the evaporator fan motor mounting bolts are secured and tightened, checking whether there is dirt or oil sludge on the fan frame and cleaning it if necessary; checking whether the bolts of each panel of the refrigerating machine are tightened and whether the panel positions are correct, and checking whether each pressure and temperature sensor or relay is intact; checking the temperature recorder, and if it is a mechanical clockwork type recorder, leaving the key on the recorder; and checking the circuit connection points and contactors in the control system box.

The defrost control of the LAKEN5BD refrigerated container evaporator is activated by the frost-thickness microswitch 63DA on the evaporator; if a failure of automatic defrosting occurs, the microswitch should be checked first, and then the defrost termination thermostat 23D, the defrost control intermediate relay 2DX and the overtemperature protector 26AH. The CPE14-2BAⅢA refrigerated container is produced by Mitsubishi of Japan and adopts microcomputer control; on the display panel there are five indicator lamps respectively indicating the system operating conditions: the ALARM lamp flashing indicates fault alarm, the DEF red lamp on indicates defrosting, the IR orange lamp on indicates holding, the COOL green lamp on indicates cooling, and the HUM lamp on indicates dehumidification. The method of setting the temperature of the CPE14-2BAⅢA refrigerated container is: press the mode selection key MODE, and the ENTER input key to make the mode code flat-lit, then use the up/down keys to adjust to the required temperature, and finally press the ENTER key to confirm; the microcomputer then accepts the new setting and controls as required. The power supply of refrigerated containers is usually listed as the second-stage load to be cut off in the preferential tripping load shedding classification of container ships, the first stage being non-important loads such as engine repair tools and galley equipment. Refrigeration equipment includes refrigeration and air-conditioning control system maintenance.

According to the requirements of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, fault analysis should be carried out while keeping the site intact; observation is exactly a sub-step of this link. For the microcomputer-controlled electrical system of refrigerated containers, the maintenance of its peripheral equipment also follows this line of thinking. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; in the microcomputer-controlled electrical system of refrigerated containers, the maintenance objects include the contactors of the compressor, fans and electric heaters. Because containers are highly mobile, this maintenance is generally arranged before loading; it is necessary to check the loose connection points in the control system box, open circuits and component damage, and to carry out specific maintenance operations on the contactors of the compressor and fans. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker; the circuit breaker is a switching device used in the ship power system to protect circuits, belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus, is divided into frame type (air type) and molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability under short-circuit faults, and the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid.

Sensors are information acquisition devices of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed respectively in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; that is, the control platform contains sensors, and the sensors send error signals in the X-axis and Y-axis directions. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.
