Recording paper is the medium used for marine weather facsimile receivers and refrigerated container temperature recorders, recording weather charts or temperature curves; the recording paper is a consumable of the weather facsimile receiver, and when its remaining length is less than 1m there is an obvious mark to remind the user that it is about to run out; when paper jamming occurs, the equipment power should be turned off and the recording paper reinstalled. When replacing the recording paper of the electronic temperature recorder of a refrigerated container, the recording pen must first be lifted and then put back. The electrical control system of refrigerated containers has developed from the relay type to the microcomputer control type, featuring a wide temperature adjustment range, high constant-temperature precision, electric heating, automatic unloading and automatic control of the number of condenser fans.

Tightening is one of the maintenance steps of the PLC control system; in electrical maintenance it is used to ensure good contact of wiring terminals, screws and fastening mechanisms or to prevent loosening; the wiring screws of electromagnetic relays should be tightened to ensure good contact, while failure to tighten the external wiring screws of a thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be disconnected. The step of checking the power supply voltage must be carried out before the refrigeration compressor is energized; it is necessary to check whether the power supply voltage matches the position of the voltage selection switch; for motor starting, operation and electrical component faults, it is used to verify the matching of the power supply state with the rated value; when a three-phase asynchronous motor fails to start, according to the principle of from simple to complex, first check whether there is a power supply; when the motor speed is low after starting, first check whether the voltage is too low and whether the power supply has phase failure; when an AC electromagnet is noisy, the power supply voltage needs to be adjusted to the rated value

0.85~
1.10 times. Before the refrigeration compressor is energized and started, it is necessary to confirm that the power supply voltage matches the position of the voltage selection switch; when the electric fan starts slowly and the speed decreases and the cause is that the power supply voltage is too low, this check is carried out; when the electric drive motor fails to start due to undervoltage, the power supply voltage needs to be checked and appropriately raised. Before the refrigeration unit is energized and started, it is necessary to check whether the power supply voltage matches the position of the voltage selection switch; for faults such as slow starting of the electric fan, failure of the motor to start or excessive temperature rise, verify whether the supply voltage is within the allowable range; in the general inspection of the PLC, if the POWER lamp is off, the step of checking the power supply fault needs to be carried out; when the electric fan starts slowly, the maintenance method includes checking whether the power supply voltage is too low; when the electric drill fails to start and there is no voltage at the power supply, the power supply line should be checked. There is another point to note in the step of checking the power supply voltage, namely that before disassembly the circuit ends should be marked one by one clearly, so that when restoring the wiring the positions will not be connected wrongly.

The elevator is a commonly used living equipment on ships, composed of the traction machine, car, landing doors and electrical control system, and requires regular maintenance to ensure safe operation;

The temperature controller is an electrical control component in the refrigeration system of refrigerators and refrigerated containers, monitoring the temperature through a temperature-sensing element and controlling the start and stop of the compressor. When terminals 10 and 11 of the electronic temperature controller 23A1 are conducting, the liquid supply solenoid valve is energized and opens, and the compressor starts refrigerating; when the temperature inside the box reaches the set lower limit, terminals 10 and 11 of the electronic temperature controller 23A1 are disconnected, and the compressor stops running; when the defrost timer 2DX operates, its normally closed contact cuts off the circuit of the electronic temperature controller and the liquid supply solenoid valve for defrosting. In a refrigerator, if the motor does not start and there is no sound after energization, it may be because the temperature controller is disconnected or in the "stop point" position; loss of the temperature-sensing agent of the temperature controller will cause an open circuit, so that the refrigerator motor cannot start, and the temperature-sensing agent needs to be reset or the thermostat replaced.

Motor overload is a fault cause to be guarded against in the control circuits of refrigeration equipment. The structure of the fault tree is a logic tree, containing the top event, intermediate events and basic events, and the logic relationships are AND and OR; fault tree analysis uses the fault tree, which is a connected logic tree containing no closed loops, using graphic symbols to represent the logical combination among various events that cause an undesired event of the system, developing downward from the tree root of the top event, with branches representing accident events and nodes representing logic relationships, among which the most commonly used logic relationships are the "AND" and "OR" relationships. Failure of the motor to start is a common fault symptom of marine asynchronous motors and DC motors, referring to the state in which the motor cannot produce rotating torque or the speed is zero after energization; the main causes of failure to start of a three-phase cage asynchronous motor include no power supply, the motor internal fault and mechanical faults; when checking this fault, the principle of from simple to complex is followed: first check the power supply, then check whether the shaft is seized or the load is excessive, and finally check the interior of the motor. Power supply problems, mechanical problems, excessive load and motor internal fault will all cause the motor to fail to start; failure of the motor to start corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, and also corresponds to checking the motor internal fault; low motor speed after starting, high motor temperature rise, and excessive sparking under the brush all correspond to checking the power supply voltage.

In the maintenance of the electrical control circuits of refrigeration equipment, the first thing to solve is the question of where to start with the fault. This step belongs to the sub-link of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, "carrying out fault analysis while keeping the site intact", and its value lies in providing first-hand basis for subsequent judgment.

Unlike traditional methods that rely on experience, fault tree analysis uses the tool of the fault tree to sort out the ins and outs of the fault. The fault tree contains three levels: the top event, intermediate events and basic events, among which the most commonly used logic relationships are the AND relationship and the OR relationship. In the maintenance of the electrical control circuits of refrigeration equipment, phenomena such as failure of the motor to start and failure of the compressor to start are often selected as the top event, and the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as normal power supply and normal control circuit.

During diagnosis, instruments are needed to read voltage and current. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA, has the nature of a current source, and has an extremely large internal resistance; the standard current on the secondary side is 5A or 1A, and the load current I flowing through the primary side is transformed into the secondary current to be connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements; its secondary side must never be open-circuited, the terminals of the externally connected ammeter need to have a short-circuit connecting piece, and it can only be opened after the wiring has been checked. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. When the compressor unit fails to start and the condenser fan does not turn, the state of the power supply and the circuit breaker should be checked. The possible cause of the compressor unit failing to start is that the compressor motor itself fails to start or the motor has no power; if the condenser fan turns, it indicates that the compressor motor itself has a failure-to-start fault; if the condenser fan does not turn, it is necessary to check whether the circuit breakers 52C1, 52C2 and the running switch 3-88 are closed. If there is voltage across the two ends of the 88C coil but it does not start, it indicates that the 88C contact itself is faulty; if there is no voltage across the two ends of the 88C coil, it is necessary to check the state of each contact in the coil circuit. When the 63HL low-pressure switch is open, it is necessary to check whether there is voltage across the two ends of the liquid supply solenoid valve 20S. The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve. During maintenance, first check whether the frost-thickness microswitch 63DA is closed; if 63DA is closed but there is no operation, it is necessary to check the defrost termination thermostat 23D, the defrost control intermediate relay 2DX and the overtemperature protector 26AH. The main cause of the fault of large temperature variation inside the box is that the electronic temperature controller works abnormally; during maintenance, check whether the temperature-sensing element is intact, check whether the leads have broken strands or are loose, and check whether the shielded wire is well grounded; if routine inspection cannot locate the problem, use the substitution method to replace the spare electronic thermostat. The relay board is controlled by the alarm processing board and is used to drive external alarm and control equipment; it has two DC 24V/2A power outputs and three DC 24V/2A active signal outputs, four relay signal outputs with a capacity of 2A, and two signal outputs in open-collector form, driving equipment such as the general alarm system, alarm bell and fire door electromagnet. The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of the ship radar and monitoring system, used to present images, data and alarm information; it belongs to radar equipment, and radar equipment contains the display; the display should be installed on the bridge in a place free of strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources and dry, fixed with a hardwood base, with the main radar display oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge; the precautions for radar display installation need to pay attention to the display; radar installation applies to the display; the display contains two maintenance items: cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface.

Refrigerated containers include the link of refrigerated container electrical control system maintenance. The ship power grid is a component of the ship power station. The precautions for connecting shore power need to be attended to with respect to the ship power station.

Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker itself.

The circuit breaker may have the fault of the contact failing to close when the circuit breaker is operated manually, that is, when the circuit breaker is operated manually, its contact cannot close into position. Besides these two cases, the circuit breaker may also have the faults of one phase contact failing to close, the shunt trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open, the undervoltage trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open, the circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker automatically opening about 1h after closing, the undervoltage trip unit being noisy, the circuit breaker temperature rise being too high, the auxiliary switch failing, and the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctioning and causing the circuit breaker to open.

As far as the circuit breaker is concerned, the contact failing to close when the circuit breaker is operated manually is a common fault, and the contact failing to close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically is another common fault; when troubleshooting, the operating mode should first be distinguished as manual or electric, and then the corresponding transmission and tripping links should be checked separately. In addition, the circuit breaker may also have the case of one phase contact failing to close; at this time, the contact of that phase and its linkage components should be mainly checked; the shunt trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open and the undervoltage trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open indicate that the tripping circuit fails to operate normally; the circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor indicates that the circuit breaker trips under the impact of the motor starting current; the circuit breaker automatically opening about 1h after closing is a delayed automatic opening phenomenon; the undervoltage trip unit being noisy reflects abnormal operation of its electromagnetic mechanism; the circuit breaker temperature rise being too high indicates abnormal heating in the conductive circuit or contact parts; failure of the auxiliary switch will affect the signal and interlock functions of the circuit breaker; malfunction of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit will cause the circuit breaker to open before the setting conditions are reached. All the above faults may occur on the circuit breaker, and when troubleshooting they should be confirmed item by item in accordance with the requirements of circuit breaker maintenance.

Voltage is one of the measurable properties, and its measuring tools include the multimeter and voltmeter; the multimeter is used to measure voltage. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; the automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve. In the direct control mode, the warning lamp lights up through the contact of the shutter connected to the emergency power supply. The sensors are located in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, and their function is to send error signals.

Refrigeration and air-conditioning control system maintenance occupies a fixed position in the daily electrical upkeep of ships, and its control elements and detection elements are both scheduled for inspection at a period of once every 2 months. For the item of control elements, the focus is on confirming whether the interlocks of the cooling pump, fans, solenoid valves, control box, etc. are reliable; during inspection, the action sequence of the interlock circuits should be checked one by one, confirming whether the fans can be put into operation at the set delay after the cooling pump starts, whether the on-off of the pipeline after the solenoid valve is energized is consistent with the command, and whether each protection link in the control box can correctly cut off under abnormal conditions; for the item of detection elements, it is necessary to confirm whether the temperature and pressure switches operate flexibly; during inspection, the method of changing the set value or simulating temperature and pressure changes can be used to observe whether the switch can reliably operate and reset near the set value. Daily maintenance also requires regular cleaning of the contacts of each relay to ensure good contact, and regular checking of the setting values of the electrical appliances, which must not deviate too much; once the setting value shifts, it will directly affect the accuracy of the interlock actions and the reliability of the protection function. The automatic fuel oil boiler also includes control system maintenance content; the program actions of its sequence controller should be flexible and reliable, and during manual operation the sound and light alarm safety facilities should be effective and normal; during inspection, the program steps should be verified item by item according to the stages of startup, operation and shutdown, confirming that the alarm sound and light signals are issued synchronously and can be manually acknowledged.

The automatic fuel oil boiler also contains a solenoid valve and a servo motor. The servo motor is used to adjust the opening of the air damper and fuel valve; it rotates according to the output signal of the bridge, driving the feedback potentiometer to adjust, so that the bridge is rebalanced; as the actuator of the temperature recorder, an abnormality of the servo motor will trigger fault code 601; when this code appears, the servo motor winding, transmission mechanism and feedback circuit should be checked first. In boiler combustion regulation, the servo motor is controlled by the differential amplifier and thyristor to energize the winding, so as to adjust the air-fuel ratio; when rotating, it drives the sliding contact of the feedback potentiometer R10 to move, and stops after the bridge reaches balance again; if the bridge can never be balanced, the servo motor will continue to rotate or stop at the wrong position, and the air-fuel ratio will accordingly be disturbed.

The main radar display should face the observer toward the bow and be installed on the starboard side of the bridge; this arrangement allows the observer to take in both the sea ahead and the screen image. The display also includes two maintenance items: cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface. Cleaning the air filter ensures internal ventilation and heat dissipation, while surface cleaning should use soft materials to avoid scratching the screen or damaging the coating.

The control platform includes sensors. The sensors are arranged in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, and their function is to send out error signals; the current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA and is used to transform the current ratio. It has the nature of a current source, and the standard secondary current is usually 5A, with one end of the secondary side earthed; its types include coil type, busbar type, and through-type, and the through-type current transformer belongs to current transformers. The primary terminals of the current transformer are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary side by K1 and K2. During operation it is equivalent to a short-circuit transformer, and the secondary winding must never be open-circuited during operation; when open-circuited, the secondary side will generate a dangerously high voltage, so the secondary terminals must be short-circuited first during maintenance.

The multimeter uses voltage, current, and diode. When using a multimeter to measure voltage, the range should be set to the voltage range and connected in parallel with the circuit under test; when measuring current, it must be connected in series; when testing a diode, its unidirectional conductivity is used to determine polarity and condition.

Marine electrical equipment uses diodes. A diode has unidirectional conductivity, is commonly denoted VD in circuits, and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; under forward voltage it conducts with low resistance, and under reverse voltage its resistance is very large or infinite. By function it can be divided into rectifier diodes such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, Schottky diodes such as BAT85, etc. The measurable properties of a diode include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop, and reverse resistance; during measurement, the resistance range of a multimeter can be used to measure the forward and reverse resistances respectively, and an obvious difference in resistance indicates normal unidirectional conductivity. Diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. A light-emitting diode has unidirectional conductivity, its emission colors include red, green, yellow, etc., its dimensions include 3mm diameter, 5mm, and 2mm×5mm rectangular, its operating current is generally 1–30mA depending on the model, and its conduction voltage is above 1.7V; its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit operating status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display, and in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage. For light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes; before connecting to the circuit, confirm that the current-limiting resistor value is appropriate and the polarity is connected correctly. The diode testing procedure applies to diodes; during testing, first cut off the power and discharge, then judge item by item in the order of polarity, forward voltage drop, and reverse resistance.

In the maintenance of the electrical control circuits of refrigeration equipment, checking the electrical parameters at each point of the circuit is a basic means of determining the fault location. Measuring the current values of load circuits such as compressors and fans helps to grasp their operating status. Contactor maintenance is exactly the inspection and upkeep work carried out for the above components. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to various circuit breakers, and its common faults have various manifestations. A circuit breaker may suffer the fault of manual operation of the circuit breaker with contacts failing to close, that is, when operated manually the contacts cannot close normally; a circuit breaker may also suffer the fault of electric operation of the circuit breaker with contacts failing to close, that is, when operated electrically the contacts likewise cannot close. The above fault symptoms correspond to different inspection points respectively, and during maintenance the voltage and current measurement results should be used to troubleshoot item by item.

The temperature controller is an important component of the electrical control of the refrigeration system. Display maintenance includes two items: cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface. Radar installation applies to the installation work of the display.

The maintenance of the electrical control circuits of refrigeration equipment cannot be separated from the measurement and judgment of electrical quantities. Voltage and current are both electrical quantities to be measured by electrical instruments, and mastering their values helps to understand the state of the equipment. Voltage values can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter, and current values can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter, or clamp-on ammeter. When using an ammeter to measure current, the circuit must be disconnected and the instrument connected in series; a clamp-on ammeter can directly clamp onto the conductor to measure the current without cutting off the circuit. In the fault diagnosis of marine electrical equipment, voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked.

The alarm code of the air-conditioning system is directly related to the power supply state. The alarm code LO indicates low supply voltage, specifically defined as a voltage deviation exceeding 20%. The fault cause of low supply voltage will cause loud noise in AC electromagnets, and will also cause contact welding, low motor speed, and washing machine faults. That is to say, low supply voltage will cause loud noise in the electromagnet (AC); when the supply voltage of the AC electromagnet is low, the noise increases noticeably, and it should be adjusted to 0.85–1.10 times the rated voltage; when the contactor causes contact welding due to insufficient holding force, check whether the supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage. The voltage can also be checked, and if too low it should be raised appropriately; if necessary, replace the power supply or raise the voltage.

The fuse is a component of marine electrical equipment and a commonly used component in electronic circuits, listed alongside resistors, capacitors, etc. It is made of protective conductive material and has the characteristics of a low melting point and certain mechanical strength; common materials are aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy. During maintenance, check the control device contacts and fuse, check the switch, fuse, and each pair of contacts, and find the fault point.

The mechanical faults of refrigeration equipment motors also have their corresponding treatment methods. Uneven friction plate clearance, long-term high-speed friction, and friction plate deformation are among the causes of the fault. Low speed under load operation, and excessive motor temperature or smoking, are fault symptoms that need to be identified. During maintenance, check against the wiring diagram and correct it; find the short circuit and earthing parts and repair them. Check the stator current, reduce the load, check the stator current, and when overload is found, lighten the load. Check the broken bars and unsoldered points and repair them. Check the air gap between rotor and stator, and the clearance between brake wheel and brake band, find the cause of rubbing, and correct it. Cut off the power, then switch on again; if there is failure to start, one phase may be open-circuited; check the power supply and the motor and repair them.

Replace the damaged bearing. Check the loose points and tighten the coupling. Check whether the bearing and bearing housing are loose, whether the shaft is bent, and whether the stator-rotor assembly is defective, and repair them.

A broken connecting rod of one phase of the circuit breaker is a cause of circuit breaker faults. For circuit breakers, the maintenance procedure includes: check the circuit, apply voltage or replace the coil; replace the energy-storing spring; adjust the reclosing contact surface to the specified value; replace the power supply; increase the operating power supply capacity; readjust or replace the pull rod; replace the rectifier tube or capacitor; replace the connecting rod; adjust to the requirements specified in the original technical conditions; replace the power supply or raise the voltage; adjust the energy-storing spring; eliminate the cause of jamming; adjust the instantaneous setting spring of the overcurrent trip unit; replace the thermal element or semiconductor delay circuit element; remove oil contamination; replace the armature or core; adjust the contact pressure or replace the spring; replace the contact or clean the contact surface; straighten or reinstall the moving contact bridge; replace the transmission rod and roller or replace the entire auxiliary switch.

Conventional fault diagnosis method and its position in the diagnostic method system. There are many ways to analyze faults in marine electrical equipment, among which the analysis methods for electronic equipment faults cover three commonly used means: the conventional fault diagnosis method, fault tree analysis, and the expert system diagnostic method. The conventional fault diagnosis method, also called the empirical diagnostic method, is a marine electrical equipment diagnostic method that judges the fault point of equipment through fault symptom analysis and past experience and then eliminates it, and is one of the currently commonly used marine electrical equipment fault analysis methods. Its diagnostic accuracy mainly depends on the quality of the diagnostician, and its basis includes personal experience or past experience obtained from books, so maintenance personnel are required to master the equipment working principles and the fault characteristics of each component, which is especially important for offshore management and maintenance personnel.

Fault tree analysis is abbreviated as FTA. It uses a logical tree structure and includes the top event, intermediate events and basic events. It is a reliability evaluation method that analyzes system faults through a logical tree structure and originates from graph theory. It was first used by Bell Labs in the United States in the design of the Minuteman missile control system to predict random failure probabilities, and was later successfully applied in the WASH-1400 report, quantitatively giving the risk of nuclear power plants for the first time and proving their safety. Fault tree analysis uses a fault tree. A fault tree is a connected logical tree that does not contain closed loops, and uses graphical symbols to represent the logical combination among various events that cause an undesired event of the system. Its structure is a logical tree, including the top event, intermediate events and basic events, and the logical relationships are AND and OR. The fault tree develops downward from the tree root of the top event; the branches represent accident events, and the nodes represent logical relationships, among which the most commonly used logical relationships are the "AND" and "OR" relationships.

The expert system diagnosis method is based on expert knowledge and includes a knowledge base and an inference engine; it uses a fault diagnosis expert system for marine electrical equipment. An expert system is a computer model that uses expert reasoning methods to handle complex problems that require analysis and judgment by experts. In the marine field it is used for fault diagnosis of highly automated electrical equipment, and its output results are consistent with the analysis results of human experts.

Implementation steps of the conventional fault diagnosis method The conventional fault diagnosis method uses a series of steps such as interviewing the operator, observation, check the monitoring and indicating device, making the fault symptom reappear when conditions permit, inspection using the five senses, evaluation of inspection results, determination of system structure and test methods, and system testing. These steps have a clear sequential relationship among them.

Interviewing the operator is the first step of fault analysis under the condition of keeping the site unchanged in the conventional fault diagnosis steps; the inquiry process conducted by maintenance personnel to the operator refers to this. The inquiry content includes the fault occurrence situation, time, equipment and operating duration; it is necessary to confirm whether abnormal phenomena such as sound, light alarm, smoke or peculiar smell have been noticed, to check whether there is any misoperation, and to pay attention to the inquiry method, asking whether the control system operates normally and whether the operating procedure has changed, and also to understand whether there were special difficulties or abnormal conditions during operation.

Interviewing the operator precedes observation. Observation belongs to a sub-link of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "fault analysis under the condition of keeping the site unchanged", and its content includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters. Specifically, it is necessary to observe whether parts are stuck or damaged, whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt, to observe changes in equipment operating parameters, and whether there are obvious interference signals or damage signals; when conditions permit, the equipment may be restarted to make the fault symptom reappear so as to observe carefully. Observation is the in-depth process of the sensory inspection means "looking" in the second step "inspection using the five senses". When identifying the type of transistor, it is necessary to observe the magnitude and direction of the multimeter pointer deflection; when testing the performance of a thermistor, insert it into hot water and observe the change of the resistor value with temperature.

Observation precedes check the monitoring and indicating device. Check the monitoring and indicating device belongs to the inspection objects of the "observation" link in the conventional fault diagnosis steps, and its inspection content includes instrument readings, alarm devices, interlock devices, print output or display. It is necessary to check whether all instrument readings are normal, such as voltage, frequency, current, etc.; to check whether the alarm devices and interlock devices are normal; and to check whether the print output or display is normal. Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis, and its voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter; the failure of a generator to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree, overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems, and no residual magnetism voltage will cause the generator to fail to build up voltage. Current is likewise a reading to be checked, and its current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter;

The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of the ship's radar and monitoring system, used to present images, data and alarm information. It should be installed in the wheelhouse in a dry place free of strong electromagnetic radiation and away from heat sources, fixed with a hardwood base, with the main radar display oriented so that the observer faces the bow, and installed on the starboard side of the bridge. This step belongs to the observation link in the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "conducting fault analysis while keeping the site intact"; the operation method is to restart the equipment when conditions permit, with the purpose of carefully observing the fault symptom; during execution, personal and equipment safety must be ensured, and the fault result must strictly not be allowed to expand.

When conditions permit, reproduce the fault symptom before using the five senses for inspection. Inspection using the five senses belongs to the second step of equipment inspection and is a process of continued in-depth observation; its inspection methods are looking, touching, listening, smelling and checking. "Looking" includes checking plugs and sockets, motor operation, control positions and whether there are signs of arcing and burning, and also includes opening circuit switches to check for faulty components; "touching" is used to sense vibration and the temperature of motors and components; "listening" is used to judge whether the equipment has abnormal sounds; "smelling" is used to detect whether there is a burnt smell or other unusual odor.

Evaluate the inspection results before inspection using the five senses. Evaluating the inspection results belongs to the second step of the equipment inspection process, that is, after inspection using the five senses; its evaluation content includes whether the fault judgment is correct, whether fault clues have been found, and whether the various inspection results are consistent. One of the core tasks is to evaluate whether the fault judgment is correct, and it is necessary to confirm whether effective fault clues have been found, requiring logical consistency among the various inspection results; this link is located before determining the fault location, that is, the third step.

Determine the system structure and test method before evaluating the inspection results.

Perform system detection before determining the system structure and test method. During system detection, the measurement method most suitable for the system structure must be adopted; the operating requirement is to measure at appropriate test points and compare the results obtained from input and feedback with normal values or performance; this step aims to finally check out the fault location and belongs to the link of further careful inspection using the five senses or instruments.

Criteria and personnel requirements of conventional fault diagnosis. The criteria of conventional fault diagnosis include being familiar with the equipment, understanding the fault symptom, determining the inspection method, and keeping records; these criteria require attention to the conventional fault diagnosis method. The criteria require maintenance personnel to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of components (assemblies) of electrical equipment, and stipulate the use of the five sensory methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling to understand the fault symptom, aiming to preliminarily diagnose the location or cause of the fault through sensory inspection.

Maintenance personnel are responsible for fault diagnosis and repair of marine electrical equipment, need to be familiar with equipment principles, structure and repair materials, and are required to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of components (assemblies) of electrical equipment, by the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. In conventional fault diagnosis, it is necessary to understand the symptom and make a preliminary diagnosis through asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, and one must be very familiar with the ship-wide electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components; diagnostic accuracy mainly depends on personnel quality and the thoroughness of mastery of equipment technical performance. During maintenance, one must be familiar with the performance of electrical materials such as conductive and insulating materials and select them reasonably; in the maintenance of DC motors, good contact between the brush and the commutator must be ensured, and the surface must be clean and smooth.

Radar equipment includes the display; the display belongs to radar equipment; the display includes cleaning of the display air filter and cleaning of the display surface; precautions for radar display installation require attention to the display; radar installation applies to the display.

Fault tree analysis is an analysis method used for faults of electronic equipment; its English abbreviation is FTA, and its full name is Fault Tree Analysis. This method carries out reliability evaluation of system faults through a logical tree structure, and its concept comes from graph theory. Fault tree analysis was first used by Bell Laboratories in the United States for the design of the Minuteman missile control system, with the purpose of predicting random failure probability; thereafter it was successfully applied in the WASH-1400 report, quantitatively giving the risk of nuclear power plants for the first time and proving their safety.

In the diagnosis of marine electrical equipment, fault tree analysis can be used to analyze the causes of a generator failing to build up voltage; in troubleshooting main engine failure to start, it is also called the fault signal flow chart tracing method.

The analytical tool used in fault tree analysis is the fault tree. Structurally, the fault tree belongs to the logic tree; it is a connected graph composed of vertices and edges that contains no closed loops, and it uses graphical symbols to represent the logical combinations among the various events that cause an undesired event of the system. The fault tree develops downward from the tree root of the top event; the branches represent accident events, and the nodes represent logical relationships, of which the most commonly used logical relationships are "AND" and "OR". When building a fault tree, generally one certain fault of the electrical equipment is selected as the top event, for example, motor fails to start. As many fault trees as there are kinds of faults of a device should be established correspondingly. The fault tree is also a foundation for developing an expert system for equipment fault diagnosis. During diagnosis, the branch-cutting method can be adopted, starting the check from an intermediate event, so as to effectively reduce the scope of inspection.

The fault tree contains three types of events: top event, intermediate event and basic event. The top event is located at the top of the fault tree, that is, at the tree root position, and represents the undesired event of the system; the events at the next level below it are the intermediate events or basic events that can cause it to occur. When building a fault tree, usually one specific fault of the electrical equipment is selected as the top event, such as motor fails to start. The top event is connected with the next-level events through logical relationships such as "AND" and "OR", until the component fault is traced. For complex large-scale systems, the faults of subsystems can be taken as top events to build subtrees, and finally synthesized with transfer symbols. During the diagnosis process, if a certain intermediate event occurs, it can be regarded as a new top event and checked downward to locate the fault point.

The intermediate event is between the top event and the basic event and represents an event caused by other events. In the fault tree symbol table, the intermediate event is defined as a result event, formed by the combination of other events, and intermediate events are connected with each other through logic gates (such as AND gate and OR gate). When building a fault tree, selecting appropriate intermediate events can make the hierarchy and logical thinking clearer; in complex systems, the faults of subsystems can be taken as intermediate events, and then subtrees can be built for analysis. When diagnosing faults, the branch-cutting method can be adopted, starting the check from a certain level of intermediate event to narrow the scope; if a certain intermediate event has not occurred, the check of the basic events associated with it can be excluded.

The basic event is located at the bottom of the fault tree and represents a basic fault event, having the attribute of being no longer decomposable. In the fault tree, the basic event is linked with the fault event represented by the top event, and belongs to the inherent fault event inside the system or an event in the path leading to the top event. The basic event is one of the fundamental elements used in fault tree analysis for diagnosing faults of marine electrical equipment.

In marine electrical fault diagnosis, voltage and current are two basic electrical quantities that need to be measured. Measuring current requires an ammeter, which is connected in series after the circuit is disconnected. During fault diagnosis, it is necessary to check whether the current reading in the monitoring and indicating device is normal. The symbol corresponding to the current transformer is TA; it has the nature of a current source, with extremely large internal resistance, and the standard current on the secondary side is 5A or 1A. The load current I flows through the primary side of the current transformer and is transformed into the secondary current to be connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements; its secondary side must strictly not be open-circuited, the terminals for the externally connected ammeter must have short-circuit connecting pieces, and these may be removed only after the wiring has been checked.

Motor fails to start is a common fault symptom of marine asynchronous motors and DC motors, referring to the state in which the motor cannot produce rotating torque or the speed is zero after being energized. The main causes of failure to start of three-phase cage asynchronous motors include no power supply, fault of the motor itself and mechanical fault. When checking this fault, the principle of from simple to complex is followed: first check the power supply, then check whether the shaft is seized or the load is excessive, and finally check the interior of the motor. In a single-speed non-reversible AC drive system, the direct causes leading to failure to start include motor fault, no power and mechanical seizure. If the contactor KM is not closed, the motor will have no power, and its root cause may be coil fault, armature seizure or open circuit of the control circuit. During the check, if KM is closed but the motor does not turn, other intermediate events need to be investigated; if KM is not closed, check downward along that branch. The eight major causes of failure to start of asynchronous motors cover no power supply, winding short circuit or open circuit, shaft seizure and excessive load, etc.; the main causes of failure to start of DC motors include absence of power supply, low voltage, brush jamming and open circuit of the excitation circuit.

When constructing a fault tree, failure to start is often selected as the top event of electrical equipment, such as motor fails to start. The boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as normal power supply and normal control circuit. Motor fails to start corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, and also corresponds to checking the motor internal fault. The power supply not being connected will cause failure to start; at this time, the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts should be checked to find the fault point. Incorrect wiring of the control equipment will cause failure to start; at this time, the wiring diagram should be checked and corrected. Undervoltage will cause failure to start; at this time, the power supply voltage should be checked, and if it is indeed too low, it should be appropriately raised. Stator winding short circuit between phases and earthing, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start; at this time, the short circuit and open circuit locations should be found and repaired, and if the wiring is incorrect, the wiring should be corrected. Excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer will cause failure to start; at this time, the load should be reduced, and the motor and reducer should be separated; if the motor can run normally, the reducer part should be checked.

Power supply problems will cause the motor to fail to start, mechanical problems will cause the motor to fail to start, excessive load will also cause the motor to fail to start, and motor internal fault will likewise cause the motor to fail to start. Excessive load is one of the basic causes (leaves) in the motor overheating fault tree, and is also one of the eight aspects of causes for failure to start of a three-phase asynchronous motor; when the motor fails to start, it is necessary to check whether the load is excessive to eliminate mechanical faults. A power supply fault will cause the RUN lamp to go out; at this time, check the power supply accordingly. In an AC electric drive system, a power supply fault is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent and thus overheating; a power supply fault is also an electrical supply abnormality cause of motor overheating, PLC control system faults and main engine remote control failure. In the PLC control system, because the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, the ship usually adopts a whole-unit replacement strategy; the PLC power supply fault check process starts with the POWER lamp status, and if it is out, the power supply, fuse and light-emitting diode are checked in sequence.

In an AC electric drive system, motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating, and winding partial short circuit or phase failure is one of the main fault causes of AC motor overcurrent and overheating. Deterioration of heat dissipation conditions is one of the indirect causes of motor overheating, belongs to the basic fault leaf node under the intermediate event "poor motor heat dissipation", is parallel with fan blade fault, and together they constitute the direct factors causing poor motor heat dissipation; it is one of the nine basic causes (leaves) of motor overheating. Deterioration of heat dissipation conditions will cause the motor temperature rise to be high. Bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in an AC electric drive system, and belongs to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and the characteristic of bearing end cover overheating. Checking bearing fault itself requires the use of the bearing, and checking the lubrication condition also requires the use of the bearing. A marine motor contains a bearing and a winding. The bearing is a mechanical component of the motor, used to support the rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration and abnormal noise. Ship motors work under long-term conditions of 15° list, 7.5° trim and 22.5° roll, which places higher requirements on the bearing structure. Before removing the end cover of a DC motor, the bearing outer cover must first be removed; if the wear is not serious, it is generally not necessary to remove the bearing, and it is only necessary to clean and replace the grease.

A winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force. The winding insulation of a marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture proofing, mildew proofing and salt-oil-mist proofing and be oil resistant; the cold-state insulation resistance of a marine motor winding shall not be less than 5MΩ, and the hot-state insulation resistance shall not be less than 2MΩ.

The main switchboard contains the main switch, and the main switch is used to control the connection between the generator and the power grid. The main switch is an air circuit breaker used in the ship's power station to connect and disconnect the generator and the main busbar, has both switching and protection functions, and is mainly composed of undervoltage, shunt and overcurrent trip units and an arc extinguishing device, etc. The main switch belongs to the undervoltage release, belongs to the shunt release, belongs to the overcurrent protection device, belongs to the arc extinguishing device, belongs to the auxiliary contact, and also belongs to the control and signal indication circuit. The DW14 circuit breaker introduces Japanese Terasaki technology and is provided with an AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit.

The generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; absence of residual magnetism voltage will cause the generator to fail to build up voltage; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems; when U_n0 > U_fe, it indicates that the voltage corrector has no main regulating action.

Fault tree analysis (FTA) applied in the maintenance of marine electrical equipment is developed around the fault tree, a graphical logic model; that is, fault tree analysis uses the fault tree as its analysis tool. The contactor contains a coil, and the coil is a component of marine electrical equipment; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; a jammed armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failing to start.

In a single-speed non-reversible AC electric drive system, motor internal fault is one of the direct causes of failure to start, referring to faults in internal components such as the motor stator winding and bearing, which will cause the motor to fail to start, automatic start failure, or excessive temperature rise; faults in the motor stator winding, bearing, etc. will also produce the phenomenon of excessive temperature rise, and in severe cases the motor overheats or even burns out. In the onboard single-speed non-reversible direct-on-line start control system, motor internal fault is one of the two major categories of common faults; apart from the main power supply, it is also a possible cause of the pump auxiliary unit failing to start automatically. In the marine auxiliary machinery electrical system, motor internal fault and control system fault are listed together as the two major categories of common faults. In a single-speed non-reversible AC electric drive system, the direct causes of failure to start include the motor internal fault, no power, and mechanical jamming. If KM has not closed, check downward along that branch.

Among the analysis methods for electronic equipment faults, the expert system diagnostic method is one category; it uses a computer model to simulate the expert's process of analysis and judgment, to handle complex problems that usually require an expert to solve. Its use in the marine field is embodied in the marine electrical equipment fault diagnosis expert system, which carries out fault diagnosis for complex, highly automated electrical equipment, and its inference results are consistent with the analysis conclusions of human experts.

The marine electrical equipment fault diagnosis expert system consists of a knowledge base, an inference mechanism, an explanation mechanism, an inquiry mechanism, a knowledge acquisition mechanism, and a fault feature vector storage mechanism. Among them, the knowledge base undertakes the task of storing professional theoretical knowledge in the marine electrical field as well as electrical fault diagnosis experience, and is one of the core components of the whole system; the inference mechanism judges the fault point based on fault features and relevant theoretical knowledge and experience, and is likewise a core component of the system. The function of the explanation mechanism is to explain the expert's inference conclusions to the inquirer, so that people are convinced of the diagnosis result; the inquiry mechanism is responsible for contacting the developer and the user; the knowledge acquisition mechanism is used to modify the knowledge in the knowledge base;

the fault feature vector storage mechanism, in parallel with the knowledge base, inference mechanism, explanation mechanism, etc., is specially used to store fault feature vectors.

When the system runs, it first collects fault symptom features through the inquiry mechanism, stores them into the fault feature vector, and then queries the knowledge base for inference. The inference mechanism carries out logical inference based on the fault feature vector and the professional theory and experience in the knowledge base; during operation it may inquire of the user multiple times to supplement fault feature information, and passes the final inference conclusion result to the explanation mechanism. After receiving the output result of the inference mechanism, the explanation mechanism explains the whole process of fault diagnosis to the user in easy-to-understand or natural language. The knowledge in the knowledge base is not fixed and unchanging; it can be modified after experimental operation through the inquiry mechanism and the knowledge acquisition mechanism, to meet the needs of experimental operation. In the development stage, tools such as PC and CM.1 can be used to establish the inquiry, knowledge acquisition, inference and explanation mechanisms; these mechanisms are pre-established in expert system development tools such as PC and CM.1 and need not be rebuilt. Knowledge acquisition is the most critical step in system development and determines the quality; when establishing the knowledge base, the collected written theory and expert experience must be input into the computer according to the tool format, and production rules are often used to represent knowledge, or a frame structure may also be used to represent knowledge. Fault tree analysis is the foundation for developing an equipment fault diagnosis expert system.

The controllable phase compound excitation constant voltage device is applied to marine electrical equipment, and the fault diagnosis of this device can adopt fault tree analysis, with the corresponding schematic diagram as shown. This device may exhibit such fault symptoms as the generator being unable to build up voltage, generator no-load voltage low, and generator no-load voltage high, and these three phenomena all belong to the fault manifestations of the controllable phase compound excitation constant voltage device. If the residual magnetism voltage polarity is correct and the brush and rotor are not open-circuited, it is determined to be a phase compound excitation device fault; the phase compound excitation device fault may be caused by a rectifier fault, with its credibility recorded as X1, may be caused by a phase-shifting reactor open circuit, with its credibility recorded as X2, and may also be caused by a compound excitation transformer fault, with its credibility recorded as X3.

As for the electric traction motor, the fault symptom of failure to start may be caused by various reasons. The power supply not being connected will cause failure to start, and during troubleshooting it is necessary to check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; incorrect wiring of the control equipment will cause failure to start, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check against the wiring diagram and correct it; undervoltage will cause failure to start; stator winding phase-to-phase short circuit and earthing, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start, and during troubleshooting the short circuit and open circuit parts should be found and repaired; excessive load or the brake not being released, and a fault in the reducer will also cause failure to start, and troubleshooting methods include reducing the load or separating the motor from the reducer for testing.

Under the load operation state, undervoltage will cause the speed to be low during load operation, excessive load or the brake not being released, and a fault in the reducer will cause the speed to be low during load operation, and bearing damage will likewise cause the speed to be low during load operation. The phenomenon of abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation may be caused by mechanical friction, manifested as mechanical rubbing caused by an abnormal air gap between the rotor and stator or an abnormal clearance of the brake components, and during troubleshooting it is necessary to check the air gap between the rotor and stator as well as the clearance between the brake wheel and the brake band; it may also be caused by two-phase operation, and if it cannot start after power-off and re-closing, there may be an open circuit in one phase causing two-phase operation, and it is necessary to check the power supply and the motor and repair them; bearing damage will cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and the treatment method is to replace the damaged bearing; a bent shaft extension will cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and the treatment method is to replace the shaft; loose coupling connection will cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check the loose places and tighten the coupling.

The phenomenon of motor temperature rise too high or smoking may be caused by excessive load or the brake not being released, and a fault in the reducer, may be caused by two-phase operation, may be caused by undervoltage, may be caused by stator winding phase-to-phase short circuit and earthing, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit, may be caused by mechanical friction, and may also be caused by poor ventilation and heat dissipation, the latter referring to the state that hinders heat dissipation and air circulation, and during troubleshooting it is necessary to remove objects obstructing ventilation to restore the heat dissipation conditions. Bearing overheating may be caused by bearing damage, and may also be caused by insufficient lubricating oil or impurities, and for insufficient lubricating oil or impurities the troubleshooting method is to replace the bearing. The motor casing being live may be caused by poor earthing, and it is necessary to find the cause and take corresponding measures to correct it; it may also be caused by the winding being damp, insulation damage or dirt on the terminal board, and for the winding being damp it is necessary to carry out drying treatment of the stator winding; it may also be caused by worn insulation of the lead-out wires. In addition, undervoltage will also cause difficulty in starting, reduced speed, excessive temperature rise or poor contactor pull-in of marine electrical equipment; when the electric fan starts slowly and its speed decreases, the possible reason is that the power supply voltage is too low; when the electric fan cannot start, bearing damage is a possible mechanical reason, and the treatment method is to replace the bearing; when the electric drill speed is too slow, the possible reason is that the power supply voltage is too low, and it is necessary to check and adjust.

In the fault diagnosis of marine electrical equipment, fault tree analysis belongs to the analysis method for electronic equipment faults, and it uses the fault tree as a tool to carry out the analysis. A fault tree is a connected logic tree that does not contain closed loops, using graphical symbols to represent the logical combinations among various events that cause unwanted events of the system, and its structure includes the top event, intermediate event and basic event, developing downward from the tree root of the top event, with branches representing accident events and nodes representing logical relationships, among which the most commonly used logical relationships are the AND relationship and the OR relationship. Fault tree analysis originates from graph theory, was first used by Bell Laboratories of the United States in the design of the Minuteman missile control system to predict random failure probability, and was successfully applied in the WASH-1400 report, quantitatively giving the risk of nuclear power plants for the first time and proving their safety; it is a reliability evaluation method that analyzes system faults through a logic tree structure.

The fault diagnosis expert system for marine electrical equipment includes a knowledge base. The knowledge base is one of the core components of the fault diagnosis expert system for marine electrical equipment, and its function is to store professional theoretical knowledge in the marine electrical field as well as electrical fault diagnosis experience; the stored content includes professional theoretical knowledge in the marine electrical field and electrical fault diagnosis experience. The inference mechanism performs logical inference and judgment on the fault feature vector based on the knowledge in the knowledge base, and the knowledge therein can be modified after experimental operation through the inquiry mechanism and the knowledge acquisition mechanism. An expert system is a computer model using expert inference methods, used to handle complex problems that require expert analysis and judgment; in the marine field it is used for fault diagnosis of highly automated electrical equipment, and its output results are consistent with the analysis results of human experts. It consists of a knowledge base, an inference mechanism, an explanation mechanism, an inquiry mechanism, etc., among which knowledge acquisition is the most critical step in system development and determines the quality, and production rules or frame structures are often used to represent knowledge.

The generator being unable to build up voltage refers to the fault symptom in which the generator cannot establish an output voltage under the condition of having residual magnetism voltage; its causes include the generator having no residual magnetism voltage, an excitation circuit fault, and a phase compound excitation device fault. If the generator has no residual magnetism voltage, the generator needs to be magnetized; if the generator has residual magnetism voltage but cannot build up voltage, it is determined to be an excitation circuit fault; in an uncontrollable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, an open circuit of the phase-shifting reactor will cause the generator to be unable to build up voltage. The phase-shifting reactor is used to regulate voltage and is a key element in the phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, used to regulate voltage and realize reactive load sharing of generators in parallel operation; if the air gap of the phase-shifting reactor is too large, it will cause the terminal voltage of the generator to be higher than the rated value, and if the air gap of the phase-shifting reactor is too small, it will cause the terminal voltage of the generator to be lower than the rated value. The rectifier converts alternating current into direct current; in a controllable phase compound excitation constant-voltage device, a rectifier fault is one of the sub-causes of the phase compound excitation device fault; if the UR rectifier has an open-circuit diode, it will cause a voltage deviation of |U0-Ufe| greater than ΔU1.

The brush contacts the collector ring to transfer current; an open circuit between the brush and the collector ring is one of the causes of the phase compound excitation device fault; the marine motor includes brushes, and brushes are required for checking the contact condition between the brush and the commutator, checking the brush holder condition, and checking the brush position.

The low no-load voltage fault of the generator has multiple causes, and the possibilities of the causes differ; its causes include the UR rectifier having an open-circuit diode, VT being fully conducting, and the L inductance increasing. The analysis of this fault needs to give credibility X1, X2, X3 according to component failure rates or expert experience, and this fault corresponds to the corresponding fault tree structure. In the fault tree of the generator output voltage being lower than the rated value, an open-circuit diode of the UR rectifier is one of the possible causes; in the generator U0<Ufe fault, if |U0-Ufe|>ΔU1, it may be caused by an open-circuit diode of the UR rectifier.

A diode has unidirectional conductivity and is commonly represented by VD in circuits; it is used for rectification, isolation, voltage regulation, etc. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite. According to function, it is divided into rectifier diodes such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, Schottky diodes such as BAT85, etc., and also includes light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The measurable performance of a diode includes polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop, and reverse resistance; the diode detection steps are applicable to diodes, marine electrical equipment uses diodes, and the multimeter is also used to detect diodes. The electrical graphic symbol of the full-wave bridge rectifier is UR; the RS_0 fuse is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers and their complete sets of equipment, and the RS_3 fuse is used for internal short circuit protection of thyristor rectifiers and their complete sets of equipment.

Generator no-load voltage high is manifested as the no-load voltage being higher than the rated value and the voltage corrector having no main regulating action; when the no-load voltage Un0 is greater than the rated voltage Ufe, it is judged that the voltage corrector has no main regulating action, that is, when Un0>Ufe it indicates that the voltage corrector has no main regulating action. The voltage corrector having no main regulating action may be caused by VT open circuit, may be caused by bleeder resistor open circuit, and may also be caused by VT having no trigger pulse. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, bleeder resistor open circuit will cause the voltage corrector to have no main regulating action. The multimeter is used to measure resistor, voltage and diode; the measurable performance of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and the voltmeter; voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing the fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems.

Basic composition of the fault tree The fault tree analysis method is carried out with the aid of the fault tree as a tool in the diagnosis of marine electrical equipment. The fault tree is a connected logic tree that does not contain closed loops; it uses graphical symbols to represent the logical combination relationships among the various events that cause the undesired event of the system. From the overall form, the fault tree develops downward from the tree root of the top event, the branches represent accident events, and the nodes represent logical relationships. Structurally, the fault tree is composed of the top event, intermediate event and basic event, that is, the fault tree contains the top event, the fault tree contains the intermediate event, and the fault tree contains the basic event. The most commonly used logical relationships in the fault tree are the AND relationship and the OR relationship: the AND relationship indicates that the output event occurs only when all input events occur simultaneously, and the OR relationship indicates that the output event occurs when any one of the input events occurs. Taking the generator failing to build up voltage as an example, it can be used as the top event selected when constructing the fault tree, and from this it is decomposed layer by layer downward until the basic event is found.

Role of electrical instruments in diagnosis Electrical instruments are the basic means of acquiring operating parameters in the maintenance and diagnosis of marine electrical equipment. Classified by application, electrical instruments can measure electrical quantities such as current, voltage, power, phase and frequency; after conversion by transducers, electrical instruments can also indirectly measure non-electrical quantities such as temperature, pressure and speed. Classified by working principle, electrical instruments are divided into magnetoelectric, electromagnetic, electrodynamic, induction, rectifier types, etc.; classified by measured object, electrical instruments are divided into ammeter, voltmeter, wattmeter, frequency meter and multi-purpose meters.

Measurement of voltage and current Voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis. To measure the voltage value, a multimeter can be used, and a voltmeter can also be used; the multimeter is used for voltage measurement, and the voltmeter is likewise used for voltage measurement. The generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing the fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems.

Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status. To measure current, an ammeter is needed, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit; a multimeter can also be used to measure current, and the multimeter is used for current measurement; the clamp-on ammeter is used for current measurement and can acquire the current value without cutting off the circuit. The measurement results of voltage and current, together with electrical quantity parameters such as power, phase and frequency, jointly provide the basis for determining the top event, intermediate event and basic event of the fault tree, enabling the fault tree analysis method to be practically applied in the diagnosis of marine electrical equipment.

Classification and application of electrical instruments Electrical instruments undertake the tasks of measuring electrical quantities and indirectly measuring non-electrical quantities in the maintenance of marine electrical equipment. Classified by working principle, the common types are magnetoelectric, electromagnetic, electrodynamic, induction, rectifier, etc.; classified by measured object, there are ammeter, voltmeter, wattmeter, frequency meter and multi-purpose meters; classified by type of working current, they can be divided into DC instruments, AC instruments and AC/DC dual-purpose instruments; classified by mode of use, there are two types: panel-mounted (switchboard-type) and portable instruments; classified by reading mode, they can be further divided into pointer type, digital type and recording type. In terms of accuracy class, electrical instruments include

5.0 seven levels. These instruments can be used to measure electrical quantities such as current, voltage, power, phase, frequency, etc., and after conversion by converters they can also indirectly measure non-electrical quantities such as temperature, pressure, speed, etc.

The structure of a typical instrument, the wattmeter, also called a watt meter, is used to measure electrical power; it consists of a current coil and a voltage coil, and calculates power by detecting the load current and voltage. The current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the two ends of the measured circuit to detect the voltage. The current coil and the voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals (such as "*"), and during measurement the currents of the two coils must flow in or out from these terminals at the same time.

The multimeter contains a measuring circuit internally, which is used to convert different electrical quantities and ranges into signals measurable by the meter head. The multimeter can be used to measure voltage and current. The clamp-on ammeter is likewise used to measure current. The voltmeter is used to measure the voltage between two points in a circuit; voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status, and equipment operating parameters, specifically involving whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt.

Before measurement, observe the symbol markings on the dial to understand the performance characteristics of the instrument, and carefully read the instrument's instruction manual to understand the precautions for use of the instrument and the working conditions required by the instrument (placement position, temperature, external magnetic field, AC current waveform and frequency). Before use, the symbol markings on the dial must be observed to understand the performance characteristics of the instrument, and the instruction manual must be carefully read to grasp the precautions and required working conditions. The working conditions required by the instrument specifically include placement position, temperature and external magnetic field; AC current waveform and frequency are also key working conditions to be confirmed before using the instrument.

Wiring and reading during measurement: during measurement, connect the instrument correctly into the measured circuit. When using a voltmeter to measure the voltage between two points in a circuit, the two test probes should be connected directly in parallel across these two points; when using an ammeter to measure the current of the branch in which a certain point of the circuit is located, the wire at that point should first be disconnected, and then the two broken ends should be connected respectively to the two test probes of the ammeter. When measuring current, the wire at the measured point should first be disconnected, and then the broken ends connected respectively to the ammeter test probes. Before use, it is necessary to understand the instrument's working condition requirements for AC current waveform and frequency. When measuring DC current and AC current, the wiring methods should respectively meet the measurement requirements of their respective current types.

For instruments requiring mechanical zeroing or electrical zeroing, the indication should also first be adjusted to zero before measurement. For pointer-type instruments, the eye must face the pointer directly when reading; when reading the value of a pointer-type instrument, the eye must face the pointer directly.

Precautions for use: the dials of voltmeters, ammeters and wattmeters used on ships should have obvious markings indicating their rated values; the dials of ship-used instruments should have obvious markings indicating the rated values. The instrument casing must not be opened arbitrarily or the internal mechanism taken out; it is forbidden to arbitrarily open the instrument casing or take out the internal mechanism.

It is strictly forbidden to place the instrument beside a generator, motor or strong-current wire; it is strictly forbidden to place the instrument in places with high temperature or sharp changes of cold and heat; it is strictly forbidden to place the instrument in places with corrosive gas; it is strictly forbidden to place the instrument in dark and damp places. It is forbidden to place the instrument in places with high temperature, sharp changes of cold and heat, or dark and damp places, and the instrument must not be placed in an environment with corrosive gas. The instrument should avoid high temperature, sharp changes of cold and heat and corrosive gas environments, and should avoid being stored in dark and damp places.

A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument, and its basic structure can be divided into three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; that is, the multimeter contains the meter head, the multimeter contains the changeover switch, and the multimeter contains the measuring circuit. The meter head generally uses a high-sensitivity moving-coil instrument as the measuring mechanism, and the current flowing through the meter head at full-scale deflection is roughly between a few microamperes and several hundred microamperes.
