The shaft is a mechanical transmission component used to transmit torque and rotational motion, commonly found in motors, contactors, and instruments; the movable parts of the two units of the electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; during contactor maintenance, the flexibility of the operating mechanism must be checked manually at regular intervals, and a small amount of lubricating oil must be injected into the shaft (if a bearing is present). The measurable performance of photoelectric power is the power value, and the measuring tool is the wattmeter. Electrodynamic instruments, induction instruments, rectifier instruments, electrostatic instruments, thermoelectric instruments, and electronic instruments all belong to the types of electrical instruments.

Audio level test steps: insert the red probe into the "dB" jack -> select the range -> connect the circuit under test -> read the value. Resistance measurement steps: select the range -> zero the meter head -> connect the test circuit or component -> read the value. Transistor measurement steps: determine the tube type and base -> determine the emitter and collector -> performance test -> estimate the current amplification factor. Thyristor measurement steps: determine the polarity -> measure the inter-electrode resistance.

Wattmeter wiring rules: connect the current coil in series into the circuit -> connect the voltage coil in parallel into the circuit -> mark the corresponding terminals.

Basic requirements for maintenance personnel: personnel engaged in the maintenance of marine electrical equipment must be very familiar with the routing and connection relationships of the whole ship's electrical equipment lines, the working principles of various types of electrical equipment, and the positions and functions of each component in the equipment. Only on this basis can they quickly determine which link the problem lies in when a fault occurs, and then take correct handling measures. At the same time, maintenance personnel should also be familiar with the performance of electrical materials such as conductive and insulating materials, and be able to select them reasonably according to specific use conditions. Whether the selection of materials is appropriate directly affects whether the equipment can operate reliably after maintenance, so this requirement is as important as familiarity with the equipment structure and principles, and neither should be neglected.

These five means each have their own emphasis, and are often used in combination. Asking means learning from the operator or relevant personnel about the phenomena before and after the fault occurred, changes in the equipment operating state, and whether there were any abnormal operations; looking means observing the equipment appearance, wiring, and components for visible abnormalities such as burning, discoloration, breakage, or looseness; touching means, on the premise of ensuring safety, using the hand to sense the temperature, vibration, and other conditions of the components or enclosure; listening means distinguishing whether the sounds emitted during equipment operation are normal, and whether there are abnormal friction sounds, discharge sounds, or impact sounds; smelling means detecting abnormal odors such as burnt smell or ozone smell. Through asking, looking, touching, listening, and smelling, maintenance personnel can form a preliminary judgment on the fault symptom, providing direction for subsequent measurement with instruments and further fault localization.

Combination of maintenance materials and diagnostic methods. Fault diagnosis and repair of marine electrical equipment require maintenance personnel not only to master knowledge of equipment principles, structure and maintenance materials, but also to skillfully apply the above-mentioned traditional diagnostic means. Being familiar with the ship-wide marine electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the positions of each component is the prerequisite for accurately determining the fault location; being familiar with the performance of electrical materials such as conductive and insulating materials and selecting them reasonably is the basis for ensuring repair quality; and asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling are common methods for obtaining fault information and narrowing the scope of troubleshooting. The three cooperate with each other and constitute the basic literacy that maintenance personnel should possess in the maintenance and repair of the measuring circuit.

The service environment of marine electrical equipment on ships differs greatly from that of land-based equipment; its insulation performance and damage are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt mist, oil mist and swaying vibration. As for vibration conditions, when the equipment is installed in general locations, it should withstand vibration of 2.0~13.2Hz displacement ±1mm or 13.2~100.0Hz acceleration ±7m/s²; when installed on reciprocating machines and in the steering gear compartment, it should withstand

2
5.0~1
0
0.0Hz acceleration ±40m/s² vibration. These two sets of values correspond respectively to two types of installation locations: the assessment focus for general locations is the displacement amplitude in the low-frequency band and the acceleration amplitude in the medium-high frequency band, while the assessment focus for reciprocating machines and the steering gear compartment is concentrated on the acceleration amplitude of 25.0~100.0Hz, whose value is significantly higher than that of general locations, indicating that the mechanical stress at such locations is more severe. In addition to vibration conditions, the equipment should also ensure reliable operation under the specified fluctuations of voltage and frequency deviating from rated values, and the electrical clearance and creepage distance between live parts at different potentials and between live parts and the earthed enclosure must be sufficient to withstand the actually applied working voltage. Electrical clearance and creepage distance are two parallel dimensional requirements: the former targets the shortest distance through space, the latter targets the shortest path along the insulating surface, and both must be adapted to the working voltage.

Regarding the degree of protection provided by the enclosure, marine electrical equipment should comply with the provisions of IEC Publication 29, Classification of Degrees of Protection Provided by Enclosures, or the equivalent national standard; this requirement constrains the enclosure's ability to block solid foreign objects and water. Under the special environmental conditions of ships, marine electrical equipment needs to meet specific requirements for insulation, vibration and voltage/frequency fluctuation, and usually uses materials of Class E or above insulation grade as insulating materials; during maintenance, insulating varnish and the corresponding solvent need to be correctly selected to meet the high insulation performance requirements. Insulating varnish and solvent must be selected as a matching set; if the solvent does not match the varnish type, it will directly affect the insulation performance after impregnation and coating.

Marine electrical equipment falls within the scope of objects served by marine cable, and its operating status is closely related to the quality of cable laying and connection. In maintenance and repair, marine electrical equipment requires attention to the conditions of use of marine materials, to the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations, and also to the performance requirements of insulating materials.

In terms of composition, marine electrical equipment uses components and functional units such as resistor, capacitor, inductor, diode, transistor, integrated circuit, power supply circuit and printed circuit board, and also involves process steps such as maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links and precautions for the use of electric soldering irons. Resistor, capacitor and inductor are passive components, diode, transistor and integrated circuit are semiconductor devices, and power supply circuit and printed circuit board are functional units and assembly substrates; these objects correspond respectively in maintenance to operations such as resistance measurement, capacitance and withstand voltage inspection, inductance inspection, polarity and volt-ampere characteristic inspection, pin and solder joint inspection, and circuit continuity inspection. Maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links targets the cleaning and heat dissipation maintenance of heat-generating components inside the equipment, and precautions for the use of electric soldering irons target the tool operation specifications during welding repair; both belong to requirements at the maintenance process level.

The environmental factors covered by the service conditions of marine materials include: the maximum ambient air temperature is +40℃ (+45℃), and the minimum ambient air temperature is -25℃; the influence of humid sea air is present, the influence of salt mist is present, the influence of oil mist is present, and the influence of mold is present; inclination is not greater than 25°, and rolling is not greater than 25°; vibration is present, and shock is present. Among these, the temperature item gives two upper limits, +40℃ being the general value and +45℃ being the high-temperature value in parentheses, while the minimum value -25℃ defines the low-temperature end; the four items of humid air, salt mist, oil mist and mold are all marked as present, indicating that these four types of factors exist simultaneously on ships; inclination and rolling are both limited to 25°, while vibration and shock are marked as present, indicating that the two must be considered as mechanical factors.

The insulation performance and damage of electrical equipment are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt mist and oil mist, and the rolling and vibration of ships are important factors causing damage to electrical equipment. The particularity of marine environmental conditions determines the special requirements for marine electrical equipment, and under different codes and rules the requirements for equipment performance indices differ slightly. General marine electrical equipment should be able to work normally under the conditions listed in the specified environmental condition table, while marine electronic equipment and electrical equipment of special ships have separate service condition provisions. Therefore, when checking the applicability of equipment, it should first be confirmed whether it belongs to general marine electrical equipment, marine electronic equipment or electrical equipment of special ships, and then the corresponding condition clauses should be checked respectively.

For explosive hazardous spaces, the relevant requirements apply to spaces with explosion hazards such as paint rooms, battery rooms and oil pump rooms of general ships. In these spaces, the class, level and temperature group of the qualified explosion-proof electrical equipment permitted to be installed should not be lower than the specified limits. Class, level and temperature group are three parallel judgment contents: the class indicates the category of explosive gas atmosphere to which the equipment applies, the level indicates the test gap or minimum ignition current ratio that the equipment can withstand, and the temperature group limits the maximum surface temperature of the equipment. Electrical equipment working in an explosive gas atmosphere must meet the relevant requirements of IEC Publication 79 and other standards, and its explosion-proof forms include eight types such as flameproof type (d), increased safety type (e) and intrinsically safe type (i). Flameproof type (d) relies on the enclosure to withstand an internal explosion without transmitting it, increased safety type (e) avoids the generation of sparks and dangerous temperatures through structural measures, and intrinsically safe type (i) limits the circuit energy so that it is insufficient to ignite the explosive mixture; the remaining types each have their own structural principles and applicable conditions.

The above provisions are directed at explosive hazardous spaces such as ship paint rooms and battery rooms, and put forward minimum standards for the class, level and temperature group of explosion-proof electrical equipment permitted to be installed, to which attention must be paid in the selection and installation of marine electrical equipment.

The above environmental conditions and provisions do not exist in isolation, but together constitute the basic basis for the selection, installation and maintenance of marine electrical equipment. As far as the service conditions of marine materials are concerned, their indices correspond respectively to different assessment objects: the maximum and minimum values of ambient air temperature are used to define the permissible ambient temperature range of the equipment, the four influences of humid sea air, salt mist, oil mist and mold are used to describe the types of corrosion and deterioration factors, the two items of inclination and rolling are used to limit the amplitude of ship motion attitude, and the two items of vibration and shock are used to describe the forms of mechanical stress. The insulation performance and damage of electrical equipment are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt mist and oil mist; this relationship shows that the causes of insulation deterioration are not single, but vary with the climate of the navigation area and the medium conditions of the compartments.

The rolling and vibration of ships are important factors causing damage to electrical equipment, so the limits for rolling and vibration must match the equipment installation location.

As for the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations, they apply to locations with explosion hazards such as paint rooms, battery rooms and oil pump rooms on general ships.

As for the composition and maintenance objects of marine electrical equipment, it uses components and functional units such as resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors, integrated circuits, power supply circuits and printed circuit boards; these components and functional units are the direct objects of insulation inspection, parameter measurement and replacement work. Marine electrical equipment also involves process steps such as maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links and precautions for the use of electric soldering irons; the former addresses the cleaning and heat dissipation maintenance of heat-generating components inside the equipment, and the latter addresses the tool operation specifications during welding repair.

The insulation performance and damage condition of marine electrical equipment are directly related to factors such as the ship's navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt spray, oil mist and rolling and vibration; therefore, when selecting and repairing materials, marine electrical equipment must pay attention to the conditions of use of marine materials, that is, the material's temperature resistance, moisture resistance, salt spray resistance, oil mist resistance and vibration resistance must be able to adapt to the environment of the location. Marine electrical equipment belongs to the category of objects served by marine cable; in maintenance, marine electrical equipment must pay attention to the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations. In any location where explosive gas or vapor exists, its selection, installation and maintenance shall be carried out according to the hazard level of that location, and the practices for ordinary locations shall not be substituted. The heat resistance grade, moisture resistance and mechanical strength of insulating materials shall match the working conditions of the equipment, and the grade shall not be arbitrarily lowered during replacement.

In fault diagnosis and status confirmation, voltage and current are two basic measurable quantities. Voltage values can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter, that is, a multimeter is used for voltage measurement, and a voltmeter is likewise used for voltage measurement; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit; a clamp-on ammeter can obtain current readings without cutting off the circuit, and is suitable for quickly checking circuit current during operation. Before measurement, first confirm that the meter range matches the range of the quantity to be measured, then connect it in the correct wiring mode, and the reading should be compared with the rated value for judgment. For these devices containing electronic components, attention must also be paid to maintenance of electrical equipment with heating links and precautions for the use of electric soldering irons, so as to avoid affecting equipment performance due to improper operation during maintenance.

Marine cable belongs to marine electrical equipment and is the basic component in marine electrical equipment that undertakes the task of transmitting electrical energy and signals; its structure consists of three major parts: the conductive copper core wire, the insulation layer and the protective layer, none of which can be omitted. The conductive copper core wire undertakes the function of conducting current and is made of copper material, utilizing copper's characteristics of low resistivity, high tensile strength and ease of processing and welding. To adapt to the working conditions of vibration and impact on board, the conductive core wire is not a single solid copper wire but is stranded from no fewer than seven round soft copper wires with a diameter of 0.26–2.74 mm; the stranded structure enables the cable to remain intact under repeated bending and vibration. The insulation layer is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer, and its function is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires from one another and prevent short circuit between core wires or earthing to ground. The protective layer is outside the insulation layer, and its function is to protect the cable from oil, water and chemical corrosion; when the use occasion requires further improvement of mechanical strength or interference resistance, an armoring layer must also be added outside the protective layer, and the specific form of armoring may be galvanized steel wire braiding or tinned steel wire braiding.

The armor layer is usually marked as armor layer in the cable structure diagram, with number 6. Besides the marine cable itself, general insulated wires are also composed of a conductive core and an insulation layer, used for control box wiring; the insulation layer of enameled wire is a paint film, formed by coating the conductor with insulating varnish and drying it.

The model designation of marine cables has clear code meanings. The code C indicates marine power cable, CH indicates marine telecommunication cable; HY indicates oil-resistant rubber sheath, HF indicates flame-retardant rubber sheath. Taking model CHY31 as an example, it represents a marine rubber-insulated oil-resistant rubber-sheathed galvanized steel wire braided cable, suitable for fixed installation and occasions where oil may be contacted. The CHHYP type is a marine rubber-insulated core shielded oil-resistant rubber-sheathed tinned steel wire braided telecommunication cable, used for telephone station combined lines.

In the fire detection loop, the communication signal is specially processed, and a general two-core unshielded marine cable can be used.

The selection of marine cables needs to follow the marine cable selection principles. This principle contains two basic bases: one is to select the cable model according to the nature and purpose of the power grid, and also to select the cable model according to the temperature and environmental conditions of the installation site; the other is to select the cable core cross-section according to the magnitude of the conducted current. That is to say, the determination of the model depends on the nature and purpose of the power grid as well as the temperature and environmental conditions of the installation site, while the determination of the core cross-section depends on the magnitude of the conducted current. For marine cables, attention must be paid to the marine cable selection principles; when selecting the type, first clarify the nature and purpose of the power grid, then check the temperature and environmental conditions of the installation site, and finally determine the core cross-section according to the magnitude of the conducted current; the three must be implemented in sequence and must not be reversed or omitted. If the model is selected incorrectly, there may be a mismatch between the insulation material and the installation environment; if the core cross-section is selected too small, the temperature rise will be too high when conducting current, and long-term operation will accelerate the aging of the insulation layer. Therefore, the selection work should be checked one by one in combination with the specific circuit, and cannot be applied solely by experience.

Besides the cable itself, conductive materials are also widely used in marine motors, and the brush is one of the important components. The brush is used as a conductive element for leading current in or out between the stationary part and the sliding part of the motor, and contacts the collector ring to transfer current. DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators all need to be equipped with brushes. Commonly used brushes are divided into three types: graphite, electrographite and metal graphite. The graphite brush is soft in texture and suitable for motors with general commutation conditions and uniform load; the electrographite brush is roasted at a high temperature above 2500°C, has good wear resistance, and is suitable for various motors; the metal graphite brush is made by mixing graphite and copper powder, has a large current-carrying capacity, and is suitable for high-current motors, specifically for DC generators such as charging and electrolysis and for starting motors.

When the contact area between the brush and the commutator is less than 70%, grinding treatment must be carried out; the axial clearance of the brush is
0.2～
0.5mm. If the brush position is not on the neutral line, it will cause excessive sparking in the DC motor, and adjustment is needed by the induction method or the trial-run method. When there is excessive sparking under the brush, the contact between the brush and the commutator should be checked, the brush holder should be checked, and the brush position should be checked. When checking the contact between the brush and the commutator, observe whether the contact surface is uniform and whether there are signs of uneven wear or burning; when checking the brush holder, confirm whether the brush holder is loose and whether the brush can move freely up and down in the brush holder; when checking the brush position, check whether the brush holder deviates from the neutral line. The above three checks should be combined with the armature vibration and the commutator segment condition, so as to determine the source of excessive sparking.

In electrical measurement and maintenance, resistance and current are two basic measurable properties. The resistance value of a resistor can be measured with a multimeter; the current value of a current can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with the power on. To measure current, an ammeter must be used, and the circuit must be disconnected and the ammeter connected in series. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, and is used to understand equipment status; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action. When using a multimeter to measure current, the test leads must be connected in series into the circuit, and attention must be paid to range selection to avoid damaging the instrument due to overcurrent.

Welding is an operating step in the maintenance of the PLC control system. The mechanism of welding is that the solder is melted by heating the weldment, atomic diffusion occurs between the weldment and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer is formed at their interface; this alloy bonding layer has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength, and the welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products. The situation of broken input wiring corresponds to welding, that is, when the input wiring is broken, the connection needs to be restored by welding. During welding operation, the heating temperature, the amount of solder and the solidification time all affect the formation quality of the alloy bonding layer; if the heating is insufficient, the solder cannot fully melt and diffuse; if the heating is excessive, the weldment or adjacent components may be damaged.

In addition, damaging the insulation protective layer during operation is one of the causes of short circuit faults in electrical lines; when measuring the insulation resistance of a cable, the guard ring should be connected to the innermost insulation layer to eliminate errors; when calculating the number of turns of a DC coil, the wire diameter d must include the thickness of the insulation layer. These details all show that the insulation layer and the protective layer play the dual role of isolation and protection in the electrical performance of cables and coils; once damaged during maintenance, they should be dealt with promptly to avoid leaving hidden dangers of short circuit.

In the internal construction of a marine cable, an insulation layer is provided between the conductive copper core wires and the protective layer; this layer undertakes the task of separating the conductive core wires from each other and isolating them from the external environment. The main function of the insulation layer is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires, avoid short circuit between the core wires, and also avoid the core wires forming an earthing path to earth.

For general insulated wires, their basic composition consists of only two parts: the conductive core wire and the insulation layer. Such wires are often used for wiring inside control boxes; during wiring, the insulation layer at the end of the core wire needs to be stripped to the corresponding length according to the requirements of the terminal, and the copper core must not be damaged after stripping. Enameled wire is another case; its insulation layer is a paint film, formed by coating insulating varnish on the surface of the conductor and then drying it. Whether the paint film thickness is uniform directly affects the inter-turn insulation performance of the coil after winding. When measuring the insulation resistance of a cable, if the error is to be eliminated, the guard ring should be connected to the innermost insulation layer, so that the surface leakage current no longer flows through the measuring circuit. When calculating the number of turns of a DC coil, the wire diameter d taken must include the thickness of the insulation layer and must not be calculated only by the diameter of the bare conductor; otherwise, the number of turns estimated by the window area will be too large, and it cannot be fitted during actual winding.

The manufacturing method of enameled wire is to coat the conductor with insulating varnish and then dry it; this type of wire is generally used to wind electrical appliance coils, motor windings and transformer coils. A coil is one of the component parts of marine electrical equipment, made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin; it has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current, which makes the coil equivalent to a through path in a DC circuit and present impedance in an AC circuit.

A winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, whose function is to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force. Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating in AC motors; for judgment, the DC resistances of the three-phase windings can be measured separately and compared with each other; the phase with a noticeably smaller resistance value often has an inter-turn short circuit, and the phase with infinite resistance is phase failure. In the fault of high no-load voltage of the generator, once the shunt resistor is open-circuited, the voltage corrector loses its main regulating function; at this time, focus on checking whether the shunt resistor is burnt out or the lead is desoldered.

One of the uses of the potentiometer is for bridge balancing. When the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R′ driven by the motor M enters the balance adjustment process; when the bridge loses balance, the output signal drives the motor M to rotate until the resistance change of the feedback potentiometer R′ makes the bridge reach balance again. A potentiometer is also called a potentiometer; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment belongs to this type of component, and it is generally considered to be manually adjustable. A potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, while the resistance between the third pin and either of the other two pins changes with the rotation of the shaft; when measuring, first measure the total resistance across the two fixed ends, then measure the resistance between the sliding end and each of the two ends respectively; the sum of the two should be close to the total resistance. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form bridge balance. The automatic oil-fired boiler contains a potentiometer; this type of component plays the role of converting pressure changes into changes in electrical parameters in the combustion regulation loop.

The sliding contact of the potentiometer needs to be made of contact conductive materials, such as silver-iron alloy, hard copper, etc.; the requirements for such materials are low resistivity and difficulty in forming high-resistance oxides, otherwise after the contact surface oxidizes, the contact resistance increases and the bridge output deviates.

Linking the above content together, the marine cable contains an insulation layer, the contactor contains a coil, the marine motor contains a winding, the automatic oil-fired boiler contains a potentiometer, and the multimeter is used to measure resistance. In the marine cable, the insulation layer is located between the conductive copper core wires and the protective layer; its function is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires and prevent short circuit or earthing between core wires; the coil, as one of the component parts of marine electrical equipment, can be wound from enameled wire and is also widely found in motor windings and transformer coils;

A fault of the KM coil in the contactor will directly cause the armature to fail to close and the motor fails to start; for the two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, inside the insulation resistance tester, the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

In the maintenance and repair of marine electrical equipment, conductive materials not only undertake the task of electrical energy transmission but are also widely used in protection, measurement and commutation, etc. The fuse is marked with the symbol FU in circuit diagrams, and its function is overload protection and short circuit protection. The protective conductive materials for making fuse and fuse need to have characteristics such as low melting point and certain mechanical strength; on ships, protective conductive materials such as aluminum-tin alloy and aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy are commonly used to make fuses. A fuse is a safety electrical appliance; when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element;

It belongs to distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the spiral type, with a voltage of 380V and a current of 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. The fuse is a component of marine electrical equipment, and its manufacturing material is a protective conductive material such as aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy. The fuse is made of protective conductive material and has the characteristics of a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength; it is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, ranking alongside the resistor and capacitance. When replacing the fuse, attention must be paid to matching the original model and specifications, and the power switch must be disconnected. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components; when replacing the fuse of the digital multimeter, the power supply should be disconnected and a fuse matching the original model and specifications should be selected. The electric main engine remote control system contains a fuse, and broken input wiring corresponds to welding treatment.

The resistor is the object whose resistance value can be measured, and the measuring tool is the multimeter. The resistor has a certain resistance value, geometric shape and technical performance, and plays a current-limiting role in the circuit. Resistors are usually divided into three major categories: fixed resistors, variable resistors and special resistors, among which fixed resistors are most widely used in electronic products. Commonly used fixed resistors can be divided by manufacturing material into RT-type carbon film resistors, RJ-type metal film resistors, RX-type wirewound resistors and chip resistors, and their power ratings include 0.125W (1/8W), 0.25W (1/4W),
0.5W (1/2W), 1W, 2W, 3W, 5W, 7W, 10W, etc. Marine electrical equipment uses resistors; resistors include variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors; the resistor detection procedure applies to resistors; resistors can develop resistor faults, and resistor faults fall within the scope of resistors.

The shunt is used to expand the range of the ammeter, and its standard output voltages are 50mV and 75mV, of which 75mV is the most commonly used. The shunt is often made of shunt manganin, whose maximum resistance point temperature is higher than that of general-purpose manganin, and the resistance temperature coefficient range of shunt manganin is 0~40×10⁻⁶/℃. The shunt is a precision resistor element used to expand the range of the DC ammeter, connected in series in the measured circuit; a DC ammeter with a larger capacity requires an external shunt to expand the range.

Welding is one of the maintenance procedures of the PLC control system.

Voltage is the object whose voltage value can be measured, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and the voltmeter. Current is the object whose current value can be measured, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, the ammeter and the clamp-on ammeter. The multimeter is used to measure resistor, voltage and current, and the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

The S-3 model has a resistivity of 8~20Ω·mm²/m, a rated current density of 11A/cm², and a permissible peripheral speed of 25m/s; the DS-4 model has a resistivity of 6~16Ω·mm²/m, a friction coefficient ≤0.2, and a permissible peripheral speed of up to 40m/s; the DS-8 model has a resistivity of 31~50Ω·mm²/m, a contact voltage drop of 1.9~2.9V, and a service pressure of 20~40kPa; the DS-52 model has a resistivity of 12~22Ω·mm²/m, a permissible peripheral speed of up to 50m/s, and a wear amount ≤
0.15mm/50h.

The electrographite brush is made from graphite, coke, carbon black, etc. as raw materials, roasted at a high temperature above 2500℃, has good wear resistance and is easy to machine, and is suitable for various types of motors as well as motors with difficult commutation conditions.

DS-72 model rated current density 12A/cm², allowable peripheral speed 70m/s; DS-74 model resistivity coefficient 35~80Ω·mm²/m, operating pressure 20~40kPa; DS-112 model 50h wear amount ≤0.1mm, contact voltage drop
2.5~
3.7V. During acceptance of DC motor overhaul, its pressure is generally controlled at
about 2.45MPa. The manufacturing material of metal graphite brush is a mixture of graphite and copper powder and other metal powders, which has good electrical conductivity and large current-carrying capacity, and is suitable for high-current motors such as DC generators for charging, electrolysis and electroplating, and is also suitable for low-voltage small traction motors and motors for starting automobiles and small diesel engines. TS-2 model resistivity coefficient is 0.1~0.35Ω·mm²/m, rated current density is 20A/cm².

During maintenance, the motor brush model is generally not easily changed, and replacement should be carried out according to the original model and specification. Replacing the brush is a maintenance procedure for equipment such as DC motors or electric drills, referring to replacing worn, damaged or poorly contacting brushes to restore electrical conductivity. When the electric drill fails to start due to brush wear, the maintenance method is to replace the brush; if the brush wire is loose, the brush should be repaired or replaced to solve the failure of the electric drill to start. When grinding the brush, if the contact area is less than 70%, it must be treated, and the axial clearance is 0.2～0.5mm; if the brush position is not on the neutral line, it will cause excessive commutation spark, which needs to be adjusted by the induction method or the trial-run method. The brush contacts the collector ring to transmit current; when the contact area between the brush and the commutator is less than 70%, grinding treatment must be carried out; if the brush position is not on the neutral line, it will cause excessive spark in the DC motor.

The commutator is a rotating sliding contact component used for current introduction and extraction in DC motors and wound-rotor motors, and is composed of commutator segments. When disassembling a DC motor, care should be taken to prevent damage to the winding ends, commutator or collector ring; carbon powder must not accumulate in the commutator grooves, so as to avoid short circuit between segments. Marine motors include commutators and brushes. When checking the contact between the brush and the commutator, use the commutator and brush; when checking the brush holder, use the brush; when checking the commutator segments, use the commutator; when checking the brush position, use the brush.

Marine cables belong to marine electrical equipment and are composed of conductive copper core wires, insulation layer and protective layer, used to conduct current and resist environmental corrosion. The insulation layer electrically insulates each conductive core wire; the protective layer is used to protect the cable from oil, water and chemical corrosion, and when necessary, armoring is added to enhance mechanical strength and anti-interference capability. Marine cables include conductive copper core wires, insulation layer, protective layer and armor, and attention should be paid to the selection principles of marine cables. The selection principles are to select the model according to the nature, purpose and environmental conditions of the power grid, and to select the core cross-section according to the magnitude of the conducted current. HY indicates oil-resistant rubber sheath, HF indicates non-flammable rubber sheath.

The standard model designation of marine rubber-insulated non-flammable rubber-sheathed cable is CHF, and the core cross-section specification range of its two-core structure is 0.8 to 120mm²; its main use is fixed installation, and contact with oil must be avoided; there is a flexible cable variant with the same name, used to connect mobile electrical equipment. The model designation of marine rubber-insulated non-flammable rubber-sheathed galvanized steel wire braided cable is CHF31, its core structure is three-core, the cross-section range is between 0.8 and 240mm², and its main use is the same as that of the CHF type, for fixed installation and avoiding contact with oil; the insulation material is rubber, the sheath is non-flammable rubber sheath, and the outer protective layer is composed of galvanized steel wire braiding. The model designation of marine rubber-insulated non-flammable rubber-sheathed flexible cable is CHF (note: the name column in the table corresponds to this model), belonging to the domestic marine cable series, with core cross-section specification range of 0.8 to 70 square millimeters; its main use is to connect mobile electrical equipment, and the use environment requires avoiding contact with oil; unlike the fixed-installation CHF type non-flammable rubber-sheathed cable, this flexible cable is specially used for mobile equipment. The model code of marine rubber-insulated oil-resistant rubber-sheathed cable is CHY, and its main use is fixed installation, different from flexible cables used for mobile equipment; it has oil-resistant characteristics and is allowed to work in environments where oil may be contacted, and the use conditions require avoiding direct sunlight; its derived models CHY31 (galvanized steel wire braiding) and CHY32 (tinned steel wire braiding) have the same use as this type.

In the practical application of marine conductive materials, the brush is a conductive part that must be equipped on DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators; its function is to complete the introduction or extraction of current between the stationary part and the sliding part of the motor. The brush contacts the collector ring to transmit current; once the contact state deteriorates, current conduction is directly affected, so the inspection of the brush occupies an important position in commutator fault diagnosis.

Graphite brushes are made by mixing and pressing natural graphite with binders such as pitch and coal tar; when not heated at high temperature, they contain more impurities and are relatively soft in texture. These parameters respectively correspond to the differences among different models of graphite brushes in resistivity coefficient, current density, peripheral speed, friction coefficient, contact voltage drop, service pressure and wear amount, and should be checked item by item during selection.

The resistivity coefficient reflects the conductive capability of the brush itself; the smaller the value, the lower the loss when current passes through. The rated current density limits the current allowed to pass per unit contact area; exceeding this value will aggravate heating. The permissible peripheral speed determines the upper limit of linear speed the brush can withstand and is directly related to the diameter and rotational speed of the commutator or collector ring. The friction coefficient and service pressure jointly affect the mechanical wear between the brush and the commutator surface. The contact voltage drop is related to the energy loss during commutation. The wear amount is measured by the reduction in length per 50 hours to indicate the service life of the brush. If any of the above indicators fails to meet the operating conditions, the brush life will be shortened and the commutation quality will be affected. Its scope of application is wider than that of graphite brushes, and it can be used for various types of motors as well as motors with difficult rectification conditions. Too high a pressure will increase friction and wear, while too low a pressure will make the contact unstable and easily produce sparking under the brush; therefore, during overhaul acceptance, the pressure must be confirmed as an independent inspection item. Because copper powder and other metal powders are added, its resistivity coefficient is significantly lower than that of graphite brushes and electrographite brushes, and the rated current density is correspondingly increased, so it is suitable for undertaking current conduction tasks in low-voltage, high-current occasions.

Abnormalities of the brush during operation often need to be judged in combination with the approach of commutator fault diagnosis. Among them, the three tasks of checking the contact between brush and commutator, checking the brush holder, and checking the brush position are all directly aimed at the brush itself. A loose brush holder can likewise cause excessive sparking under brush, and motor overload as well as poor contact between brush and commutator are also common causes of this phenomenon.

The conductive parts that cooperate with the brush are the coil and the winding. Enameled wire is made by coating insulating varnish on a conductor and then drying it, and is generally used for winding electrical appliance coils, motor windings and transformer coils. Once a local short circuit or phase failure occurs in the winding, the current distribution will deviate from the normal state, thereby causing overcurrent and a rise in temperature rise; therefore, when dealing with the problem of motor overheating, the winding state is an object that needs to be checked with priority.

In the maintenance and testing stage, the multimeter is the most frequently used instrument and can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current. Voltage measurement is likewise accomplished with a multimeter or voltmeter. When measuring resistance, voltage and current, the range selection should match the measured value, and the connection method must also be correct; otherwise the reading cannot reflect the true state of the equipment. When an input wiring disconnection occurs, welding treatment must be carried out accordingly to restore the continuity of the line. During welding, the control of the heating degree, the amount of solder and the solidification process all affect the quality of the bonding layer; a poor bonding layer will increase the contact resistance, thereby affecting the signal transmission and power supply reliability of the entire control system.

Marine electrical equipment cannot operate without the support of various insulating materials, and the quality of their insulation performance is directly related to whether the equipment can work safely and reliably. Marine electrical equipment usually uses materials of Class E or above insulation grade as insulating materials, and during maintenance the insulating varnish and corresponding solvent must be correctly selected to meet the high insulation performance requirements. For insulating materials, there are a series of performance requirements that need to be grasped. The dielectric withstand strength refers to the voltage kV value that a 1 mm thick insulating material can withstand when broken down; insulating materials should have high insulation resistance and withstand strength to avoid earth leakage breakdown phenomena; when the electric field electromotive force strength increases to the limit value, the insulating material will be broken down.

In addition to dielectric strength, mechanical strength is measured by the tensile strength value; the larger the tensile strength value, the higher the mechanical strength; a small expansion coefficient is required; thermal stability is used to set the component operating temperature according to the physical, chemical and electrical properties of the insulating material; biological resistance is used to prevent mold growth. These indicators together constitute the technical requirements that marine insulating materials must meet in terms of dielectric properties, mechanical strength and thermal stability. The reason why the indicator of insulation dielectric strength uses 1mm thickness as the reference is to establish a comparable scale among different materials; the higher its value, the greater the applied voltage per unit thickness of material that it can withstand without breakdown, so when selecting, calculation can be made according to the working voltage and material thickness. Mechanical strength is expressed by the tensile strength value; the larger the tensile strength value, the less likely the material is to be pulled apart or torn during operations such as wrapping, coil insertion and binding.

Biological resistance addresses the problem of mold growth, preventing the material from growing mold and deteriorating in a damp and warm environment.

Marine electrical equipment is closely related to marine cables; marine cables are a component of marine electrical equipment, and marine cables in turn contain an insulation layer. The function of the insulation layer is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires, preventing short circuit or earthing between core wires; in the marine cable structure, the insulation layer is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer; the conductive copper core wire is responsible for conducting current, the insulation layer covers the outside of the copper core wire to achieve electrical isolation between core wires and between core wires and earth, and the protective layer is then wrapped outside the insulation layer for protection. When selecting materials for marine electrical equipment, attention must also be paid to the conditions of use of marine materials, the requirements for electrical equipment in explosive hazardous locations, and the performance requirements of insulating materials.

As far as the operating environment is concerned, the insulation performance and damage of marine electrical equipment are directly related to the navigation area, air temperature, humidity, salt spray, oil mist and swaying vibration; under the special environmental conditions of ships, electrical equipment must meet specific requirements for insulation, vibration and voltage/frequency fluctuation. Marine electrical equipment should ensure reliable operation under the specified fluctuations of voltage and frequency deviating from rated values, and its enclosure protection degree should comply with IEC Publication 29, Classification of Degrees of Protection Provided by Enclosures, or the equivalent national standard. When installed in general locations, it should withstand vibration of ±1mm displacement at 2.0~13.2Hz or ±7m/s² acceleration at 13.2~100.0Hz; this vibration condition indicates that the equipment and its insulation fixing parts must withstand larger displacement amplitudes in the low-frequency range and larger acceleration amplitudes in the high-frequency range.

In the composition of marine electrical equipment, resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors, integrated circuits, power supply circuits, printed circuit boards, etc. are all common constituent links. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and the voltmeter. When using a multimeter to measure resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on, otherwise the charge stored in the capacitor will discharge through the test leads, which both affects the reading and may damage the instrument. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action.

Among the solid insulating materials commonly used on ships, polyester film is an important variety. Its thickness range is 0.006～0.10mm, its insulation strength is >130kV/mm, and the measured breakdown voltage is 130~230 kV/mm. Polyester film is a main insulating material of class B heat resistance (permissible working temperature 130℃), and is also a commonly used solid insulating material on ships with a heat resistance class of E and an insulation strength greater than 130kV/mm. It is often made into polyester film adhesive tape, thickness 0.055～0.17mm, withstand voltage >100kV/mm; in addition, there also exists a polyester film insulating paper composite foil form, whose breakdown voltage is 40 kV/mm. In the repair of small motors, a composite of 0.05mm thick polyester film and blue shell paper can be used as slot insulation.

When selecting polyester film, the thinner the thickness, the easier it is to fit in the slot and at the winding ends, but the withstand voltage level must match the working voltage; the value of insulation strength greater than 130kV/mm can be used as the basis for verification.

Blue shell paper is commonly used in the repair of motors and electrical appliances; its thickness range is 0.1～0.4mm, the generally commonly used blue shell paper thickness is 0.15mm, and the insulation strength is 7kV/mm. For class E insulation of small motors, polyester film can be composited with blue shell paper; when used as slot insulation, a layer of 0.15mm thick blue shell paper is commonly used, that is, the polyester film bears the higher withstand voltage, and the blue shell paper provides certain mechanical support and isolation. Pressboard is likewise commonly used in the repair of motors and electrical appliances; its color is mostly red, also called red pressboard, and in daily maintenance it is used for padding and making surrounding frames, etc. The standard thickness of pressboard is 0.5～2.5mm, the thickness range of light red pressboard is 0.5～3.0mm, and light red pressboard at

a thickness of 0.5～
0.9mm has a withstand voltage of not less than 7kV. The selection of thickness for gaskets and surrounding frames depends on the assembly clearance and the required mechanical strength, while the withstand voltage value is used to judge whether they can be used in locations of the corresponding voltage level.

Among the various insulating tapes commonly used on ships, polyester film adhesive tape is generally commonly used because of its good electrical performance, relatively thin thickness and high withstand voltage; its thickness range is 0.055～0.17mm, and its withstand voltage strength is greater than 100kV/mm. White cloth tape is divided into two structural forms: twill and plain weave; when selecting white cloth tape, the basis is its tensile strength. If not subjected to varnish impregnation treatment, white cloth tape has poor electrical performance and easily absorbs moisture; therefore, white cloth tape is generally only used for reinforcing mechanical strength and for binding, and is usually not used as an insulating material. The twill and plain weave structures differ in tensile strength and extensibility; when the binding location is subjected to greater force, selection should be made according to tensile strength.

The coil is a component of marine electrical equipment. It is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. A contactor contains a coil, and the state of the coil directly affects whether the contactor can operate normally. It can thus be seen that the coil is both a functional component that performs electromagnetic action and a key component inside insulation testing instruments; its winding quality, the state of the insulated wire, and the insulation condition of the bobbin are all related to the insulation level of the entire equipment.

Linking the above content together, the voltage measurement result can reflect whether insulating materials such as polyester film have been broken down or are close to breakdown, while the coil, as a component inside the contactor and the insulation resistance tester, has its insulated wire winding and bobbin insulation treatment directly dependent on materials such as polyester film.

When rewinding the slot insulation of a small motor, the insulation can be restored by the method of combining 0.05mm polyester film with blue shell paper, or by using polyester film adhesive tape with a thickness of 0.055～0.17mm and a withstand voltage greater than 100kV/mm, as well as polyester film insulating paper composite foil with a breakdown voltage of 40 kV/mm. For parts with higher heat resistance requirements, attention should be paid to the limitation that the allowable working temperature of polyester film is 130℃, which is the B-class heat resistance grade, while also taking into account the general statement that it is a material of E-class heat resistance grade with an insulation strength greater than 130kV/mm. When measuring with an insulation resistance tester, it is necessary to confirm that the relative positions of the two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, are accurate, so as to avoid obtaining an incorrect voltage reading due to improper coil positions, which would in turn affect the judgment of the insulation state of the polyester film.

There are many types of components commonly used in electronic equipment; resistor, capacitor, inductor, diode, transistor, thyristor, integrated circuit, fuse, connector, and various sensors all fall into this category. During the maintenance and repair of marine electrical equipment, the performance of these components needs to be measured and judged, and the multimeter is the most basic testing tool.

A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch, and the measuring circuit. At full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. Multimeters are divided into two types: pointer type and digital type. The MF-47 multimeter is a specific model of multimeter, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and its panel is provided with four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V", and "5A". A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, current, and capacitance, and can also be used to detect diode, transistor, thyristor, photosensitive device, and thermocouple. The clamp-on ammeter is specially used to measure current, and the circuit does not need to be disconnected during measurement. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit; voltage measurement uses a multimeter or voltmeter.

Resistors are generally divided into three major categories: fixed resistor, variable resistor, and special resistor, among which fixed resistor is the most widely used in electronic products. Commonly used fixed resistors can be divided by manufacturing material into RT-type carbon film resistor, RJ-type metal film resistor, RX-type wirewound resistor, and chip resistor. In the model naming rule, R represents resistor, T represents carbon film, J represents metal, and X represents wirewound, all taking the first letter of the pinyin. The color ring marking method is commonly used internationally; a four-ring resistor is generally a carbon film resistor, and a five-ring resistor is generally a metal film resistor. A chip resistor is an SMT-packaged resistor, usually marked with three or four digits, for example, 334 means 33×10^4Ω, that is, 330kΩ. Rated power refers to the maximum allowable power consumption under specified ambient temperature and humidity and without air circulation, under long-term continuous load without damage; power grades include 0.125W (1/8W), 0.25W (1/4W),
0.5W (1/2W), 1W, 2W, 3W, 5W, 7W, 10W, etc.

A resistor has a certain resistance value, geometric shape and technical performance, and plays a current-limiting role in a circuit. Resistors include variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors. A variable resistor, also called a potentiometer, has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the two pins changes with shaft rotation; it is generally considered that a potentiometer can be adjusted manually, while a variable resistor is smaller in size and mounted on a circuit board without frequent adjustment. In voltage-stabilized power supply debugging, a variable resistor is connected in series as a load to test the overcurrent protection current value. For a master controller using a variable resistor, the contact condition between the sliding arm and the resistor must be checked during secondary maintenance. A potentiometer is often used as a zeroing element in a differential amplifier circuit; in voltage-stabilized power supply debugging, the output voltage is made to vary within a specified range such as
1.25~
7.5V by adjusting the voltage-regulating potentiometer.

In automatic boiler combustion regulation, potentiometer R1 driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure is lower than the set value, YBD drives the sliding contact of potentiometer R0 upward, causing the bridge to become unbalanced and triggering the servo motor to act. In the voltage circuit of the insulation resistance tester, a potentiometer is connected in series as a regulator to adjust the error of the pointer at the "∞" position. The volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is this type of element. When measuring a resistor in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if a capacitor exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistor, and never measure with power on. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open circuit in the shunt resistor causes the voltage corrector to lose its main regulating action. The resistor detection steps apply to resistors; a resistor may develop a resistance fault, and a resistance fault belongs to the resistor.

A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in between, and its characteristic is to block direct current and pass alternating current. In a circuit, a capacitor is generally denoted by "C" plus a number, for example C25 denotes the capacitor numbered 25. The hindering effect on an alternating current signal is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC), which is related to the signal frequency and capacitance. According to polarity, capacitors are divided into polarized capacitors such as electrolytic capacitors and tantalum capacitors, and non-polarized capacitors. The main performance indicators include capacitance, withstand voltage value and temperature withstand value; the withstand voltage value is the maximum working voltage. According to dielectric material, they are divided into electrolytic, mica, paper, ceramic, glass glaze capacitors, etc. Common types include electrolytic capacitors, ceramic disc capacitors, chip capacitors, monolithic capacitors, etc. In the digital marking method, the first two digits are significant digits, the third digit is a multiple of 10, and the unit is usually pF.

In a filter circuit, a capacitor is connected in parallel with the load, and charging and discharging are used to filter out the alternating current component; the withstand voltage value of the capacitor in the filter circuit should not be less than
1.42 times the AC effective value. Common faults include open circuit due to pin corrosion, desoldering and cold solder joints, capacitance reduction due to leakage, or breakdown short circuit. When measuring earth leakage with a multimeter, if the pointer cannot return to infinity, the reading multiplied by the range is the leakage resistance; when measuring earth leakage with an analog multimeter, the leakage resistance value is from tens to hundreds of megohms, except for electrolytic capacitors. The larger the capacitance, the greater the swing amplitude of the multimeter pointer to the right and the slower the recovery speed. An electrolytic capacitor has a small leakage current when connected with correct polarity; when the end connected to the black test lead is the positive electrode, the polarity can be determined on this basis. Slow starting and reduced speed of an electric fan may be due to insufficient capacitance, and a capacitor of the same specification needs to be replaced.

An inductor is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulated bobbin; its characteristic is that it passes direct current and blocks alternating current, and the higher the frequency, the greater the coil impedance. Inductors are mainly used for circuit functions such as filtering, notch filtering, oscillation and magnetic energy storage. The basic unit is the henry (H), commonly the millihenry (mH) and microhenry (μH). Classification includes air-core inductors and magnetic-core inductors such as core and copper-core inductors. Common types include fixed inductors, adjustable inductors, color-code inductors, etc. An inductance coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulated bobbin; direct current can pass through while alternating current is blocked. The two ends of a solenoid valve coil are usually connected in parallel with a freewheeling diode to prevent the coil from producing a high-voltage output when the transistor loses power. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked. The inductor test steps apply to inductors.

A diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity; under forward voltage it conducts with small resistance, and under reverse voltage it cuts off. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite; it is commonly used in circuits such as rectification, isolation, voltage regulation and polarity protection. By function it is divided into rectifier diodes such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, Schottky diodes such as BAT85, etc.; in addition there are light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The circuit symbol is VD, numbered such as VD5; the light-emitting diode symbol is VL, the photodiode is VDL, and the Zener diode is VS. The exterior of low-power diodes often marks the negative electrode with a color ring, or marks polarity with a dedicated symbol and the letters P/N.

The rated current of the 1N4000 series is all 1A, and the withstand voltage increases from 50V for 1N4001 to 1000V for 1N4007. When an analog multimeter measures polarity, the resistance is small when the black probe contacts the anode and the red probe contacts the cathode, which is forward bias; when a digital multimeter tests a diode, the red probe contacts the positive electrode and the black probe contacts the negative electrode and displays the forward voltage drop, less than 1V. The diode test steps apply to diodes. Diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes.

A light-emitting diode is a semiconductor device capable of emitting light in colors such as red, green and yellow; it has unidirectional conductivity, and its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode; it is commonly used as a circuit working-status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display screen.

Outline dimensions include diameters of 3mm, 5mm and 2mm×5mm rectangular. The operating current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model, and in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage. The conduction voltage is generally above 1.7V, therefore a single
1.5V battery cannot light a light-emitting diode. The method for identifying the positive and negative electrodes is: the long pin is the positive electrode; in the visual method, the smaller and shorter electrode is the positive electrode, and the larger electrode is the negative electrode. An ordinary multimeter cannot test a light-emitting diode on the R×1 range through the R×1k range; the R×10k range, i.e. a higher-voltage range, is needed to light it for testing. In fault checking of the PLC control system, if the POWER lamp off and the fuse is not blown, it is necessary to check whether the light-emitting diode is broken down, and if so, replace the light-emitting diode. In the simulation test device of the main engine remote control system, light-emitting diodes are used to display the working status of the remote control system and the action conditions of external solenoid valves.

For light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes.

A Zener diode is commonly represented in circuits by "VS" plus a number, e.g. VS5 represents the Zener diode numbered 5. Its main characteristic is that after breakdown the voltage across its terminals remains basically unchanged, and its forward conduction characteristic is the same as that of an ordinary diode. After it is connected into a circuit, if the power supply voltage fluctuates or the voltages at various points change, the voltage across the load will remain basically unchanged. Fault manifestations are mainly three cases: open circuit, short circuit and unstable regulation value. An open-circuit fault manifests as a rise in power supply voltage; a short circuit and an unstable regulation value manifest as the power supply voltage dropping to 0V or unstable output. Commonly used models include the 1N4728 to 1N4761 series, with corresponding regulation values ranging from 3.3V to 75V.

In two-wire wiring of a fire detector, the terminal device may use a Zener diode to maintain the microampere-level monitoring current. When black smoke is checked and there is no response to smoke and no alarm is ever given, it may be caused by damage to the Zener diode. A Zener diode will suffer a Zener diode fault, and a Zener diode fault belongs to the Zener diode.

A transistor contains two PN junctions internally and has current amplification capability; it is divided into two types, NPN type and PNP type, and their operating characteristics can complement each other, such as the complementary pair in an OTL circuit. In circuits it is commonly represented by "VT" plus a number, e.g. VT17 represents the transistor numbered 17. Commonly used PNP-type models include A92, 9015, etc.; NPN-type models include A42, 9014, 9018, 9013, 9012, etc.

The common-emitter circuit is commonly used in the intermediate stage of a multistage amplifier, and the emitter-follower circuit is used for low-frequency input/output stages or impedance matching. Use the unidirectional conductivity of the PN junction to determine the transistor type: if a low resistance is measured with the red test lead connected to the base, it is PNP type; if a low resistance is measured with the black test lead connected to the base, it is NPN type. For a medium- or small-power silicon transistor of good performance, the forward resistance of the emitter junction and collector junction is several hundred ohms to one thousand ohms, and the reverse resistance is several hundred kilohms or more. The faster the leakage current increases with temperature, the worse the transistor performance; the greater the pointer deflection, the more unstable the performance. A transistor will suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to the transistor.

A thyristor is also called SCR, also known as a silicon controlled rectifier; its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode can be measured. An integrated circuit has the advantages of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration increases, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits have appeared.

Pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise; to facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often welded on the circuit board for direct plugging in. Common package forms include the type with inward-hooked pins on four sides, i.e. PLCC, the type with gull-wing pins on two sides, i.e. SOIC, the dual in-line pin type, i.e. DIP, and power integrated circuit packages. The 4000 series CMOS integrated circuits are numbered 4000 to 4500, most of them are 14- or 16-pin packages, are powered by a wide voltage of 3 to 15V, and are very sensitive to static electricity. TTL logic chips are numbered starting from 74××00, such as 74LS, 74HC, and all use a single 5V power supply. Common testing methods include non-online measurement, i.e. comparing the DC resistance values of each pin, online measurement, i.e. detecting pin voltage/resistance/current, and the substitution method, i.e. replacing with a good component of the same model. It is strictly forbidden to use an insulation resistance tester to test an integrated circuit, so as to avoid breakdown of the electronic devices therein due to high voltage. In the main engine remote control system, the contactless electric remote control system may be constructed with integrated circuits; the failure rate of such electronic control systems is constant, and regular preventive maintenance is not required.

The fuse is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, alongside resistors and capacitors. A fuse is a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material, featuring a low melting point and certain mechanical strength; its material is a protective conductive material such as aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy. When replacing it, note that it must match the original model and specifications, and switch off the power supply. The fuse is used for circuit overload or short circuit protection; in the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Connectors are used for circuit connection and assembly; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of connectors is a common electrical fault.

The sensor is the information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching-value sensors. One function of the differential amplifier circuit in the signal conditioning circuit is to amplify and convert the small signal sent by the sensor into the required signal. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The photoresistor is made by depositing a layer of cadmium sulfide (CdS) film on a ceramic substrate, and belongs to semiconductor components. In complete darkness its resistance can reach several megohms or more, and under strong light it can drop to several thousand ohms or even below 1kΩ. The photoresistor uses photoconductive characteristics to convert optical signals into electrical signals, and is used in automatic detection, photoelectric control and alarm circuits. The resistance value of the photoresistor changes with the strength of external light: when light is strong the resistance is small, and when light is weak the resistance is large. In ship boilers it serves as a flame monitoring element; when ignition succeeds, the resistance decreases, causing the relay to act and stop the ignition. During troubleshooting, check whether it is aged, whether the photosensitive window is covered by accumulated oil grime affecting the light flux, or whether it is aligned with the flame. During testing, the R×1k range of a multimeter can be used to measure; normally the resistance values under light and in darkness show an obvious change;

if the measured resistance value does not change, it indicates failure; if both are zero, it indicates a short circuit; if both are infinite, it indicates an open circuit. In automatic boiler control, the photoresistor is used to detect the flame; when ignition succeeds, the resistance value of the photoresistor decreases, energizing 1JY, which energizes 3JZ, which energizes 4JZ; 4JZ (31, 28) opens, and the ignition transformer is de-energized. The rectifier is used to convert alternating current into direct current; the electrical graphic symbol of the full-wave bridge rectifier is UR. In the controllable phase compound excitation constant-voltage device, rectifier fault is one of the sub-causes of phase compound excitation device faults; if the UR rectifier has an open-circuit diode, it will cause a voltage deviation where |U0-Ufe| is greater than ΔU1. The RS_0 fuse is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers and their complete sets.

In the maintenance of electronic equipment, the multimeter is the most basic testing tool. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, and is divided into two types: analog and digital. The analog multimeter uses a magnetoelectric high-sensitivity meter head; at full scale the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. The MF-47 multimeter belongs to the multimeter category, and its dial has six scales, while common models such as the MF-30 have only four scales. The digital multimeter likewise belongs to the multimeter category and is an electronic measuring instrument; when using it, the power switch must first be turned on, and models without an automatic shutdown function must be switched off after use; it has capacitance, diode and transistor hFE testing functions.
