When using a multimeter to measure direct current, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range, and the meter head is connected in series in the disconnected branch; when measuring direct voltage, the test probes are connected in parallel across the component under test, and when the range is uncertain, set the maximum range first. This measurement method is equally applicable in the maintenance of the PLC control system, judging equipment faults by measuring voltage, current or resistance.

The thermistor is a special semiconductor device whose resistance value changes with the surface temperature. The commonly used NTC thermistor has a negative temperature coefficient, that is, the resistance value decreases as the temperature rises. The thermistor was originally used to enable electronic equipment to work normally at different ambient temperatures, which is called temperature compensation. The CPU temperature measurement and over-temperature alarm functions of the computer motherboard utilize the characteristics of the thermistor. On ships, thermistor sensors with a negative temperature coefficient are commonly used for temperature measurement. A multimeter set to the R×10 or R×100 range can be used to measure the lead resistance of the sensor inserted into hot water to check its performance.

Resistors may develop resistance faults during use. High temperature, especially when the power is relatively large, causes the resistor to heat up and burn out, which is a common fault; some faults appear as the resistor turning black with burn marks, which can be directly observed with the naked eye. To determine whether a resistor is damaged, its resistance must be measured; if it differs from the marked value, or is a short circuit or open circuit, it is damaged. Measurement on the circuit board is easily disturbed by other loops, so it is best to remove the resistor and measure it separately. When testing with a digital multimeter, an appropriate ohm range must be selected according to the resistance range. The resistor testing steps apply to resistors, and their content is: for resistances below 200Ω select the 200 range, for resistances from 200Ω to 2kΩ select the R×2k range, and so on; if the measurement result differs from the marked value, or a short circuit or open circuit is displayed, the resistor is judged to be damaged; when using an auto-ranging multimeter, it is only necessary to select the resistance measurement function.

Capacitors are usually indicated in circuit diagrams by the letter C plus a number, for example C25 indicates the capacitor numbered 25. The units of capacitance are the farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF) and picofarad (pF). The filter circuit is part of the power supply circuit; the capacitor is connected in parallel with the load, and filtering is achieved by charging in the positive half-cycle and discharging in the negative half-cycle; connecting an inductor in series with the load can more effectively filter out the AC component in the pulse current. Types of filter circuits include the L-type filter circuit, the π-type filter circuit and the RC filter circuit. The L-type filter circuit consists of one inductor and one capacitor and is named for its resemblance to an inverted L; the π-type filter circuit consists of one inductor and two capacitors and is named for its resemblance to the letter π; a resistor is commonly used instead of an inductor to form the RC filter circuit, in order to solve the problems of high cost and large volume of the inductor.

Capacitors may develop capacitor faults. The main fault manifestations include open-circuit faults caused by pin corrosion and breakage and by desoldering or cold solder joints; leakage of electrolytic capacitors will lead to reduced capacitance, open circuit, or severe earth leakage and breakdown faults. Most capacitor faults can be found by visually observing the appearance, and some require removing the instrument for measurement. The capacitor testing steps require that before testing, the two pins of the electrolytic capacitor be touched together to discharge the residual charge, so as to prevent it from affecting the measurement result; use the R×1k range of an analog multimeter or the resistance range of a digital multimeter for measurement; the resistance indicated when the pointer stops is the leakage resistance, and the larger this value the better, preferably approaching infinity; if the leakage resistance is only several tens of kilohms, it indicates severe leakage of the electrolytic capacitor; the larger the initial swing angle of the pointer to the right (the smaller the value), the larger the capacitance; it is normal for the digital meter to display a small resistance value first and then slowly increase until infinity.

When testing a diode, the red probe is connected to the positive pole of the internal power supply and the black probe to the negative pole, which is opposite to the polarity of the analog multimeter.

The inductor testing steps are for inductors. The first step is an appearance check, which requires confirming that the magnetic core has no defects or cracks, the metal has no corrosion or oxidation, and the wiring has no breakage or bending damage; the second step is to use a multimeter to measure the DC resistance of the coil and compare it with a known normal value to determine the fault; if the measured resistance is significantly increased or the pointer does not move, it is judged that the inductor body is open-circuited; if the measured resistance is much smaller than the normal value, it is judged that the inductor body is severely short-circuited; a local short circuit of the coil cannot be found by conventional resistance measurement and requires detection with special instruments. The height of the radar antenna should ensure that the horizontal distance from the line of sight at the bow to the sea surface does not exceed 500m or two times the ship's length, whichever is smaller; the radar antenna position should ensure that there is no shadow sector within the range from dead ahead to 2 to 2.5° abaft the beam on both the port and starboard sides. The precautions for radar antenna installation require attention to the antenna; radar installation applies to the antenna.

Among the electronic components of marine electrical equipment, the diode belongs to a widely applied category of semiconductor devices, whose main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity, that is, under forward voltage the conducting resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite. By virtue of this characteristic, diodes are commonly used in circuits such as rectification, isolation, voltage regulation and polarity protection. When identifying its positive and negative electrodes, the long pin is the positive electrode and the short pin is the negative electrode; the light-emitting diode belongs to current-type devices, its operating voltage is 3V but it is easily damaged, so a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series, its operating current is 1～30mA, and its conducting voltage is above 1.7V; its positive and negative electrodes can be identified by pin length, the long pin being positive and the short pin being negative.

Testing the above devices cannot be done without a multimeter. When using a digital multimeter to test polarity, the red probe is connected to the positive electrode and a displayed voltage value below 1V indicates the forward conducting state; when a digital multimeter detects earth leakage of an electrolytic capacitor, the numerical indication first shows a relatively small resistor value, then slowly increases until infinity. Capacitance test steps of the digital multimeter: turn the changeover switch to the capacitance measurement range -> insert the capacitor to be tested into the capacitance jack -> read the displayed reading.

Diode test steps of the digital multimeter: insert the probes -> turn the changeover switch to the diode test range -> connect the diode under test -> read the forward voltage drop; during the test the red probe is connected to the positive electrode of the diode and the black probe to the negative electrode, and the multimeter must be set to the diode symbol range for measurement; when forward conducting it displays a voltage value (such as 0.597V), and when reverse non-conducting it displays OL or 1×××; the probe connection method is exactly opposite to that of the analog multimeter. Transistor test steps of the digital multimeter: transistor type discrimination -> collector, emitter and current amplification factor test -> performance discrimination. The diode detection steps require selecting the diode symbol range, the measurement method is to connect the red probe to the positive electrode of the diode and the black probe to the negative electrode of the diode, and the judgment criterion is that the measured value is the voltage value of the diode during forward conduction, while a reverse display of OL indicates the diode is non-conducting; this probe connection method is opposite to the test connection method of the analog multimeter, and the polarity of a light-emitting diode can be identified by pin length to assist detection. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, check whether parts are seized or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt.

The resistor is one of the components widely used in marine electrical equipment. Resistors include variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors.

Capacitors are likewise widely used in marine electrical equipment. The circuit symbol of the diode is VD, with designations such as VD5; the diode detection steps apply to diodes. The larger the pointer deflection, the more unstable the performance. The criterion for judging a transistor fault is the abnormal reading when measuring with the diode range (buzzer range) of a digital multimeter; typical phenomena include the case where two pins always show a small numerical value, the case where no small numerical value is displayed during measurement, and the inability to measure the transistor by the normal method (such as pinching the base and collector to compare the β value). This fault judgment is based on the principle that the amplification factor β is large when the emitter and collector of an NPN/PNP transistor are correctly connected.

The power supply circuit supplies energy to electronic equipment and has three types: linear rectifier power supply, switching power supply and inverter power supply; the power supply in electronic circuits is generally low-voltage direct current. The power supply circuit includes a filter circuit and a voltage regulator circuit. The linear rectifier power supply consists of four main parts: transformation, rectification, filtering and voltage regulation; the switching power supply adopts pulse-width modulation (PWM) control to convert direct current into high-frequency alternating current. When analyzing the power supply circuit, it should be decomposed stage by stage in the order of "rectification-filtering-voltage regulation"; in the switching regulated power supply, the inductor, capacitor and freewheeling diode are the main components. The filter circuit is used to filter out the alternating current component in the pulsating direct current after rectification to obtain smooth direct current; its types include the L-type filter circuit, the π-type filter circuit and the RC filter circuit.

The voltage regulator circuit is used to stabilize the output voltage and current of the rectified power supply, so as to eliminate the influence of power grid fluctuations and load changes. Its types include the Zener diode voltage regulator circuit, the series-type voltage regulator circuit, the switching-type voltage regulator circuit, and the integrated voltage regulator circuit. The simplest form is a circuit composed of a Zener diode and a load connected in parallel; the series-type voltage regulator circuit detects voltage changes through sampling and stabilizes the output by amplifying and controlling the adjustment transistor; the switching-type voltage regulator circuit has the advantages of low power consumption, high efficiency, and small size but complex circuit; the three-terminal integrated voltage regulator integrates a high-power adjustment transistor and a protection circuit into the chip, with few peripheral components. The LM7800 series is a three-terminal integrated voltage regulator with positive voltage output, and the LM7900 series outputs negative voltage. Linear regulated power supplies usually add a voltage regulator circuit after rectification and filtering to meet high-quality power supply requirements.

Welding is an important step in the maintenance procedure of the PLC control system. The welding mechanism is to heat the weldment to melt the solder, produce atomic diffusion between the weldment and the solder, and form an alloy bonding layer at the interface after solidification. The formed alloy bonding layer has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength, and the welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products. If the welding essentials are not mastered, virtual welding is easy to occur; if too much solder is added, bridging (short circuit) will be caused, resulting in product performance not meeting design requirements. The copper foil pattern on the PCB is often covered with a thin layer of solder to reduce oxidation and promote solderability, and the effective time of this solder layer usually lasts about six months. During welding, flux (most commonly rosin) is needed to remove the oxide film on the surface of the metal to be welded and ensure solder wetting. When welding electronic components on the PCB, the principle of small first then large, low first then high should be followed; otherwise, after large or high components are welded, the welding quality of small components will be affected.

When the shading coil of the AC electromagnet is broken or falls off, it can be repaired by copper welding or replacing the shading coil.

The contactor includes a core and a coil.

In the power supply link of electronic equipment, the power supply circuit undertakes the task of supplying energy to circuits at all levels. It is generally composed of three parts: a rectifier circuit, a filter circuit, and a voltage regulator circuit. By type, there are three kinds: linear rectifier power supply, switching power supply, and inverter power supply.

The function of the filter circuit is to filter out the AC component in the pulsating direct current after rectification, thereby obtaining relatively smooth direct current. Common types include the L-type filter circuit, the π-type filter circuit, and the RC filter circuit. A filter circuit composed of an inductor and a capacitor is named the L-type filter circuit because its shape resembles an inverted L;

Photosensitive devices are widely used in automatic detection, photoelectric control, communication and alarm circuits.

The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel; during ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation circuit and fuel enters the nozzle for injection. Its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control fine water mist fire-extinguishing zones; it is energized in the burner ignition program, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit so that fuel enters the nozzle for injection. The PLC output interface converts digital signals into voltage or current to drive the solenoid valve to act. The automatic fuel boiler contains a photoresistor, a solenoid valve and a potentiometer. The control platform contains a sensor. The clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

In the electronic circuits of marine electrical equipment, a transistor is a semiconductor device containing two PN junctions internally and having current amplification capability, divided into NPN type and PNP type. The operating characteristics of the NPN type and the PNP type can complement each other, and the complementary pair in an OTL circuit works by making use of this feature. The measurable properties of a transistor include the tube type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor. When measuring with a multimeter, the larger the pointer deflection, the more unstable the performance.

The diode, used in conjunction with the transistor, has unidirectional conductivity as its main characteristic, that is, under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is very large or infinite. The circuit symbol of the diode is VD, with designations such as VD5; for the resistor, there is a dedicated resistor detection procedure applicable, and during maintenance the resistor can be judged good or bad by measuring item by item according to this procedure. The capacitor detection procedure is applicable to the capacitor, and during maintenance the earth leakage and capacitance can be measured according to this procedure. The pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise;

The switching power supply adopts pulse width modulation (PWM) control to convert direct current into high-frequency alternating current; in the switching regulated power supply, the inductor, capacitor and freewheeling diode are the main components. The programmable logic controller (PLC) includes a power supply section, which is responsible for converting AC or DC power into the DC working power required by the internal circuits, wherein the first type of power supply feeds the integrated circuit, providing +5V and +15V DC power.

The printed circuit board consists of a base material and traces; the base material is an insulating material, often called the substrate, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the trace part is made of conductive copper, laid on the substrate, and the required pattern is obtained by etching. Besides the conductive traces, the printed circuit board also includes sockets, earthing points, slots and pads (connection points). Dust, oil mist and salt mist on board ships easily cause the insulation performance of the printed circuit board to deteriorate or even cause a short circuit; when cleaning, an electrical cleaner can be used to spray-wash oil stains and salt crystals, and the operation must be carried out with the external power supply cut off.

For the printed circuit board, attention must be paid to the soldering requirements for electronic components; before assembly, the overall circuit of the unit must be basically finalized, and the assembly method of the components on the printed circuit board must be determined according to the volume and the dimensions of the enclosure. Layout generally starts with the larger components such as the power transformer and the integrated circuit; connectors are also larger components and are usually laid out first, while small components are laid out flexibly according to the gaps. The assembly methods of diodes, inductors and resistance-capacitance components generally include the upright type, the prone type and the mixed type; upright mounting means resistors, capacitors and diodes are mounted vertically on the printed circuit board, with the advantage that more components are accommodated per unit area and the arrangement is compact. The welding sequence should follow the principle of small before large and low before high, otherwise, after the large or high devices are welded, the welding quality of the small components will be affected; at the same time, unnecessary component pins need to be cut off, and the surface of the printed circuit board must be cleaned. The circuit board repair procedure is applicable to the printed circuit board, and during maintenance the fault can be located by troubleshooting level by level according to this procedure. If the welding essentials are not mastered, virtual welding is easily produced;

When using an electric soldering iron, pay attention to the high temperature of the metal part to prevent personal burns; frequently check whether the power cord has exposed copper wire, and if so, wrap it with insulating tape; when the electric soldering iron is not in use, cut off the power supply in time and let it cool naturally. These contents constitute the precautions for using an electric soldering iron; marine electrical equipment requires the precautions for using an electric soldering iron during welding and maintenance operations to ensure operational safety. The multimeter is widely used in maintenance; the multimeter can be used to measure resistor, voltage, capacitance, diode and transistor. Voltage is one of the meter readings that need to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis; voltage can be measured using a multimeter or a voltmeter; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems.

A timer is a digital logic circuit application component used in household appliances; in marine living equipment it is often used to control the start and stop of electric fans, the washing and spinning programs of the washing machine, and the defrosting cycle of cold storage; the electric fan contains a timer; in the troubleshooting of the electric fan, if it sometimes rotates and sometimes does not, one of the possible causes is timer failure, and the remedy is to replace the timer; in the troubleshooting of the washing machine not working after the power is switched on, it is necessary to check whether the wiring of the timer is loose or disconnected, whether the timer knob slips, and whether the contact is in good contact.

Electronic equipment extensively uses various passive and active components, and the judgment of their performance and fault handling are common contents of maintenance work. The variable resistor is one of the three major classifications of resistor. If the pointer cannot return to infinity, the reading multiplied by the range is the leakage resistance.

The circuit symbol is VD, numbered such as VD5; marine electrical equipment uses transistors, and a transistor may develop a transistor fault. The larger the pointer deflection, the more unstable the performance. Marine electrical equipment uses integrated circuits. Marine electrical equipment uses power supply circuits. The power supply part is a component of the PLC, responsible for converting AC and DC power into the three types of DC working power supplies required by the internal circuits; the first type of power supply feeds the integrated circuit and is a +5V and +15V DC power supply. If the welding essentials are not mastered, virtual welding is likely to occur; both the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter belong to multimeters. The multimeter uses resistor, voltage, current, capacitance, diode, transistor, thyristor, photosensitive device and thermocouple for measurement; the clamp-on ammeter uses current. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and the voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, the ammeter and the clamp-on ammeter.

The conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation; interview the operator before observation, and check the monitoring and indicating device before observation. Before switching on the power supply, it must be checked whether there is a short circuit or earthing fault in the input and output parts, and only after confirmation can the power be switched on. During the debugging of the regulated power supply, after switching on the power supply, if there is no abnormality, the first step should be to adjust the potentiometer to test the output voltage range. The PLC starts the self-diagnosis process as soon as the power supply is switched on; if an internal error occurs in the CPU, the panel "CPU Error" lamp indicates an abnormality; after eliminating the interference of external surge voltage, it is necessary to switch on the power supply again to observe whether the PLC fault disappears, otherwise replace the CPU board.

In the maintenance practice of marine electrical equipment, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure and working principle of the electrical equipment as well as the functions and locations of the components (assemblies), which is the basic prerequisite for carrying out fault diagnosis and repair work. Maintenance personnel should master the whole set of methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, and be very familiar with the ship-wide electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components in actual work, so as to quickly narrow the scope of troubleshooting.

The multimeter is the most commonly used multi-purpose instrument in the maintenance of electronic equipment; it consists of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit. The current flowing through the meter head of the multimeter at full scale is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes; the changeover switch of the multimeter is used to switch between different measurement functions and ranges; the measuring circuit of the multimeter performs signal conversion. Multimeters are divided into two types, analog and digital; the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter each have their own advantages. Taking the MF-47 multimeter as an example, it is a typical product in the multimeter family, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and its panel is provided with four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The MF-30 multimeter is an instrument commonly used in FU-related circuit testing. The multimeter can be used to measure various parameters and devices such as resistors, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples, and is a basic tool for judging whether components are good or bad and the state of a circuit.

In circuit diagrams, the fuse serves as a protective component and its graphical symbol is FU; the fuse corresponds to FU, and FU is the symbol of the fuse. The fuse is a safety device that, when overload and short circuit occur in the power network or electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. It belongs to distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is a screw-type fuse, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. FU fuse blowing is one of the causes of the contactor KM coil being de-energized and unable to close. The fuse performs the overload and short circuit protection function in the ship power system, and its symbol FU is used uniformly in circuit diagrams.

The printed circuit board consists of two parts: the base material and the wiring. The base material is often called the substrate; the most commonly used are phenolic resin board and epoxy glass; the phenolic resin board is yellow and insulating, while epoxy glass uses glass fiber as the base material. Marine electrical equipment widely uses printed circuit boards, and printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components, since welding quality directly affects the reliability of the circuit board.

A circuit board fault may occur on the printed circuit board, and the circuit board fault is a typical fault on this type of carrier, the printed circuit board. The manifestations of a circuit board fault include integrated ICs or other components being burnt or cracked, and the circuit board being broken or cracked. The circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards. Before maintenance, the user shall be carefully asked about the fault symptom of the circuit board, and when conditions permit, the site shall be visited to confirm the correctness of connections and the standardization of operation so as to eliminate misjudgment. When it is necessary to confirm a circuit board fault, the correctness of connections, the firmness of plugging and the situation of setting changes shall be checked, and whether the steps of operating the equipment are correct shall be verified, so as to avoid misjudgment caused by improper operation. Improper operation is one of the causes of a single-phase earthing fault in the power system; faults caused by improper operation commonly include improper closing operation, unbalanced load control of the generator, and improper operation caused by observation errors; during parallel operation, improper grasp of the closing moment or reversed adjustment direction of load sharing may cause the generator reverse power protection to trip.

If it is not confirmed before maintenance whether the steps of operating the equipment are correct, misjudgment of the circuit board fault may be caused by improper operation. The recent use of the faulty circuit board shall be understood, to distinguish whether it is an aging phenomenon or a newly occurring symptom; if there is a repair record, the repair history and the replaced devices shall be confirmed to assist fault analysis. When an abnormal function of a device is found, the surrounding related devices and wiring shall be further checked; when the fault cannot be confirmed, the suspected device may be removed and measured separately for judgment. The complete flow of the circuit board repair procedure includes such steps as asking about the fault symptom, observing fault traces, preliminary analysis of the fault location, preparation before power-on testing, and division of functional areas, among which the preparation before power-on testing requires confirming the power supply type, positive and negative polarity, vulnerable devices of the faulty circuit board, and whether there is a short circuit, missing parts or other problems.

Contactor A contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in marine power systems; it belongs to the low-voltage control apparatus and undertakes the control task of motors in electric drive systems. The power of various auxiliary machinery on board is almost entirely driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on board. This type of apparatus features accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. A contactor comprises an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil; the arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the main contacts open, the main contacts undertake the task of making and breaking the main circuit, and the core and coil together form the electromagnetic mechanism; after the coil is energized, electromagnetic attraction is generated to drive the core to act, thereby driving the main contacts to close or open. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and its content is developed around the above-mentioned arc chute, main contacts, core, coil and other components.

Circuit breaker A circuit breaker is a switching apparatus used to protect circuits in marine power systems; it belongs to the low-voltage distribution apparatus and is divided into the frame type (air circuit breaker) and the molded-case type, having both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. Air circuit breakers are mostly used as generator main switches and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers and deals with various abnormalities occurring during operation of the circuit breaker.

A circuit breaker may have various faults. The circuit breaker may have the fault that when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close, that is, when the circuit breaker is operated manually, its contacts cannot close normally. In addition, the circuit breaker may also have the condition that the contacts of one phase cannot close. The shunt trip unit being unable to make the circuit breaker open, and the undervoltage trip unit being unable to make the circuit breaker open, both belong to faults in the trip unit. The circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor, and the circuit breaker automatically opening about 1 h after closing, are two types of opening abnormalities occurring during operation. In addition, noise in the undervoltage trip unit, excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, failure of the auxiliary switch, and malfunction of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit causing the circuit breaker to open are also faults that may occur in the circuit breaker. For these faults, each item should be checked and handled in accordance with the requirements of circuit breaker maintenance, so that the circuit breaker resumes normal switching and protection functions.

Basic categories of marine electrical apparatus Marine electrical equipment is of many kinds; according to the task undertaken in the circuit, it can be broadly classified into two major categories: distribution apparatus and control apparatus. Distribution apparatus undertakes the distribution of electrical energy and the protection of circuits, with fuses and circuit breakers as typical representatives; control apparatus undertakes the switching on and off of circuits and the control of operating states, and contactors belong to this category. In addition, there is another category of apparatus used for measurement and detection, such as the changeover switch, and the resistor as a basic constituent unit of the circuit. The functions, model designation and common faults of these are described below by category.

Distribution apparatus The symbol of the fuse in circuit diagrams is FU; it is a protective apparatus that, when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element, and thus has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. As distribution apparatus, the fuse has the feature of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. Among commonly used models, the RL93 series is of screw-type structure, voltage 380 V, current 6~600 A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection; the fuse corresponds to the symbol FU, and this should be used for identification when reading drawings.

A circuit breaker is a switching apparatus used to protect circuits in marine power systems; it belongs to the low-voltage distribution apparatus and can likewise maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. Circuit breakers are divided into two types, the frame type (air circuit breaker) and the molded-case type, and have both switching and protection functions. Air circuit breakers are mostly used as generator main switches and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid; molded-case circuit breakers are used as branch, load panel or lighting panel switches and have overload or short circuit protection. A circuit breaker may have many faults during operation. If the circuit breaker is operated manually and the contacts cannot close, this is a common fault; in addition, the circuit breaker may also have the contacts of one phase unable to close, the shunt trip unit unable to make the circuit breaker open, the undervoltage trip unit unable to make the circuit breaker open, the circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker automatically opening about 1 h after closing, noise in the undervoltage trip unit, excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, failure of the auxiliary switch, and malfunction of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit causing the circuit breaker to open, etc.

For these situations, circuit breaker maintenance should be a fixed part of routine inspection.

The control device contactor is an electrical device used in the ship's power system to control motors. It belongs to low-voltage control devices and is used in electric drive systems, featuring accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost entirely driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor is composed of an arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and the condition of these components directly determines whether the contactor can operate reliably. Contactor maintenance requires keeping it clean; in particular, the contactors in the deck crane control box should have dust and oil dirt removed to prevent the moving system from jamming.

The function of the changeover switch for measurement and detection electrical devices is to select the measurement object and select the range. On the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set working states and issue operating commands, and it has relatively many selection positions and contacts. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not left open. The multimeter contains a changeover switch, by means of which the switching of measurement functions and ranges is realized.

The multimeter can be used to measure resistor, voltage and current. When measuring resistor, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistor, and never measure with power on. Current measurement can use a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter; the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement; to measure current an ammeter must be used, connected in series after breaking the circuit.

Resistor and its detection Resistors are widely used in marine electrical equipment. A resistor is an electronic component with a certain resistance value, geometric shape and technical performance that serves to limit current in a circuit, and is usually divided into three major categories: fixed resistors, variable resistors and special resistors, among which fixed resistors are most used in electronic products. Variable resistors, photoresistors and thermistors all fall within the category of resistors. Common fixed resistors can be divided by manufacturing material into RT-type carbon film resistors, RJ-type metal film resistors, RX-type wirewound resistors and chip resistors, with power ratings of 0.125W (1/8W), 0.25W (1/4W),
0.5W (1/2W), 1W, 2W, 3W, 5W, 7W, 10W, etc. The resistor detection steps are applicable to the inspection and judgment of resistors; a resistor may develop a resistance fault, and a resistance fault is a common problem in the use of resistors. The resistance value of a resistor can be measured with a multimeter.

Junction box The junction box is a component used in the ship's electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical components. The general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc. The solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box, but is connected directly into the local control box; this difference should be noted when wiring.

The position of the contactor in the ship's power system is determined by the drive mode of the ship's auxiliary machinery. The power of various auxiliary machinery on board is almost entirely provided by motors, and the starting, stopping and running switching of the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on board. As a ship's low-voltage control device, the contactor is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, featuring accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. In the automatic transfer circuit of the lighting busbar power supply, contactor interlocking is also used to realize the delayed connection and automatic transfer of the standby power supply.

Contactor maintenance is the regular work of marine electrical equipment management personnel, and its content covers cleaning, tightening, inspection of moving mechanisms, adjustment of contact parameters, and coil inspection, among other aspects.

Keeping the contactor clean is the primary step of maintenance work. Excessive accumulation of dirt will cause the moving system to jam and increase mechanical wear, so dust and oil dirt on parts must be removed promptly. Contactors in the control box of deck cargo winches are in the midst of loading and unloading dust and should be cleaned more frequently. When cleaning, first blow with compressed air, then brush with a bristle brush, then wipe off oil dirt with a cleaning agent or alcohol-soaked cloth; spray-type electrical cleaners may also be used for cleaning. General cleaning practice is connected with the basic content of motor maintenance work, which includes cleaning the motor itself and the motor installation environment, removing external dirt to ensure normal operation and heat dissipation of the motor; during general cleaning, attention must be paid to precautions for cleaning motor windings so as to avoid damaging winding insulation.

Regularly inspecting all fastening screws and fasteners of the contactor is one of the core contents of regular maintenance work for marine contactors. During inspection, special attention must be paid to the fastening state of the stationary contacts and the fastening state of the wiring terminals. Once these parts become loose, they will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance, thereby causing local overheating and even faults such as phase failure or phase-to-phase short circuit. Poor contact, as a fault state, means that the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation, or foreign matter; under harsh conditions on board, wiring heads and terminals are prone to rust, which also easily causes poor contact in the input and output circuits of the programmable logic controller, i.e. PLC, and poor contact will cause random output actions, with the corresponding remedy being to check the terminal wiring. When the surface of the commutator of a DC motor is too dirty or the brush spring pressure is too small, poor contact between brush and commutator will likewise result.

Regularly checking by hand whether the moving mechanism of the contactor operates flexibly and injecting a small amount of lubricating oil into the shaft constitute the third routine item of marine contactor maintenance work. During operation, check the flexibility of the moving mechanism by hand; if a bearing is installed at the shaft, a small amount of lubricating oil needs to be injected into the bearing, the purpose being to prevent the moving system from jamming or increased mechanical wear due to accumulated dirt. The shaft is a mechanical transmission component used to transmit torque and rotary motion, commonly found in motors, contactors, and instruments; the moving parts of the two units of an electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; a changeover switch is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a shaft, and a panel, assembled by bolts. One of the fault causes for a contactor fails to pick up or releasing slowly is precisely moving parts jammed, or the shaft being rusted or skewed. When an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud non-uniform noise and the characteristic of the bearing end cover overheating. Therefore, checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition both need to be carried out using the bearing as the object.

Regularly checking and adjusting the pressure, opening distance, and overtravel of contactor contacts is another routine maintenance item. The main contact is the switching component in a contactor used to make or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor. After maintenance, measuring tools such as calipers and feeler gauges are needed to measure the opening distance of the main contacts, i.e. the minimum distance between the moving and stationary contacts when fully separated; the overtravel of the main contacts refers to the displacement of the moving contact after the stationary contact is removed when fully closed, which can be obtained by conversion from measuring the gap. If copper main contacts discolor or give off a burnt smell, it indicates that the contacts have already developed poor contact and generated overheating; at this time the opening distance and overtravel need to be adjusted and the oxide film removed. Silver main contacts should not be rubbed with abrasive cloth; they should be cleaned with a dry cloth or cleaning agent, and applying lubricating oil is prohibited to prevent poor contact. When the three-phase main contacts wear unevenly, the clearance can be adjusted by bending the moving contact bridge arm; after adjustment, synchronous contact of the three phases must be ensured. If the contacts have been overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected as a replacement; serious burning of the contact surface causing poor contact or burrs is also one of the causes of contact welding.

Regularly checking whether the contactor coil is firmly mounted on the core and whether the temperature rise is too high is likewise not to be neglected.

Before use, the insulation resistance of the coil shall be tested with an insulation resistance tester; the insulation resistance between phases and to earth is required to be greater than 1MΩ. The insulation resistance tester, also called a megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is a portable instrument used for measuring the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables; according to the highest voltage generated by the hand-cranked generator, it is divided into specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V and 2500V. When measuring the insulation resistance of an electrical equipment coil to earth, the E terminal post of the insulation resistance tester may be connected to the core. A coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulation framework and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, namely the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions shall be checked.

Coil open circuit is one of the main fault causes leading to the contactor failing to pick up; the detection method is to measure the coil resistance with a multimeter after de-energizing, to determine whether it is open-circuited. If an open circuit occurs at the surface layer of the coil, the coil may be removed, the broken turns removed, and the same enameled wire used to make up the turns and weld them firmly; if the open circuit is in the deep layer of the coil or at the inner contact, it cannot be repaired and the coil can only be rewound. Coil open circuit also manifests in other equipment; for example, in the disc-type electromagnetic brake of deck machinery, a coil open circuit causes the spring to push the armature back and generate braking torque; a broken conductor of a motor winding or an electrical appliance coil belongs to the type of open-circuit fault existing in the equipment itself. The KM coil fault in the contactor is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature being unable to close and the motor failing to start.

The core is the magnetic-conducting component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as the reference point for insulation measurement. During contactor maintenance, it is necessary to check whether the coil is firmly mounted on the core and to test the insulation resistance between the coil and the core. If there is oil dirt or rust on the core surface, it shall be removed to keep the contact surface clean; if the shading coil is broken, the core shall be repaired or replaced. Oil sludge adhering to the core pole face will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed; oil dirt, dust or poor contact on the core pole face will cause loud noise of the electromagnet; the causes of loud noise of an AC electromagnet also include foreign matter on the core pole face, poor contact, or breakage and falling-off of the shading coil. The shading coil is a copper ring-shaped component mounted on the core pole face of an AC electromagnet, used to eliminate armature vibration noise; its breakage or falling-off will cause the AC electromagnet to produce relatively loud noise; when damaged, it may be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil may be directly replaced; one of the causes of noise in the undervoltage trip unit is also breakage of the shading coil; during the secondary maintenance of the contactor, it is necessary to check the non-magnetic shim, the shading coil and the copper sleeve for damage. When estimating the number of turns of an AC coil, the formula N = 45 * U / (B * A) may be used, in which B is usually taken as 0.9～1.2T, and A represents the cross-sectional area of the original coil core, in cm²; when calculating the number of turns of a DC coil, the wire diameter d shall include the thickness of the insulation layer.

The insulation layer is used to electrically insulate the conductive core wires and prevent short circuit or earthing between core wires; in the structure of a marine cable it is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer, and a marine cable contains such an insulation layer.

The arc chute is a component of the contactor and the circuit breaker, used to extinguish the arc generated when the contact breaks. When the arc chute is cracked, damaged or severely carbonized, it shall be replaced in time; when the grid plates are severely burnt, deformed or loose, a new chute shall be replaced; the fallen objects in the chute and the metal particles produced by contact arcing shall also be removed. The integrity of the arc chute plates shall be checked and the soot and fine metal dust on the surface shall be removed; the outer cover shall be intact, and if damaged it shall be replaced. When troubleshooting the jamming fault of the moving part of the contactor, the arc chute shall be removed first.

In the measurement stage, the multimeter may be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. When measuring a resistor in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test shall be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply shall be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it shall be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with the power on. Measuring current requires an ammeter, which is connected in series after the circuit is opened. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open circuit of the shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating function.

Relay maintenance, circuit breaker maintenance and PLC maintenance all belong to the maintenance items of ship electrical equipment. Relay maintenance applies to transistor relays, circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers, and PLC maintenance applies to programmable logic controllers, that is, programmable logic controllers (PLCs). As far as the scope of the evidence involved is concerned, the evidence only involves contactor maintenance and does not contain the specific content of circuit breaker maintenance, and PLC maintenance is also not mentioned in the evidence.

Contactors are used in large quantities on ships because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the operation of the motors is controlled by contactors. As electrical equipment for controlling motors in the ship power system, the contactor internally contains parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, among which the main contact undertakes the task of making or breaking the main circuit current, and its closed state directly determines whether the motor can run. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors. During daily maintenance, the contactor should be kept clean, especially the contactors in the deck cargo winch control box, where dust and oil dirt must be removed in time to prevent the moving system from being stuck.

At the same time, the fastening screws and wiring terminals should be checked regularly; once they become loose, faults such as poor contact, local overheating, phase failure or phase-to-phase short circuit will be caused.

If the main contact shows copper discoloration or gives off a burnt smell, it indicates that poor contact has already caused overheating; at this time, the gap and overtravel need to be adjusted, and the oxide film on the contact surface should be removed. When the main contact has been overheated for a long time or has already been welded together, the contactor should be replaced with one whose rated current is one grade larger. After the repair is completed, measuring tools such as calipers and feeler gauges should be used to measure the gap of the main contact, that is, the minimum distance when the moving and stationary contacts are completely separated; the overtravel of the main contact refers to the displacement produced by the moving contact after the stationary contact is removed in the fully closed state, and this value can be obtained by conversion through measuring the clearance.

The contact spring is related to the contact pressure. The initial contact pressure is the pressure acting on the contact when the moving and stationary contacts just touch, and the final contact pressure is the pressure acting on the contact when the contact is fully closed. During measurement, the height of the spring installation space in the two states of contact separation and closure can first be measured, and then the spring pressure can be measured, thereby obtaining the initial contact pressure and final contact pressure. If there is no original data, the final contact pressure can be calculated according to the formula F_z =
9.8 ×
2.25 I_N / 100.

If the contact spring pressure is too large or the overtravel is too large, the noise of the AC electromagnet will become louder; while too small a contact spring pressure is one of the causes of contact welding.

The maintenance of the core must not be neglected either. Once the shading coil is broken, the core should be repaired or replaced. The causes of loud noise in the AC electromagnet include foreign matter on the pole face of the core, poor contact, and breakage or falling off of the shading coil; at this time, the armature position needs to be checked and corrected, mechanical jamming should be eliminated, and the core should be made to attract flatly and firmly. Failure or damage of the armature reaction spring is also one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed. In contactor maintenance, measuring the insulation resistance is a task that must be completed; it is necessary to measure the insulation resistance between contacts, between the coil and the core, and between live parts and ground. During measurement, the voltage grade of the insulation resistance tester should be selected according to the rated voltage of the contactor. The commonly used measuring tool is the insulation resistance tester, such as an ohmmeter.

As a switching device for protecting circuits in the ship power system, the circuit breaker is divided into the frame type and the molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. Among them, the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. Among its common faults, when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contact cannot close; when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contact likewise cannot close; in addition, one phase contact cannot close, the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1 h after closing, the undervoltage trip unit has noise, the temperature rise of the circuit breaker is too high, the auxiliary switch fails, and malfunction of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit causes the circuit breaker to open.

In the ship power system, the contactor undertakes the task of controlling motors and is used in large quantities on ships because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor itself contains parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; the maintenance work should be carried out around these components. During maintenance, the flexibility of the operating mechanism needs to be checked manually at regular intervals, and a small amount of lubricating oil should be injected into the shaft (or bearing, if any).

The contactor fails to pick up, which is one of the common faults, and may be caused by a broken power supply line, a coil open circuit, or moving parts jammed. When judging, first measure the voltage across the two ends of the coil: if there is no voltage across the two ends of the coil, it indicates that the power supply line is broken, and the line needs to be checked to eliminate the broken line; if there is voltage, it indicates a coil open circuit. After de-energizing, use a multimeter to measure the coil resistance to determine whether it is open circuit so as to decide to replace the coil. In addition, undervoltage of the power supply (below 85% of the rated voltage) or large fluctuation, insufficient capacity of the operating power supply, and internal short circuit of the coil can also cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force. If the voltage of the contactor coil measured with a multimeter is lower than 85% of the rated voltage, it can be determined as undervoltage of the power supply.

Failure or damage of the return spring of the armature will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly when the stop button is pressed; when handling, the return spring needs to be replaced or adjusted, and care should be taken that the return force is not too large. Contact welding will also cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly when the stop button is pressed; if contact welding occurs frequently, the contactor should be changed to one of the next higher current rating. Such faults usually appear in parallel with failure of the armature return spring, contact welding, etc.

There are many causes of coil overheating or burning. Overvoltage of the power supply (>1.1U~) or undervoltage (<0.85U) will cause coil overheating or burning, and the handling method is to adjust the power supply voltage to the normal range. If the technical parameters of the coil (such as rated voltage, frequency, duty ratio, etc.) do not match the actual operating conditions, coil overheating or burning will result, and the handling method is to select a coil or contactor that matches the actual working conditions. Local internal short circuit of the coil will cause coil overheating or burning, which can be determined by the resistance comparison method, and after determination the coil should be replaced. Too high an operating frequency will cause contactor coil overheating or burning, and the contactor should be changed to one of the next higher current rating. Special operating environments, such as humid air, corrosive gases, or too high an ambient temperature, can cause coil overheating or burning, and a contactor suitable for the special conditions should be used. Moving parts jammed causing long-time energization will also cause contactor coil overheating or burning; for handling, refer to the measures for moving parts jammed when the contactor fails to pick up.

Regarding contact welding, too small a contact capacity is one of the main causes; a load short circuit will cause contact welding, and the contact should be replaced after the fault is eliminated; insufficient holding force (such as voltage below 85%U_N) may cause contact welding; too small a contact spring pressure is one of the factors causing contact welding; too frequent operation or overload use will likewise cause contact welding. The handling method is to open the contact and trim the burrs with a fine file or replace the contact; if welding occurs frequently, the contactor should be changed to one of the next higher current rating. In the JZF-H motor, welding of the ZDC auxiliary contact will cause long-term locked-rotor of the medium-speed winding; welding of the brake contactor auxiliary contact or jamming in the closed state will cause long-term locked-rotor of the winding. Moving parts jammed and long-time energization are often caused by mechanical factors such as shaft rusting, skewing, or oil sludge adhesion on the core pole face; for handling, likewise refer to the measures for moving parts jammed when the contactor fails to pick up.

During detection, the multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument, which consists of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch, and the measuring circuit; at full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. The analog multimeter is a type of multimeter, and the digital multimeter is also a type of multimeter. The MF-47 multimeter is a type of multimeter, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and its panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V", and "5A". The multimeter can be used to measure the resistance value of a resistor, the voltage value of a voltage, and the current value of a current, and can also be used to detect capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices, and thermocouples. When measuring direct current, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range, and the meter head is connected in series in the broken branch; when measuring direct voltage, the test leads are connected in parallel across the two ends of the component under test, and when the range is uncertain, first set to the maximum range. The generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in an AC electric drive system; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in an AC electric drive system.

Structurally, the contactor includes the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and all of these must be attended to one by one during maintenance. The work of contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; routine maintenance must first keep it clean, especially the contactors in the deck cargo winch control box, where dust and oil dirt must be removed promptly, otherwise the moving system is easily jammed. Fastening screws and wiring terminals must be checked regularly; once loose, they will cause poor contact, the contact resistance will then increase, and this in turn will cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure or short circuit between phases. Discoloration of copper contacts or scorching of insulating parts often indicates that the contacts are already in poor contact and have generated overheating. During servicing, also check whether the coil is firmly mounted on the core, and measure the insulation resistance between the coil and the core;

Loud noise of the electromagnet (AC) is one of the common fault manifestations of the contactor, and its causes involve several aspects. Low supply voltage will cause loud noise of the electromagnet (AC); in this case the supply voltage must be adjusted to 0.85~1.10 times the rated voltage; excessive contact spring pressure or excessive overtravel will likewise cause loud noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the corresponding remedy is to adjust the contact spring and overtravel; a skewed armature or mechanical jamming, so that the core cannot pull in flat and firmly, will also cause loud noise of the electromagnet (AC), and when dealing with it the armature position should be corrected and the mechanical jamming removed; foreign matter on the core pole face (such as oil dirt, dust and mud) or poor contact will cause loud noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the pole face must be cleaned and the core adjusted so that it makes good contact; a broken or fallen-off shading coil will cause loud noise of the electromagnet (AC), and the repair method is to weld it properly with copper or replace the shading coil. The shading coil is a copper ring-shaped part mounted on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core, used to eliminate armature vibration noise; once it breaks, besides causing noise of the AC electromagnet, it will also cause noise of the undervoltage trip unit, in which case the armature or core should be replaced accordingly.

Contact welding is another type of fault that requires key handling; contact welding will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly when the stop button is pressed. There are many causes of contact welding: too small a contact capacity will cause contact welding, and a suitable contactor should be selected as a replacement; a load short circuit will cause contact welding, and when dealing with it the load short circuit fault must first be eliminated before replacing the contacts; insufficient holding force will cause contact welding, and it is necessary to check whether the supply voltage is below 85% of the rated voltage and to remove the mechanical resistance; too small a contact spring pressure will cause contact welding, and the contact spring must be replaced or repaired and the contact pressure adjusted to standard; if welding occurs frequently, a contactor one current rating larger should be substituted. After opening the contacts, dressing the burrs with a fine file or replacing the contacts is a common means of dealing with welding.

Insufficient holding force is itself also a type of fault cause of the contactor; when the contactor fails to pick up or has insufficient holding force, it is often accompanied by a humming sound. Insufficient capacity of the operating power supply will cause insufficient holding force of the contactor; an internal short circuit of the coil will cause the contactor to exhibit the phenomenon of insufficient holding force; jamming of the moving part, excessive spring reaction force or rusted shaft can also cause insufficient holding force of the contactor. In the electromagnetic brake, a too dirty core pull-in face will cause insufficient holding force, resulting in failure to release the brake or a half-released state.

Checking the power supply is a maintenance procedure that runs through the handling of the above faults. When the AC electromagnet is noisy, the supply voltage must be adjusted to 0.85~1.10 times the rated value; when contact welding is caused by insufficient holding force, it should be checked whether the supply voltage is below 85%U_N. Motor fails to start, motor speed low after starting, motor temperature rise high and excessive sparking under brush all correspond to the procedure of checking the power supply. A multimeter or voltmeter may be used to measure the voltage. When carrying out the procedure of checking the power supply, note that before disassembly the circuit terminals must be marked clearly one by one, so as to avoid confusion when the wiring is restored. A power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply.

In the ship's power system, the contactor undertakes the task of controlling the motor. The power of almost all kinds of auxiliary machinery on board comes from motors, and the starting, stopping and running of the motors are controlled by contactors, so the contactor is used in large quantities. Structurally, the contactor includes the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, etc. The work of contactor maintenance is exactly applicable to the contactor itself, and daily maintenance must be carried out around these parts. The primary content of maintenance work is to keep it clean, especially the contactor in the control box of the deck cargo winch; dust and oil dirt should be removed in time to prevent the moving system from being stuck. For an AC coil, its number of turns can be estimated according to N = 45 * U / (B * A), where B is usually taken as 0.9~1.2T.

In fault diagnosis, current is an electrical quantity that needs to be mastered; the measurable performance is the current value, and a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter can be used for measurement. To measure current, it is generally necessary to disconnect the circuit and then connect the ammeter in series.

One of the common fault symptoms of the contactor is contact overheating or burning. There are many causes of this symptom. Insufficient contact spring pressure or too small overtravel will cause contact overheating or burning; the corresponding treatment is to adjust the spring pressure and overtravel to the specified values, and this operation belongs to the maintenance procedure of adjusting the spring. Poor contact of contacts will likewise cause contact overheating or burning; during treatment, the contact surface should be cleaned, the surface should be dressed, and the contact should be firmly fastened to the conductive plate. Severe wear and desoldering of contacts are also one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning; the criterion is that the contact wear reaches one third of the original thickness or desoldering occurs, and at this time new contacts should be replaced to eliminate the fault. Too frequent operation or excessive current, or insufficient contact capacity, will also cause contact overheating or burning; for this cause, a contactor with a larger capacity should be selected. In addition, too high an ambient temperature or use inside a closed control box is also one of the fault causes of contact overheating or burning; in such cases the contactor should be used with derating.

Another fault symptom is excessive wear of contacts, which is numbered 8 among the fault symptoms. Too frequent operation and excessive working current are one of the main causes of excessive wear of contacts; for frequent operation and excessive current, derating should be applied or a contactor suitable for frequent operation and matching the working current should be selected; if contact overheating is caused by this reason, a contactor with a larger capacity needs to be selected. Three-phase contacts being out of synchronization is also one of the causes of excessive wear of contacts; if it is caused by three-phase asynchronism, the contacts need to be adjusted to make them synchronous. A short circuit on the load side will likewise cause excessive wear of contacts; after a load-side short circuit occurs, the short circuit fault must first be eliminated, and then the contacts should be replaced.

The contact spring is an important part of the contactor. During measurement, the initial pressure and final pressure can be obtained by measuring the height of the spring installation space when the contacts are open and closed, and then measuring the spring pressure. When the reaction spring becomes smaller, the corresponding treatment is to adjust the spring.

The influence of poor contact is not limited to the contact itself; it will also cause random output action, and the corresponding inspection measure is to check the terminal wiring.

When maintaining the contactor, cleaning is the first step, especially for the contactor in the control box of the deck cargo winch; dust and oil dirt must be removed in time, otherwise the moving system is easily stuck. Before use, the insulation resistance of the coil should also be measured with an insulation resistance tester; the insulation resistance between phases and to ground must both be greater than 1MΩ. If the contacts have been overheated for a long time or have already been welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected as a replacement. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and the above operations such as cleaning, fastening, insulation testing and replacement are all carried out around the contactor.

Failure of the contactor to pick up is a common fault symptom, manifested as the armature being unable to pull in after the coil is energized, or being able to pull in but with insufficient holding force. There are many causes of this symptom; a broken power supply line, a coil open circuit or a stuck moving part may all cause the contactor to fail to pick up.

If there is voltage, it indicates a coil open circuit. After de-energizing, use a multimeter to measure the coil resistance to determine whether the coil is open-circuited, thereby deciding whether the coil needs to be replaced.

After pressing the start button, the contactor fails to pick up or has insufficient holding force accompanied by a humming sound; the causes can be classified into several categories. Undervoltage of the power supply or large fluctuations will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force accompanied by a humming sound after pressing the start button; a short circuit inside the coil will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force accompanied by a humming sound after pressing the start button; jamming of moving parts, excessive spring reaction force, or rusted or skewed shaft will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force accompanied by a humming sound after pressing the start button; too large contact gap (i.e., too large armature air gap) will cause the contactor to fail to pick up or have insufficient holding force accompanied by a humming sound after pressing the start button.

Among these, when the power supply voltage is too low, the voltage across the coil terminals may be lower than 85% of the rated voltage specified for the product;

For the above faults, the handling methods correspond respectively. When the power supply voltage is too low or fluctuates greatly, use a multimeter to measure the voltage across the coil terminals; if it is lower than 85% of the rated voltage, it is determined as undervoltage of the power supply. If the operating power supply capacity is insufficient, the handling method is to replace the operating power supply. If there is a short circuit inside the coil or a coil open circuit, the corresponding handling method is to replace the coil; for jamming of moving parts, excessive spring reaction force, or rusted or skewed shaft, remove the arc chute and press the armature to check whether it can flexibly drive the contacts; if the action is not flexible, remove the relevant parts for derusting, oiling, or tightening and alignment, and directly replace parts that are already deformed or damaged. If the rated voltage of the coil is higher than the line rated voltage, replace the coil with one matching the coil rated voltage.

If the contact gap is too large (i.e., the armature air gap is too large), the handling method is to adjust the armature air gap. A jammed armature will likewise prevent the contactor KM from closing, causing the motor to have no power and failure to start; when checking an open-circuit fault with or without power, the armature can be manually pushed to close the contacts so as to narrow the scope of inspection.

A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, and is divided into analog and digital types; at full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. The analog multimeter and the digital multimeter both fall within the category of multimeters. Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting, failure to start, low speed during load operation, and even excessive motor temperature or smoking. Load short circuit or overload corresponds to measurement with a multimeter, while coil short circuit corresponds to replacing the coil.

There are many types of electrical equipment used for control or protection in ship power systems, and the relay is one widely used category. According to the different sensing elements, relays can be divided into electromagnetic relay, induction relay and thermal relay, etc.; according to the nature of the input signal, there are voltage relay, current relay, power relay, temperature relay, pressure relay and water level relay, etc. These relays each perform their own functions in the control and protection circuits of ship electrical systems, and their maintenance quality directly affects the reliability of equipment operation.

An electromagnetic relay is basically similar in structure to a contactor; its sensing part is composed of a coil, and the coil carries an electrical signal, reflecting the input quantity of the relay. The voltage relay, current relay, time relay and intermediate relay all belong to specific types of electromagnetic relay.

When maintaining an electromagnetic relay, it is necessary to check the contact tightness between the armature and the core, and remove dust and dirt to ensure the accuracy of the operating value; parameters such as contact pressure, overtravel and gap should comply with the specifications in the manual, and no lubricating oil shall be applied to the contacts.
