The contactor itself contains components such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil; the maintenance method for the contactor is likewise applicable to the contactor itself, while the construction of the intermediate relay is the same as that of the contactor, and its function is to expand the contact capacity and number of contacts; fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the contactor maintenance method. The time relay often appears in circuits with symbols such as KT, SJ and SL, and is a type of electromagnetic relay classified by function.

The voltage relay belongs to the electromagnetic relay, and its coil uses voltage as the excitation input.

When the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced; winding it oneself will affect the operating value due to inaccurate number of turns. During periodic maintenance, it is necessary to check and adjust the operating voltage and release voltage values of its coil so that they meet the technical requirements. In the constant-power three-speed cargo winch, the voltage relay is used for undervoltage protection; after being energized, the normally open contact closes to energize the control circuit. The current relay likewise belongs to the electromagnetic relay, its coil carries the electrical quantity, and its structure is basically similar to that of the contactor. In the AC three-speed electric windlass, the current relay picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%; in the windlass system, misoperation of the overcurrent relay GLJ will cause the fault of no high speed at startup.

The thermal relay belongs to the thermal relay according to the classification of the sensing element, and its sensing part is a bimetallic strip. This kind of relay is used in large quantities on ships and is generally used to accomplish the overload protection task of small motors.

The setting value of the thermal relay should be set between 1.15 and 1.3 times the rated current of the motor; the rated current selection should be the same as the rated current of the motor, and the dial value must match. During daily maintenance, it is necessary to check whether the rated current value or dial value matches the rated current of the motor. The heat generated by poor contact of the wiring terminals will cause an error in the operating value, so the wiring terminals must be kept in good contact. If the bimetallic strip undergoes permanent deformation due to a huge short circuit current, it must be replaced rather than corrected. In control circuits such as those of the air compressor, the thermal relay realizes overload shutdown by opening the normally closed contact to break the control circuit; in the water supply circuit, the thermal relay FR and the fuse FU constitute overload and short circuit protection respectively.

The pressure relay belongs to the non-electrical quantity relay, its sensing part is usually an air bag, and its actuating part is the contact. In the auxiliary boiler, the pressure relay is used as a control appliance to automatically control the steam pressure; in the main engine system, the pressure relay is used as a protective appliance to monitor the main engine lubricating oil pressure.

Daily maintenance requires that the sampling conduit comply with the manual and be sealed to prevent leakage from affecting operation. When used as a protective appliance, the operating value must not be easily adjusted; after adjustment, an operating value test must be carried out; when used as a control appliance, the return coefficient must be reasonably adjusted to avoid too frequent starting and stopping of equipment or excessive output fluctuation. In the automatic control system of the air compressor, the pressure relay controls the starting and stopping of the motor through the high-pressure and low-pressure contacts; in the automatic control system of the fuel pump, the pressure relay detects the system pressure to trigger automatic switching of the pump and an alarm.

The temperature relay belongs to the non-electrical quantity relay, is used in relatively large quantities on ships, and has both control and protection functions. When used for cooling water temperature alarm, the temperature relay acts as a protective appliance; when used in scenarios such as the auxiliary boiler, the temperature relay can act as a control appliance.

Daily maintenance requires that the temperature-sensing element be in good contact with the heat source of the controlled object, otherwise it will cause an operating error. The probe used for monitoring the cooling water temperature of the main and auxiliary diesel engines should be in good contact with the wall of the measuring hole. In the cold storage system, the temperature relay acts as a regulating switch, and a deviation in its setting value will cause a serious deviation in the storage temperature; a contact fault, that is, failure to close or open, will cause abnormality of the liquid supply solenoid valve, resulting in refrigeration failure or overcooling. The water level relay is one of the relay types classified by the nature of the input signal, alongside the voltage relay, current relay, power relay, temperature relay and pressure relay. The water level relay has two major parts, the sensing part and the actuating part; when the input quantity reaches the setting value, it causes a step change in the controlled quantity, and in protection circuits it measures the controlled quantity and operates when the setting value is reached.

Failure of the thermal relay to operate is a common fault manifestation of the thermal relay. An excessively large setting value is one of the main causes of the thermal relay failing to operate, and it must be reset according to the rated current of the motor. Burning out of the thermal element will cause the thermal relay to lose its temperature-sensing function and fail to operate, and the thermal relay must be replaced. Jamming of the operating mechanism will cause refusal of the thermal relay to operate; during maintenance the cover plate must be opened to eliminate the fault and the flexibility must be tested manually. Accumulation of dust, rust, or wear and deformation of the transmission mechanism can all cause the thermal relay to fail to operate, and the dirt must be removed or the parts replaced. Damage to the adjustable part or failure to align with the scale will cause the setting of the thermal relay to become ineffective and it will fail to operate, and the thermal relay usually must be replaced. Incorrectly adjusting the setting value of the thermal relay too high, for example to 2, will cause it to fail to operate, thereby causing fuse blowing or the motor to smoke. When the motor is overloaded and the thermal relay does not operate, the fuse will blow to cut off the circuit.

The fuse uses FU as its symbol and has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. When overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or electrical equipment, the fuse automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. The fuse is a distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is a screw-type fuse, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection.

The electric remote control system of the main engine includes fuses and wiring terminals; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals is one of the common faults of electrical components. If the wiring terminals of the thermal relay have poor contact, the heat generated by the contact resistance will cause an error in the operating value. The wiring screws of the electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact; failure to tighten the external wiring screws of the thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be disconnected. In the case of a loose "COM" screw, tightening should be carried out accordingly. In electrical maintenance, tightening is the operating step used to ensure good contact of wiring terminals, screws and fastening mechanisms or to prevent loosening; if the fastening mechanism of the main switch is loose, tightening should be carried out, and when the screws connecting the two conductive parts of the circuit breaker are loose and cause excessive temperature rise, the screws also need to be tightened.

During maintenance, voltage, current and resistance are the electrical quantities that often need to be measured. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; the measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter. The multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. To measure current, an ammeter must be used, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with the power on.

The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. The core is the magnetically conductive component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil, and serve as an insulation measurement reference point; when measuring the insulation resistance to ground of the coil of electrical equipment, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in a through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor under test is directly interlinked with the core to replace the primary winding. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil's magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start; failure or loss of the armature return spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed.

If it is caused by the external wiring screws not being tightened, the maintenance method is to tighten the external wiring screws. If the main switch fastening mechanism is loose, tightening treatment should be carried out;

There are three aspects to the fault causes of the thermal relay control circuit not being energized. The first is that the thermal relay has not been reset, and the corresponding maintenance method is to perform the reset operation. In the ship's main propulsion device, the thermal relay not being reset is one of the causes of the control circuit not being energized; the second is burning out of the contacts or loss of elasticity of the movable contact spring, causing poor contact or inability to contact between the movable and fixed contacts, and the maintenance method is to replace the movable contact spring and the burned contacts. The third is that the dial or adjusting screw is turned to an unsuitable position and pushes the contacts open, and the corresponding maintenance method is to adjust the dial or adjusting screw. Poor contact of contacts will cause the contacts to overheat or burn; methods for handling poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface, and tightening the contacts and the conductive plate.

When the thermal relay cannot reset, too short an interval between reclosing and tripping is a common cause; when it is caused by too short a time interval, manual reset reclosing should be performed at about 5 mm; breakage of the reset leaf spring will cause the mechanical structure to be unable to reset, and when it is caused by breakage of the reset leaf spring, the entire thermal relay needs to be replaced. Inability of the mechanism to reset and reclose is one of the fault causes of the thermal relay being unable to reset, and its causes include too short an interval between reclosing and tripping and breakage of the reset leaf spring; the maintenance method for a short time interval is manual reset reclosing at about 5 mm, and the maintenance method for breakage of the reset leaf spring is to replace the thermal relay. Inability of the mechanism to reset and reclose will cause the contacts not to close during manual operation of the circuit breaker; at this time the reclosing contact surface should be adjusted to the specified value so that the mechanism can reclose normally.

Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance increases due to looseness, oxidation, or foreign matter at an electrical connection; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact, increase contact resistance, and can cause local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit, and other faults. Poor contact will cause random output action, and the corresponding measure is to check the terminal wiring. When the COM screw is loose, the corresponding handling method is to tighten it.

The types of non-electrical relays commonly used on ships include temperature relays and pressure relays, which are used in large quantities.

Transistor relays have the advantages of high precision, small size, wide delay range, resistance to impact and vibration, convenient adjustment and long life, and are composed of five major circuits: voltage conversion, rectification, amplitude monitoring, delay and execution. The voltage conversion circuit converts the input physical quantity X into a linear voltage signal, satisfying the relationship U=KX; the rectification circuit converts the weak AC voltage into DC to improve conversion accuracy and maintain the proportional relationship; the amplitude monitoring circuit judges whether the input signal reaches the set value, and often uses a voltage regulator tube or a Schmitt circuit. Relay maintenance is applicable to transistor relays; transistor relays with non-electrical inputs are difficult to repair on board and need to be sent to the factory for processing; those with electrical inputs are repaired according to the methods for electronic equipment. The transistor relay for motor overload protection converts power into voltage, satisfying the relationship U=KP. The fuse can only be used as short circuit protection for the motor, and should not be used as overload protection for the motor; excessive refrigerant charging in the refrigeration system causing excessively high pressure and excessive load will cause motor overload; the thermal relay FR operates when the motor is overloaded, disconnecting the control circuit and de-energizing the contactor KM to stop the machine.

A transistor contains two PN junctions inside and has current amplification capability. It is divided into two types, NPN type and PNP type, and their operating characteristics can complement each other, such as the complementary pair in an OTL circuit. In circuits, it is often represented by the letter VT plus a number, such as VT17 representing transistor number 17. Main models include PNP-type transistors such as A92 and 9015, and NPN-type transistors such as A42, 9014 and 9018. When marine electrical equipment uses transistors, the transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to the category of the transistor device. A multimeter can be used to measure voltage, current and transistors, and a clamp-on ammeter can be used to measure current. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status;

Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems.

When a thermal relay malfunctions, the cause can be found from multiple aspects. Bimetallic strip deformation is one of the fault causes of thermal relay malfunction; for the fault caused by bimetallic strip deformation, the maintenance method is to replace the thermal relay. Excessive motor starting time is also one of the fault causes of thermal relay malfunction; for this fault cause, the maintenance method is to reduce the motor starting time. Looseness of adjustable parts of the thermal relay is also one of the fault causes of thermal relay malfunction; the corresponding maintenance method is to tighten the loose parts. Too large a change in ambient temperature is one of the fault causes of thermal relay malfunction; for the fault caused by too large a change in ambient temperature, the maintenance method is to improve the operating environment. In thermal relays, too frequent operation is a common cause of malfunction; to deal with thermal relay malfunction caused by frequent operation, the operating frequency must be limited and reduced. A too-small setting value is one of the common fault causes of thermal relay malfunction; the corresponding maintenance method is to rotate the current adjustment knob to adjust the setting current, and the adjustment target is to set the setting current to the rated current value of the motor.

The repair of transistor relays falls within the scope of application of relay maintenance.

Transistors and printed circuit boards are used in marine electrical equipment. A transistor can measure the transistor type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor; the transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to the transistor. A printed circuit board is composed of an insulating base plate and conductive copper traces; the base material is often called the base plate, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the circuit part is made of conductive copper, laid on the base plate, and the required pattern is obtained by etching; the printed circuit board may suffer a circuit board fault, and a circuit board fault belongs to the printed circuit board; the circuit board repair procedure is applicable to printed circuit boards, and printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components.

The multimeter is used in maintenance to measure various objects. The multimeter is used for transistor measurement; the multimeter is used for thyristor measurement, and the thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, whose polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode can be measured. The time relay can be represented in circuits by KT, SJ, SL.

In the ship power system, the circuit breaker undertakes the tasks of making and breaking circuits and implementing protection under abnormal conditions. According to different structural forms and application occasions, circuit breakers can be divided into two types: air circuit breaker and molded-case type; the former has the model code DW and belongs to the frame-type automatic air circuit breaker, while the latter has the model code DZ. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and is the connecting component for connecting the generator to the power grid; when a short circuit occurs in the power grid or undervoltage occurs in the generator, it can automatically disconnect the generator from the power grid, thereby protecting the power grid;

it simultaneously has the functions of a switching device and a protective device, and can also implement protection under abnormal operating conditions such as overload. Once the air circuit breaker fails, the corresponding generator set will also fail. The molded-case circuit breaker is generally used as the switch of branch circuits, load panels, lighting panels or boxes; different models respectively have overload protection, short circuit protection, or both, and some models also have earth leakage protection; if the molded-case circuit breaker fails, the corresponding branch circuit will lose power. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker itself, and both types of circuit breakers usually require comprehensive maintenance and inspection every six months.

When maintaining the circuit breaker, the arc chute is one of the key components to be inspected. Both the contactor and the circuit breaker contain an arc chute, whose function is to extinguish the arc generated when the contact breaks. During inspection, check whether the arc chute plates are intact and remove soot and fine metal dust from the surface; the outer cover should be intact and undamaged, and should be replaced if damaged. When the arc chute is cracked, damaged or severely carbonized, it should be replaced in time; when the chute plates are severely burned, deformed or loose, a new chute should also be replaced.

The main switch is a component of the main switchboard. In the ship power station, it is used to connect and disconnect the generator and the main busbar, and has both switching and protection functions. It mainly consists of the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device and arc extinguishing device, etc., and also includes auxiliary contacts and the control and signal indication circuit. The main switch requires performance verification of undervoltage, overload, short circuit, reverse power, etc. every 4 to 5 years. If a local short circuit occurs inside the undervoltage coil, the suction force will decrease, and it will take a period of time before the trip unit operates, thereby causing automatic tripping after operating for a period of time; when mechanical assembly quality problems cause the three-phase contacts not to close simultaneously, a phase failure fault of the power grid may be caused. The DW14 circuit breaker adopts Japanese Terasaki technology and is equipped with an additional AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, which is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker.

The trip unit is an electrical component in the circuit breaker used to implement protection functions such as overload, short circuit and undervoltage and to drive the contacts to break. When inspecting the trip unit, the working pole faces of the electromagnet should be clean, flat and smooth, without rust or burrs. Misoperation of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit is often caused by external electromagnetic interference generated by the operation of nearby large electromagnets. The circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the cause may be that the instantaneous setting current of the overcurrent trip unit is too small. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; jamming of the armature will cause the contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start, while failure or damage of the armature reaction spring is one of the main reasons why the contactor does not release or releases slowly after the stop button is pressed.

Various fault symptoms occur during the operation of a circuit breaker. When the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contact cannot close, which is a common fault of the circuit breaker; when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contact likewise cannot close, which also belongs to the fault symptoms that can occur in a circuit breaker. In addition, there may also occur such cases as one phase contact failing to close, the shunt trip unit failing to trip the circuit breaker, the undervoltage trip unit failing to trip the circuit breaker, the circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker tripping automatically about 1 h after closing, noise in the undervoltage trip unit, excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, failure of the auxiliary switch, and the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctioning and causing the circuit breaker to open. For excessive temperature rise, if it is found to be caused by loose connecting screws of two conductive parts, the screws need to be tightened; if the fastening mechanism of the main switch is loose, it should also be tightened. In addition, if the "COM" screw is loose, this likewise corresponds to the operation of tightening. During diagnosis, voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked; the voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter;

Maintenance of circuit breakers occupies a considerable proportion of the maintenance of marine electrical equipment; their fault manifestations are diverse, and the handling methods also vary with the fault type. As far as the circuit breaker itself is concerned, the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator in the event of a fault to protect the power grid; the molded-case circuit breaker is used as a branch, load panel or lighting panel switch and has overload or short circuit protection functions. Common faults of circuit breakers include tripping immediately when starting, automatic tripping after closing, and excessive temperature rise; circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers, and during maintenance a comprehensive inspection is required every six months, focusing on checking the integrity of the arc chute and the burn condition of the contact surface.

The circuit breaker tripping immediately when starting the motor is a relatively typical fault symptom. The main cause of this phenomenon is that the instantaneous operating setting current of the overcurrent trip unit is too small; the instantaneous operating setting current of the overcurrent trip unit being too small directly causes the circuit breaker to trip immediately when starting the motor.

For this cause, the handling method is to adjust the instantaneous setting spring of the overcurrent trip unit, that is, to restore its instantaneous operating value by adjusting the overcurrent trip unit. This adjustment belongs to the scope of overcurrent trip unit maintenance and adjustment and is used to solve the automatic tripping fault caused by failure of the overcurrent trip unit or too low an operating current value. When the main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration, the measure of adjusting the overcurrent trip unit is also correspondingly taken. In addition, if the overcurrent trip unit has already approached the operating value at normal load current, this adjustment likewise needs to be performed.

The circuit breaker tripping automatically about 1 h after closing is another phenomenon whose cause needs to be distinguished. An incorrect long-time delay setting value of the overcurrent trip unit will cause the circuit breaker to trip automatically about 1 h after closing, and deterioration of the thermal element or semiconductor delay circuit elements will likewise cause the circuit breaker to trip automatically about 1 h after closing. These two causes often appear side by side, but the handling methods are different: for the incorrect long-time delay setting value of the overcurrent trip unit, the corresponding handling method is readjustment, that is, readjusting the long-time delay setting value of the overcurrent trip unit; for deterioration of the thermal element or semiconductor delay circuit elements, the thermal element or semiconductor delay circuit elements need to be replaced. This fault symptom is distinguished from the tripping caused by an incorrect long-time delay setting value of the overcurrent trip unit; during troubleshooting, the specific cause should first be identified before taking action.

Noise in the undervoltage trip unit is a fault manifestation in which the circuit breaker emits an abnormal sound in the closed state. Excessive force of the reaction spring is one cause of noise in the undervoltage trip unit, oil contamination on the working surface of the core will cause the undervoltage trip unit to produce noise, and a broken shading coil is a common cause of noise in the undervoltage trip unit. These three causes exist side by side, and the handling methods are different: for noise caused by excessive force of the reaction spring, the spring should be readjusted; oil contamination on the working surface of the core corresponds to removing the oil contamination, and removing the oil contamination from the working surface of the core can eliminate the noise caused by oil contamination; a broken shading coil corresponds to replacing the armature or core, and replacing the armature or core can handle the noise caused by a broken shading coil. The shading coil is installed on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core and is used to eliminate armature vibration noise; a broken or detached shading coil will cause the AC electromagnet to produce relatively loud noise, and when damaged it can be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil can be directly replaced. The reaction spring is a spring component that provides release force or reset force; excessive force will cause the trip unit to produce noise, and readjustment is the means of eliminating this noise.

Excessively high temperature rise of the circuit breaker is a common fault in which the equipment temperature rises abnormally. Too low contact pressure is one of the causes leading to excessively high temperature rise of the circuit breaker; excessive wear of the contact surface or poor contact of contacts will cause excessively high temperature rise of the circuit breaker; and loosening of the connecting screws of two conductive parts will likewise cause excessively high temperature rise of the circuit breaker. For the temperature rise caused by too low contact pressure, the contact pressure must be adjusted or the spring replaced; for the temperature rise caused by poor contact of contacts, the contacts must be replaced or the contact surfaces cleaned; for the temperature rise caused by loosened connections of conductive parts, the screws must be tightened. Too low contact pressure is usually caused by failure of the contact pressure spring or improper adjustment, while poor contact refers to a state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loosening of fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact and increase the contact resistance; poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, short circuit between phases and other faults, and can also cause random output actions, correspondingly requiring inspection of the terminal wiring. Screw loosening in marine electrical and mechanical equipment is caused by vibration, improper installation or aging, which reduces the fastening force of connecting parts and further leads to poor contact, open circuit, overheating or mechanical faults; the vibration and swaying environment unique to ships can very easily cause loosening of wiring clamping screws, of the connections between cable connectors and the base, and of the fixing screws inside the PLC, creating hidden fault risks. In the PLC input/output circuits, loosening of the "COM" screw will cause the numbers of the relays acting abnormally to show a regular pattern in units of 8 points, and retightening is required, that is, loosening of the "COM" screw corresponds to tightening treatment.

If the fastening mechanism of the main switch is loose, tightening treatment should also be carried out.

A fault of the auxiliary switch manifests as damage or jamming of the internal mechanical parts of the auxiliary switch. One fault cause is that the moving contact bridge of the auxiliary switch is stuck or has fallen off, and another fault cause is that the transmission rod of the auxiliary switch is broken or the roller has fallen off. Treatment methods include straightening or reinstalling the moving contact bridge, and replacing the transmission rod and roller or replacing the entire auxiliary switch. The moving contact bridge of the auxiliary switch being stuck or fallen off is one of the direct causes of the auxiliary switch of the circuit breaker failing, and the corresponding treatment method is to straighten or reinstall the moving contact bridge; breakage of the transmission rod of the auxiliary switch or falling off of the roller is one of the common causes, and the corresponding treatment method is to replace the transmission rod and roller, or, if they cannot be repaired separately, to replace the entire auxiliary switch.

Misoperation of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit, which trips the circuit breaker, falls within the scope of common fault maintenance of circuit breakers, and its consequence is tripping of the circuit breaker. The prerequisite for treatment is to identify the fault and confirm that the semiconductor trip unit itself is not damaged. A local short circuit inside the undervoltage coil reduces the attractive force, so that a period of time is required before the trip unit operates.

The circuit breaker may also exhibit the situation in which, when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contacts cannot close; if this is caused by excessive force of the reaction spring, readjustment is required. When the circuit breaker exhibits the situation in which, under electric operation of the circuit breaker, the contacts cannot close, if the positioning switch of the motor operation has failed, readjustment is correspondingly required. When the circuit breaker exhibits the situation in which one phase of contacts cannot close, if the reclosing contact surface is too large, readjustment is correspondingly required. When the circuit breaker exhibits the situation in which the shunt trip unit cannot cause the circuit breaker to open, loosening of internal screws is a possible fault cause; loosening of screws causes the shunt trip unit to be unable to open the circuit breaker, and the corresponding treatment is to tighten the screws. When the circuit breaker exhibits the situation in which the undervoltage trip unit cannot cause the circuit breaker to open, the possible cause is that the reaction spring has become weaker, and the spring must be adjusted.

In the measurement and judgment stage, current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments and is used to understand equipment status; the current value can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter; the multimeter is used for current measurement, and the clamp-on ammeter is used for current measurement. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after the circuit is opened. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. In a through-type current transformer, the large-current conductor under measurement is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding.

Troubleshooting of circuit breakers cannot be separated from instrument measurement, and the multimeter is the most frequently used of these. The multimeter is composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; it is a multi-purpose instrument and is divided by display mode into two types, analog and digital; the analog multimeter is a multimeter, the digital multimeter is likewise a multimeter, and the MF-47 multimeter is one type of analog multimeter. When the meter head is at full scale, the current flowing through it is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes; the MF-47 can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and the panel is provided with four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". With the multimeter, various electrical quantities and device parameters such as resistance, voltage, current, capacitance, diode, transistor, thyristor, photosensitive device and thermocouple can be measured. When measuring direct current, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range and the meter head is connected in series in the opened branch; when measuring direct voltage, the test probes are connected in parallel across the component under measurement, and when the range is uncertain, the maximum range is selected first. Voltage, as one of the instrument readings to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis, can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter; the generator being unable to build up voltage can be selected as the top event when constructing a fault tree, and overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system.

The capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by insulating material in between; it has the function of charging and discharging, and its characteristic is blocking direct current and passing alternating current. In circuit diagrams it is usually represented by the letter C plus a number, such as C25. Its obstructive effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC). A multimeter can be used to measure its earth leakage, capacitance, and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. A transistor contains two PN junctions internally and has current amplification capability; it is divided into NPN type and PNP type. In circuits it is commonly represented by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17. Main models include PNP-type transistors such as A92 and 9015, and NPN-type transistors such as A42, 9014, and 9018. When marine electrical equipment uses transistors, transistor fault may occur; this type of fault is a problem of the transistor itself and can be judged by using a multimeter to measure its transistor type, base, collector, emitter, and current amplification factor.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control the motor in the ship's power system; it belongs to low-voltage control apparatus and is mainly used to control the motor in electric drive systems. It has the characteristics of high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size. The power of various auxiliary machinery on board is almost entirely driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on board. The contactor includes components such as the arc chute, main contact, core, and coil; contactor maintenance applies to the contactor. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked.

The circuit breaker is a switching device used to protect circuits in the ship's power system; it belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus and is divided into frame type (air circuit breaker) and molded-case type. It has both switching and protection functions and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during a short circuit fault. When the circuit breaker serves as generator protection, it opens after a delay of less than 2 min at 10%-50% overload.

There are many possible faults of the circuit breaker: when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contact cannot close; when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contact cannot close; one phase contact cannot close; the shunt trip unit cannot cause the circuit breaker to open; the undervoltage trip unit cannot cause the circuit breaker to open; the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1 h after closing; the undervoltage trip unit has noise. Load short circuit or overload is judged correspondingly by the method of measurement with a multimeter.

When a circuit breaker fault occurs, the fault cause should be carefully sought. If a large electromagnet is operating nearby, such as the opening of a contactor or electric welding, it should be isolated or the line should be replaced. This step is used to troubleshoot circuit breaker faults caused by the operation of nearby large electromagnets such as contactor opening and electric welding. When it is found that a large electromagnet is operating nearby, measures should be taken to isolate it or replace the line. In most cases, this type of fault cause may be external electromagnetic interference.

The circuit breaker performs the function of protecting circuits in the ship's power system. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. The work of circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker itself, and there are many possible fault symptoms of the circuit breaker; the following explains them separately according to operating mode and trip unit category.

One of the causes of this symptom is that the undervoltage trip unit has no voltage or its coil is burnt out; this cause directly results in the contacts failing to close when the circuit breaker is operated manually. For the cause of the undervoltage trip unit having no voltage or its coil being burnt out, the corresponding remedy is to check the circuit, apply voltage or replace the coil; if the coil is already damaged, replace the coil. Deformation of the energy-storing spring reduces the closing force and likewise results in the contacts failing to close when the circuit breaker is operated manually; the remedy is to replace the energy-storing spring. Among the above causes, the undervoltage trip unit having no voltage or its coil being burnt out, deformation of the energy-storing spring reducing the closing force, excessive reaction spring force, and the mechanism being unable to reset and relatch all fall under the fault symptom of the contacts failing to close when the circuit breaker is operated manually. An incorrect operating power supply voltage will cause the contacts to fail to close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically; the power supply should be replaced during handling. Insufficient power supply capacity will also cause the contacts to fail to close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically; the corresponding measure is to increase the operating power supply capacity. Insufficient stroke of the electromagnet pull rod will likewise cause the contacts to fail to close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically; the remedy is readjustment or replacement of the pull rod. Damage to the rectifier tube or capacitor in the controller will also cause the contacts to fail to close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically; for the cause of damage to the rectifier tube or capacitor in the controller, the corresponding remedy is to replace the rectifier tube or capacitor. Once the rectifier tube or capacitor inside the controller is damaged, the normal operation of the electrical operating circuit will be affected.

The angle between the foldable links of the current-limiting switch tripping mechanism becoming larger is an abnormal mechanical fit of the current-limiting switch tripping mechanism and will also cause one phase contact to fail to close; during handling, the angle between the links should be adjusted to the requirements specified in the original technical conditions. In the fault of excessive temperature rise of the circuit breaker, loosening of the connecting screws of two conductive parts is also one of the main causes and likewise needs to be handled by tightening the screws. A decrease in the reaction spring force is one of the causes of this fault; the remedy is to adjust the spring to restore the reaction force. Abnormal energy storage release will also cause this fault to occur; for the refusal to trip of the undervoltage trip unit caused by energy storage release, the remedy is to adjust the energy-storing spring. Mechanism jamming is the mechanical cause of this fault; during handling, the cause of the mechanism jamming needs to be eliminated. Excessive reaction spring force of the undervoltage trip unit of the circuit breaker will cause the trip unit to produce noise; this point should also be noted when checking the reaction spring. The main switch is mainly composed of the undervoltage release, the shunt release and the overcurrent protection device; the DW14 circuit breaker is provided with an additional AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker.

Other components belonging to marine electrical equipment together with the circuit breaker also need to be maintained. Capacitor types include electrolytic capacitors, ceramic capacitors, chip capacitors, monolithic capacitors, tantalum capacitors and polyester capacitors; capacitance units are the farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF) and picofarad (pF). When marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, the capacitor testing steps apply to capacitors; a capacitor fault may occur in a capacitor, and a capacitor fault falls under the category of the capacitor. The function of a capacitor is charging and discharging; the measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors, and a multimeter is used for measurement. Voltage is likewise one of the meter readings to be checked; its measurable property is the voltage value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter or voltmeter; the multimeter is used both for measuring voltage and for measuring capacitance.

The reaction spring is a spring component in contactors and circuit breakers, used to provide release force or reset force; failure or absence of the contactor armature reaction spring will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed. When handling a contactor release fault, the reaction spring needs to be replaced or adjusted, but care must be taken that the reaction force is not too large. The energy-storing spring, as a component of the circuit breaker, will reduce the closing force of the circuit breaker when deformed; if the contacts fail to close when the circuit breaker is operated manually due to deformation of the energy-storing spring, the energy-storing spring needs to be replaced; if the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open due to energy storage release, the energy-storing spring needs to be adjusted.

The multimeter is used to measure voltage and is a basic means of judging the state of a circuit; during measurement, the corresponding range should be selected according to whether the circuit being measured is AC or DC, and it should be confirmed that the range is higher than the voltage value being measured, so as to avoid inaccurate readings or damage to the meter head.

There are many possible fault forms of a circuit breaker. When the temperature rise of the circuit breaker is too high, the contact resistance of the contacts, the tightness of the connecting screws and the integrity of the arc chute should be checked; when the auxiliary switch fails, the contact contact and the position of the transmission link should be checked; when the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctions and opens the circuit breaker, the setting value of the trip unit and whether the secondary circuit wiring of the transformer is correct should be checked.

Models and Uses of Common Fuses Fuses are represented by the symbol FU in circuit diagrams; they belong to distribution apparatus and are a type of protective apparatus. When overload or short circuit occurs in the power network or electrical equipment, it relies on melting the fuse element to automatically cut off the circuit, and thus has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. The protective conductive materials used to make fuse wires and fuse elements need to have conditions such as a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength. The fuses commonly used in ship power systems include the RL93, RS0, RSo, RS3, RLS, RM10, BX and other series, each suitable for different voltage and current ranges and protection objects.

The RL93 series is a marine fuse of spiral structure, with a rated voltage of 380V and a rated current range of 6 to 600A, used as an overload or short circuit protection element in circuits.

The RS0 series fuse has a rated voltage of 250 to 900V and current specifications of 30 to 480A; it is dedicated to the short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers and their complete sets, and can also provide appropriate overload protection for certain devices. The voltage specification range of RSo is 250V to 900V, and the current specification is marked as 30sim480V (as in the original text); its main use is to protect semiconductor rectifiers or complete sets composed of such elements, providing short circuit protection and providing appropriate overload protection for certain devices. The rated voltage of the RS3 series includes three levels of 250V, 500V and 750V, with current specifications of 10 to 300A, used for internal short circuit protection of thyristor rectifiers and their complete sets, as well as overload protection of devices that do not permit overcurrent. The RLS series fuse has a rated voltage of 500V and rated current specifications including 10A and 50A, used for internal short circuit protection of silicon rectifier elements, thyristor rectifier elements and complete sets composed of silicon or thyristor elements, and also used for overload protection of certain devices that do not permit overcurrent. The RM10 series fuse has a rated voltage of 500V and a rated current range of 15 to 600A, used as an element for overload or short circuit protection in circuits.

The BX series fuse has a rated voltage of 250V and a rated current range of 1 to 5A, applied to the protection of electrical installations and radio installations, having both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. A rectifier is a component that converts alternating current into direct current; the electrical graphical symbol of a full-wave bridge rectifier is UR. In a controllable phase-compounding constant-voltage device, a rectifier fault is one of the sub-causes of phase-compounding device faults; if the UR rectifier has an open-circuit diode, it will cause a voltage deviation where |U0-Ufe| is greater than ΔU1. The RS0 type fuse is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers and their complete sets, and the RS3 type fuse is used for internal short circuit protection of thyristor rectifiers and their complete sets, precisely addressing the protection requirements of such rectifier elements.

Selection of the Rated Current of the Fuse Element The fuse element is the main component of the fuse, and its rated current should be selected according to the specific conditions of the protected circuit. In lighting and electric heating circuits, the rated current of the fuse element should be greater than or equal to the rated current of the total load. For a circuit with a single asynchronous motor started directly, the rated current of the fuse element is taken as 1.5 to 2 times the rated current of the motor; for a motor circuit with light load and infrequent starting, 2.5 to 4 times the rated current of the motor is taken; for a motor circuit with heavy load and frequent starting, 3 to 6 times the rated current of the motor is taken. In a circuit where multiple asynchronous motors are started directly, the fuse is used only as short circuit protection and should not be used as overload protection. This is because the fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not serve as overload protection for the motor; motor overload protection is usually realized by a transistor relay converting power into voltage and satisfying the U=KP relationship, and the thermal relay FR operates when the motor is overloaded, disconnecting the control circuit so that the contactor KM loses power and stops. In addition, excessive refrigerant charging in the refrigeration system causing excessively high pressure and excessive load will also cause motor overload, and such overload should likewise not rely on the fuse for protection.

Judging the phenomena after a fuse is blown. A fuse blown is a common cause of equipment failure, and its phenomena differ noticeably depending on the nature of the interrupted current. When the fuse blowing occurs under overload current, the sound is not loud, the fuse element breaks at only one or two places, there are no scorch marks inside the tube, and there is no large amount of vapor deposit. When the limiting current, that is, a short circuit, is interrupted, the sound is loud, accompanied by flame, the fuse element breaks into multiple sections, and there are vapor or scorch marks on the tube wall. A fuse blown will cause the POWER lamp to go out, and will also cause the relay with unit number 8 to operate abnormally; in the PLC system, one possible cause of the POWER lamp going out is the fuse blown of the input circuit, and one possible cause of all PLC outputs failing to be connected is the fuse blown of the power supply. The typical manifestation when a short circuit fault occurs in the control circuit is also the fuse element burning open. Under the long-term action of power supply surge current, the fuse element may also burn open under non-short-circuit fault conditions.

Operating requirements for replacing the fuse. After a fuse is blown, the corresponding operation is to replace the fuse; a fuse blown of the power supply likewise corresponds to replacing the fuse. When replacing the fuse, generally the fuse should be removed for replacement with no voltage applied; if live replacement is permitted, the load must first be cut off to avoid danger. Before replacing with a new fuse element, the slag, soot and dust, etc. on the inner surface of the tube and on the contact surfaces must be carefully wiped clean, because after the fuse element interrupts the limiting current, the fuse element often melts and welds onto the contact surfaces. This operation is item 2 of the requirements in the fuse replacement instructions.

When replacing the fuse element, attention must be paid to the current value of the fuse element and the number of fuse element pieces; the fuse element must be the same as the original fuse element, and it is strictly forbidden to arbitrarily replace it with a fuse element of a different specification to substitute for the original fuse element; the fuse element of a fast-acting fuse must not be replaced with the fuse element of an ordinary fuse. When replacing the fuse element, care should be taken not to bend or twist the fuse element, because the fuse element material is relatively soft and easily broken, with a high risk of physical damage; bending or twisting will cause cracks in the fuse element, and mechanical damage will reduce the effective cross-sectional area of the fuse element, and the reduced cross-sectional area will in turn cause the rated current value of the fuse element to decrease.

For a closed-tube fuse, the fuse tube must not be replaced with another insulating tube; replacing the closed-tube fuse tube with another insulating tube easily leads to bursting and personal injury; drilling holes in the closed-tube fuse tube is prohibited, otherwise arc extinction will be difficult, and drilling holes in the tube may also spray high-temperature metal and gas, endangering the safety of personnel and equipment.

Use of instruments in fuse fault inspection. In fault diagnosis of fuses and related circuits, voltage and current are the instrument readings that need to be checked. The voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter, and the current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter; measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit. A multimeter can also be used to measure the polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode of a thyristor; a thyristor is also called SCR or controlled silicon. The MF-30 multimeter is an FU-related measuring instrument. In the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line via FU.

The programmable logic controller (PLC) is equipment that undertakes control tasks in ship automation systems; its full English name is Programmable Logical Controller, and in some materials it also appears written as PLD. This type of equipment came into being in the 1960s and, together with robot technology and CAD/CAM technology, is called one of the three pillars of industrial production automation. PLC has the advantages of simple programming, easy modification and debugging, convenient maintenance, high reliability, small size and moderate price, so it is often listed by engineers as the preferred scheme in automation scheme design. On ships, PLC is used to control equipment such as cargo winches, automatic oil separators, boilers and automated power stations, and its operating condition is directly related to whether these controlled objects can work normally.

Structurally, the programmable logic controller (PLC) belongs to the category of special-purpose industrial computers, and its basic structure is composed jointly of a central processing unit (CPU), memory (RAM/EPROM), input interface, output interface, programmer and power supply section. The central processing unit (CPU) is the core component of the central controller and plays the role of overall monitoring; it reads the input signals into the memory, fetches the user-written program according to the program counter address and compiles it, controls the various executing components to complete the operations specified by the user instructions, and finally sends the operation results to the output interface. The memory (RAM/EPROM), in parallel with the central processing unit (CPU) and the input and output interfaces, is one of the constituent parts of the basic structure of the PLC. Inside the PLC, a bus-type structure is used for the transmission of data and instructions; once a fault occurs on the bus, for example a CPU bus fault will cause abnormal action of the input relay, and an I/O bus fault in the CPU will cause abnormal action of the output relay.

The input interface accepts control information from field devices such as pushbuttons, limit switches, contactor contacts and sensors, and converts the received field control information into digital signals that the CPU can accept and process. In the microcomputer-type engine room monitoring and alarm system, the input interface is used to input the status of switching-value sensors into the computer; in the switching-value input interface, the input voltage is 24V when the switch is closed and 0V when it is open. If all PLC inputs are abnormal and wiring problems have been ruled out, it is usually determined to be an input interface circuit fault and replacement is required. The output interface, in turn, converts the digital signals output by the CPU into voltage or current to drive actuating devices such as solenoid valves and contactors; the switching-value output interface controls the display and alarm devices via an optical isolator and a driver. The power supply section provides a higher-voltage and large-current power supply for the output interface circuit. In the final stage of PLC operation, the output interface status is refreshed according to the output register results. Vibration and jolting on board the ship often cause poor contact of the output interface terminals or open-circuit faults in the loop; if the output indicator lamp is lit but there is no action, the fault may be in the drive circuit, the actuating device or the external wiring. The input interface and the output interface are collectively called the I/O interface, which is the channel through which the CPU exchanges information with the outside and is easily damaged by faults of external devices.

The power supply section has the function of converting AC or DC power into the DC working power required by the internal circuits, and its outputs are divided into three categories. The first category of power supply feeds the integrated circuits and is a +5V and +15V DC power supply; the third category of power supply is a lithium battery, which ensures that the memory does not lose information when power is cut off. Different categories of power supply have different wiring and capacities, which must be noted during expansion and maintenance. When the POWER lamp is off and faults of the fuse, diode and wiring have been ruled out, the entire power supply section needs to be replaced. The lithium battery belongs to the third category of DC working power supply of the PLC and is dedicated to memory backup; its main function is to ensure that the PLC memory does not lose information when power is cut off, and it needs to be replaced periodically according to the battery manufacturer's data to prevent loss of RAM/ROM information. Before replacement, the AC power must be connected for 10s to charge the backup capacitance; during replacement, the AC power must be disconnected, and the battery must be taken out of the battery clip and a new battery installed; when installing the new battery, attention must be paid to the polarity, and the shorter the operation time, the better.

Modern PLCs use EEPROM storage technology and do not require replacement of the backup lithium battery.

The programmer is the most important peripheral device of the PLC, and its main uses include inputting, editing, debugging, modifying and checking the user program and monitoring execution. In PLC fault diagnosis, the programmer can display "error" information to assist in distinguishing internal and peripheral faults; in the troubleshooting process, the programmer needs to be connected to check whether the program has an END instruction or whether the program is appropriate; the programmer can also be used to input the simplest ladder diagram simulation signal to test the controllability of the output channel circuit.

The input terminals of the PLC, in cooperation with the COM terminal, form the input loop interface, and the output terminals are located between COM and the load, corresponding to the external contacts of output coils such as Y31-Y32.

The harsh environment on board easily causes wiring heads and terminals to rust, resulting in poor contact, which needs timely cleaning. Loose input terminals or poor contact will cause the PLC POWER lamp to go out, and poor contact of input terminals is also one of the common causes of random input actions. If the terminal voltage is still abnormal after removing the load, first check whether the output terminals and output fuse are normal; poor contact of output terminals is one of the causes for a certain output relay failing to energize while its indicator lamp is lit, and the troubleshooting measure for this type of fault is reconnect.

The PLC control system consists of a CPU, input/output interface circuits and peripheral equipment; faults in peripheral connecting lines or components will cause system failure or misoperation, endangering personal safety. Its input signals originate from switches, contacts and sensors, and the goodness of contact and deviation of analog signals need to be checked regularly; the output control objects are mainly relays and solenoid valves, whose working status needs to be checked periodically to eliminate hidden dangers.

External surge voltage noise interference can cause CPU misoperation, manifested as the "CPU Error" lamp staying lit. Abnormal phenomena that may occur in the PLC control system include the POWER lamp going out, fuse blowing repeatedly, the RUN lamp going out, all inputs failing to energize, all PLC inputs abnormal, a certain input relay failing to energize, a certain input relay normally closed, random input actions, the relay number of abnormal action being in units of 8 points, input relays acting correctly but indicator lamps going out, all outputs failing to energize, all outputs failing to turn off, a certain output relay failing to energize while its indicator lamp goes out, a certain output relay failing to energize while its indicator lamp is lit, a certain output relay failing to turn off while its indicator lamp goes out, a certain output relay failing to turn off while its indicator lamp is lit, etc.

PLC maintenance applies to the programmable logic controller (PLC) itself, and its periodic maintenance work includes several specific steps. One step is to check whether the connecting lines are damaged or aged, and whether solder joints are desoldered, cold-soldered or oxidized; if the above abnormal phenomena are found, the relevant components should be replaced in time; for rusting of wiring heads and terminals caused by the harsh environment on board, timely cleaning is required to prevent poor contact. Another step is to check for loosening of wiring clamping screws caused by ship vibration and swaying. A further step is to open the outer cover, blow away dust with a hair dryer, and spray-wash with electrical cleaner to wash away oil stains and salt crystals; this step is used to remove dust, oil mist and salt mist on the printed circuit board inside the PLC, and before the operation the PLC outer cover must be opened and the external power supply cut off, using a hair dryer to remove dust and electrical cleaner to spray-wash oil stains and salt crystals, aiming to prevent deterioration of the insulation performance of the circuit board or short circuit between components due to contamination.

Periodically replacing the lithium battery inside the unit is also one of the maintenance steps, and its purpose is to ensure that the RAM and ROM inside the PLC do not lose information during a short-term power failure; replacement must be carried out periodically according to the data provided by the battery manufacturer; in addition, it is necessary to check whether the switches and contacts of input peripheral equipment are in good contact and whether the analog signals sent by sensors deviate too much; this step belongs to the connecting line inspection content in the periodic maintenance of the PLC control system, and faults in the connecting lines of peripheral equipment will cause the PLC control system to fail to work normally or even fail, and connecting line faults may cause PLC misoperation, resulting in equipment damage or endangering personal safety. At the same time, check whether the relays, solenoid valves, etc. of output peripheral equipment are in good working condition.

Harsh conditions on board cause wiring heads and terminals to rust, which easily causes poor contact in PLC input/output circuits. Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance, and further causing faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit. The vibration and swaying environment unique to ships very easily causes loosening of wiring clamping screws, of cable connectors relative to the base, and of fixing screws inside the PLC, creating hidden fault risks; in the PLC input/output circuits, loosening of the "COM" terminal screw will cause the numbers of relays acting abnormally to show an 8-point unit pattern, and they need to be tightened again. Loose screws are a common cause in ship electrical and mechanical equipment of reduced fastening force of connecting parts due to vibration, improper installation or aging, which further causes poor contact, open circuit, overheating or mechanical faults; in the fault of excessively high temperature rise of a circuit breaker, loosening of the screws connecting two conductive parts is one of the main causes and is handled by tightening the screws; when an open-circuit fault occurs in a line, loosening of screws or falling off of nuts at wire joints is also one of the common causes.

Among the peripheral actuating devices of the PLC, the solenoid valve is used to control the on/off of fuel, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit at ignition so that fuel enters the nozzle and is injected; the PLC output interface converts digital signals into voltage or current to drive the solenoid valve to act. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control fine water mist fire-extinguishing zones; it is energized in the burner ignition program, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit so that fuel enters the nozzle and is injected; its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve. A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors; in the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where equipment status is monitored and parameter values are also displayed. The control platform contains sensors.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system; it belongs to low-voltage control appliances and is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, featuring high operating frequency and long life, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor contains an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and its inspection and repair methods can likewise be used for reference for appliances of similar construction such as intermediate relays. The intermediate relay is a type of electromagnetic relay, similar in construction to the contactor, used to expand contact capacity and the number of contacts and for control logic conversion; its function is to expand contact capacity and the number of contacts, its construction is the same as the contactor, and fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the inspection and repair methods of the contactor. The coil is an electrical component made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start;

The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

In testing and repair, voltage is one of the measurable performance parameters, and the measuring tool is a multimeter or voltmeter; current is likewise a measurable performance parameter, and the measuring tool is a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter; the multimeter is used to measure voltage, current and capacitance, and the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. The function of capacitance is charging and discharging, and the measurable performance includes earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors; a capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle, its characteristic is blocking direct current and passing alternating current, and in circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; its hindering effect on alternating current signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC).

Marine electrical equipment uses integrated circuits and printed circuit boards. Integrated circuits have the advantages of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration increased, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits appeared; their common package forms are 14-pin or 16-pin, and the types include CMOS circuits and TTL circuits; the pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise; to facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often welded on the circuit board for direct plug-in; common package forms include the four-side J-lead type (PLCC), the two-side gull-wing lead type (SOIC), the dual in-line lead type (DIP) and power integrated circuit packages.

The printed circuit board consists of a base material and traces; the base material is an insulating material, such as phenolic resin board and epoxy glass, and the traces are conductive foil, usually copper; dust, oil mist and salt mist on board ships easily cause the insulation performance of the printed circuit board to deteriorate or even cause a short circuit; when cleaning, an electrical cleaner may be used to spray-wash oil stains and salt crystals, and the operation must be carried out with the external power supply cut off. The printed circuit board consists of an insulating base plate and conductive copper traces, and is the carrier for mounting and interconnecting electronic components, with patterns formed by an etching process; the base material is often called the base plate, and the most commonly used are phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the trace part is made of conductive copper, laid on the base plate, and the required pattern is obtained by etching. For the printed circuit board, attention must be paid to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to the printed circuit board; circuit board faults will occur on the printed circuit board, and circuit board faults fall within the scope of the printed circuit board.

The power supply section of the PLC undertakes the task of converting AC or DC power into the DC working power required by the internal circuits; according to the different objects supplied, it can be divided into three types of DC working power.

Power supply faults are a common type of fault in PLC control systems. Switching inverter power supplies are prone to faults and difficult to repair, so on board ships the strategy of overall replacement is usually adopted. The inspection process for power supply faults starts with the state of the POWER lamp; if the POWER lamp is off, then check the power supply, fuse and light-emitting diode in sequence. The fault symptom of the POWER lamp being off may be caused by a fuse blown, poor contact of the input terminal, or a broken input power line. During troubleshooting, first confirm whether there is power input; if the power supply is normal, check whether the fuse is blown; if the fuse is intact, check whether the light-emitting diode is broken down, and if so, replace the light-emitting diode; if the above components are normal, measure the output voltage at the terminal; if there is no voltage output at the terminal, check the terminal wiring.

Power supply faults correspond to the maintenance procedure of checking the power supply; in the overall inspection of the PLC, if the POWER lamp is off, the step of checking the power supply fault must be performed.

The RUN lamp being off is another type of fault symptom of the PLC. When the RUN lamp is off, first check whether the PC switch is set to the run position; if the switch is normal, confirm whether the RAM/ROM is inserted correctly; connect a programmer to check whether there is an END instruction in the program; if the program is appropriate, check whether the input and output terminals are in good contact; after eliminating external factors, it may be an internal circuit fault, and the circuit board must be replaced; if accompanied by the CPU Error lamp flashing, check whether the battery voltage has dropped. The absence of an END indication in the program, a power supply fault, and duplicate I/O port addresses will all cause the RUN lamp to be off. Poor input contact corresponds to the maintenance procedure of checking the terminal wiring; no load power supply corresponds to the maintenance procedure of switching on the power supply.

The PLC starts the self-diagnosis process as soon as the power supply is switched on; if an internal CPU error occurs, the panel "CPU Error" lamp indicates an abnormality. After eliminating external surge voltage interference, the power supply must be switched on again to observe whether the PLC fault disappears; otherwise, replace the CPU board. Before switching on the power supply, the input and output sections must be checked for short circuit or earthing faults, and only after confirmation of no error may power be applied.

The PLC control system consists of the CPU, input and output interface circuits and peripheral equipment, and is susceptible to surge interference causing malfunction. The input interface receives field information such as push buttons and sensors and converts it into digital signals that the CPU can process; the PLC input interface receives sensor information from field devices and converts it into digital signals that the CPU can accept and process. The automatic fuel oil boiler contains solenoid valves. The control platform contains sensors.

The PLC input and output interfaces exchange information with the controlled object through terminal blocks and connecting wires, and are susceptible to vibration causing poor contact. Severe vibration and pitching on board often cause poor contact of terminal blocks, thereby causing faults such as broken circuits. Terminal blocks are metal contact components used in electrical systems to connect wires to equipment or circuit nodes, commonly found in PLC interfaces, instruments and control circuits; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of terminal blocks is one of the common faults of electrical components. The electric main engine remote control system contains fuses and terminal blocks.
