The motor fails to start corresponds to the step of check the power supply voltage; according to the principle of from simple to complex, first check whether there is a power supply; it also corresponds to checking the motor internal fault, and this step is applicable to the fault analysis of the three-phase cage-type asynchronous motor, is analyzed by adopting the fault tree (FTA) method, follows the check principle of from simple to complex and from the surface to the interior, needs to be carried out after confirming that the power supply is normal, the shaft is not seized and the load is moderate, and is used to deal with the fault of motor fails to start or motor speed low after starting. When checking the power supply voltage, attention should be paid to marking the circuit terminals before disassembly; when checking the motor internal fault, attention should be paid to marking the joint surfaces before disassembly. In addition, the power supply not being connected will cause failure to start, incorrect wiring of the control equipment will cause failure to start, undervoltage will cause failure to start, stator winding short circuit between phases and earthing, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start, and excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer, will also cause failure to start. For failure to start, the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts should be checked to find the fault point; the wiring diagram should be checked and corrected; the power supply voltage should be checked, and if it is indeed too low, it should be raised appropriately; the short circuit and open circuit locations should be found and repaired, and if the wiring is incorrect, the wiring should be corrected;

The load should be reduced, and the motor and the reducer should be separated; if the motor can run normally, the reducer part should be checked.

The fault of motor speed low after starting is applicable to analyzing the cage-type three-phase asynchronous motor commonly used on ships, and there are eight aspects of possible causes of this fault. In the check steps, it is first necessary to confirm whether the voltage is too low and whether the power supply has phase failure, and to check whether the line incorrectly connects the delta connection as a star connection; after excluding external factors, it is necessary to further check whether the load is excessive; if all the above conditions are normal, it is necessary to further check the motor internal fault. Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting, phase failure of the power supply will cause motor speed low after starting, and incorrect line connection will cause motor speed low after starting, among which the line connecting the delta connection as a star connection is one of the possible causes of the asynchronous motor having low speed after starting. Motor speed low after starting corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, also corresponds to checking phase failure of the power supply, and also corresponds to checking the load. Checking phase failure of the power supply is one of the check steps for the fault of the marine three-phase asynchronous motor having low speed after starting, is carried out after checking whether the voltage is too low and before checking the load, and is executed in parallel with checking whether the line connects the delta connection as a star connection; if the phase failure of the power supply and the wiring are normal, it is necessary to further check the motor itself.

When checking the load, if the motor fails to start, it is necessary to check whether the load is too large to eliminate mechanical causes; if the motor speed is low after starting, it is necessary to check whether the load is too large as a preliminary troubleshooting step. This check follows the principle of from simple to complex and from the surface to the interior, and is located after the power supply and shaft seizure checks; if the load check is normal and the electrical parameters are correct, then further check for motor internal fault.

For the fault symptom of motor temperature rise being high, fault tree analysis shows that there are 12 causes of this fault in total, and the fault causes are divided into four categories: power supply fault, internal fault, mechanical fault and impaired heat dissipation. Specific power supply causes include voltage not matching the rated value (U≠UN) and phase failure; motor internal fault causes include winding short circuit, open circuit, earthing and rotor open circuit; mechanical fault causes include bearing damage, stator-rotor rubbing and overload; heat dissipation fault causes include damaged fan blade, impaired ventilation and high ambient temperature. Power supply phase failure will cause motor temperature rise to be high, line voltage mismatch will cause motor temperature rise to be high, long-term overload will cause motor temperature rise to be high, and deterioration of heat dissipation conditions will cause motor temperature rise to be high. Motor temperature rise being high corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, and also corresponds to checking the long-term overload condition.

In the fault tree for motor speed being lower than synchronous speed (n<n₀), low winding voltage is one of the main branches; the direct causes of low winding voltage include low supply voltage and incorrect △→Y connection; low supply voltage is a branch cause of low winding voltage. Long-term overload operation of an asynchronous motor will cause insulation performance degradation, ageing or mechanical damage, and may also cause stator winding earthing fault. A marine motor contains windings; a winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; partial short circuit or phase failure of a winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of an AC motor; the winding insulation of a marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture proofing, mould proofing and salt-oil-mist proofing, and must also be oil resistant.

In fault diagnosis, voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked, and its voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter. Generator failure to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in an AC electric drive system. Low supply voltage will cause loud noise of an AC electromagnet; when an AC electromagnet is loud, the power supply voltage needs to be adjusted to 0.85~1.10 times the rated voltage; when the contactor contact is welded and the holding force is insufficient, check whether the power supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage. A current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA, has current source characteristics, has extremely high internal resistance, and its secondary side standard current is 5A or 1A. The primary side of TA carries the load current I, which is transformed into a secondary current connected to an AC ammeter or other series current element; its secondary side must never be open-circuited, the terminals of the external ammeter need to have a short-circuit connecting piece, and it can only be disconnected after wiring verification.

Marine motors operate in the harsh environment of the ocean with high humidity, salt mist, vibration and confined spaces, and their insulation, mechanical structure and electrical performance all have special requirements. Chinese standards stipulate that the ambient temperature for marine motors is 45℃, and require that they can still work normally under the condition of 95% relative air humidity; the winding insulation must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture proofing, mould proofing and salt-oil-mist proofing, and must also be oil resistant. This major category of marine motors includes marine asynchronous motors, marine DC motors and AC single-phase motors, etc.; their constituent parts involve bearings, windings, commutators, brushes and shafts, and daily maintenance work includes general cleaning, working environment inspection and bearing maintenance. When repairing marine asynchronous motors, fault tree analysis is often used to sort out the ins and outs of faults, and the basic tool used in fault tree analysis is the fault tree. Its structure consists of top event, intermediate event and basic event, and the most commonly used logical relationships are "AND" and "OR".

Among them, the specific causes of the power supply category include voltage not matching the rated value (U≠UN) and phase failure, that is, power supply phase failure will cause the motor temperature rise to be high, and line voltage not matching will likewise cause the motor temperature rise to be high; the causes of mechanical faults include bearing damage, stator-rotor rubbing and overload, and long-term overload will cause the motor temperature rise to be high; the causes of heat dissipation faults include damaged fan blades, obstructed ventilation and high ambient temperature, that is, deterioration of heat dissipation conditions will cause the motor temperature rise to be high. During the inspection process, voltage and current are both electrical quantities that need to be read with instruments; the multimeter can be used to measure voltage and can also be used to measure current, the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used to measure current, and in addition the voltmeter and ammeter are also commonly used measuring tools. Bearing damage is one of the specific causes under the mechanical fault branch; once bearing damage is confirmed, a bearing of the same model and same specification must be replaced; if the lubricating oil has also deteriorated, it is also necessary to clean and replace the lubricating oil.

Large noise during motor operation is another common fault symptom; this fault is caused by 16 specific causes and can likewise be analyzed by means of a fault tree. The noise generated during motor operation is divided into two categories: electromagnetic noise and mechanical noise; electromagnetic noise is caused by electromagnetic asymmetry in the motor, while mechanical noise is caused by the mechanical parts of the motor, and both will cause large noise during motor operation. The nature of the noise is determined by means of a no-load test: during the no-load test, cut off the power supply; if the noise disappears immediately, it can be determined to be electromagnetic noise caused by electromagnetic asymmetry; if the noise decreases significantly as the speed decreases and disappears only at low speed, it is determined to be mechanical noise caused by the mechanical parts; if after cutting off the power supply the noise only weakens but does not completely disappear, it indicates that electromagnetic noise and mechanical noise exist simultaneously. This determination process corresponds respectively to the two maintenance procedures of checking electromagnetic noise and checking mechanical noise; the two are used to determine the subsequent inspection direction in the fault of large noise during motor operation, that is, large noise during motor operation corresponds to checking electromagnetic noise and also corresponds to checking mechanical noise.

The no-load test itself is a test in which the motor, after major repair or when newly installed, is operated at no load under rated voltage to check electrical balance, rotation direction and mechanical state; before the test, a bridge is needed to measure the three-phase winding resistance, and the difference in resistance value among the phases should be less than ±5%; at the start, an inching test should first be carried out to check whether the rotation direction meets the requirements of the mechanical load.

Excessive vibration during motor operation is generally caused by electromagnetic asymmetry or by mechanical aspects; there are seven aspects of causes for this fault, and it can be analyzed from the two aspects of electromagnetic and mechanical by constructing a fault tree. Electromagnetic noise will cause excessive vibration during motor operation, and mechanical noise will likewise cause excessive vibration during motor operation; therefore this fault also corresponds to the two inspection tasks of checking electromagnetic noise and checking mechanical noise. Bearing overheating is another fault symptom that requires special attention; its fault causes are mainly summarized in three aspects: bearing fault, lubrication fault and installation fault, that is, bearing fault will cause bearing overheating, lubrication fault will cause bearing overheating, and installation fault will also cause bearing overheating. During diagnosis, if the noise disappears during no-load operation, it indicates poor coupling installation; if the noise still exists and is accompanied by vibration, it points to a fault of the shaft or the bearing itself.

If, after cutting off the power supply, the vibration is relieved only as the speed decreases, it indicates that the overheating is caused by a mechanical fault rather than electromagnetic asymmetry. For bearing overheating, the corresponding inspection tasks include checking bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition and checking the installation condition, among which checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition both must be carried out around the bearing. When checking bearing fault, this process needs to be started when the motor reaches rated speed and noise is heard on auscultation; first disengage the coupling so that the motor runs at no load to eliminate the factor of poor installation; if noise and vibration still exist during no-load operation, it is determined to be a fault of the shaft or the bearing itself, and after it is confirmed as bearing fault the motor must be dismantled for inspection. When checking the lubrication condition, if there is no noise when the motor reaches rated speed, it indicates that there is a lubrication fault. When checking the installation condition, at the instant when the motor is running at no load and the power supply is cut off, if the vibration disappears it is determined to be caused by electromagnetic asymmetry, and if the vibration is relieved or disappears only after the speed decreases it is determined to be caused by a mechanical fault; for bearing overheating, if the noise disappears after disengaging the coupling it is determined to be poor coupling installation, and if the noise still exists and there is vibration it is determined to be a fault of the shaft or the bearing itself. In addition, too much, too little or deteriorated lubricating oil can all cause bearing overheating; when adding oil, it must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space; improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover and poor assembly of the generator set are also common causes of bearing overheating.

In the maintenance involving thermal relays and circuit breakers, there are also two types of fault causes related to the re-trip operation that need to be explained together. When the thermal relay cannot reset, one of the causes lies in the re-trip and trip time interval being too short, that is, the interval between the two operations of re-trip and trip is too short, and the corresponding maintenance method is to perform manual reset re-trip at about 5mm. When the shunt trip unit of the circuit breaker cannot make the circuit breaker open, one of the causes is that the re-trip contact surface is too large, and the treatment method for this fault is readjustment of the re-trip contact surface.

In the maintenance of marine asynchronous motors, fault tree analysis is a commonly used diagnostic means, which uses the fault tree, a graphical tool, to sort out the ins and outs of the fault. Taking the generator being unable to build up voltage as an example, it can serve as an optional top event when building the fault tree, and incorrect wiring is precisely one of the causes that prevent the generator voltage from being built up normally.

The diagnostic process cannot do without various instruments. A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, and is divided into two types: analog and digital, among which the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter both belong to the category of multimeters, and the MF-47 multimeter likewise belongs to multimeters; it can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and its panel is provided with four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The current flowing through the meter head of a multimeter at full scale is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. With the aid of a multimeter, various electrical quantities and devices such as resistors, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples can be measured. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after the circuit is disconnected, and the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for measuring current. When measuring a resistor in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistor, and never measure with power on.

The measurement of insulation resistance relies on the insulation resistance tester, also called the megohmmeter, which is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, has three terminal posts L, E and G, and is mainly used to measure and detect the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, electrical lines and cables. The insulation resistance tester is divided according to the maximum voltage emitted by the hand-cranked generator into specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V and 2500V. When measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and their relative position accuracy needs to be checked. Selection principle of the insulation resistance tester: select according to the rated working voltage of the object under test -> also take into account not damaging the object under test.

Precautions for use of the insulation resistance tester: perform the open-circuit and short-circuit tests before measurement -> it is strictly forbidden to measure while the electrical equipment is energized -> discharge the equipment under test after measurement -> the surface of the equipment under test must be wiped clean -> place it horizontally on flat, hard ground -> keep the rotational speed within the specified range -> use a guard ring when necessary -> pay attention to safety and avoid electric shock -> select the instrument according to the rated voltage of the equipment -> use a single-strand wire for connection -> it is strictly forbidden to measure low-voltage electronic equipment. Error adjustment steps of the insulation resistance tester: check the electrical circuit and mechanical mechanism -> adjust the "∞" position -> adjust the "0" position -> fine-tune the pointer or the guide wire. Calibration methods of the insulation resistance tester: calibration with a standard resistor -> calibration with a self-made resistance box -> rough calibration.

Overheating and vibration faults of the motor are often closely related to mechanical components. Bearing damage is one of the mechanical fault causes leading to excessive temperature rise of the motor, and bearing fault is also one of the direct causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance. When an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud non-uniform noise and the characteristic of bearing end cover overheating. The surface of the motor winding conductors has an insulation layer; under normal conditions the turns are insulated from each other, and the function of the insulation layer is to electrically insulate the conductive core wires and prevent short circuit or earthing between core wires; in the marine cable structure it is located between the conductive copper core wire and the protective layer, and the marine cable includes the insulation layer. The contactor includes a core and a coil; the coil is an electrical component made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start.

Bearing fault, lubrication fault and installation fault all lead to bearing overheating; bearing damage also leads to bearing overheating, and insufficient lubricating oil or impurities likewise lead to bearing overheating. Improper assembly of the motor end cover, poor assembly of the generator set or a bent shaft may all lead to bearing overheating. For bearing overheating, the corresponding troubleshooting directions are checking bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition and checking the installation condition, among which checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition both require the bearing component. When the generator bearing is overheating, troubleshooting can be carried out by observation of the output current and power and keeping them below the rated values.

Excessive temperature rise of the motor is also related to long-term overload and incorrect wiring. Long-term overload is one of the specific causes under the mechanical fault branch in the fault tree of excessive motor temperature rise; in the motor temperature rise inspection step, it is necessary to check whether there is long-term overload on the mechanical side, that is, to check the long-term overload condition. Long-term overload also leads to generator overheating. In DC machines, long-term overload is one of the root causes of armature winding overheating; long-term overload operation of the cargo winch fan causes the thermal relay to operate, so that high and medium speeds cannot run.

Incorrect wiring leads to the generator voltage failing to build up normally; winding incorrect wiring causes the current direction to reverse, causing severe vibration, abnormal noise and serious three-phase current imbalance of the motor; if the power supply is not cut off in time, winding incorrect wiring may cause the motor winding to burn out.

Repair of broken bars in a squirrel-cage rotor can adopt the welding method: enlarge the crack, heat the rotor to about 450℃, then gas-weld and repair with a brazing filler metal composed of tin (63%), zinc (33%) and aluminum (4%). The mechanism of welding is to melt the filler metal by heating the weldment, producing atomic diffusion between the weldment and the filler metal, and after solidification forming an alloy bonding layer at their interface; this bonding layer has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength, and welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products. When checking inter-turn and inter-phase short circuit faults of the stator winding, a megohmmeter can be used to judge by measuring the inter-phase insulation resistance.

In the maintenance of marine asynchronous motors, broken bars in the squirrel-cage rotor are a relatively common fault form, in which a broken ring refers to one or several cracks in the end ring. For cast-aluminum rotors, end ring cracking can generally be found by visual inspection; maintenance personnel can make a preliminary judgment by means of this intuitive feature, and the position and direction of the crack can be observed at the rotor end without disassembly. For broken bar faults, the welding method can be used for repair: first enlarge the end ring crack so that the area to be repaired exposes a clean metal surface, then heat the rotor to about 450℃, and subsequently gas-weld and repair with a brazing filler metal composed of tin (63%), zinc (33%) and aluminum (4%). If the bar replacement method is used for repair, the original end ring must first be turned off on a lathe so as to remove the aluminum bars, and then the guide bars are reassembled according to the original slot positions. For copper bar rotors, when replacing bars the new end ring should be drilled according to the slot positions, fitted over the copper bars and firmly brazed with phosphor copper, so that a reliable conductive connection is formed between each guide bar and the end ring; for small motors, the copper bars protruding from the slots may also be bent and fused into a whole to serve as the end ring, thereby omitting the separate machining of the end ring.

The end ring, as an annular conductive component at the end of the cage rotor, together with the cage bars forms a short-circuit winding; whether it is intact directly affects the conductive performance of the rotor. Once the end ring cracks or separates from the guide bars, the resistance of the rotor circuit increases, and both the starting and running performance of the motor are affected. In the rotating magnetic field method, placing the shading coil at the center of the stator cavity can indicate the rotation of the magnetic field; although this use differs in occasion from the role of the end ring in the rotor, both reflect the function of annular conductive components in the detection and constitution of the motor magnetic field. The shading coil itself is a copper annular component installed on the pole face of the core of an AC electromagnet, used to eliminate armature vibration noise; once the shading coil breaks or falls off, the AC electromagnet will produce relatively large noise; when the shading coil is damaged, it can be repaired by copper welding, or the shading coil can be replaced directly; after repair, it should be confirmed that it fits well with the pole face of the core. Desoldering of the end ring of the shaded-pole winding of an electric fan will cause failure to start, while open welding of the guide bars and end ring of a traction motor will cause faults during load operation; these cases all show that the integrity of the end ring and its related connection parts is a necessary condition for the normal operation of motors and electrical appliances, and during maintenance the end ring welds and the connections of the guide bars should be listed as key inspection points.

Excessive temperature rise of the motor is a problem often encountered during operation; under the mechanical fault branch of its fault tree, bearing damage is included as a specific cause.

After bearing damage, a bearing of the same model and specification must be replaced; bearing damage will cause low speed during load operation, will also cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and will also cause bearing overheating; these three phenomena often appear simultaneously and can serve as circumstantial evidence for judging bearing failure. When diagnosing bearing overheating, if the no-load operation noise disappears, it indicates poor installation of the coupling; checking the bearing fault itself and checking the lubrication condition both need to focus on the bearing as the component, the former focusing on wear and pitting of the raceway, rolling elements and cage, and the latter focusing on whether the grease is dried out, deteriorated or mixed with impurities. The marine motor itself includes components such as the bearing, winding and shaft, among which the bearing is used to support rotor rotation, and its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration and abnormal noise. The fault of the bearing running on the inner circle is manifested as a blackened mating surface between the bearing inner ring and the shaft, and in severe cases the mating surface becomes roughened; this shows that the fit state between the shaft and the bearing is an important basis for judging the fault, and when the fit is too loose, repair of the shaft journal or replacement of the bearing should be considered. The shaft, as a mechanical transmission component, is used to transmit torque and rotational motion and is commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments; the movable parts of the two units of the electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a shaft and a panel, and is assembled by bolts.

Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system, and overvoltage is also one of the causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system; therefore, monitoring of current and voltage cannot be ignored in fault diagnosis, and during operation instrument readings should be used to judge whether the motor is in an abnormal operating condition. The MF-47 multimeter is a type of multimeter and can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A; the panel has four jacks "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A"; when measuring high voltage or large current, the test leads should be inserted into the corresponding jacks and the range should be checked; the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter are also common types of multimeters, the former relying on meter head pointer deflection for readings, and the latter displaying measurement results digitally.

Voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; when measuring voltage, the corresponding range should be selected according to whether the circuit under test is DC or AC. The contactor includes a core and a coil; a fault of the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; during maintenance, check whether the coil leads are loose and whether the coil is burned. The core is the magnetic conductive component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as a reference point for insulation measurement;

Once local short circuit or phase failure occurs in the winding of a marine asynchronous motor during operation, it often causes abnormal current rise, and current is one of the important electrical quantities for judging the operating state of the motor.

To measure current values, a multimeter, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter may be used; among these, the clamp-on ammeter is suitable for on-site use because it can measure without disconnecting the circuit; if an ammeter is used for measurement, the circuit must be disconnected and the ammeter connected in series. Corresponding to current, resistance is also a basic electrical quantity measured by electrical instruments, and its resistance value can be measured with a multimeter. These measurement principles also apply to the inspection of components such as motor windings and contactor coils. As for whether a coil has a coil open circuit, its resistance value must be measured with a multimeter after power is cut off; if the resistance value is in an open-circuit state, it can be judged. The reason resistance measurement emphasizes disconnecting one end and cutting off the power supply is that if the branch being measured is still connected in parallel with the circuit, what is measured will be the equivalent resistance after paralleling, which cannot reflect the true state of the coil itself; capacitance discharge is to avoid the meter's internal power supply superimposing on the charge stored in the capacitance, which would affect the reading or even damage the instrument.

The contactor is a key component in the motor control circuit, and its interior contains a core and a coil. In a through-type current transformer, the large-current conductor being measured is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. When the contactor fails to pick up and the coil has a coil open circuit, the resistance should be measured with the power off to determine the open circuit, and then the step of replace the coil should be carried out; when the contactor coil overheats due to an internal partial short circuit, the resistance comparison method can be used to determine it, and the coil also needs to be replaced. The so-called resistance comparison method is to compare the measured resistance value of the faulty coil with the resistance value of a good coil of the same model; if it is obviously too small, it indicates that a short circuit path exists between turns. This correspondence between coil short circuit and replace the coil shows that a partial short circuit cannot be restored by simple adjustment but must be replaced. The engine room has high humidity, heavy salt mist and much oil mist, and ordinary insulation treatment is difficult to withstand for a long time; therefore, after rewinding or replacement, the winding still needs to have its insulation performance restored according to the "three-proof" requirements.

After the motor winding coil is replaced, varnish impregnation treatment must be carried out to improve insulation and mechanical strength; after replacing the coil or rewinding, it must be pre-dried to remove moisture before varnish impregnation can be carried out. If residual moisture remains in the winding and varnish impregnation is carried out directly, the varnish liquid is difficult to penetrate into the insulation interior, and air gaps are easily left after drying, so that both insulation strength and mechanical strength fail to meet requirements; therefore, drying is an indispensable step before varnish impregnation. After varnish impregnation and drying, excess attached varnish needs to be scraped off and an appearance inspection carried out.

Appearance inspection is an inspection step before acceptance of marine electrical equipment, covering aspects such as installation workmanship, mechanical assembly and appearance quality; for a motor, before energizing after major repair, the component installation, rotor flexibility, shaft extension runout and brush contact surface should be checked. Checking component installation is to confirm that all parts have been reassembled in their original positions and that no fasteners are missing; checking rotor flexibility is to turn the rotor to confirm that it rotates freely without jamming or friction; checking shaft extension runout is to confirm that the radial runout of the shaft extension is within the allowable range; checking the brush contact surface is to confirm that the brush is in good contact with the commutator or slip ring and that the pressure is appropriate. These checks connect with the appearance inspection after varnish impregnation and constitute steps that cannot be skipped after replacing the coil.

In the repair of small motors, the choice of slot insulation material is related to the winding insulation class. For small motors with class E insulation, a composite of polyester film and blue shell paper can be used as slot insulation; specifically,

0.05mm thick polyester film can be composited with blue shell paper. The thickness range of blue shell paper is 0.1~0.4mm, the commonly used thickness is 0.15mm, and the insulation strength is 7kV/mm; when used as slot insulation, one layer of
0.15mm thick blue shell paper is commonly used. The thickness of polyester film is 0.006~0.10mm, the insulation strength is greater than 130kV/mm, the measured breakdown voltage value is 130~230 kV/mm, and the heat resistance class is class E, so it is a commonly used solid insulation material for ships. The combined use of blue shell paper and polyester film can take into account the requirements of both heat resistance class and insulation strength: blue shell paper is thicker and has good mechanical support, while polyester film has high insulation strength and a heat resistance class of class E; when the two are laminated, they can both withstand mechanical friction during coil insertion and meet the heat resistance requirements of class E insulation. When selecting, note that the commonly used thickness of blue shell paper is 0.15mm, while that of polyester film is 0.05mm; improper thickness matching will affect the slot fill factor and the quality of coil insertion.

Broken bars of a squirrel-cage rotor can be repaired by welding. The crack is enlarged so that the brazing filler metal can penetrate into the interior of the fracture, avoiding merely overlapping on the surface; the rotor is heated to about 450°C so that the brazing filler metal fully wets and forms an alloy bonding layer with the cage bar metal during repair welding. Broken input wiring likewise corresponds to the maintenance procedure of welding, that is, restoring the continuity of the conductor by welding. Although the objects differ in the two cases, both rely on the mechanism of heating and melting the solder, producing atomic diffusion and solidifying into an alloy bonding layer to achieve connection, and therefore the quality of welding directly affects the reliability of the conductive path after repair.

In summary, the links of measurement, selection of insulating materials, coil replacement and welding involved in motor maintenance are interrelated: measuring resistance and current with a multimeter and measuring current with a clamp-on ammeter are the basis for judging coil short circuit, open circuit and winding overcurrent; the core and coil in the contactor and the winding in the marine motor have their insulation state directly related to varnish dipping, drying and appearance inspection after replacement; the combined use of blue shell paper and polyester film provides a slot insulation scheme for small E-class insulated motors; and broken bars of the squirrel-cage rotor and broken input wiring are repaired by welding respectively.

In the maintenance of marine asynchronous motors, resistance measurement is a basic and frequent operation. The measurand of resistance is the resistance value, and the determination of the resistance value is accomplished by means of a multimeter, that is, the multimeter is used to measure resistance; by measuring the object under test with the resistance range of the multimeter, the magnitude of the resistance value can be read directly. This correspondence constitutes the basic means of judging whether windings, leads and various connection circuits are normal. During measurement, the appropriate resistance range of the multimeter should be selected so that the pointer or digital display falls in an interval convenient for reading, so as to judge the measured resistance value. For the stator winding, rotor winding, lead joints of the motor and various resistance elements in the control circuit, this method can be used to measure point by point, and the measured resistance value and the normal value or the comparison results among the three phases are used as the basis for judgment, thereby determining whether there are abnormalities such as open circuit, short circuit, poor contact or resistance value deviation. Therefore, the sequence of operations should be: first cut off the power supply, then discharge the capacitance in the circuit, then disconnect at least one end of the resistor under test from the circuit, and finally measure with the multimeter; after the measurement is completed, restore the wiring in the reverse order. For circuits such as motor windings in which inductance and capacitance coexist, this sequence must especially be observed, and the two links of discharging and disconnecting must not be omitted out of eagerness to obtain a reading.

In the maintenance practice of marine asynchronous motors, resistance measurement is also often extended to the related control and excitation circuits. This phenomenon shows that although the resistor element is simple in structure, its continuity state directly affects whether the entire regulating link can work normally. Once the shunt resistor is open, the voltage regulator loses its main regulating channel, and the no-load voltage of the generator cannot be pulled back to the normal range; at this time, measure the resistance value of the shunt resistor with a multimeter, and if it displays infinity or obviously deviates from the normal value, it can be determined to be open. Therefore, when troubleshooting such faults, it is likewise necessary to measure the resistance values of the relevant resistors with the aid of a multimeter, and to follow the principle of first cutting off the power, then disconnecting at least one end of the resistor under test, and discharging the capacitance first if any, confirming point by point whether the resistor is open, short-circuited or has a resistance value deviation, thereby providing a reliable basis for the maintenance of the motor and its associated electrical equipment.

Marine DC motors have basically been eliminated in ship power systems, but they still account for a certain proportion in deck G-M systems and have been retained in some ship applications because of their good speed regulation performance and improvements in manufacturing technology. Within the major category of marine motors, the maintenance of marine DC motors has its particularities, among which excessive sparking under brush is the most common fault, and most faults can be reflected by it. Around this fault symptom, it is necessary to sort out its causes, the components involved and the corresponding maintenance and inspection procedures.

One of the direct sources of excessive sparking under brush is motor overload. When a DC motor is overloaded, the current flowing per unit area of the brush increases, commutation becomes difficult, and sparks are thus produced under the brush. Motor overload is a fault state in which the motor operating current or power exceeds the rated value; in a DC motor it causes difficult commutation and excessive sparking, while in a generator it triggers overload protection; a generator whose output power or current exceeds its rated value is defined as overloaded, and for a generator without an automatic step unloading device, when the overload reaches 125%–135% of the rated current, it trips after a delay of 15–30 s.

Poor contact between brush and commutator likewise causes excessive sparking under brush, which is one of the common faults of DC motors. Its causes include the commutator surface being too dirty, the brush spring being too weak, or brush sticking. The effective contact area between brush and commutator must be greater than 70%; when the contact area is less than 70%, it must be repaired by grinding the brush, and the maintenance methods include adjusting brush pressure, grinding or replacing the brush. In a DC generator, this poor contact causes low output voltage or failure to build up voltage; in a motor, it may cause starting failure due to excessively large contact resistance. Protruding mica between commutator segments also causes poor contact and triggers sparking. Poor contact as a fault state means that at an electrical connection, contact resistance increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs cause poor contact, increasing contact resistance, which in turn causes local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults, and may cause random output action, correspondingly requiring inspection of terminal wiring.

A loose brush holder is another common cause of excessive sparking under brush. The brush holder is the device that fixes the brush; a loose brush holder causes the brushes to be out of line during motor operation, and the greater the brush position deviation, the greater the sparking caused, which causes excessive brush sparking by affecting the commutation process. If the brush holder clearance fit is too tight, it causes brush sticking, and the tightness must be adjusted by grinding off the side of the brush. For marine motors under long-term 15° list, 7.5° trim and 22.5° roll, the brush holder connecting parts must be ensured not to loosen; when grinding the contact surface between brush and commutator, the brush must be placed in the brush holder for the operation, and when checking the contact surface of a running motor, the brush can be taken out of the brush holder for observation.

Armature vibration also causes excessive sparking under brush. Armature vibration is produced by uneven magnetic field caused by uneven clearance between the armature and each magnetic pole, resulting in different voltages in the branches of the armature winding and producing equalizing currents that make the brush sparking excessive. Causes of uneven clearance include improper installation of magnetic poles (such as lost or loose shims), bearing wear or damage, and failure to align the motor and load axes; in addition, poor armature balance, wrong fan blade installation or shifted balance weights may also cause armature vibration.

Short circuit between commutator segments is one of the causes of excessive sparking under brush. Brush powder or commutator copper powder filling the grooves causes short circuit between commutator segments; falling off or mildew corrosion of the insulating mica between commutator segments causes short circuit between segments; and burrs formed by undercutting the commutator that are not smoothed in time also cause short circuit between segments. The commutator should be maintained frequently, keeping the commutator segments clean and smooth to prevent this fault. The commutator is the rotating sliding contact component used for leading current in and out in DC motors and wound-rotor motors, and is composed of commutator segments; a too dirty commutator surface or brush sticking causes poor contact between brush and commutator, producing sparks; desoldering of the armature winding from the commutator can be judged by measuring the resistance between adjacent commutator segments. Graphite brushes are soft in texture and easily damage the commutator, and are suitable for motors with general commutation conditions and uniform load; when disassembling a DC motor, the winding ends, commutator or slip rings should be protected from being damaged.

Brush position not on the neutral line likewise causes excessive sparking under brush. This fault is caused by moving the brush holder or loosening of the brush holder bolts during repair, which makes the brush position deviate from the neutral line; the brush deviating from the neutral line makes the commutation process not occur on the zero-potential element, thereby producing excessive sparking. There are two adjustment methods: the induction method is to connect a millivoltmeter to adjacent brushes while stationary, and press the excitation button until the pointer stops, at which point this is the neutral line; the trial-run method is to run in separately excited mode, and when the speeds in both directions are equal, the brush position is on the neutral line.

Bearing wear or damage causes uneven clearance between the armature and each magnetic pole, causing excessive brush sparking, and it is also one of the main causes of large armature vibration in DC motors. Bearing wear manifests as excessive bearing clearance or surface damage, causing vibration, overheating and performance degradation of the motor or mechanical components; when rolling bearing wear causes excessive clearance, it manifests as loud rotational noise, wobbling of the outer ring, or impact noise between the balls and the outer ring. For rolling bearings with an inner diameter of 20–59 mm, the allowable wear value is about 10 times the original clearance; the clearance of a new bearing is 0.01–0.02 mm, and the maximum allowable wear value can reach 0.15–0.25 mm.

The bearing, as a mechanical component of the motor, is used to support the rotation of the rotor; its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration and abnormal noise, and is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud non-uniform noise and the feature of bearing end cover overheating. For bearing maintenance, on the one hand, the bearing fault must be checked; this step takes the bearing as the object and checks whether its surface damage and fit clearance exceed the standard; on the other hand, the lubrication condition must be checked, likewise taking the bearing as the object, to confirm whether its lubrication state is normal.

For excessive sparking under brush, a series of inspection steps needs to be performed. When the contact surface between brush and commutator is less than 70%, it is necessary to check the contact condition between brush and commutator; the inspection content includes whether the commutator surface cleanliness and the brush spring pressure are too small; if the brush is found to be stuck in the brush holder, the fit clearance should be adjusted by grinding the side surface; this inspection aims to solve the DC motor commutation difficulty caused by poor contact; during inspection, the commutator and brush are needed, and power supply voltage monitoring must be noted. Checking the brush holder condition is used to eliminate the commutation failure and excessive sparking fault caused by the brushes not being arranged in a straight line; during inspection, the brush is needed.

Checking the armature vibration condition requires investigating uneven clearance caused by improper magnetic pole installation (such as loss or loosening of shims), investigating armature vibration caused by bearing wear or damage, and investigating vibration caused by the axes of the motor and load not being aligned. Checking the commutator segment condition requires the use of the commutator. When checking the brush position, the greater the brush position deviation, the greater the spark generated by the DC motor; loosening of the brush holder causes the brushes not to be arranged in a straight line, affecting commutation and causing sparks; after commutation sparks appear during no-load operation of the DC motor, this inspection step should be performed; during inspection, it is necessary to confirm whether the brush jumps and its contact condition with the commutator, and armature current monitoring must be noted. In addition, excessive sparking under brush also corresponds to checking the power supply voltage; for faults such as slow starting of the electric fan, motor fails to start, or excessive temperature rise, it is necessary to verify whether the supply voltage is within the allowable range; when the electric fan shows slow starting and reduced speed, the power supply voltage should be checked to eliminate the undervoltage fault; when the traction motor fails to start due to undervoltage, the power supply voltage needs to be checked and appropriately raised.

During inspection, voltage, current and resistance are three basic measurable performances. The multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

A winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes leading to overcurrent and overheating of AC motors; the winding insulation of marine motors must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proof, mildew-proof and salt-oil-mist-proof and be oil-resistant. A coil is a component of marine electrical equipment, made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; the contactor contains a coil; a fault of the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

Regarding DC generators, the possible causes for a DC generator failing to build up voltage include absence of residual magnetism, reversed connection of the excitation winding after maintenance, open-circuit fault of the excitation winding and voltage regulator, and reverse rotation of the generator; these all belong to the fault symptom of a self-excited DC generator failing to build up voltage due to residual magnetism, wiring or rotation direction. Low voltage of a DC generator is related to reversed connection of the commutating pole coil; reversed connection of the commutating pole coil leads to loss of the commutation improvement effect, making commutation more difficult during operation and producing larger sparks under the brush; the polarity of the commutating pole can be judged with a small magnetic needle test; the polarity of the generator commutating pole is the same as that of the preceding main magnetic pole in the direction of rotation; the faults of generator voltage build-up and low voltage involve improper compensation of the commutating pole magnetic field; a commutating pole magnetic field that is too strong or too weak will both produce sparks, affecting the operation of the DC generator.

When a DC motor fails to start, if the supply voltage is too low, the starting torque will be less than the load torque, and the motor will therefore stall and fail to start. This phenomenon overlaps in cause with the fault symptom of failure to start: the power supply not being connected, incorrect wiring of the control equipment, undervoltage, short circuit and earthing between phases of the stator winding, incorrect wiring, stator winding short circuit, as well as excessive load or the brake not being released and a fault in the reducer, will all lead to failure to start. For failure to start, check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage and, if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find the short-circuit and open-circuit locations and repair them, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer; if the motor can run normally, check the reducer part.

The causes of failure to start of the motor matched with a self-excited DC generator include no power supply, low voltage, brush sticking and open excitation circuit; the main causes of failure to start of a DC motor include absence of power supply, low voltage, brush sticking and open excitation circuit. From the perspective of the fault tree, power supply problems, mechanical problems, excessive load and motor internal fault will all lead to the motor failing to start, and motor fails to start is often selected as the top event of fault tree analysis, whose analysis boundary conditions are usually set as the power supply being normal and the control circuit being normal.

One of the main causes of low speed of a DC motor is that the applied supply voltage is lower than the rated value; the applied supply voltage being lower than the rated value is one of the causes of low motor speed; the brush not being on the neutral line will cause the motor speed to decrease; short circuit or earthing of the armature winding is a fault cause of low motor speed. In contrast to low speed, for high motor speed, according to the electromotive force balance equation, when the rated voltage is applied its main cause is a decrease in effective magnetic flux. An increase in excitation circuit resistance is one of the causes of a decrease in effective magnetic flux and thus high speed; an electrically excited motor under light-load starting conditions may cause a decrease in effective magnetic flux and high speed; reversed connection of the series winding of a cumulative compound motor will cause a decrease in effective magnetic flux and high speed; an open circuit in one branch of the shunt excitation winding will cause a decrease in effective magnetic flux and thus high speed.

The brush position not being on the neutral line will cause excessive commutation sparking, which must be adjusted by the induction method or the trial-run method; the brush position not being on the neutral line will cause excessive sparking in the DC machine. Armature vibration is caused by uneven gap due to improper mounting of the magnetic poles (such as loss or loosening of shims), by uneven gap due to bearing wear or damage, by uneven gap due to the axis of the motor and the load not being aligned, and may also be caused by the armature balance not being properly calibrated, the fan blade being installed incorrectly or the balance weight moving.

For the fault symptom of large armature vibration, its causes include the armature balance not being properly calibrated, bearing wear or damage, the fan blade being installed in the wrong position or the balance weight moving during maintenance, mutual friction between stator and rotor, loosening of foot screws, and uneven armature gap. Bearing wear causes an uneven gap between the armature and the magnetic poles, causing equalizing current and brush sparking. The allowable wear value of bearings with an inner diameter of 20–59 mm is about 10 times the original gap, up to a maximum of 0.15–0.25 mm;

The root cause of overheating or burning of the armature winding is overcurrent. Long-term overload of the motor is one of the causes of overcurrent; short circuit of the armature winding or short circuit of the commutating pole winding can cause overcurrent; when the load is unchanged, an applied voltage lower than the rated value will cause overcurrent; short circuit of the external load of the generator causes excessive current and overheating; too frequent forward and reverse starting of the motor is one of the causes of overcurrent. Long-term overload in a DC machine is the cause of overcurrent and thus overheating of the armature winding, and is also one of the root causes of overheating of the armature winding; long-term overload will cause the temperature rise of the motor to be high and will cause the generator to overheat. Mutual friction between stator and rotor is one of the root causes of overheating of the armature winding because the resisting torque increases, and is also one of the causes of large armature vibration, usually triggered by bearing wear or uneven gap; mutual friction between stator and rotor will cause the generator to overheat.

Motor locked-rotor will cause the motor to overheat, or even burn out; when the motor is locked-rotor, the stator current greatly increases, such as the domestic constant-power JZF-H type three-speed asynchronous motor 28-pole, 8-pole, 4-pole locked-rotor currents are respectively 2Ic, 4Ie, 4Ie, the temperature rise is fast and high; the supply voltage is too low or the starting resistor is too large causing insufficient torque, causing the DC motor locked-rotor failure to start. Poor contact between brush and commutator will cause the DC generator voltage low or unable to build up voltage. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, the shunt resistor open circuit will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect. The brush is an important conductive element used for leading in or leading out current between the stationary part and the sliding part of the motor; DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators all need to be equipped with brushes; commonly used brushes are divided into three types: graphite, electrographite and metal graphite;

Loose motor foot screws will cause large armature vibration, which belongs to the mechanical fault cause caused by unbalanced factors. Loose screws are a common cause in ship electrical and mechanical equipment of reduced fastening force of connecting parts due to vibration, improper installation or aging, thereby causing poor contact, open circuit, overheating or mechanical faults; in the circuit breaker temperature rise too high fault, the loose connecting screws of two conductive parts is one of the main causes, which needs to be handled by tightening the screws; the ship-specific vibration and swaying environment can easily cause the wiring clamping screws, between the cable connector and the base, and the fixing screws inside the PLC to loosen, creating hidden fault dangers.

The measurable performance of a resistor is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable performance of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable performance of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is a capacitor in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with power on. To measure current, an ammeter must be used, and the circuit is disconnected and then connected in series.

Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failure to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in the AC electric drive system. Low supply voltage will cause large noise of the AC electromagnet, that is, the fault cause of low supply voltage will cause the phenomenon of large noise of the AC electromagnet; low supply voltage of the AC electromagnet will cause large noise, and it needs to be adjusted to 0.85~1.10 times the rated voltage; the electrical cause leading to large electromagnet noise, contact welding, low motor speed and washing machine faults usually refers to a deviation below 85% of the rated value or exceeding 20%; when insufficient holding force of the contactor causes contact welding, check whether the supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage. Too low supply voltage will cause the electromagnetic force generated by the circuit breaker shunt trip unit coil to be insufficient, so that the circuit breaker cannot break; in the PLC control system, too low supply voltage of the input signal source will cause all input terminals to fail to connect.

AC single-phase motors occupy a certain position in marine motors, and their common types include the power motors used in electric fans, electric drills, refrigerators and washing machines, etc. Such motors are especially common on small and old ships, because such ships often do not have a central air-conditioning system, and the use of electric fans is correspondingly greater; the room of each senior crew member on board is usually also equipped with a refrigerator, whose power motor is likewise mostly an AC single-phase motor. As far as the refrigerator is concerned, its faults are mainly divided into three categories: motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system, and the indirect-cooling refrigerator is also provided with a cold air circulation fan and an air door adjusting knob. The faults of the washing machine can be divided into three categories: motor fault, electrical control circuit fault and mechanical fault; failure to work after power-on may be caused by poor contact of contacts of the timer or slipping of the knob, slow impeller speed and unclean washing may be caused by reduced capacitance or deterioration of the capacitor, the impeller turning and stopping from time to time is mainly caused by the timer fault, and the impeller of the套-cylinder washing machine being unable to reverse may be caused by damage to the clutch torsion spring.

When the electric drill fails to start, possible causes include no voltage at the power supply, a damaged switch, or poor brush contact; if the brush holder insulation is cracked and moisture-pierced to earthing, the brush holder must be remade. Possible causes of motor speed too slow for the electric drill include undervoltage at the power supply, too little grease in the gearbox, or worn meshing gears; if the connection between the rotor winding and the commutator segment is loose, use a multimeter to check and weld it firmly. Possible causes of abnormal running sound of the electric drill include damaged meshing gears, insufficient grease, or bearing wear.

Slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan is a fairly typical fault symptom in the maintenance of AC single-phase motors, and its possible causes are numerous. Undervoltage at the power supply will cause the electric fan to start slowly and run at reduced speed; in this case, check the power supply voltage; incorrect wiring of the main and auxiliary windings can also cause this phenomenon, and the wiring must be corrected; desoldering of the shading coil set is likewise one of the possible causes, and the shading coil should be re-welded.

Insufficient capacitance will cause the electric fan to start slowly and run at reduced speed, and the corresponding remedy is to replace the capacitor with one of the same specification. A dropped ceiling-fan rotor will cause the electric fan to start slowly and run at reduced speed, and it must be reassembled to eliminate the problem. Dried-up or worn bearing grease, or overload caused by deformed fan blades with excessive twist angle, can also trigger this fault, and the bearing should be cleaned or replaced. A short circuit between turns of the winding, specifically a short circuit between turns of the main winding, is one of the causes of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan, and the corresponding repair method is to rewind the winding, that is, to restore its performance by repairing the main winding. Taken together, the repair methods for this fault include checking the voltage, correcting the wiring, re-welding the shading coil, and replacing the capacitor, and also reassembling to eliminate rotor drop and cleaning or replacing the bearing to restore performance.

The capacitor is an important component of AC single-phase motors, and the electric fan contains a capacitor. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material; its characteristic is that it blocks direct current and passes alternating current, and in circuits it is generally denoted by the letter C plus a number, e.g. C25 denotes capacitor number 25. The opposition of a capacitor to AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC). Its types include electrolytic capacitor, ceramic capacitor, chip capacitor, monolithic capacitor, tantalum capacitor, and polyester capacitor, and its units include farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF), and picofarad (pF). The measurable properties of a capacitor include earth leakage, capacitance, and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. When marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, the capacitor must be tested according to the capacitor testing procedure; a capacitor may develop a capacitor fault, and a capacitor fault falls within the scope of the capacitor component. Insufficient capacitor capacitance is one of the possible causes of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan; in the context of AC single-phase motor maintenance, this often refers to insufficient running capacitor capacitance, and the corresponding repair method is to replace the capacitor with one of the same specification. A multimeter can be used when measuring capacitance, and a multimeter can likewise be used when measuring voltage, or a voltmeter can also be used.

Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting; motor fails to start, motor speed low after starting, motor temperature rise high, and excessive sparking under brush all correspond to the troubleshooting step of checking the power supply voltage. When performing the check of the power supply voltage, note that circuit terminals should be marked before disassembly. A power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply. When the electric fan starts slowly, the repair methods include checking whether the power supply voltage is too low; when the electric drill fails to start and there is no voltage at the power supply, check the power supply line; when the washing machine does not work when energized, check whether the power supply lead is live and whether the plug and socket are intact. Undervoltage will cause the electric drill to run too slowly, and the power supply voltage must be checked and adjusted; when it is 15% below the rated voltage, it will cause the refrigerator motor not to start and to make no sound after energizing, and will also cause the refrigerator motor to make a sound but fail to start after energizing, the latter requiring the installation of an AC voltage regulator.

The shading coil is a component of marine electrical equipment, installed on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core; it is a copper ring-shaped part used to eliminate armature vibration and noise; breakage or detachment of the shading coil will cause the AC electromagnet to produce greater noise; when the shading coil is damaged, it can be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil can be replaced directly. In an electric fan, desoldering of the shading coil assembly is one of the possible causes of slow starting and reduced speed.

The bearing is a part included in the marine motor, used to support the rotation of the rotor; its fault will cause the motor to overheat, and vibration and noise to be abnormal. Bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud non-uniform noise and the feature of bearing end cover overheating. Rolling bearing wear causes excessive clearance, manifested as loud rotation noise, wobbling of the outer ring, or impact noise between the balls and the outer ring; when the inner diameter of the rolling bearing is 20–59 mm, the allowable wear value is about 10 times the original clearance; the clearance of a new bearing is 0.01–0.02 mm, and the maximum allowable wear value can reach
0.15–
0.25 mm.

Electric fan bearing wear will cause slow starting, reduced speed and rotor sinking, and the bearing needs to be cleaned or replaced; electric drill bearing wear may cause failure to start, abnormal operating noise or overheating. Checking the bearing fault itself and checking the lubrication condition both need to be carried out on the bearing. Replacing the bearing is used to repair slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan caused by bearing wear, to eliminate the noise generated during operation of the electric fan due to bearing damage, to solve the failure to start of the electric fan caused by bearing damage, and also to repair the failure to start of the electric drill caused by bearing wear; when dealing with electric drill bearing wear, an appropriate amount of good-performance grease must be added at the same time.

The electric fan includes a capacitor, fan blades, a timer and a speed control switch. Deformation of the fan blades or too large a twist angle will increase the load of the electric fan, causing it to run in an overloaded state, which is one of the possible causes of the fault of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan.

When correcting the fan blades, for a ceiling fan the blades can be removed and overlapped for comparison and correction; for a desk fan, repeated correction should be made according to the deformation condition; the correction objects include the highest and lowest points and the twist angle of the fan blades; when the deformation is severe, the fan blades need to be replaced rather than only corrected if necessary; this step is used to solve the slow starting fault caused by increased load due to fan blade deformation. Noise during operation of the electric fan may be due to foreign matter in the stator-rotor air gap or looseness of the silicon steel sheets of the speed-regulating reactor; sometimes rotating and sometimes not rotating may be caused by an open circuit of the shading winding of a shaded-pole motor or soft breakdown of the capacitor; abnormal operation of the oscillating mechanism may be due to the clutch teeth on the clutch being unable to slide down along the engagement shaft to engage with the lower clutch teeth; when there is failure to start, if it is a broken stator winding in the slot, the winding should be removed and replaced rather than only welding the lead wires.

AC single-phase motors often appear on ships in the form of electric fans, and are used in large numbers in small or old ships, as a supplement to or replacement for the central air-conditioning system. The electric fan belongs to the power load equipment of the AC single-phase motor, used for ship ventilation and cooling, and its common faults include slow starting, noise and heating, etc. Capacitors are commonly used in marine electrical equipment, and the multimeter is used to test capacitance; the capacitor testing steps are applicable to capacitors. In an electric fan, if starting is slow and the speed is reduced, it may be due to insufficient capacitance, and a capacitor of the same specification needs to be replaced.

The fault symptom of the electric fan sometimes rotating and sometimes not rotating may be caused by various reasons. The fault cause of poor line contact is specifically manifested as poor contact of the electric fan speed control switch causing the fan to sometimes rotate and sometimes not rotate; the presence of desoldered points in the connecting wires is a manifestation of poor line contact.

For the fault of poor switch contact, the treatment method is to repair or replace the switch; for poor contact caused by desoldering of the connecting wire, it is necessary to find the desoldered point and resolder it. Unstable power supply voltage is also a related cause of the electric fan sometimes rotating and sometimes not rotating; checking the stability of the power supply voltage and checking the line contact condition are the corresponding troubleshooting steps. Poor contact will cause random output actions, and the corresponding step is to check the terminal wiring. Poor contact, as a cause of equipment failure, refers to a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and terminal ends will cause poor contact and increase the contact resistance; poor contact can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit. When the electric fan is running, it emits abnormal sound, caused by mechanical friction, loose parts or deformation. Bearing damage refers to the failure of bearing components, often leading to excessive temperature rise, noise and vibration, and difficulty in starting; in the fault tree of motor excessive temperature rise, bearing damage is classified as one of the specific causes under the mechanical fault branch. Bearing damage will cause the speed to be low during load operation, will cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and will also cause bearing overheating. When the traction motor has abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, bearing damage is a possible cause, and the damaged bearing needs to be replaced.

The marine motor includes a bearing, a winding and a shaft. The winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of AC motors; the winding insulation of a marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proofing, mildew-proofing and salt-oil-mist-proofing and be oil-resistant. The shaft is a mechanical transmission component used to transmit torque and rotational motion, commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments; the movable parts of the two units of an electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a shaft and a panel, assembled by bolts. When measuring the insulation resistance of a coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in a through-type current transformer, the large current conductor under test is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding.

The fault symptom of electric fan heating may be caused by rubbing between the stator and rotor of the motor; partial winding short circuit will also cause electric fan heating; lack of oil or inflexible oscillating mechanism will likewise cause electric fan heating. When heating is due to stator-rotor rubbing, it is necessary to check the shaft bearing and ensure a uniform air gap; when heating is due to winding short circuit, the treatment method is to rewind the winding; when heating is due to lack of oil or inflexible oscillation, the oil should be cleaned and replaced or the oscillating mechanism repaired. Lack of oil will cause moving parts jammed; lack of oil is a common cause of jamming of the piston of the fuel cutoff cylinder of the main engine remote control system. Electric fan heating manifests as an abnormal rise in the temperature of the machine body. Bearing damage is a possible mechanical cause, and the treatment method is to replace the bearing; damage to the speed control switch is also one of the possible causes of failure to start of the electric fan.

For the above faults, the maintenance involves steps such as replacing the capacitor, replacing the bearing, replacing the switch and inspection and repair.
