Replacing the capacitor is used to repair the intermittent rotation fault of a capacitor-type electric fan caused by soft breakdown of the capacitor, is also used to solve the problem of slow speed of an impeller washing machine caused by reduced capacitance, deterioration or loose wiring of the capacitor, is used to deal with the abnormal operation fault of a spin-dry motor caused by capacitor damage, is used to repair the fault of a refrigerator motor in which, after power-on, it does not start and there is no sound, caused by damage to the starting capacitor, and is also used to eliminate the fault caused by short circuit of the resonance capacitor in the failure of the generator voltage to build up normally. Replacing the switch is used to repair the fault of an electric fan sometimes rotating and sometimes not rotating caused by poor contact of the speed control switch, is used to repair the failure to start of an electric drill caused by poor contact or damage of the hand-press switch, and in electric drill maintenance, if the switch is damaged, the replacement operation is performed to eliminate the starting obstacle. Inspection and repair is suitable for the post-disassembly treatment of an electric fan when the oscillating parts fit too tightly or the shaded-pole winding is open, is also used to solve the automatic tripping fault caused by the free tripping mechanism of the main switch failing to hold, and is a necessary measure when severe heating and three-phase current imbalance are caused by inter-turn short circuit of the transformer winding; the main switch being prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration corresponds to inspection and repair.

In addition, when the timer fails, the handling method is to replace the timer; in the troubleshooting of the washing machine not working after power-on, it is necessary to check whether the timer wiring is loose or disconnected, whether the timer knob slips, and whether the contact is in good contact; the main cause of the washing machine impeller rotating intermittently is timer failure, and the impeller being unable to reverse may be caused by partial damage to the timer; possible causes of washing machine earth leakage faults include the timer or program switch being damp, and the maintenance method may use a hair dryer to blow it dry. As a digital logic circuit application component used in household appliances, the timer is commonly used in marine living equipment to control the start and stop of electric fans, the washing and dehydration programs of washing machines, and the defrost cycles of cold storage; in the cold storage defrost control system, the defrost timer DT₁ is used to control the automatic switching of the defrost cycle, and when the defrost time ends, its two sets of switches automatically return to the non-defrost state; when the cold storage selector switch is placed in the "REF" position for manual refrigeration, it cuts off the defrost timer motor, so that the defrost heating does not work.

The speed control switch is used to adjust the speed of the electric fan or the active power distribution of parallel generator sets. In the marine power station, this switch is manually operated to adjust the servo motor of the diesel engine governor; adjusting this switch can change the diesel engine throttle opening, thereby realizing active power distribution among parallel operating units. Different inclination angles of the fan blades will cause vibration and noise during operation of the electric fan; ceiling fan blade faults can be corrected by removing the blades and overlapping them for comparison to correct the highest and lowest points and the twist angle; table fan blades should be repeatedly corrected according to the deformation, and the blades should be directly replaced if necessary; noise caused by blade problems requires inspection and correction of the blades, and replacement if necessary. If the electric drill fan blade does not fit tightly with the shaft, abnormal operating sound will result, and copper sheet needs to be wrapped around the shaft so that it fits tightly on the shaft.

In marine electrical equipment, the capacitor is a relatively commonly used component, and marine electrical equipment uses capacitors to achieve the function of blocking direct current and passing alternating current. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together with an insulating material separating them in the middle. In circuit diagrams it is generally represented by the letter C plus a numerical number, for example, C25 means the capacitor numbered 25. The capacitor detection procedure is applicable to capacitors. During detection, a multimeter can be used to measure capacitance, and through the use of the capacitance function of the multimeter, it is possible to determine whether there is earth leakage, the capacitance value, and whether the polarity of an electrolytic capacitor is normal. Capacitor faults will occur, and capacitor faults belong to the category of problems under the component category of capacitors. It may also be caused by the ceiling fan rotor sinking or the shading coil set being desoldered. Insufficient capacitor capacitance is a type of fault cause for abnormal starting of the electric fan, manifested as slow starting and reduced speed, and the handling method is to replace the capacitor with the same specification.

The fault symptom that the motor can only start after being given a push may be caused by a broken auxiliary winding of the motor, or may be caused by a short circuit, open circuit, or poor contact of the capacitor. For an open-circuit starting winding, the maintenance method is to find the break point and reconnect it or replace the winding, that is, restore it by repairing the starting winding; for capacitor faults, the maintenance method is to check the capacitor and replace the damaged part with the same specification. An open-circuit starting winding will cause the motor auxiliary winding to be broken, thereby making the motor require a vibration to start.

Abnormal operation of the electric fan oscillating mechanism is another common fault symptom. This symptom may be caused by the steel wire pull cord being loose or damaged, and the pull cord needs to be fixed securely or replaced with the same specification. Failure of the clutch-type oscillating mechanism is often caused by insufficient spring force of the upper clutch tooth compression spring or burrs on the meshing shaft pin; clutch failure causes torque to be unable to be transmitted to the crank, and the burrs need to be filed off and grease added or the spring replaced. Failure of the sliding plate-type oscillating mechanism may be caused by the catch lever slipping at the recess of the oscillating disk, so that the oscillating disk cannot be positioned well; it can be repaired by adjusting the position of the steel wire pull cord so that the catch lever engages tightly with the recess of the oscillating disk. Serious wear or poor meshing of the helical gear will cause abnormal oscillation, and the helical gear needs to be replaced. Looseness of parts in the oscillating mechanism covers various situations: loosening of the screws on the gearbox cover causes displacement of the cover plate, resulting in poor meshing of the helical gear;

The retaining ring connecting the oscillating connecting rod and the crank has fallen off or the connecting rod is too loose; in the clutch-type mechanism, the compression spring force of the upper clutch teeth is insufficient; in the sliding-plate mechanism, the catch lever slips at the recess of the oscillating disk, causing positioning failure; the wire cable is loose or damaged, affecting the operation of the oscillating mechanism. Lack of oil in the oscillating mechanism will likewise affect its normal operation.

For the above mechanical faults, tightening the parts of the oscillating mechanism is the main maintenance procedure. If there are burrs on the meshing shaft pin, file off the burrs and add a little grease to repair the clutch mechanism; this operation also falls within the scope of adding oil to the oscillating mechanism. When the sliding-plate mechanism fails due to slipping of the catch lever, adjust the wire cable so that the catch lever engages tightly with the recess. When the gearbox cover screws are loose and cause the cover plate to shift, tighten the cover plate screws to restore gear meshing. When the retaining ring has fallen off, replace it with a new one; when the connecting rod is too loose, add appropriate washers.

In terms of electrical connections, poor contact is one of the causes of equipment failure; loose, oxidized or foreign matter at electrical connections will increase contact resistance. Poor contact of the input terminal corresponds to reconnect; loose terminal contact corresponds to reconnect; loose input terminal or poor contact of the input terminal corresponds to reconnect; poor contact (terminal block) corresponds to reconnect; poor contact of the output terminal corresponds to reconnect; poor contact of the terminal connection block likewise corresponds to reconnect. Reconnect is one of the maintenance procedures of the PLC control system, used for rewiring operations to deal with terminal poor contact, looseness or broken wires; the treatment method for the fault of loose input terminal or poor contact is reconnect, and the treatment method for poor contact of the output terminal block causing all outputs to fail to connect is also reconnect.

AC single-phase motors are often used on ships as the power source for equipment such as electric drills, electric fans and refrigerators, among which the fault diagnosis and repair of electric drills account for a relatively large proportion. The electric drill fails to start is one of the common fault symptoms, and its possible causes involve many aspects such as the power supply, switch, brush, winding and mechanical transmission. No voltage at the power supply or an open power supply circuit will directly cause the electric drill to fail to start; at this time, check the power supply circuit to eliminate the power supply problem. Poor contact or damage of the hand-pressed switch will likewise cause the electric drill to fail to start; for this situation, the operation of replacing the switch should be performed. Severe brush wear, insufficient spring pressure or a dirty commutator will all cause poor contact between brush and commutator, thereby causing the electric drill to fail to start; if the poor contact is caused by brush wear, the brush should be replaced directly; if the brush wire is loose, the brush needs to be repaired or replaced.

An open circuit in the armature winding or stator winding is one of the common causes of the electric drill fails to start; an open stator winding needs to be checked and determined for repair or rewinding.

Too slow a speed of the electric drill is another common fault symptom. Too little grease in the gearbox will cause too slow a speed of the electric drill. Wear of the meshing gears is a mechanical fault cause of too slow a speed of the electric drill; for wear of the meshing gears, the worn gears should be replaced, and this operation is replacing the gears. Excessive brush spring pressure may cause too slow a speed of the electric drill. The brush not being on the neutral line will also cause too slow a speed of the electric drill. Damage to the meshing gears will cause abnormal noise during operation of the electric drill, and the damaged gears need to be replaced. When large sparks occur during operation of the electric drill and are caused by poor contact between brush and commutator, the brush needs to be ground or replaced. An uneven or unclean commutator surface needs to be cleaned and re-treated.

In the maintenance of electric drills, the multimeter is a commonly used test instrument. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, and is divided into two types: analog and digital; the analog multimeter belongs to the multimeter, the digital multimeter likewise belongs to the multimeter, and the MF-47 multimeter also belongs to the multimeter; it can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and the panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The multimeter contains three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; at full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. Using the resistance measurement function of the multimeter, the continuity and resistance value of the winding can be checked; using the voltage measurement function, the power supply voltage and the potential at each point can be checked; using the current measurement function, whether the loop current is normal can be judged; using the capacitance measurement function, the capacitance of the capacitor can be checked; using the diode measurement function, the polarity and quality of the diode can be judged; using the transistor measurement function, the amplification capability of the transistor can be checked; using the thyristor measurement function, the trigger and conduction state of the thyristor can be judged; using the photosensitive device measurement function, the light response of the photosensitive element can be checked; using the thermocouple measurement function, the thermoelectric potential corresponding to the temperature can be measured.

In an electric fan, this instead causes slow starting and reduced speed; both checking for bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition take the bearing as the object. The commutator is a rotating sliding contact component used for leading current in and out in DC machines and wound-rotor machines, is composed of commutator segments, and the graphite brush is soft in texture and easily damages the commutator, being suitable for machines with general commutation conditions and uniform load; when disassembling a DC motor, care should be taken to prevent damage to the winding ends, the commutator or the slip rings. The brush is an important conductive element used for leading current in or out between the stationary part and the sliding part of a machine, and DC machines, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators all need to be equipped with brushes. Checking the contact condition between the brush and the commutator takes the commutator and the brush as the object, checking the brush holder condition takes the brush as the object, checking the commutator segment condition takes the commutator as the object, and checking the brush position takes the brush as the object. For brushed machines, excessive brush wear is one of the common faults, ranking alongside open circuit and short circuit of the stator winding; during routine maintenance of a DC motor, a hand blower or hair dryer must be used to remove brush powder and dust near the winding ends and the commutator; after replacing the brush, if the contact area is less than 70%, the contact surface between the brush and the commutator must be ground in; when grinding a newly replaced brush, the brush must be placed in the brush holder, and 00# abrasive cloth is wrapped around the commutator surface and pulled back and forth.

Reduction gears are also used in marine radar equipment; the antenna base contains a reduction gearbox structure, and the antenna base needs to be painted once every six months to prevent corrosion.

AC single-phase motors are often used on ships as the power source for equipment such as electric fans, refrigerators and electric drills, among which the electric drill is a hand-held electric tool, and its operating condition is directly related to work efficiency and operating safety. Common faults of the electric drill can be summarized into several categories such as failure to start, too slow speed, abnormal noise during operation, large spark between the brush and the commutator, and overheating of the electric drill; in addition, there is also the special phenomenon that the electric drill fails to start at a certain position. These fault symptoms are often caused by multiple reasons, and each item should be checked one by one during maintenance. Damage to the reduction gear can likewise cause the electric drill to fail to start; at this time the damaged gear should be replaced, that is, the maintenance procedure of replacing the gear is carried out. When the electric drill fails to start due to brush wear, the maintenance method is to replace the brush; if the brush wire is loose, the brush should be repaired or replaced to eliminate the fault.

The phenomenon that the electric drill fails to start at a certain position likewise needs to be checked in combination with the above electrical and mechanical factors. The fault of the electric drill failing to start caused by bearing wear is likewise solved by replacing the bearing, and after replacement an appropriate amount of good-performance lubricating grease needs to be added. For damage to the meshing gears, the maintenance method is to replace the damaged gear; this operation is replacing the gear, and is applicable to the case where abnormal noise occurs during operation of the electric drill and the cause is damage to the meshing gears, the specific operation being to replace the damaged gear; for insufficient or unclean lubricating grease, the gearbox should be cleaned and filled with sufficient good-performance lubricating grease; for bearing wear, the bearing needs to be replaced and an appropriate amount of good-performance lubricating grease added; for the heating fault of the electric fan, the shaft and bearing need to be checked, symmetrical repair or replacement carried out, and attention paid to the uniformity of the air gap.

When the sparking between the brush and commutator is relatively large, the possible causes include the brush not being on the neutral line, short circuit or poor contact of the stator and rotor windings, and poor contact between brush and commutator. Poor contact between brush and commutator will cause excessive sparking under brush, and its causes include the commutator surface being too dirty, the brush spring being too small, or brush sticking. For the brush not being on the neutral line, the maintenance procedure is to correct the brush position; for short circuit or poor contact of the stator and rotor windings, it is necessary to check the fault point and determine repair or rewinding; for poor contact between brush and commutator, the maintenance procedure is to adjust the brush pressure and grind or replace the brush. When checking the contact condition between brush and commutator, both the commutator and brush must be used; when checking the brush holder condition, the brush is used; when checking the commutator segment condition, the commutator is used; when checking the brush position, the brush is used. If the commutator surface is uneven or unclean, it must be cleaned and reprocessed. When adjusting the brush, mark the brush rocker of the DC motor with paint before disassembly so that the brush position can be adjusted quickly and accurately.

When the electric drill overheats, overload of the electric drill, bearing overheating, heating of the reduction gearbox surface, and heating of the stator and rotor windings may all be possible causes of overheating. For overheating caused by overload of the electric drill, the maintenance procedure is to reduce the load; for overheating caused by bearing overheating, it is necessary to eliminate the fault of poor mechanical assembly and clean and change the oil. When checking bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition, the bearing must be used. Bearing overheating of the generator corresponds to the maintenance procedure of replacing the bearing, which is used to eliminate the condition of severe bearing wear in the generator bearing overheating fault, and is also used to repair the overheating fault caused by bearing damage of the motor. Poor ventilation and open circuit of the armature winding are also possible fault causes of the electric drill, and the corresponding maintenance procedures include grinding the commutator, improving ventilation, repairing the stator winding, and repairing the armature winding.

AC single-phase motors are widely used in marine equipment, and appliances such as washing machines, electric fans, refrigerators, and electric drills mostly use this type of motor as the prime mover. For a washing machine, its faults can be classified into three categories: motor faults, electrical control circuit faults, and mechanical faults. When troubleshooting, first determine which category the fault belongs to, then check item by item.

When the washing machine does not work after being energized, the possible causes include an open circuit in the power supply, low voltage, timer fault, poor contact of the program switch, or capacitor damage; mechanical causes include blockage at the bottom of the impeller, excessive or tangled clothing, damage to the transmission pulley or belt, and jamming of the main shaft. During maintenance, it is necessary to check the power supply leads, plug and socket, and fuse condition, and eliminate electrical path faults one by one, that is, check whether the power supply leads are energized and whether the plug and socket are intact, and check whether the fuse is blown.

Slippage of the timer knob is mostly caused by the loosening of the positioning pin, which can be repaired by bonding with 502 glue; when the contacts of the program selection switch have poor contact of contacts, they should be polished with fine sandpaper and the metal parts should be repaired; if the break point of the motor winding is external, it can be reconnected, and if the internal damage is present, the winding needs to be replaced. Poor contact of contacts of the timer will cause the washing machine not to work after being energized, and the timer needs to be repaired or replaced. Capacitor damage will cause the whole machine not to work after being energized; when handling the fault of the washing machine washing motor, the capacitor of the same specification needs to be replaced. If the transmission belt is too loose, slips, or falls off, it will also cause no operation after being energized; the maintenance procedure is to adjust the transmission belt or replace it with a new belt. Debris blocking the clearance at the bottom of the impeller, excessive washing clothes, or clothes tangling the impeller can also cause no operation after being energized. When the supply voltage is low, the maintenance procedure is to install an AC voltage stabilizer.

For the fault symptom of slow impeller speed and unclean washing, mechanical causes include loose connection between the impeller and the shaft, and an excessively loose or slipping drive belt; electrical causes involve reduced capacitance and deterioration of the capacitor and partial short circuit of the motor winding; low supply voltage or broken rotor cage bars of the motor can also cause this fault; loosening of the small pulley fastening screw and timer failure are potential causes; excessive laundry or laundry tangling the impeller are non-equipment fault causes. Maintenance methods include tightening the fixing screws, adjusting or replacing the drive belt or capacitor. When slow speed is caused by a loose connection between the impeller and the shaft, the fixing screws should be tightened; when slow impeller speed is caused by loosening of the small pulley fastening screw, it should be repaired by tightening the screw. Slow impeller speed with unclean washing may be caused by reduced capacitance or deterioration of the capacitor, and a capacitor of the same specification needs to be replaced; the main cause of the impeller turning intermittently is timer failure, and the maintenance method refers to the treatment of the failure to work after power-on; when the washing machine has large vibration and noise during operation, one cause is friction between the impeller and the washing tub, and loose fastening screws at the pulley, base plate and other places need to be tightened; an out-of-round or deformed impeller can be carefully trimmed with a knife, and the impeller needs to be replaced if necessary.

Damage to the capacitor of the electric fan will cause failure to start, and a part of the same specification needs to be replaced during maintenance; if the fan sometimes turns and sometimes does not, one possible cause is timer failure, and the treatment is to replace the timer; soft breakdown of the capacitor can also cause intermittent turning, and the capacitor needs to be replaced. When the refrigerator motor does not start and there is no sound, the possible cause may be a blown power fuse, or damage to the motor starting capacitor, the latter requiring replacement of the capacitor; poor contact of the contacts of the refrigerator temperature controller automatic control will cause frequent starting of the motor. Damage to the capacitor of the spin-dry motor is one cause of abnormal operation of the spin-dry tub, and the capacitor needs to be replaced during treatment. If no capacitor of the same capacitance is available, one of close capacitance may be substituted, but it must strictly not be too small or too large. Failure of the generator voltage to build up normally corresponds to replacing the capacitor, and a power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply.

Loose screws correspond to tighten the screws, loose connecting screws of two conductive parts correspond to tighten the screws, and a loose COM screw corresponds to tightening. The operation of tightening is used in electrical maintenance to ensure good contact of wiring terminals, screws and fastening mechanisms or to prevent loosening; the wiring screws of an electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact, and failure to tighten the external wiring screws of a thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be open. Low supply voltage will cause loud noise in an AC electromagnet, and at this time the power supply needs to be adjusted to 0.85~1.10 times the rated voltage; when insufficient holding force of the contactor causes welding of contacts, check whether the supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage. Poor contact of contacts will cause contact overheating or burning, and methods for treating poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface and fastening the contacts to the conductive plate. The electric main engine remote control system contains a fuse, and fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Voltage can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter; voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis; failure of the generator to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems.

In the maintenance of AC single-phase motors, capacitance and the capacitor are unavoidable inspection objects. The main performance indicators of a capacitor include capacitance, withstand voltage value, i.e. the maximum working voltage, and temperature resistance value. When marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, a multimeter can be used to test the capacitance, and the capacitor testing steps apply to the capacitor, determining by measurement whether its earth leakage and capacitance are normal. Once a capacitor fault occurs in a capacitor, the fault still belongs to the category of the capacitor component and usually manifests as soft breakdown, reduced capacitance, deterioration or damage.

Capacitor damage will cause obvious abnormalities in various marine and household appliances. Damage to the starting capacitor of the refrigerator motor will cause no sound and failure to start after power-on. In addition, the fault of failure of the generator voltage to build up normally corresponds to replacing the capacitor, so as to eliminate the failure of voltage build-up caused by short circuit of the resonant capacitor.

AC single-phase motors include those in washing machines and also include capacitors; electric fans likewise include capacitors and timers. Washing machines are generally used as the power machine for electric fans, electric drills, refrigerators, washing machines, etc., and their faults can be divided into three categories: motor faults, electrical control circuit faults and mechanical faults. If the gap at the bottom of the impeller is blocked by debris, or if too much laundry is loaded or the laundry wraps around the impeller, the washing machine will also fail to work after power is applied. Possible causes of electric fan heating faults include lack of oil or a stiff oscillating mechanism. Loose screws on the electric fan bearing bracket will cause uneven rotor clearance, resulting in rubbing between the stator and rotor and thus failure to start.

Among the lubrication problems of the washing machine transmission mechanism, lack of oil in the bearing is a specific case of poor lubrication of the impeller washing machine transmission mechanism; for this fault the motor must be removed and lubricating oil added for repair. It is listed alongside lack of oil in the seal ring, V-belt friction and poor lubrication of the shaft hole, all belonging to transmission lubrication problems. At the impeller shaft of the washing machine, if the seal ring does not fit tightly with the shaft, water leakage will result; if there is a lack of lubrication between the impeller shaft and the seal ring, an appropriate amount of lubricating oil can be applied to the seal ring. A lack of lubrication between the impeller shaft and the seal ring of the washing machine will cause poor lubrication of the transmission mechanism.

Lack of oil in the refrigerator compressor may cause a sound after power is applied but failure to start.

Abnormal operation of the spin tub is also related to the brake drum. The brake drum is a component of the brake device of the washing machine spin motor; looseness between the spin motor shaft and the brake drum will cause abnormal noise during spin tub operation, and deformation of the brake drum or too small a clearance will also cause abnormal noise during spin tub operation. The method for repairing looseness between the spin motor shaft and the brake drum is to tighten the lock nut; for the fault of brake drum deformation or too small a clearance, the brake drum must be repaired and the clearance adjusted.

Faults in the drainage link also require attention. In a washing machine, if the drain valve is blocked by debris, drainage will be poor or impossible; the repair method is to open the drain valve and remove the debris. If the drain valve pull strap is too tight or there is debris in the valve, the washing machine may leak water; the strap should be appropriately loosened and the debris removed. If the washing machine drain hose is folded into a dead corner or has a crease, it is easily blocked by debris and drainage will be poor; aging and cracking of the drain hose will cause water leakage, and the hose must be replaced and the pipe mouth firmly glued; when clearing a blocked drain hose, a thin iron wire bent into a hook can be used to pull out the debris inside.

Poor contact and loose screws are common fault causes running through the above equipment. Loose screws are a common cause in ship electrical and mechanical equipment whereby, due to vibration, improper installation or aging, the fastening force of connections decreases, thereby causing poor contact, open circuits, overheating or mechanical faults; in the fault of excessively high temperature rise of the circuit breaker, loose connecting screws of two conductive parts are one of the main causes and must be handled by tightening the screws; loose connecting screws of two conductive parts correspond to tightening the screws; loose screws will cause the shunt trip unit to fail to trip the circuit breaker, corresponding to tightening the screws; a loose "COM" screw corresponds to tightening. The vibration and swaying environment unique to ships can easily cause loosening of wiring clamping screws, of the connections between cable connectors and the base, and of the fixing screws inside the PLC, creating hidden fault risks.

The cabins of senior crew members on ships are usually equipped with a refrigerator, whose power machine is mostly an AC single-phase motor; therefore, the maintenance of AC single-phase motors occupies a certain place in the maintenance of marine motors. Refrigerator faults can be broadly classified into three categories: motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system; maintenance personnel should master the troubleshooting of common faults of the refrigerator motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system. Personnel undertaking such work need to be familiar with the structure of electrical equipment, the working principle, the functions and locations of components (assemblies), and to master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, so as to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary diagnosis through inquiry, observation, touching, listening and smelling.

After the refrigerator is powered on, the motor failing to start and having no sound is one of the common faults. There are many causes of this phenomenon: a blown power fuse, poor contact of the plug, or the thermal relay not being reset will all prevent the motor from starting; the temperature controller being open or in the "stop" position will likewise cause the motor to fail to start; damage to the coil of the starting relay or poor contact of its contacts will also cause the motor to fail to start and have no sound after power is applied; damage to the defroster and damage to the refrigerator motor starting capacitor are both possible causes of this fault. In addition, when the supply voltage is 15% below the rated value, the motor will also fail to start and have no sound after power is applied. If the motor makes a sound but fails to start after power is applied, this may be caused by low supply voltage, in which case an AC voltage regulator needs to be installed;

For the above faults, troubleshooting should be carried out item by item. If the power supply fuse is blown, check whether the power supply lead and the fuse are blown and replace them; if the plug has poor contact, check the plug and socket; if the thermal relay has not been reset, perform the reset operation; if the temperature controller is open or in the "stop point" position, readjust it; loss of the temperature-sensing agent in the temperature controller will cause an open circuit, making the refrigerator motor fail to start, and the temperature-sensing agent must be re-set or the temperature controller replaced. For the WSF-type temperature controller, turning the differential adjustment screw counterclockwise increases the on-off differential, and one turn of the screw changes the differential by about 4℃; for the WDF-type temperature controller, turning the on-point adjustment screw clockwise raises the on-point temperature and vice versa lowers it, while stop-point adjustment is the opposite. Sticking contacts of the temperature controller will cause the refrigerator to run continuously; repeatedly turning the knob may restore it, otherwise repair or replacement is required. If the starting relay coil is damaged, repair or replace the coil; if the contact has poor contact, repair or replace it; contact sticking may cause the refrigerator motor to stop suddenly during starting or running, and the stuck contact likewise needs repair or replacement.

If the defroster is damaged, repair or replace the component. If the starting capacitor is damaged, replace the capacitor. If the refrigerant leaks seriously or the refrigeration system is blocked, the phenomenon of running continuously without cooling will occur. Frost-free refrigerators are provided with a cold-air circulation fan and an air-door adjustment knob, which should also be noted during troubleshooting. The performance of a capacitor to be tested includes earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors; a multimeter can be used for the test, and the capacitor testing procedure applies to capacitors.

Capacitor damage is the cause of various equipment failing to work normally. If soft breakdown of the capacitor causes intermittent rotation or intermittent stopping, the capacitor should also be replaced. In addition, failure of the generator voltage to build up normally may be caused by a short-circuited resonant capacitor, and the corresponding measure is to replace the capacitor. It may also be low supply voltage, in which case check the power supply voltage. When the electric drill speed is too slow, the possible cause is low supply voltage, and the power supply voltage needs to be checked and adjusted. Failure of the electric drill to start may be caused by a damaged switch, poor brush contact, an open winding or bearing wear.

Undervoltage will cause motor speed low after starting, will also cause low speed under load operation, and will also cause the motor temperature to be too high or smoking. The contactor contains a coil; if the contactor fails to pick up or has insufficient holding force accompanied by a humming sound, the cause may be low supply voltage or large fluctuation; a voltage across the coil lower than 85% of the rated voltage specified by the product is regarded as undervoltage. The thermal relay uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and is mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors; it is used in large quantities on ships, and generally the overload protection of small motors is performed by it.

For the fault symptom of failure to start, several troubleshooting measures correspond during maintenance: check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage and, if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find the short circuit or open circuit part and repair it, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer, and if the motor runs normally, check the reducer part. Failure of the power supply to be connected, incorrect wiring of the control equipment, undervoltage, short circuit to earth between stator winding phases, incorrect wiring and stator winding short circuit will all cause failure to start.

A multimeter or voltmeter can be used when measuring voltage, and a multimeter is also used to measure capacitance. Marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, and capacitors are widely used in marine electrical equipment.

On ships, the cabins of senior crew members are usually each equipped with a refrigerator, whose prime mover is mostly an AC single-phase motor; therefore the refrigerator is one of the typical loads of AC single-phase motors. Refrigerator faults can be broadly classified into three categories: the motor, the electrical control circuit and the refrigeration system; troubleshooting often requires the use of a multimeter or voltmeter to measure voltage, judging whether the power supply is normal by the voltage value. That is to say, a multimeter is used to measure voltage, and a voltmeter is likewise used to measure voltage; the voltage values read by the two are the direct basis for judging whether the power supply circuit is normal. If the supply voltage is lower than 15% of the rated value, the motor neither starts nor makes any sound after being energized;

The indirect-cooling refrigerator is additionally provided with a cold-air circulation fan and an air-door adjusting knob. When its air adjusting door fails, although the compressor can still start and stop automatically, the temperature inside the cabinet is on the high side; at this time the air adjusting door should be removed to check whether the mechanism has failed and to adjust it.

The temperature controller performs the electrical control function in the refrigeration systems of refrigerators and refrigerated containers; it relies on a temperature-sensing element to monitor temperature and control starting and stopping of the compressor. After power is applied, the motor fails to start and there is no sound; one of the causes is that the temperature controller is open or the knob is in the "stop" position. Loss of the temperature-sensing agent will open the temperature controller circuit, and the refrigerator motor then fails to start; the remedy is to reset the temperature-sensing agent or replace the temperature controller. If the contacts of the temperature controller stick, the refrigerator will run continuously; the knob can be turned repeatedly to try to restore it, and if this is ineffective, overhaul or replace it. When terminals 10 and 11 of electronic temperature controller 23A1 are conducting, the liquid-supply solenoid valve is energized and opens, and the compressor begins refrigerating; when the temperature inside the cabinet reaches the set lower limit, terminals 10 and 11 of 23A1 open and the compressor stops running.

Once the contacts stick, the motor may suddenly stop rotating during starting or running. The corresponding remedy is to repair or replace the coil, and to repair or replace the contacts that have stuck. Poor contact of contacts is essentially a decrease in electrical conductivity caused by contamination, oxidation or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface; in a contactor it is one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning, and when dealing with it the contact surface must be cleaned, the surface reconditioned, and the contacts and conductive plate tightened. Poor contact is mostly caused by looseness, oxidation or foreign matter at electrical connections increasing the contact resistance; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals can cause it, and it can result in local overheating, phase failure, short circuit between phases, and also make the output act randomly; the corresponding treatment is to check the terminal wiring. When the temperature rise of a circuit breaker is too high, looseness of the screws connecting the two conductive parts is one of the main causes, and the screws must be tightened; failure of the shunt trip unit to trip the circuit breaker may also originate from loose screws, and the remedy is likewise to tighten the screws.

A thermal relay is a protective relay that uses a bimetallic strip as its sensing element; classified by sensing element it belongs to the bimetallic-strip type, is used in large quantities on ships, and is generally used to accomplish overload protection of small motors. When the motor is overloaded, thermal relay FR operates, opening the control circuit so that contactor KM is de-energized and the machine stops; a fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not act as overload protection. The transistor relay for motor overload protection converts power into voltage, satisfying the relationship U=KP.

Charging too much refrigerant into the refrigeration system will cause excessively high pressure and too heavy a load, thereby causing motor overload. A motor internal fault will cause the motor to fail to start, automatic start failure, and motor overheating or even burning out; it is also one of the potential causes of noise or vibration when the refrigerator compressor is running; faults in the motor stator winding, bearing, etc. will also produce the phenomenon of excessive temperature rise.

Noise and vibration during operation of the refrigerator have several other sources. The damping rubber pad is used to fix the refrigerator compressor; if it is pressed too tightly, too loosely or has aged, it will make the motor produce noise during operation, and it is sufficient to adjust its tightness or replace it with a new pad during maintenance. Breakage of the vibration-damping suspension spring will increase noise inside the compressor; the remedy is to replace the compressor or repair the vibration-damping suspension spring. Noise may be emitted when the capillary tube and the high- and low-pressure lines collide due to compressor operation; gently moving the lines by hand to avoid collision will eliminate it;

Wax deposition in the capillary tube is one of the fault causes of high temperature inside the cabinet; the wax deposit can be flushed out or the capillary tube replaced. A poor door seal will cause serious cold leakage and cause frequent starting of the motor; if the door seal leaks seriously or the door is opened too many times, the refrigerator will not cool. For a poor door seal, the door gap should be repaired or the magnetic door seal strip replaced; for serious door seal leakage, the door seal strip should be overhauled or replaced. Damage to the lamp switch will make the lighting lamp stay on continuously or fail to light; it is sufficient to overhaul the lamp switch or directly replace it. As for electric fans, damage to the speed control switch is a possible cause of the motor failing to start, and the switch should be overhauled; if the rotor of a ceiling fan sinks, the symptom is slow starting and reduced speed, and it must be reassembled and the cause eliminated so that the rotor returns to its original position.

AC single-phase motors appear on ships mostly in the form of equipment such as electric fans, electric drills and washing machines, and the prime movers of these devices are all single-phase motors. Electric drills and washing machines likewise use AC single-phase motors as their power; among them, the washing machine washes clothes by rotation of the impeller, and its faults can be divided into three categories: motor faults, electrical control circuit faults and mechanical faults.

Failure to start of an electric fan is a common fault symptom, and its causes involve both electrical and mechanical aspects. The power supply not being connected is the first possible cause, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check the power supply circuit. An open-circuit in the stator winding can also cause failure to start of the electric fan; if the lead portion is broken, it should be re-welded, and if the wire is broken inside the slot, the winding should be removed and replaced rather than only welding the lead, and this handling process is to find the broken-circuit point and repair it. Detachment by unsoldering of the end ring (shading winding) can likewise cause failure to start, and the handling method is to re-weld the end ring. Mechanically, bearing damage, burrs or foreign matter in the bore of the oil-impregnated bearing, or lack of lubricating oil all cause excessive mechanical resistance, and the bearing needs to be replaced; severe shaft wear or loosening of the bearing bracket screws causing rubbing between stator and rotor requires replacing the shaft or adjusting the clearance, wherein loosening of the bearing bracket screws causes uneven rotor clearance, leading to rubbing between stator and rotor and thus inability to start; poor motor assembly affecting concentricity requires re-assembly to ensure smooth operation. The troubleshooting methods also include checking whether the voltage is too low, and replacing the bearing that has failed due to bearing wear. If the fan blade does not fit tightly with the shaft, copper sheet should be wrapped around the shaft so that it fits tightly on the shaft, and after replacing the bearing, an appropriate amount of good-performance lubricating grease should be added. The impeller turning intermittently is mainly caused by a timer fault. When a capacitor fault occurs in the capacitor, this fault belongs to a problem of the capacitor itself.

The marine motor contains a bearing, a winding and a shaft. The shaft is used to transmit torque and rotational motion.

Bearing overheating of the generator corresponds to the handling method of replacing the bearing. Abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation corresponds to replacing the shaft, and bearing overheating corresponds to replacing the bearing. A power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply. The wiring diagram should be checked and corrected; the voltage should be checked, and if it is indeed too low, appropriately raised;

For the repair of the refrigerator, the faults need to be treated separately in three categories: motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system, because the fault manifestations and troubleshooting directions of different categories are not the same.

As far as the motor category is concerned, when the voltage is lower than the rated value by 15%, after energization the motor will exhibit the phenomenon of failure to start and no sound, which is a direct basis for judging whether there is an undervoltage problem on the supply side. In this case, it should first be checked whether the voltage meets the rated value requirement, and then it is decided whether to disassemble and inspect the motor itself.

Faults in the electrical control circuit likewise manifest as the motor failing to start normally or operating abnormally, so when troubleshooting, the control circuit and the motor body must be distinguished, and the continuity and contact condition of the circuit confirmed section by section, to avoid misjudging a circuit problem as motor damage.

Faults in the refrigeration system manifest as another sign: when the refrigerant leaks severely or the refrigeration system is blocked, the refrigerator will run continuously without cooling. At this time the motor is still running continuously, but the temperature inside the cabinet cannot drop, indicating that the problem is not whether the motor can start, but whether the refrigerant is sufficient and whether the pipeline is unobstructed.

For the indirect-cooling refrigerator, its structure is also provided with a cold-air circulation fan and an air-door adjustment knob. The cold-air circulation fan is responsible for delivering the cooling capacity from the evaporator side into the cabinet, and the air-door adjustment knob is used to adjust the distribution of cold air.

When servicing the indirect-cooling refrigerator, in addition to checking the motor, the electrical control circuit and the refrigeration system separately according to the above three categories of faults, attention should also be paid to whether the cold-air circulation fan can rotate normally and whether the position of the air-door adjustment knob is appropriate, because once these two are abnormal, they will likewise cause the temperature inside the cabinet to fail to meet the requirement, and their appearance is similar to refrigerant leakage or system blockage, and they need to be distinguished in combination with the motor operating condition and the control circuit state.

In summary, fault judgment of the refrigerator can be carried out along three lines: motor, electrical control circuit and refrigeration system: a voltage lower than the rated value by 15% corresponds to failure to start and no sound of the motor after energization; for the indirect-cooling refrigerator, the cold-air circulation fan and the air-door adjustment knob must also be included in the inspection scope.

Daily maintenance points for marine transformers. Transformers commonly used on ships include three types: three-phase transformers, single-phase transformers and special-purpose transformers. Among them, three-phase transformers are mainly used to supply power to loads such as lighting and electric heating, and are mostly of the large-capacity type; single-phase transformers, together with three-phase transformers and special-purpose transformers, belong to the types of transformers commonly used on ships; special-purpose transformers are designed for specific working conditions. The structural forms of these transformers include dry-type, air-cooled and waterproof types.

Avoiding moisture in the transformer is the first matter to pay attention to in daily maintenance. The purpose of strictly preventing moisture is to prevent the transformer winding from becoming damp and thereby reducing the insulation resistance. Daily maintenance should regularly check whether the sealing of the transformer is good and whether the screws are loose. The insulation resistance between phases and to earth of a marine transformer is measured with a 500V insulation resistance tester and should be not less than 0.5MΩ; when the insulation resistance is lower than 0.2MΩ, measures must be taken to raise the insulation resistance value. The insulation resistance tester used here, also called a megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is a portable instrument used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables; when measuring the insulation resistance of a coil to earth, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester may be connected to the core.

Keeping the lead-out terminal clean is likewise not to be neglected. Dirt and oil scale on the terminal need to be removed to ensure good contact of the terminal; if traces of overheating are found on the terminal, the oxides should be removed and it should be tightened again, preventing short circuit or earthing faults by reducing the contact resistance. In the maintenance of marine transformers, when the lead-out terminal has traces of overheating, removing the oxides and then tightening again is this type of operation.

Monitoring transformer heating is a routine requirement during operation. The heating condition of the transformer should be monitored frequently, and its temperature rise must not exceed the maximum temperature rise permitted by the insulation. This precaution applies to the three-phase, single-phase and special-purpose transformers commonly used on ships. When installing a single-phase load of relatively large capacity, heating must be monitored in conjunction with ensuring the balance of the three-phase currents: the degree of unbalance of the three-phase currents must not exceed ±5% of the rated current, and the maximum phase current must not exceed the rated value.

Paying attention to transformer wiring is mainly aimed at the use scenarios of various small transformers. When using a small transformer, it is strictly forbidden to connect the secondary winding to the power supply, so as to avoid burning out the transformer; incorrect wiring will cause the transformer to burn out.

Winding faults and insulation treatment. A winding is the coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to produce a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force. A marine motor contains windings, and the winding insulation of a marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proofing, mould-proofing and salt-oil-mist-proofing and be oil-resistant. Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes leading to overcurrent and overheating of an AC motor. When inter-turn short circuit of the transformer winding causes severe heating and unbalance of the three-phase currents, inspection and repair are necessary measures. Inspection and repair means detection and repair carried out against faults of electrical equipment and components, covering mechanical mechanisms, winding insulation and contact components, etc., and is also used to solve the automatic tripping fault caused by the free tripping mechanism of the main switch failing to hold, as well as the post-disassembly treatment when the oscillating part of an electric fan fits too tightly or the shaded-pole winding is open. The phenomenon that the main switch is liable to trip automatically due to hull vibration corresponds to the measure of inspection and repair.

Use and maintenance of AC arc welding machines. AC arc welding machines belong to the category of special transformers and are all structurally movable equipment. Precautions for use of welding machines: when used in the open air, seawater or rainwater must be prevented from entering the interior of the equipment; after use, it should be placed in a dry, rain-sheltered place and secured, the securing measure being intended to prevent movement as the ship rolls; during operation, the current and temperature rise need to be observed to ensure they do not exceed the maximum values permitted by the insulation. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, the state of parts, the state of conductors and the operating parameters of the equipment, specifically such as whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, chafed or burnt.

Selection of related instruments and transformers. Resistance, voltage and current are the basic electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand the state of equipment. A multimeter is used for the measurement of resistance, voltage and current; a clamp-on ammeter is used for the measurement of current, contains a current transformer inside, and by the principle of the through-type current transformer can directly clamp and measure AC current without disconnecting the conductor; the through-type current transformer is a kind of current transformer in which the conductor carrying the large current to be measured is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit.

Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems, and local winding short circuit or phase failure, overvoltage, etc. are all related causes.

The wattmeter contains a current coil and a voltage coil. The current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load, and is used to detect the current of the circuit under test; the branch in which the voltage coil is located is connected in series with an additional resistor and connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test, and is used to detect voltage. The voltage range of the wattmeter is realized by connecting additional resistors of different resistance values in series with the voltage coil; the current coil and the voltage coil are respectively marked with corresponding terminals (such as "*"), and during measurement the current must flow in or out from this terminal at the same time.

The voltage transformer corresponds to symbol TV, is used to transform the voltage ratio, the secondary side voltage is 100V, and one end of the secondary side is earthed. When selecting a voltage transformer, the rated voltage ratio of the transformer should be selected according to the rated voltage of the voltage coil of the instrument used; its rated capacity should be not less than the power consumed by all measuring instruments, and the primary rated voltage is equal to or slightly greater than the voltage of the line under test.

The voltage transformer has the nature of a voltage source, and the secondary side standard voltage is usually 100V or 110V; its working principle is consistent with that of a transformer, but its internal resistance is extremely small, and the output voltage hardly changes with the load; when working it is equivalent to a no-load transformer, the secondary side must strictly not be short-circuited, and a fuse must be installed on the primary side for short circuit protection.

The current transformer corresponds to symbol TA, is used to transform the current ratio, the secondary side current is 5A, and the types include coil type, busbar type and through-core type, with one end of the secondary side earthed. When selecting, the secondary rated current should be slightly greater than or equal to the current of the line under test. The current transformer has the nature of a current source, and the secondary side standard current is usually 5A; the primary side terminals are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary side by K1 and K2; when working it is equivalent to a short-circuited transformer, the secondary winding must strictly not be open-circuited during operation, and a fuse must not be installed in the primary winding of the current transformer.

The fuse corresponds to symbol FU, has overload protection and short circuit protection functions, and is a safety appliance; when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; it belongs to distribution appliances and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, and is used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. The lighting busbar power supply automatic transfer circuit includes fuses such as FU1, FU2, FU3. In the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line via FU. The MF-30 multimeter is a related instrument under the symbol system of FU. A fuse must be installed on the primary side of the voltage transformer to provide short circuit protection for the power grid and the transformer.

The contactor is a ship low-voltage control appliance, mainly used to control the motor in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of high operating frequency and long life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size; it is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor. The core is the magnetic conducting component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as an insulation measurement reference point; the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start.

The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked. Welding is a process in which heating melts the solder, causing atomic diffusion between the weldment and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer with good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength is formed; its mechanism is to heat the weldment to melt the solder, cause atomic diffusion between the weldment and the solder, and after solidification form an alloy bonding layer at their interface, which has good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength, and welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products. The corresponding treatment measure for broken input wiring is welding, and the corresponding treatment measure for a loose "COM" screw is tightening. In addition, overheating of the magnetic field coil, adding oil to the bearing, etc. are also situations requiring attention and treatment in maintenance and repair.

Marine transformers and their power supply automatic transfer circuits In the ship electrical system, three-phase transformers undertake the power supply task for loads such as lighting and electric heating, usually have a relatively large capacity, and have several structural forms: dry-type, air-cooled and waterproof. Such transformers are often configured in pairs on ships, and the two can serve as mutual standby for each other, with a selector switch setting which one is in the main state and which one is in the standby state. When the main transformer loses power, the secondary circuit needs to automatically switch the load to the standby transformer, and this transfer is usually realized by contactor interlocking: the secondary sides of the two transformers are each connected by one contactor, and the coil circuits of the two contactors are mutually connected in series with the other's normally closed contact, thereby ensuring that only one contactor can be energized at any time and avoiding parallel connection of the secondary sides of the two transformers. The action of the standby contactor is not instantaneous but is put in after a delay, and the delay is completed by the time relay, so that false transfer caused by instantaneous fluctuation of the main power supply can be avoided.

Basic requirements and diagnostic methods for maintenance personnel Personnel engaged in the maintenance of marine transformers and auxiliary machinery electrical systems must be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions of each component and assembly, and their installation positions on the equipment, and must also be very familiar with the routing of the whole ship's electrical equipment, the working principle and the positions of each component. In traditional fault diagnosis, maintenance personnel rely on the method of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary judgment: asking is to learn from the operator about the operating conditions before and after the fault, looking is to observe the appearance, indications and action states, touching is to check the temperature rise and tightening conditions, listening is to distinguish whether the operating sound is abnormal, and smelling is to detect any burnt odor. This method is equally applicable to the inspection of transformers and their transfer circuits.

Contactor and its maintenance The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system, belongs to low-voltage control electrical appliances, is mainly used in power transmission systems, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The power of various auxiliary machinery on board is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so contactors are used in large quantities on board. The contactor includes an arc chute, and the arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the main contact breaks; the contactor includes a main contact, and the main contact undertakes the task of connecting and disconnecting the main circuit; the contactor includes a core, and the contactor also includes a coil, and the core and the coil together form the electromagnetic mechanism; after the coil is energized, it attracts the core, thereby driving the main contact to act. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor as equipment, and the maintenance content is carried out around the above-mentioned components, including the contact condition of the contacts, the inspection of the core and coil, and the cleaning of the arc chute.

Time relay and thermal relay Time relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in ship power systems, used to set the operating time in applications such as delayed switching-in of transformer standby power supply, with common codes KT, SJ, SL. Thermal relay is also an electrical device used for control or protection in ship power systems; it uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and belongs to the thermal relay classified by sensing element, its sensing part being the bimetallic strip. Thermal relay is mainly used for overload protection of small motors on ships and is used in large quantities on board; generally the overload protection task of small motors is completed by it. Common fault symptoms of thermal relay include thermal relay not operating, main circuit not conducting after thermal relay is connected, control circuit not conducting with thermal relay, and thermal relay unable to reset; fault diagnosis of the thermal relay body does not involve internal winding faults of the motor, nor does it involve problems of external actuating elements such as a burnt contactor coil.

Circuit breaker and its maintenance Circuit breaker is a switching device used to protect circuits in ship power systems, belonging to low-voltage distribution devices, divided into two types, frame type (air circuit breaker) and molded-case type, having both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. Air circuit breakers are mostly used as generator main switches, capable of automatically disconnecting the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker equipment; during maintenance the following fault symptoms need to be checked and handled: the circuit breaker may have the situation that when manually operating the circuit breaker the contact cannot close, that is, the contact cannot close during manual operation; the circuit breaker may have the situation that when electrically operating the circuit breaker the contact cannot close, that is, the contact likewise cannot close during electrical operation; in addition there is one phase contact unable to close; the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open; the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open; circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1h after closing;

the undervoltage trip unit has noise; the circuit breaker temperature rise is too high; the auxiliary switch has a fault; the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctions, causing the circuit breaker to open. These symptoms cover several aspects including the circuit breaker operating mechanism, trip unit, auxiliary switch and the electronic components of the trip unit, and inspection should be carried out item by item according to the specific symptoms.

The maintenance work of the ship auxiliary machinery electrical system starts from the accurate reading of electrical control circuit diagrams. Diagram reading is a key skill that maintenance personnel must master, among which the wire-tracing diagram-reading method is used to analyze faults of the auxiliary machinery control system and is the basic means of tracing circuit continuity item by item and determining the fault section. The wire-tracing diagram-reading method requires checking section by section along the control circuit, starting from the power supply end, passing through protective devices and control devices up to the actuating devices, comparing the open/closed state of each contact with the diagram markings, thereby narrowing the fault range to a certain circuit or a certain component. At the same time, proficiently mastering the general fault checking methods for the three situations of short circuit, open circuit and earthing is also a basic skill that maintenance personnel should possess. Short circuit manifests as instantaneous fuse blowing or tripping, open circuit manifests as the circuit not conducting and the device not operating, and earthing manifests as decreased insulation to earth or contact with the casing; the three have different checking means and different bases for judgment. These two capabilities together determine whether fault troubleshooting can quickly locate the specific circuit and specific component.

When using the conventional fault diagnosis method, the first step is observation. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters. Specifically for parts, check whether there is jamming or damage; specifically for wires, check whether there is looseness, breakage, abrasion or burning; specifically for operating parameters, compare the deviation between instrument readings and rated values to judge whether the equipment deviates from the normal working state. In this process, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure, working principle, component (assembly) functions and their locations of the electrical equipment, and understand the phenomena and make a preliminary diagnosis by means of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. Maintenance personnel must also be very familiar with the whole-ship electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components, otherwise diagram reading and wire tracing cannot be carried out at all.

In the ship's power system, the contactor is an electrical device used to control the motor. It belongs to the low-voltage control apparatus and is mainly used to control the motor in the electric drive system, featuring accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The amount of contactors used on ships is very large, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost entirely driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor itself includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil. The arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the main contact breaks, the main contact undertakes the task of making and breaking the main circuit, and the core and coil form the electromagnetic mechanism; after the coil is energized, electromagnetic attraction is generated to make the armature act. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start; during inspection, the voltage across the coil and the coil resistance can be measured to determine whether the coil is open or the power supply circuit has lost power. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor as an electrical apparatus, and its content is carried out around the state inspection and upkeep of the above-mentioned components, including whether the arc chute is damaged or has carbon deposits, whether the main contact is eroded or welded, whether the core is jammed or rusted, and whether the coil is overheated and discolored.

The thermal relay likewise belongs to the electrical devices used for control or protection in the ship's power system. It uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and is mainly used for overload protection of small motors on ships; the amount used on board is very large, and generally the overload protection task of small motors is completed by it. In control circuits such as air compressors, the thermal relay realizes overload shutdown by opening the control circuit through its normally closed contact; in the air compressor control circuit, its normally closed contact is connected in series in the control circuit to realize overload shutdown. In the water supply circuit, the thermal relay FR and the fuse FU respectively form overload and short circuit protection; the former acts according to the thermal effect of current, and the latter fuses according to the thermal effect of current, with a clear division of labor between the two. The thermal relay not acting, the main circuit not being connected after the thermal relay is connected, the thermal relay control circuit not being connected, and the thermal relay being unable to reset are common fault manifestations of this type of protective device, wherein the difference between not acting and being unable to reset is that the former manifests as the contact not closing or the mechanism being stuck during overload, while the latter manifests as being unable to restore the initial state by manual reset after tripping; the difference between the main circuit not being connected and the control circuit not being connected is that the former affects the motor power supply circuit, while the latter only affects control signal transmission. During inspection, first confirm whether the setting current matches the motor rated current, then check whether the normally closed contact is in good contact and whether the reset mechanism is flexible.

The time relay is also an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship's power system; in control circuits it often appears with text symbols such as KT, SJ and SL, and is used to realize delayed action, cooperating with the contactor and thermal relay to complete control logic acting in time sequence. When encountering KT, SJ and SL while reading diagrams, one should distinguish the circuit where the coil is located from the circuit where the delay contact is located, clarify whether it is on-delay or off-delay, and then judge the influence of the delay length on the subsequent action sequence.

The fuse performs the overload and short circuit protection function in the ship's power system, and its text symbol corresponds to FU. The fuse is a safety device; when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. It belongs to the distribution apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. A line short circuit fault manifests as the fuse blowing instantaneously or tripping, and it is necessary to distinguish by live inspection whether it is an external line short circuit or an internal component breakdown.

The fuse and the fuse element are closely related; the state of the fuse element directly reflects whether the fuse has already operated, and when replacing the fuse element it must be selected according to the original specification, and the capacity must not be arbitrarily increased or copper wire used as a substitute.

The functions of the changeover switch include selecting the measurement object and selecting the range. It is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has relatively many selection positions and contacts. On the main switchboard, the changeover switch is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The multimeter contains a changeover switch; during measurement, the measurement object and range are selected through the changeover switch, so the contact state of the changeover switch directly affects the credibility of the multimeter reading; if the contact is oxidized or in poor contact, the false appearance of a jumping reading or a zero indication will occur.

When an open-circuit fault occurs in the line, it manifests as the power supply not being connected after closing the switch or pressing the button, and neither the electrical appliances nor the motor operate.
