Switching on the power supply is a key step in the maintenance procedure of the PLC control system, referring to the process of connecting the power supply to perform functional testing or self-diagnosis after confirming that there is no short circuit or earthing fault. Before switching on the power supply, the input and output sections must be tested for the presence of short circuit or earthing faults, and only after confirmation of correctness may power be applied. Once the PLC is switched on, the self-diagnosis process begins; if an internal error occurs in the CPU, the "CPU Error" lamp on the panel indicates an abnormality. Applying power without a load corresponds to the step of switching on the power supply, that is, energizing first under the condition of no load, observing the action of the control circuit itself, and then gradually putting the load into service, so that even if incorrect wiring exists in the circuit, the fault range will not be expanded by putting the load into service.

After observation, the monitoring and indicating device should be further checked, and the current state of the equipment judged with the aid of instrument readings. Maintenance personnel, as the executors of fault diagnosis and repair, must be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of the electrical equipment's components (assemblies); their methods can be summarized as asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. Reading diagrams is a key skill for maintenance personnel, who need to master the method of tracing lines on diagrams to analyze faults in the auxiliary machinery control system; maintenance personnel must also be very familiar with the lines, working principles and positions of all components of the ship's electrical equipment, and need to be familiar with the equipment principles, structure and maintenance materials; in traditional fault diagnosis, they understand the phenomena and make a preliminary diagnosis by asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling.

Measuring instruments are important tools for fault checking.

The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; it is divided into two types, the analog type and the digital type. The MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter, and the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter also respectively belong to the category of multimeters. The multimeter comprises the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, wherein the current flowing through the meter head at full scale is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes, and the measuring circuit is used to convert different electrical quantities and different ranges, because the moving-coil meter head can only pass microampere-level current, and a conversion circuit is needed to measure different electrical quantities and ranges. The MF-47 multimeter can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A, and the panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The multimeter can be used to measure various objects such as resistors, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples.

When measuring a resistor in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistor, and never measure with power applied. Capacitance is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in between; its characteristic is to block direct current and pass alternating current, and in circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; its hindering effect on alternating current signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC). The insulation resistance tester, also called the megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, includes a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, has terminal posts L, E and G, and is used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables; according to the maximum voltage generated by the hand-cranked generator, it is divided into specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V and 2500V. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

The contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil. The main contact is the switching component in the contactor used to make or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor. If the motor does not rotate and the power supply is normal, a multimeter can be used to push the armature to close the main contacts, so as to troubleshoot an open-circuit fault in the main circuit. Discoloration of the copper main contacts or a burnt smell indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel must be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the main contacts are overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade higher should be selected as a replacement. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch, used for auxiliary control, and also used for self-locking of the control circuit, signal indication and interlock protection; it is one of the main components of the generator main switch, and as a series system element, its failure will cause the fault of the indicator light not lighting. In the forward rotation control of the motor, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize the self-locking of the contactor coil; the on-off state is used to control the lighting and extinguishing of the running indicator light to display the working state of the equipment; the normally closed auxiliary contact can control the action of the solenoid valve, used to release residual air when the air compressor stops; the coordinated action of the normally open and normally closed auxiliary contacts can switch the signal display of the water pump pumping state.

Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor, and circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker. The circuit breaker is a switching device used to protect the circuit in the ship power system, belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus, is divided into the frame type (air circuit breaker) and the molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during a short circuit fault; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. The failure of the shunt trip unit to make the circuit breaker open is a fault manifestation of the circuit breaker, meaning that when the shunt trip unit operates it fails to drive the circuit breaker contacts to open; a coil short circuit is one of the causes for the shunt trip unit failing to make the circuit breaker open, and too low a power supply voltage will also cause the shunt trip unit to be unable to make the circuit breaker open. The fuse element is a component of the fuse; long-term action of the power supply surge current may cause it to blow under a non-short-circuit fault, and the typical manifestation of a short circuit fault in the control circuit is fuse blowing. In lighting and electric heating circuits, the rated current of the fuse element is greater than or equal to the total load rated current; when a single asynchronous motor is started directly, the rated current is taken as 1.5 to 2 times the motor rated current; in the circuit of a lightly loaded motor that is not started frequently, the rated current is taken as the motor rated current

2.5 to 4 times.

Line short circuit fault is a common fault in the ship electrical system; a very large current flows through the short circuit point, causing the fuse to blow or the protective apparatus to operate automatically, accompanied by abnormal indications of the monitoring instruments and system alarm signals, and in severe cases the line insulation burns and smokes. Its causes include insulation being soaked in water and dampened, damaged bedding causing the insulation to be worn through, and dirty terminal posts discharging; metal parts falling onto wire ends or bare conductors can cause a short circuit, and there are also non-continuous short circuits, such as dirt being burned away after oil-grime discharge or conductive objects falling off by themselves. Poor maintenance management and improper operation will lead to line short circuit faults, and are one of the main causes of electrical line short circuit faults; specific manifestations include the insulation of electrical lines being soaked in water or seriously dampened, the bedding being damaged and not replaced in time when the marine cable passes through a metal hole or sharp edge, causing insulation damage, and damaging the insulation layer during operation belonging to this cause, terminal posts of the line being too dirty between them causing discharge between posts when energized, and metal parts falling onto wire ends or bare conductors during operation or maintenance.

Improper operation is also one of the causes of short circuits; during operation, damaging the insulation layer or metal parts falling onto wire ends can cause electrical line short circuit faults, and common manifestations include improper closing operation, unbalanced generator load control and improper operation caused by observation errors; during parallel operation, improper grasp of the closing moment or reversing the adjustment direction of load sharing can cause the generator reverse power protection to trip. Defects of the equipment itself will likewise lead to line short circuit faults; hidden dangers such as poor insulation and local insulation damage exist before the equipment leaves the factory, and a short circuit occurs after long-term operation; the coil of a motor or electrical apparatus has weak insulation because the winding does not meet the requirements, thereby causing a short circuit; aging of the insulation of the equipment or line and deterioration of materials belong to the causes of short circuits resulting from defects of the equipment itself. The marine cable includes a protective layer; the protective layer is used to protect the cable from oil, water and chemical corrosion, and is one of the three main components of the marine cable structure, on a par with the conductive copper core wire and the insulation layer; damaging the insulation layer during operation is one of the causes of electrical line short circuit faults.

Line short circuit fault corresponds to the short circuit fault inspection steps. When detecting a line short circuit, the power supply should first be cut off and the blown fuse found; use the resistance range of the multimeter to measure the resistance between the two ends of the circuit. If the resistance value is zero, it is a short circuit. To ensure measurement accuracy, the multimeter should be set to the R×1 range for measurement. When the line under test contains a large-capacitance capacitor, it must be disconnected before inspection to avoid misjudging it as a short circuit. For a single-loop short circuit, all terminal posts, series-connected appliance coils or components can be checked one by one along the line. When multiple parallel lines have a short circuit, the "disconnect one by one method" can be used to find the branch where the short circuit occurs. The short circuit fault inspection steps require attention to the precautions for short circuit fault detection: during measurement, the multimeter should be set to the R×1 range, and the normal resistance value of the line under test should be referenced to ensure accuracy; if the line contains a large-capacitance capacitor, it must be disconnected before inspection to prevent the charging current from being misjudged as a short circuit; when the circuit appears to be connected but is not, an insulation resistance tester can be used as an auxiliary judgment, and a zero indication means a short circuit exists; lines containing electronic equipment must strictly not use an insulation resistance tester, to avoid high voltage damaging components; when multiple parallel lines have a short circuit, the disconnect one by one method should be used to locate the branch where the short circuit occurs.

A line open circuit fault is manifested as normal power supply voltage and a good switch, but after closing, the appliance motor does not operate and the lamps do not light. Its causes include fuse element blowing or loose screws or detached nuts at wire joints, poor contact of contactor contacts, damage to the changeover switch or non-reset of protective appliance contacts, conductor breakage, breakage by foreign objects, or internal equipment failures such as a burnt-out filament or coil open circuit. Blowing of the line fuse element will cause a line open circuit fault; loose screws or detached nuts at wire joints will cause a line open circuit fault; poor contact of line contactor contacts will cause a line open circuit fault; conductor breakage in the wire will cause a line open circuit fault; damage or poor contact of the changeover switch will cause a line open circuit fault; the line being broken by a foreign object will cause a line open circuit fault; poor contact or non-reset of the contacts of protective appliances will cause a line open circuit fault.

In the control circuit of the AC boat davit, the forward contactor KMF not operating indicates an open circuit fault; during live inspection, if the multimeter connected across the two ends of a component displays the power supply voltage, then the interior of that component is open-circuited.

There are many causes of line open circuit faults, which can be summarized into several categories.

The first category is blowing of the line fuse element. Under the long-term action of power supply surge current, the fuse element may blow under non-short-circuit fault conditions; after the fuse element blows, loads such as appliances and motors in the line will stop operating, and various lamps will not light. In the air compressor control circuit, FU provides protection during a short circuit; in the water supply circuit, the motor obtains power through FU, and FU constitutes short circuit protection. On ships, the cross method is commonly used to check FU open circuits, using the lighting and extinguishing of a test lamp to determine the open circuit point.

The second category is loose screws or detached nuts at wire joints. Loose screws are a common cause in ship electrical and mechanical equipment of reduced fastening force of connecting parts due to vibration, improper installation or aging, which in turn causes poor contact, open circuit, overheating or mechanical faults; in the fault of excessively high temperature rise of a circuit breaker, loose connecting screws of two conductive parts are one of the main causes and must be handled by tightening the screws. The vibration and swaying environment unique to ships can easily cause loosening of wiring compression screws, between cable connectors and bases, and of fixing screws inside PLC cabinets, creating hidden fault risks. In the open circuit fault of the AC boat davit control line, loose screws are one of the more common specific causes than poor contact of contacts. Loosening of fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance; poor contact can cause local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults, and can also cause random output actions; the corresponding treatment is to check the terminal wiring. In addition, loose screws can also cause the shunt trip unit to fail to trip the circuit breaker.

The third category is poor contact of line contactor contacts. Poor contact of contacts refers to an electrical fault state in which contamination, oxidation or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface leads to reduced electrical conductivity. It is one of the causes of ship electrical line open circuit faults and also one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning; methods for handling poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface, and tightening the contact and conductive plate.

The fourth category is that the conductor in the wire is broken, and the fifth category is that the line is broken by a foreign object striking it; both categories belong to the physical breakage of the line itself, and their consequence is likewise that when the power supply voltage is normal, the power supply cannot be connected after switching on, the electrical appliances, motors, etc. in the line do not operate, and various lamps do not light up.

The sixth category is that some changeover switches are damaged or have poor contact. In distribution lines, a damaged changeover switch or poor contact is one of the fault causes of an open-circuit fault; in a refrigerator, a damaged lamp switch will cause the lighting lamp to stay on continuously or not light up; for the lighting lamp fault, the maintenance method is to repair the lamp switch or directly replace it. The consequence caused by a damaged changeover switch or poor contact is manifested as: after switching on or pressing the power-on button, the power supply cannot be connected, the loads such as electrical appliances and motors in the line do not operate, and various lamps do not light up, and this fault occurs on the premise that the power supply voltage is normal and the power switch opens and closes well.

The seventh category is that the contacts of some protective electrical appliances in the line have poor contact or are not reset. Poor contact or non-reset of the contacts of protective electrical appliances will lead to an open-circuit fault of the line; its specific manifestation is that the contacts of the protective electrical appliances have poor contact, or the protective electrical appliances are not reset after operating; all the above situations will cause the circuit to be open.

The eighth category is the open-circuit fault of the equipment itself. The open-circuit fault of the equipment itself will lead to an open-circuit fault of the line; it refers to an open circuit in the conductors of the motor winding and the electrical appliance coil, the filament of some lamps being burnt out, or the coil open circuit of the ballast, etc. An open circuit in the conductors of the motor winding and the electrical appliance coil belongs to the type of open-circuit fault existing in the equipment itself. Coil open circuit refers to the fault in which the internal conductor of the electrical coil is broken, causing the circuit to be disconnected; it is common in equipment such as contactors and electromagnetic brakes; in a contactor, coil open circuit is one of the main fault causes leading to the contactor fails to pick up; the method for detecting coil open circuit is to measure the coil resistance with a multimeter after de-energizing, and judge whether it is open. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil's magnetic force to pull in or release, and used to control the contact action or braking; a jammed armature will cause the contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start; failure or defect of the armature reaction spring is one of the main causes for the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed.

For the line open-circuit fault, the corresponding inspection methods are divided into two types: live inspection of the line open-circuit fault and dead inspection of the line open-circuit fault. The live inspection of the open-circuit fault can use the voltage range of a multimeter, but its range should not be lower than the power supply voltage; a test lamp can also be used for inspection. Before inspection, confirm that the power supply voltage is normal and that the power switch has no open circuit or poor contact; close the power switch, and after measuring that the voltage is normal, the inspection can be carried out. The principle basis is: due to the line open circuit, there is no current in the circuit, and the resistors, electrical appliance coils or motor windings, etc. connected in the circuit have no voltage drop. If the voltmeter indication is the power supply voltage, it indicates that the line or component between the two test pens is open. In complex interlock lines, the armature of the electrical appliance can be manually pushed to close the contacts, so as to narrow the inspection scope; on ships, the cross method is commonly used together with a test lamp to inspect fuse open circuits. During live or dead inspection of an open-circuit fault, the armature can be manually pushed to close the contacts to narrow the inspection scope.

A multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit; it is divided into pointer type and digital type; at full scale, the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes; the MF-30 multimeter belongs to FU-related measuring instruments. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit, and a clamp-on ammeter can also be used to measure current; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open circuit in the shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect.

The inspection of an open-circuit fault is divided into two approaches: live and dead; the former corresponds to the live inspection of the line open-circuit fault, and the latter corresponds to the dead inspection of the line open-circuit fault. During the dead inspection of the line open-circuit fault, the resistance range of a multimeter is used for measurement, and the range should be selected at R×1k or R×10k, because the resistance of some components is very large, and a too-small range will make the judgment inaccurate.

During measurement, the two test pens measure the resistance across components or terminal posts along the line in sequence; if the resistance measured between the two test pens is infinite, it is determined that an open circuit exists in that section. During operation, it is forbidden to touch the metal parts of the two test pens with both hands at the same time, so as not to affect measurement accuracy.

Checking line open-circuit faults without power requires attention to several precautions, and these precautions constitute the precautions for open-circuit fault checking. The circuit being checked or the components in the circuit must not have parallel paths; otherwise R=∞ cannot be measured at the break point, and in this case one end of the component should be disconnected from the circuit before measurement. When the circuit under test contains contacts of electrical appliances, the armature must be pushed manually to close them, so as to avoid measurement errors. The range of the multimeter should be set to the R×1k or R×10k position, to avoid inaccurate judgment caused by the very large resistance of some components. When using the multimeter, the metal parts of the two test pens must not be touched with both hands at the same time, so as not to affect measurement accuracy. The measurable property of a resistor is resistance, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and the voltmeter.

In addition, broken conductors, being broken by foreign objects, or internal equipment causes such as a burnt-out filament or a coil open circuit are all among the causes.

The AC boat davit control circuit is composed of two parts, the raising circuit and the lowering circuit, connected in parallel. The raising circuit goes from the fuse through the normally closed contact of FR to point C, then through the KMF coil and two limit switches SQ in series to point D, and finally through SBP and ST back to point B of the power supply; the lowering circuit goes from the fuse through the KMR coil, the lowering interlock switch S and ST back to point B of the power supply. Both circuits return to point B of the power supply through the emergency stop button ST. In the AC boat davit control circuit, the motor may fail to start when the raising start button SBTF is pressed, and the phenomenon is that the motor does not start when the raising start button SBTF is pressed.

If it is observed that the forward contactor KMF does not operate, it indicates that an open-circuit fault exists in the control circuit. The troubleshooting steps for the AC boat davit control circuit fault are applicable to the scenario where the motor does not start when the raising start button SBTF is pressed and the forward contactor KMF does not operate: the preliminary check requires confirming that the power supply is normal and that the motor drive system is not jammed, that is, check whether the power supply is normal and whether the motor drive system is jammed; first use a test lamp to cross-check the fuse; if both fuses are normal, the open-circuit fault occurs in the subsequent line, and then check whether contacts such as FR, SQ and ST have reset or are in good contact. During live checking, the SBTF button needs to be pressed and fixed in place to prevent automatic disconnection; when using a test lamp or voltmeter for live checking, if the multimeter connected across the two ends of the KMF coil displays the power supply voltage value, it indicates an open circuit in the internal wire of the coil; if KMF is normal, the open-circuit point is between the two terminals where the multimeter indicates the power supply voltage value. Common open-circuit faults include loose screws, poor contact of contacts or open circuit of winding lead wires, among which loose screws are one of the more common specific causes than poor contact of contacts.

Line earthing fault: in a three-phase three-wire ship power network, when one point is earthed, the electrical equipment can still operate normally; if another point is earthed, a multi-point earthing indirect short circuit fault is formed. The ship power network is a component of the ship power system and usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system; after one point is earthed, the electrical equipment can still operate normally, but it needs to be eliminated in time to improve reliability. The earthing fault checking steps are: the earthed line can be easily found by means of the earth lamps on the switchboard, then the line is disconnected from the power supply, and the earthing point is found by the "progressive section reduction method"; divide the line into two parts, use the insulation resistance tester to determine the earthed line, then divide the earthed line into two parts to find the earthed part of the line, and so on, so as to find the earthing fault point; the fault point can also be found directly by checking with the earth lamps on the switchboard, switching off each equipment or lamp switch in turn, and if the brightness of the earth lamps returns to normal, the equipment is determined to be earthed.

The conventional fault diagnosis method lists observation as the first step. Before starting to look, one must first ask the operator to clarify the operating process and abnormal manifestations before and after the fault, and only after asking does one move on to observation. In the observation step, attention should be paid to abnormal phenomena, the state of parts, the state of wires, and the operating parameters of the equipment; specifically, whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded, or burnt. After observation is completed, the next step is to check the monitoring and indicating device. Maintenance personnel should be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of electrical equipment and components; the means can be summarized as asking, looking, touching, listening, and smelling. Reading diagrams is a key skill; the method of checking wires while reading diagrams must be mastered in order to analyze faults in auxiliary machine control systems; the general fault checking methods for the three conditions of short circuit, open circuit and earthing are basic skills and must be proficient. The working principles of various electrical components must also be understood, otherwise one cannot read or analyze electrical diagrams. The MF-30 multimeter is classified among instruments for uses of the FU type. Both the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter belong to multimeters.

To measure the resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor being measured must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must also be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, discharge it before measuring resistance, and measuring while energized is absolutely not allowed. Voltage can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter, and current can be measured with a multimeter, an ammeter, or a clamp-on ammeter; the clamp-on ammeter is also for measuring current. To measure current with an ammeter, the circuit must be broken and the ammeter connected in series. Measuring with a multimeter belongs to the maintenance procedure of the PLC control system, judging equipment faults by measuring voltage, current, or resistance; when measuring DC current, turn the changeover switch to the milliampere range and connect the meter head in series into the broken branch; when measuring DC voltage, place the test probes across the two ends of the component being measured, and if unsure of the range, first set it to the maximum range. The changeover switch handles two things: selecting the measurement object and selecting the range; the changeover switch used for measuring current has a transition state when switching circuits, the purpose being to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not left open.

The wattmeter contains a current coil, which is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the current of the circuit being measured. The current coil and the voltage coil each mark a corresponding terminal (such as "*"), and during measurement the current must flow in or out from that terminal at the same time. In the main circuit fault check, the state of the current coil of electrical components such as the contactor coil can be detected with a multimeter.

The fuse symbol is written as FU, and it has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions; when the power grid or electrical equipment is under overload or short circuit, the fuse element melts and automatically cuts off the circuit. It is classified as a distribution apparatus, and can maintain thermal stability and dynamic stability during a short circuit fault. On ships, checking FU for an open circuit mostly uses the cross method, judging the open circuit point by whether the test lamp lights up or goes out. In the air compressor control circuit, FU provides protection during a short circuit; in the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line through FU. If the fuse element is subjected to the surge current of the power supply for a long time, it may also blow under non-short-circuit faults; the typical manifestation of a short circuit fault in the control circuit is that the fuse element blows.

The contactor is responsible for controlling the motor in the ship's power system; it is a low-voltage control apparatus used in electric drive systems, with high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size. The contactor is composed of an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil. The main contacts connect or break the main circuit current, and their closed state directly determines whether the motor can run; contactor maintenance is for the contactor, and circuit breaker maintenance is for the circuit breaker. When the motor is overloaded, the thermal relay FR operates, breaking the control circuit, and the contactor KM loses power and stops the machine. The transistor relay for motor overload protection converts power into voltage, satisfying the relationship U=KP; the fuse can only provide short circuit protection for the motor and is not suitable for overload protection; in a refrigeration system, charging too much refrigerant causes excessively high pressure and too heavy a load, which can also cause motor overload.

The marine motor contains windings, which are wound from enameled wire and installed in the motor or transformer to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; a partial short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating in AC motors; the winding insulation of a marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proofing, mildew-proofing and salt-oil-mist-proofing, and be oil-resistant. In the main circuit of a DC drive system there are many resistors and electrical components and many wiring terminals, so inspection is relatively complicated; an electrical component fault is one of the common faults of the electrical parts of the main engine remote control system.

The manifestation of a short circuit in the control circuit is fuse blowing; the inspection steps are: first disconnect the control circuit from the power supply, then carefully examine the circuit for abnormal conditions. A large current generally flows through the short-circuit point, which may leave scorch marks; during inspection, first determine which parallel branch the short circuit is on, then use a multimeter to check the contactor coil, and at the same time check whether there is dirt or fallen metal parts between the terminals. A short circuit in the control circuit may occur in the AC boat hoist control circuit, and a control circuit short circuit corresponds to the control circuit short circuit inspection steps.

When the start button SBT is pressed, contactor KMF operates but the motor does not start; this phenomenon corresponds to the main circuit fault inspection steps. When the power supply voltage and the main circuit fuse or circuit breaker are normal, this phenomenon indicates that there may be an open-circuit fault in the main circuit wiring. For inspection, first cut off the power supply, and use a multimeter to test whether the heating element of the thermal relay connected in series in the main circuit is open-circuited; if the heating element is normal, test at the power supply knife switch which phase is not conducting, and push the contactor armature by hand to close the main contact, so as to locate the open-circuit point. These steps are applicable to the scenario where the contactor operates when the start button is pressed but the motor does not start and the power supply voltage is normal; before inspection, confirm that the motor winding has no fault and that the main circuit fuse or circuit breaker is normal; if the heating element is normal, test at the power supply knife switch which phase is not conducting to determine the open-circuit phase; during measurement, push the contactor armature by hand to close the main contact to simulate the working state; after finding the open-circuit phase, use the aforementioned method (sectional measurement) to find the specific open-circuit point.

The air compressor control circuit is divided into the main circuit and the control circuit; the main circuit includes contactor KM, thermal relay FR, transformer T and fuse FU; the control circuit includes changeover switch SC, buttons SBT1, SBT2, SBP1, SBP2, pressure relays KP1, KP2, solenoid valve YV and indicator lamp HL. When changeover switch SC is turned to the manual position, the air compressor is controlled by the buttons; when turned to the automatic position, the air compressor is controlled by the pressure relay.

Contactor KM is the power contactor; when it is closed, the motor starts, and when it is opened, the motor stops; thermal relay FR operates when the motor is overloaded, cutting off the control circuit and stopping the main contactor KM; transformer T isolates the main circuit from the control circuit; fuse FU provides protection when the circuit is short-circuited. The air compressor control circuit belongs to the AC boat hoist control circuit and includes starter box maintenance; faults that may occur include failure to start, the motor stopping immediately after the start button SBT resets, sudden stopping of the motor during operation, loud noise from the starter box after starting, the indicator lamp not lighting, and early changeover. The pressure relay takes pressure as its input signal, and its sensing element is an air bag; it is used for automatic control and protection of marine boilers, air compressors and pump sets, controls the starting and stopping of the motor through high-pressure and low-pressure contacts in the air compressor automatic control system, and serves as a control device in auxiliary boilers to automatically control steam pressure.

The ability to read diagrams is the foundation for maintenance personnel to carry out fault analysis of auxiliary machine control systems, and the method of checking wiring while reading diagrams especially needs to be mastered proficiently. At the same time, the general inspection methods for the three common faults of short circuit, open circuit and earthing are also basic skills that electrical maintenance personnel must master. Maintenance personnel should be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of the electrical components of the electrical equipment, and understand the fault symptom by means of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, so as to make a preliminary judgment. The prerequisite for understanding and analyzing electrical diagrams is to understand the working principles of various electrical components, so knowledge of the electrical components themselves is indispensable. In a DC drive system, there are a relatively large number of resistors and electrical components in the main circuit and also many wiring terminals, so inspection is relatively complicated.

The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch, used for auxiliary control, and is also one of the main components of the contactor, undertaking functions such as control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection. The main switch is one of the carriers of the auxiliary contact, and the main components of the generator main switch also include the auxiliary contact.

The thermal relay is a protective relay with a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors; it belongs to thermal relays classified by sensing element, and its sensing part is the bimetallic strip. Thermal relays are used in large quantities on ships, and generally the overload protection task of small motors is completed by them. The symbol of the fuse is FU; the fuse corresponds to FU and serves as a protective element in circuit diagrams, with the graphical symbol identified as FU. In the air compressor control circuit, FU plays a protective role in the event of a short circuit;

The automatic water supply control circuit consists of the main circuit, the water level control circuit, the motor start-stop control circuit, the single-phase bridge rectifier circuit and the sound-light-electric signal circuit; it belongs to the category of AC boat davit control circuits and is a marine auxiliary machinery control circuit with functions of automatic water level control, motor protection and sound-light display. In its main circuit, the motor M obtains power through the thermal relay FR, the contactor KM, the fuse FU and the switch QS; when QS is closed, the contactor KM closes to make the motor run, and KM opens to make the motor stop. Besides automatic water level control, this circuit also has complete motor protection and sound and light display functions. The water level control circuit is composed of the transistor VT1 and others, and is a typical transistor switching circuit; when the base of VT1 obtains a bias voltage and saturates and conducts, the relay K1 is energized and operates, and when the base of VT1 loses the bias voltage and cuts off, the relay K1 is de-energized and released to perform the control function. In the automatic water tank water level control circuit, the potentiometer RP1 provides base bias current for the transistor VT1.

The potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes with the rotation of the shaft; it is generally considered to be manually adjustable, and the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance, used for bridge balancing; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by the potentiometer R driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R′ driven by the motor M changes accordingly.

The automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve and a potentiometer. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel oil circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control the water mist fire extinguishing zone. In the air compressor system, the solenoid valve is controlled by the normally closed contact of the contactor and opens when the machine stops to release residual air. In the burner ignition program, the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that oil enters the oil nozzle and is sprayed; its purpose is to control the on-off of the fuel oil, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit during ignition so that oil enters the oil nozzle and is sprayed.

The solenoid valve drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge.

A diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity, commonly represented by VD in circuits, used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite. Diodes can be divided by function into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), etc.; diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The diode detection procedure applies to diodes. A transistor contains two PN junctions inside and has current amplification capability, and is divided into NPN type and PNP type; in circuits it is commonly represented by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17 representing the transistor numbered 17; main models include A92, 9015 (PNP type) and A42, 9014, 9018, etc. (NPN type). Transistors are divided into two types, NPN type and PNP type, and their operating characteristics can complement each other, such as the complementary pair in an OTL circuit. Transistor faults occur in transistors, and transistor faults belong to problems under the category of transistors. Marine electrical equipment uses diodes and also uses transistors.

The function of capacitance is charging and discharging; its earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors can be measured. The measurable property of a resistor is resistance, and the measuring tool is a multimeter.

In use, a multimeter can measure resistance, voltage, capacitance, diodes and transistors.

In the ship auxiliary machinery electrical system, the maintenance work of the single-speed drive control system first requires facing the measurement and judgment of various electrical parameters. Voltage, as a basic measurable property, its value can be obtained by a multimeter or a voltmeter; current also belongs to measurable electrical quantities, and the measuring tools include a multimeter, an ammeter and a clamp-on ammeter, among which the clamp-on ammeter is used for measuring current without interrupting the power supply. The detection results of these electrical quantities are an important basis for understanding the operating state of the equipment and judging the fault location.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control the motor in the ship power system, belongs to low-voltage control electrical appliances, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. The power of various auxiliary machinery on board is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors, so the consumption of contactors is very large. The contactor is composed of multiple components, including the arc chute, main contact, core and coil. The arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the contact breaks; the installation should be firm, the number of arc chute grids must not be insufficient, and if rupture, defect or severe carbonization occurs it should be replaced in time; when the grids are severely burnt, deformed or loose, a new chute should also be replaced. The main contact is used to connect or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor. Silver main contacts should not be rubbed with abrasive cloth; they should be decontaminated with a dry cloth or cleaning agent, and applying lubricating oil is prohibited to prevent poor contact; if copper main contacts discolor or emit a burnt smell, it indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel need to be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the three-phase main contacts wear unevenly, the clearance can be adjusted by bending the moving contact bridge arm, and after dressing, synchronous contact of the three phases must be ensured; in the forward-reverse drive system, poorly maintained main contacts are prone to burning, overheating or even welding shut and failing to break due to frequent commutation; when the main contacts are overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected for replacement.

The core is the magnetic conductive component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil, and can serve as a reference point during insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in the through-type current transformer, the large current conductor under test is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil's magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start, while failure or defect of the armature reaction spring is one of the main reasons why the contactor does not release or releases slowly after the stop button is pressed. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current, and a KM coil fault is one of the direct reasons causing the contactor armature to fail to close and the motor to fail to start; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

The item of contactor maintenance applies to the contactor, and its content covers the inspection and maintenance of the above-mentioned components, and is the basis for ensuring reliable operation of the contactor.

Starting box maintenance is a maintenance item of regular rust removal, contact maintenance and safety inspection for the starting box; the air compressor control circuit includes the link of starting box maintenance. Before sailing, the starting boxes of stopped or standby equipment should be checked, and when docking, the starting box of the main engine service pump shaft should be checked. During maintenance, the power supply must be cut off, and a "Switching On Strictly Prohibited" warning sign must be hung at the distant switch. Use abrasive cloth or a scraper for rust removal; scraping and grinding should remove oxides as much as possible without grinding away metal; for surfaces of parts that are non-conductive and not subject to friction, vaseline or grease may be applied after scraping and grinding; when the anti-rust layer on painted parts peels off, anti-rust paint may be applied after rust removal, but painting on terminal posts, smooth surfaces in frictional contact, threads, springs, etc. is prohibited. The contact surfaces of the contacts must be clean and expose a metallic luster, and the initial and final pressures and overtravel should meet the specifications; fine files or glass abrasive cloth may be used to rub off oxides on the contacts, and emery cloth is prohibited.

During acceptance of the starting box, if the deviation of the factory-set value of the protective device is too large, readjustment should be carried out.

In the single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control system, common faults can be classified into two major categories, namely control system faults and motor internal faults. Motor internal faults refer to faults occurring in internal components such as the motor stator winding and bearing, which will cause the motor fails to start, automatic start failure, motor overheating or even burning out, and the phenomenon of excessively high temperature rise will also occur; its maintenance method is usually referred to elsewhere and will not be repeated here. The fault symptoms of the control system include failure to start of the system, the motor stopping immediately after the start button SBT resets, sudden stop of the motor during operation, loud noise of the starting box after starting, and the indicator light not lighting up, etc.

The failure to start of the system is one of the common faults of the single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control system, and its maintenance method is referred to elsewhere. When the thermal relay FR does not operate and the motor suddenly stops, troubleshoot according to this fault. There are various causes of failure to start: the power supply not being connected will cause failure to start, incorrect wiring of the control equipment will cause failure to start, undervoltage will cause failure to start, short circuit to earthing between phases of the stator winding, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start, and excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer will also cause failure to start.

For these causes, the corresponding handling methods are: check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find out the short circuit or open circuit part and repair it, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer, and if the motor can run normally, check the reducer part. In addition, poor contact will cause random output action, and at this time the terminal wiring should be checked; situations such as excessive reaction spring force, failure of the motor operating positioning switch, too large re-tripping contact surface, incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, and too large reaction spring force all need to be handled by readjustment.

The phenomenon that the motor stops immediately after the start button SBT resets is manifested as the motor running when the start button SBT is pressed and the motor stopping immediately after release and reset; this fault is classified as a control system fault rather than a motor internal fault, and special maintenance treatment is required for this phenomenon in ship electrical maintenance. The cause of this fault is that the self-holding auxiliary contact KM connected in parallel across both ends of the button SBT loses its function; this contact is specifically the self-holding brush contact KM1 connected in parallel across both ends of the button SBT, and during maintenance it is necessary to check whether the KM1 contact is intact, whether the lead is loose, and whether the contact is good.

If FR does not operate and the motor suddenly stops, its fault maintenance method is the same as that for the failure to start of the system.

Sudden stop of the motor during operation is a common motor fault symptom in the single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control system, manifested as the motor suddenly stopping during operation after starting, and the operation of the thermal relay FR is the cause of this phenomenon. It is normal for FR to operate when the motor heats up or is overloaded, and the load should be reduced, FR should be reset, and the motor restarted; if the motor does not heat up and shows no sign of overload while FR operates, it is abnormal operation, and the setting value of FR needs to be readjusted, or FR itself is damaged and needs to be replaced, and the setting value readjusted.

Loud noise of the starting box after starting is one of the common control system faults of the single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control system; the noise inside the starting box is generated by the contactor, and its maintenance method is referred to elsewhere.

The indicator light not lighting up is likewise one of the common faults of the single-speed non-reversible direct-start drive control system; it is a series functional logic event composed of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact. As long as one of the above four components fails, the event of the indicator light not lighting up will inevitably occur; that is, if one of the functional logic event composed of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact fails, it will cause the indicator light not to light up, so during maintenance the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact must be checked separately. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch, used for auxiliary control; as a series system element, its failure will cause the fault of the indicator light not lighting up; in the motor forward rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize the self-locking of the contactor coil. In the single-speed reversible drive system, the fault checking steps and methods for the indicator light not lighting up are the same as those for the non-reversible starting box; if this fault exists in both forward and reverse states, the common parts such as the power supply and thermal relay should be checked.

In the electrical maintenance of refrigeration and cold-storage equipment, phenomena such as relatively large temperature changes, failure to defrost automatically, and large temperature variations inside the box are also encountered. Relatively large temperature changes manifest as large or high fluctuations in room temperature, which may be caused by the external environment, the refrigeration system, or the electrical control. External high temperatures, such as high seawater temperature, will affect the refrigeration effect and cause the room temperature to rise; this fault is easily triggered when a ship passes through high-temperature sea areas such as the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf in summer. Failure to defrost automatically specifically refers to the evaporator of the LAKEN5BD refrigerated container being unable to execute the automatic defrosting program; normal defrosting is initiated by the frost-thickness microswitch 63DA on the evaporator. Large temperature variations inside the box are mainly caused by abnormal operation of the electronic temperature controller; during maintenance, check whether the temperature-sensing element is intact.

The changeover-type faults that occur during operation of the single-speed drive control system are concentrated in three forms: early changeover, late changeover, and failure to change over, all three of which are closely related to the operating conditions of the time relay KT, the contactor KM2, and their coil circuits. As for early changeover, its direct consequence is that an excessively large second inrush current is generated when the motor starts; this current acts on the motor itself and further impacts the power grid. There are two causes of early changeover: first, the delay time of the time relay KT is too short; second, the motor is difficult to start and the starting time is too long. When troubleshooting, one should not rush to make adjustments; instead, one should first turn the motor shaft by hand and check whether the resistance torque is too large, so as to determine whether the problem is on the load side or the control parameter side. Only if inspection confirms that the delay is too short may the time relay knob be adjusted to increase the delay; if it is confirmed that the cause is difficulty in starting the motor, it is forbidden to directly adjust the time relay delay knob, otherwise it will only conceal the real mechanical or load defect. The above early changeover phenomenon occurs in the air compressor control circuit, that is, the air compressor control circuit will experience early changeover.

Late changeover is another kind of timing deviation. Although it reduces the impact on the power grid, it prolongs the starting time of the motor, causing the motor to operate in an undervoltage state and thereby causing the motor to heat up. To address this phenomenon, the measure is to adjust the time relay delay and reduce the delay time.

Compared with early changeover, the adjustment direction for late changeover is exactly the opposite, so determining which category the fault belongs to is a necessary prerequisite before taking action. Late changeover also occurs in the air compressor control circuit, that is, the air compressor control circuit will experience late changeover.

The consequences of failure to change over are more serious than the previous two. It first causes the machinery driven by the motor to fail to work normally, and at the same time causes the motor to overheat, after which the thermal protection relay operates; if the system uses autotransformer reduced-voltage starting, failure to change over will also cause the autotransformer coil to burn out. This fault is mostly caused by faults in the time relay KT and the contactor KM2 themselves and faults in their coil circuits; that is, faults in the time relay KT and the contactor KM2 themselves and faults in their coil circuits are the direct causes of failure to change over. Whether the starting control has successfully changed over can be indicated by the indicator lamp not lighting or the audible signal not stopping. During troubleshooting, focus on checking the time relay KT, the contactor KM2 themselves, and their coil circuits, rather than only looking at the main circuit. The phenomenon of failure to change over also occurs in the air compressor control circuit, that is, the air compressor control circuit will experience failure to change over.

The indicator lamp not lighting is itself also one of the common faults of the single-speed non-reversing direct-on-line starting drive control system; the air compressor control circuit will experience the indicator lamp not lighting.

The motor fails to start is another type of fault that requires systematic troubleshooting. Power supply problems, mechanical problems, excessive load, and motor internal fault can all cause the motor to fail to start. Specifically for the phenomenon of failure to start, its causes include the power supply not being connected, incorrect wiring of the control equipment, undervoltage, short circuit to earth between phases of the stator winding, incorrect wiring, stator winding short circuit, and excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer. The corresponding measures are: check the switch, fuse, and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage and, if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; for the fault of the motor fails to start, one should also check the motor internal fault, that is, the motor fails to start corresponds to the troubleshooting direction of checking the motor internal fault.

In this troubleshooting process, current, voltage and resistance are three basic measurable quantities: a multimeter, an ammeter and a clamp-on ammeter can be used to measure current values, a multimeter and a voltmeter to measure voltage values, and a multimeter to measure resistance values. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after the circuit is disconnected; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system, and partial short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes leading to overcurrent and overheating of the AC motor, so the measurement results of the above electrical quantities have direct reference value for determining the fault location. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; its coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start.

The time relay often appears in circuits with symbols such as KT, SJ and SL, and is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship's power system. The current relay is an electromagnetic relay classified according to the nature of the input signal; its coil carries the electrical quantity, and its structure is basically similar to that of the contactor; in the AC three-speed electric windlass, it picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%. The symbol of the fuse is FU, and it has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions; when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or the electrical equipment, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; the thermal relay uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and is mainly used for overload protection of small motors on ships, and is used in large quantities on board. When the motor suddenly stops due to abnormal operation of the thermal relay, its setting value needs readjustment.

The air compressor control circuit includes the acceptance after overhaul of the starting box. The acceptance after overhaul of the starting box applies to acceptance after overhaul and before new installation of reversible or non-reversible starting boxes. The appearance check requires that the paint quality of the starting box shell and surface meet the requirements, all fixing screws are tightened, the earthing screw has a red mark, and the watertight condition meets the regulations; the electrical circuits in the box must fully conform to the schematic diagram and wiring diagram, and all electrical appliances and components are intact and correctly installed; pushing the movable parts by hand should be flexible without jamming, and the three-phase contacts must contact well at the same time; use a 500V insulation resistance tester to measure the insulation resistance to earth, which shall not be less than 2MΩ; when the setting values of the thermal relay, overcurrent relay and time relay deviate too much, readjustment is required. The insulation resistance tester, also called the megohmmeter, consists of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is divided according to the highest voltage generated by the hand-cranked generator into specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V and 2500V.

The multimeter includes a changeover switch; the changeover switch is used to select the measurement object and select the range, and on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set working states and issue operating commands; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The shaft is used to transmit torque and rotational motion; the movable parts of the two units of the electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch is also assembled from the contact system, operating handle, shaft and panel by bolts.

In the maintenance of the single-speed drive control system, the conventional fault diagnosis method takes observation as the starting step. The objects of observation cover abnormal phenomena, part conditions, wire conditions and equipment operating parameters, that is, checking whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt.

In instrument measurement, the insulation resistance tester is also called a megohmmeter; the hand-cranked generator and the moving-coil ratio meter together form its main body, and the panel is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G. The insulation resistance tester contains a hand-cranked generator and also contains a moving-coil ratio meter; inside it, the voltage circuit and the current circuit each have one measuring coil, and whether the relative positions of these two coils are accurate needs to be checked. Classified by the highest voltage the hand-cranked generator can produce, insulation resistance testers have specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V and 2500V. When measuring the insulation resistance of an electrical equipment coil to ground, terminal post E can be connected to the core. If there is capacitance in the circuit, discharge it before measuring resistance; live measurement is absolutely not permitted. Current values can likewise be measured with a multimeter, and can also be measured with an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter. When measuring current with an ammeter, the circuit must be broken and the ammeter connected in series. The clamp-on ammeter is composed of a current transformer and an ammeter, and works on the principle of the single-turn through-type current transformer; the conductor under test is equivalent to the primary winding, and its structure is a current transformer with an openable core plus an ammeter connected to it, so the circuit need not be cut during measurement. The quantity measured by the clamp-on ammeter is current; it is used to check the starting current and three-phase balance of a motor, and the range selected must be greater than 7 times the rated current.

The symbol corresponding to the fuse is FU; it undertakes the two functions of overload protection and short circuit protection. When overload or short circuit occurs in the power grid or electrical equipment, the fuse element melts and the circuit is automatically cut off. The fuse belongs to distribution apparatus; when a short circuit fault occurs it can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability. The RL93 series is of spiral structure, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for overload or short circuit protection of circuits. The fuse element is a component part of the fuse; in lighting and electric heating circuits, the rated current of the fuse element must be greater than or equal to the total load rated current; when a single asynchronous motor is started directly, the rated current of the fuse element is taken as 1.5~2 times the motor rated current; for motor circuits with light load and infrequent starting, the rated current of the fuse element is taken as 2.5~4 times the motor rated current.

The contactor is responsible for controlling motors in the ship power system; it is a low-voltage control apparatus, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, with high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size. The contactor contains an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin; it passes direct current and blocks alternating current; a fault in the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor being unable to start. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic part in the electromagnetic mechanism, pulled in or released by the coil's magnetic force, used to control contact action or braking; if the armature is stuck, the contactor KM cannot close, and the motor cannot be energized and thus cannot start; the shading coil is mounted on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core, is a copper ring-shaped part, and its function is to eliminate armature vibration noise; once the shading coil breaks or falls off, the AC electromagnet will emit relatively loud noise; after damage it can be repaired by copper welding, or the shading coil can be replaced directly.

The external wiring must also be checked. Whether the contactor operates flexibly must be carefully checked; if the contactor armature is obstructed and cannot pull in properly, the coil current will be too large and burn out the coil. Use a 500V insulation resistance tester to measure the insulation resistance. When the driven machinery is not allowed to reverse, the coupling must be disconnected to start the motor so as to confirm the direction of rotation. Use a clamp-on ammeter to detect the starting current; the range should be selected at more than 7 times the rated current. During the reduced-voltage starting commissioning, verify whether the changeover is accurate and detect the balance of the three-phase current. If the contactor noise is too loud, check the cleanliness of the core mating surface and the state of the shading coil. During the load test, measure the motor current under rated load and, if necessary, adjust the setting values of the protective devices. After 2 hours of rated operation, measure the hot insulation resistance of the starting box and record the data.

The automatic pump control system consists of the control circuit, motor and main power supply, and undertakes tasks such as remote-control starting and stopping, automatic starting and automatic changeover, sequential starting and alarming in ship auxiliary machinery. It is generally required that the system can perform remote-control starting and stopping of each group of pumps in the central control room; when in the automatic control state, the pumps of the same group can be automatically changed over; after the power grid loses power and power supply is restored, the pumps of each group are automatically restarted one by one in sequence according to the primary and secondary relationship. The system should also be provided with alarms and support local control of the pumps. During daily maintenance, the setting values of the time relay and pressure relay need to be checked regularly; before sailing, check whether the automatic changeover operation is normal and whether the remote-control function is available. The automatic control system of the ship pump box also has the functions of remote-control starting and stopping, automatic changeover, sequential starting and alarming.

The time relay, pressure relay, voltage relay and contactor all belong to the electrical equipment used for control or protection in the ship power system. The time relay often appears in circuits with text symbols such as KT, SJ and SL. The pressure relay is a non-electrical relay with pressure as the input signal; its sensing element is an air bag and its actuating part is a contact, and it is used for the automatic control and protection of ship boilers, air compressors and pump groups; in auxiliary boilers it serves as a control device for automatically controlling steam pressure; in the fuel pump automatic control system, the pressure relay detects the system pressure to trigger the automatic changeover of the pump and alarming. The voltage relay is classified according to the nature of the input signal and belongs to the electromagnetic relay; it realizes the control or protection function through the voltage change induced by the coil, and its coil uses the electrical quantity, namely voltage, as the excitation input quantity;

When the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced; winding it by oneself will affect the operating value due to inaccurate number of turns. The contactor is a low-voltage control device, mainly used to control the motor in the electric drive system; it has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size, and is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of almost all kinds of auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors; the contactor consists of an arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance is carried out on these parts. The circuit breaker is a low-voltage power distribution device, divided into the frame type and the molded-case type, and has both switching and protection functions; it can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during a short circuit fault. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid; circuit breaker maintenance is carried out according to the above characteristics.

The changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts; its functions include selecting the measurement object and selecting the range; on the main switchboard, the changeover switch is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The multimeter contains a changeover switch internally, and with it uses the measurement functions of resistance, voltage, current, capacitance and diode, etc. The clamp-on ammeter is used with current as the measurement object, and the conductor need not be disconnected during measurement. The voltage transformer corresponds to the symbol TV and is used to transform the voltage ratio; the secondary side voltage is 100V, and one end of its secondary side is earthed; it belongs to instrument transformers and has the nature of a voltage source; the standard secondary voltage is usually 100V or 110V, and its working principle is the same as that of the transformer, but its internal resistance is extremely small, and the output voltage hardly changes with the load, so it is equivalent to a no-load transformer during operation; the secondary side must not be short-circuited, and a fuse must be installed on the primary side for short circuit protection. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA and has the nature of a current source; its internal resistance is extremely large, and the standard secondary current is 5A or 1A; the load current I flows through its primary side, is transformed into the secondary current and then connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements; the secondary side must not be open-circuited, the terminals of the externally connected ammeter must have a short-circuit connecting piece, and it may be disconnected only after the wiring has been checked.

The capacitance is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle; its characteristic is that it blocks direct current and passes alternating current; in circuit diagrams it is usually represented by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; its hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC); its measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. The measurable property of the resistor is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; in the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in marine electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree, and overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems. The measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; the diode has unidirectional conductivity, with a small conducting resistance under forward voltage and cutoff under reverse voltage; its measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance; in circuits it is commonly denoted by VD and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; by function it can be divided into rectifier diodes such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, Schottky diodes such as BAT85, as well as light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes, etc.; when marine electrical equipment uses diodes, the above categories are involved, and the diode detection steps are applicable to diodes.
