The potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes as the shaft rotates; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component and is generally considered manually adjustable; in the auxiliary boiler control circuit, potentiometers W1 and W2 are used to adjust the delay or sensitivity of the time relay; in automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by the potentiometer R driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R′ driven by the motor M changes accordingly; the automatic oil-fired boiler contains such potentiometers. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start; the insulation resistance tester contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked. Damage to the coil of the starting relay or poor contact of its contacts will cause the motor not to start and to make no sound after the refrigerator is energized, while sticking of the contacts may cause the refrigerator motor to suddenly stop during starting or running; its troubleshooting methods include repairing or replacing the coil, and repairing or replacing the stuck contacts.

The pump automatic control system will suffer automatic start failure, that is, the pump auxiliary cannot start automatically. Main power supply faults, motor internal faults and failure of control system components will all lead to automatic start failure. The causes of main power supply faults include fuse blowing of RD, K not closing and the line not being supplied with power; when analyzing automatic start failure, main power supply faults are considered in parallel with motor and control system component faults; main power supply faults are also one of the top events in the fault tree leading to the fuel pump failing to switch over automatically, and one of the causes of the fuel pump unit failing to start automatically, and in the fault tree they belong to one of the top-level branches of automatic start failure. Main power supply faults will also cause neither ahead nor astern starting to be possible when the master controller handle is moved, that is, once problems such as fuse blowing of RD on the main power supply side, K not closing or the line not being supplied with power occur, neither the ahead nor the astern direction can establish a starting process after the master controller handle is operated.

During maintenance it is assumed that the wiring connections are intact and there is no short circuit or open circuit; the fault analysis covers three aspects: the main power supply, the motor and the control system components. The motor internal fault is the cause of the pump auxiliary unit failing to start automatically, and it must be checked after eliminating faults of the main power supply and control elements; in the fault tree of failure to switch over automatically, it appears as a branch cause of "no power to the motor", and is also one of the basic events of the fault tree causing the unit to fail to switch over automatically. The motor internal fault refers to faults occurring in internal components of the motor such as the stator winding and bearing, which will cause the motor to fail to start, low speed or excessive temperature rise; it is one of the eight causes in the fault tree of the three-phase asynchronous motor failing to start, and is also one of the eight possible causes of motor speed low after starting; in the ship's single-speed non-reversible direct-on-line starting control system it belongs to one of the two major categories of common faults, and is one of the direct causes of the single-speed non-reversible AC electric drive system failing to start; the motor internal fault will cause the motor to fail to start, and will also cause the motor to overheat or even burn out.

The specific causes of control system component failure include C not operating, J0 not operating, the WH changeover switch not being placed in the automatic start position, the run/standby selector switch KK not being closed, J2 not operating, the contact not being closed, ZL having no DC voltage output, and open-circuit faults existing in J2 itself and the components related to the J2 coil circuit. C not operating will cause the pump auxiliary to fail to start automatically, the cause being C itself being faulty or J0 not operating; the causes of J0 not operating include J0 itself being faulty, the WH switch not being placed in the automatic position or the KK switch not being closed; the causes of the J2 contact not being closed include J2 itself being faulty, the coil circuit being open or a control power supply fault; the J2 contact not being closed or J2 itself being faulty can lead to automatic start failure, the J3 normally closed contact being open is one of the possible fault sources, and M1 being open or SJ being open can cause automatic start failure.

This fault analysis excludes faults of the main power supply and the motor itself, and focuses on the logic elements of the control system.

The pump automatic control system will also have fault symptoms such as failure to switch over automatically, failure to start automatically in sequence, and failure of the unit to start and run during manual operation. Power supply not being connected, incorrect wiring of control equipment, undervoltage, short circuit and earthing between phases of the stator winding, incorrect wiring, stator winding short circuit, as well as excessive load or the brake not being released and a fault in the reduction gearbox, will all cause failure to start; for failure to start, check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point. In the main engine remote control system, a power supply fault is one of the main causes on the main power supply side of the unit failing to start automatically; a power supply fault will also cause the motor to overheat, PLC system faults and main engine remote control failure; in the AC electric drive system, a power supply fault is one of the direct causes of the motor overcurrent and thus overheating; in the PLC control system, the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, so on board the strategy of overall replacement is usually adopted.

Fault tree analysis uses a fault tree. A fault tree is a connected logic tree that contains no closed loops, using graphical symbols to represent the logical combinations among various events that cause an undesired event of the system; its structure is a logic tree, developing downward from the tree root of the top event, with branches representing fault events and nodes representing logical relationships, the most commonly used logical relationships being the AND relationship and the OR relationship. A fault tree contains the top event, intermediate events and basic events. When building a fault tree, electrical equipment faults such as motor fails to start are often selected as the top event, and the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as the power supply being normal and the control circuit being normal.

Automatic start failure is manifested as the pump auxiliary failing to start automatically, and its fault analysis covers three aspects: the main power supply, the motor and the control system components. A main power supply fault is one of the causes of the fuel pump unit failing to start automatically, with specific manifestations including RD fuse blowing, K not being closed and the line not being supplied with power; in the fault tree it is one of the top-level branches of automatic start failure. The motor internal fault will likewise lead to automatic start failure, and control system component failure is also one of the parallel causes. During maintenance it is assumed that the wiring connections are intact and there is no short circuit or open circuit, and on this basis the above links are checked item by item.

Failure to switch automatically is manifested as the standby pump auxiliary failing to start automatically and put into operation. Normal switching relies on the normally closed contact closing after the running pump J1 loses power to control the starting of the standby pump, so the fault causes include two aspects: the standby pump failing to start automatically, and the normally closed contact of J1 failing to close when power is lost. During judgment, the standby unit KK can be placed in the running position; if it can start, it is determined to be a fault of the running unit J1; if it still cannot start when placed in the running position, it should be checked according to the automatic start failure fault. The cause of the standby pump auxiliary failing to start automatically needs to form a complete fault tree together with the J1 normally closed contact fault; its inspection method is the same as the automatic start failure fault inspection, involving the detection of the same components, and is distinguished from the switching failure caused by the normally closed contact not closing after the running pump auxiliary J1 loses power. The normally closed contact of J1 failing to close when power is lost is one of the causes of the pump auxiliary control system failing to switch automatically; under normal logic, after J1 loses power the normally closed contact should close to control the automatic starting of the standby pump auxiliary; during maintenance, it is necessary to check whether J1 and its normally closed contact in the running pump auxiliary control system are faulty. This fault tree covers causes such as the main power supply, RD fuse blowing, WH, J2, J3 contacts and coil open circuit.

In another system, when b1 is placed in the "0" position the system is in manual mode, and automatic switching is prohibited.

Failure to start automatically in sequence is manifested as the unit failing to start and put into operation at the set delay according to the primary/secondary sequence. The sequential start function is realized under the control of delay relay SJ2 or SJ3; after the power grid is energized the unit should start and put into operation at the set delay according to the primary/secondary sequence, and a fault of delay relay SJ2 or SJ3 will cause the system to fail to start automatically in sequence. During maintenance, first check whether delay relay SJ2 operates normally; after confirming SJ2 is normal, continue troubleshooting according to the method for automatic start failure fault. A power supply fault will also cause the RUN lamp to go out; at this time the power supply should be checked. The corresponding handling methods are: check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts to find the fault point;

Check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find out the short circuit and open circuit parts and repair them, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer; if the motor can run normally, check the reducer part.

When troubleshooting the above faults, the multimeter is a commonly used tool; it can be used to measure voltage and detect diodes. A diode has unidirectional conductivity; under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage it is cut off; its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity, and it is commonly used in circuits such as rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization and polarity protection, and is commonly represented by VD in circuits. Diodes include categories such as light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes; the diode detection steps are applicable to diodes, and during detection its polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance can be measured. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment.

The contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil; contactor maintenance is applicable to contactors. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; a jammed armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failing to start; failure or damage of the armature reaction spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed. The main contact is the switching component in the contactor used to connect or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor; discoloration of the copper main contact or a burnt smell indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel need to be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the main contact has been overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected for replacement.

The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch and the contactor, used for control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection, and is also one of the main component parts of the generator main switch. In motor forward-rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize self-locking of the contactor coil. In the main/standby pump automatic switching logic, the auxiliary contact is used to cut off the circuit of the originally running unit and provide self-holding for the new unit. In the pump unit automatic switching system, the intermediate relay, after pressure is established, is energized and self-holds and prevents erroneous switching after the start delay ends; it belongs to the electromagnetic relay, its construction is similar to that of the contactor, and it is used to expand contact capacity and number of contacts and for control logic conversion, and its fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the maintenance method of the contactor. The thermal relay is a protective relay using a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small marine motors, and is used in large quantities on ships. The time relay undertakes the delay task in the control circuit, and its setting value needs to be checked periodically.

The pump automatic control system consists of the control circuit, motor, main power supply, etc., and has the functions of remote-control starting and stopping, automatic starting and automatic switching, sequential starting and alarming.

Troubleshooting of the pump automatic control system usually starts with the conventional fault diagnosis method, and the first step of this method is to use observation. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, check whether parts are jammed or damaged, whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt, and note whether operating parameters deviate from the normal range. For more complex control logic, fault tree analysis is adopted, and analysis is carried out with the aid of the fault tree as a tool. The time relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship power system, with common designations KT, SJ and SL. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker, and is the maintenance work carried out on the circuit breaker body.

The contactor contains two component parts: the main contact and the coil.

As far as the motor itself is concerned, faults in the stator winding, bearing, etc. will cause the phenomenon of excessively high temperature rise; such internal faults include stator winding and bearing damage, and are one of the direct causes of failure to start of the single-speed non-reversible AC electric drive system, and belong to one of the two common categories of faults in the single-speed non-reversible direct-on-line starting control system on ships.

The pump automatic control system may also exhibit the phenomenon that the unit cannot be started and run during manual operation, that is, in manual operation mode the pump unit cannot be started and run. During maintenance, first press the start button 1b2 and observe whether contactor 1c1 operates. If 1c1 operates and the motor hums, it indicates phase failure of the power supply or mechanical jamming of the pump shaft; when the humming is heard, the stop button should be pressed immediately to prevent the motor from being burnt out by prolonged locked-rotor operation. Power supply phase failure is a fault state in which one phase is missing from the three-phase power supply, often causing the motor to fail to start or to have abnormal speed; it will cause motor speed low after starting, and will also cause the motor temperature rise to be high; when phase failure causes locked rotor, it should be stopped immediately to prevent the motor from being burnt out by prolonged operation.

If 1c1 operates but there is no sound, it is necessary to check the closing of the main circuit contacts, motor faults and the state of thermal relay 1e. If 1c1 does not operate but intermediate relay 1d1 operates, it indicates that 1c1 itself is faulty or the 1d1 contact is not closed; this is one situation in which 1c1 does not operate. If 1c1 does not operate and 1d1 does not operate, it is necessary to check the control power supply and the components of the 1d1 coil circuit; at this time it is judged that 1d1 does not operate, and it should be checked whether there is control power supply and whether the components in the 1d1 coil circuit are intact. The case where 1d1 does not operate is different from the case where 1d1 operates but 1c1 does not operate; the latter points to a fault in 1c1 itself or the 1d1 contact not being closed. Both the case where 1c1 does not operate and the case where 1d1 does not operate will cause the unit to fail to start and run during manual operation; this phenomenon appears after the start button 1b2 is pressed, and serves as the basis for judging a main circuit or control circuit fault.

Check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately;

If the main circuit is not connected after the thermal relay is connected in, one of the causes is that the external wiring screws are not tightened; the corresponding maintenance method is to tighten the external wiring screws. Various fault symptoms may occur in the circuit breaker during operation: when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contact cannot close, that is, when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contact cannot close; in addition, there is also the case where one phase contact cannot close, the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1 h after closing, the undervoltage trip unit has noise, and the temperature rise of the circuit breaker is too high.

The electrical system of a ship's cargo winch can be divided by power supply type into two major categories: AC electric cargo winch and DC electric cargo winch, among which the AC electric cargo winch is more commonly used on ships. The AC electric cargo winch is generally driven by a squirrel-cage pole-changing variable-speed motor, with three speeds; according to the speed regulation range from medium speed to high speed, it can be divided into constant-power speed regulation and constant-torque speed regulation. Domestic systems mostly use constant-power speed regulation or derived forms, such as PHKJ-1A-H matched with a JZF-H type motor; foreign systems mostly use constant-torque speed regulation systems. Some AC electric cargo winches use three-phase wound-rotor asynchronous motors, with speed regulation by rotor series resistors or thyristors. The constant-power speed regulation system requires reliable overload protection and interlock control for two derricks at the same speed. There are many types of drive control for DC electric cargo winches, including generator-motor set drive systems, relay-contactor control systems, magnetic amplifier control systems, and AEC control systems, etc. Because DC motors have good speed regulation performance, they are often used in ship G-M systems. At present, ships generally use AC power systems, and DC electric cargo winches with relay-contactor control are no longer common.

From the perspective of mechanical structure, AC electric cargo winches include three types: double-derrick cargo winch, single-derrick cargo winch, and deck crane. The double-derrick cargo winch uses two motors to separately drive the cargo winches; the starting, speed regulation, forward and reverse rotation, and braking control of the motors are realized by the electrical control system. It has the characteristics of stable operation, low noise, compact design, and convenient operation and daily maintenance; its disadvantages are that cargo positioning and luffing are difficult, and it is convenient for remote control and automation. In the application of DC electric cargo winches, an AC motor can drive a DC generator to simultaneously supply power to the two DC motors of the double-derrick cargo winch, that is, a double-shaft output system. The single-derrick cargo winch uses three motors to separately drive the hoisting winch, luffing winch, and slewing winch; the starting, speed regulation, forward and reverse rotation, and braking of each motor are completed by their respective electrical control circuits, and it belongs to a classification form of electric cargo winches.

The hoisting mechanism, slewing mechanism, and luffing mechanism of the deck crane and their control equipment are all on the same working platform, and the winch, platform, and derrick can all rotate together about their central axis. Operation is relatively flexible, cargo handling speed is fast, and production efficiency is high, but the structure is complex and compact, and maintenance is inconvenient. The deck crane often uses a three-shaft output system in which an AC motor drives a DC generator to supply power to three DC motors; during maintenance, check whether various limit protection and alarm devices are normal.

The maintenance of the electrical system of a cargo winch involves multiple aspects. The AC electric cargo winch includes the maintenance of the electromagnetic control panel and control box, the maintenance of the master controller and cam controller, the electromagnetic brake and its maintenance, and the daily maintenance of the electrical system of the AC electric cargo winch, etc.

The first-level maintenance cycle of electromagnetic control panels and control boxes is generally once every 2 to 3 months, and the content includes removing accumulated dust and dirt from each component, checking the completeness of components such as pushbuttons, indicator lights, switches and meters, ensuring fasteners are not loose, checking and maintaining relays and contactors, ensuring mechanical and electrical interlocks are reliable, ensuring mechanical moving parts are flexible, and adding lubricating oil when necessary. The first-level maintenance of master controllers and cam controllers should be carried out once per voyage or before use, checking external devices such as handles, handwheels, indicator lights, switches and pushbuttons, verifying whether the actual position of the controller pointer matches and the positioning accuracy, cleaning the contact and cam surfaces, checking whether the internal springs are damaged or misaligned, and cleaning the arc chute; if damaged or with poor insulation it must be repaired or replaced. For master controllers using a variable resistor, the contact condition between the sliding arm and the resistor needs to be checked during second-level maintenance.

A resistor includes a variable resistor; a variable resistor is also called a potentiometer and has three pins, and the resistance value can be changed by rotating the shaft to adjust the voltage or current in the circuit, wherein the resistance between two of the pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either of the two pins changes with shaft rotation.

An electromagnetic brake is composed of an electromagnetic armature disc, springs, a moving plate, a friction plate or friction block, an end cover, etc.; it often adopts a disc-type structure and is integrated with the motor to improve watertightness and braking stability. When the coil is energized, the electromagnet pulls in and compresses the spring so that the moving plate rotates freely; when power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. The power supply of a DC electromagnetic brake must be supplied by the same power source after rectification. When the coil current is less than the holding current, the medium- and high-speed windings should be de-energized in time to prevent the load from falling.

When friction plate wear causes an excessively large gap, the braking torque decreases and the slip distance is large; when the gap is too small, the temperature of the brake rises sharply. Besides the disc type, there is also the open-type electromagnet shoe brake, which uses a lever mechanism to brake by spring tension when power is cut off. Maintenance of the electromagnetic brake is divided into multiple levels: first-level maintenance is carried out once per voyage or before use, mainly measuring the gap and adjusting it; second-level maintenance has a cycle of 3 to 6 months and requires partial disassembly and cleaning of the core attraction surface to prevent insufficient holding force or failure to release the brake caused by the core being too dirty; third-level maintenance is carried out every 3 to 4 years or during ship repair, and is handled synchronously when the motor is disassembled. The electromagnetic brake corresponds to operational contents such as the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, electromagnetic brake gap adjustment and electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment.

During maintenance and testing, the multimeter is used to measure parameters such as resistor, voltage, current and the polarity and inter-electrode resistance of the thyristor, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. The thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, and its measurable characteristics include polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode. The measuring tool for resistor is the multimeter; when measuring a resistor in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistor, and never measure with power on. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect. The measuring tools for current include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. The measuring tools for voltage include the multimeter and voltmeter; voltage is one of the meter readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree; overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system.

The contactor is an electrical device used in the ship's power system to control the motor; it belongs to the low-voltage control apparatus and features accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size, and is used in large quantities on board, because the power of almost all auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor comprises components such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil. The arc chute is used to extinguish the arc generated when the contact breaks; if it is damaged or has poor insulation, it must be repaired or replaced; when cracked, damaged or severely carbonized, it should be replaced in time; when the grid plates are severely burnt, deformed or loose, a new chute should be replaced. During the secondary maintenance of the contactor, it is necessary to check whether the non-magnetic shim, shading coil and copper sleeve are damaged; during periodic maintenance, it is necessary to confirm that the shading coil on the contactor armature is not loose or higher than the contact surface.

The shading coil is installed on the pole face of the AC electromagnet core; it is a copper ring-shaped component used to eliminate armature vibration and noise; breakage or falling off of the shading coil will cause the AC electromagnet to produce greater noise; when damaged, it can be repaired by copper welding or the shading coil can be directly replaced. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. The above inspection and maintenance contents all belong to the scope of contactor maintenance, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor body and its components such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil.

The time relay is used for control or protection in the ship's power system, with designations such as KT, SJ and SL. The thermal relay uses a bimetallic strip as the sensing element and is mainly used for overload protection of small motors on ships; it is used in large quantities on board, and generally the overload protection of small motors is accomplished by it.

The AC electric cargo winch may experience various fault symptoms during operation, including high temperature rise of the electromagnetic brake and excessively fast wear of the friction plate, as well as the electromagnetic brake failing to pull in and the motor being locked-rotor. In addition, the motor may overheat or even burn out, the control system may lose control, the motor fails to start when the master controller handle is moved to either ahead or astern, the motor starts only in ahead or only in astern when the master controller handle is moved, there is no high speed and medium speed in either ahead or astern, the cargo sliding distance is too large during braking, the motor runs single-phase, the constant-power cargo winch cannot run at high speed under light load, the electromagnetic brake fails to release, the electromagnetic brake releases immediately after pulling in, the electromagnetic brake heats up, and the friction plate wears too fast, etc.

The AC electric cargo winch is widely used on ships, and its electrical system covers different models such as the double-lever cargo winch, single-lever cargo winch and deck crane. The DC electric cargo winch is also a member of the electric cargo winch family, and its drive control scheme is often the same as that of the ship's AC electric cargo winch. Constant-torque speed control systems are mostly adopted abroad; the mooring winch has basically the same drive control scheme as the cargo winch, and mooring winches are divided into DC and AC types; at present, AC three-speed windlasses, mooring winches or G-M system windlasses and mooring winches are mostly adopted, and the drive control systems of the two are basically the same; they belong to short-time duty equipment and are allowed to start 25 times within 30 min.

Daily maintenance is divided into three parts: inspection patrol, general maintenance each voyage and periodic maintenance. The inspection patrol system should be formulated according to the type of cargo loaded and unloaded and the technical condition of the equipment, and the temperature rise of the motor and electromagnetic brake should be monitored; during operation it should not exceed the allowable temperature rise; if the motor overheats, it should be checked whether the motor ventilation and cooling system is normal, and at the same time it should be checked whether the locked-rotor of the motor and the action and release of the electromagnetic brake meet the technical requirements. If the AC electric cargo winch is improperly maintained, the motor may overheat or even burn out, and consequences such as high temperature rise of the electromagnetic brake and excessively fast wear of the friction plate may also occur.

The electromagnetic brake is an important braking component of the drive motor of deck machinery such as cargo winches and windlasses, and realizes brake release or brake application through electromagnetic pull-in and spring return. When power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. If the gap is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply. In the disc-type electromagnetic brake of deck machinery, a coil open circuit will cause the spring to push the armature back and produce braking torque. In the disc-type brake, the armature disc is pushed back by the spring and jammed between the end cover and the friction plate to produce braking torque;

Adjusting the manual release screw can limit the return stroke of the armature disc being sprung back, thereby adjusting the tightness of the brake; if the gap between the armature disc and the electromagnetic core is measured to be too large, the friction plate or block should be adjusted or replaced with a new one. When the shoe-type brake is energized, the armature pulls in and pushes the lever to lift the brake shoe and release the brake; when de-energized, braking is achieved by spring tension. In the electromagnetic shoe-type brake, when de-energized, the spring tension forces the brake shoe to grip the brake wheel tightly and brake. The surface roughness of the brake wheel is required to be not less than 3.2, the steady-state working temperature should be less than 180℃, and it is necessary to prevent erosion by oil, rain and ice and snow. The wear amount of the brake shoe must be less than 2mm; the tightness wear amount of the brake shoe of each model of traction machine should be less than 2mm, and if it exceeds the standard, the brake shoe or brake arm must be replaced; in the brake-released state, the gap between the brake shoe and the two arc surfaces of the brake wheel should be maintained at 0.1~0.3mm.

The maintenance of electromagnetic brakes is divided into three levels. The first-level maintenance is carried out every voyage or before use, mainly measuring the gap and adjusting it if necessary. The second-level maintenance cycle is 3~6 months, and its content includes partial disassembly and cleaning to prevent the core holding surface from being too dirty, which causes insufficient holding force and results in the fault of failure to release the brake or a seemingly released but not fully released brake; check whether the armature, copper sleeve and spring are deformed, and if deformed, they should be repaired or replaced; when replacing the brake plate spring, attention should be paid to the relevant assembly requirements. In an electromagnetic brake, a too dirty core holding surface will cause insufficient holding force, resulting in failure to release the brake or a seemingly released but not fully released brake. Insufficient holding force is also a fault cause that leads to welding of contactor contacts or the inability of the electromagnetic brake to release the brake, usually caused by low voltage, mechanical resistance or a dirty core; to deal with insufficient holding force of the contactor, it is necessary to check whether the power supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage and eliminate mechanical resistance.

For the electromagnetic brake, there are three corresponding maintenance procedures, namely the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, the electromagnetic brake gap adjustment and the electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment. The electromagnetic brake gap adjustment stipulates that when the friction plate or block is severely worn, the gap will be too large, and at this time the friction plate or block can only be replaced; after replacing with a new friction plate or block, if the gap is still too large, it may be that the end cover is not screwed in place or that the armature disc and the end cover have worn due to long-term friction, causing the gap to be too large. When the brake is too tight and causes the end cover temperature to rise sharply, the spring return stroke can be changed by adjusting the manual release screw; for insufficient braking caused by a large gap due to wear of the armature disc and end cover, shims need to be inserted into the spring holes; the thickness of the shims placed in each spring hole must be consistent to prevent local stress and severe heating during braking. When after replacing with a new friction plate or friction block the slip is too large and the braking torque is insufficient, the manual release screw should be unscrewed; if the slip is still too large at this time, it indicates that the working length of the spring has increased, causing insufficient spring force; at this time, take out the end cover 3 and remove the spring from the shaft for inspection. When the spring force is insufficient due to long-term working fatigue of the spring, new springs should be replaced; it is recommended to replace all of them or place old and new ones alternately and evenly.

The contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil. Coil open circuit is one of the main fault causes leading to the contactor failing to pick up; the method for detecting a coil open circuit is to measure the coil resistance with a multimeter after power-off to determine whether it is open. A stuck armature will cause the contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start; failure or damage of the armature reaction spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and its fault analysis and handling can be carried out with reference to the relevant inspection and repair methods. The intermediate relay is a type of electromagnetic relay, similar in construction to the contactor, used to expand contact capacity and number and for control logic conversion, and its fault analysis and handling can be carried out with reference to the inspection and repair methods of the contactor; in a constant-power three-speed cargo winch, when the load exceeds half load, the intermediate relay operates to cut off the high-speed winding circuit.

The marine motor includes the shaft, a mechanical transmission component; the shaft is used to transmit torque and rotational motion and is commonly found in motors, contactors and instruments; the moving parts of the two units of the electrodynamic three-phase wattmeter are fixed on the same shaft, and the total torque is the algebraic sum of the torques of the two units; the changeover switch is composed of a contact system, an operating handle, a shaft and a panel, assembled by bolts. The core is the magnetic-conducting component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as a reference point for insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of a coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in the through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor under measurement is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked.

The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the magnetic force of the coil to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking. Observation includes abnormal phenomena, part condition, conductor condition and equipment operating parameters; specifically, check whether parts are stuck or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, divided into analog and digital types, and mainly consists of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; at full scale the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. The MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter, capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A, and its panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The analog multimeter and the digital multimeter are also multimeters. The multimeter can be used to measure various electrical quantities and device parameters such as resistance, voltage, current, capacitance, diode, transistor, thyristor, photosensitive device and thermocouple.

Overheating and even burning out of the motor of an AC electric cargo winch are often not caused by a single reason. Failure of the load relay ZJ is the main cause of heavy-load overspeed operation; the domestic constant-power motor cargo winch precisely uses the load relay to prevent the speed from rising when the load exceeds half load. The original load relay ZJ has poor reliability and cannot perform its protective function well; through continuous improvement, a transistor-type load relay is now available, which has high sensitivity and is little affected by supply voltage fluctuations. If it is not discovered, adjusted and repaired in time, motor overheating will occur, and over time or with other faults the motor may be burnt out. Long-time overload and excessively high operating frequency are another cause of motor overheating: when using the cargo winch, because loading personnel find it difficult to accurately estimate the cargo weight, it is operated overloaded, and at the same time they wish to increase loading and unloading speed, so the operating frequency often exceeds 240/480/480 making operations/hour; once this limit is exceeded, the operating frequency is regarded as excessively high. In pursuit of speed and because it is difficult to accurately estimate cargo weight, loading personnel easily cause excessively high operating frequency of the cargo winch, and excessively high operating frequency is one of the main causes of motor overheating and even burning out in cargo winch motors.

Long-time overload and excessively high operating frequency likewise cause motor overheating and even burning out. In addition, motor stalling and motor internal fault also cause motor overheating and even burning out. As far as the protection links are concerned, the thermocouple in the stator slot is easily damaged before leaving the factory and cannot be repaired, resulting in poor protection reliability; the setting value of the thermal relay RJ in the main circuit is difficult to set accurately, and protection against large currents is coarse; the transistor-type load relay has high sensitivity and can replace ZJ to prevent heavy-load overspeed.

The thermocouple is often embedded in the winding end in the motor stator slot for overheating protection, but it is easily damaged before leaving the factory and cannot be repaired. Normally the resistance between the two terminal posts is zero; if infinity is measured, it indicates that the hot end is open and the thermocouple has been damaged.

The voltage relay is used for undervoltage protection in the constant-power three-speed cargo winch; after being energized, its normally open contacts close to energize the control circuit; poor contact of contacts is one of the fault causes that prevent the AC electric cargo winch from rotating in either forward or reverse. During periodic maintenance, the pick-up voltage and release voltage values of the voltage relay coil must be checked and adjusted to meet the technical requirements; when the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced, and self-winding will affect the operating values due to inaccurate number of turns. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, core and coil. Too high an operating frequency will cause the coil to overheat or burn out; when handling a contactor coil fault caused by too high an operating frequency, a contactor with a current rating one size larger should be selected as the replacement. When power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. If the gap is too small, the temperature of the brake rises sharply.

The marine motor includes bearings and windings. The bearing is used to support the rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause the motor to overheat, vibrate and produce abnormal noise; bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system and belongs to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud non-uniform noise and the feature of the bearing end cover overheating. Checking the bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition are both performed on the bearing. Generator bearing overheating and bearing overheating both correspond to replacing the bearing; replacing the bearing is directed at bearing wear, bearing damage or bearing overheating faults in equipment such as electric fans, electric drills and generators, and is used to repair the fault of slow starting and reduced speed of the electric fan caused by bearing wear, and also to eliminate the operating noise of the electric fan caused by bearing damage. The winding is the coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of the AC motor; the winding insulation of the marine motor must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture-proof, mildew-proof and salt-oil-mist-proof and be oil-resistant.

The insulation resistance tester, also called the megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is a portable instrument composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, used to measure the insulation resistance of marine electrical equipment, lines and cables. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand the equipment status; the multimeter is used for the measurement of resistance, voltage, current, transistor and thermocouple; the clamp-on ammeter is used for the measurement of current.

The transistor contains two PN junctions internally and has current amplification capability, is divided into NPN type and PNP type, and is commonly represented in circuits by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17. Main models include A92, 9015 (PNP type) and A42, 9014, 9018, etc. (NPN type). The measurable properties of the transistor include the tube type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor; marine electrical equipment uses transistors, the transistor has a transistor fault, and the transistor fault belongs to the transistor.

In the AC electric cargo winch, the electromagnetic brake is a key component related to hoisting safety, and its common faults are manifested as high temperature rise and excessively fast wear of the friction lining. The causes of this phenomenon can be found from two aspects: the control circuit and the brake itself. In terms of the control circuit, if the setting of time relay 2SJ is too short, the regenerative braking of the motor cannot take effect in time, and the speed has not yet decreased when the electromagnetic brake brakes at high speed, thereby causing the temperature rise of the brake to be high and the wear of the friction lining to accelerate. If the discharge resistor of the electromagnetic brake coil circuit is too large and discharges too fast, high-speed braking will likewise occur, with consequences similar to too short a setting of 2SJ. If the resistance of the economy resistor is too large or it is connected in too early, the brake will be in a state of seeming to open but not opening, directly causing accelerated wear of the friction lining. After the diode in the discharge circuit of the brake coil breaks down, the discharge resistor becomes a shunt circuit in the circuit, which also leads to excessively fast wear of the friction lining.

The above-mentioned time relay 2SJ setting being too short, the electromagnetic brake coil circuit discharge resistor being too large, the economy resistor resistance being too large or being connected in too early, and the breakdown of the diode in the brake coil discharge circuit all belong to the control circuit side causes of the fault of high temperature rise and excessively fast friction plate wear of the electromagnetic brake.

From the perspective of the brake body, too small a friction plate clearance, uneven clearance, and friction plate deformation will all cause brake heating and severe wear. Too strong spring force inside the brake, internal short circuit of the coil, insufficient holding force, the spring falling off so that the armature is obstructed, and uneven or reduced clearance are also causes of excessively fast friction plate wear. These factors are parallel to the aforementioned control circuit causes and together constitute the fault sources of high temperature rise and excessively fast friction plate wear of the electromagnetic brake. When power is cut off, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. If the clearance is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply. For the electromagnetic brake, maintenance correspondingly includes an electromagnetic brake clearance measurement method, used to determine the size of the clearance between the armature disc and the electromagnet core; there is also corresponding electromagnetic brake clearance adjustment, so as to restore a suitable distance between plates when the clearance is too large or too small; there is also corresponding electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment, obtaining the required braking effect by changing the spring compression amount or the position of the manual release screw.

Motor stalling is another type of fault in the cargo winch electrical system that requires attention. When the motor stalls, the stator current increases greatly, and the temperature rise is fast and high. For the domestic constant-power JZF-H type three-speed asynchronous motor, the stall currents of the 28-pole, 8-pole, and 4-pole are 2Ie, 4Ie, and 4Ie respectively. If the master controller handle is quickly thrown to the medium-speed or high-speed position during starting, the accelerating contactor 2C and the ZDQ coil of the medium-speed winding are energized at the same time; when 2C acts faster than ZDQ, short-time stalling of the medium-speed winding may occur. In the JZF-H type motor, welding of the ZDC auxiliary contact will cause long-term stalling of the medium-speed winding; welding or jamming in the closed state of the auxiliary contact of the braking contactor will also cause long-term stalling of the winding. When the brake itself fails and cannot release, it will directly cause the motor to stall. The braking contactor ZDC does not pick up and its auxiliary contact is welded or jammed closed, causing long-term stalling of the medium-speed winding. During braking, if the 2SJ delay is too long and the ZDQ discharge resistor is relatively large, stalling of the low-speed winding will occur; failure of the time relay 5SJ will cause stalling of the low-speed winding. Motor stalling will cause the motor to overheat or even burn out.

In the control of the JZF-H type three-speed asynchronous motor, quickly throwing the master controller handle so that operation is too frequent will cause severe motor heating. Too frequent operation belongs to the causes of electrical faults, referring to the equipment acting too many times per unit time or the operation interval being too short, resulting in contact overheating, wear, or misoperation of the thermal relay. In a contactor, too frequent operation will cause contact overheating or burning, and is also one of the main causes of excessive contact wear.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system, belonging to ship low-voltage control apparatus, mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of high operating frequency and long life, as well as accurate and reliable operation and small size. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contact, core, and coil.

Contact welding is a fault symptom in which the contactor contact cannot release due to welding, often caused by insufficient capacity, short circuit, or too little pressure. Contact welding will directly cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed; that is, the contactor not releasing for a long time or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed is precisely the consequence of contact welding. Too small contact capacity is one of the main causes of contact welding; load short circuit will cause contact welding, and the contact must be replaced after the fault is cleared; insufficient holding force, serious burning of the contact surface causing poor contact or burrs, metal particles, etc., too little contact spring pressure, and too frequent operation or overload use will all cause contact welding. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. The circuit breaker is a switching device used to protect circuits in the ship power system, belonging to ship distribution apparatus, divided into frame type and molded-case type, having both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid.

A motor internal fault will cause the motor to fail to start and automatic start failure, and will also cause the motor to overheat or even burn out. Faults in the stator winding and bearing will cause the motor to show excessive temperature rise. A marine motor contains a bearing and a winding;

When measuring electrical quantities and device performance such as resistance, current and diode, the multimeter is a commonly used tool. The measurable performance of a resistor is its resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; a diode has unidirectional conductivity and is commonly denoted VD in circuits, and is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity, with a small conduction resistance under forward voltage and an extremely large or infinite resistance under reverse voltage. By function, diodes are divided into rectifier diodes, isolation diodes, Schottky diodes, etc., for example 1N4004, 1N4148, BAT85; diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. The diode test steps apply to diodes, and marine electrical equipment also uses diodes.

Once the control system of an AC electric cargo winch loses control, cargo handling can no longer proceed according to the operating intention. So-called loss of control of the control system refers to the phenomenon in which the cargo winch does not work as required by the master controller handle, causing control failure. When the cargo winch loses control, maintenance personnel must quickly eliminate the fault to ensure normal operation. Maintenance personnel undertaking this work should be familiar with the structure of the electrical equipment, the working principle, the functions of the components (assemblies) and their locations, and should master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, and through these means understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary diagnosis. Maintenance personnel must also be very familiar with the lines of the whole ship's electrical equipment, the working principle and the location of each component, so as to quickly determine on site in which link the fault occurs.

Pulling the master controller handle, neither forward nor reverse can start, which is one of the more common loss-of-control faults. The fault cause of this symptom lies in the common part of the forward and reverse control lines. Main power supply fault, fuse blowing in the control line, brake contactor not actuating or poor contact of contacts, poor closing of master controller contacts or damage to the master controller, damper switch not connected, temperature relay not reset or poor contact of contacts, poor contact of contacts of the undervoltage relay, and poor contact of the emergency switch will all cause neither forward nor reverse to start when the master controller handle is pulled. During troubleshooting, if the fan does not turn, check whether the main power supply, the fuse and the thermal relay RJ are reset; if the fan turns, check the auxiliary contact of the fan contactor FSC and the pull-in condition of the zero-voltage relay. In addition, check whether the internal contacts of the master controller are in good contact, whether any have fallen off or are damaged, confirm whether the brake has been released, and troubleshoot whether the motor itself has a fault.

As far as the power supply not being connected is concerned, it will likewise lead to the result of failure to start.

Pulling the master controller handle, only forward or only reverse, is another manifestation of loss of control. One of the directional contactors being faulty, poor contact of the contacts of a directional contactor, or a fault in the master controller will all lead to this symptom. Specifically, poor contact of the contacts of the cargo winch directional contactor (ZC or FC) will cause only forward or only reverse when the handle is pulled; during troubleshooting, check the contact condition of the main and auxiliary contacts of the two contactors ZC or FC, and at the same time check the contact state of the master controller to eliminate the fault.

The symptom of no high speed and no medium speed in either forward or reverse has many causes. Long-term overload operation of the cargo winch fan will cause the thermal relay to actuate, so that high and medium speeds cannot run, among which long-term overload of the fan causing the thermal relay 2RJ to actuate and the contactor FSC to release is one of the main causes. Poor contact of the auxiliary contact of the fan contactor FSC can trigger this fault, poor contact of the auxiliary contact of the brake contactor is also a possible cause, and a fault in the internal contacts of the master controller can likewise lead to the absence of high and medium speeds. When this fault occurs, the cargo can only be lowered using the low speed position. Long-term overload will not only prevent high and medium speeds from running, but will also cause a high temperature rise of the motor, and in severe cases even cause the generator to overheat; long-term overload operation of an asynchronous motor will cause reduced insulation performance, aging or mechanical damage; when checking excessive motor temperature rise, it is necessary to troubleshoot whether a long-term overload condition exists on the mechanical side.

Excessive cargo slip during braking is a typical fault of the braking link of a cargo winch. Generally, when the rated speed of an AC electric cargo winch is 40m/min, the slip should not exceed 0.4m. The main causes include poor coordination of the three-stage braking or a fault in the electromagnetic brake. If the delay setting process of time relay 2SJ is short, the regenerative braking time of the motor is short, and braking the system at high speed will increase the slip; if the 2SJ delay is too long, the electromagnetic brake will brake too late, which will also make the slip too long. To avoid excessive slip, the 2SJ delay is generally set to 0.7s. When the core of the electromagnetic brake has residual magnetism, under the action of residual magnetic attraction, the armature will be released too late, causing the cargo to be in free fall and producing a relatively large slip. Friction plates that are too smooth, excessive clearance, and insufficient reaction spring force will all affect the slip; the above factors are one of the manifestations of an electromagnetic brake fault.

Single-phase operation of the motor is also often accompanied by cargo winch faults. When the three-phase contacts of a certain position contactor in the main circuit cannot contact simultaneously, or when a contact of one phase is damaged or falls off, single-phase operation faults often occur, and the motor fails to start when energized; however, after starting at medium or high speed, when the handle is turned back to the low-speed position, the low speed can still rotate, but the load torque is small, and the same phenomenon also occurs in the medium and high speed positions. When single-phase operation is caused by damage or falling off of the contacts of the main circuit contactor, the motor fails to start at the instant of energization. The motor failing to start may also be caused by power supply problems, mechanical problems, excessive load, or motor internal fault. When checking, the principle from simple to complex should be followed: first check the power supply, then check whether the shaft is stuck or the load is excessive, and finally check the inside of the motor, and correspondingly check the power supply voltage and check the motor internal fault.

At the component level, the fuse symbol is FU, which has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. When overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, the circuit is automatically cut off by melting the fuse element; the designations of the time relay include KT, SJ, and SL. For the electromagnetic brake, maintenance requires mastering the method for measuring the clearance of the electromagnetic brake, and accordingly carrying out electromagnetic brake clearance adjustment, and on this basis completing electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment, so that the brake restores normal braking performance.

Poor contact of contacts is a common cause of various cargo winch faults. Contamination, oxidation, or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface will lead to reduced electrical conductivity. In a contactor, poor contact of contacts is one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning. Methods for dealing with poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface, and tightening the contacts and conductive plate. Loose, oxidized, or foreign matter at electrical connections increases contact resistance, that is, forms poor contact. Loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact and increase contact resistance. Poor contact can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure, and phase-to-phase short circuit. After identifying the fault, when it is confirmed that the semiconductor trip unit itself is not damaged, most cases may be external electromagnetic interference.

AC electric cargo winches are widely used in ship deck machinery. Their drive motors are generally cage-type pole-changing variable-speed motors with three speeds. According to the speed regulation range from medium speed to high speed, this type of cargo winch can be divided into two forms: constant power speed regulation and constant torque speed regulation. Foreign products mostly use constant torque speed regulation systems. Constant power speed regulation systems have relatively high requirements for overload protection and interlock control for two derricks at the same speed. Although DC electric cargo winches differ from AC models in driving and control methods, in terms of fault analysis thinking they can still be considered together within the scope of AC electric cargo winches.

In troubleshooting the electrical system of a cargo winch, resistance measurement is a basic task. Poor contact of contacts is a common fault state in contactors. Contamination, oxidation, or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface will lead to reduced electrical conductivity. Poor contact of contacts will cause contact overheating or burning. During handling, it is necessary to clean the contact surface, dress the surface, and tighten the contacts and conductive plate.

Poor contact of the contacts of the cargo winch direction contactor ZC or FC will cause that when the handle is moved there is only forward drive or only reverse drive, that is, the AC electric cargo winch will have the fault that when the master controller handle is moved there is only forward drive or only reverse drive. Poor contact of the internal contacts of the cargo winch master controller may cause neither forward nor reverse drive to have high speed and medium speed operation. Poor contact of the contacts of the AC electric cargo winch brake contactor will cause the brake not to be released, so that neither forward nor reverse drive turns. These phenomena all belong to the faults that may occur during operation of the AC electric cargo winch, and alongside them there are also overheating and even burning out of the motor, loss of control of the control system, failure to start in either forward or reverse drive when the master controller handle is moved, excessive cargo slip during braking, and single-phase operation of the motor, etc. The AC electric cargo winch will also have the fault of high temperature rise of the electromagnetic brake and excessively fast wear of the friction plates; this phenomenon is directly related to the various causes of brake heating and abnormal wear of the friction plates.

The constant-power cargo winch being unable to run at high speed under light load is one of the common faults of the AC electric cargo winch, and is listed as an independent item in the fault and cause comparison data. One direct cause of this fault is failure of the load relay, and the second direct cause is an incorrect setting value of the load relay, that is, failure of the load relay or an incorrect setting value will cause the constant-power cargo winch to be unable to run at high speed under light load.

The load relay ZJ is a component that frequently causes faults, mainly manifesting as overheating of the motor when running at high speed under heavy load; therefore, in cargo winch management, the load relay should be carefully adjusted and monitored. The causes of this phenomenon include open circuit or short circuit in the electromagnetic brake circuit, and failure of the time relay KT. Open circuit or short circuit in the electromagnetic brake circuit is one of the direct causes of the electromagnetic brake not pulling in, will cause the AC electric cargo winch to have motor stalling, and together with failure of the time relay KT constitutes the cause of the brake not pulling in; failure of the time relay KT will cause the electromagnetic brake not to pull in, and further cause the motor to stall.

The electromagnetic brake not releasing is another fault symptom, manifesting as the electromagnetic brake being unable to release the braking state. Fragmentation and jamming of the friction plates is one of the causes of the electromagnetic brake not releasing; the auxiliary contact of the accelerating contactor not opening so that the electromagnetic brake is not de-energized will likewise cause the electromagnetic brake not to release; a fault in the brake contactor is also one of the causes of the electromagnetic brake not releasing.

The mechanism of the fault of the auxiliary contact of the accelerating contactor not opening is that the auxiliary contact not opening causes the electromagnetic brake not to be de-energized; in the AC electric cargo winch it is one of the three main causes of the electromagnetic brake not releasing, and usually together with a brake contactor fault causes the brake not to be de-energized. Fragmentation and jamming of the friction plates is somewhat different from excessive slip or small braking torque caused by too large a gap between the friction plates.

The phenomenon of the electromagnetic brake releasing immediately after pulling in may be caused by interruption arising from improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting; too short a delay setting of the time relay KT2 may also cause this fault; too large an economy resistance value of the brake coil is a potential fault cause; and too strong a return spring force of the brake will likewise cause immediate release after pulling in.

The cause of improper transfer and interruption of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting belongs to the items in the fault and cause comparison data of the AC electric cargo winch, and together with too short a KT2 delay, too large a coil economy resistance, etc. constitutes the causes of the same fault symptom; too short a KT delay, that is, too short a KT2 delay, is one of the fault causes of the electromagnetic brake releasing immediately after pulling in, and is usually listed alongside factors such as improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting, the coil resistance or the spring force; too large a resistance value of the economy resistor of the brake coil is listed alongside factors such as improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting and too short a KT2 delay, and belongs to the common fault causes of the electromagnetic braking system of the AC electric cargo winch; too strong a return spring force of the brake is listed alongside improper transfer of the accelerating contactor during gear shifting, too short a KT2 delay, and too large an economy resistance value of the coil.

The fault causes of electromagnetic brake heating include inter-turn short circuit in the brake coil, deformation of the friction plates or too small a gap between plates, and too small an economy resistance value or too late insertion. Inter-turn short circuit in the brake coil is one of the main fault causes of heating of the electromagnetic brake of the AC electric cargo winch, and often occurs together with deformation of the friction plates, too small a gap or an improper economy resistance value to cause brake heating. Deformation of the friction plates or too small a gap between plates is one of the fault causes of electromagnetic brake heating; too small a gap between plates will cause excessively fast wear of the friction plates, and deformation of the friction plates caused by long-term high-speed friction will cause brake heating.

The economic resistor resistance being too small or being connected in too late is one of the main fault causes of electromagnetic brake heating; specifically, the economic resistor resistance in the brake coil is set too small, or the economic resistor is connected into the circuit too late, failing to limit the current in time; the corresponding fault symptom is that the brake releases immediately after engaging, the cause of which is that the economic resistor value is too large.

Rapid wear of the friction lining is a type of fault symptom of the electromagnetic brake, manifested as abnormally rapid wear of the friction lining accompanied by excessive temperature rise. The time relay 2SJ being set too short causes regenerative braking to fail, resulting in high-speed braking and thus rapid wear; the discharge resistor in the coil circuit being too large causes discharge to be too fast, causing high-speed braking and thus accelerating friction lining wear; the economic resistor value being too large or being connected in too early prevents the brake from fully opening, causing accelerated friction lining wear; the friction lining gap being too small, uneven or deformed directly causes brake heating and severe wear; the spring force inside the brake being too strong, the coil short circuit causing low attraction force, or the armature being obstructed all cause rapid wear.

The inter-lining gap being too small is one of the main causes of heating of the electromagnetic brake of the AC electric cargo winch, and causes rapid wear of the friction lining of the electromagnetic brake; in the fault-and-cause comparison data it is listed both as a specific fault cause of electromagnetic brake heating and as a specific fault cause of rapid friction lining wear. Poor friction lining quality and poor wear resistance is one of the causes of the rapid friction lining wear fault of the AC electric cargo winch, and together with the inter-lining gap being too small and the regenerative braking time being too short, etc., constitutes the causes of rapid friction lining wear, and is an inducing factor of electromagnetic brake-related faults, distinct from cracking/jamming or heating causes. The motor regenerative braking time being too short and high-speed braking occurring is one of the fault causes of rapid friction lining wear of the electromagnetic brake of the AC electric cargo winch, manifested as the motor regenerative braking time being too short and then high-speed braking occurring; this fault cause is listed alongside the friction lining gap being too small, poor quality and uneven gap. If the gap is too small, the brake temperature rises sharply. For the electromagnetic brake, the maintenance work correspondingly includes the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, electromagnetic brake gap adjustment and electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment, i.e., the electromagnetic brake corresponds to the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, corresponds to the electromagnetic brake gap adjustment, and also corresponds to the electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment; the three together constitute the basic work content of brake maintenance.

Constant-torque speed control systems are mostly used abroad; DC electric cargo winches also belong to the category of electric cargo winches.

The phenomenon that the winch cannot be started in either forward or reverse when the master controller handle is moved can be caused by multiple causes. A blown fuse in the control circuit causes this phenomenon; the brake contactor not operating or poor contact of contacts causes this phenomenon, the direct consequence of which is that the brake is not released; poor closing of the master controller contacts or damage to the master controller causes this phenomenon; the damper switch not being closed causes this phenomenon; poor contact of the contacts of the undervoltage relay causes this phenomenon; poor contact of the emergency switch likewise causes this phenomenon. The above causes, together with the power supply voltage not being connected, etc., constitute the possible factors for the cargo winch being completely unable to start. One of the direction contactors being faulty is a fault at the direction contactor assembly level, distinct from detailed problems such as poor contact of contacts;

A master controller fault may cause either forward operation without reverse operation, or reverse operation without forward operation. A voltage relay is a relay classified by the nature of the input signal, which performs control or protection functions through the coil sensing voltage changes, and belongs to the electromagnetic relay, with the coil using electrical quantity, i.e., voltage, as the excitation input; the temperature relay in the AC electric cargo winch not being reset or poor contact of contacts will also cause the motor not to turn in either forward or reverse;

Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; a multimeter is used when measuring voltage, the multimeter being used to measure voltage, and a voltmeter may also be used to measure its voltage value; it belongs to the distribution apparatus, having the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series fuse is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection.

In the ship's auxiliary machinery electrical system, the windlass and the mooring winch both belong to deck machinery, and their drag control schemes are generally the same as those of the ship's AC electric cargo winch. The electric windlass is divided into DC and AC types, and the mooring winch is likewise divided into DC and AC types; at present, AC three-speed windlasses and mooring winches or G-M system windlasses and mooring winches are mostly adopted, and the drag control systems of the two are basically the same. As regards equipment attribution, the mooring winch belongs to the large category of deck machinery of the electric windlass, and the maintenance of the electrical systems of the windlass and mooring winch is included within the maintenance scope of the electric windlass. The mooring winch is usually listed as the first-level non-important load for priority disconnection.

The AC three-speed electric windlass adopts a three-speed cage-type asynchronous motor as the drive motor, and the cage-type asynchronous motor is the main form of marine asynchronous motor; the three-phase asynchronous motor used on most ships is the cage-type asynchronous motor.

The stator core of the three-speed cage-type asynchronous motor has two sets of windings, one high-speed set and one shared medium-low-speed set; the high-speed winding of this motor is 4-pole, the medium speed is double-star connection (8-pole), and the low speed is single-delta connection (16-pole). Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of the AC motor.
