In the AC three-speed windlass, the two sets of stator windings are respectively the high-speed 4-pole and the shared medium-low-speed pole-changing type; this type of windlass has undervoltage and high-speed overload protection, and automatically switches to medium-speed operation on high-speed overcurrent.

The motor of the electric windlass should be able to withstand a locked-rotor current for 1 min, with a locked-rotor torque of twice the rated torque; during emergency anchor raising, the motor is allowed to start 25 times within 30 min;

When anchoring in deep water, the control system makes the motor operate in the regenerative braking or dynamic braking state. At an anchoring depth of 45 m, the average speed of raising both anchors is not less than 6 m/min; the electric drag device should be able to satisfy, within the given voyage area, raising both anchors after a single anchor breaks ground.

The maintenance content of the electrical systems of the windlass and mooring winch includes: the number of starts should not be too frequent, generally 25 starts are allowed within 30 min; the locked-rotor time must not be too long, generally 1 min is allowed, and when the ammeter indication exceeds the rated current of the motor for a relatively long time, the machine should be stopped. For the maintenance of the electrical control panel of the windlass and mooring winch, refer to the maintenance requirements of the cargo winch control panel; the maintenance requirements for the electromagnetic brake and the master controller are the same as those of the cargo winch. The equipment belongs to short-time duty, and operation should be carried out according to the state of the anchor chain and mooring rope and the current reading.

The electromagnetic brake is composed of an electromagnetic armature disc, springs, a moving plate, a friction plate or friction block, an end cover, etc., and is used as the braking component of the drag motor of deck machinery such as cargo winches and windlasses; it realizes brake release or brake application through electromagnetic attraction and spring return, and often adopts a disc-type structure integrated with the motor to improve watertightness and braking stability. When the coil is energized, the electromagnet attracts and compresses the spring so that the moving plate rotates freely; when de-energized, the spring pushes the armature back to produce braking torque. The AC electric cargo winch includes an electromagnetic brake, and the electromagnetic brake corresponds to the electromagnetic brake gap measurement method, electromagnetic brake gap adjustment, and electromagnetic brake braking torque adjustment. The contactor includes a core; the core is a component of ship electrical equipment, serving as the magnetic-conducting component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil, and serve as an insulation measurement reference point; when measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in the through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor under test is directly linked with the core to replace the primary winding.

The commissioning of the electrical control system of the windlass and mooring winch applies to the electric windlass. Electrical and mechanical combined braking is adopted to meet the requirement of rapid stopping; the electric drive device should satisfy the requirement that after a single anchor breaks ground it can raise both anchors; this equipment belongs to short-time duty equipment, and starting should not exceed 25 times within 30 min. During commissioning, carry out the no-load test first and roughly set each protective electrical apparatus: the zero-voltage relay LYJ can be set to 80%U; the overcurrent relay GLJ is set to 110%Ie for AC and slightly greater than 2Ie for DC. Switch on the power supply, place the master controller handle at the zero position, and observe the action of each electrical apparatus; the zero-voltage relay LYJ and the three time relays 1SJ~3SJ should operate, and other electrical apparatuses should not operate.

Among the protective electrical apparatuses, the current relay in the AC three-speed electric windlass picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%; in the windlass system, misoperation of the overcurrent relay GLJ will cause the fault of no high speed during starting;

During commissioning of auxiliary machines, the AC overcurrent relay is set to 110%I_e, and the DC one to slightly greater than 2I_e. The current relay belongs to the electromagnetic relay classified by the nature of the input signal and is used for control and protection of the ship's electrical system; its coil carries electrical quantity, and its structure is basically similar to that of the contactor; after the generator is paralleled and trips, the overcurrent relay needs to be reset to restore closing of the main switch. Time relays are often denoted in circuits by KT, SJ, SL. The thermal relay is a protective relay with a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small motors on ships; it belongs to the thermal relay classified by sensing element, its sensing part is the bimetallic strip, and it is used in large quantities on ships, generally to complete the overload protection task of small motors.

Current is one of the measurable performances, and its measuring tools include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; voltage is likewise a measurable performance, and its measuring tools include the multimeter and voltmeter. The multimeter can be used to measure both voltage and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system.

During operation of the electric windlass, the fault symptom of serious motor heating occurs, and its main causes include frequent operation, harsh working conditions and motor internal fault. From the control circuit point of view, the control circuit allows direct starting at medium speed, and the relatively large starting current easily causes overheating after multiple starts; the windlass often requires high-speed braking, which causes serious heating of the brake and aggravates the overall temperature rise; when heating is serious, thermal relays 1RJ and 2RJ operate to cut off the circuit; during emergency anchor raising, the emergency button AN can be pressed to force operation to cope with the overheating protection action. Frequent operation and harsh working conditions are, apart from motor internal fault, the main causes of serious heating of the windlass motor; because the control circuit allows direct starting at medium speed, multiple starts with large current lead to overheating, and the working characteristics of the windlass require frequent high-speed braking, causing serious heating of the brake.

Apart from frequent operation and harsh working conditions, motor internal fault is also one of the causes of serious heating of the AC three-speed electric windlass; faults in the motor stator winding, bearing, etc. will also produce the phenomenon of excessively high temperature rise, and this fault will cause the motor to fail to start, automatic start failure, motor overheating, or even burning out; it is one of the direct causes of failure to start of the single-speed irreversible AC electric drive system, belongs to one of the two major categories of common faults in the single-speed irreversible direct-start control system on ships, is also one of the eight causes in the fault tree of failure to start of the three-phase asynchronous motor, and one of the eight possible causes of motor speed low after starting. When analyzing faults of cage asynchronous motors, the fault tree (FTA) method is usually adopted, covering eight categories of causes such as failure to start and low speed.

The electric windlass also has the fault symptom of only medium speed and low speed and no high speed; this fault belongs to the scope of common fault troubleshooting of the AC three-speed electric windlass, specifically manifested as the windlass motor having only medium and low speed positions available and completely lacking high-speed operation capability. Misoperation of the overcurrent relay GLJ will cause only medium speed and low speed and no high speed; poor contact of contacts of the master controller, contactor and relay will cause only medium speed and low speed and no high speed; too short a delay setting of the 2SJ time relay will likewise cause only medium speed and low speed and no high speed. In addition, the electric windlass also has the fault symptom of brake failure.

In the electrical faults of refrigeration and ventilation auxiliary equipment, compressor control failure is manifested as the compressor being unable to start and stop normally in the automatic operating state; during automatic operation, the start and stop of the compressor are controlled by the suction-side low-pressure switch 63HL(L). If it can start normally after switching to manual, it is determined that the low-pressure switch 63HL(L) is damaged or its contact is not closed. Too large a cold-storage temperature deviation is a temperature-control deviation fault symptom occurring during the operation of the refrigerating installation. Fan fault refers to the fan motor stoppage fault in the refrigeration system of the cold-storage room controlled by the defrost timer relay; the fan operating state is controlled by the defrost timer relay, and the fan should run when not defrosting. If it is in the defrosting state, the fan stopping is a normal phenomenon rather than a fault. Failure to self-defrost is a fault symptom in refrigeration equipment in which the defrost timer or control switch fails, resulting in the inability to automatically defrost. During troubleshooting, first place CS in the "DEFROST" position for manual defrosting to determine the scope of the fault; if manual defrosting succeeds, it indicates that the two sets of switches of the defrost timer cannot change over automatically.

If the AC three-speed electric windlass has only medium speed and low speed but no high speed during starting, troubleshooting can usually start from three clues. All three will cause no high speed during starting of AC three-speed electric auxiliary machines. Poor contact of contacts may both independently cause no high speed and be one of the causes of misoperation of the overcurrent relay GLJ; the two often occur together. When the delay setting of the 2SJ time relay is too short, the overcurrent protection is connected too early, likewise causing no high speed during starting; this fault also often acts together with poor contact of contacts, causing the protection to operate too early. The zero-voltage relay can be set to 80% rated voltage during commissioning of auxiliary machines.

Brake failure may also occur in the electric windlass. If the brake is applied immediately after pull-in during starting, it indicates that the economy resistor is open-circuited; if it cannot pull in and release the brake, first check whether 3SJ operates normally, then check whether 3SJ pulls in when the master controller handle is in the zero position. If 3SJ pulls in, it indicates that the brake power supply and 3SJ are normal; at this time, check whether the master controller contacts, the brake relay ZDC and the electromagnetic brake coil are open-circuited. If the brake cannot pull in and release the brake while 3SJ is normal, also check whether the master controller contacts have poor contact or are open-circuited.

The mooring winch is short-time duty equipment and is permitted to start 25 times within 30 min;

In the no-load test during commissioning of auxiliary machines, it is necessary to observe the direction of rotation, speed, and the starting current and no-load current of each step under step-by-step forward and reverse operation; in the final stage, it is necessary to listen to the sound of the gearbox and bearings at each step, and run at no load for 2 h to check the temperature rise. In the no-load test, when the power supply is switched on and the master controller is in the zero position, only the zero-voltage relay and the time relay operate; the link of switching on the power supply corresponds to no load applied. After the windlass system has run at no load for 2 h normally, the insulation resistance needs to be measured at final shutdown. Measuring insulation resistance is used to check the insulation performance of electrical equipment, often after major overhaul of equipment or after shutdown following operation, and is also one of the mandatory checks and test items for acceptance of a motor after new installation or major overhaul; in contactor maintenance, it is necessary to measure the insulation resistance between contacts, between the coil and the core, and between live parts and ground. Observation contents include abnormal phenomena, part conditions, conductor conditions, and equipment operating parameters, specifically such as whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Checking the bearing fault itself and checking the lubrication condition are both carried out for the bearing;

A contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in ship power systems and belongs to low-voltage control apparatus; it has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size, and is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of almost all kinds of auxiliary machinery is driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil; contactor maintenance applies to contactors. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; the insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. Time relays are often marked as KT, SJ, SL in diagrams. A voltage relay realizes control or protection functions by sensing voltage changes through its coil; when the coil is damaged, only a coil of the same model can be replaced, and self-winding will affect the operating value due to inaccurate turns.

The multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current; the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current, and an ammeter is also used to measure current. If capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance; never measure with power on. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit in the shunt resistor will cause the voltage corrector to lose its main regulating action.

The electro-hydraulic steering gear is an important part of the ship's auxiliary machinery electrical system. Its electrical control system is equipped with an autopilot or automatic track keeper, which controls the course error according to certain requirements by proportional, proportional-derivative or proportional-derivative-integral laws, or keeps the ship sailing on a given course. The steering gear used on large ocean-going or offshore passenger and cargo ships has an electrical control system equipped with an autopilot or autopilot selector. The electro-hydraulic steering gear should be supplied by two power sources, the emergency power supply and the main switchboard, and the lines should be routed far apart and separately. The electric oil pump unit adopts a cold-standby bypass scheme and can operate independently, automatically switch over to each other, or operate two units in parallel.

At maximum speed in deep draft, the time for the rudder to turn from 35° on one side to 30° on the other side must not exceed 28 s. The error of the rudder angle indicator indicating the rudder blade position should not be greater than ±1°. The system is provided with a rudder blade deflection limit switch, and power loss and overload audible and visual alarm devices.

The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the ship's power station. The ship's power station includes the main switchboard, and the main switchboard includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The main switchboard has the functions of circuit making and breaking, protection and alarm, parameter detection and power regulation. Its main functions include making or breaking circuits, protection device operation and alarm, detection and display of various electrical parameters, and it can regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station and the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel.

In the fault diagnosis of the steering gear electrical system, the conventional fault diagnosis method uses the step of observation. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding check the monitoring and indicating device. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status and equipment operating parameters, specifically involving whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Observation belongs to a sub-step of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged". The multimeter is used to measure resistance and voltage; voltage is one of the measurable performance quantities, and its measuring tools include the multimeter and the voltmeter. Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis. When measuring the resistor in the measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance; never measure with power on.

The electro-hydraulic steering gear includes three maintenance items: rudder alignment during pre-departure preparation, patrol inspection during navigation, and maintenance of the steering gear electrical system. Rudder alignment during pre-departure preparation requires checking whether the steering console control switches, buttons, indicator lights and devices such as power loss and overload alarms are complete and effective; the power supply changeover between the two sides should be observed, and trial operation should be carried out separately on the bridge and in the steering gear room using the emergency power supply; trial operation should be carried out using various steering modes to check the effectiveness of the emergency steering, the reliability of automatic changeover of the units and the flexibility of mechanical transmission. The autopilot and electric steering gear system should not exhibit rudder drift, rudder overshoot, failure to return to midships or oscillation during trial operation. At midships, the deviation between the steering gear, indicator and actual position should be 0°, and the deviation at large rudder angles should not be greater than 2°. It is also necessary to recheck whether the time for the rudder to turn from 35° on one side to 30° on the other side meets the requirements, and to check whether there is any abnormal noise during rudder turning.

During navigation, the patrol inspection needs to check the unit operating conditions, the motor running sound and temperature rise, confirm whether the actions of the solenoid valve, servo motor, limit switch, etc. are reliable, and observe whether the readings of each instrument, the unit operation indications and the steering angle indication device work normally. For ships whose steering gear control system is driven by two sets, they should be replaced and used regularly. In terms of maintenance of the steering gear electrical system, the transmission part of the main steering gear of the autopilot control console shall be lubricated once every 6 months, and the oil quality of the transmission parts such as gears and miniature bearings shall be checked once every year; if deteriorated, clean and re-lubricate, and at the same time remove the dust and dirt inside the steering gear, and replace vulnerable parts if necessary. For the follow-up control system, the resistor, brush and conductive ring of the transmitter and receiver of the AEG-type steering gear shall be checked every voyage, and corresponding checks shall also be made for the slip ring structure.

In steering gear maintenance, the solenoid valve needs to be disassembled, cleaned and inspected to ensure that the movable part of the valve body is free from jamming and the stroke meets the requirements. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel circulation circuit, release the residual air of the air compressor or control the fine water mist fire extinguishing zone; it is energized in the burner ignition procedure, cuts off the fuel circulation circuit so that the oil enters the fuel nozzle and is injected, and its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The automatic fuel boiler includes a solenoid valve and a servo motor. The servo motor belongs to the content of the patrol inspection of the steering gear electrical system, and its action needs to be confirmed to be reliable. The servo motor is a motor controlled by the signal of a bridge or regulator, which drives the feedback potentiometer or the throttle actuator through rotation to achieve automatic balance and position control; in boiler combustion regulation, the winding is energized under the control of a differential amplifier and a thyristor to adjust the air-fuel ratio, and when rotating it drives the sliding contact of the feedback potentiometer R10 to move, so that the bridge reaches balance again and then stops.

A resistor is ship equipment whose resistance can be measured, and the measuring tool is a multimeter. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect.

The printed circuit board is composed of a base material and circuits; the base material is an insulating material, including phenolic resin board and epoxy glass, and the circuits are conductive foil, usually copper. The base material is often called the substrate, most commonly phenolic resin board and epoxy glass; the circuit part is made of conductive copper, laid on the substrate, and the required pattern is obtained by etching. Marine electrical equipment uses printed circuit boards; printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards; a circuit board fault occurs in a printed circuit board, and the circuit board fault belongs to the scope of printed circuit boards. The printed circuit boards of a dual-channel system with mutual standby should be frequently interchanged to ensure working performance, and spare printed circuit boards and components should be stored sealed or dry.

The coil is a component of marine electrical equipment, made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. The KM coil fault is one of the direct causes for the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked. The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system, belongs to low-voltage control appliances, is used in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size; it is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to contactors.

The brush contacts the collector ring to transmit current, and is used as an important conductive element for leading current in or out between the stationary part and the sliding part of the motor; DC motors, AC wound-rotor motors and synchronous generators all need to be equipped with brushes. Motor overload, poor contact between brush and commutator, and loose brush holder will all lead to excessive sparking under brush.

The fuse is used for overload and short circuit protection in the ship's power system, its symbol is FU, and it is a protective electrical appliance; when the power network or electrical equipment undergoes overload or short circuit, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. The fuse belongs to distribution electrical appliances and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. Fuse blown corresponds to replace the fuse, and power supply fuse blown also corresponds to replace the fuse. When replacing the fuse, it should generally be removed and replaced under the condition of no power; if live replacement is permitted, the load must first be cut off to prevent danger. Before replacing with a new fuse element, the inner surface of the tube and the contact surfaces must be carefully wiped clean of fuse slag, soot and dust.

In troubleshooting the steering gear system, if the main power supply has no fault but emergency steering fails, the fuse needs to be replaced after inspection.

The electro-hydraulic steering gear may exhibit three types of fault symptoms: autopilot not working, autopilot not sensitive (sluggish operation), and excessive autopilot error. Autopilot not working belongs to one of the four main summarized types of general autopilot faults, namely not working, not sensitive, unstable, and inaccurate. Autopilot not working is generally caused by obvious faults, such as open power supply, blown fuse, broken wire (open circuit) short circuit, various electronic component faults, etc., and appears as the primary troubleshooting category in the general fault troubleshooting process of the PR4507 autopilot, and may occur concurrently with other faults or occur intermittently. Autopilot not sensitive (sluggish operation) may be due to improper amplifier gain setting, phase mismatch, failure of components within the system, etc.; in complex systems such as the PR4507 autopilot, troubleshooting of this fault is relatively difficult. Excessive autopilot error may be caused by reasons such as inflexible operation of the autopilot actuator, and is listed as a main inspection item in the fault troubleshooting process of equipment such as the PR4507 autopilot.

The commissioning after maintenance of the steering gear drive electrical control system applies to the electro-hydraulic steering gear. Different faults of the steering gear drive electrical control system have different specific commissioning methods; although the specific methods differ, the commissioning content of the steering gear drive electrical control system is the same; it is impossible to describe the specific commissioning method of the steering gear drive electrical control system for a single circuit. Before the first power-on, the entire system needs to be cleaned, including cleaning the control box, motor and junction box, feedback device, solenoid valve and actuator motor, etc., while checking the autopilot; familiarize with the drawings and the working principle of the steering gear system, check the wiring and installation, whether they conform to the wiring diagram; check or install all fuses in the system according to the capacity required by the drawings, and install the indicator bulbs in the specified number; check the insulation resistance.

The junction box is a component used in the ship's electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical components; the general alarm device includes a junction box, and the general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc. The maintenance cycle of the rudder angle indicator is 3 months, and the content includes removing dust and check the power supply. During autopilot commissioning, it is necessary to measure whether the output voltages of the power transformer are correct. Power supply fault corresponds to check the power supply; in the overall PLC inspection, if the POWER lamp off, the step of checking the power supply fault needs to be executed; when the electric fan starts slowly, the maintenance method includes checking whether the power supply voltage is too low; when the electric drill fails to start and the power supply has no voltage, the power supply line should be checked.

The maintenance of the steering gear electrical control system, in addition to the control logic and hydraulic actuator, also involves the inspection of a large number of general electrical devices and motor components. The error of the rudder angle indicator indicating the rudder blade position should not be greater than ±1°. During operation, the electro-hydraulic steering gear may experience autopilot not working, may also experience autopilot not sensitive, i.e. sluggish operation, and may also experience excessive autopilot error; these phenomena are often related to the power supply, line connections and the state of control devices. During maintenance of the steering gear follow-up control system, it is necessary to check the various linkage parts in the system and confirm whether the linkage is deformed, loose or jammed.

These practices all show that check the power supply is a common step in handling many types of electrical faults.

Measuring circuit parameters cannot be done without a multimeter. The multimeter contains a changeover switch; the changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measuring points or issue operating commands, has many selection positions and contacts, and on the main switchboard is mainly used to select indication and measuring points, set the working state and issue operating commands; the changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The multimeter can be used to measure resistor, voltage and the polarity and inter-electrode resistance of the thyristor. The thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier; measuring its control electrode and inter-electrode resistance is the basic means of judging whether it is good or bad. If a line short circuit fault occurs in the steering gear system, it often manifests as instantaneous fuse blowing or tripping, and it is necessary to distinguish by live inspection whether it is an external line short circuit or an internal component breakdown. The corresponding treatment measure for input wiring disconnection is welding. Welding is a process in which the solder is melted by heating, atomic diffusion occurs between the weldment and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer with good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength is formed; welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products.

Marine electrical equipment widely uses printed circuit board.

The marine motor contains components such as bearing and brush. The bearing is used to support the rotation of the rotor; its fault will cause the motor to overheat, vibration and abnormal noise, and it is one of the direct causes of the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when the upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very large uneven noise and the characteristic of overheating of the bearing end cover. Checking the bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition are both maintenance contents for the bearing. Breakage of the connecting rod of one phase of the circuit breaker will cause the contact of that phase to fail to close, and the treatment method is to replace the connecting rod; an increase in the angle between the detachable connecting rods of the current-limiting switch release mechanism will cause the contact to fail to close, so the state of the connecting rod also needs to be included in the inspection scope.

Ships whose main engine is a diesel engine are usually equipped with an auxiliary fuel oil boiler to undertake the heating task; what is used more on ships in our country is the automatic fuel oil boiler with an evaporation capacity of 1.8t/h, and its air pressure range is 294～686kPa. The control system of this automatic fuel oil boiler is composed of parts such as the automatic regulation system, program controller, automatic protection and sound and light alarm; the control box should be centrally installed near the boiler, has manual and automatic control functions, and the two can be switched. During boiler operation, water level control is realized by automatic water supply at low water level and stopping water supply at high water level; once the water level drops to the dangerous water level, the system immediately gives a sound and light alarm and stops all systems from working; pressure control is manifested as automatic ignition at low pressure and automatic extinguishing at high pressure; when the steam pressure reaches the maximum value, a sound and light alarm is given and the safety valve is automatically opened to release steam and reduce pressure.

In addition, the system is also provided with an automatic fuel oil temperature regulation link to keep the fuel oil at a suitable temperature. The ignition procedure follows the principle of "fire waits for oil", and sequentially completes pre-purge, fuel oil pump starting, ignition transformer energization and fuel injection; if ignition fails, the system performs automatic extinguishing, post-purge and alarm actions.

During operation, the automatic fuel oil boiler will have a variety of typical faults, including failure to ignite, failure to automatically supply water, failure to automatically ignite and burn to raise pressure, automatic extinguishing after flame is produced during ignition, failure to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature, as well as automatic flameout, too frequent ignition, etc. That is to say, the automatic fuel oil boiler will have the phenomenon of failure to automatically ignite and burn to raise pressure, and will also have the situations of automatic flameout and too frequent ignition. For these faults, there are respectively maintenance methods for failure to ignite, maintenance methods for failure to automatically supply water, maintenance methods for failure to automatically ignite and burn to raise pressure, maintenance methods for automatic extinguishing after flame is produced during ignition, maintenance methods for failure to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature, and maintenance methods for automatic flameout and too frequent ignition that can be adopted.

Among them, the maintenance methods for failure to ignite automatically and failure to raise pressure by combustion are applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers, and the maintenance methods for automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition are likewise applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers. Supporting the maintenance are also the debugging of the alarm subsystem, the debugging of the automatic feedwater system and the debugging of the ignition control system, and these debugging items are likewise applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers. The maintenance work of automatic oil-fired boilers covers control system maintenance, ignition system maintenance, feedwater system maintenance, air-oil regulating device maintenance and exhaust gas boiler mechanical transmission maintenance, and attention must be paid to the various requirements in the daily maintenance precautions for boiler control systems. In terms of component composition, the automatic oil-fired boiler includes the ignition rod, photoresistor, solenoid valve, water level sensor, proportional pressure regulator and electric proportional operator, and the servo motor is also one of its constituent parts.

Flame monitoring is accomplished by means of the photoresistor. The photoresistor is a semiconductor element whose resistance value changes with the strength of external light; the resistance is small when the light is strong and large when the light is weak, and it is made by depositing a layer of cadmium sulfide (CdS) film on a ceramic base. In complete darkness its resistance can reach several megohms or more, and under relatively strong light it can drop to several thousand ohms or even below 1kΩ. In marine auxiliary boilers, the photoresistor is used to detect the flame; when ignition succeeds, its resistance value decreases, causing 1JY to be energized, which in turn causes 3JZ to be energized and 4JZ to be energized, and contacts 31 and 28 of 4JZ open, the ignition transformer is de-energized, thereby stopping ignition. During debugging, the photoresistor can be taken out of the furnace chamber and illuminated with a flashlight to verify whether its resistance value decreases and whether the subsequent relay actions are normal. Common faults of the photoresistor include aging, the photosensitive window being covered by accumulated oil soot affecting the luminous flux, or the photosensitive tube not being aligned with the flame; during maintenance it is necessary to check whether it is aged, whether the photosensitive window is covered by accumulated oil soot affecting the luminous flux, or whether it is aligned with the flame. In terms of component classification, the photoresistor belongs to a type of resistor, and its resistance value can be measured with a multimeter; during measurement, at least one end of the resistor under test should be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistor, and never measure with power on.

The ignition rod is used to generate the ignition spark and ignite the fuel oil. When maintaining the ignition rod, it is necessary to check its gap, the insulation performance of the rod electrodes and the carbon deposit at the tip; if ignition fails, it is necessary to check whether the insulation of the ignition rod to ground or between each other is good. During debugging, pressing the manual button can make it generate an ignition spark; when there is no spark during the test, it is necessary to take it out of the furnace chamber to check its condition; if ignition fails and there is an ignition spark and oil traces, it may be caused by the ignition rod being too far from the oil nozzle. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of the fuel oil; during ignition it cuts off the fuel oil circulation circuit, causing the oil to enter the oil nozzle and spray; in the burner ignition program the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that the oil enters the oil nozzle and sprays. If ignition fails, it should be checked whether the solenoid valve coil is open-circuited and whether the valve core is stuck.

The automatic regulation of the combustion process is accomplished jointly by the proportional pressure regulator and the electric proportional operator. The model code of the proportional pressure regulator is YBD, and together with the electric proportional operator (DBC) it realizes the automatic regulation of the combustion process. The electric proportional operator internally contains core components such as the differential amplifier, thyristor and servo motor, and uses the bridge balance state formed by potentiometer R10 and R0 to control the start and stop of the servo motor. When the boiler steam pressure reaches the set value of the pressure regulator, the bridge is balanced and the servo motor stops; when the boiler steam pressure is lower than the set value, the bridge loses balance and the servo motor rotates in the direction of increasing the oil and air dampers. Specifically, when the steam pressure is lower than the set value, YBD drives the sliding contact of potentiometer R0 to rise, causing the bridge to lose balance and triggering the servo motor to act, triggering the thyristor to make the motor rotate in the direction of increasing the oil and air dampers; when the servo motor rotates, it drives the sliding contact of the feedback potentiometer R10 to move until a new bridge balance is formed with the setting potentiometer, and then it stops.

The maintenance cycle of the proportional pressure regulator is once every 2 months, and it is necessary to check whether the upper and lower pressure setting values meet the requirements. In automatic combustion regulation of the boiler, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance. During daily maintenance, the contacts of each potentiometer must be cleaned frequently to prevent oil and water from entering the control box and affecting contact performance; during troubleshooting, check whether the sliding contact of the potentiometer driven by the pressure regulator is in good contact, and whether the moving parts are jammed. The servo motor is used to adjust the opening of the air damper and the oil damper, rotates according to the bridge output signal, and drives the feedback potentiometer to adjust so that the bridge is rebalanced. In boiler combustion regulation, the differential amplifier and thyristor control the winding to be energized so as to adjust the air-fuel ratio.

Daily maintenance of the boiler control system has several specific requirements: regularly clean the control box to prevent oil and water from entering the interior of the control box; clean the contacts of the multi-circuit time relay and other relays and contactors; frequently clean the contacts of each potentiometer to maintain good contact; frequently check the insulation of the ignition system, especially the insulation condition of the ignition rod; clean the carbon deposits on the tip of the ignition rod to maintain ignition performance; regularly check the insulation resistance of each motor and monitor the heating condition during operation;

Clean the water level observer to prevent scale accumulation. The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship power system. It is a low-voltage control device with the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size, and is used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself. The time relay is also an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship power system, and its codes are KT, SJ, SL. The pressure relay is a non-electrical relay with pressure as the input signal, the sensing element is an air bag, and the actuating part is a contact. It is used for automatic control and protection of ship boilers, air compressors and pump sets, and is used as a control device in auxiliary boilers for automatic control of steam pressure. The thyristor, also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, has its polarity, inter-pole resistance and control electrode measured with a multimeter.

During diagnosis and maintenance, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions of components (assemblies) and their locations of electrical equipment. They must be very familiar with the ship-wide electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components, and master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. The contents of observation include abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status and equipment operating parameters. Specifically, check whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. In the maintenance and debugging of PLC and electrical control systems, switching on the power supply is a key step, referring to the process of connecting the power supply for functional testing or self-diagnosis after confirming that there is no short circuit or earthing fault; before switching on the power supply, the input and output parts must be tested for short circuit or earthing faults, and only after confirmation can power be switched on; when the PLC is switched on, the self-diagnosis process begins. If an internal CPU error occurs, the panel "CPU Error" lamp indicates an abnormality.

Troubleshooting of the electrical control system of a marine auxiliary boiler usually starts with the conventional fault diagnosis method, and the first step of this method is to use observation. After observation, it is also necessary to further check the monitoring and indicating device in order to judge the scope of the fault.

When testing components and devices, the multimeter is a common tool for measuring resistance and can be used to measure their resistance values. The category of resistors includes the photoresistor. The photoresistor is a semiconductor element whose resistance value changes with the intensity of external light: when the light is strong, the resistance is small, and when the light is weak, the resistance is large. In ship boilers, the photoresistor is used as a flame monitoring element. When ignition is successful, its resistance decreases, causing the relay to operate and stop ignition. During debugging, the photoresistor can be taken out of the furnace chamber and illuminated with a flashlight, and the operation of the relay can be observed to verify whether its performance is normal. The contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, among which the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start.

There are many causes of failure to ignite: ignition gap problems, ignition rod insulation problems, ignition transformer problems, solenoid valve faults, clogged oil nozzle, oil circuit system pressure problems, and 2JZ faults can all cause failure to ignite. The troubleshooting method for failure to ignite is applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers and requires investigation from both the electrical and oil circuit aspects. On the electrical side, first check whether an ignition spark is produced at the ignition gap; if there is no spark, check the insulation of the ignition rod and leads to ground or the insulation between them, check the insulation of the ignition transformer to ground, and check whether the ignition gap is too large or too small, and finally check the ignition transformer and ignition button 4LA. If there is a spark, check whether DF operates; if it does not operate, check whether it is open-circuited. On the oil circuit side, if the oil nozzle does not inject oil, check whether the oil nozzle is clogged and whether pressure is established in the oil circuit system. If the normally open contact of 2JZ is not closed, the combustion ratio regulator will be put into operation during ignition and will open the air damper very wide, causing ignition failure; at this time, check 2JZ itself, the coil circuit and the contact closing condition. During commissioning, if there is a spark and oil traces but ignition still fails, it may be that the ignition rod is too far from the oil nozzle or the oil pressure is insufficient causing poor atomization; the air damper is linked with the oil throttle, and if the air damper is closed too small ignition is difficult, so check whether the air damper opening is appropriate. During commissioning, pressing the manual button can make it produce an ignition spark; when testing for no spark, it needs to be taken out of the furnace chamber to check its condition.

Failure to feed water automatically is another type of fault symptom of automatic oil-fired boilers and belongs to a specific fault type of the automatic feed water system. Faults in the circuit or relay controlling 7JZ or 8JZ, as well as faults in contactor 1CJ or the pump auxiliary unit, will cause failure to feed water automatically. The troubleshooting method for failure to feed water automatically is likewise applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers: first perform manual feed water; if manual feed water is normal, it indicates that the fault lies in the circuit or relay controlling 7JZ or 8JZ itself, and at this time only 7JZ itself and the normally closed contact of 2JY need to be checked; if manual feed water is also abnormal, it indicates a fault in contactor 1CJ or the pump shaft unit itself, and contactor 1CJ or the pump shaft unit should be checked.

The step of interviewing the operator is the preceding step of observation; after observation, the step of checking the monitoring and indicating device is entered, that is, observation is the preceding step of checking the monitoring and indicating device. In the measurement step, the multimeter is a commonly used tool; it contains a changeover switch and can be used to measure resistance and thyristors. The function of the changeover switch is to select the measurement object and select the range; it is used to set the working state, select the measurement point or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts; a changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. A thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier; its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode can be measured.

Automatic oil-fired boilers will experience several typical faults during operation. They may fail to ignite automatically and build up pressure by combustion, may produce a flame during ignition and then extinguish automatically, may fail to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature, and may also extinguish automatically or ignite too frequently. As for the former fault, the automatic changeover switches K1~K7 not being in position can cause failure to ignite automatically and build up pressure by combustion; mistaken operation of relays 6JZ and 5JZ for minimum water level and ignition failure can cause this phenomenon; faults in pressure relays YD and 1JZ can cause this phenomenon; and a fault in sequence controller 1JS can likewise cause this phenomenon. During troubleshooting, first switch to manual operation; if the furnace also cannot be started, troubleshoot according to the failure-to-ignite fault; if manual operation is normal, it indicates that the automatic control system has a problem, and at this time press the start button to see whether the fan and oil pump are running. If the fan and oil pump do not run, the first step is to confirm whether the automatic changeover switches K1~K4 are in position, whether the two relays 6JZ and 5JZ for minimum water level and ignition failure have operated mistakenly, and whether pressure relays YD and 1JZ are normal.

If the fan and oil pump operate normally, it is determined that the sequence controller 1JS is faulty; it is necessary to check whether each contact of the 1JS relay operates according to the delay table, and at the same time check whether the normally closed contact of 4JZ (31, 28) is closed.

A flame generated at ignition then extinguishing automatically belongs to a fault in the flame monitoring link. Aging of the photoresistor Rg can cause a flame generated at ignition to extinguish automatically, and a fault in the 1JT relay or its circuit can also cause this phenomenon. The maintenance procedure for a flame generated at ignition then extinguishing automatically is likewise applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers; it is necessary to focus on checking whether the photoresistor Rg is aged, whether the photosensitive window is covered by accumulated oil soot affecting the luminous flux, and to check whether the 1JT relay itself or its circuit has an open-circuit fault, as well as whether its working power supply rectifier bridge 1ZX has an open-circuit fault. Faults in the above components will cause the system not to detect the flame, thereby triggering the ignition-failure automatic protection action.

Failure to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature, manifested as relatively large fluctuations in air pressure and air temperature during boiler combustion, indicates that the air-oil ratio regulator is not working normally. A change in the setting value of the pressure regulator YBD can cause failure to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature, and a fault in the electric proportional regulator DBC can also cause this phenomenon. During maintenance it is necessary to confirm whether the setting value of the pressure regulator YBD has changed, whether its own working state is good, whether its moving parts are jammed, and whether the sliding contact of the potentiometer driven by it makes reliable contact; it is also necessary to check whether the parameters of the differential amplifier of the electric proportional regulator DBC are symmetrical, whether components are damaged, whether the AC electronic switch thyristors VTH1～VTH4 are normal, whether the servo motor M works normally, and whether the contact of the feedback potentiometer driven by it makes good contact. The maintenance procedure for failure to automatically maintain normal air pressure and air temperature is applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers. The automatic oil-fired boiler includes a photoresistor, a servo motor and a potentiometer. In boiler combustion regulation, the differential amplifier and thyristor control the winding to be energized so as to adjust the air-oil ratio; when rotating, it drives the sliding contact of the feedback potentiometer R10 to move, so that the bridge reaches balance again and then stops. The potentiometer is used for bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 driven by the motor M is balanced;

Automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition are another fault symptom. Too small a deviation between the upper and lower limit values of the air pressure relay YD can cause automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition, and improper adjustment of the air damper mechanical linkage can also cause this phenomenon. The maintenance procedure for automatic flameout and excessively frequent ignition is applicable to automatic oil-fired boilers; it is necessary to check whether the deviation between the upper and lower limit values of the air pressure relay YD is too small, so as to prevent frequent ignition and furnace startup and shutdown caused by a small deviation; it is necessary to check whether the electric proportional regulator can automatically adjust the air-oil ratio with changes in steam pressure, to prevent loss of control leading to a pressure rise and flameout; if the electric proportional regulator still maintains large air damper and large oil throttle combustion when the deviation between the steam pressure and the given value is small, automatic flameout will soon result; it is also necessary to check whether the air damper mechanical linkage is properly adjusted, because improper adjustment also often causes the boiler to flame out.

When the marine auxiliary boiler electrical control system fails to ignite, troubleshooting can be started according to the conventional fault diagnosis method, and the starting point of this method is the maintenance procedure of observation. After observation is completed, the step of checking the monitoring and indicating device is entered, and there is likewise a sequence between the two.

The phenomenon of failure to ignite occurs during operation of the automatic oil-fired boiler, and its causes involve multiple aspects. During maintenance, first check whether there is a spark at the ignition gap; if there is no spark, check the insulation, the transformer and button 4LA. If there is a spark but ignition still fails, check whether the solenoid valve DF operates; if it does not operate, check for an open coil or a jammed valve core. In the oil circuit, check whether the oil nozzle is clogged, whether the oil circuit pressure is established, and whether the normally open contact of 2JZ is closed. If 2JZ does not operate, the combustion proportional regulator will open the air damper too wide, resulting in ignition failure. When there is no spark during the test, it is necessary to take it out of the furnace chamber to check its state; during commissioning, pressing the manual button can make it produce an ignition spark;

The commissioning of the alarm subsystem applies to automatic oil-fired boilers. Before commissioning, close only DZ1 and pull out 1RD so that only the alarm and water level detection sections are energized. At this time, if there is no water in the boiler, the alarm bell will sound immediately; if the armature of 3JY or 5JY is pushed once with a screwdriver, the alarm can be stopped; if the armature of the ignition failure relay 5JZ is pushed once, the alarm will also sound immediately, indicating that the alarm subsystem works normally. In the same way, the armatures of contactors 1C to 5C need to be pushed to observe whether the indications of each operation indicator lamp are normal. If the simulated action does not conform to the circuit principle, the fault should be found and eliminated to restore the correct logic. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in the electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the magnetic force of the coil to pull in or release, and is used to control the action of the contact or braking; a stuck armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start; failure or loss of the armature return spring is one of the main reasons why the contactor does not release or releases slowly after the stop button is pressed.

The commissioning of the automatic feed water system likewise applies to automatic oil-fired boilers. Before commissioning, close DZ1 and DZ2 to supply power to the control circuit, and close K8 of the water level detection section to the 71 side. Commissioning follows the principle of manual first and automatic second: first set K1 to the manual position to make the feed water pump run and inject water into the boiler; when the boiler is full of water, close K1 to the automatic position, open the drain valve to drain the boiler water to the low water level to test automatic starting. If the feed water pump can start automatically, open DZ2 to stop feed water, so that the water level continues to reach the lowest limit position; at the lowest limit water level an alarm should be triggered; if it cannot alarm, the 6JZ relay and its circuit need to be checked. The function of the drain valve in this process is to drain the boiler water to the low water level after opening, so as to observe whether the feed water pump can start automatically.

The commissioning of the ignition control system applies to automatic oil-fired boilers. Before commissioning, ensure that the boiler water level is normal, and close DZ1 to DZ4 to energize the ignition control subsystem; close K3 to the manual position to energize 1JZ and energize the ignition control subsystem; close K to the manual position, 3C is energized, the fan runs, and pre-purge is performed; if it is the first pre-purge, the time should be longer; after pre-purge, close the air damper a little smaller and make a mark. Close K5 to the manual position to start the fuel oil pump so as to build up oil pressure in the pipeline. When the manual ignition button 3LA is pressed, the ignition rod produces a spark and the fuel oil valve opens to inject oil. If ignition fails, it is necessary to open DZ5 to stop the oil pump or close the fuel oil valve, and take out the ignition rod for inspection. If there is a spark and oil traces but ignition fails, it may be caused by the ignition rod being too far away or insufficient oil pressure leading to poor atomization.

The automatic oil-fired boiler includes periodic maintenance items such as ignition system maintenance, feed water system maintenance, air-oil regulating device maintenance and exhaust gas boiler mechanical transmission maintenance. The cycle of ignition system maintenance is once every 2 months; the maintenance content and requirements are to check the gap of the ignition rod, the insulation performance of the rod electrodes, and the working conditions of the photosensitive element and the solenoid valve, maintain good light transmittance of the photosensitive element, and the photosensitive element should be used in rotation periodically. The cycle of feed water system maintenance is once every 2 months; it is necessary to check whether the action of the automatic feed water controller and the water level sensor is sensitive and reliable, and whether the watertightness is good. The cycle of exhaust gas boiler mechanical transmission maintenance is once every 2 months; the core content is to check whether the electrical and mechanical parts of the three-way commutation valve are flexible and reliable. The water level sensor is used to detect the boiler water level; when the water level reaches the high water level, feed water is automatically stopped; when the water level drops to the dangerous water level, it can send out an audible and visual alarm signal and stop all systems from working; its maintenance cycle is once every 2 months, and it is necessary to check whether its action is sensitive and reliable and whether its watertightness is good. When the boiler steam pressure reaches the set value, the potentiometer R1 driven by it balances the bridge, and the servo motor stops rotating; the sensor is placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, and its function is to send out an error signal; the control platform contains the sensor.

Composition and control modes of the general alarm device The general alarm device is alarm equipment that issues emergency general mobilization and assembly signals to all crew members and passengers when a ship encounters an emergency such as a major marine casualty or fire. In terms of composition, the general alarm device includes four parts: the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box. The shutter is used to perform on and off operations for the alarm signal, the alarm bell is responsible for emitting the audible signal, the alarm lamp is responsible for emitting the light signal, and the junction box serves as the connection and distribution link between the various components and between the device and the ship's electrical network. The above four together constitute the on-site execution part of the general alarm device, and none can be omitted.

In terms of control mode, the general alarm device includes two modes: direct control mode and indirect control mode. In direct control mode, the emission of the alarm signal is driven directly by the operating component to the loads such as the alarm bell and alarm lamp, with few control links and direct action; in indirect control mode, the operating component does not directly drive the loads, but instead connects or disconnects the load circuits such as the alarm bell and alarm lamp through an intermediate control link.

The coexistence of the two control modes enables the general alarm device to adapt to the requirements of different ships and different installation locations for the structure of the alarm circuit. Regardless of which control mode is adopted, the general alarm device includes the general alarm device control system, by which the execution part composed of the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box is uniformly controlled and coordinated, so that the audible alarm and the light alarm act according to predetermined requirements.

Inspection points of the general alarm device in the maintenance of the auxiliary boiler electrical control system In the maintenance work of the marine auxiliary boiler electrical control system, the general alarm device is an important link in the alarm branch. Since the general alarm device includes the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, the four parts should be inspected item by item during maintenance. For the shutter, it should be confirmed whether its on-off action is reliable and whether its contacts are in good contact; for the alarm bell, it should be confirmed whether its sound is normal and whether there is abnormal sound caused by damp or vibration; for the alarm lamp, it should be confirmed whether its filament, lamp holder and light-transmitting cover are intact; for the junction box, it should be confirmed whether its internal wiring is firm, whether the markings are clear, and whether there are hidden dangers of looseness and short circuit.

These inspections should all be carried out with the cooperation of the general alarm device control system, that is, alarm commands are applied separately through the control system, and observation is made as to whether the responses of the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box at each link are consistent with the commands.

In the inspection of the control mode, a distinction should be made as to whether the ship's general alarm device adopts the direct control mode or the indirect control mode. If it is the direct control mode, the focus should be on inspecting the direct circuit from the operating component to the alarm bell and alarm lamp; if it is the indirect control mode, the focus should be on inspecting the intermediate control link and its connection relationship with the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box. The circuit structures of the two control modes are different, and the distribution of fault points is also different, so they cannot be treated the same during maintenance.

The general alarm device includes the general alarm device control system, so the inspection of the control system should also include whether its control logic for the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box is normal, and whether the control system itself can correctly drive the above execution components after an alarm command is issued.

Coordination relationships to be noted during maintenance The general alarm device includes the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, and also includes the direct control mode, indirect control mode and general alarm device control system. These constituent parts are not isolated from one another. The action result of the shutter must be sent to the alarm bell and alarm lamp through the junction box; whether the alarm bell and alarm lamp act simultaneously and in what order they act depends on the control mode adopted by the general alarm device control system. During maintenance, if only the alarm bell is replaced or only the alarm lamp is adjusted without inspecting the shutter and junction box, the fault in the alarm branch often cannot be completely eliminated. Similarly, if only the circuit under the direct control mode is inspected while the role of the intermediate link under the indirect control mode is ignored, missed inspection will also result.

Therefore, in the maintenance of the electrical control system of marine auxiliary boilers, the general alarm device should be regarded as a whole, and inspection and repair should be carried out item by item around the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp, junction box, direct control mode, indirect control mode and the control system of the general alarm device, so that the general alarm device can reliably issue emergency general mobilization and assembly signals to all crew members and passengers under emergency conditions such as major marine casualties or fires.

Composition and control modes of the general alarm device Under emergency conditions such as major marine casualties or fires on a ship, the general alarm device undertakes the task of issuing emergency general mobilization and assembly signals to all crew members and passengers, so it is also called the emergency assembly alarm. The device is composed of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp, junction box, etc., among which the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box each undertake different functional links and together constitute a complete alarm circuit. According to the different ways of connecting the emergency power supply, the control modes of the general alarm device are divided into two types: direct control mode and indirect control mode.

The direct control mode is suitable for ships with a small number of installed alarm bells and a small current capacity of the feeder main. In this mode, when the shutter is pressed on the bridge, its contact directly connects the emergency power supply, and the alarm bells and alarm lamps of the whole ship immediately emit sound and light signals simultaneously. That is to say, in the direct control mode, the shutter undertakes the function of directly connecting the emergency power supply, while the alarm bells and alarm lamps rely on this power supply to sound and light respectively.

The fundamental difference between the direct control mode and the indirect control mode is that no contactor is used; instead, power is supplied directly by the shutter contact.

The indirect control mode is suitable for ships with a large number of alarm bells and a large current capacity of the feeder main, also for ships with a relatively thick cross-section of the main feeder, and for ships where it is difficult to connect the alarm bell power supply to the bridge and then feed it. In this mode, a contactor is installed on the battery charge/discharge panel and controlled by the shutter or button on the bridge; the alarm bells and alarm lamps of the whole ship connect the emergency power supply through the closing of the normally open contact of the contactor. It can be seen that in the indirect control mode, the alarm bells and alarm lamps are no longer directly supplied by the shutter contact, but obtain the emergency power supply via the normally open contact of the contactor.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship's power system, belongs to low-voltage control apparatus, is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor itself includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance is carried out on these parts.

Functions and interfaces of the control system of the general alarm device The control system of the general alarm device is provided with two buttons, "general alarm" and "manual alarm", and is provided with a sound and light alarm device for main power supply failure. The general alarm signal is output in a cycle of seven short and one long, repeated every 2 s; the manual alarm signal is output in the on/off rhythm of the key switch. When this system is connected to the public address system, sounds of different rhythm frequencies can be played from the loudspeaker to distinguish the alarm modes. Its external input terminals include the emergency alarm button, fire alarm equipment (connected with a 2 min delay) and the remote control box beside the lifeboat; when output to the alarm bell control terminal, a closed contact is output under the alarm state to control the electric bell. In addition, the system is also provided with a general alarm remote control box and can output to the engine room alarm indicator terminal, the fog horn control terminal and the public address system.

Diagnosis and treatment of common faults The control system of the general alarm device of a certain bulk carrier will show several typical faults during use, which can be troubleshooted one by one according to the phenomena.

When only one of the remote start/stop buttons works, the cause is that the common wire of the remote buttons is connected incorrectly. The phenomenon that only one of the remote start/stop buttons works corresponds to the treatment measure of checking whether the common wire of the remote buttons is connected correctly, and by restoring the correct connection of the common wire, both buttons can function normally.

When there is no response to the start operation of the remote button and the control panel, the common cause is that the remote start/stop button is connected to the normally closed contact. The phenomenon that there is no response to the start operation of the remote button and the control panel corresponds to the treatment step of checking whether the remote start/stop button is connected to the normally closed contact, and if so, changing it to the normally open contact; if it is confirmed to be connected to the normally closed contact, change it to be connected to the normally open contact, and the operation will resume responding.

When the situation occurs that after a start operation the remote start/stop button indicator lamp is on and the indicator lamp on the control board is off, the root cause is that the power supply polarity is reversed. Reversed power supply polarity will cause the remote start/stop button indicator lamp to be on and the indicator lamp on the control board to be off after a start operation; and the phenomenon that after a start operation the remote start/stop button indicator lamp is on and the indicator lamp on the control board is off corresponds to checking whether the power supply polarity is reversed, and if so, correcting it as the corrective measure. If reversed power supply polarity is confirmed, correcting the polarity will eliminate the fault; its manifestation is that the remote start/stop button indicator lamp remains on while the indicator lamp on the control board is off, and the corrective method is to correct the power supply polarity connection.

When the indicator lamp on the control board is off after the general alarm device is started, it is likewise necessary to check whether the power supply polarity is reversed. The phenomenon of the indicator lamp being off may also be caused, in single-speed non-reversing and reversing drive control systems, by failure of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer or KM auxiliary contact; if any one of the functional logic events composed of the bulb, lamp holder, transformer and KM auxiliary contact fails, the indicator lamp will be off, and the phenomenon of the indicator lamp being off can also occur in the air compressor control circuit.

In the overall PLC inspection, if the POWER lamp off, the step of checking for a power supply fault shall be performed, and a power supply fault corresponds to the corrective measure of check the power supply; when the electric fan starts slowly, the troubleshooting method includes checking whether the power supply voltage is too low; when the electric drill fails to start and there is no voltage at the power supply, the power supply line should be checked. These practices of check the power supply are consistent with the approach of checking whether the power supply polarity is reversed when the indicator lamp on the control board of the general alarm device is off.

When inspecting and measuring the relevant electrical apparatus to troubleshoot the above faults, instruments are often needed to measure circuit parameters. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instrument, used to understand equipment status; the measurable performance is the current value, and the measuring tools used include the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. Using a multimeter to measure current and using a clamp-on ammeter to measure current are both commonly used on-site means. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after opening the circuit.

Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems, so when checking the power supply circuit of the alarm device, attention to the current value helps determine whether the circuit is in a normal state.

The fuse is used for overload and short circuit protection in the ship's power system, and the fuse corresponds to the symbol FU. The fuse is a protective electrical apparatus that, when overload and short circuit occur in the power network or electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element; it belongs to the distribution electrical apparatus and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. In the power supply circuit of the general alarm device, the fuse likewise performs the role of overload and short circuit protection.

The junction box is a component used in the ship's electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical elements. In the general alarm device, the junction box is one of the constituent parts; the solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box but is connected directly into the local control box; when testing the thermal resistance type sensor, the wiring of the temperature sensor must be disconnected in the junction box. These practices show that the connection method of the junction box differs in different circuits, and during maintenance it should be handled according to the actual connection of each circuit.
