The alarm lamp is used in the general alarm device to emit a light signal. In direct control mode, the alarm lamp is connected to the emergency power supply through the shutter contact to emit light; in indirect control mode, the alarm lamp is connected to the emergency power supply through the normally open contact of the contactor to emit light. During a fault alarm, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room flashes; after the fault alarm is silenced, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room goes out. The alarm bell, together with the alarm lamp, emits sound and light signals by connecting to the emergency power supply: in direct control mode, the alarm bell is connected directly to the emergency power supply by the shutter contact in the wheelhouse; in indirect control mode, the alarm bell is connected to the emergency power supply through the closing of the normally open contact of the contactor.

Ship automatic fire monitoring and alarm devices are mainly divided into three categories according to installation area and detection medium: automatic fire monitoring and alarm devices for cabins, automatic fire monitoring and alarm devices for dry cargo holds, and combustible gas detection devices. The complete device consists of two major parts, the alarm controller and the fire detector; its basic function is to receive signals sent from the detectors, and after processing, give audible and visual alarms and display the specific location where the fire alarm occurs, thereby helping the crew to take fire-fighting measures as early as possible.

The alarm controller is the core component of this device. At present, the main types used on ships are relay-contactor control type, PLC control type and microcomputer control type. Its task is to receive the fire signal sent from the fire detector at the monitoring site, and after processing, give audible and visual fire alarm signals and display the location of the fire alarm. In the bus-coded transmission system, the fire alarm judgment function is undertaken by the controller, that is, the controller realizes the fire alarm judgment of analog signals. This type of controller can be used in conjunction with intelligent ion smoke detectors, etc., and improves moisture resistance through adjustment of circuit parameters. As the core component of the bus-coded transmission type centralized alarm system, the alarm controller represents the development direction of marine fire monitoring systems.

There is a typical phenomenon during installation: if the two wires on the detector base are connected in reverse, after the detector is installed on the ceiling base, the alarm controller will display an alarm in that area; at this time, a multimeter can be used to check the polarity and then reconnect them correctly.

The fire detector consists of a fire parameter sensor or measuring element, a detection signal processing unit and a fire judgment circuit, in which the sensor is responsible for converting physical and chemical effects into measured values. Fire detectors include four major types: smoke fire detectors, heat fire detectors, light fire detectors and combustible gas fire detectors; the detectors are mainly composed of these four types. The interior of the smoke detector contains an ionization chamber or a photosensitive element, and detection is achieved through the influence of smoke on the ion current or luminous flux. In actual systems on ships, detectors are usually connected in parallel, divided into two-wire and four-wire systems; in the two-wire system, the power supply and signal lines coincide, and when a fault occurs, the internal terminal post disconnection will cause an open-circuit alarm in the loop.

Heat detectors are suitable for locations with more dust and oil mist; the fixed-temperature operating temperatures are generally 60℃, 70℃ and 90℃. Light detectors need to be used in conjunction with smoke or heat detectors, and there must be no light interference of the same wavelength in the detection area.

According to statistics, smoke fire detectors can detect more than 70% of fires and are widely used in ships; their main types include ion type and photoelectric type. The ion type uses the principle of air ionization to detect fires; the photoelectric type uses smoke to change the light intensity received by the photosensitive element to send an alarm signal, and is divided into laser type and scattering type according to the absorption and scattering effects of smoke on light. The moisture-resistance adaptive performance of the single-source ion smoke detector is superior to that of the dual-source type. According to the structural form of the internal ionization chamber, it is further divided into dual-source smoke fire detectors and single-source smoke fire detectors. The dual-source smoke detector uses the adsorption effect of smoke particles on charged ions to change the characteristic curve of the detection ionization chamber, and then processes the voltage difference ΔV formed by the change of the characteristic curve through an electronic circuit to confirm the fire and give an alarm; the dual-source design can reduce the influence of changes in ambient temperature, humidity and air pressure on the ion current; compared with the single-source type, its environmental adaptability and working stability are higher, and it is currently used more in ships. When the single-source smoke fire detector is detecting a fire, both its smoke detection ionization chamber and compensation ionization chamber work in the sensitive region of their characteristic curves, and the fire detection and alarm function is realized by using the change in electrode potential;

it improves the ability to adapt to slow changes of tiny particles in the operating environment; in terms of the moisture resistance required in humid areas, its adaptive performance is much better than that of the dual-source ion smoke fire detector.

The photoelectric smoke fire detector is a type of point-type fire detector, and is divided into laser type and scattering type according to the absorption and scattering effects of smoke particles on light. In the laser type detector, smoke particles reduce the luminous flux passing through the light path, causing the photocurrent of the light-receiving element to decrease, and the magnitude of the change of the photocurrent relative to the initial calibration value reflects the smoke concentration. Photoelectric smoke fire detectors include two types: light-attenuation photoelectric smoke fire detectors and scattered-light photoelectric smoke fire detectors. The working principle of the light-attenuation photoelectric smoke fire detector is: when smoke appears around the detector, the smoke particles entering the photoelectric detection dark chamber absorb and scatter the light emitted by the light source, reducing the luminous flux passing through the light path, thereby reducing the photocurrent generated on the light-receiving element; the magnitude of the change of this photocurrent relative to the initial calibration value reflects the smoke concentration.

Photosensitive fire detectors include two types: ultraviolet detectors and infrared detectors. The ultraviolet detector responds to the ultraviolet spectrum emitted by flames; its sensitive element may use solid substances such as zinc sulfide and lead selenate, or may use a light pipe; the detection angle is 90°, and during installation it is necessary to ensure that the protected area is within the coverage area; it is suitable for areas with visible flames such as oil treatment areas on drilling platforms, wellheads, and explosion-proof areas of chemical tankers; because of its high sensitivity and susceptibility to interference, there must be no light of the same wavelength as the detector within the detection area, and in the same area it must be used together with a smoke-sensing or heat-sensing detector as an auxiliary detector. The basic structure of the infrared detector includes a filtering device and a lens system; it works by screening out unwanted wavelengths such as the spectra of the sun and fluorescent lamps, and focuses the incoming light energy onto an infrared-sensitive phototube or photoresistor; it has the advantages of a broad field of view, high sensitivity, and strong anti-interference capability, and its general detection angle is 140°; it likewise belongs to the photosensitive detectors in the classification of fire detectors commonly used on ships.

Combustible gas fire detectors, also called flammable gas detection systems, belong to one of the four major types of fire detectors commonly used on ships, alongside smoke-sensing, heat-sensing, and photosensitive types.

In the maintenance and testing process, resistance, voltage, and current are commonly measured quantities. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; when measuring resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter or voltmeter. The measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter, ammeter, or clamp-on ammeter; measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. The multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, and current, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control the motor in the ship's power system; it belongs to low-voltage control apparatus and is mainly used to control the motor in electric drive systems, featuring accurate and reliable operation, high operating frequency, long life, and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost entirely driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes components such as the arc chute, main contact, core, and coil; contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the control platform includes sensors. Analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The core component of the automatic fire monitoring and alarm device is the fire detector. The fire detector consists of a fire parameter sensor or measuring element, a detection signal processing unit, and a fire judgment circuit; its function is to convert the fire phenomenon into a signal that can be recognized by the alarm controller. In terms of wiring form, actual systems on ships usually adopt the parallel wiring method, specifically divided into two-wire and four-wire types. Smoke-sensing fire detectors include two main types: ionization smoke-sensing fire detectors and photoelectric smoke-sensing fire detectors. The photoelectric smoke-sensing fire detector uses smoke to change the intensity of light received by the photosensitive element to issue an alarm signal; it contains a photosensitive element internally and achieves detection through the effect of smoke on luminous flux. Photoelectric smoke-sensing fire detectors can further be divided, according to the absorption and scattering effects of smoke on light, into laser type and scattering type, among which is included the scattered-light photoelectric smoke-sensing fire detector.

The working process of the scattered-light photoelectric smoke-sensing fire detector can be described as follows: when smoke appears around the detector, the smoke particles entering the light-shielding dark chamber scatter the light of a certain wavelength emitted by the light-emitting element, i.e., the light source, causing the impedance of the light-receiving element located at a certain angle to change and generating a photocurrent. The magnitude of this photocurrent is related to the intensity of the scattered light, and thus reflects the concentration of smoke particles. When the scattered light energy is sufficient to generate a photocurrent of a certain magnitude, the excitation signal processing circuit issues a fire signal, and then, after the fire information is amplified, compared, or subjected to parameter calculation through the electronic circuit, the fire signal is transmitted.

The heat-sensitive fire detector is suitable for places where a large amount of dust, oil mist, and water vapor often exist, and smoke detectors cannot be used in such places. In important places, heat-sensitive detectors can be used together with smoke detectors to improve monitoring reliability or ensure accurate fire-extinguishing actions. According to the operating principle, heat-sensitive fire detectors are divided into three major categories: fixed-temperature type, rate-of-rise type, and rate-compensated type.

The operating principle of the fixed-temperature fire detector is: within a specified time, when the temperature rise caused by a fire exceeds a certain fixed value, an alarm is initiated. It has the characteristics of simple structure, high reliability, and few false operations but poor sensitivity. Common operating temperature set values are 60℃, 70℃, and 90℃. The main forms include bimetallic type, fusible alloy type, and thermistor type, and it is generally suitable for high-temperature places or places with large environmental changes such as kitchens, boiler rooms, and clothes-drying rooms. Environmental temperature changes in winter or summer will have a certain impact on the response time of the probe. The thermistor is a common form of fixed-temperature fire detector and is suitable for environments such as kitchens and boiler rooms; the thermistor is a special semiconductor device whose resistance value changes with the surface temperature. The commonly used NTC thermistor is a negative temperature coefficient one, that is, the resistance value decreases as the temperature rises, and it can be used for temperature compensation.

The operating condition of the rate-of-rise fire detector is: within a specified time, the rate of temperature rise caused by a fire exceeds a specified value. The point-type rate-of-rise detector operates according to the local thermal effect, and its main temperature-sensing elements include an air diaphragm chamber and a thermal semiconductor resistor.

The rate-compensated fire detector is formed by combining the functions of the fixed-temperature type and the rate-of-rise type detectors. If one function fails, the other function still works. Because of this redundant function, the reliability of fire monitoring is greatly improved, and it is widely used in actual ships. The rate-compensated fire detector is generally of point-type structure of the diaphragm chamber type or thermal semiconductor resistor type.

The photosensitive fire detector, also known as the flame detector, is divided into an ultraviolet detector sensitive to short wavelengths and an infrared detector sensitive to long wavelengths. The photosensitive fire detector is suitable for high-risk areas where visible flames may occur and smoke is relatively small. In the same area, it must be used together with a smoke or heat-sensitive detector as an auxiliary. Because of its high sensitivity, it is prone to false alarms, and light of the same wavelength is prohibited in the detection area.

In the infrared fire detector, the photoresistor serves as the photosensitive element and receives the light energy concentrated by the lens system.

The photoresistor is a semiconductor element whose resistance value changes with the intensity of external light. When the light is strong, the resistance is small; when the light is weak, the resistance is large. It is made by depositing a cadmium sulfide (CdS) film on a ceramic substrate and belongs to semiconductor elements. In complete darkness, its resistance can reach several megohms or more, and under relatively strong light it can drop to several thousand ohms or even below 1kΩ. In automatic oil-fired boilers, the photoresistor is used to detect the flame. When ignition succeeds, the resistance value of the photoresistor decreases, energizing 1JY, energizing 3JZ, and energizing 4JZ; 4JZ (31, 28) opens, and the ignition transformer is de-energized. Among the large category of resistor elements, in addition to the photoresistor, thermistors are also included.

The flammable gas detection system is suitable for ro-ro ships, ferries, fireboats, and oil tankers, and is used to detect whether flammable gas in cargo holds or certain compartments on board has reached a dangerous concentration. Since combustible gas density is usually greater than that of air and is not easily dispersed, it is necessary to detect whether its volume exceeds the lower explosion limit to prevent explosion. Among its detection methods, the chemical reagent method measures concentration by the length of color change from the reaction of gas with the reagent; it is accurate but cannot be reused. Infrared, spectrophotometer, and chromatographic separation methods can measure continuously and accurately, but because of high price they are only suitable for specialized industrial analysis. The catalytic filament method uses the principle that the resistance of a metal wire changes with gas concentration, but it is affected by inert gas, resulting in unreliable readings. In the fire alarm system, the combustible gas fire detector refers to the flammable gas detection system.

Water vapor is a type of fault cause that leads to false alarms of fire detectors. Water vapor can enter the detector and interfere with its normal operation, and water vapor condensed on relevant elements will affect the emission and reception of light. The presence of water sources and vapor sources such as kitchens, laundry rooms, or water leakage indoors is one of the main causes. In summer, especially during the plum rain season, seasonal effects easily lead to high indoor humidity. Most detectors are suitable for environments with relative humidity below 85%, and smoke detectors cannot be used in places where a large amount of water vapor often exists.

In the two-wire wiring mode, the power line and the signal line coincide. When the status is normal, terminal posts ⑥ and ⑦ inside the detector are closed to transmit power; the terminal probe is provided with terminal equipment such as a resistor or a Zener diode, and under normal monitoring status the system has a monitoring current in the microampere range. When a fire occurs, the detector operates so that the resistance drops sharply, generating an operating current in the milliampere range. If a probe fault causes the internal terminal posts to be unable to close, the system will display an open circuit of the loop or a probe fault. In the two-wire wiring of the fire detector, the terminal equipment may use a Zener diode to maintain the microampere-range monitoring current. In the four-wire wiring mode, the power line and the signal line are separated from each other; its working principle is similar to that of the two-wire wiring mode, and it is suitable for the wiring scenarios of marine fire detectors, requiring the ability to detect states such as detector detachment, faults and line open circuits, and requiring the ability to implement terminal resistor failure detection and fire alarm functions.

A Zener diode is a semiconductor diode whose voltage across the two terminals remains basically unchanged after breakdown; its circuit symbol is VS, and in circuits it is commonly denoted by "VS" plus a number, for example VS5 denotes the Zener diode numbered 5, and its forward conduction characteristics are the same as those of an ordinary diode. Zener diode faults manifest as open circuit, short circuit and unstable regulation value. When checking for black smoke, if there is no response to smoke and no alarm is ever given, it may be caused by damage to the Zener diode. A diode has unidirectional conductivity and is commonly denoted by VD in circuits; it is used for rectification, isolation, voltage regulation, etc., and according to its function it is divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), etc.; this broad category of diodes includes light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment, and the diode testing procedure is applicable to diodes.

The marine fire alarm system adopts bus-coded transmission technology to form a centralized alarm system, and this technical route constitutes the bus-coded transmission type centralized alarm system. This system is composed of parts such as the fire alarm controller, the zone display, the audible and visual alarm device and the control module; the temperature-sensing or smoke-sensing intelligent detector must be provided with an address module before it can be connected to the system, the control module is used to control fire-fighting linked-control equipment, and the zone display may be installed in the central control room or the accommodation area. A typical system adopts single-chip microcomputer technology, has the characteristics of few wires and convenient installation and commissioning, and is the development direction of marine fire monitoring systems. During maintenance, it is necessary to confirm that the detector bus has no short circuit and to measure the voltage at the detection bus output terminal of the controller; if after disconnecting the detector bus the voltage at the detection bus output terminal of the controller is still 8～12V, then the bus is faulty. The first two digits of the physical number represent the position of the detection bus on which the detector or module is located. Reversed wiring of the base will cause the zone alarm to be displayed on the alarm controller immediately after installation.

The central unit adopts a modular structure, and all circuit boards are installed in a standard frame; corresponding modules can be selected according to system requirements. It includes components such as the alarm processing board, the detection loop interface board, the relay board, the communication interface board, the digital input board, the digital output board, the digital detector interface board and the power supply unit. The alarm processing board is the core part of the central unit and is installed in the standard frame; the board contains one internal serial port and two external serial ports, the internal serial port is used to receive information from the detection loop interface board, the external serial ports are used to communicate with the operating unit, etc., and through the relay board the corresponding alarm and control functions are completed, through the communication interface board serial communication with an external computer and printer is realized, and it also controls the digital input board and the digital output board to complete the corresponding functions. The detection loop interface board is used to communicate with the detectors in the detection loop and to transmit the status of the detectors to the alarm processing board; each detection loop interface board can connect two detection loops, up to 95 detection loop interface boards can be inserted in one central unit, and their addresses are set by means of the multi-row switches on the board.

The relay board is controlled by the alarm processing board and drives equipment such as the general alarm system, alarm bells, and fire door electromagnets. It has two DC 24V/2A power outputs and three DC 24V/2A active signal outputs, provides four relay signal outputs with a capacity of 2A, and has two signals output in open-collector form. The communication interface board is controlled by the alarm processing board and is equipped with two RS-232 and two RS-485 serial communication ports to implement serial communication with external computers and printers. It is a modular component of the central unit and is installed in a standard frame. The digital input board is controlled by the alarm processing board and can accept 24 optoelectrically isolated digital signals; the digital output board is likewise controlled by the alarm processing board and can output 24 optoelectrically isolated digital signals. The digital detector interface board is specially used to connect detection branches composed of non-intelligent digital detectors, and the maximum connection capacity of a single digital detector interface board is four detection branches. The power supply unit contains two main components, the rectifier power supply and the storage battery, and has the functional characteristic of automatic switching between the two power supplies.

In terms of detection loops, one central unit can connect up to 190 detection loops, each loop can install 99 analog detectors or address units, and one loop can cover several decks of the ship; ordinary two-core unshielded marine cable can meet the requirements. The communication signals of the fire detection loop are specially processed, and ordinary two-core unshielded marine cable can be used. Marine cable is composed of conductive copper core wires, an insulation layer, and a protective layer, and is a component of marine electrical equipment. Its conductive core wires are stranded from no fewer than seven round soft copper wires of 0.26–2.74 mm to cope with vibration and impact on board. The insulation layer electrically insulates the conductive core wires, and the protective layer protects the cable from oil, water, and chemical corrosion; when necessary, armoring is added to enhance mechanical strength and interference resistance. When selecting, attention must be paid to the selection principles of marine cable.

The operating unit is the device through which the operator conducts human-machine dialogue with the system, and it is composed of the fire alarm large lamp, two groups of three-digit digital tubes, the liquid crystal display window, and the keyboard. When a fire alarm occurs in the system, the fire alarm large lamp in the upper left corner flashes, and the two groups of three-digit digital tubes on the right respectively display the alarm loop number and detector number; the liquid crystal display window in the upper right displays system information, and the keyboard below is used to input control commands such as date, time, and sensitivity. Some operating functions can be realized only after entering the corresponding password, so as to avoid misoperation by irrelevant personnel. When a fault occurs in the system, the fault lamp in the lower right corner flashes, and the corresponding light-emitting diode above it indicates the specific fault type. The display, as a component of the fire monitoring system, displays regional fire alarm information in the central control room or living area; in the water mist fire extinguishing system, it displays the release area on the bridge and gives an alarm indication;

The display belongs to radar equipment and is used to display radar images. Radar equipment includes the display, and the display involves cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface. The precautions for radar installation require attention to the display, and radar installation applies to the display. The display should be installed in the wheelhouse in a dry place without strong electromagnetic radiation and away from heat sources, fixed with a hardwood base, and the main radar display should be oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge.

In testing and maintenance, the multimeter includes a measuring circuit, the multimeter uses a resistor, and the multimeter uses a diode. The function of the measuring circuit is to convert different electrical quantities and different ranges. In the gas detection alarm device, it cooperates with gas-sensitive semiconductor elements to realize the continuous detection function. It is also one of the three basic components of the MF-30 and MF-47 analog multimeters. Because the magnetoelectric meter head can only pass microampere-level current, a conversion circuit is needed to measure different electrical quantities and ranges. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating function.

A light-emitting diode is a semiconductor device capable of emitting light in colors such as red, green and yellow, and has unidirectional conductivity; its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit operating-status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display screen; its outline dimensions include diameters of 3mm and 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle, and its operating current, depending on the model, is generally 1 to 30mA; in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage; for the precautions for using light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the light-emitting diode. RS is used in ship power systems for overload and short circuit protection, and belongs to the fuse series used in ship power systems for short circuit and overload protection of devices such as semiconductor rectifiers or thyristor rectifiers; the RS_0 type has a rated voltage of 250 to 900V and current specifications of 30 to 480A, and the RS_0 type is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers or their complete sets.

The flammable gas detection system is suitable for ro-ro ships, ferries, firefighting ships and oil tankers, to monitor cargo holds or compartments where flammable gases may accumulate. Its detection methods include the chemical reagent method, the infrared/spectrophotometer/chromatographic separation method, the catalytic filament method and the gas-sensitive semiconductor method. In the chemical reagent method, gas is passed through a glass tube containing a chemical reagent, and a color change caused by a chemical reaction is used for detection, with the length over which the reagent in the tube is decolorized serving as the measurement scale for gas concentration; this method is relatively accurate in measurement, but the indicating tube cannot be reused, and it is suitable for fixed-point measurement scenarios and cannot perform continuous monitoring. The infrared/spectrophotometer/chromatographic separation method can perform continuous and accurate concentration measurement, but the equipment is relatively expensive and is only suitable for specialized industrial analysis scenarios. The principle of the catalytic filament method is that gas reacts and burns on a catalytic metal wire, causing the temperature to rise, and detection is performed through the change in the resistance of the metal wire with the concentration of combustible gas; its disadvantage is that it is affected by the inert gas in an inerted compartment, and because of the influence of the inert gas it cannot provide reliable readings. In the gas-sensitive semiconductor method, a metal oxide is coated on a platinum wire and fired at high temperature; the resulting gas-sensitive semiconductor elements are divided by property into two major categories, N-type and P-type; the resistance of an N-type gas-sensitive semiconductor element decreases when it encounters a sensitive gas, and the resistance of a P-type gas-sensitive semiconductor element increases when it encounters a sensitive gas; at present this method is used relatively often in practical applications of flammable gas detection.

The explosion-proof safety probe is specially designed for continuous detection and alarming of flammable gas in dangerous areas such as cargo pump rooms and pipelines of oil tankers; it has a flameproof structure, so that even if an explosion occurs inside it will not ignite flammable gas in the external environment; its enclosure is made of nylon material, and its core detection component is a gas-sensitive semiconductor element; the gas-sensitive element is placed in a stainless steel cavity and protected and isolated by sintered metal particles, and the flame-arresting effect of the sintered metal particles and metal mesh is used to form the explosion-proof structure.

In the automatic ship fire monitoring and alarm device, the fire detector and the alarm controller are the two basic components; the former is responsible for converting fire phenomena into alarm signals, and the latter is responsible for receiving and processing these signals and giving audible and visual alarms and displaying the fire location. Among them, the alarm processing board is the core part, receiving detection information through an internal serial port and communicating with the operating unit through an external serial port; the communication interface board has two RS-232 and two RS-485 serial communication ports built in, used for communication with external computers and printers.

In gas detection, the intrinsically safe pump-suction detection device meets the intrinsically safe requirements through its pump-suction design; its pump box is placed in a safe area to avoid electrical sparks causing ignition of flammable gas; during measurement, gas from monitoring points in the dangerous area is drawn through pipes into the pump box, measured by the gas-sensitive semiconductor, and then this dangerous gas is returned to its original place or discharged into the atmosphere at a safe location; the pipe is fitted with a flame arrester where it passes through the wall from the safe area to the dangerous area, and the flame arrester adopts a structure in which sintered metal is embedded in a stainless steel housing, which can effectively prevent the spread of flame and explosion; the pump box is also provided with a pipeline blockage monitoring circuit, which gives a clear indication and reminder when blockage occurs. Used in conjunction with it is an alarm device for multi-point cyclic monitoring, which performs cyclic monitoring of multiple points (dozens of points) and can complete the drawing and measurement of gas for each monitoring point within a set time period; each monitoring point undergoes pre-suction before the measurement suction, so as to obtain the latest sample gas of the monitoring point; the purpose of pre-suction is to ensure that differences in pipe length do not affect the quality of the evenly allocated measurement time; the pipe of each monitoring point waiting to be measured is protected by a back-pressure device to prevent the intake of water or blockage by debris; the central measurement device is equipped with standard-concentration sample gas, so that the equipment can be calibrated at any time.

The fault causes of fire detectors are mainly divided into two categories: missed alarms and false alarms. A missed alarm of a fire detector means that the fire has developed to a scale at which an alarm should be given, but no alarm is given; it is parallel to false alarms and is one of the main types of fire detector fault causes, and contact-type detectors such as heat-sensing, smoke-sensing and gas-sensitive semiconductor detectors may all have missed alarms. When the detector and the wiring are fault-free, a missed alarm is often caused by the detector not detecting enough smoke; this situation belongs to the missed alarm situation of contact-type detectors such as heat-sensing, smoke-sensing and gas-sensitive semiconductor detectors, on the premise that the detector itself and the wiring are fault-free, and is commonly seen in scenarios where a fire starts near the floor and the ceiling height of the monitored cabin exceeds 10m, because the smoke can only be detected when smoke of sufficient concentration or sufficient heat reaches the position; the ceiling height of a monitored cabin using a common smoke-sensing detector generally does not exceed 10m. The detector being too close to the ceiling, causing smoke thermal descent, can also cause a missed alarm: when the ambient temperature is relatively high in summer, the air temperature under the indoor ceiling rises, and the high-temperature ceiling air causes the smoke produced by combustion to be unable to reach the ceiling; this phenomenon is usually called smoke thermal descent, and if the detector is too close to the ceiling, a missed alarm may also be caused by thermal descent; to avoid thermal descent, a smoke-sensing detector should keep a certain distance from the ceiling. Forced air flow formed by an indoor ventilation device causing smoke deflection is likewise one of the causes of missed alarms of smoke-sensing detectors; it is triggered by the forced air flow formed by the indoor ventilation device, causing the smoke deflection phenomenon, so that the smoke cannot reach the position of the smoke-sensing detector.

A false alarm of a fire detector means that an alarm signal is issued although no fire has occurred; it is one of the common fault causes of fire detectors and is parallel to missed alarms; in an automatic fire alarm system, faults occur most often in the detector and the peripheral wiring. There are many causes of false alarms. Too high detector sensitivity is one of the structural causes; too high sensitivity easily causes false alarms, while too low sensitivity causes alarm delay; when the room ceiling is relatively low and the sensitivity is relatively high, smoking easily triggers a false alarm, and three people smoking at the same time is enough to make a high-sensitivity smoke-sensing detector issue a fire alarm signal. The smoking process is mostly smoldering, and the generated smoke particles are relatively large, which easily causes false alarms of smoke-sensing detectors; when the room ceiling is relatively low and the detector sensitivity is relatively high, smoking more easily causes false alarms, and the smoke produced by three people smoking at the same time is enough to trigger a smoke-sensing detector to issue a fire alarm signal, while a single person smoking can interfere with the normal operation of a high-sensitivity smoke-sensing detector.

The large amount of smoke produced during electric welding operations easily makes fire detectors issue fire alarm signals; when electric welding operations are carried out in the engine room workshop, ship management personnel should pay special attention to prevent false alarms; when electric welding operations are carried out during ship repair at a repair yard, vigilance should be exercised against their interference with fire detectors. The mesh aperture of the smoke inlet of common detectors is 1.25mm, which can block large insects but cannot block small insects and small spiders; the purpose of providing smoke inlets and mesh is to block insects while allowing smoke to enter, and the aperture size needs to be balanced; small insects and spider webs are one of the electrical fault causes that lead to false alarms or interference with the operation of fire detectors. Cooking often produces a large amount of smoke, especially during stir-frying, steaming and boiling, when the amount of smoke is even greater; cooking smoke is often mixed with oil vapor, which has a serious impact on the detector; the presence of a vapor source in the kitchen causes excessive indoor moisture, and water vapor can enter the detector and interfere with its operation. The influence of the factor of lack of cleaning on the detector accumulates gradually; after long-term use of the detector, pollutants will always accumulate inside it, and ship management personnel often do not maintain fire detectors for several years, so false alarms inevitably occur frequently. A fault of the detector itself is manifested as the system displaying an alarm in a certain area while there is actually no fire in that area; the specific causes include reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor, low dose of the Am-241 source (or tin-241 source), thyristor breakdown, etc., and the treatment measure is to replace the faulty detector.

After the detector is installed on the ceiling base, the alarm controller immediately displays an alarm in that area; this is generally caused by the two wires on the base being connected in reverse (except for detectors without polarity requirements), belongs to the category of base incorrect wiring in the common fault causes of detectors, and the treatment method is to check the polarity with a multimeter and then swap the wiring. For the phenomenon that after the detector is installed on the ceiling base the alarm controller immediately displays an alarm in that area, the corresponding treatment method is to check the polarity with a multimeter and then swap the connections. The maintenance procedure of checking the polarity with a multimeter and then swapping the connections applies to the case except for detectors without polarity requirements, that is, incorrect wiring of the base of a detector with polarity requirements; this step is used to solve the fault in which the alarm controller immediately displays an area alarm after the detector is installed, and the root cause of the fault is usually that the two wires on the base are connected in reverse; before the operation, a multimeter must be used to check the polarity of the wiring to confirm the reverse connection state. In addition to being manifested as the two wires of the fire detector base being connected in reverse (except for those without polarity requirements), which causes an area alarm to be displayed immediately after installation, incorrect wiring on equipment such as motors can also cause the current direction to be reversed due to incorrect winding wiring, causing severe vibration of the motor, abnormal noise and serious imbalance of the three-phase current; if the power supply is not cut off in time, incorrect winding wiring may cause the motor winding to burn out; incorrect wiring can also cause the generator voltage to fail to build up normally.

The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument composed of a meter head, a changeover switch and a measuring circuit, and is divided into two types: analog and digital. The analog multimeter belongs to the multimeter, the digital multimeter also belongs to the multimeter, and the MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter; it can measure a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum DC current of 5A, and the panel has four jacks: "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A". The multimeter can be used to measure resistors, voltage, current, capacitance, diodes, transistors, thyristors, photosensitive devices and thermocouples. A transistor is a semiconductor device containing two PN junctions internally and having current amplification capability, divided into two types: NPN and PNP; in circuits it is commonly denoted by the letter "VT" plus a number, such as VT17, and its main models include A92, 9015 (PNP type) and A42, 9014, 9018, etc. (NPN type); when marine electrical equipment uses transistors, the transistor may develop a transistor fault, and a transistor fault belongs to transistor-related faults. A thyristor, also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, allows measurement of its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode.

In the maintenance of automatic fire monitoring and alarm devices, the multimeter is one of the most frequently used instruments. The multimeter is composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit, and belongs to multi-purpose instruments; by display mode it is divided into two types: analog and digital. The MF-47 multimeter is one type of analog multimeter, and the digital multimeter likewise belongs to the broad category of multimeters. Marine electrical equipment uses large numbers of diodes and transistors, so it is very necessary to master the testing methods for these two types of devices.

A diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity, commonly denoted by VD in circuits; under forward voltage its conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage its resistance is very large or infinite. By function, diodes include rectifier diodes, isolation diodes, Schottky diodes, light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes, among which rectifier diodes include 1N4004, isolation diodes include 1N4148, and Schottky diodes include BAT85. The diode testing procedure applies to the above various types of diodes, and the measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance.

A transistor may develop a transistor fault, and this fault belongs to the failure of the transistor itself.

A fault of the detector itself will cause the fire detector to give a false alarm. When the fire alarm shows an alarm in a certain area but there is no fire in that area, this is a false alarm fault in a certain area, and its cause lies in a fault of the detector itself, such as reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor, a low dose of the Am-241 source, or breakdown of the thyristor. Specifically, reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor is one manifestation of a fault of the detector itself, a low dose of the Am-241 source (or tin-241 source) is likewise a cause of a fault of the detector itself, and breakdown of the thyristor is one of the specific situations leading to a fault of the detector itself. Such faults will cause a false alarm in a certain area when there is no fire. For the phenomenon that the fire alarm shows an alarm in a certain area but there is no fire in that area, the corresponding treatment measure is to replace that detector. When there is no fire in a certain area but the alarm shows an alarm, and it is confirmed to be a detector fault, replace that detector; this measure applies to the false alarm situation caused by reduced input impedance of the field-effect transistor, applies to the false alarm situation caused by a low dose of the Am-241 source, and also applies to the false alarm situation caused by breakdown of the thyristor.

No response to smoke during a smoke test is another typical fault symptom. Damage to the field-effect transistor will cause the fire detector to show no response to smoke during a black smoke test, never giving an alarm; damage to the thyristor or Zener diode will likewise cause no response to smoke during a black smoke test, never giving an alarm. This fault is one possible cause of internal component failure of the fire detector, among which breakdown of the thyristor may also cause the fire alarm to show a false alarm in a certain area. Damage to the field-effect transistor and damage to the thyristor or Zener diode have similar symptom manifestations, and such faults can be checked by blowing cigarette smoke through a plastic tube or by using a dedicated tester to perform a black smoke test. The black smoke test can be performed by blowing cigarette smoke through a plastic tube, and using a dedicated tester for the black smoke test gives better results. If there is no response to smoke during the black smoke test and no alarm is ever given, and it is component damage, replacement is required; this replacement step applies to the no-response situation in the black smoke test caused by damage to the field-effect transistor.

The bus-controlled fire monitoring system adopts bus-coded transmission technology to form a centralized alarm system. Its troubleshooting focuses on checking peripheral equipment, lines, detectors, input/output modules and the detector bus. When the fire monitoring system fails, generally the main check is on peripheral equipment and lines, and the key points are all fire detectors, input/output modules and the detector bus; it is necessary to confirm that the detectors have no short circuit and that the wiring between the input/output modules and the controlled equipment is not shorted. Under normal conditions, all fire detectors and input/output modules should be fully registered in the controller. During maintenance, the step of connecting the detection bus to the detection bus output terminal of the controller, energizing the controller, and checking whether all fire detectors and input/output modules are registered must be performed. If all detectors and input/output modules of a certain loop are registered, it is determined that the loop has no fault. If not a single detector or input/output module of a certain loop is registered, the voltage at the detection bus output terminal of the controller needs to be measured; under normal conditions this voltage should be 8～12V; if only part of the detectors and input/output modules of a certain loop are registered, it indicates that the unregistered detectors and input/output modules have open-circuit faults, and also duplicate-address faults exist, that is, the unregistered detectors and input/output modules have faults such as broken wires and duplicate addresses.

In addition, if registered detectors and input/output modules report a fire alarm or fault, but there is no fire alarm or fault at the location of the detectors or input/output modules, this phenomenon likewise indicates that the detectors and input/output modules have duplicate addresses, and it is a typical fault that needs to be investigated during the maintenance and commissioning of the bus-controlled fire monitoring system.

When programming the fire detectors and input/output modules on the fire alarm controller, it is necessary to confirm before execution that all fire detectors and input/output modules have been registered in the system. The second step of the programming operation is to select the detector or input/output module type; the selectable types include ion-type smoke detector, photoelectric-type smoke detector, input module, photoelectric composite detector, ion-type smoke-temperature composite detector, zone display, temperature-sensing detector, manual alarm button, output module and fire hydrant alarm button; before a type is selected, all detectors or input/output modules are preset by default as ion-type smoke detectors, and the core purpose of this step is to make the types registered in the system consistent with the actually installed hardware types.

After completing the above two steps, display address programming is performed. For output modules, the display address is generally programmed as the name and location of the equipment it controls; for input modules, the display address is generally programmed as the name and location of the detector or equipment it displays; the display addresses of other equipment are programmed as the location of the detector, so as to quickly locate after an alarm. After completing display address programming, output modules still need subsequent programming work, while detectors and manual alarm buttons are fully programmed after display address programming. Module location programming applies only to input/output modules, not to other equipment such as detectors or manual alarm buttons; the module location is defined as the specific position number of the input/output module on the linkage panel, and its value range is a number from 0 to 599; this step is located after display address programming and before linkage logic relationship programming. After repair, it is necessary to confirm that all equipment has been registered, and then program the physical number and type.

The marine fire alarm system adopts bus-coded transmission technology to form a centralized alarm system, in which the bus is both the bus-type structure for transmitting data and instructions inside the programmable logic controller and the coded transmission line connecting detectors and the controller in the fire monitoring system. Among the faults of the programmable logic controller, a CPU bus fault will cause abnormal action of the input relay.

The automatic fire monitoring and alarm device includes an alarm controller and fire detectors.

When detectors and input/output modules have duplicate addresses, it is manifested as only part of the detectors and input/output modules of a certain loop being registered on the controller, and also as registered equipment reporting a fire alarm or fault while there is no fire or fault at the actual location; this is one of the common fault types of detectors and modules in the bus-controlled fire monitoring system. The second step of the programming operation is to select the detector or input/output module type; before a type is selected, the equipment is preset by default as an ion-type smoke detector.

The linkage logic programming is likewise only applicable to input/output modules, and its logic relations include: when any fire hydrant button alarms, the fire pump control module is automatically started; when any water flow indicator alarms, the sprinkler pump control module is automatically started; when a fire alarm occurs in any zone, the fire alarm broadcast control module of the adjacent zone is started.

Whether the input/output modules work normally should be checked before programming the logic relations. The checking method is: on the linkage panel, use the mouse to start the selected input/output module, and the indicator lamp on the module should light; when the two ends of the module input signal are short-circuited, the lamp at the corresponding position of this module on the alarm controller panel should light. If the lamps do not light in the above two cases, it indicates that there is a fault in the module or the wiring. During commissioning, the control output end is not connected to the controlled equipment, and is connected only during joint commissioning; the feedback signal input can remain connected to the controlled equipment throughout commissioning. During commissioning, the control output end of the input/output module is not connected to the controlled equipment, that is, during system commissioning the control output end of the input/output module must not be connected to the controlled equipment; only when system commissioning is completed and joint commissioning is required is the control output end connected to the controlled equipment, while during commissioning the feedback signal input end can remain connected to the controlled equipment at all times.

The ship's water mist fire extinguishing system mainly consists of three major parts: the local control part, the cargo control room part and the bridge display part. The local control part is one of the three main parts, and its composition includes the local control box, fresh water tank, inlet valve, fresh water supply pump, filter, check valve, fresh water cabinet, drain valve, high-pressure fresh water pump, pressure gauge, main isolation valve, safety valve, solenoid valves of each zone and nozzles of each zone, and includes a level indicator with four indication functions: high level, low level, low-low level and lowest level. Fresh water enters the fresh water tank through the inlet valve, supply pump, filter and check valve; when the water level is above the low level and any zone operates, the high-pressure fresh water pump is started. The local control part is responsible for the water mist release execution of seven zones in total: the main engine zone, No.1-3 generators, the incinerator, the oil separator and the boiler.

The cargo control room part mainly consists of a control box; on the cargo control room control box, remote release of each sub-zone can be realized, and the signals of the ship's fire system can enter the water mist fire extinguishing system from the cargo control room part. The bridge display panel part corresponds to the component numbered 16 in the system diagram, and its main function is to display the release status of each zone in the engine room, and together with the local control part and the cargo control room part it constitutes the system as a whole.

The solenoid valves of each zone belong to the components of the local control part of the water mist fire extinguishing system, are numbered 17 in the system, are located after the main isolation valve and before the nozzles of each zone, and are usually powered by DC24V. The high-pressure fresh water passes through this solenoid valve and is then released through the nozzles for fire extinguishing; when it operates, the cargo control room control box and the bridge display display the release zone and give an alarm, and remote control is exercised through the cargo control room control box to realize release control of each sub-zone. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel oil; at ignition it cuts off the fuel oil circulation loop and enters the oil nozzle to inject oil; the automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve. The display is used to display radar images and, as a component of the fire monitoring system, displays zone fire alarm information in the central control room or the accommodation area; the display also includes two maintenance items: cleaning of the display air filter and cleaning of the display surface.

Faults occurring in the commissioning and operation of the water mist fire extinguishing system can often be traced separately in the several links of fresh water supply, pressure build-up, zone release and communication. After the fresh water supply pump is started, if it is found that there is no water flow or too little water flow in the fresh water tank, the emergency stop button should be pressed immediately; this operation corresponds to preventing the centrifugal pump from rotating in reverse and dragging down the motor, thereby burning out the fuse. There is more than one cause of this phenomenon: the water valve from the fresh water tank to the fresh water pump not being opened or not being fully opened will directly cause no water flow or too little water flow in the fresh water tank; the incorrect rotation direction of the motor connected to the fresh water supply pump will likewise cause no water flow or too little water flow in the fresh water tank; the filter or check valve being installed in the reverse direction will also cause no water flow or too little water flow in the fresh water tank. For the first cause, the corresponding treatment is to check whether the water valve from the fresh water tank to the fresh water pump is opened or fully opened; if it is not opened or not fully opened, this valve should be fully opened immediately at this time;

For the second cause, the corresponding treatment is to check whether the rotation direction of the motor connected to the fresh water feed pump is correct; if the rotation direction is reversed, it must be adjusted immediately. The fresh water feed pump is composed of six ordinary centrifugal pumps connected in series, and the rotation is directional; once the motor rotation is reversed, the centrifugal pumps will not discharge water or only a small amount of water will flow out, and at the same time the motor will be in an overload state, the current will be too large, and the fuse of the motor in the local control box may be burned out. Therefore, after the system is energized, the rotation direction of the motor connected to the fresh water feed pump should be checked first, and if reversal is found, the motor wiring or rotation direction should be adjusted immediately. As for the filter or the check valve, each has a specific installation direction requirement; if either one or both are installed in reverse, there will be no water flow or too little water flow in the fresh water tank, and they need to be reinstalled according to the direction requirements.

In order to confirm the fresh water feed pump link before energizing, the following step should be carried out: before the system is energized, the drain cock of the fresh water feed pump should be opened; if a large amount of water flows out, it means this link is normal. The purpose of this pre-check is precisely to avoid the fault of no water flow or too little water flow in the fresh water tank after startup.

Current value is a measurable electrical quantity; the multimeter is used for current measurement, the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement, and in addition an ammeter is also used to measure current, so that the equipment state can be understood through the current, wherein the ammeter needs to be connected in series after the circuit is disconnected. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system, and the overload caused by the aforementioned reversed rotation belongs to this category. The fuse, as a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material with a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength, together with the resistor, capacitance and the like, is a commonly used component in electronic circuits; its material is mostly aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, and it burns out first under overload to cut off the circuit.

The faults concerning the main isolation valve are manifested as main isolation valve fault and incorrect wiring of the main isolation valve limit switch. During the debugging of the local control box, the valve should be closed first, but the limit switch should be manually put in the open state; the purpose of doing so is to prevent high-pressure fresh water from directly spraying into each sub-area before it is truly confirmed whether the solenoid valves of each sub-area work properly, thereby causing damage to unprotected equipment. The main isolation valve limit switch of this system should be connected at the closed contact; if the main isolation valve limit switch is connected at the normally open contact, it will lead to incorrect wiring of the main isolation valve limit switch, and the corresponding treatment is to connect the main isolation valve limit switch at the closed contact.

The cause of damage to the pressure gauge at the high-pressure pump outlet is: there is a small amount of air in the small pipeline from the high-pressure pump outlet to the pressure gauge; when the high-pressure pump is started directly after the bypass valve is closed, the pressure gauge is very easily damaged under the impact of the small amount of high-pressure air. The corresponding treatment is that before the test the bypass valve must first be in the open state, and the high-pressure pump should be started manually on the local control box so that it runs for 2–3 min in the bypass state of the bypass valve, ensuring that the air in the small pipeline connected to the pressure gauge is driven out; then the bypass valve is closed, the high-pressure pump is started manually, and the high-pressure pump outlet pressure is checked. The normal range of the high-pressure pump outlet pressure of this system is 70–130 kg; under normal circumstances the high-pressure pump outlet pressure is adjusted to 100 kg.

Abnormality of the sound and light alarms and solenoid valves in each area is another common type of fault, involving the sound and light alarms and solenoid valves in each area of the water mist fire extinguishing system. The sound and light alarms in each area give alarm indications on the control box in the cargo control room and on the display on the bridge. One cause of the abnormality is that the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarms and solenoid valves are connected in reverse; the corresponding treatment is to swap the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarms and solenoid valves; under normal circumstances, swapping the positive and negative poles of the power supply can solve this fault. The second cause is that the wiring mode of the solenoid valve in the paint room area is different from that of the other six areas; the solenoid valve in this area is not connected in the external junction box, but is connected directly from the solenoid valve to the local control box, and this part of the wiring is very easily misconnected to the solenoid valve of the fresh water feed pump. The third cause is that the valve core of the solenoid valve is stuck with impurities such as iron filings; at this time the solenoid valve function will fail and high-pressure fresh water will be sprayed mistakenly, manifested as high-pressure fresh water directly spraying into each area; the corresponding treatment is that before formal spraying, the manual release switch should be manually opened and closed several times, and this operation is carried out on the manual release switch below the solenoid valve in each area, with the purpose of preventing impurities such as iron filings in the pipelines of a new ship from sticking at the valve core of the solenoid valve. In the water mist fire extinguishing system, it serves as the release device of each area and is usually powered by DC24V; its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil, to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge.

The communication between the local control box and the cargo control room (ECR) is abnormal, and its causes include incorrect connection of the communication line and incorrect connection of the power line. For incorrect connection of the communication line, when connecting the communication line it is only necessary to ensure that the color and number of the line are correct; for incorrect connection of the power line, a multimeter can be used to check the line, and before power-on the power line in the cargo control room should be disconnected, and after power-on the positive and negative poles are distinguished with a multimeter before connection.

The sound and light alarm devices and solenoid valves of each zone of the water mist fire extinguishing system are all powered by a DC24V power supply; if the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarm devices and solenoid valves are connected in reverse, the sound and light alarm devices and solenoid valves of each zone will be abnormal. To eliminate this fault, generally it is only necessary to swap the positive and negative poles of the power supply of the sound and light alarm devices and solenoid valves, that is, to restore normal operation of the alarm devices and solenoid valves by exchanging the positive and negative power supply connections.

The junction box is used in the ship electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical components; the general alarm device is composed of the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc.; when testing the thermal resistor type sensor, it is necessary to disconnect the wiring of the temperature sensor in the junction box. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to cut off the fuel oil circulation circuit, release the residual air of the air compressor or control the water mist fire extinguishing zone; the automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve, and in the burner ignition program the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that oil enters the oil nozzle and is sprayed; its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil, to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge;

If the valve core of the solenoid valve is stuck by impurities such as iron filings, it will also cause the sound and light alarm devices and solenoid valves of each zone to be abnormal. If impurities stick the valve core, the solenoid valve will fail to function and high-pressure fresh water will be sprayed erroneously; this fault manifests as high-pressure fresh water being sprayed directly into each zone.

When the communication between the local control box and the cargo control room (ECR) is abnormal, three measures can be taken. Second, use a multimeter to check the line, which is used to distinguish the lines when the models of the power lines in the cargo control room are mixed, and to distinguish the positive and negative poles of the power line after power-on; before operation, the power line in the cargo control room needs to be disconnected. Third, before power-on the power line in the cargo control room should be disconnected, and after power-on the positive and negative poles are distinguished with a multimeter before connection; this step is applicable to the connection of the communication power line between the local control box and the cargo control room of the water mist fire extinguishing system. In view of the situation that multiple power lines of different models may appear in the cargo control room and cause wiring confusion, the operation requires that the power line in the cargo control room must be disconnected before the system is powered on, and after power-on the positive and negative poles of the power line must be distinguished with a multimeter before connection can be carried out.

The object targeted by this step is the main isolation valve of the water mist fire extinguishing system; the operation requires first closing the main isolation valve, and at the same time manually making the limit switch in the disconnected state, the purpose being to prevent high-pressure fresh water from being sprayed directly into each sub-zone before it is truly confirmed whether the solenoid valves of each sub-zone work well, causing damage to unprotected equipment; the limit switch of the main isolation valve of this system should be connected at the closed contact.

No water flow or a small water flow in the fresh water tank is a common fault symptom of the water mist fire extinguishing system, referring to no water flow or a small flow in the tank after the fresh water supply pump is started. For no water flow or a small water flow in the fresh water tank, it should be checked whether the water valve from the fresh water tank to the fresh water pump is open or fully open; if it is not open or not fully open, this valve should be fully opened immediately at this time.

Motor reversal will cause the centrifugal pump to deliver no water and the motor to overload and burn out the fuse. When this fault occurs, the emergency stop button should be pressed immediately; the preventive inspection method is to open the drain cock before energizing and observe whether there is a large flow of water. During commissioning, first open the bypass valve and run for 2–3 min to expel air, then close the bypass valve to check this pressure; if the air in the piping is not expelled and the high-pressure pump is started directly, the impact of a small amount of high-pressure air can easily damage the pressure gauge.

Nozzle blockage mostly occurs at the small nozzles on the second layer from the main engine side, which is the lowest point of the system; dirt in the piping gathers at the lowest point of the system due to gravity, i.e., at the second layer from the main engine side, and this accumulation phenomenon causes the seven small nozzles on the second layer from the main engine side to become the most easily blocked points of the system. The treatment measure is to remove these seven small nozzles before each water discharge of the system, flush them with high-pressure fresh water for about 1 min, and then reinstall them; the execution timing is to carry out the removal and flushing operation before each water discharge of the system, and the specific operation is to remove the seven nozzles, flush them with high-pressure fresh water for about 1 minute, and reinstall the nozzles after flushing to ensure that blockage no longer occurs subsequently.

The refrigerated store call alarm device consists of a call switch, a call lamp installed in this store, and call bells provided in the kitchen and dining room. When a crew member is mistakenly locked in the store and cannot get out, pressing the call switch K3 in the store immediately triggers the alarm. Switch K3 has one set of contacts; when this set of contacts closes, the call lamp HL3 of this store lights up to issue a call signal; switch K3 also has another set of contacts, and when this set of contacts operates, the call bells HA1 and HA2 in the kitchen and dining room sound, forming a rescue alarm sound. At the same moment the alarm operates, the call lamps HL1 and HL2 corresponding to the kitchen and dining room are also lit. To cancel the alarm, the method adopted is to directly close the call switch. The whole device relies on the call switch to link the lamp in the store with the bells and lamps of the kitchen and dining room, forming a refrigerated store safety alarm device, so that a mistakenly locked person can promptly send a help signal to the outside. From the circuit relationship, call switch K3 is the signal initiating element of this device, and the call lamp HL3 of this store, the call lamps HL1 and HL2 of the kitchen and dining room, and the call bells HA1 and HA2 are all its controlled objects; therefore, to judge whether the device is normal, it should be confirmed separately whether the two sets of contacts of K3 make and break reliably, whether HL3 can light up, whether HA1 and HA2 can sound, whether HL1 and HL2 can light up synchronously, and whether all signals disappear after the call switch is closed.

The patient call alarm system mainly consists of a call board, a call button, and a responder installed in the chief officer's room and other places; its purpose is for the patient to call when medical staff are needed at the sickbed in the ward. After the patient presses the call button SB provided beside the sickbed, the relay KM in the call board in the wheelhouse is energized and operates, one set of its contacts performs the self-holding function so that the relay continues to remain in the operating state; another set of contacts lights up HL1 on the ward alarm board, and at the same time connects the call bells in the dining room, the chief officer's room and the wheelhouse. Pressing the answer button SB2, SB3 or SB4 at any one location can de-energize and release the relay, thereby completing silencing. At the same time as silencing, the call lamp HL1 on the ward call board goes out accordingly, from which the patient knows that the alarm signal has been received.

This system belongs to the ship's medical cabin alarm device, consists of a call board and buttons, and is used by the patient to call medical staff at the sickbed. When inspecting this system, each item should be confirmed around the call button SB, the self-holding contact of relay KM, HL1 on the ward alarm board, and the call bells in the dining room, the chief officer's room and the wheelhouse, and it should be verified that the three answer buttons SB2, SB3 and SB4 can all de-energize and release KM and that HL1 goes out accordingly.

The general alarm device includes the alarm lamp as a component; the function of the alarm lamp is to issue a light signal in an emergency, and it is also one of the components of the general alarm device, i.e., the emergency assembly alarm. When the direct control mode is adopted, the alarm lamp is connected to the emergency power supply via the shutter contact and lights up. As a component of the general alarm device, whether the alarm lamp lights depends on whether the shutter contact connects the emergency power supply; therefore, when inspecting the alarm lamp in the direct control mode, the connected state of the shutter contact and the power supply condition of the emergency power supply should be confirmed together.

The engineer safety alarm system is suitable for unattended engine rooms or one-man engine rooms, and its function is to ensure that the engineer works safely. Before the engineer goes down to the engine room to work, this system needs to be switched on first. If personal injury occurs during work and the system cannot be reset within a fixed time, the system will issue an alarm, and the alarm signal is sent to the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the engine room monitoring and alarm system; the engine room monitoring and alarm system will again send this alarm signal to the extension alarm system, and then forward it to the bridge, crew rooms and public places to remind relevant personnel to go for rescue. If it can be reset within the fixed time, the system restarts the alarm timing until the engineer leaves safely and switches off the system. The control circuit of this system consists of three parts, namely the control circuit in the centralized control console, the start/stop button box at the engine room entrance and the reset button box at the stairway entrance. In the control circuit, the knob switch K2 is connected in parallel with the start/stop button at the engine room entrance, and both can control the start and stop of the system.

The working process of this system can be understood in chronological order as follows: before entering the engine room, the engineer first switches on the system, and the system immediately starts timing; if personal injury occurs during work and no reset is made within the fixed time, the alarm is sent step by step via the engine room extension alarm lamp column, the engine room monitoring and alarm system and the extension alarm system to the bridge, crew rooms and public places; if reset is completed within the fixed time, the timing restarts until the engineer leaves safely and switches off the system.

The control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system consists of the control circuit, the start/stop button box and the reset button box. Among them, the control circuit is arranged in the centralized control console, the start/stop button box is located at each engine room entrance, and the reset button box is arranged at the stairway entrance of the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the engine room monitoring and alarm system.

If injury occurs during work and no reset is made within the fixed time, the system will issue an alarm to the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the like; the alarm signal is sent via the engine room monitoring and alarm system to the bridge and relevant crew rooms to remind personnel to carry out rescue. If reset is successfully completed within the fixed time, the system will restart the alarm timing until the engineer leaves safely. This control circuit is used in unattended engine rooms to ensure the personal safety of the engineer, and consists of the control circuit in the centralized control console, the entrance start/stop box and the stairway entrance reset box.
