As for the installation positions, the control circuit is in the centralized control console, the start/stop button box is distributed at each engine room entrance, and the reset button box is arranged at the stairway entrance of the engine room extension alarm lamp column and the engine room monitoring and alarm system; the three are located at different positions in space, and during inspection they should be checked one by one according to this distribution.

When inspecting and maintaining the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system, one requirement is to check whether the wiring of all components is correct and firm, and another requirement is to measure that there is no short circuit on the power supply side and that the polarity is correct. Both requirements apply to the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system.

Checking whether the wiring of all components is correct and firm applies to each component and its connection points in the control circuit, the start/stop button box and the reset button box, with the purpose of eliminating incorrect wiring and looseness; measuring that there is no short circuit on the power supply side and that the polarity is correct is to confirm the power supply inlet end before energizing, so as to avoid damage to components caused by short circuit or reversed polarity. In addition, for the convenience of commissioning, the delay of time relay KT1 can be adjusted from 27min to 2min, and KT2 can be adjusted to 1min; this adjustment also applies to the control circuit of the engineer safety alarm system. A time relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in ship power systems, and common designations are KT, SJ and SL. A contactor contains a coil, and the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes that make the contactor armature unable to close and the motor fails to start.

The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

Before energizing the control circuit of the engineer's safety alarm system, a series of preparatory work must be done, and one of the first items is to check whether all component wiring is correct and secure. According to the acceptance criteria, components should be installed correctly and fixed firmly, the system should be kept clean, the structure should be complete without missing parts, and the electrical insulation performance should be good. This maintenance procedure applies to the control circuit of the engineer's safety alarm system and is the basic work that must be carried out before energization.

After the wiring check is completed, the next step is to measure that there is no short circuit on the power supply side and that the polarity is correct. This step also applies to the control circuit of the engineer's safety alarm system; it is necessary to measure and confirm that there is no short circuit on the power supply side, and at the same time confirm that the power supply polarity is connected correctly.

It is located after checking the component wiring and before adjusting the time relay; only when there is no short circuit on the power supply side and the polarity is correct do the subsequent energization and commissioning have the required conditions.

Further on, for the convenience of commissioning, the delay of time relay KT1 is adjusted from 27min to 2min, and KT2 is adjusted to 1min. This step also applies to the control circuit of the engineer's safety alarm system and belongs to the preparatory work before energization, with the purpose of facilitating subsequent commissioning. The specific method is to adjust the delay of time relay KT1 from 27min to 2min, and adjust the delay of time relay KT2 to 1min. The time relay performs control or protection functions in the ship's power system, and is often marked with symbols such as KT, SJ, and SL on circuit diagrams. The above settings are only for the commissioning stage: KT1 is changed from 27min to 2min, and KT2 is changed to 1min.

In terms of fault diagnosis, the conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation. The objects of observation include abnormal phenomena, component status, wire status, and equipment operating parameters, that is, checking whether components are jammed or damaged, whether wires are loose, broken, abraded, or burnt, and noting whether operating parameters deviate from the normal range. Observation is a sub-item of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site intact." In the diagnostic sequence, interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation: first learn the situation from the operator, then proceed to on-site observation; observation is in turn the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device: after obtaining a preliminary impression, check the various monitoring and indicating devices.

Voltage is a measurable performance; the measuring tool is the multimeter, and a voltmeter may also be used. In ship electrical fault diagnosis, voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked.

There is a co-occurrence association between the engineer's safety alarm system and the alarm lamp, and there is likewise a co-occurrence association between the control circuit of the engineer's safety alarm system and the alarm lamp; when troubleshooting alarm system faults, the alarm lamp and its power supply circuit should be checked together.

For the engine room monitoring and alarm system to complete the monitoring of equipment operating status and parameter display, it must first rely on various sensors to convert changes in the measured quantity into signals that are easy to transmit and easy to process. According to differences in output signal form, the information acquisition devices in ship monitoring and control systems are divided into two major categories: analog and switching-value sensors. Analog sensors convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, and can both monitor equipment status and display the specific values of parameters; they are suitable for occasions where it is necessary both to judge whether the equipment is normal and to read actual values such as temperature, pressure, and liquid level.

This type of sensor outputs an electrical quantity that varies continuously with the measured variable. After the computer reads this quantity, it can either compare it with a set value to determine whether the equipment exceeds limits, or send the value directly to the display screen for the duty personnel to read; therefore it simultaneously undertakes the two tasks of status monitoring and parameter display. A switching-value sensor, on the other hand, converts the parameter limit-exceedance condition into switching-value information in the form of contact opening or closing; it gives only the two states of on and off, and is therefore used only to monitor whether the equipment is normal, and does not undertake the task of continuously displaying parameter values. This type of sensor is usually composed of elements such as pressure relays, temperature switches and level switches; when the measured variable reaches the actuation value, the contact flips, and the computer only needs to identify whether the contact is closed or open to determine whether the corresponding equipment is in a normal or abnormal state. These two types of sensors have a clear division of labour in the engine-room monitoring and alarm system: the former is oriented toward continuous measurement of quantities, the latter toward out-of-limit judgement of limit values; when configuring measuring points, any parameter for which a specific numerical value needs to be read out should use an analog sensor, while any parameter for which only normality or abnormality needs to be judged may use a switching-value sensor.

The signal sent out by the sensor cannot enter the computer directly; it must pass through the corresponding input interface and alarm control unit in between. The measuring circuit of the analog alarm control unit undertakes the task of converting the information sent by the analog sensor into a voltage signal; for example, the resistance change of a thermistor is converted by the measuring circuit into a corresponding voltage signal and then subjected to subsequent processing. The reason the measuring circuit must first convert a quantity such as resistance into voltage is that the subsequent links of comparison, judgement and feeding into the computer all use voltage as the unified intermediate quantity; only by normalizing the outputs of different types of sensors to the voltage form can the same set of circuits be used to process different parameters such as temperature, pressure and level. This measuring circuit also has a self-check capability: when the sensor has an open circuit or short circuit, it sends a fault signal, enabling the system to distinguish an abnormality of the sensor itself from a parameter limit exceedance. This distinction is crucial for maintenance judgement: if a measuring point displays a fault signal rather than a limit-exceedance alarm, it indicates that the problem lies in the sensor and its connecting circuit, and the wiring should be checked for looseness and the sensor for damage; if a limit-exceedance alarm is displayed, it indicates that the sensor itself is working normally and that the operating parameter of the monitored equipment has indeed exceeded the set range.

The function of the analog input interface is to convert the analog signal sent by the analog sensor into a digital quantity through the A/D converter and feed it into the computer, and the computer then performs comparison, judgement, display and alarm. The A/D converter is the key link in the analog channel; only the converted digital quantity is convenient for the computer to store, compute and send to other display terminals via the communication network. The switching-value input interface, on the other hand, achieves electrical isolation between the sensor circuit and the I/O interface and CPU by means of an optical isolator; in this way the field circuit is separated from the interface board, so as to protect the interface board from damage by abnormal voltages on the field side. The optical isolator transmits signals by means of light, and there is no direct electrical connection between the field side and the interface board side; therefore, when surges, induced overvoltages or earthing potential differences occur in the field circuit, the components on the interface board side will not be subjected to impact, and the interface board is effectively protected.

The installation positions and uses of sensors on ships are not limited to the interior of the engine room. In the ship-station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively; when the ship pitches and rolls, the sensors in these two directions send out error signals to control the compensating motion so that the antenna platform remains stable. The sensor in the X-axis direction detects the tilt deviation in that direction, and the sensor in the Y-axis direction detects the tilt deviation in the other direction; the error signals of the two directions are fed together into the control link to drive the actuator to perform the corresponding compensating action, thereby cancelling the influence of hull sway on the antenna pointing. It can thus be seen that the control platform contains sensors, and the sensors are the sensing link by which the control platform achieves error detection and compensating action; without the error signals sent out by the sensors in these two directions, the compensating motion would lose its basis for action.

Also belonging to the sensing link is the field of fire detection. A fire detector is composed of a fire parameter sensor or measuring element, a detection signal processing unit and a fire judgment circuit, wherein the sensor is responsible for converting the physical and chemical effects generated during the combustion process into measured values, for the subsequent circuit to judge whether a fire has occurred. The detection signal processing unit performs amplification, shaping and other processing on the measured values sent by the sensor, and the fire judgment circuit then determines, based on the processed signals, whether the fire condition has been reached; the three work together in the order of sensing, processing and judgment.

Once an alarm is established, in addition to giving a prompt on the display screen, the system must also attract the attention of the duty personnel through sound and light devices. The general alarm device includes an alarm lamp; the alarm lamp is one of the constituent parts of the general alarm device and emits a light signal in emergency situations. The general alarm device is used on occasions such as emergency muster; the alarm lamp works together with the sound device so that personnel can learn of the alarm through the visual channel even in a noisy environment. In direct control mode, the alarm lamp is lit by connecting the emergency power supply through the shutter contact, so that a visible alarm indication can still be given under emergency power supply conditions. The significance of this power supply mode lies in that, when the main power supply fails, the alarm lamp can still be lit by the emergency power supply, and the alarm indication will not disappear together with the main power supply.

As far as the engine room monitoring and alarm system is concerned, when a fault alarm occurs, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room will flash, prompting the occurrence of a fault with flashing light; when the duty personnel press the silence button and the fault alarm is silenced, the rotating alarm lamp in the engine room goes out, and the light signal stops accordingly. The rotating alarm lamp expands the visible range of the light by rotating, and flashing makes the light different from normally lit illumination, making it easier for the duty personnel to notice. These two states of the alarm lamp, flashing and going out, correspond to the two stages of alarm establishment and silencing, and constitute the basic visual manifestation of the engine room alarm. When checking the alarm function, whether the system works normally can be judged according to the state of the alarm lamp: if an alarm occurs but the alarm lamp does not flash, the alarm lamp itself and its power supply circuit should be checked; if the alarm lamp still does not go out after silencing, the coordination between the silencing link and the alarm lamp control circuit should be checked.

Looking at the above links in series, the engine room monitoring and alarm system obtains information from sensors: analog sensors provide continuously changing electrical signals, and switch-type sensors provide switch-type information on contact opening and closing; the measuring circuit of the analog alarm control unit converts the analog information into voltage signals and sends out a fault signal when the sensor is open-circuited or short-circuited; the switch-type input interface uses an optical isolator to separate the sensor circuit from the I/O interface and CPU, protecting the interface board; after an alarm is established, the alarm lamp in the general alarm device emits flashing light, and after silencing the alarm lamp goes out. The sensor sends error signals in the X-axis and Y-axis directions of the ship station antenna control platform to control the compensation motion, and in the fire detector it converts physical and chemical effects into measured values; all these show that the sensor, as an information acquisition device, has its specific form and installation position varying with the monitored object, but its basic function of converting the measured quantity into a processable signal is the same.

As far as maintenance is concerned, mastering this signal flow helps to locate faults link by link: first confirm whether the sensor output is normal, then check the conversion and isolation links of the measuring circuit and the input interface, and finally check the action of the alarm lamp at the alarm output end; by troubleshooting section by section, the fault scope can be narrowed down to a specific component or wiring.

In the engine room monitoring and alarm system, the analog sensor undertakes the task of converting the monitored parameter into a continuously changing electrical signal, and the thermistor is one of the commonly used types. The thermistor belongs to the broad category of resistors and is a special semiconductor device whose resistance value changes with the surface temperature; its resistance value changes with the surface temperature, and the commonly used NTC type has a negative temperature coefficient, that is, the resistance value decreases as the temperature rises, which makes it suitable for temperature compensation. In the monitoring system, the thermistor is used as an analog sensor, and its resistance value is converted into a voltage signal for use by the comparison link.

Unlike analog sensors, switching sensors convert parameter limit violations into switching information of contact opening or closing, and are only used to monitor whether equipment is normal; while analog sensors are suitable for occasions where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. The measurement circuit must not only complete normal signal conversion, but also give a fault indication when an abnormality such as open circuit or short circuit occurs in the sensor circuit, so that operating personnel can distinguish whether it is a parameter limit violation or a problem in the measurement circuit itself. For an analog sensor such as a thermistor, judging whether it works normally depends on one hand on whether the displayed reading changes continuously with changes in the monitored parameter, and on the other hand on whether the measurement circuit issues an open-circuit or short-circuit fault signal; once a fault signal appears, first check whether the sensor wiring is loose, broken or shorted, then check the conversion link of the measurement circuit, and do not conclude that the sensor is damaged merely because the displayed value is too high or too low.

The comparison link in the analog alarm control unit is usually composed of an alarm value setting potentiometer and upper and lower limit alarm jumpers. A potentiometer is a manually adjustable component with three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes with rotation of the shaft; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment belongs to this type. In automatic fuel oil boilers, the potentiometer has a specific application: the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 driven by the motor M form a bridge for achieving bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the balance state of this bridge changes accordingly. When adjusting the alarm value, a screwdriver can be inserted into the small hole on the panel to adjust the alarm value setting potentiometer Rp, thereby changing the setting value UL.

After replacing the analog alarm plug-in board, if the displayed reading is different from the original alarm value, the alarm value setting potentiometer needs to be adjusted accordingly. This adjustment is necessary because after the plug-in board is replaced, the setting state of each channel may be inconsistent with the original plug-in board; only by readjusting the displayed reading to match the original alarm value can the alarm action point be consistent with the original setting requirements. In terms of operation sequence, first confirm that the plug-in board has been inserted in place and the channel correspondence is correct, then adjust channel by channel against the original alarm values; during adjustment, use the displayed reading as the basis and check while adjusting, avoiding turning too much at one time and overshooting the setting point. The upper and lower limit alarm jumpers determine whether the channel is for upper limit alarm, lower limit alarm, or both upper and lower limit alarm; with different jumper positions, the action direction corresponding to the same setting value is also different, so before adjusting the setting value, first check whether the jumpers are consistent with the required alarm direction.

In the microcomputer-based engine room monitoring alarm system, the input interface is used to input the status of switching sensors into the computer. In the switching input interface, when the switch is closed, the input voltage is 24V, and when open, it is 0V. Regarding the output interface, the switching output interface controls the display and alarm devices via an optical isolator and a driver. A programmable logic controller (PLC) includes an input interface and an output interface; the input interface accepts control information from field devices such as pushbuttons, limit switches, contactor contacts and sensors, and converts it into digital signals that the CPU can process; the output interface converts the digital signals output by the CPU into voltage or current to drive actuators such as solenoid valves and contactors. In the basic structure of the PLC, the input interface and output interface together with the CPU and memory constitute its components; the former is responsible for bringing in field control information, and the latter is responsible for sending out processing results; together they complete the information transfer between the monitoring alarm system and field devices. When checking the switching input interface, whether the input state is correct can be judged according to the quantitative relationship that the switch is closed at 24V and open at 0V: if the field contact is already closed but 24V cannot be measured at the interface terminal, or the contact is already open but it is still 24V, it indicates an abnormality in the input circuit, and the optical isolator and its peripheral wiring should be checked.

The function of the optical isolator is to electrically separate the sensor circuit from the I/O interface and the CPU, so that overvoltage, interference or earthing problems occurring on the field side do not act directly on the interface board and the CPU; therefore, when replacing the interface board or troubleshooting faults, the optical isolator should not be arbitrarily short-circuited or bypassed.

Resistance and voltage are the two basic quantities to be measured in fault diagnosis. A multimeter is used to measure resistance, while a multimeter or voltmeter is used to measure voltage. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and measurement must never be carried out with power on. The essence of these two precautions is to avoid the bypassing influence of other components or residual charge in the branch under test on the reading, and also to avoid damage to the instrument or personal injury caused by live measurement. In specific operation, the power supply of the circuit under test should first be cut off, then one end of the resistor under test should be disconnected from the circuit, so that the measuring current flows only through the resistor under test itself; if a capacitor is connected in parallel in this branch, the capacitor must also be discharged first, and the meter should be connected for measurement only after confirming that there is no residual charge. Voltage, as one of the meter readings, is an object to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; when checking such faults, the resistance of the shunt resistor may first be measured to determine whether it is open-circuited, and then, in combination with the operating condition of the voltage regulator, the cause of the high no-load voltage may be analyzed.

Although the specific tasks undertaken by sensors in different situations differ, the common point is that they convert the measured quantity into a signal form that subsequent circuits can process: analog sensors output continuously varying electrical signals, while switching-value sensors output switching-value information indicating whether contacts are open or closed, and the two correspond respectively to the two types of requirements of parameter display and status monitoring. As far as the engine room monitoring and alarm system is concerned, which type of sensor is selected depends on the monitoring purpose: where continuous display of parameter values is required and the trend of change is to be judged accordingly, analog sensors are used; where it is only necessary to judge whether equipment exceeds limits or is normal, switching-value sensors are used. The signals sent out by the sensors finally enter the computer through the input interface; analog signals are first converted into digital quantities by the A/D converter, while switching-value signals are acquired in the voltage state of 24V or 0V, and the two paths each complete the corresponding signal conversion and isolation, constituting the basic links of information acquisition and transmission in the monitoring and alarm system.

The electrical characteristics of the switching-value input interface are as follows: when the switch is in the closed state, the input voltage is 24V, and when the switch is open, the input voltage is 0V. In order not to create a direct electrical connection between the field sensor circuit and the I/O interface and the CPU, the input interface achieves electrical isolation between the two through an optical isolator, thereby protecting the interface board.

Switching-value signals are read into the CPU via the data bus, and this reading process is controlled by the state of the three-state gate. As components of the programmable logic controller (PLC), the input interface, together with the output interface, the CPU and the memory, constitutes the basic structure of the PLC; it receives control information sent from field devices such as pushbuttons, travel switches, contactor contacts and sensors, and converts this information into digital signals that the CPU can process. In the switching-value output interface, display and alarm devices are controlled via the optical isolator and the driver. The input interface and the output interface have a clear division of labor in the PLC: the former is oriented to the acquisition and conversion of field control information, and the latter is oriented to the output and driving of processing results; both are separated from the CPU and the field circuit by means of the optical isolation link, avoiding external interference or faults directly affecting the interface board and the CPU.

The sensors used in the engine room monitoring and alarm system are divided into two major categories: analog and switching-value. The measuring circuit of the analog alarm control unit converts the information sent by the analog sensor (for example, the resistance of the thermistor) into a voltage signal, and sends a fault signal when the sensor is open-circuited or short-circuited. As far as the inspection sequence is concerned, for the analog channel it should first be confirmed whether the sensor output signal varies continuously with the monitored parameter, then it should be checked whether the measuring circuit can convert this signal into a voltage signal, and finally it should be verified whether the digital quantity sent by the A/D converter into the computer corresponds to the parameter change; for the switching-value channel, it should first be confirmed whether the contact can reliably open or close when the parameter exceeds the limit, and then it should be checked whether the electrical isolation on both sides of the optical isolator is intact.

A thermocouple is a temperature sensor with a simple structure and small thermal inertia; it detects the temperature level of the measured object by outputting a thermal electromotive force, and its electromotive force increases as the temperature rises. As for specific models, the platinum-rhodium 10-platinum type (LB-3) has a measurement range of 0~+1300℃, and when the temperature does not exceed 600℃ the permissible error is ±3℃; the tungsten-rhenium 5-tungsten-rhenium 20 type (WR) has a measurement range of 10~+2800℃, and when the temperature is higher than 1000℃ the permissible error is 1t; the copper-constantan type (CK) has a permissible error of ±0.6% in the range of -40~+80℃; the nickel-chromium-constantan type (NK) has a permissible error of ±1% when the temperature is higher than 400℃. Under normal conditions the resistance value between the two terminal posts of the thermocouple is zero; if the measured resistance value is infinite, it indicates that the hot end is already open and the thermocouple is damaged. The measurement ranges and permissible errors of the above models are the quantitative basis for judging whether the thermocouple is qualified: when the measured temperature falls within the corresponding range, the measured deviation should not exceed the permissible error given for that model; if it exceeds the range or the deviation is too large, the measurement result of the resistance value between the terminal posts should be combined to further judge whether the thermocouple itself has failed.

A diode is a semiconductor device with unidirectional conductivity, commonly denoted by VD in circuits, and is used in rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization and other applications. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: when a forward voltage is applied, the conduction resistance is small; when a reverse voltage is applied, the resistance is extremely large or infinite. Classified by function, diodes include rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85) and other types, and also include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. A light-emitting diode can emit light of colors such as red, green and yellow, has unidirectional conductivity, and its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode; it is commonly used to indicate the working state of a circuit or to form a large-screen color electronic display screen; its external dimensions include diameters of 3mm and 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle, its working current is generally 1~30mA depending on the model, and its conduction voltage is above 1.7V.

Light-emitting diode precautions: in actual use, a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage, the working current should be controlled within the range of 1~30mA, and when selecting, the external dimensions such as diameter 3mm, 5mm or 2mm×5mm rectangle should also be matched to the installation position. In an optical isolation circuit, when the input Q=0, the light-emitting diode inside the optocoupler emits light, causing the light-emitting transistor to conduct; when the input Q=1, the light-emitting diode does not emit light, and the light-emitting transistor is cut off. Diodes and transistors are widely used in marine electrical equipment; testing a diode requires following the corresponding diode testing steps, and these testing steps are applicable to diodes. During testing, the measurable performances of polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance should be addressed: first determine the polarity, then measure the forward voltage drop and reverse resistance, so as to confirm whether the unidirectional conductivity is normal.

A transistor is a semiconductor device containing two PN junctions internally and having current amplification capability; it is divided into two types, NPN type and PNP type, and is commonly denoted in circuits by the letter "VT" plus a number, for example VT17 indicates the transistor numbered 17. Its main models include PNP-type transistors such as A92 and 9015, and NPN-type transistors such as A42, 9014 and 9018. The working characteristics of the NPN type and the PNP type can complement each other; for example, the complementary pair in an OTL circuit utilizes this feature.

A transistor may suffer a transistor fault, and a transistor fault is a common problem under the device category of transistor. When testing a transistor, the measurable performances include the transistor type, base, collector, emitter and current amplification factor; the inspection order is usually to first determine the transistor type and base, then distinguish the collector and emitter, and finally measure the current amplification factor, so as to judge whether its amplification capability has decreased, whether its switching characteristics have deteriorated, or whether there is an open circuit between electrodes.

In the fault diagnosis process, a multimeter is used to measure voltage and current, and is also used to test diodes, transistors and thermocouples; a clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. Voltage, as a measurable performance quantity, can be measured by a multimeter or a voltmeter; measuring current requires an ammeter, which is connected in series after the circuit is disconnected. Voltage and current are both electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, and are used to understand the equipment status; the measurable performances of a diode include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance; the measurable performances of a thermocouple include resistance and electromotive force, and its electromotive force increases as the temperature rises.

In the composition of marine electrical equipment, integrated circuits and printed circuit boards are two types of fundamental devices that are widely used. Marine electrical equipment uses integrated circuits and also uses printed circuit boards. Integrated circuits have the characteristics of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration continues to increase, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits have also appeared. Their common package forms include PLCC with inward-hooking pins on four sides, SOIC with gull-wing pins on two sides, DIP with dual in-line pins, and power integrated circuit packages; common pin counts are 14 pins or 16 pins. Pin numbering starts from the notch or dot and proceeds counterclockwise. To facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often soldered on the circuit board for the integrated circuit to be plugged in directly. Integrated circuits can be divided by type into CMOS circuits and TTL circuits. A printed circuit board consists of two parts: the base material and the traces; the base material is the insulating substrate, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber); the trace part is made of conductive copper, laid on the substrate, with the required pattern obtained by etching, usually using copper foil.

Printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards; printed circuit boards will have circuit board faults, and circuit board faults are problems that must be faced within the scope of printed circuit boards.

Once the microcomputer monitoring and alarm system experiences a program interruption or shutdown during operation, the state of the power supply fuse needs to be checked. The fuse is a component of marine electrical equipment, made of a low-melting-point protective conductive material, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection; its manufacturing material is aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, etc., and it has the characteristics of a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength, and is listed together with resistors, capacitors, etc. as commonly used components in electronic circuits. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Power supply faults also deserve attention: in the microcomputer monitoring system, a power supply fault of the integrated circuit chip on the circuit board can cause the system to shut down completely with no fault information output; power supply faults can also cause motor overheating, PLC system faults and main engine remote control failure; in AC electric drive systems, it is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent and thus overheating; in PLC control systems, the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, so on board the strategy of overall replacement is usually adopted.

The main engine remote control system is used for remote operation of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge; when operating away from the engine side, this system needs to be installed between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. By type, the main engine remote control system includes the pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electric main engine remote control system, the electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, the electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, the microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and the field bus type main engine remote control system; in addition, it also includes the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system and the main engine remote control system simulation test device. There are several points to note in the maintenance of the main engine remote control system: do not arbitrarily adjust the parameters in the system or disassemble components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer; when disassembling the pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; drain residual water every day, check the filter every month, and replace dirty filter screens; before using the keyboard to modify system operating parameters or modifying system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record their original data or original positions; when performing electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance; when plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, the power supply must be switched off; also remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.

In terms of preventive measures, the links that can be prevented in the main engine remote control system include keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean, inspection inside the control box, inspection of input and output components, the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing, and the content of periodic effectiveness tests of all system functions.

Various fault symptoms will occur during the operation of the main engine remote control system. The main engine remote control system will have the situation where microcomputer remote control starting must be carried out twice each time, with the first attempt failing and the second succeeding; that is, microcomputer remote control starting must be carried out twice each time, the first failing and the second succeeding, and this phenomenon is precisely one of the faults occurring in the main engine remote control system. The main engine remote control system will have the phenomenon that after the main engine starts it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; the main engine remote control system will have serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; the main engine remote control system will have air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; the main engine remote control system will have moving parts jammed; the main engine remote control system will have fuse blowing or power supply faults; the main engine remote control system will have poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; the main engine remote control system will have electrical component faults; the main engine remote control system will have incorrect wiring after maintenance; in addition, the main engine remote control system will also have the main engine cannot be started by remote control.

Maintenance personnel are responsible for fault diagnosis and repair of marine electrical equipment. They need to be familiar with equipment principles, structures and repair materials, must be thoroughly familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components, and be familiar with the structures, working principles, functions and locations of electrical equipment components (assemblies). In conventional fault diagnosis, maintenance personnel need to understand the phenomena and make a preliminary diagnosis through asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. The conventional fault diagnosis method uses system testing, and determining the system structure and test method is a precondition for system testing. System testing adopts the measurement method most suitable for the system structure; its purpose is to check out the fault location. During operation, measurement must be carried out at suitable test points, and the fault location is checked by comparing the input feedback with normal values. When dealing with difficult faults for which the microcomputer system has no fault information, the module segmentation method is often used to narrow the scope.

The external test programs of some systems (such as memory and CPU tests) are often stored on floppy disks and temporarily loaded for running. As a magnetic medium, a floppy disk must be stored away from magnetic objects at an ambient temperature of 10~40℃; the usage requirement is to use a dedicated floppy disk and not to run it on other computers. In the C ship station, the floppy disk is used for operation; a dedicated floppy disk should be used to prevent virus infection, the storage ambient temperature should preferably be 10~40℃, and it must be kept away from magnetic objects.

The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of the ship's radar and monitoring system, used to present images, data and alarm information. It should be installed in the wheelhouse in a dry place free of strong electromagnetic radiation and away from heat sources, fixed with a hardwood base, and the main radar display should be oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge. The electrical control system of refrigerated containers has developed from the relay type to the microcomputer control type, featuring a wide temperature adjustment range (generally ±30℃), high constant-temperature accuracy, electric heating, automatic unloading and automatic control of the number of condenser fans; its technical requirements include that the temperature adjustment range inside the container is generally within ±30℃, and the adjustment accuracy needs to be improved by controlling intermittent operation of the compressor, hot-gas bypass of the refrigerant, refrigerant flow and evaporator fan speed; when the temperature inside the container is lower than the set value, the electrical control system of the refrigerated container can perform electric heating and can automatically perform unloading operations according to the size of the heat load, and automatically control the number of condenser fans according to the external environment and condenser pressure.

In the fault diagnosis of the engine room monitoring and alarm system, the conventional fault diagnosis method takes observation as the primary means. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, it is necessary to see whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Only after observation is completed does it turn to checking the monitoring and indicating device, that is, observation is the preceding step for checking the monitoring and indicating device. This sequence reflects the requirement of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site intact", and observation is exactly a sub-link under this step. As for applicable objects, observation applies both to the alarm device itself and to its associated sensor circuits, interface boards and various actuators;

As for the basis of judgment, abnormal phenomena reflect that the current working state of the equipment deviates from normal, part status reflects the integrity of the mechanical part, wire status reflects the reliability of the electrical connection, and equipment operating parameters reflect the actual values of the monitored object. As for the basis of judgment, the signal sent out by an analog sensor is a continuously changing electrical signal, whose value changes synchronously with the monitored parameter, so it can be used both for out-of-limit alarms and for parameter display; the switch-type sensor sends out only two states, contact on and off, and can only judge whether the equipment is normal, but cannot give the specific value of the parameter. As for the order of checking and operation, it should first be confirmed whether the sensor is analog or switch-type, and then the corresponding input interface and measurement circuit should be selected accordingly; during checking, attention should be paid to whether electrical isolation has been achieved between the sensor circuit and the I/O interface and CPU through an optical isolator, so as to avoid damage to the interface board due to circuit abnormalities.

In automatic fuel oil boilers, the potentiometer is used for bridge balancing: when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by potentiometer R1 driven by pressure regulator YBD and feedback potentiometer R10 driven by motor M loses balance, thereby reflecting the pressure deviation. The control platform contains sensors, which echoes the situation in the aforementioned antenna control platform where sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions. As for the components involved, the alarm value setting potentiometer and the upper/lower limit alarm jumper wires together form the comparison link; the level of the set value UL is determined by the resistance of potentiometer Rp, and the jumper wires determine whether the alarm takes the upper limit or the lower limit. As for the operating sequence, the alarm value should be adjusted after confirming that the plug-in board works normally; insert a screwdriver into the small hole on the panel and turn slowly, observing the displayed reading while adjusting, until the set value UL meets the requirement; after replacing the plug-in board, if the reading is inconsistent with the original alarm value, readjust by the same method; do not directly change the jumper wires to accommodate the reading.

The multimeter contains a measuring circuit, whose function is to convert different electrical quantities and different ranges. Since the magnetoelectric meter head can only pass microampere-level current, a conversion circuit is necessary to measure different electrical quantities and ranges; the measuring circuit is therefore one of the three basic components of MF-30 and MF-47 analog multimeters. The multimeter uses the resistance range to measure the resistance of a resistor. As for the applicable object, the measuring circuit is suitable for uniformly converting different electrical quantities and different ranges into microampere-level signals measurable by the meter head, and a resistor is one of the objects it frequently measures. As for the basis for judgment, whether the resistance of a resistor matches the nominal value is the basic basis for judging whether a component is good or bad; once the shunt resistor is open-circuited, the voltage corrector loses its main regulating function, and the no-load voltage of the generator rises accordingly. As for the precautions, the power supply must be cut off before measurement, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and if there is a capacitor in the circuit it should be discharged first; measuring with power on is strictly prohibited, so as to avoid damage to the meter head or distortion of the reading.

Readjustment is a maintenance operation for electrical components such as circuit breakers and relays with parameter deviation or abnormal mechanical state, restoring them to the specified values by adjusting springs, setting values or travel. When the reaction spring force is too large, readjustment is required; when the reaction spring force is too large and causes noise in the undervoltage trip unit, the noise is likewise eliminated by readjustment. Failure of the motor-operated positioning switch corresponds to readjustment; too large a reclosing contact surface also corresponds to readjustment; when an incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit causes the circuit breaker to trip automatically, this is still solved by readjustment. In the liquid level monitoring alarm unit, after interchange the delayed alarm time needs to be readjusted to meet the requirement. It can be seen that readjustment is used both for correcting the mechanical and electrical parameters of components such as circuit breakers and relays, and for setting the time parameters after interchange of alarm units. As for the applicable object, readjustment covers electrical components such as circuit breakers and relays, and also covers alarm devices such as the liquid level monitoring alarm unit. After interchange of the liquid level monitoring alarm unit, the delayed alarm time not meeting the requirement is likewise a case requiring readjustment. As for the operating sequence, it should first be determined whether it is an abnormal mechanical state or a setting value deviation, and then the specified value should be restored respectively by adjusting the spring, changing the setting value or correcting the travel; after adjustment, it is necessary to recheck whether the action has returned to normal and whether the delayed alarm time meets the requirement.

During observation, electrical quantity parameters need to be verified with the aid of instruments; the multimeter is a commonly used tool and can be used to measure objects such as resistors, voltage and thermocouples. In the ship station antenna control platform, the control platform contains sensors, with sensors placed respectively in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. When a thermocouple is normal, the resistance between its two terminal posts is zero; if infinity is measured, it indicates that the hot end is open-circuited and the thermocouple is damaged; this resistance criterion is the simplest method for judging on site whether a thermocouple is good or bad. When testing a thermocouple-type sensor, the wiring of the temperature sensor must be disconnected in the junction box; when testing a thermal resistor-type sensor, the wiring of the temperature sensor likewise must be disconnected in the junction box, and after disconnection its resistance or electromotive force is measured separately, so as to prevent other components in the circuit from affecting the reading. Thermocouples of different graduation numbers each have their own measuring range and permissible error: the platinum-rhodium 10-platinum type (LB-3) has a measuring range of 0~+1300℃, with a permissible error of ±3℃ at ≤600℃; the nickel-chromium-constantan type (NK) has a permissible error of ±1% at >400℃. These values are the basis for judging whether a thermocouple is out of tolerance and whether it needs to be replaced; when selecting, the temperature under measurement should also fall within the measuring range of the corresponding graduation number.

The junction box serves to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical components in the alarm device. The general alarm device includes a junction box; the general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc., and the junction box is one of its components; the wiring among the shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box is all routed through the junction box. The solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box but is connected directly into the local control box; this point must be distinguished when tracing line faults, so as to avoid taking a detour by tracing according to the routing of a conventional junction box. In addition, incorrect connection of the power supply line is also a cause of abnormality in the alarm and monitoring circuits; during troubleshooting, check whether the connection of the power supply line is consistent with the drawing requirements, focusing on whether the phase sequence, polarity and earthing terminal are connected wrongly, and energize for testing only after confirming they are correct.

Composition and types of the main engine remote control system. When operating away from the engine side, a main engine remote control system must be provided between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. The main engine remote control system is used for remote manipulation of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge; according to the implementation mode and the components used, it includes the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and field bus type main engine remote control system, etc. At the equipment level, the main engine remote control system includes the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system and also includes the digital electronic governor system, and is equipped with a main engine remote control system simulation test device for commissioning and function verification. Functionally, the main engine remote control system has logic program functions such as commutation, starting, repeated starting, restarting and slow-turning starting.

Precautions for daily use and maintenance. For maintenance of the main engine remote control system, first of all, do not arbitrarily adjust the parameters in the system or disassemble components sealed with the manufacturer's red paint. When disassembling pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in. Residual water should be drained daily, the filter should be checked monthly, and dirty filter screens should be replaced.

moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of terminals or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after repair; main engine cannot be started by remote control; cannot repeat starting; cannot remotely commutate. The above faults involve specific components included in the main engine remote control system, such as the commutation solenoid valve and orifice 3; during inspection, these components should be checked item by item in combination with their working states.

Classification of the main engine remote control system. The function of the main engine remote control system is to remotely manipulate the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge. Once the operating position is moved away from the engine side, this system must be configured between the operating position and the main engine so that remote control can be realized. If classified according to the differences in the components used by the remote control device and the driving mechanism, the main engine remote control system includes the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system, field bus type main engine remote control system and other types;

The NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system, and the main engine remote control system simulation test device also belong to this category.

The pneumatic main engine remote control system consists of a pneumatic remote control device plus a pneumatic actuating mechanism, and is additionally equipped with a small number of electrical components such as solenoid valves and speed-measuring circuits. Its advantages lie in large drive power, reliable operation, simple and intuitive structure, and ease of mastery and management; its disadvantages are the lag in pressure transmission, which limits the control distance, and its high requirements on air supply quality, with pneumatic components prone to air leakage, dirt blockage and wear. The pressure reducing valve is a component within this system.

In the electric main engine remote control system, the remote control device and the actuating mechanism are entirely composed of electrical components. Its structure is compact, the remote control distance is unlimited, the control performance is good, and the realization of various functions is relatively flexible; its shortcomings are the small drive power of the actuating mechanism and the higher technical level required of management personnel.

Distinguished by component form, it has two types: the contact relay type and the contactless integrated circuit type. The contactless electric remote control system can build its electronic control section with the aid of integrated circuits. The advantages of integrated circuits are small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; package forms are commonly 14-pin or 16-pin, and by type they are divided into CMOS circuits and TTL circuits; after the increase in integration density, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits also appeared. Their pin numbers are numbered counterclockwise starting from the notch or dot; to facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is usually soldered on the circuit board for direct plugging-in. There are four common package forms: PLCC with inward-hooked pins on four sides, SOIC with gull-wing pins on two sides, DIP with dual in-line pins, and power integrated circuit packages.

The failure rate of this type of electronic control system is constant, and periodic preventive maintenance is not required. In marine electrical equipment, the application of integrated circuits is very common.

The electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system has a remote control device based mainly on electrical components and an actuating mechanism using pneumatic components, combining the advantages of both the electric and pneumatic types, and is regarded as a relatively perfect main engine remote control system. The electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system consists of an electric remote control device and a hydraulic actuating mechanism; large drive power, good controllability and ease of remote control are its advantages; complex structure, the need for a hydraulic oil recovery system, and susceptibility to oil leakage and air seepage are its disadvantages.

The microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system has a hardware section based mainly on a PLC or microcomputer and its interface circuits, with pneumatic or electric components used only in the actuating mechanism, and most system functions are realized by software. It is flexible in application, powerful in function, highly adaptable and highly reliable; almost all ships launched in recent years have selected it, and it is currently evolving toward distributed and networked directions.

Data and instruction transmission inside the PLC adopts a bus-type structure, and the bus is one of the constituent parts of the PLC; once a CPU bus fault occurs, the input relay will act abnormally.

The fieldbus-type main engine remote control system is the product of the widespread application of computer networking technology on ships. Its constituent parts are controlled by distributed computer nodes, and the control nodes are interconnected via the fieldbus. Compared with traditional methods, the connecting cables are greatly reduced, wiring costs are thereby lowered, installation and maintenance are extremely convenient, and system reliability is also improved by the fieldbus interconnection.

The technical requirements of the main engine remote control system include logical program functions such as commutation, starting, repeated starting, restarting and slow-turning starting, all of which the main engine remote control system possesses; it can also automatically avoid operating in the critical speed range, and executes the load program when the load reaches 70%-75%. The safety protection program is also part of the system; when conditions such as low lubricating oil pressure occur, it can automatically reduce speed or stop the engine and give an alarm.

The microcomputer control system is additionally provided with a self-diagnostic program; the fault point can be displayed and the fault type can be printed.

For daily maintenance, the air supply pressure must be kept normal and clean, valves must be overhauled regularly, and the contact condition of plug-in units must be checked. There are several preventive tasks for the main engine remote control system: keep the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean; check the interior of the control box; check the input and output components; the items to be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing; and periodically carry out the effectiveness test of all system functions.

The following points must be noted for the main engine remote control system during maintenance. Do not adjust the parameters in the system at will, and do not disassemble components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer. When disconnecting pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in. Residual water is drained daily, the filter is checked monthly, and dirty filter screens are replaced in time.

Before using the keyboard to modify system operating parameters, or modifying system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record the original data or original position. When performing electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance. When inserting or removing the printed circuit board, turn off the power. Also remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.

The possible fault symptoms of the main engine remote control system include: microcomputer remote control starting requires two attempts each time, the first fails and the second succeeds; after the main engine is started, it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent hole of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; electrical component fault;

incorrect wiring after repair; main engine cannot be started by remote control; cannot repeat starting; cannot perform remote control reversing.

Regarding the maintenance of related equipment, the solenoid valve undertakes the control task of fuel on-off; during ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation circuit so that the oil enters the fuel nozzle for injection. This kind of valve controlled by an electrical signal can also be used to release residual air from the air compressor, or to control fine water mist fire-extinguishing zones; solenoid valves are also found in automatic fuel boilers. Its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil, the purpose being to prevent high voltage from being generated when the power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The marine motor contains bearings; the function of the bearing is to support the rotation of the rotor, and once a fault occurs, the motor will exhibit overheating, vibration and abnormal noise; one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems is bearing fault; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is often accompanied by very loud uneven noise and the characteristic of bearing end cover overheating. Checking the bearing fault itself and checking the lubrication condition must both be carried out around the bearing.

The main engine remote control system can be divided by implementation method into pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and field bus type main engine remote control system, etc.; the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the digital electronic governor system and the main engine remote control system simulation test device all belong to this category. This system is used for remote manipulation of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge; when the operating position is away from the engine side, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. The goal of daily maintenance is to keep the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean; around this goal, several maintenance items for preventing faults have been formed, including checking the interior of the control box, checking the input and output components, the items to be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing, and periodically carrying out the effectiveness test of all system functions.

For the main engine remote control system, it must be noted that the maintenance item of keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean requires draining residual water every day, checking the filter every month, and replacing dirty filter screens; for the main engine remote control system, it must be noted that when disconnecting pneumatic pipelines, prevent external debris and dust from falling in.

Under the condition that the air source is dry and clean, valve components with a working pressure of 1MPa shall be overhauled once every four years, and valve components with a working pressure of 3MPa shall be overhauled once every two years; during regular overhaul, aged sealing rings, sealing rings and worn moving parts shall also be replaced in time. The air source pressure and cleanliness are directly related to the working state of the sealing elements in pneumatic valve components. The sealing ring is used to prevent air leakage in the air circuit. Once the sealing ring in the two-position three-way valve is damaged or lost, it will cause air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit, thereby causing the actuating air pressure at the control end of the valve component to be too low and the valve position to be unable to switch. During daily maintenance, aged sealing rings and sealing rings shall be replaced in time; aging of sealing rings is one of the problems that must be dealt with in regular overhaul.

Internal inspection of the control box is applicable to electrical control devices in plug-in form. The inspection contents include: whether the plug-in is loose and whether the contact is good, whether there is corrosion between the plug-in and the socket and timely removal thereof, whether the control box and external signal lines are fastened and in good contact, whether the shielding earthing is reliable, and regular inspection of the contact condition of sliding-contact electrical appliances such as relay contacts and potentiometers.

The potentiometer plays an important role in the microcomputer remote control system. The telegraph handle controls only one potentiometer, and different positions send different voltage signals to the microcomputer; in automatic combustion regulation of the boiler, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance. When the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by the potentiometer driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer driven by the motor M changes accordingly. A potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes with shaft rotation. The volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is this type of component and is generally considered manually adjustable.

The inspection objects of input and output components include components such as transmitters, sensors and actuators, and each item shall generally be inspected once every three months. During inspection, it is necessary to check the electrical contacts of sensors such as temperature and pressure sensors and the parallel high-resistance resistors, verify the upper and lower limit set values of the sensing and detection components and readjust the deviation, confirm that the error between the display device of the control station and the actual value is within the required range, and also check whether actuator components such as the actuating motor and solenoid valve are in good condition.

The sensor is the information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system and is divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors; in the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively to send error signals to control compensation motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by electrical signals and is used to cut off the fuel circulation circuit, release residual air from the air compressor, or control water mist fire-extinguishing zones; the automatic fuel boiler includes a solenoid valve and a potentiometer. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit during ignition and allowing fuel to enter the nozzle for injection.

Before sailing, the items to be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation include: check whether the working power supply, emergency power supply and alarm power supply of the device are normal; carry out transfer and interlock tests for the control stations at the bridge, centralized control room and engine-side; carry out closed-loop maneuvering tests and simulation tests for each remote control station according to function; observe and judge whether components such as the telegraph transmitter and program controller work correctly and reliably; check the status of auxiliary power and automatic control devices related to the main engine remote control system. Any auxiliary or automatic regulating device that does not meet the technical requirements shall not be put into use.

Regular effectiveness tests of all system functions cover: verification of program control functions such as commutation, starting, braking, speed regulation and stopping; testing of the safety interlock logic among the turning gear, starting device and remote control stations; verification of the effectiveness of functions such as stopping, deceleration and emergency maneuvering by simulating faults; testing of the limiting functions of the device using simulated signals such as scavenging pressure, torque and fuel throttle; checking of alarm functions under conditions such as power supply failure, emergency maneuvering, commutation failure or starting failure; testing of the accuracy indicators of the speed detection system and the governor.

For the main engine remote control system, note that the parameters in the system must not be adjusted at will, and the components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer must not be disassembled; this precaution applies to the daily maintenance of the electrical main engine remote control system and is located after the periodic inspection requirement of keeping the air supply pressure normal and clean. For the main engine remote control system, note that before using the keyboard to modify the system operating parameters or modifying the system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record their original data or original positions. For the main engine remote control system, note that when performing electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance. For the main engine remote control system, note that when simulating the closed state of an external relay contact (short-circuiting two electrical wiring terminals), it must be confirmed that there is no voltage between the two terminals, or that although there is voltage, there is a current-limiting resistor, so that no short circuit will be caused and the fault will not be expanded. For the main engine remote control system, note that when plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, the power must be turned off, and the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot must be remembered.

Various faults will occur during the operation of the main engine remote control system, including: the microcomputer remote control start requires two attempts each time, with the first failing and the second succeeding; after the main engine is started, it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after maintenance; the main engine cannot be started by remote control; failure to repeat starting. Among them, serious air leakage from the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve may be caused by blockage of the orifice, aging of the rubber diaphragm, or incorrect installation position of some components during disassembly and assembly; during handling, a cleaning needle can be used to clear the blocked orifice, clean the dirt and replace the rubber diaphragm; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit may be caused by air leakage at the pipe joint or damage or loss of the sealing ring in the two-position three-way valve; a pressure gauge can be used to quantitatively measure from the air source to the end to locate the leakage point;

Jamming of moving parts is often caused by lack of oil; the main engine cannot be started by remote control may be caused by incorrect setting of operating parameters, the control mode selection switch not being at the selected control station, the working air source of the main engine remote control pneumatic system not being opened, or the starting conditions not being met; failure to repeat starting may be caused by a fault in the timing circuit or time relay (according to the time principle) or a fault in the speed detection and judgment circuit (according to the speed principle); failure to remotely reverse may be caused by a fault in the logic circuit or logic relay circuit, or a fault in the mechanical and control detection circuits and devices that cannot switch to a certain direction. Power supply fault is the cause of abnormal electrical power supply that leads to motor overheating, PLC system faults and main engine remote control failure; in AC electric drive systems, power supply fault is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent and thus overheating; in the PLC control system, the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, so the ship usually adopts the strategy of overall replacement.

Fault diagnosis and maintenance work place clear requirements on maintenance personnel. Maintenance personnel must be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of the components (assemblies) of the electrical equipment, must be very familiar with the circuits, working principles and positions of all components of the whole ship's electrical equipment, and must master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling. Observation is also the preceding step of checking the monitoring and indicating device; after completing the observation, the monitoring and indicating device is then checked. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status and equipment operating parameters; specifically, it is necessary to check whether the parts are jammed or damaged, and whether the wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Observation is a sub-step of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, "carrying out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged". After the motor or drive system is energized, it cannot establish rotational motion, that is, the fault symptom of failure to start occurs; when constructing a fault tree, it is often selected as the top event of electrical equipment, such as motor fails to start; the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as normal power supply and normal control circuit.

Marine electrical equipment uses integrated circuits. Integrated circuits have the advantages of small size, light weight, high reliability and stable performance; as the degree of integration has increased, large-scale and very-large-scale integrated circuits have appeared. Their common package forms are 14-pin or 16-pin, and the types are divided into CMOS circuits and TTL circuits; the pin numbers start from the notch or dot and are numbered counterclockwise. To facilitate maintenance and replacement, a chip socket is often welded on the circuit board for direct plugging. Common package forms also include the four-side package with inward-hooking pins (PLCC), the two-side package with gull-wing pins (SOIC), the dual in-line package (DIP) and power integrated circuit packages. If capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance; never measure with power on.

In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage corrector to lose its main regulating action.
