In daily maintenance, keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean is a basic task that can prevent faults; at the same time, the internal inspection of the control box and the inspection of input and output electrical components should be done well, and before sailing, the items to be checked in conjunction with the main engine preparation should be implemented one by one, and the effectiveness test of all system functions should be carried out periodically. During system operation, the phenomenon may occur that microcomputer remote control starting requires two attempts each time, with the first failing and the second succeeding; such abnormalities are often related to parameter settings or the state of electrical components.

There are several precautions that must be observed in maintenance work. When opening the air piping, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; drain residual water daily, check the filter monthly, and replace dirty filter screens. When performing electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance.

The daily maintenance of the main engine remote control system also requires regular inspection of the contact condition of relay contacts and sliding-contact electrical appliances (potentiometers). In the microcomputer remote control system, the telegraph handle controls only a potentiometer, and different positions send different voltage signals to the microcomputer; therefore, whether the potentiometer contact is reliable directly affects the accuracy of command transmission.

As for pneumatic valve components, during normal use the output air pressure of the pressure regulating valve is stable at the set value, and when the working condition is unchanged, no air leaks from the vent hole. Its fault manifestation is serious leakage from the vent hole, with causes including a blocked throttle orifice, aging of the rubber diaphragm or incorrect assembly of parts; the repair method is to clear the blocked throttle orifice with a cleaning needle, clean off dirt and replace the aging rubber diaphragm. In the local control system of the Sulzer RTA84c diesel engine, the pressure regulating valve is used to manually adjust the speed-governing air pressure signal.

As for electrical components, poor contact is a common cause of equipment faults. At electrical connections, looseness, oxidation or foreign matter causes the contact resistance to increase; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact and increase the contact resistance, which may further cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure and interphase short circuit. Common faults of the main engine remote control system include air leakage and jamming of pneumatic valve components, poor contact of electrical components and incorrect parameter settings; in addition, there are fuse blowing or power supply faults, poor contact of wiring terminals or connectors, corrosion, electrical component fault, incorrect wiring after maintenance, etc.

As for fault diagnosis methods, fault tree analysis belongs to the analysis method for electronic equipment faults and is also called the fault signal flow chart tracing method in troubleshooting main engine starting faults; it determines the fault location by tracing and checking the various signal paths and states related to the fault.

Fault tree analysis uses a fault tree. A fault tree is a connected logic tree that contains no closed loops, and it uses graphical symbols to represent the logical combinations among various events that cause undesired events of a system. Its structure is a logic tree, containing the top event, intermediate events and basic events. The logical relationships include AND and OR, of which the most commonly used are the "AND" and "OR" relationships. The fault tree develops downward from the tree root of the top event; the branches represent accident events, and the nodes represent logical relationships. Fault tree analysis originates from graph theory. It was first used by Bell Labs in the United States in the design of the Minuteman missile control system to predict random failure probability, and was later successfully applied in the WASH-1400 report, quantitatively giving the risk of nuclear power plants for the first time and proving their safety. The generator being unable to build up voltage is also an optional top event when constructing a fault tree.

Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding check the monitoring and indicating device. Overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems. The secondary side must not be open-circuited; the external ammeter terminals must have short-circuit connecting pieces, and they may be disconnected only after the wiring has been checked.

Marine electrical equipment uses printed circuit boards. A printed circuit board consists of a base material and circuits. The base material is an insulating material, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber). The circuit part is made of conductive copper, laid on the base board, and the required pattern is obtained by etching. Printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components; the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards; circuit board faults will occur on printed circuit boards, and circuit board faults fall within the scope of printed circuit boards.

Serious air leakage from the vent hole of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve; air leakage in the pneumatic logic circuit; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after maintenance; main engine cannot be started by remote control; cannot repeat starting. These all belong to the category of common faults, among which air leakage and jamming of pneumatic valve components, poor contact of electrical components and incorrect parameter settings are relatively typical.

When handling faults, changes to parameters must be made with particular care. This precaution applies to the electrical measurement process of the main engine remote control system. Its operating scenario is short-circuiting two electrical wiring terminals to simulate the closed state of an external relay contact. Before execution, it must be confirmed that there is no voltage between the two terminals. If there is voltage between the two terminals, it must be confirmed that a current-limiting resistor exists to prevent a short circuit from expanding the fault.

These precautions apply to the fault analysis and handling steps of the main engine remote control system. When performing the operation of inserting and removing the printed circuit board, the power supply must be switched off first, and at the same time the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot must be recorded; this step must be carried out in conjunction with the power-off operation. The printed circuit board consists of a base material and circuits; the base material is an insulating material, such as phenolic resin board or epoxy glass, and the circuits are conductive foil, usually copper.

Resistance is measured with a multimeter, and voltage is measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter. The property that can be measured for resistance is the resistance value, and the property that can be measured for voltage is the voltage value. When measuring a resistor in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off;

The pneumatic main engine remote control system includes a pressure reducing valve, a pressure regulating valve and a sealing ring, all three of which are components of its pneumatic valve parts. Once a fault occurs, a relatively serious air leakage phenomenon can be found at the vent hole. The causes of this phenomenon are usually of three types: blocked throttle orifice, aging rubber diaphragm, or incorrect position of some components during disassembly and assembly. The corresponding repair method for this type of fault is to clear the blocked throttle orifice with a cleaning needle, clean the dirt, and replace the rubber diaphragm; the specific operation is to clear the blocked throttle orifice with a cleaning needle, clean the dirt and replace the aged rubber diaphragm. For that caused by a blocked throttle orifice, it is sufficient to clear the blockage with a cleaning needle and clean the dirt; for that caused by an aging rubber diaphragm, directly replace the rubber diaphragm; incorrect position of some components during disassembly and assembly will likewise cause the above-mentioned air leakage fault of the valve parts, and this must be corrected during disassembly and assembly. The sealing ring is a sealing element in the pneumatic valve parts, used to prevent air leakage in the air path; damage to or loss of the sealing ring in the two-position three-way valve will cause the control-end actuating air pressure of the valve part to be too low and the valve position to be unable to switch, and in daily maintenance the aged sealing ring and sealing ring must be replaced in time. When locating such air leakage points, it is best to use an air pressure gauge to perform quantitative measurement from the air source toward the end; compared with judging by listening to the sound, quantitative point-by-point measurement from the air source toward the end with an air pressure gauge is a better locating method, and this method is suitable for solving the problem of too-low control-end air pressure caused by damage to pipe joints or sealing rings.

A fuse is a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material, having the characteristics of a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength, and is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, ranking alongside resistors and capacitors; its manufacturing material is a protective conductive material such as aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy. Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter; loose fastening screws and wiring terminals will cause poor contact and increase the contact resistance; poor contact can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit, and will cause random output actions, and the corresponding handling method is to check the terminal wiring. In addition, a circuit breaker has a mechanical fault in which one phase contact cannot close, generally caused by breakage of one phase connecting rod of the circuit breaker, that is, the fault cause is generally breakage of one phase connecting rod of the circuit breaker, and the handling method is to replace the broken connecting rod.

The control mode selection switch not being at the selected control station, the working air source of the main engine remote control pneumatic system not being opened, etc., will cause the main engine cannot be started by remote control; the control mode selection switch not being at the selected control station, the working air source of the main engine remote control pneumatic system not being opened, etc., correspond to checking whether the control mode selection switch is at the selected control station, whether the working air source of the main engine remote control pneumatic system is opened, etc.; during troubleshooting, first check whether the control mode selection switch is at the selected control station and confirm that the working air source of the main engine remote control pneumatic system has been opened; if the above routine checks show no abnormality, then further verify whether the main engine starting conditions are met. The starting conditions include the turning gear disengaged signal and the main engine starting position signal, and also include the starting air pressure signal and the control air pressure signal. Incorrect setting of working parameters is one of the common fault causes of the main engine remote control system; setting the ignition speed preset value, starting fuel quantity or main starting air valve opening time limit to zero will cause main engine starting failure; even if the system components have no hardware fault, incorrect parameter settings will also cause main engine starting failure, and system aging causing the original working parameters to no longer match is the cause of incorrect parameter settings. For starting conditions not being met, each starting condition or sensing detection element should be checked one by one for faults, on the basis that only when all starting conditions are met and detection is normal is the main engine permitted to start;

If the confirmation conditions and components in this step are normal, the logic discrimination circuit of the control box should be checked subsequently. If repeated starting is by the time principle, a fault in the timing circuit or time relay (by the time principle) will cause failure to repeat starting; a fault in the timing circuit or time relay (by the time principle) corresponds to checking the timing circuit or time relay (by the time principle), and emphasis should be placed on checking the timing circuit or time relay; if repeated starting is by the speed principle, a fault in the speed detection and judgment circuit (by the speed principle) will cause failure to repeat starting; a fault in the speed detection and judgment circuit (by the speed principle) corresponds to checking the speed detection and judgment circuit (by the speed principle), and emphasis should be placed on checking the speed detection and judgment circuit; if the combined speed and time principle is used, both the speed detection and conversion circuit and the time circuit need to be checked.

Failure of remote-control commutation may be caused by a fault in its own logic circuit or logic relay circuit; a fault in the logic circuit or logic relay circuit will cause failure of remote-control commutation; it may also be caused by a fault in the mechanical and control detection circuits and devices for failure to commutate to a certain direction; a fault in the mechanical and control detection circuits and devices for failure to commutate to a certain direction will cause failure of remote-control commutation; a fault in the commutation solenoid valve will also cause failure of remote-control commutation. In the event of a fault, correct response cannot be made, and emphasis should be placed on checking the components and circuits of both the mechanical and control detection parts.

The preventable maintenance items of the main engine remote control system include keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean, including inspection inside the control box, including inspection of input and output components, and also including the items to be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing.

When disassembling the pneumatic pipeline, prevent external debris and dust from falling in; its pin numbers are numbered counterclockwise starting from the notch or dot; the automatic fuel oil boiler includes a potentiometer. Failure to meet starting conditions likewise causes the main engine cannot be started by remote control. The time relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship's power system, with common designations KT, SJ, and SL. A fault in the logic circuit or logic relay circuit is one of the possible fault causes of failure of main engine remote-control commutation; if a relay logic circuit is used, the relays of this part and their related contacts need to be checked; if an electronic integrated circuit is used, it can be checked by the waveform test method or the substitution method; if it is a microcomputer control system, the fault point can be found by the self-test program or the simulation board.

A fault in the logic circuit or logic relay circuit corresponds to the maintenance procedure of checking the logic circuit or logic relay circuit; this procedure is one of the possible causes of the failure of main engine remote-control commutation; if a relay logic circuit is used, the relays of this part and their related contacts need to be checked; if an electronic integrated circuit is used, it can be checked by the waveform test method or the substitution method; in a microcomputer control system, the fault point can be found through the self-test program or the simulation board function; when all starting conditions are met and the detection elements are normal, the discrimination circuit in the control box should be checked. A fault in the mechanical and control detection circuits and devices for failure to commutate to a certain direction corresponds to the maintenance procedure of detecting the mechanical and control detection circuits and devices for failure to commutate to a certain direction; this fault is one of the possible causes of the failure of main engine remote-control commutation; the fault manifests as failure to correctly respond to the commutation state or command; during maintenance, emphasis should be placed on detecting the relevant mechanical and control detection components and circuits; this link belongs to the fault of the execution and feedback links outside the logic discrimination circuit of the remote control system.

The pressure reducing valve sets working parameters such as the starting fuel quantity through a set value in the main engine remote control system. During normal use, the output air pressure is stabilized at the set value, and when the working condition is unchanged, no air leaks from the vent hole;

Routine maintenance of the main engine remote control system focuses on keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean, and regularly inspecting the interior of the control box and the input and output components. Before sailing, the items to be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation must be confirmed, as well as the contents of the periodic effectiveness test of all system functions. Specifically, the main engine remote control system can prevent faults caused by unclean air supply or abnormal pressure, and the method is to keep the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean; the main engine remote control system can prevent faults inside the control box caused by dust accumulation, dampness or looseness, and the method is to carry out internal inspection of the control box; the main engine remote control system can prevent faults of input and output components caused by poor contact or damage, and the method is to carry out inspection of input and output components; the main engine remote control system can prevent hidden dangers from being discovered only after sailing, and the method is to confirm item by item before sailing in conjunction with the items to be checked in main engine preparation; the main engine remote control system can prevent functional failure, and the method is to periodically carry out the effectiveness test contents of all system functions.

The types of main engine remote control systems cover pneumatic main engine remote control systems, electric main engine remote control systems, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control systems, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control systems, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control systems and field bus type main engine remote control systems. The NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system is one of them, and there are also digital electronic governor systems and main engine remote control system simulation test devices. It may also happen that after the main engine is started it cannot accelerate and automatically stops;

The control modes of the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system include microcomputer remote control, pneumatic remote control and local control. Normal use is microcomputer remote control, pneumatic remote control is used as backup, and local control is only used as emergency. The system is provided with a two-time starting mechanism; after the first failure, the second Heavy Start is automatically carried out. The starting fuel quantity air pressure set on the simulation board for the first start is 1.1 bar, and the Heavy Start starting fuel quantity set air pressure set on the panel for the second start is

1.8 bar. When a fault occurs in which microcomputer remote control starting requires two attempts each time, with the first failing and the second succeeding, while local control and pneumatic remote control modes are both normal, parameters and safety protection devices are not abnormal, and simulation board tests show no hardware fault in the microcomputer and control valve themselves, the root cause is that the first-start starting fuel quantity air pressure set value of 1.1 bar is lower than the second Heavy Start set value of 1.8 bar, that is, the starting fuel quantity is too small. After 10 years of operation of this engine, due to wear of the cylinder and fuel throttle transmission mechanism, continuing to use the new-engine starting fuel quantity parameters will result in it being too small. At this time, the handling method corresponding to the starting fuel quantity being too small is to set the starting fuel quantity air pressure for the first start to 1.5 bar, that is, adjust the starting fuel quantity air pressure for the first start from 1.1 bar to 1.5 bar. The second start automatically switches to Heavy Start mode, and starting can succeed using the 1.8 bar speed setting air pressure signal, so the fault is eliminated. The original setting of 1.1 bar is the new-engine standard, and after 10 years of operation it needs to be appropriately modified according to the machine condition.

During inspection, if the safety interlock is normal and local control is normal, the possibility of actuator failure can be ruled out, and analysis should focus on the starting link including the starting fuel quantity setting and holding link. One cause of this fault is that orifice 3 is dirty and blocked; orifice 3 is located at the one-way variable throttle valve 3 between regulating valve 2 and air reservoir 4. When the main engine starts, through the action of orifice 3, the solenoid valve is made to operate in the upper position to supply the starting fuel quantity; after the starting signal disappears, the air in the air reservoir is released through this orifice, and its release time determines the holding duration of the starting fuel quantity. Dirty blockage will cause the two speed signals not to switch in time after starting, so that the main engine cannot accelerate; because the orifice becomes smaller, the transition process between the two states is too long, causing the valve spool to remain in a critical state for too long and resulting in shutdown.

The maintenance procedure corresponding to the dirty blockage of orifice 3 is to clean and adjust the throttle valve; the operating object is the one-way variable throttle valve (No. 3) in the main engine governor system. After this step is performed, the above governor fault can be eliminated, allowing valve 1 to reset and normal speed regulation to be carried out.

The reversing solenoid valve fault is one of the fault causes listed in the fault handling examples of the main engine remote control system and will cause failure of remote reversing. The maintenance procedure corresponding to the reversing solenoid valve fault is to check the reversing solenoid valve. In the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, the reversing solenoid valve fault is one of the potential causes of abnormal main engine starting. In troubleshooting burner ignition faults, if there is an ignition spark but no fuel injection, it is necessary to check whether solenoid valve DF operates; if solenoid valve DF does not operate, further check whether its coil is open and whether the valve core is stuck. The solenoid valve drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge.

Among the common faults of the PLC control system, the possible fault causes for a certain input relay failing to energize include an input signal source (device) fault; the direct cause of a certain input relay being normally closed is judged to be an input circuit (circuit) fault, and the handling method is to check the circuit or replace the relevant components. On the output side, the manifestations are: a certain output relay fails to energize while the indicator lamp is off, the possible cause being that the output ON time is too short or an output circuit fault; a certain output relay fails to energize while the indicator lamp is on, possibly caused by damage to the output relay or a broken output wiring; a certain output relay fails to turn off while the indicator lamp is off, possibly caused by damage to the output relay, requiring replacement of the relay, or possibly caused by excessive earth leakage current of the output drive transistor, requiring replacement of the output transistor; a certain output relay fails to turn off while the indicator lamp is on, possibly caused by an output drive circuit fault, requiring replacement of the output port circuit, or possibly caused by repeated port addresses in the output instructions, requiring modification of the program.

Technical requirements and general maintenance principles of the digital electronic governor system. The main engine remote control system is used for remote operation of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge. When the operator leaves the local operating position beside the engine, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. According to different implementation methods, the main engine remote control system includes the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system, and field bus type main engine remote control system, among which the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system is one specific product. The main engine remote control system also includes a main engine remote control system simulation test device, used for simulated verification of system functions before mooring or sailing.

The digital electronic governor system is a component of the main engine remote control system; it directly operates the fuel lever through an electric actuator, changing the fuel opening and thereby regulating the main engine fuel supply.

The basic technical requirements for the digital electronic governor system include the following aspects. The regulating link should adopt a PI control law with no steady-state error and have good performance in tracking telegraph commands. The output characteristic curve of the governor system should conform as closely as possible to the propeller operating characteristics to achieve optimal regulating performance. The system should be able to accept various limits, such as maximum speed limit, minimum speed limit, maximum fuel limit, etc., but under emergency operation these limits can be automatically cancelled. The system should be able to immediately execute fault slowdown or shutdown commands sent from the main engine safety system.

In maintenance work, there are several points requiring special attention in the main engine remote control system.

Do not arbitrarily adjust the parameters in the system or disassemble components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer. When disassembling the air circuit piping, prevent external debris and dust from falling in. Drain residual water every day, inspect the filter every month, and replace dirty filter screens. Before using the keyboard to modify system operating parameters or using the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board to modify system operating parameters, it is best to record their original data or original positions. When performing electrical measurements, the test plan should be designed in advance. When simulating the closed state of external relay contacts (short-circuiting two electrical terminal posts), confirm that there is no voltage between the two terminal posts, or that although there is voltage, there is a current-limiting resistor that will not cause a short circuit and expand the fault. When plugging or unplugging the printed circuit board, turn off the power and remember the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot.

The preventable faults of the main engine remote control system are realized through a series of preventive maintenance measures. Keeping the starting and control air supply pressure normal and clean is a basic requirement for the preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Internal inspection of the control box is likewise an important part of the preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Inspection of input and output components also falls within the scope of the preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Before sailing, the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation are routine work for the preventable faults of the main engine remote control system. Regularly conducting effectiveness tests of all system functions ensures, from the perspective of overall function, the prevention of faults in the main engine remote control system. In addition, the main engine remote control system may also exhibit the phenomenon that microcomputer remote control starting requires two attempts each time, that is, the first start fails and only the second start succeeds; attention should be paid to this phenomenon during maintenance.

Composition and maintenance items of the DGS-8800e digital electronic governor system The DGS-8800e digital electronic governor system is a product of NOR-CONTROL Company and is a specific implementation of the digital electronic governor system. It consists of two major parts, the regulator and the actuator, which are controlled by two microcomputer systems respectively. This system can serve as the speed control circuit in the main engine remote control system and can also directly receive telegraph commands. The regulator performs rate-limiting control and critical speed avoidance processing on the telegraph commands, and after comparing the current telegraph command with the current main engine speed, issues a fuel supply signal. The actuator drives the servo motor to act according to the command, so as to adjust the throttle position.

The preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system are implemented item by item through the following maintenance items. Testing the relevant indicator lights and promptly replacing damaged bulbs or light-emitting diodes is one aspect of the preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Tightening the plug-in boards and plug-in board sockets can keep the circuit board plug-ins secure and in good contact, and is a measure for the preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Tightening the fuse and terminal posts is likewise for keeping the circuit board plug-ins secure and in good contact, and is also a measure for the preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system.

Checking whether the electric (hydraulic) converter valve works normally, that is, checking the working state of the electro-pneumatic (hydraulic) converter valve, is an inspection item for the preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Checking whether the AC and DC working power supply voltages are normal, with the inspection objects including the AC working power supply voltage and the DC working power supply voltage, is likewise an inspection item for the preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. Carefully checking whether the various lead cables have open-circuit faults and whether the shielding ends are reliably earthed also falls within the scope of the preventable faults of the digital electronic governor system. If the actuator is a servo motor, the motor should be serviced regularly. The relay, servo motor, and brake in the control circuit should also be checked.

In the DGS-8800e system, the actuator causes the servo motor to act according to the regulator command, pulling the throttle to the fuel supply position corresponding to the regulator command. When disassembling and inspecting the servo motor, special attention should be paid to the corresponding positional relationship among its position feedback, the synchro, and the throttle opening; the corresponding relationship among the position feedback, the synchro, and the throttle opening should be verified. This maintenance item falls within the scope of control circuit inspection, and the relay and brake must be checked at the same time.

A multimeter can be used to measure voltage and can also be used to test diodes. When measuring voltage, a multimeter or a voltmeter may be used.

A diode is a semiconductor device widely used in marine electrical equipment, having unidirectional conductivity, and is commonly denoted by VD in circuits. A diode has a small conduction resistance under forward voltage, and an extremely large or infinite resistance under reverse voltage, and is commonly used in circuits such as rectification, isolation, voltage regulation and polarity protection. Diodes include many types, and by function can be divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), light-emitting diodes, Zener diodes, etc. The diode testing steps are applicable to the testing of this class of diode devices. The measurable performance of a diode includes polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance.

A light-emitting diode is one type of diode, having unidirectional conductivity and capable of emitting red, green, yellow and other colors of light. Its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit working-status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display. The external dimensions of light-emitting diodes include diameters of 3mm, 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle.

The working current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model, and the conduction voltage is above
1.7V. For light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes; in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage.

A fuse is a component of marine electrical equipment, belongs to one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, and is listed alongside resistors, capacitors, etc. A fuse is made of protective conductive material and has the characteristics of a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength, and is made of aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, etc. A fuse is used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. The maintenance content of the electronic governor system includes tightening the fuse and terminal posts.

The servo motor is used to adjust the opening of the air damper and the fuel control, rotates according to the bridge output signal, and drives the feedback potentiometer to adjust, so that the bridge is rebalanced. An automatic fuel oil boiler contains a servo motor; in boiler combustion regulation, the servo motor is energized by the winding controlled by the differential amplifier and the thyristor to adjust the air-fuel ratio, and when rotating drives the sliding contact of the feedback potentiometer R10 to move, so that the bridge stops after reaching balance again. In the DGS-8800e governor system, the servo motor receives the power amplifier signal and rotates to pull the fuel control to the specified position.

The display is used in the main engine remote control system to display the actual speed, and in the event of a fault displays error information of core components such as the CPU. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, and are used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals, and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The main engine remote control system is used to carry out remote maneuvering of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge. When the operator leaves the local operating position, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine in order to achieve remote control. According to different implementation methods, the main engine remote control system can be divided into pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and fieldbus-type main engine remote control system, etc.; the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system and the digital electronic governor system also belong to this category. The main engine remote control system includes a main engine remote control system simulation test device, which is used to check the functions and operating conditions of the main engine remote control system.

The basic design purpose of the main engine remote control system simulation test device is to provide simulation signals in order to check the remote control system functions, determine faults and adjust parameters. It utilizes the characteristic that the remote control system cannot distinguish between actual speed and simulated speed, and performs functional testing when the main engine is stopped. Structurally, the device consists of two parts: the main engine simulated speed setting board and the system function simulation test board. The main engine simulated speed setting board includes a selector switch, a potentiometer and an indicating voltmeter, and is used to replace the speed sensor signal; the system function simulation test board is equipped with LED display of working status, as well as a digital display and keyboard for querying and modifying parameters. In a microcomputer control system, the device shares the same microcomputer with the control system to process the analog input signals.

In the analog test device of the main engine remote control system, the light-emitting diode is used to display the working status of the remote control system and the action of the external solenoid valve.

The light-emitting diode is a semiconductor device capable of emitting light in colors such as red, green and yellow, and has unidirectional conductivity; its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit working status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display screen. Its external dimensions include a diameter of 3mm, 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle; the working current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model, and the conduction voltage is above 1.7V; in actual use, a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage. Marine electrical equipment uses diodes, and the diode detection procedure is applicable to diodes. The multimeter is used to measure voltage and is also used to detect diodes. The voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or a voltmeter.

The sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, and is divided into two major categories: analog quantity and switching quantity sensors. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, and are used to send error signals to control the compensation motion when the ship pitches and rolls. The analog quantity sensor in the engine room monitoring and alarm system converts the parameter into a continuously changing electrical signal, and is suitable for scenarios where both the equipment status is monitored and the parameter value is displayed.

The automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve and a potentiometer. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of the fuel oil; during ignition it cuts off the fuel oil circulation circuit, and the fuel oil enters the oil nozzle for injection. The solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, and is used to cut off the fuel oil circulation circuit, release the residual air of the air compressor, or control the water mist fire extinguishing zone. In the burner ignition procedure, the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel oil circulation circuit so that the oil enters the oil nozzle for injection. In the solenoid valve drive circuit, a freewheeling diode is connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when the power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The potentiometer is used for bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 driven by the motor M is balanced. The potentiometer is also called a potentiometer; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is this type of component, and it is generally considered to be manually adjustable. The potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes as the shaft rotates. In the automatic combustion regulation of the boiler, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 is balanced.

The conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status, and equipment operating parameters. In the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, the maintenance procedure of visually inspecting abnormal phenomena of the equipment, part status and operating parameters belongs to a sub-step of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged". The content of observation includes whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt.

The main engine remote control system is used to carry out remote control of the main diesel engine in the centralized control room or on the bridge. When the operator leaves the local operating position beside the engine, this system must be installed between the operating position and the main engine to achieve remote control. According to differences in implementation methods and components used, the main engine remote control system includes types such as the pneumatic main engine remote control system, electric main engine remote control system, electro-pneumatic main engine remote control system, electro-hydraulic main engine remote control system, microcomputer-controlled main engine remote control system and field bus type main engine remote control system. At the specific product level, the main engine remote control system also includes the NABCO M-800 main engine remote control system, digital electronic governor system and main engine remote control system simulation test device.

These different implementation forms have different emphases in maintenance and testing, but all require maintenance personnel to be familiar with their composition and adjustment parts.

When maintaining the main engine remote control system, there are a series of precautions requiring special attention. For the main engine remote control system, note that the parameters in the system should not be adjusted at will, and components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer should not be opened. The parameters in the system often correspond to setting values, delays and action thresholds; arbitrary changes will shift the original control relationships; components sealed with red paint by the manufacturer have usually been calibrated at the factory, and once opened, it is difficult to restore the original position and the seal is easily invalidated. For the main engine remote control system, note that when opening the pneumatic pipeline, external debris and dust must be prevented from falling in. The bore of pneumatic pipelines is generally small; once debris or dust enters, it may remain on the pipe wall or at throttling points, changing the original flow area, so after opening, the pipe openings should be plugged in time, kept facing upward or fitted with temporary plugs. For the main engine remote control system, note that residual water should be drained daily, the filter checked monthly, and dirty filter screens replaced. Residual water accumulates at the lower part of the air source processing elements; daily draining can prevent moisture from entering valves and pipelines with the airflow; the filter is checked once a month, and dirty filter screens should be replaced in time to ensure the flow capacity and cleanliness of the air source.

For the main engine remote control system, note that before using the keyboard to modify system operating parameters or modifying system operating parameters through the trimming potentiometer on the printed circuit board, it is best to record their original data or original positions. Parameters modified by keyboard are usually stored in digital form, while the trimming potentiometer reflects the setting value as a mechanical rotation angle; both should be recorded before modification for comparison, so that the original values can be restored if the adjustment effect is unsatisfactory. For the main engine remote control system, note that when performing electrical measurements, a test plan should be designed in advance. Before measurement, the measuring point positions, ranges used, probe connections and measurement sequence should be clarified, to avoid affecting the measurement results, or even affecting adjacent circuits, due to improper selection of measuring points or probe slippage.

For the main engine remote control system, note that when simulating the closed state of external relay contacts (short-circuiting two electrical terminals), confirm that there is no voltage between the two terminals, or that although there is voltage, a current-limiting resistor is present and no short circuit will be caused that expands the fault. The short-circuit operation is equivalent to artificially giving a contact closure signal; if voltage exists between the two terminals and there is no current-limiting resistor in the circuit, a short circuit will be formed at the moment of short-circuiting, expanding the fault range from the original local area to the power supply or related boards. For the main engine remote control system, note that when inserting or removing the printed circuit board, the power supply must be turned off. Live insertion and removal will subject the components on the board to the current impact and potential difference at the moment of insertion and removal, and easily damage the slots and pins. For the main engine remote control system, note that the model of the printed circuit board and its original position in the slot should be remembered. There are often multiple boards of similar appearance in the same system; once the model and slot position are confused, the result may range from abnormal function to board damage, so before insertion and removal, each should be checked one by one and marked.

The above precautions address daily maintenance and adjustment, while in terms of preventive maintenance, the main engine remote control system can prevent faults by keeping the starting and control air source pressure normal and clean. Normal and clean air source pressure is the prerequisite for pneumatic and electro-pneumatic circuits to act according to the setting values; low pressure will make the actuators slow or fail to reach position, while high pressure may make the valves act too violently, and moisture and impurities in the air source will likewise change the flow state, so keeping the starting and control air source pressure normal and clean falls within the preventable fault range of the system. The main engine remote control system can prevent faults by internal inspection of the control box, which mainly covers the wiring, terminals, board fixing inside the box, as well as traces of abnormal heating, dust accumulation and dampness. The main engine remote control system can prevent faults by inspection of input and output components, which covers command input components and execution output components, confirming whether their action and signal transmission are normal. The main engine remote control system can prevent faults by the items that must be checked in conjunction with main engine preparation before sailing; these items should be implemented one by one so that the system is in a usable state before departure.

The main engine remote control system can be preventively subjected to periodic effectiveness tests of all system functions; this work verifies each function one by one on the basis of the above checks. These tasks constitute the routine preparations that should be completed before the simulation test.

During operation, the main engine remote control system will exhibit a variety of typical fault symptoms. These include: the microcomputer remote control start must be performed twice each time, with the first attempt failing and the second succeeding; after the main engine starts it cannot accelerate and automatically stops; the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve vent holes leak seriously; the pneumatic logic circuit leaks; moving parts jammed; fuse blowing or power supply fault; poor contact or corrosion of terminal posts or connectors; electrical component fault; incorrect wiring after maintenance;

These measurement and judgment methods are equally applicable to the inspection of the electrical part of the main engine remote control system.

The marine motor includes a bearing; the bearing is the mechanical component of the motor, used to support the rotation of the rotor. A bearing fault will cause the motor to overheat, vibration and abnormal noise; it is also one of the direct causes of motor overheating in the AC electric drive system, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance. When an upper bearing fault causes the motor to overheat, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and the characteristic of the bearing end cover overheating. During inspection, first observe the bearing end cover temperature and running noise, then judge in combination with the lubrication condition whether the lubricant needs to be replenished or replaced. If an abnormality occurs in the part of the main engine remote control system related to the motor, the bearing condition should also be considered together.

The simulation test device of the main engine remote control system provides the conditions for reproducing and troubleshooting the above fault symptoms.

During the test, attention must be paid to the working state of the reversing solenoid valve and orifice 3, the sealing condition of the vent holes of the pressure reducing valve and pressure regulating valve, the tightness of the pneumatic logic circuit, and the flexibility of the moving parts. When measuring voltage, use a multimeter or a voltmeter to provide a basis for judgment.

The simulation test of the main engine high-temperature alarm device needs to be designed around the operating characteristics of the thermocouple. The thermocouple is a temperature sensor with a simple structure and small thermal inertia; it reflects the temperature of the measured object by outputting a thermoelectromotive force, and its electromotive force increases as the temperature rises, so the performance that can be measured includes two items: resistance and electromotive force. Under normal conditions, the resistance value between the two terminal posts of the thermocouple is zero; once the resistance value is measured as infinity, it indicates that the hot end is open and the component itself is damaged.

Based on this characteristic, the simulation test of the main engine high-temperature alarm device can be carried out by the resistance method, voltage method or current method, that is, simulating the temperature signal respectively according to the change in the resistance value, the change in the electromotive force and the change in the current of the thermocouple, to check whether the alarm device can operate correctly.

In the simulation test and the subsequent troubleshooting, observation is the first step of the conventional fault diagnosis method and also the most frequently used link. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, the state of parts, the state of wires and the operating parameters of the equipment; specifically, it is necessary to see whether the parts are stuck or damaged, and whether the wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. Only after observation does the check of the monitoring and indicating device follow, and the fault location is further judged through the instrument readings. This sequence shows that interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device.

Measuring resistance, voltage and current is the main means of obtaining the operating parameters of the equipment during observation. A multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and can also be used to check whether a thermocouple is good or bad; when measuring current, an ammeter or a clamp-on ammeter can also be used, and the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test should be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with the power on.

A sensor is the information acquisition device of the ship's monitoring and control system, and is divided into two major categories: analog quantity and switching quantity. An analog sensor converts a parameter into a continuously changing electrical signal, and is suitable for occasions where the state of the equipment is monitored and the parameter value is also displayed. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed respectively in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, and are used to send out error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; it can be seen that the control platform contains sensors as a constituent relationship.

The simulation test of the main engine remote control system is likewise inseparable from the signals sent out by various sensors. In the test, it is necessary to combine observation, measurement and instrument readings to confirm together the state of the actuating components, including the piston of the fuel cutoff cylinder, and to judge whether they are stuck or damaged, thereby ensuring that the simulation test results can truly reflect the working condition of the system.

The maintenance and upkeep of the ship's gyrocompass first involves grasping the starting conditions of the equipment. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass consists of the master compass, repeater compasses and course recorder, etc., and usually needs to be started 4 to 5 hours before sailing; if the ship is berthed at the dock and the course has not changed, it can be started 2 to 3 hours before sailing. The starting procedure is: after connecting the ship's power supply and the transformer power supply, connect the follow-up switch 20 minutes later.

Inside the small door on the left side of the master compass there is a switchboard and a follow-up switch; before use, it is necessary to calibrate and confirm that the courses of all repeater compasses are consistent with that of the master compass.

For the pre-start check and preparation of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass, it is necessary to confirm that the ship's power switch and the power switch on the transformer box are placed in the "OFF" position, to check whether the follow-up switch on the switchboard inside the small door on the left side of the master compass is in the "OFF" position, to calibrate and confirm that the courses of all repeater compasses should be consistent with the course of the master compass, to check that the course of the course recorder is consistent with that of the master compass and that the time mark on the recording paper is consistent with ship time, and also to check that the instruments of the master compass are clean and dry, that the mechanical transmission is flexible, and that the cable joints are firm and normal. These checks cover the confirmation of the power supply, the state of the master compass, the follow-up switch and the course consistency of the repeater compasses, and are the concrete embodiment of the pre-start check and preparation of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass as applicable to this type of compass.

The starting process of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass is applicable to the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass and includes the steps of connecting the ship's power switch, connecting the power switch on the transformer box, and connecting the follow-up switch. The first step is to turn the ship's power switch and the power switch on the transformer box to the ON position; 20 minutes after the main power supply is connected, turn the follow-up switch from position 0 to position 1. Before starting, it must be checked that the ship's power switch and the transformer box switch are in the OFF position, and before starting it must be confirmed that the follow-up switch on the switchboard on the left side of the master compass is in the OFF position.

The pre-startup inspection and preparation of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass is the preliminary step of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass startup process, and the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass startup process is in turn the preliminary step of the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass daily use inspection.

As a ship navigation device, the gyrocompass is used to provide heading information and control the antenna azimuth axis (AZ axis) to compensate for heading changes; one of its functions is to provide the control signal for the AZ axis, causing the antenna to rotate in the opposite direction by the same angle as the heading changes, i.e., the AZ axis uses the gyrocompass. When starting the Sperry MK37, the changeover switch must be turned to the "rotate" position, and the heading is adjusted to deviate 30° from the true heading. After starting the Arma-Brown 10, it is necessary to wait 5 min for the gyro motor to reach rated speed, after which the follow-up system automatically comes into operation.

After the Anschutz 22 is switched on the power supply for about 3 h, the pointing accuracy is ≤2°, and after 5 h the static accuracy is less than 0.1×1/cosφ. The Anschutz 22 quick-settling function is available only when the ship's position has not changed between the previous shutdown and the current startup. The supporting liquid of the Anschutz 22 should be replaced every 18 months as specified, with a filling volume of 840 cm³.

When using the recording paper in the gyrocompass heading recorder, it is necessary to check whether it is sufficient and whether the time mark is consistent with ship time. The reminder mark for the remaining length of the recording paper is <1 m; when the remaining length of the recording paper is less than 1 m, there will be an obvious mark reminding the user that it is about to run out. The recording paper belongs to the weather facsimile receiver and is used as the medium for marine weather facsimile receivers and refrigerated container temperature recorders, recording weather charts or temperature curves; when a paper jam occurs, the equipment power supply should be switched off and the recording paper reinstalled.

The observation content includes abnormal phenomena, part condition, wire condition, and equipment operating parameters, specifically involving whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, cracked, abraded, or burnt. Observation is a sub-step of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, "carrying out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged."

The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass daily use inspection applies to the Anschutz 4 gyrocompass and includes checking the supporting liquid level height, the gyrosphere height, and the composition and function of the supporting liquid. The distance from the supporting liquid level to the top of the filling hole should be maintained at 4–5 cm, which can be measured with a small wooden stick. If the liquid level is insufficient, the top electrode is exposed and cannot conduct, so the liquid quantity must be checked frequently to maintain the conductive path of the follow-up sphere. Under normal conditions, the red engraved line at the equator of the gyrosphere is 2 mm above the reference horizontal line, with an allowable deviation of ±1 mm. An abnormal gyrosphere height will cause friction with the follow-up sphere, resulting in random error. To check the gyrosphere height, the compass must be stable, the liquid temperature normal, and the unit level, and observation is made through the small door at the rear.

The supporting liquid consists of 10 L distilled water, 1 L glycerin (specific gravity 1.23), and 10 g benzoic acid. Glycerin is used to increase the specific gravity of the liquid, and benzoic acid is used for conduction. The distance from the liquid level to the top of the filling hole should be maintained at 4–5 cm. Adding 20 mL of glycerin can raise the liquid level by 1 mm, and adding 125 mL of distilled water can lower it by 1 mm. The Anschutz 22 gyrocompass specifies that the supporting liquid be replaced every 18 months, and during replacement 840 cm³ of new liquid is added through the supporting liquid screw hole. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass contains supporting liquid, and the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass also contains supporting liquid.

The gyrosphere is the core component of the gyrocompass; it is supported by the follow-up sphere, suspended by the supporting liquid, and forms a conductive path with the follow-up sphere.

Insufficient liquid level causes the top electrode to be exposed and unable to conduct; the level must be kept 4–5 cm from the top of the filling hole. Abnormal height will cause friction with the follow-up sphere and produce indeterminate errors; normally the equatorial red graduation line is 2 mm ± 1 mm higher. In the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass, the liquid friction between it and the follow-up sphere is used to push the follow-up sphere to reduce the initial azimuth. During maintenance it must be taken out from the lower hemisphere, and its outer surface and conductive electrode parts cleaned with a clean cotton cloth and distilled water.

The follow-up sphere is used to support and control the movement of the gyrosphere, supporting the gyrosphere through the internal supporting liquid and forming the follow-up conductive path of the gyrosphere. By means of the friction of the liquid between it and the gyrosphere, it pushes the gyrosphere to reduce the initial azimuth so as to stabilize quickly. The follow-up sphere consists of upper and lower hemispheres connected by six screws, and is provided internally with a distilled water reservoir and a vent screw.

A vent screw is provided at the top center, and a distilled water filling hole and a supporting liquid filling hole are provided on the side. It is provided with four removal locking screws, which must be turned 90° and loosened in two steps before it can be taken out.

The function of the changeover switch is to select the measurement object and select the range; it is a device used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts. On the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands. A changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. A multimeter contains a changeover switch. The load current I flowing through the primary side is converted into a secondary current which is connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements. The secondary side must never be open-circuited; the external ammeter terminals must have a short-circuit connecting piece, which may be removed only after the wiring has been checked.

The Sperry MK37 gyrocompass includes the electronic control box, transmitter box, compensator and other components. Normal starting of the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass applies to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass; before starting, confirm that all switches on the transmitter box and the changeover switch on the electronic control box are in the "OFF" position. The equipment power supply is started by switching on the power switch located on the electronic control box. Turn the changeover switch to the "SLEW" position, and adjust the heading deviation by 30° according to the plus or minus of the altitude angle indicator. If the altitude angle indication is (+), use the slewing switch to reduce the heading by 30° from the true heading; if it is (-), increase it by 30°. After completing the preset, turn the changeover switch to the "START" position. After starting, wait 10 minutes to ensure that the gyro motor speed reaches the rated value.

Operation of this gyrocompass involves the altitude angle indicator on the electronic control box, which is used to determine the adjustment direction. Shutdown of the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass applies to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass: place the changeover switch on the electronic control box in the "OFF" position, place the power switch on the electronic control box in the "OFF" position, and place all switches on the transmitter box in the "OFF" position. Radar range error correction applies to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass, and radar bearing error correction also applies to the Sperry MK37 gyrocompass.

The Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass includes the power supply box, main gyrocompass control panel, repeaters and other components. After switching on the power supply box switch, all repeaters also enter the working state.

Turn the rotation rate knob clockwise to increase the gyrocompass heading reading, and counterclockwise to decrease it. The speed error correction knob should be set to the position corresponding to the ship's speed, and set to zero when the ship is stationary. The latitude error correction knob should be set to the latitude at which the ship is sailing, with an allowable error not exceeding 5°. Daily inspection requires confirming that the latitude knob on the compensator is at the latitude value of the ship's location. During startup, press the rotation button and turn the rate knob so that the master gyrocompass azimuth dial indicates close to the true heading. Turn the rotation rate knob clockwise to increase the gyrocompass reading, and counterclockwise to decrease it; upon reaching the true heading, return the knob to the center and then release it. Before startup, check that the ship's power supply is normal; after switching on the power supply, confirm that the power indicator lamp on the master gyrocompass control panel is lit. Startup of the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass is a prerequisite step for shutdown of the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass; shutdown of the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass applies to the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass and includes steps such as cutting off the power supply box switch, cutting off the power failure alarm switch, and cutting off the ship's power supply switch.

Regarding power failure, when starting the Arma-Brown 10 gyrocompass, the power failure alarm switch must be switched on before subsequent operations can be carried out.

A power failure causes the RUN lamp to go out; for a power failure, check the power supply; for no-load power supply, switch on the power supply. Before switching on the power supply, the input and output sections must be tested for short circuit or earthing faults, and power may be applied only after confirming there are no problems. The PLC starts its self-diagnosis process as soon as the power supply is switched on; if an internal CPU error occurs, the "CPU Error" lamp on the panel indicates an abnormality. Startup of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass applies to the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass; after closing the ship's power supply switch, the entire set of equipment automatically completes the startup process. The panel digital display can show heading, operating status and alarm information. After switching on the power supply for 5 h, it becomes fully stable and points north, with a static accuracy of less than 0.1×1/cosφ and a dynamic accuracy specification of less than
0.4×1/cosφ.

An optional quick-settling function is supported to shorten the gyrocompass settling time, using the heading value retained from the previous shutdown to calculate the initial azimuth. It is only necessary to close the ship's power supply switch, and the entire gyrocompass equipment will automatically complete the whole startup process. The content of the digital display on the master gyrocompass panel must be observed to judge whether operation is normal. The gyrocompass is usually not switched off while in port; after shutdown under special circumstances, it needs to be restarted. For the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass quick-settling function, and these precautions also require attention for the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass.

The display is used to display radar images; the Anschutz gyrocompass digital display shows heading, operating status and heating-stage temperature codes. The radar equipment includes the display, and the display belongs to the radar equipment. The display includes cleaning of the display air filter and cleaning of the display surface. The radar display installation precautions require attention to the display, and radar installation applies to the display. The display should be installed in the wheelhouse in a location free from strong electromagnetic radiation, away from heat sources and dry, fixed with a hardwood base. The main radar display is oriented so that the observer faces the bow, and is installed on the starboard side of the bridge.

The supporting liquid of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass serves the dual function of supporting the gyrosphere and forming the conductive path between the gyrosphere and the follow-up sphere, and its composition is prepared from distilled water, glycerin and benzoic acid. An abnormal height of the gyrosphere will cause it to rub against the follow-up sphere, thereby causing erratic errors; under normal conditions, the red equatorial scribed line of the gyrosphere should be 2 mm above the horizontal line of the transparent glass block, with an allowable deviation of ±1 mm. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass also contains the gyrosphere as a core component. When replacing the supporting liquid of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass, the gyrosphere, follow-up sphere and supporting liquid must be used together in the operation.

The startup process of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass is characterized by automation; the operation of startup of the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass applies to the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass itself.

After switching on the power supply for about 3h, the pointing accuracy is ≤2°; after 5h, the static accuracy is less than 0.1×1/cosφ, and the dynamic accuracy index is less than 0.4×1/cosφ. In the Anschutz 22 gyrocompass, the operating unit can control the fast settling function to shorten the startup time; adjust the display brightness and contrast by pressing the Dim Up/Down and Contr. Up/Down keys; use the Up/Down keys to change the latitude value and press the Set key to confirm, and the system calculates the speed error accordingly. This function can only be used when the ship's position has not changed between the previous shutdown and the current startup, because the driving capability of the liquid friction is limited. After startup, if it can be activated, the fast settling button flashes continuously for 2 minutes; press the flashing button and it lights up to activate the function; otherwise start according to the normal procedure. If it is not activated within 3 minutes, start according to the normal procedure, and the settling time is about 3 hours.

As equipment that provides the AZ-axis control signal, the gyrocompass has various models and startup methods in ship navigation. The operation of switching on the power supply is also a key step in the maintenance and commissioning of PLC and electrical control systems, referring to the process of connecting the power supply to perform functional testing or self-diagnosis after confirming that there is no short circuit or earthing fault. The no-load power supply corresponds to the operation step of switching on the power supply.

In the testing and maintenance of marine electrical equipment, both the multimeter and marine electrical equipment use diodes. A diode has unidirectional conductivity and is commonly denoted by VD in circuits; it is used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc. Its main characteristic is unidirectional conductivity: under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite. According to their function, they can be divided into rectifier diodes (such as 1N4004), isolation diodes (such as 1N4148), Schottky diodes (such as BAT85), etc. Diodes include types such as light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. A light-emitting diode has unidirectional conductivity and can emit red, green, yellow and other colored light; its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit working status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display. Its external dimensions include diameters of 3mm and 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle; the operating current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model, and in actual use a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage; the conduction voltage is above 1.7V. For light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes. The diode testing procedure is suitable for judging the performance of devices such as diodes.

Radar equipment includes a display, and the display belongs to radar equipment. The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of ship radar and monitoring systems, used to present images, data and alarm information.

The control platform includes sensors. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls. A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching sensors. Analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals, and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed.

The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass, which belongs to the same series as the Anschutz 22, requires checking before startup whether the follow-up switch on the switchboard inside the small door on the left side of the master compass is set to the "cut off" position. The Anschutz 4 gyrocompass also includes components such as the supporting liquid and the gyrosphere. As ship navigation equipment, one of the functions of the gyrocompass is to provide the AZ-axis control signal; the AZ axis uses the heading information output by the gyrocompass to make the satellite communication antenna rotate in the reverse direction by the same angle as the heading changes, so as to compensate for course changes.

During maintenance, it is also necessary to check the sealing ring between the upper and lower hemispheres to ensure good sealing performance. Marine electrical equipment generally uses printed circuit boards. A printed circuit board consists of an insulating base plate and conductive copper traces; the base material is often called the base plate, most commonly phenolic resin board (yellow insulation) and epoxy glass (glass fiber), and the circuit part is made of conductive copper laid on the base plate, with the required pattern obtained by etching. For printed circuit boards, attention must be paid to the soldering requirements for electronic components, and the welding quality directly affects the working reliability of the circuit board. The circuit board repair procedure is suitable for printed circuit boards. When a circuit board fault occurs on a printed circuit board, the fault falls within the scope of printed circuit boards. When the "COM" screw is loose, tighten it accordingly to restore the normal connection of the circuit.

Radar equipment is a ship navigation safety detection system, composed of the antenna, transceiver, display and other components, in which the antenna undertakes the radiation and reception of targets, the transceiver is responsible for the transmission and reception of signals, and the display is used to present radar images. The complete set of equipment also includes the waveguide, magnetron and air filter and other components, the waveguide is used to transmit radar microwave signals, the magnetron is a device inside the transceiver, and the air filter serves the heat dissipation and ventilation of each unit. As for maintenance and correction work, radar installation, radar acceptance, radar periodic maintenance and servicing, radar range error correction and radar bearing error correction are all applicable to radar equipment; the antenna, transceiver, display and waveguide all belong to radar equipment, and the magnetron and air filter are also included among the components of radar equipment. Among the maintenance items included in radar equipment, one is power supply air filter cleaning, that is, cleaning the air filter of the power supply unit.
