That is to say, damage to the generator prime mover is one of the common causes in the equipment itself that cause ship power system faults, and both failure of the prime mover governor and overheating of the cylinder block are specific manifestations of damage to the generator prime mover; insulation damage of the cable junction box is one of the common equipment-itself faults that cause ship power system faults.

When an excitation system fault causes underexcitation or loss of excitation, reactive circulating current is generated between units operating in parallel, which may cause tripping. Common faults caused by improper operation include: improper closing operation; unbalanced generator load control; improper operation caused by erroneous observation. Improper paralleling operation may cause the generator main switch overcurrent protection to operate and trip or the reverse power protection to operate and trip; during paralleling operation, improper grasp of the closing moment or reversing the adjustment direction of load sharing may cause the generator reverse power protection to trip; during operation, damaging the insulation protective layer or metal parts falling onto wire ends may cause short circuit faults of the electrical lines. Accidental accidents refer to various accidents that occur unexpectedly, such as sudden short circuit and open circuit; common forms of accidental accidents include sudden short circuit and open circuit;

In the ship power system, short circuit is classified as severe overload; the heat and electrodynamic force generated by short circuit current are the main causes of generator damage; short circuit refers to two points in a circuit being connected artificially or accidentally through an extremely small impedance. Maladjustment of synchronous generator operating parameters refers to the generator operating parameters exceeding the allowable values, which may damage the generator set or the power-consuming equipment, and protective measures need to be taken to avoid accidents; its specific manifestations include overcurrent, overload, short circuit, reverse power, undervoltage, overvoltage, low frequency and high frequency. In the ship power system, a relatively small overcurrent is called overload, and only a relatively large overcurrent such as short circuit is called overcurrent; 1.1 times rated current is called small overload, 1.5 times rated current is called relatively large overload, and short circuit is called severe overload. The heat generated by long-time overcurrent operation will age the insulation; the current range allowed for generator operation is mainly determined by the current flowing through the stator (armature) winding.

The influence of harsh environmental conditions refers to various faults caused by the reduction of the electrical insulation capability of equipment due to harsh environmental conditions. It mainly leads to two types of problems: one-phase earthing fault of the power system and low insulation resistance fault of the power system. The low insulation resistance fault of the 400V system mostly occurs in electrical equipment on open decks or inside the main switchboard. The low insulation resistance fault of the 220V system often occurs in the lighting of each deck, galley electrical equipment or deck lighting system. The one-phase earthing fault is manifested as the insulation indicator lamp of one phase going out and the other two phases being abnormally bright. If the low insulation resistance fault is not handled in time, a short circuit current may be formed, causing the switch trip unit to operate or trip. Faults of the equipment itself, improper operation, accidents and maladjustment of operating parameters of the synchronous generator may all lead to one-phase earthing fault of the power system.

AC generators operating in parallel in the ship's power station should be provided with reverse power protection that operates with a delay of 3 to 10 s. For a generator driven by a diesel engine prime mover, the reverse power protection setting value is 8% to 15% of the rated power; for a generator driven by a turbine prime mover, the reverse power protection setting value is 2% to 8% of the rated power. Undervoltage protection is mainly for the protection of generators operating in parallel, and also protects users such as asynchronous motors.

Precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the relevant requirements of the ship's power station.

Regarding the instruments and electrical quantities used for maintenance and testing, the measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter; the measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. The multimeter is used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand the equipment status; to measure current, an ammeter must be used, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if there is capacitance in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with the power on.

In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating function. Local short circuit or phase failure of the winding is one of the main fault causes of overcurrent and overheating of AC motors.

The ship's power station consists of the main switchboard and the ship's power network. The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the power station, undertaking tasks such as circuit making and breaking, protection and alarm, parameter detection and power regulation, and is capable of regulating the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel. The ship's power network usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system, and single-phase earthing at any point is an abnormal state; if another phase is earthed, a short circuit will be formed. Therefore, a network insulation detection device is installed on the lighting distribution panel of the main switchboard to monitor the insulation condition of the network.

During the operation of the power station, voltage and current are two basic electrical quantities that need to be measured frequently.

The circuit breaker may have the fault that the contact cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated manually, that is, the contact cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated manually. At this time, there is an obstruction in the manual closing circuit itself. During inspection, first confirm whether the operating mechanism is in place and whether the trip unit is in the reset state, and then check whether the contact and transmission components are jammed. The circuit breaker may also have the fault that the contact cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, that is, the contact cannot close when the circuit breaker is operated electrically. At this time, the electric closing circuit fails to operate normally. During inspection, start with the operating power supply, closing coil and its control circuit, and confirm level by level whether the signal is delivered. The circuit breaker may also have the problem that the contact of one phase cannot close, indicating that the three-phase contacts do not operate consistently, and the cause must be found separately for the contact of that phase and its transmission link.

If the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, it indicates that the shunt trip circuit fails to effectively drive the tripping mechanism; the coil of the shunt trip unit and its control circuit should be checked. If the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open, it indicates that the undervoltage tripping link has lost its proper breaking capability; the undervoltage trip unit and its setting state should be checked. If the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, it indicates that the circuit breaker trips under the impact of the motor starting current; this should be checked against the setting value of the overcurrent trip unit. If the circuit breaker opens automatically about 1 h after closing, it indicates that the opening occurs after a period of operation; the cause should be found in combination with the temperature rise and the state of the trip unit. If the undervoltage trip unit produces noise, it indicates that its electromagnetic system is not working properly; its core and coil should be checked. If the temperature rise of the circuit breaker is too high, it indicates that there is abnormal heating in the conductive circuit or the connection parts; the contact condition of the contacts and the tightness of the connections should be checked. If the auxiliary switch fails, it will affect the correct operation of the control and signal indication circuit; the contacts and transmission of the auxiliary switch should be checked.

If the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctions and causes the circuit breaker to open, it indicates that the trip unit issues a tripping command before the setting condition is reached; its detection and setting links should be checked.

The current relay is an electrical device used for control or protection in the ship's power system, and it belongs to the electromagnetic relay classified by the nature of the input signal; the coil is energized with electricity, and its structure is basically similar to that of the contactor. In the AC three-speed electric windlass, it picks up when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%. After the generator is connected in parallel and trips, the overcurrent relay needs to be reset to restore the closing of the main switch. The reverse power relay is used to detect and protect against reverse power and is one of the control and protection devices commonly used on the ship's main switchboard; it is used to detect the reverse power of the AC generator and trigger the protection action. The setting value for the diesel engine prime mover is 8% to 15% of the rated power, with an operating delay of 3 to 10 s. When improper operation of parallel connection causes the reverse power relay to operate and trip, some panels and cabinets need to be reset manually.

Motor overload refers to the fault state in which the motor's operating current or power exceeds the rated value. When the output power or current of the generator exceeds its rated value, it is defined as overload. In DC motors, it will cause difficult commutation and excessive sparking. When the DC motor is overloaded, the current per unit area of the brush is large, causing difficult commutation and excessive sparking under brush; in the generator, it triggers overload protection. The expansion of a systematic fault may cause abnormal frequency and voltage of the power grid, and then cause generator overload. Improper operation can also cause a single-phase earthing fault in the power system.

The main generator that undertakes the power generation task in the ship's power station is currently mainly divided into two forms: the brushed synchronous generator and the brushless synchronous generator. Both types of generators include components such as the generator prime mover, generator stator winding, excitation system, generator bearing and generator shaft, and their daily maintenance and upkeep requirements are basically the same.

As for the excitation system, it is the voltage regulation system that provides excitation current for the generator. Common forms include uncontrollable phase compounding, controllable phase compounding, thyristor excitation and brushless excitation voltage regulation systems. The maintenance cycle of the excitation system is once every half a year, and the insulation resistance value is required to be not less than 1 MΩ. During maintenance, it is necessary to check whether the wiring of each terminal post of the excitation system is good; if a loose wire end is found, it must be tightened; and check the gap size of the linear reactor and whether there is abnormal noise. If the gap is not appropriate, it should be adjusted to the required value; if there is abnormal noise, the cause should be identified and eliminated; at the same time, check whether the insulation between phases and between phase and earth of the excitation system is good.

The uncontrollable phase compounding voltage regulation system is one of the common forms of excitation voltage regulation systems for ship synchronous generators, and its structural feature is that the number of components is small and the circuit connection is simple. When troubleshooting this system, it is necessary to find the fault point against the schematic diagram according to its working process and phenomena. Common faults include failure to build up voltage at rated speed or abnormal terminal voltage; when voltage build-up fails, it is necessary to check the residual magnetism voltage and the state of the phase-shifting reactor and the resonant capacitor.

The controllable phase-compounding voltage regulation system is likewise one of the four main forms of marine synchronous generator excitation voltage regulation systems, and in classification it is listed in parallel with the uncontrollable phase-compounding voltage regulation system and the thyristor excitation voltage regulation system. The thyristor excitation voltage regulation system is also one of these four main forms; during fault troubleshooting, the thyristor main circuit is checked first, followed by the trigger circuit, and common faults include failure to build up voltage at rated speed and sudden loss of power during operation; if voltage still cannot be built up after flashing, the cause may be breakdown of the thyristor or rectifier diode in the flashing circuit, while a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases is one of the typical fault symptoms of this system. The brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system is likewise among these four main forms, listed in parallel with the uncontrollable phase-compounding, controllable phase-compounding and thyristor excitation voltage regulation systems, and is applicable to the brushless synchronous generator forms currently used on ships.

The interior of a brushless synchronous generator contains a coaxially rotating main generator excitation winding, exciter armature winding and rotating rectifier device; the static excitation system supplies power to the exciter stator and, after rotating rectification, provides DC current to the main generator excitation winding.

Its common faults include breakdown or open circuit of the rotating commutator, and short circuit or open circuit of the rotating-armature-type excitation winding; during maintenance, special attention must be paid to the fact that centrifugal force can easily cause the rotating rectifier armature to loosen and open-circuit. In a brushless system, breakdown of the rotating rectifier module will cause the voltage to drop, and when one diode is damaged the voltage can drop to above 200V. In a thyristor system, if a rectifier element is open-circuited or the trigger half-wave fails, the terminal voltage will drop greatly when the load increases. Damage to components of the static excitation system will cause insufficient DC current, and the exciter stator winding current must be detected to determine the fault. When an excitation system fault causes underexcitation or loss of excitation, reactive circulating current is produced between units operating in parallel, which may cause tripping; in parallel operation, brushless synchronous generators usually employ a current stabilizing device to achieve even distribution of reactive power.

Common fault types of brushed synchronous generators include stator winding open circuit, phase-to-phase short circuit, turn-to-turn short circuit, as well as poor brush contact and brush wear. Poor brush contact is a common fault type of brushed motors and is often mentioned in parallel with faults such as stator winding open circuit and rotor excitation winding short circuit; it is distinct from the rotating commutator breakdown or rotating-armature-type winding faults of brushless synchronous generators. For brushed motors, excessive brush wear is also one of the common faults, listed in parallel with stator winding open circuit and short circuit. The commutator is the rotating sliding contact component used for leading current in and out in DC motors and wound-rotor motors, and is composed of commutator segments; graphite brushes are soft in texture and easily damage the commutator, and are suitable for motors with general commutation conditions and uniform load. When disassembling a DC motor, the winding ends, commutator or slip rings should be protected from being damaged by impact. When excessive sparking under brush occurs, it is necessary to check the contact between the brush and the commutator, check the brush holder, check the armature vibration, check the commutator segments and check the brush position.

Regarding the maintenance and servicing of generator bearings, in oil-ring-lubricated sliding bearings the oil quantity of the bearing should be kept constant, and oil is generally not added during operation; the oil quantity should be below the specified liquid level, and the bearing should not throw oil, so as to avoid splashing onto the winding. Lubricating oil samples must be taken periodically for inspection, and if the oil color darkens, becomes turbid, or contains water or dirt, it should be replaced; when the bearing heats up, new oil should be replaced in all cases, generally once every 250~400 working hours, but at least once every six months. Fault causes of generator bearing overheating include severe bearing wear; the lubricating oil quantity of the generator bearing must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space; improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover will cause generator bearing overheating; poor assembly of the generator set is also one of the fault causes of generator bearing overheating; bending of the generator shaft will cause generator bearing overheating; when the stator and rotor rub against each other, it is necessary to check whether the motor bearing is loose. A marine motor contains components such as the bearing, winding, commutator and brush, among which the bearing is the mechanical component of the motor used to support rotation of the rotor, and its fault will cause motor overheating, vibration and abnormal noise; bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems and belongs to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance; when an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud non-uniform noise and the feature of bearing end cover overheating.

Daily maintenance and servicing requirements for the generator: to ensure normal operation of the generator, water, oil and dirt must not accumulate near it, and corrosive gases must not be present, so as to avoid damaging the generator winding insulation; while preventing moisture and dust, care must be taken not to affect the normal ventilation and cooling of the generator, dust and dirt in the ventilation ducts must be cleaned frequently to keep them unobstructed, and the temperature of the cooling air must not be too low, so as to avoid condensation water forming on the winding and other conductive components. These requirements apply to both brushed synchronous generators and brushless synchronous generators.

In terms of testing and repair means, the multimeter can be used to measure resistance, voltage, current as well as the polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode of the thyristor, while the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current. When measuring the resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if a capacitor is present in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with the power on.

The thyristor, also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, has its polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode all detectable by means of a multimeter. Printed circuit boards are widely used in marine electrical equipment; they consist of an insulating base material and conductive foil traces, the base material is often called the substrate, with phenolic resin board and epoxy glass being the most commonly used, and the trace portion is made of conductive copper laid on the substrate and etched to obtain the required pattern. During maintenance, the contact of plug-in printed circuit boards must be checked for good condition, discrete components must be checked for solder joints and copper film corrosion, printed circuit boards require attention to the soldering requirements for electronic components, the circuit board repair procedure applies to printed circuit boards, printed circuit boards are subject to circuit board faults, and circuit board faults fall within the scope of printed circuit boards. Electrical connections that are loose, oxidized or contaminated with foreign matter will cause the contact resistance to increase, i.e. poor contact; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact and increase the contact resistance; poor contact can cause faults such as local overheating, phase failure and phase-to-phase short circuit, therefore the terminal screws of the electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact, and failure to tighten the external terminal screws of the thermal relay will cause the main circuit to be disconnected.

The rectifier is used to convert alternating current into direct current; the electrical graphical symbol of the full-wave bridge rectifier is UR; the rotating rectifier of the brushless synchronous generator is prone to the armature coming loose and opening due to centrifugal force, rectifier breakdown is one of the fault causes of a large voltage drop when the generator load increases, an open phase in the phase-shifting reactor, rectifier or phase-compounding transformer will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value, and a residual magnetism voltage of the generator opposite in polarity to the rectifier output voltage will prevent the voltage from building up normally; in the controllable phase-compounding constant-voltage device, a rectifier fault is one of the sub-causes of phase-compounding device faults, and if the UR rectifier has an open diode, it will cause a voltage deviation of |U0-Ufe| greater than ΔU1. In the generator no-load voltage high fault, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to lose its main regulating action.

To troubleshoot such systems, it is necessary, based on their working process, to compare the observed phenomena with the schematic diagram and locate the fault position point by point. Common faults include failure to build up voltage at rated speed, terminal voltage deviating from the rated value, sudden failure to generate during operation, a large voltage drop when the load increases, and generator overheating; generator bearing overheating is also counted among the common faults of such systems.

Failure of the generator voltage to build up normally means that the voltage still cannot be built up when the speed has reached the rated value. This phenomenon is relatively common in uncontrolled phase-compounding voltage regulation systems.

Preliminary troubleshooting should first check whether there is residual magnetism voltage; if there is none, magnetize; if residual magnetism exists but the voltage still does not build up, the state of the voltage regulator and the phase-shifting reactor must be checked. There are many causes of this fault: no residual magnetism or insufficient residual magnetism will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; an open excitation winding will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; rusted and blackened non-conductive generator slip rings will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; brushes stuck in the brush holders or broken brush pigtails will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; a linear reactor with no air gap or too small an air gap will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; a broken-down or open rectifier element of the voltage regulator will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; incorrect wiring will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; a broken connection between the reactor, the resonant capacitor and the phase-compounding transformer will cause failure of the generator voltage to build up normally; in addition, an open phase-shifting reactor will likewise prevent the generator from building up voltage, and a short-circuited or broken-down resonant capacitor is also a possible fault cause.

The generator voltage is lower than the rated value, manifesting as the terminal voltage being lower than the rated voltage. Too small an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; too small a setting resistor will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; too low a speed will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; an open circuit in the generator excitation winding will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; a change in the tap of the reactor or the phase-compounding transformer will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; an error in the voltmeter will cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value; among the various fault causes of voltage being lower than the rated value, this item is listed as the 7th item, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to calibrate the voltmeter. For the low voltage caused by too small a setting resistor, the setting resistor needs to be adjusted. Too large an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor is one of the causes, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to reduce the air gap as required, the object of operation being the air gap structure of the phase-shifting reactor; this measure is listed as the first item among the various troubleshooting methods for generator voltage being higher than the rated value. The sliding contact of the setting resistor being burnt, rusted, in poor contact, or the resistor being burnt out is one of the main causes, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and repair or replace the resistor, that is, to check and repair or replace the damaged resistor element. A change in the tap of the reactor or the phase-compounding transformer will also cause the voltage to be higher, and readjustment as required is needed, the specific operation being to readjust the changed taps of the reactor and the phase-compounding transformer. An error in the voltmeter will likewise cause the reading to be higher, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to calibrate the voltmeter; this item is listed as the fourth item among the various troubleshooting measures.

The generator suddenly failing to generate power during operation is also one of the common faults of the uncontrolled phase-compounding voltage regulation system. If it still cannot generate power after magnetization, it indicates that the excitation coil of the generator itself has an open-circuit fault; such an open-circuit excitation coil should be handled by the method for the case where the speed is rated but no voltage can be established; if it can generate power after magnetization, it may be that the thyristor of the main circuit has broken down or the trigger circuit has stopped working, and the rectifier main circuit and the power supply output of the trigger circuit need to be checked. The causes of this fault include: breakdown of the rectifier will cause the generator to suddenly fail to generate power during operation; no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit will cause the generator to suddenly fail to generate power during operation; loosening of the reactor core, resulting in a reduced air gap, will cause the generator to suddenly fail to generate power during operation; a short circuit in the coil of the reactor or the phase-compounding transformer will cause the generator to suddenly fail to generate power during operation; breakdown of the resonant capacitor will cause the generator to suddenly fail to generate power during operation. When one phase of the phase-shifting reactor, rectifier or phase-compounding transformer is open, the generator will also suddenly fail to generate power during operation.

When the load increases, the generator voltage drops greatly, characterized in that when the generator load increases, the terminal voltage drops greatly. An open circuit in the rectifier will cause the generator voltage to drop greatly when the load increases; inconsistency in the polarity of the current winding and the voltage winding of the phase-compounding transformer will also cause the generator voltage to drop greatly when the load increases.

To deal with this fault, the fault point needs to be found by comparing with the working principle diagram according to the specific phenomenon, and during maintenance, fault analysis and diagnosis need to be carried out in combination with the working process.

Generator overheating is one of the common faults of the uncontrolled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, and its fault causes and troubleshooting methods need to be analyzed item by item in combination with the specific working process of this system. Generator bearing overheating manifests as an abnormal rise in bearing temperature and is likewise a common fault of this system. If the overheating is caused by too much lubricating oil, the oil quantity must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space; too little or deteriorated lubricating oil can also cause bearing overheating. When it is caused by severe bearing wear, the bearing needs to be replaced; when it is caused by improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover, it needs to be reinstalled; when it is caused by poor assembly of the generator set, it needs to be realigned and installed; when it is caused by bending of the generator shaft, the shaft needs to be straightened;

Mutual friction between the stator and rotor, such as bearing looseness, may also cause bearing overheating, and the bearing, shaft and rotor core need to be checked. From the classification of causes, a bearing fault will cause bearing overheating, a lubrication fault will cause bearing overheating, and an installation fault will cause bearing overheating; therefore, bearing overheating corresponds to the three tasks of checking the bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition, and checking the installation condition; both checking the bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition require the use of the bearing, and the marine motor contains the bearing. If the noise disappears during no-load operation, it indicates poor installation of the coupling; if the noise still exists and is accompanied by vibration, it points to a fault of the shaft or the bearing itself.

When diagnosing the above faults, maintenance personnel need to be familiar with the structure, working principle, functions and locations of the components (assemblies) of the electrical equipment; they must be very familiar with the circuits, working principles and positions of the components of the whole ship's electrical equipment, and master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, so as to understand the phenomenon and make a preliminary diagnosis through these five approaches.

A multimeter or voltmeter can be used to measure voltage values, and a multimeter is also used to measure resistance and capacitance. A capacitor is composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in between; its characteristic is that it blocks direct current and passes alternating current. In circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25. Its hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC). Its measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance, and the polarity of electrolytic capacitors. The measurable property of a resistor is its resistance value, and the measuring tool is a multimeter; poor contact is one of the fault causes leading to equipment failure, referring to a fault state in which the contact resistance at an electrical connection increases due to looseness, oxidation, or foreign matter. Loose fastening screws and terminal posts will cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance, and thereby causing local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults.

As the heart of the ship's power system, the reliability and survivability of the ship's power station are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks. Its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur.

When the load increases, a large drop in generator voltage is a relatively common type of abnormality in the operation of the ship's power station. There is more than one cause of this phenomenon, among which no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit is a typical case. The so-called no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit means that no current passes through the circuit in which the excitation winding is located; at this time the excitation magnetic field of the generator cannot be established or maintained, and once the load increases, the terminal voltage drops significantly accordingly. For this fault cause, the troubleshooting method is to check whether the wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding is loose or broken, that is, to lock the inspection object onto this section of wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding, and confirm point by point whether its connection is reliable and whether the conductor is intact. This maintenance procedure corresponds to no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit in the troubleshooting table, and is one of the troubleshooting methods for the fault of a large drop in generator voltage caused by increased load.

Alongside the above causes, there is also rectifier breakdown. The rectifier is responsible for converting alternating current into direct current; once its internal components break down, the supply of excitation current loses its normal path, and the generator voltage will likewise drop significantly when the load increases. For rectifier breakdown, the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and replace the rectifier components that have broken down; the core of the operation is to find the rectifier components that have broken down and replace them. This step is used to troubleshoot the fault of a large drop in generator voltage caused by rectifier breakdown; in the troubleshooting table, this method corresponds to the fault cause rectifier breakdown. The electrical graphical symbol for a full-wave bridge rectifier is UR.

Loosening of the reactor core, resulting in a reduced air gap, is another fault cause that can cause a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases.

Its mechanism is that the reactor core becomes loose, causing the magnetic circuit air gap to decrease, and the operating state of the magnetic circuit changes accordingly. When dealing with this fault, the air gap should be adjusted to the required value and the core tightened, that is, after adjusting the air gap the action of tightening the core must be performed. This step is used to solve the fault in which the reactor core is loose and the air gap is reduced, and is one of the troubleshooting methods for the fault of a large drop in generator voltage when the load increases. As a component of ship electrical equipment, the core is the magnetic-conducting component in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil, and serve as a reference point for insulation measurement; when measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core; in a through-type current transformer, the large current-carrying conductor under test is directly interlinked with the core to replace the primary winding. The contactor is a component that includes the core.

A broken-down resonant capacitor will likewise cause abnormal generator voltage. The resonant capacitor is used in a resonant circuit; once broken down, its original resonant function is lost, excitation regulation then becomes abnormal, and when the load increases the generator voltage drops substantially. For the fault of a broken-down resonant capacitor, the treatment method is to replace the broken-down capacitor, and the operation content is to directly replace the broken-down capacitor element. A broken-down resonant capacitor is one of the troubleshooting items for the stator winding short circuit fault of the reactor or the phase compound excitation transformer, and is one of the troubleshooting methods for the fault of a substantial drop in generator voltage. Besides breakdown, a short circuit of the resonant capacitor will also cause the generator voltage to fail to build up normally; in this case the troubleshooting method is to replace the capacitor; correspondingly, the phenomenon that the generator suddenly stops generating during operation corresponds respectively to the four treatment measures of checking and replacing the broken-down rectifier element, checking whether the wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding is loose or broken, adjusting the air gap to the required value and tightening the core, and replacing the broken-down capacitor.

In the detection stage, electrical quantities and parameters such as voltage, current and capacitance can all be measured with the aid of instruments. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools include the multimeter and the voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools include the multimeter, the ammeter and the clamp-on ammeter. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating of the AC electric drive system. The function of a capacitor is charging and discharging, and its measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and the polarity of the electrolytic capacitor. The obstructive effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC), which is related to the signal frequency and capacitance. Types of capacitors include electrolytic capacitor, ceramic capacitor, chip capacitor, monolithic capacitor, tantalum capacitor and polyester capacitor; the units are farad (F), microfarad (uF), nanofarad (nF) and picofarad (pF); the main performance indicators include capacitance, withstand voltage value (maximum working voltage) and temperature withstand value. Marine electrical equipment uses capacitors, the capacitor detection steps are applicable to capacitors, capacitors will suffer capacitor faults, and capacitor faults belong to the category of capacitors. AC single-phase motors and electric fans both contain capacitors.

The uncontrollable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system will exhibit several typical faults during operation, and generator overheating is one of them. Generator overheating is also related to factors such as long-term overload, short circuit of the excitation winding or stator winding, unbalanced three-phase load, and mutual rubbing of the stator and rotor; all these causes will make the motor temperature exceed the normal range. For generator overheating, during troubleshooting the generator output current and power should be observed and controlled below the rated values; at the same time the motor stator and rotor windings should be checked and the short-circuited winding repaired; generator overheating also corresponds to checking whether there is a single-phase high-power load or single-phase operation of the motor, that is, it is necessary to check whether a single-phase high-power load or single-phase operation of the motor exists; in addition, it is necessary to check whether the motor bearing, shaft and rotor core are loose. The fault causes and troubleshooting methods of generator overheating are listed item by item in the relevant fault troubleshooting table.

When the load increases and the generator voltage drops substantially, this often corresponds to a variety of fault causes. Poor performance of the speed governor of the prime mover will cause the generator voltage to drop substantially when the load increases; displacement of the stator core will also cause the generator voltage to drop substantially when the load increases.

Although the above several causes have similar manifestations, their corresponding treatment measures are different.

For the fault of one phase open circuit in the phase-shifting reactor, rectifier or phase compound excitation transformer, during troubleshooting the open-circuit point of the wiring among the three should be checked and repaired. This fault involves one phase open circuit in one of the phase-shifting reactor, rectifier and phase compound excitation transformer, and the check focuses on the open-circuit point of the wiring among the above three and its repair; if it is confirmed to be an internal open circuit of the rectifier, then the rectifier and its wiring need to be checked and made continuous. An open circuit in the rectifier is one of the specific fault causes listed in the troubleshooting of phase compound excitation generator faults, and its corresponding troubleshooting method is to check the rectifier and its wiring and make them continuous; the core of the operation is to check the state of the rectifier itself and its connecting lines, and the ultimate purpose is to reconnect the disconnected rectifier circuit. This cause is listed in parallel with phase-shifting reactor open circuit, inconsistent polarity of the phase compound excitation transformer winding, etc.

The polarity of the current winding and the voltage winding of the phase compound excitation transformer is inconsistent, which manifests as inconsistent polarity of the current winding and the voltage winding of the phase compound excitation transformer; the troubleshooting method is to swap the current winding or the voltage winding so that the polarities of the two are consistent. This fault is item 3 in the troubleshooting list of faults of generator-related equipment (such as the phase-shifting reactor and rectifier).

For the fault of poor speed regulation performance of the prime mover, the measure of repairing the speed governor should be taken; poor speed regulation performance of the prime mover is one of the causes listed in generator fault troubleshooting, and repairing the speed governor is the 4th measure in the generator-related fault troubleshooting methods. Displacement of the stator core is one of the causes listed in the phase compound excitation generator fault troubleshooting table; for the fault of stator core displacement, the core needs to be adjusted back to its original position and fixed securely, and this step includes two actions, adjusting the core back to its original position and fixing it securely, and is a specific repair measure in the generator fault troubleshooting methods.

In the diagnosis process, voltage and current are two basic measurable quantities. The core is a component of marine electrical equipment, and the contactor contains a core; the phase-shifting reactor is used to regulate voltage, and if its air gap is too large, it will cause the generator terminal voltage to be higher than the rated value;

When the motor temperature is too high or it smokes, the corresponding treatment measure is to remove objects that hinder ventilation and clear dust and dirt from the coil ends.

In troubleshooting of the marine power station, the conventional fault diagnosis method takes observation as the first step, and before observation it is usually necessary to first interview the operator to understand the operating conditions and abnormal manifestations before and after the fault occurs, that is, interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation. The content of observation covers abnormal phenomena, part conditions, wire conditions and equipment operating parameters, specifically including whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. After observation, the step of checking the monitoring and indicating device is entered; observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device. During observation, instruments are needed to measure electrical quantities; voltage and current are both objects measured by electrical instruments, and the multimeter can be used to measure voltage values and current values, and can also be used to test diodes and thyristors;

Generator bearing overheating is one of the common faults of the uncontrolled phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, manifested as an abnormal rise in bearing temperature, and its causes can be summarized in three aspects: bearing fault, lubrication fault and installation fault. As for lubrication, too much, too little or deteriorated lubricating oil (grease) will all cause generator bearing overheating; when adding oil, the oil quantity must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space. For this cause, the treatment method corresponding to generator bearing overheating is to check and add oil or change oil, and the lubricating oil quantity must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space. As for installation, improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover and poor assembly of the generator set will both cause bearing overheating; the former needs reinstallation, and the latter needs re-alignment and installation. Bending of the generator shaft will likewise cause bearing overheating, and the treatment method is to correct the shaft. The generator bearing is used to support the generator shaft; a marine motor usually contains components such as the bearing, winding and shaft, among which the winding is wound from enameled wire and is used to generate a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; the insulation of the marine motor winding must undergo the "three-proof" treatment of moisture proofing, mildew proofing and salt-oil-mist proofing and be oil-resistant; the shaft is used to transmit torque and rotational motion;

For bearing overheating, the corresponding troubleshooting directions are checking bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition and checking the installation condition, and all checks should be carried out around the bearing. If the noise disappears during no-load operation, it indicates poor coupling installation; long-term overload will cause the motor temperature rise to be high and will also cause the generator to overheat; long-term overload operation of an asynchronous motor will also cause insulation performance degradation, aging or mechanical damage, so when checking excessive motor temperature rise, it is necessary to troubleshoot whether a long-term overload condition exists on the mechanical side. In traction motors, a stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start and will also cause the motor temperature to be too high or smoking. For three-phase load imbalance, it should be checked whether there is a single-phase high-power load or single-phase operation of a motor, that is, check whether a single-phase high-power load exists in the system and whether any motor is in a single-phase operating state.

The thyristor is also called SCR or silicon controlled rectifier, and its measurable properties include polarity, inter-electrode resistance and control electrode.

A diode has unidirectional conductivity; under forward voltage the conduction resistance is small, and under reverse voltage the resistance is extremely large or infinite. In circuits it is commonly denoted by VD, and according to its function it can be divided into rectifier diode, isolation diode, Schottky diode, light-emitting diode and Zener diode, etc., for example rectifier diode 1N4004, isolation diode 1N4148, Schottky diode BAT85. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment, and the diode detection steps are applicable to various types of diodes; their measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance.

In troubleshooting of the ship power station, the conventional fault diagnosis method often takes observation as the starting step, that is, first asking the operator about the operating conditions before and after the fault, and then carrying out fault analysis on the premise of keeping the site unchanged. Only after this step is completed does it turn to checking the monitoring and indicating devices.

During observation, instruments are needed to measure electrical quantities and components, and the multimeter is one of the commonly used tools. The multimeter is a multi-purpose instrument, composed of three parts: the meter head, the changeover switch and the measuring circuit; at full scale the current flowing through the meter head is about several microamperes to several hundred microamperes. Distinguished by display mode, multimeters fall into two types: the analog multimeter and the digital multimeter; the MF-47 multimeter is one type of multimeter, and its panel is provided with four jacks "+", "-", "2500V" and "5A", capable of measuring a maximum voltage of 2500V and a maximum direct current of 5A. The multimeter can be used to measure various objects such as resistor, voltage, current, capacitance, diode, transistor, thyristor, photosensitive device and thermocouple;

When measuring current, a clamp-on ammeter can also be used; the clamp-on ammeter is likewise used for current measurement. When measuring direct current, the changeover switch is set to the milliampere range, and the meter head is connected in series in the broken branch; when measuring direct voltage, the test probes are connected in parallel across the two ends of the component under test, and when the range is uncertain the maximum range is set first. A diode has unidirectional conductivity and is commonly denoted by VD in circuits; its measurable properties include polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance; according to function, diodes include rectifier diode, isolation diode, Schottky diode, light-emitting diode and Zener diode, etc., among which the rectifier diode is such as 1N4004, the isolation diode such as 1N4148, and the Schottky diode such as BAT85. Diodes are widely used in marine electrical equipment; the diode detection steps are applicable to diodes, and the breakdown condition can be judged by detecting their continuity.

The brush contacts the collector ring to transfer current, and the device that fixes the brush is the brush holder. For marine motors under long-term 15° list, 7.5° trim and 22.5° roll, the brush holder connecting parts must be ensured not to loosen; too tight a clearance fit between the brush and the brush holder will cause jamming, resulting in excessive brush sparking; a loose brush holder will cause the brushes to be arranged out of line, affecting commutation and increasing sparking. Checking the contact between the brush and the commutator, checking the condition of the brush holder and checking the brush position all revolve around the brush. When the generator voltage cannot be established normally, the brush, brush holder and brush pigtail need to be checked and repaired; troubleshooting of the generator excitation circuit also includes checking whether the brush is stuck in the brush holder.

The potentiometer is also called a potentiometer; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is such a component, generally considered manually adjustable; it has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes as the shaft rotates. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge balance formed by the potentiometer R& driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R' driven by the motor M changes accordingly. The automatic oil-fired boiler contains a potentiometer, and this is the purpose of the potentiometer.

There are several causes for this phenomenon: breakdown of the rectifier will cause the generator to suddenly stop generating during operation; the fault of the generator suddenly stopping generating during operation corresponds to several handling methods: for that caused by rectifier breakdown, the broken-down rectifier elements should be checked and replaced; for that caused by no excitation current in the excitation winding circuit, check whether the wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding is loose or broken; for that caused by loosening of the reactor core and reduction of the air gap, the air gap should be adjusted to the required value and the core tightened; for that caused by short circuit of the reactor or phase-compounding transformer coil, check and repair or replace the coil with a new one; for that caused by breakdown of the resonant capacitor, replace the broken-down capacitor. When using a multimeter to test the fault of the rotating rectifier module, the breakdown condition is judged by detecting the continuity of the diode.

The generator voltage cannot be established normally, which means that the generator speed has reached the rated speed, but the voltage cannot be established. This phenomenon is one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase-compounding voltage regulation system. During troubleshooting, first confirm whether there is residual magnetism voltage; if there is no residual magnetism voltage, use an external power supply (DC) to magnetize and build up voltage; if there is already residual magnetism voltage but the voltage still does not rise, then check the state of the voltage regulator and the phase-shifting reactor. No residual magnetism or insufficient residual magnetism is manifested as the generator lacking an initial magnetic field or insufficient residual magnetism strength, and the corresponding handling method is to use an external power supply (DC) to magnetize and build up voltage. Open circuit of the excitation winding is one of the main fault causes; during troubleshooting, check whether there is looseness or breakage from the rectifier to the excitation winding, and the inspection scope covers the entire line from the rectifier to the excitation winding, specifically checking whether the line is loose or broken. The brush being stuck in the brush holder or the brush braid being broken is specifically manifested as the brush being stuck in the brush holder or the brush braid being broken, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and repair the brush, brush holder and brush braid, and the operation objects include the three components: brush, brush holder and brush braid.

The linear reactor has no air gap or the air gap is too small, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to adjust the air gap to an appropriate size, the core of the operation being to adjust the air gap to an appropriate size. The rectifier element of the voltage regulator is broken down or open-circuited, which is listed as cause item 6 (⑥) in the fault troubleshooting table; this fault involves abnormal state of the rectifier element in the voltage regulator assembly, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and replace the broken-down rectifier element. Incorrect wiring, that is, incorrect wiring of the generator excitation circuit, and the corresponding step is to carefully check the wiring and correct the wrongly connected places; this step corresponds to fault cause number ⑦ (incorrect wiring). The polarity of the generator residual magnetism voltage is opposite to that of the rectifier output voltage, which is manifested as the polarity of the residual magnetism voltage being opposite to that of the rectifier output voltage, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to swap the connections of the excitation winding.

Short circuit of the resonant capacitor is one of the fault causes for the generator voltage not being able to be established normally; for the resonant capacitor short circuit fault, the troubleshooting method is to replace the capacitor. The main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration, and the corresponding handling method is inspection and repair; inspection and repair carry out detection and restoration for faults of electrical equipment and components, covering mechanical mechanisms, winding insulation and contact components, etc., and are also used to solve the automatic tripping fault caused by the free tripping mechanism of the main switch failing to hold. The maintenance operation for faults such as soft breakdown, capacitance reduction, deterioration or damage of the capacitor is to replace the capacitor; this operation is also used to repair the intermittent rotation fault of the capacitive electric fan caused by soft breakdown of the capacitor, and to solve the slow speed problem of the impeller washing machine caused by capacitance reduction, deterioration or loose wiring of the capacitor. The marine motor includes a winding and a brush.

Similarly, an open circuit in one phase of the reactor, rectifier and phase-compound transformer will also cause the generator voltage to be lower than the rated value. At this time, check whether the wiring among the three is loose or broken; after finding it, connect and fasten it well to restore the circuit connection to normal. Too low generator speed is another possible cause. During handling, increase the speed to the rated value and check the frequency to confirm whether the frequency meets the requirement after the speed is raised. If the generator excitation winding has an open circuit, the terminal voltage will also be lower than the rated value. At this time, check the excitation winding, and after confirming the open circuit, repair or replace it. Changes in the taps of the reactor or phase-compound transformer will also cause low voltage. During troubleshooting, check and verify the voltage, and then redo the tap wiring. In addition, an error in the voltmeter will also make the reading low, thus appearing as generator voltage lower than the rated value. This cause is listed as item 7 in the fault table for voltage lower than the rated value, and the corresponding troubleshooting method is to calibrate the voltmeter.

There is a clear correspondence between the above causes and handling measures. Generator voltage lower than the rated value corresponds to increasing the setting resistor, used to eliminate the effect of the setting resistor being too small; generator voltage lower than the rated value corresponds to increasing the speed to the rated value and checking the frequency, used to solve the problem of too low speed; generator voltage lower than the rated value corresponds to checking the excitation winding, repairing or replacing it, used to handle an open circuit in the excitation winding; generator voltage lower than the rated value corresponds to checking and verifying the voltage and redoing the tap wiring, used to eliminate tap changes; generator voltage lower than the rated value corresponds to calibrating the voltmeter, used to eliminate the reading deviation caused by voltmeter error.

In contrast to low voltage, generator voltage higher than the rated value is also one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase-compound voltage regulation system.

An excessively large air gap of the phase-shifting reactor is the cause of terminal voltage higher than the rated value; during handling, reduce the air gap as required. A burned, rusted or poorly contacting sliding contact of the setting resistor, or a burned-out resistor, will also cause generator voltage higher than the rated value; at this time, check and repair or replace the resistor. An error in the voltmeter may make the reading high; the voltmeter should be calibrated. These correspondences show that generator voltage higher than the rated value corresponds respectively to reducing the air gap as required, checking and repairing or replacing the resistor, readjustment as required, and calibrating the voltmeter.

In addition to voltage abnormality, generator overheating is also one of the common faults of the uncontrollable phase-compound voltage regulation system; its fault causes and troubleshooting methods may refer to the relevant fault comparison data. Check the motor stator and rotor windings, and repair the short-circuited winding; check whether the motor bearing, shaft and rotor core are loose.

When severe bearing wear causes generator bearing overheating, the corresponding remedy is to replace the bearing; when improper assembly of the motor end cover or bearing cover causes generator bearing overheating, the corresponding remedy is to reinstall it properly; when a bent generator shaft causes generator bearing overheating, the corresponding remedy is to straighten the shaft. Among the above troubleshooting methods, replacing the bearing is used to eliminate the cause of severe bearing wear, while checking and adding or changing oil, reinstalling properly, re-aligning the installation, and straightening the shaft respectively correspond to the several conditions of abnormal lubrication, improper assembly of the end cover or bearing cover, poor unit assembly, and bent shaft.

Excessive, insufficient or deteriorated lubricating oil is a common cause of bearing overheating; when adding oil, it must not exceed 2/3 of the bearing chamber space. Improper assembly of the motor end cover, poor assembly of the generator set, or a bent shaft may all lead to bearing overheating. Mutual rubbing between the stator and rotor is also one of the potential causes of bearing overheating; in this case, the looseness of the bearing and shaft must be checked, and the rotor core must be checked as well. Severe wear of the generator bearing will cause bearing overheating and must be handled by replacing the bearing. A bent generator shaft is one of the fault causes of bearing overheating, and the remedy is to straighten the shaft.

From the perspective of judging by wear amount, when the inner diameter of a rolling bearing is 20–59 mm, the allowable wear value is about 10 times the original clearance; a new bearing has a clearance of 0.01–0.02 mm, and the maximum allowable wear value can reach 0.15–0.25 mm. When wear of a rolling bearing causes excessive clearance, it manifests as loud rotational noise, wobbling of the outer ring, or impact noise between the balls and the outer ring. If the noise disappears during no-load operation, it indicates improper installation of the coupling; if the noise persists and is accompanied by vibration, it points to a shaft or bearing fault. The maintenance procedure of replacing the bearing, besides being used for the overheating problem of a generator caused by severe bearing wear, is also applicable to bearing wear or bearing damage faults in equipment such as electric fans, electric drills and generators; it can be used to repair slow starting and reduced speed of an electric fan caused by bearing wear, and to eliminate the noise generated during operation of an electric fan due to bearing damage.

The ship power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its prescribed tasks. The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the ship power station; its functions include making and breaking circuits, issuing alarms when protective devices operate, detecting and displaying various electrical parameters, and regulating the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active power and reactive power of parallel-operating generator sets. The main switchboard is equipped with commonly used electrical apparatus such as circuit breakers, changeover switches, excitation rheostats, reverse-power relays and various measuring instruments. The lighting distribution panel is also equipped with a network insulation detection device, such as earth lamps and a switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The operation of changing over to shore power is also carried out on the main switchboard, which is provided with a shore power switch and an indicator lamp indicating that the shore power box has been closed.

In the measurement and detection stage, the multimeter contains a changeover switch internally; the function of the changeover switch is to select the measurement object and select the range, and it is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands. It has many selection positions and contacts, and on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands. A changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not left open. If capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance; never measure with power on.

The clamp-on ammeter contains a current transformer internally; the current transformer is used to transform the current ratio and has the nature of a current source. The standard current on the secondary side is usually 5 A, its symbol is TA, the primary-side terminals are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary side by K1 and K2. During operation it is equivalent to a short-circuited transformer; the secondary winding must never be left open during operation, and one end of the secondary side is earthed. The through-type current transformer is one type of current transformer; current transformers also include coil-type and busbar-type types. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA and is used inside the circuit breaker to provide current detection sampling; the nameplate indicates the reference current I0 and the current ratio ITA, and the current ratio is selected according to the rated current, for example, when the generator rated current is 720 A, the TA specification may be 800/5 A. The load current I flows through the primary side of the current transformer and is transformed into a secondary current that is connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements; its secondary side must never be left open, the terminals for connecting an external ammeter must have a short-circuit link, and the link may be removed only after the wiring has been checked.

The insulation resistance tester, also called a megohmmeter, is composed of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter. It is a portable instrument used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, lines and cables, and often adopts a ratio meter structure. According to the highest voltage emitted by the hand-cranked generator, it is divided into specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V and 2500V, and its terminal posts are L, E and G. The wattmeter, also called a watt meter, is composed of a current coil and a voltage coil and is used to measure electrical power, calculating power by detecting the load current and voltage. The current coil of the wattmeter is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test to detect the voltage. The current coil and the voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals (such as "*"), and during measurement the currents of the two coils must flow in from or out of these terminals at the same time.

The circuit breaker is a switching device used to protect circuits in the ship's power system. It belongs to low-voltage distribution devices and is divided into the frame type (air type) and the molded-case type. It has both switching and protection functions and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. The air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker itself. The main switch is used to control the connection between the generator and the power grid. It is the air circuit breaker in the ship's power station that connects and disconnects the generator and the main busbar, has both switching and protection functions, and can automatically disconnect the generator from the power grid when the power grid has a short circuit or the generator has undervoltage. Every 4 to 5 years, performance verification of undervoltage, overload, short circuit, reverse power, etc. is required. The main switch is mainly composed of the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device and arc extinguishing device, etc., and also includes auxiliary contacts and the control and signal indication circuit.

The undervoltage release is one of the main components of the generator main switch. Together with the shunt release, overcurrent protection device, etc., it constitutes the main switch, and it exists as a standard configuration component in the DW14 circuit breaker, used to implement the undervoltage protection function. The shunt release is one of the main components of the generator main switch. Together with the undervoltage release, overcurrent protection device, etc., it belongs to the main switch components and is used for shunt control. The overcurrent protection device is one of the main components of the generator main switch. In the DW14 circuit breaker it is specifically embodied as the AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, which is set with the generator rated current as the reference value, is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker, has long-time delay, short-time delay and instantaneous tripping functions, and is provided with three operating current setting knobs and two delay time setting knobs. The arc extinguishing device is one of the main components of the generator main switch. Together with the undervoltage release, shunt release, etc., it constitutes the main switch, serves the coordinated work of connecting and disconnecting the generator and the main busbar, and is used to extinguish the arc when the switch is connected and disconnected. The auxiliary contact is one of the main components of the generator main switch, used for control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection. In the motor forward rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is often used to realize the self-locking of the contactor coil, and through its on-off state it controls the on and off of the running indicator lamp to display the working state of the equipment.

The control and signal indication circuit is one of the main components of the generator main switch. Together with the undervoltage, shunt, overcurrent protection and arc extinguishing devices, it constitutes the main switch, and it exists as a component in commonly used ship main switches such as the DW14 circuit breaker.

The trip unit is a component of ship electrical equipment. In a circuit breaker it is used to implement protection functions such as overload, short circuit and undervoltage and to drive the contacts to open. The undervoltage protection of the ship generator is implemented by the undervoltage release in the circuit breaker, and the generator external short circuit protection is also implemented by the overcurrent trip unit in the circuit breaker. The AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit, as the overcurrent protection device, is one of the components of the generator main switch. It is usually additionally installed on the DW14 circuit breaker, its operation setting uses the generator rated current as the reference value, and its physical installation position is on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker. The DW14 circuit breaker is produced by introducing the AH type and AS type circuit breaker technology of Japan's Terasaki company and is widely used in domestic ships. When used as the generator main switch, the AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit is added; its overcurrent trip unit uses the generator rated current as the reference value and is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker.

The reverse power relay is one of the commonly used control and protection devices on the ship's main switchboard, used to detect reverse power of the AC generator and trigger a protection action; the setting value for the diesel engine prime mover is 8% to 15% of rated power, with a time delay of 3 to 10 s for operation; for the GG-21 induction-type relay, the starting value of the moving contact differs from the actual contact value. Failure of the reverse power relay will cause the AC generator to exhibit reverse power; one of its causes is that wiring was not carried out as required, and the troubleshooting method for incorrect wiring is to change to correct wiring; the second cause is that the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, and once the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, the reverse power relay ceases to function; it is precisely because the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out and the reverse power relay ceases to function that the reverse power relay fails, and the troubleshooting method for a burnt-out coil is to check and replace the coil.

The generator main switch failing to close (excluding electric closing) is one of the common faults. The undervoltage trip unit failing to pick up normally will cause the generator main switch to fail to close, specifically manifested as the undervoltage trip unit coil being open-circuited, wiring being loose, or abnormal return spring tension causing failure to pick up; severe wear of the tripping mechanism and failure to latch will also cause the generator main switch to fail to close, requiring adjustment of bolts or replacement of parts; the overcurrent or electromagnetic trip unit being out of adjustment (i.e., the operating value being too small) will hinder closing, and it must be corrected and adjusted to the required value; the thermal trip unit not being reset after operation will likewise cause failure to close, in which case one should wait 1~2 s for the thermal element to reset, and this corrective measure is precisely the corresponding handling method for the fault of the generator main switch failing to close. During troubleshooting, first detect whether the voltage across the undervoltage coil is normal; if normal, check whether the coil is open-circuited, whether the terminal posts are loose, whether the tension of the trip unit return spring is normal, and whether the mechanical mechanism is jammed; if the coil voltage is abnormal, the undervoltage coil circuit should be detected and the series resistor checked. If the voltage across the undervoltage coil is normal but it cannot pick up, check whether the mechanical mechanism is jammed; if the voltage across the undervoltage coil is abnormal, detect the circuit and check the series resistor. For problems with the tripping mechanism, check the tripping mechanism and adjust the corresponding bolts or replace with new ones.

No voltage on the network after the main switch closes is also a common fault. The main contact being burnt out and the moving and fixed contacts not touching will cause no voltage on the network after the main switch closes, and the troubleshooting method for a burnt-out main contact is to check, repair or replace the main contact; the moving contact being loose or the wire being broken will also cause no voltage on the network after the main switch closes, and the troubleshooting method for a loose moving contact is to check the wiring and connections and connect them properly or tighten the screws.

Tripping during use after the main switch closes likewise belongs to common faults. The armature of the undervoltage trip unit failing to latch the tripping shaft will cause tripping, and the tripping mechanism needs to be checked; the tripping mechanism being aged and failing to latch will cause tripping, and the tripping mechanism needs to be checked and the corresponding bolts adjusted or replaced with new ones; the series resistor of the undervoltage coil being too large will cause tripping, and it is necessary to check whether the resistor and wiring are in good condition; the return spring force of the undervoltage trip unit being too large will cause tripping, and the spring tension needs to be checked; a sudden increase in load causing undervoltage operation will cause tripping, and the voltage regulator or governor needs to be checked, or the spring tension reduced; the delay of the overload relay being too small or having no delay action will also cause tripping.

In the fault where the main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration, the resistance value of the undervoltage coil being too large, resulting in weak electromagnetic attraction, or the core return spring force being too large and the core not picking up firmly, will cause this phenomenon, and troubleshooting should be carried out by increasing the electromagnetic attraction or reducing the spring return force; the free tripping mechanism failing to latch will cause this phenomenon, and it needs to be checked and repaired; the overcurrent trip unit being out of adjustment, the operating current value being too low, and it having already approached the operating value at normal load current will cause this phenomenon, and the overcurrent trip unit should be adjusted to correct the operating current value.
