Motor overload refers to the fault state in which the motor's operating current or power exceeds the rated value; in DC motors it causes difficult commutation and excessive sparking, and in generators it triggers overload protection; when a DC motor is overloaded, the current per unit area of the brush is large, causing difficult commutation and resulting in excessive sparking under brush; a generator whose output power or current exceeds its rated value is defined as being overloaded.

When a single generator is running, starting a large load such as an air compressor, or starting a large load without observing the power, can easily cause the generator to trip due to overload. During parallel operation, if one generator set trips due to a fault and stepped unloading fails, the remaining generator sets may trip due to overload. Generator overload protection operation often occurs when a single generator is running with a large load, starting large equipment such as an air compressor or ballast pump without observing the power; during parallel operation, if stepped unloading fails or overload still exists after unloading, the running generator set will trip due to protection operation; it may also be caused by another generator set tripping immediately due to a motor fault, causing the remaining generator sets to overload. Generator undervoltage protection operation mainly occurs in cases where the governor and fuel system or the voltage regulator have faults. When caused by a governor and fuel system fault, the speed first decreases and then tripping occurs; whether the speed has decreased can be judged by the sound of the diesel engine to confirm tripping caused by a governor fault; when caused by a voltage regulator fault, the voltage first decreases and then tripping occurs; whether the voltage has decreased can be judged by the change in brightness of the lighting lamps to confirm tripping caused by a voltage regulator fault.

The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the ship's power station. The ship's power station includes the main switchboard, the ship's power network, and the shore power box, and also includes brushed synchronous generators, brushless synchronous generators, as well as uncontrolled phase-compound excitation voltage regulation systems, controlled phase-compound excitation voltage regulation systems, thyristor excitation voltage regulation systems, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation systems, and DW14 type circuit breakers. The main switchboard includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. Its main functions include connecting or disconnecting circuits, protection device operation and alarm, detection and display of various electrical parameters, and it can regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel. When changing over to shore power, the shore power switch must be closed immediately after disconnecting the generator main switch.

The fuse corresponds to the symbol FU in circuit diagrams and is a protective electrical device. When the power network or electrical equipment undergoes overload and short circuit, it automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. It belongs to distribution electrical devices and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and electrodynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs, and has both overload protection and short circuit protection functions. The RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection.

The ship's power network belongs to the ship's power station and usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system. Single-phase earthing at any point is an abnormal state. If another phase is earthed, a short circuit is formed. After one-point earthing occurs, electrical equipment can still operate normally, but it must be eliminated promptly to improve reliability. The earthed line and fault point can be found through the earth lamps on the switchboard or the section-by-section narrowing method. An insulation detection device for the power network is installed on the lighting distribution panel of the main switchboard. Insulation measurement must be carried out when the power network is energized, and a portable insulation resistance tester cannot be used. Earthing faults in the ship's power network mostly occur in the lighting network, and the search order is from the accommodation area to the navigation and communication equipment in the wheelhouse.

The switchboard-type insulation resistance meter is used to measure the insulation resistance of the power network. It is installed on the lighting panel of the main switchboard and consists of a meter head and a rectifier power supply. It is used for live measurement of the insulation resistance to earth of the power and lighting networks.

Structurally, it consists of two parts: the measuring mechanism (meter head) and the auxiliary device (rectifier power supply). Through the changeover switch, it can separately measure the insulation resistance of the 380V/440V power network and the 220V/110V lighting network. Its working principle is based on the magnitude of earth leakage current: the lower the insulation resistance, the larger the earth leakage current, and the greater the deflection angle of the meter head pointer; when a single-phase earthing fault occurs, the meter head pointer deflects the most, indicating an insulation resistance value of "0". Measurement must be carried out when the ship's power network is energized, and it is strictly prohibited to use a portable insulation resistance tester as a substitute. It is often used to find earthing faults in the lighting network, locating the fault point by pulling off distribution switches one by one and observing whether the reading recovers. The meter head serves as the measuring mechanism in the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter; the larger the earth leakage current, the greater the pointer deflection; its type is a high-sensitivity moving-coil instrument, and the number of scales is 4-6.

The multimeter contains a meter head and a changeover switch; the multimeter uses resistance, voltage, current and capacitance. The meter head is the core measuring component of the multimeter, employing a high-sensitivity moving-coil instrument with a full-scale current in the microampere range, and is one of the three major components of the basic structure of the multimeter (the other two being the changeover switch and the measuring circuit); a high-sensitivity moving-coil instrument is usually employed as the measuring mechanism. The function of capacitance is charging and discharging; the measurable properties include earth leakage, capacitance and polarity (electrolytic capacitors); it is a component composed of two metal films placed close together and separated by an insulating material in the middle, its characteristic being that it blocks direct current and passes alternating current; in circuit diagrams it is usually denoted by the letter C plus a number, such as C25; its hindering effect on AC signals is called capacitive reactance, with the formula Xc=1/(2πfC).

The reverse-power protection of the generator operates as follows: the generator reverse-power protection trips; improper mastery of the closing moment during paralleling operation causes the main switch of the incoming generator set to trip after being closed; during parallel operation, adjusting the load distribution in the reverse direction causes the reverse-power protection to trip; during paralleling, damage to the speed governor of one of the diesel engines or interruption of fuel supply causes reverse-power tripping; improper paralleling operation causing the generator current to reach 250A may be misjudged as an external short-circuit fault; the generator main switch trips due to the protection being triggered by reverse power. A generator external short-circuit fault means the main switch trips when the generator current is greater than or equal to 2IN; the criterion for judgment is the generator external short-circuit protection operating threshold required by the specifications: the main switch trips when the current ≥2I_N; in an automatic power station management system, if the main switch trips and there is no other reaction in the engine room with only a short-circuit fault reported, this fault can be determined; in a conventional power station, excluding the situations of large-load starting, cargo handling operations, and tripping after first reducing speed/voltage, this fault can be concluded to have occurred; improper paralleling operation causing the generator current to reach 250 (unit not explicitly stated, suspected to be amperes or multiples) may also cause similar tripping.

Improper operation refers to faults caused by improper operation, the common ones being: ① improper closing operation; ② unbalanced generator load control; ③ improper operation caused by erroneous observation. During paralleling operation, improper mastery of the closing moment or adjusting the load distribution in the reverse direction may cause the generator reverse-power protection to trip.

An earthing fault of the lighting network means the insulation resistance of the lighting network is low or earthing occurs; earthing faults of the ship's network mostly occur in the lighting network; the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter indicating "0" is the direct basis for judging an earthing fault of the lighting network; the order of pulling area switches for troubleshooting is: crew living area—deck lighting area—engine room lighting area—wheelhouse communication and navigation equipment; in front of the main switchboard, pull off the lighting distribution switches one by one and observe whether the insulation resistance tester returns to normal to locate the faulty circuit; in front of the distribution boxes, use a portable insulation resistance tester to measure the insulation condition to earth of the branch circuits of the secondary distribution network; when searching for the specific earthing point, disconnect from the intermediate junction box to determine which small area (such as a room) is earthed. The lighting network earthing fault corresponds to the troubleshooting steps for a lighting network earthing fault, which are: first turn on the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter to measure the lighting network, and the insulation resistance tester indicates that the insulation resistance value at this time is "0"; after finding the distribution switch where the earthing fault occurs, cut off the power supply of that circuit and check the insulation resistance tester indication again to verify the fault point; after determining the earthed branch, pull off the distribution switch of that circuit and close the remaining switches, and restore the power supply of that circuit at the main switchboard. When troubleshooting an earthing fault of the lighting network, disconnect from the intermediate junction box to determine the small earthed area; if the earthing point still cannot be found by checking the lamp holders, etc., the cables between the junction box and the electrical appliances should be checked.

The junction box is a component used in the ship's electrical system to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical elements; the general alarm device includes a junction box; the general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc.; the solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box, but is directly connected inside the local control box.

The shore power box is used to connect shore power and is usually located on the main deck level; it receives power supply from the onshore power source through a cable, and is generally equipped with a shore power indicator lamp, a circuit breaker (or a switch plus fuse) and shore power terminal posts; it is provided with a phase-sequence indicator lamp (or negative-sequence relay) to detect the consistency of the phase sequence between shore power and ship power, and is marked with a nameplate indicating the rated voltage and rated frequency of the ship power; when the shore power is a three-phase four-wire system, the neutral line needs to be connected to the terminal post on the shore power box that is connected to the hull; if a negative-sequence relay is used, when the phase sequence is inconsistent, the shore power box switch will trip immediately upon closing. Precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the ship's power station: when connecting shore power, the type of current of the shore power and the ship power must be kept consistent, and the rated frequency and rated voltage of the shore power should be consistent with the ship power parameters; for three-phase four-wire shore power, the neutral line must first be connected to the hull terminal post before connection can be made; only when the phase sequence of the shore power is consistent with that of the ship power may transfer be carried out at the main switchboard; during the period of connecting shore power, it is strictly forbidden to close the ship's generator, and the two must not supply power at the same time.

The generator main switch failing to close means a type of fault in which the switch still cannot complete the closing action after the electric closing function is excluded. There are many causes of this phenomenon, among which the undervoltage release failing to pull in normally is one of the common causes. If the coil voltage is normal, it is necessary to check whether the coil is open-circuited and whether the terminal posts are loose, and at the same time check whether the tension of the release return spring is normal and whether the mechanical mechanism is jammed. If the voltage across the undervoltage coil is abnormal, the undervoltage coil circuit should be tested, and the resistor connected in series in this circuit should be checked.

In addition to the undervoltage release failing to pull in normally, severe wear of the trip mechanism, which cannot hold, will likewise cause the generator main switch to fail to close. At this time the trip mechanism cannot hold reliably due to wear, and the maintenance procedure corresponding to the generator main switch failing to close is to check the trip mechanism, adjust the corresponding bolts or replace with new ones, that is, check the trip mechanism, adjust the corresponding bolts or replace with new parts. The thermal trip unit not resetting after operation is also one of the causes of the generator main switch failing to close; during handling it is necessary to stop for 1~2s and wait for the thermal element to reset. Among the above causes, severe wear of the trip mechanism, which cannot hold, corresponds to checking the trip mechanism, adjusting the corresponding bolts or replacing with new ones;

The moving contact coming loose or being broken will likewise cause no voltage on the power grid after the main switch is closed; during troubleshooting, check the wiring and connections, and connect the wiring properly or tighten the screws. That is to say, no voltage on the power grid after the main switch is closed corresponds to two maintenance procedures: first, check, repair or replace the main contact; second, check the wiring and connections, and connect properly or tighten the screws.

Tripping during use after the main switch is closed is also related to the state of the trip unit. At the same time, this fault also corresponds to the maintenance procedure of checking the trip mechanism. The main switch is a combination of the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device, arc extinguishing device, auxiliary contact and control and signal indication circuit. The main switchboard contains the main switch. The DW14 type circuit breaker adopts Terasaki technology from Japan and is provided with an additional AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit; this trip unit is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker and has long-time delay, short-time delay, instantaneous tripping and trip pre-alarm functions.

If the voltage coil in the reverse power relay is burned out, the relay will fail to function. The wattmeter contains a voltage coil, which is used to detect the voltage across the two ends of the circuit under test; a additional resistor is connected in series in the branch where it is located, and the branch is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test; the voltage range of the wattmeter is realized precisely by connecting additional resistors of different resistance values in series with the voltage coil. A coil is an electrical component made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and it has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. The contactor contains a coil and main contacts; a fault of the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start; failure or loss of the contactor armature return spring will cause the contactor not to release or to release slowly after the stop button is pressed; during handling it is necessary to replace or adjust the return spring, but care must be taken that the return force is not too large. The main contact is the switching component in the contactor used to make or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor; if the copper main contact discolors or gives off a burnt smell, it indicates poor contact and overheating, and it is necessary to adjust the gap and overtravel and remove the oxide film; when the main contact has been overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected as the replacement.

The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, the voltage circuit and the current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions needs to be checked.

Resistance is a quantity whose resistance value can be measured, and the measuring tool is the multimeter. When measuring a resistor in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; in the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open-circuit shunt resistor will cause the voltage regulator to have no main regulating effect. Voltage is a quantity whose voltage value can be measured, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; current is a quantity whose current value can be measured, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter; the multimeter is used to measure resistance, voltage and current, and the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current.

Tripping of the main switch during closing operation is a common type of fault in ship power station switchgear, and its causes involve multiple links such as the tripping mechanism, coil circuits, and protection settings. Aging of the tripping mechanism, which fails to hold, can likewise cause tripping of the main switch during closing operation; the troubleshooting method is to check the specific condition of the tripping mechanism, and the corrective measures include adjusting the corresponding bolts or replacing with new parts. Tripping of the main switch during closing operation also corresponds to the treatment approach of checking the tripping mechanism and adjusting the corresponding bolts or replacing with new parts, that is, inspecting the mechanical tripping part item by item, adjusting the bolts according to wear and fit conditions, and replacing with new parts if necessary. When the main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration and the cause is that the free tripping mechanism fails to hold, inspection and repair are also required. The above two causes relating to the tripping mechanism are listed in the fault table respectively as cause item ① and another cause; their common feature is hooking failure, and the difference is that the former occurs between the armature of the undervoltage trip unit and the tripping shaft, while the latter is caused by aging of the tripping mechanism itself.

Improper setting of protective devices can also cause tripping. In the troubleshooting table, this corresponds to the troubleshooting method of adjusting the overcurrent trip unit, but the wording "correct and adjust to the required value" is not directly used. If the delay of the overload relay is too small or there is no delay action, this can likewise cause tripping of the main switch during closing operation; the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check and adjust to the specified delay value, and the core of the operation is to correct the delay parameter of the overload relay to the specified value.

In addition, the case where the overcurrent or electromagnetic trip unit operating value is too small also needs to be handled by correcting and adjusting to the required value in the fault of the generator main switch failing to close.

Abnormality of circuits related to the undervoltage trip unit is another important type of cause. If the series resistor of the undervoltage coil is too large, this will cause tripping of the main switch during closing operation; the corresponding troubleshooting method is to check whether the series resistor and wiring are in good condition, and the objects involved are the undervoltage coil and its series resistor. Tripping of the main switch during closing operation also corresponds to the corrective measure of checking and reducing the spring tension, that is, by checking the spring tension condition and appropriately reducing it so that the trip unit operating value returns to the normal range. A sudden increase in load, causing undervoltage operation, can likewise cause tripping of the main switch during closing operation; the troubleshooting method includes checking whether the characteristics of the voltage regulator and governor are normal, and the alternative or auxiliary measure is to reduce the opposing spring tension of the undervoltage trip unit. By checking the characteristics of the voltage regulator and governor, or reducing the spring tension of the undervoltage trip unit, the problem of false tripping caused by voltage sag due to load fluctuation can be solved. When the generator main switch fails to close, it is necessary to check whether the opposing spring tension of the undervoltage trip unit is normal; the main switch is a component of the main switchboard, used to control the connection between the generator and the power grid, and can automatically disconnect the generator from the power grid when there is a short circuit in the power grid or undervoltage of the generator; every 4 to 5 years, performance verification of undervoltage, overload, short circuit, reverse power, etc. is required.

Measurement and component inspection related to troubleshooting of tripping faults must likewise not be ignored. The armature is the movable ferromagnetic component in an electromagnetic mechanism, driven by the coil magnetic force to pull in or release, and is used to control contact action or braking; jamming of the armature will cause contactor KM to fail to close, resulting in the motor having no power and failure to start; failure or damage of the armature opposing spring is one of the main causes of the contactor not releasing or releasing slowly after the stop button is pressed. The opposing spring is a spring component in contactors and circuit breakers, used to provide release force or reset force; when handling contactor release faults, the opposing spring needs to be replaced or adjusted, but care must be taken that the opposing force is not too large.

The fault symptom that the main switch is prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration is not uncommon in the operation of ship power stations.

The causes of this phenomenon are not single; the resistance value of the undervoltage coil being too large, resulting in weak electromagnetic attraction, or the core opposing spring force being too large so that the core does not pull in firmly, is one direct cause. Specifically, if the resistance value of the undervoltage coil is too large, the electromagnetic attraction will become weak; or if the core opposing spring force is too large, both will prevent the core from pulling in firmly, and the main switch will therefore lose hold and trip under hull vibration. For this cause, troubleshooting should increase the electromagnetic attraction or reduce the spring opposing force. Another cause is that the free tripping mechanism fails to hold, that is, the free tripping mechanism cannot maintain the locked state; this should be inspected and repaired. The third cause is misadjustment of the overcurrent trip unit, with the operating current value too low, already close to the operating value at normal load current, manifested as failure of the overcurrent trip unit, characterized by the operating current value being too low and already close to the operating value at normal load current; the corresponding troubleshooting method is to adjust the overcurrent trip unit. The above three causes all lead to the main switch being prone to automatic tripping due to hull vibration, and the handling respectively corresponds to increasing the electromagnetic attraction or reducing the spring opposing force, inspection and repair, and adjusting the overcurrent trip unit.

Among the components of the main switch, the trip unit is one of the key components.

The wattmeter contains a voltage coil, which is used to detect the voltage across the circuit under test; its branch is connected in series with an additional resistor and connected in parallel into the circuit. The core in electromagnetic equipment is the magnetic-conducting component, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil, and serve as the reference point for insulation measurement. The contactor contains a core and a coil. When measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core. In the through-type current transformer, the large-current conductor under test is directly interlinked with the core to replace the primary winding.

Resistance, voltage and current are the basic electrical quantities to be measured in fault diagnosis. The measurable property of resistance is the resistance value, and the measuring tool is the multimeter. Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis. The generator being unable to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing the fault tree. Overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems.

The measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, used to understand equipment status. Measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems.

When the generator voltage cannot be built up normally, the corresponding troubleshooting and maintenance procedure includes several items. An external DC power supply can be used for magnetization to build up voltage; check whether there is looseness or a break in the wiring from the rectifier to the excitation winding, this step addresses the cause of an open excitation winding; polish the surface of the collector ring with fine sandpaper, used to solve the faults of generator voltage not being adjustable and the generator not conducting; check and repair the brush, brush holder and brush braid, addressing the fault of the brush being stuck in the brush holder or the brush braid being broken;

Adjust the air gap to an appropriate size, addressing the fault of the linear reactor having no air gap or too small an air gap; check and replace the broken-down rectifier element, addressing the fault of the rectifier element of the voltage regulator being broken down or open-circuited; carefully check the wiring and correct the wrongly connected places, addressing the cause of incorrect wiring; swap the connections of the excitation winding, addressing the fault that the residual magnetism voltage of the generator is opposite in polarity to the output voltage of the rectifier; check the connections and reconnect them properly, addressing the fault of broken connections among the reactor, the resonance capacitor and the phase-compound excitation transformer; replace the capacitor, addressing faults such as soft breakdown, reduced capacitance, deterioration or short circuit of the capacitor, and also used to repair the fault of the capacitor-type electric fan turning and then stopping due to soft breakdown of the capacitor, as well as to solve the problem of slow speed of the impeller washing machine caused by reduced capacitance, deterioration or loose wiring of the capacitor.

When the generator voltage is lower than the rated value, the corresponding handling steps include: adjust to increase the air gap, addressing the fault of the generator voltage being lower than the rated value caused by too small an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor; check whether the wiring among the three is loose or broken, and tighten it properly after finding it, addressing the fault of one phase being open-circuited in the reactor, rectifier and phase-compound excitation transformer; increase the setting resistor; raise the speed to the rated value and check the frequency, addressing the cause of too low a speed; check the excitation winding and repair or replace it, addressing the fault of an open-circuit excitation winding of the generator; check and verify the voltage and reconnect the taps, addressing the cause of tap changes in the reactor or phase-compound excitation transformer; calibrate the voltmeter, performed when an error in the voltmeter causes the displayed voltage to be low. When the generator voltage is higher than the rated value, the corresponding handling steps include: reduce the air gap as required, addressing the fault of the generator voltage being higher than the rated value caused by too large an air gap of the phase-shifting reactor; check and repair or renew the resistor, addressing the faults of the sliding contact of the setting resistor being burnt, rusted, in poor contact, or the resistor being burnt out.

When the AC generator produces a reverse power phenomenon, it is often directly related to the fault symptom of reverse power relay failure. There are two causes of reverse power relay failure: first, it is not wired as required; second, the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, and the reverse power relay does not function. Not being wired as required means the wiring method does not meet the specification requirements, which will directly cause the reverse power relay to fail; for this cause, the troubleshooting method is to change to correct wiring, that is, to correct the wiring that does not meet the requirements. If the voltage coil or current coil is burnt out, it manifests as the reverse power relay not functioning, and its root cause lies in the voltage coil or current coil inside the relay being burnt out; for this cause, the troubleshooting method is to check and replace the coil, that is, first check the coil and replace it after confirming it is burnt out.

During the inspection process, instruments are needed to measure voltage and current. Voltage is a measurable quantity, and its value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter; current is likewise a measurable quantity, and can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. The clamp-on ammeter is used to detect current without disconnecting the circuit. The multimeter is used both to measure voltage and to measure current, and is a common tool for judging whether the coil is burnt out.

The wattmeter internally contains a current coil and a voltage coil. The function of the current coil is to detect current; it is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the current of the circuit under test; the current coil and the voltage coil are respectively marked with corresponding terminals, for example the end marked with "*", and during measurement the current must flow in or out from this end at the same time.

Reverse power relay failure may be caused by a burnt-out current coil, in which case the coil needs to be checked and replaced; when the contactor fails to pick up and the coil has an open circuit, the resistance is measured with the power off to determine the open circuit, and then the coil needs to be replaced; when the contactor coil overheats due to an internal partial short circuit, it is determined by the resistance comparison method and the coil also needs to be replaced. A coil short circuit corresponds to the maintenance procedure of replacing the coil. When the reverse power relay fails due to a burnt-out voltage coil or current coil, the step of replacing the coil needs to be carried out after inspection.

The content of observation covers abnormal phenomena, part status, conductor status and equipment operating parameters, specifically including whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. After observation, the monitoring and indicating device should be further checked, and the nature and scope of the fault judged from the instrument readings.

In the monitoring and indicating device, voltage and current are the two most basic measurable performances. The voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter, and the current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. The multimeter is used both to measure voltage and to measure current; the clamp-on ammeter is specially used to measure current without disconnecting the circuit. When measuring current, if an ammeter is used, the circuit must be disconnected and the ammeter connected in series. As far as parallel operation is concerned, the voltage difference and current distribution between two units are often important bases for judging whether the synchronizing conditions are met and whether the load is balanced; therefore, when reading these values, they should be recorded together with the parallel state at that time.

Power measurement relies on the wattmeter, also called the watt meter, whose function is to measure electric power. The wattmeter consists of a current coil and a voltage coil; the current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the two ends of the circuit under test to detect voltage, and the power is calculated by detecting the load current and voltage. The current coil and voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals, for example marked with "*", and during measurement the currents of the two coils must flow in or out from this end at the same time. If the corresponding terminals are connected in reverse during wiring, the reading direction of the wattmeter will deviate; therefore, in the active power measurement of parallel-operated units, the marking of the corresponding terminals should be checked before wiring to confirm that the connection directions of the current coil and voltage coil are consistent.

The ship power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system, and the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in accomplishing its specified tasks; its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. The ship power station includes the main switchboard, the ship's power network, and the shore power box, and also includes brushed synchronous generators and brushless synchronous generators, as well as different types of excitation voltage regulation devices such as the uncontrolled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, the controlled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, the thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, and the brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system. The ship power station also includes the DW14 circuit breaker, which was introduced from Japanese Terasaki technology and is provided with an AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit. The ship's power network is a component of the ship power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the relevant operating requirements of the ship power station. Fault handling for parallel operation is carried out around the above-mentioned parts; whether it is the generator proper, the excitation voltage regulation system, or the circuit breaker and power network links, all may become sources of abnormal phenomena.

The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the power station, and has the functions of circuit making and breaking, protection and alarm, parameter detection, and power regulation; its main functions include making or breaking circuits, protection device operation and alarm, detection and display of various electrical parameters, and regulation of the voltage and frequency of the power station and the active and reactive power of generators operating in parallel. The main switchboard includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. The main switch is used to control the connection between the generator and the power network; in the ship power station it is the air circuit breaker used to connect and disconnect the generator and the main busbar, and has both switching and protection functions, mainly consisting of the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device, and arc extinguishing device, etc., and is additionally provided with auxiliary contacts and a control and signal indication circuit. The main switch belongs to the undervoltage release, belongs to the shunt release, belongs to the overcurrent protection device, belongs to the arc extinguishing device, belongs to the auxiliary contacts, and also belongs to the control and signal indication circuit. In parallel operation, the closing and opening timing of the main switch is directly related to whether the generator set can be smoothly connected to the power network; its undervoltage release operates when the power network loses voltage, the shunt release is used for remote disconnection, the overcurrent protection device cuts off the circuit when the current exceeds the set value, the arc extinguishing device is responsible for extinguishing the arc generated during the breaking process, and the auxiliary contacts and control and signal indication circuit feed back the position status of the main switch to the control panel for the operator to judge.

In terms of active power distribution during parallel operation, the manual speed control switch on the generator control panel is used to adjust the diesel engine servo motor. The speed control switch in the ship power station is used to adjust the diesel engine governor servo motor through manual operation; adjusting this switch can change the diesel engine throttle opening, thereby realizing active power distribution among generator sets in parallel operation. The servo motor is used for active power distribution of generator sets in parallel operation, realizing load transfer by changing the diesel engine throttle opening; the automatic fuel oil boiler includes a servo motor, which is controlled by a bridge or regulator signal and drives a feedback potentiometer or throttle actuator through rotation to achieve automatic balance and position control; the speed control switch is also found in electric fans, and an electric fan includes a speed control switch for adjusting the fan speed; poor contact of the speed control switch will cause the electric fan to sometimes rotate and sometimes not, and damage to the speed control switch is one of the possible causes of failure to start of the electric fan. From this it can be seen that once a manual adjustment component such as the speed control switch has poor contact or is damaged, it will likewise cause failure of active power distribution during parallel operation, manifested as no response of load transfer during adjustment or uneven power distribution between the two generator sets.

The choice of parallel operation method is related to the specific conditions of the ship power station. The manual synchronization method is suitable for small ship power stations where parallel operation is infrequent, or as a backup for the automatic method; the automatic quasi-synchronization method is suitable for ship power stations with many generator sets in parallel, large power, and high requirements. A generator operating on the power network should carry more than 50% rated load before another generator may be connected in parallel. When disconnecting a generator from parallel operation, the speed control switches of the two generator sets need to be adjusted in the same direction to transfer active power. If during the disconnection process the adjustment directions of the speed control switches of the two generator sets are inconsistent, the transfer of active power cannot be completed smoothly; therefore, during operation the same-direction adjustment should be maintained, and the wattmeter should be used to monitor the active power changes of the two generator sets until the active power of the generator set to be disconnected drops to a level at which it can be broken, after which the main switch completes the disconnection from the power network.

In parallel operation, the even distribution of reactive power is usually achieved by means of current stabilizing devices, and the brushless synchronous generator adopts this method. The AC equalizing connection method, also called the phase-shifting reactor equalizing connection method, is suitable for parallel operation of generators of different capacities; through the phase-shifting reactors of the voltage regulators of the generators in parallel operation, better distribution of reactive load can be achieved with smaller equalizing current. The phase-shifting reactor is a key element in the phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, used to regulate voltage and to achieve reactive load distribution of generators in parallel operation; in the uncontrolled phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, an open circuit of the phase-shifting reactor will cause the generator to fail to build up voltage, and if its air gap is too large, it will cause the terminal voltage of the generator to be higher than the rated value.

The DC equalizing line connecting contactor is controlled by the normally open auxiliary contact of the generator main switch. If the normally open auxiliary contact of the main switch has poor contact, it may cause failure of paralleling or tripping of the power grid. When the generator is paralleled, poor contact of the contacts of the equalizing line contactor will open the equalizing line, likewise causing failure of paralleling or tripping of the power grid. Poor contact of contacts refers to an electrical fault state in which the conductive performance is reduced due to contamination, oxidation or insufficient mechanical pressure on the contact surface; in a contactor, it is one of the main causes of contact overheating or burning; methods for dealing with poor contact of contactor contacts include cleaning the contact surface, dressing the surface and tightening the contacts and the conductive plate. Poor contact is a fault state in which the contact resistance increases due to looseness, oxidation or foreign matter at an electrical connection; loose fastening screws and terminal lugs will cause poor contact, increasing the contact resistance and thereby causing local overheating, phase failure, phase-to-phase short circuit and other faults.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control motors in the ship's power system; it belongs to low-voltage control apparatus, is mainly used to control motors in electric drive systems, has the characteristics of high operating frequency and long life, and has the advantages of accurate and reliable operation and small size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes an arc chute, main contacts, a core and a coil; the coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin and has the characteristic of passing direct current and blocking alternating current; a fault of the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor failing to start. Contactor maintenance applies to contactors, and circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch, used for auxiliary control, and also used for self-locking of control circuits, signal indication and interlock protection; in the forward rotation control of a motor, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to achieve self-locking of the contactor coil.

The ship's power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, controlled phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 circuit breaker, ship's power grid and shore power box; the ship's power grid belongs to the ship's power station, and the main switchboard includes the main switch. The brushed synchronous generator includes the excitation system; the brushless synchronous generator is one of the main generator types adopted on ships, comes with a rotating-armature exciter and a rotating rectifier, has no brush and slip ring structure, and is listed together with the brushed synchronous generator as one of the two main generator forms currently adopted on ships; internally it includes the coaxially rotating main generator excitation winding, exciter armature winding and rotating rectifier device. The daily maintenance and upkeep of the generator applies to the brushless synchronous generator; the maintenance of the excitation system applies to the excitation system. The excitation system provides excitation current for the synchronous generator and includes brushed, brushless and thyristor forms; common forms include uncontrolled phase compound excitation, controlled phase compound excitation, thyristor excitation and brushless excitation voltage regulation systems; its maintenance cycle is once every half year, and the insulation resistance value is required to be not less than 1MΩ.

The wattmeter, also called a power meter, is used to measure electrical power; it is composed of a current coil and a voltage coil, and calculates power by detecting the load current and voltage. The wattmeter contains a current coil and a voltage coil; the multimeter uses voltage and current, and the clamp-on ammeter uses current. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems. The measurable quantity of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools include the multimeter and the voltmeter;

The text symbol corresponding to the fuse in a circuit diagram is FU, and its function is overload protection and short circuit protection; it is a safety electrical appliance that, when overload and short circuit occur in the power grid or electrical equipment, automatically cuts off the circuit by melting the fuse element. The fuse belongs to the class of distribution electrical appliances and has the characteristics of maintaining thermal stability and dynamic stability when a short circuit fault occurs; the RL93 series is of the screw type, voltage 380V, current 6~600A, used for circuit overload or short circuit protection. The circuit breaker is a switching electrical appliance used in the ship's power system to protect the circuit; it belongs to the class of low-voltage distribution electrical appliances and is divided into the frame type (air type) and the molded-case type, having both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and dynamic stability during a short circuit fault; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid.

The marine motor contains a winding;

Setting principles of generator overload protection: when the generator output power or current exceeds its rated value, it is defined as motor overload. In a ship's power station, motor overload is the direct cause that triggers the overload protection action, and its setting value must match the permissible heating characteristics of the generator. For a generator not equipped with an automatic stepwise unloading device, when the current reaches 125%~135% of the rated current, the protection device should trip after a delay of 15~30s; for a generator equipped with an automatic stepwise unloading device, since part of the non-important loads can be cut off first, its overload capacity is correspondingly increased, and when the current reaches 150% of the rated current, the protection device should trip after a delay of 10~20s. The above two sets of values are the basic basis for adjusting the overload protection delay and operating current, and they must not be changed arbitrarily during setting.

The actuating element of overload protection is the trip unit in the circuit breaker. The undervoltage protection of the ship's generator is realized by the undervoltage release in the circuit breaker, and the external short circuit protection of the generator is realized by the overcurrent trip unit in the circuit breaker. The main switch, as the air circuit breaker controlling the connection between the generator and the power grid, is mainly composed of an undervoltage release, a shunt release, an overcurrent protection device, an arc extinguishing device, auxiliary contacts, and a control and signal indication circuit. The DW14 circuit breaker adopts technology introduced from Japan's Terasaki; its additional AOJ-1s overcurrent trip unit is installed on the upper right side of the front of the circuit breaker. During adjustment, first confirm the installation position and adjustable parts of the trip unit, and then determine the setting value according to the generator long-time-delay trip current.

Setting of the priority trip overcurrent relay: the operating current setting value of the priority trip overcurrent relay is based on the long-time-delay setting current of the generator overload protection. Its delay is usually set to less than 15s, for example 5~10s. This delay is shorter than the long-time delay of the generator overload protection, so that part of the non-important loads is cut off before the generator reaches the tripping condition, avoiding the generator tripping due to overload.

There are clear provisions for the stepwise sequence of load shedding by priority trip. The mooring winch is usually listed as the first-stage non-important load for priority trip load shedding. The mooring winch belongs to the category of deck machinery such as the electric windlass, and is divided into DC and AC types; its drive control scheme is generally the same as the ship's electric cargo winch control scheme. At present, AC three-speed windlasses, mooring winches, or windlasses and mooring winches of the G-M system are mostly used, and the drive control systems of the two are basically the same. In the load shedding stepwise sequence of priority trip for container ships, the refrigerated container power supply is usually listed as the second-stage load to be cut off, and the first stage is non-important loads such as machine repair tools and kitchen equipment. The electrical control system of refrigerated containers has developed from the relay type to the microcomputer control type; the temperature adjustment range inside the container is generally within ±30℃, with high constant-temperature accuracy, and it has functions such as electric heating, automatic unloading, and automatic control of the number of condenser fans; when the temperature inside the container is lower than the setting value, electric heating can be carried out, and unloading operation can be automatically carried out according to the size of the heat load, and the number of condenser fans can be automatically controlled according to the external environment and the condenser pressure.

Refrigerated containers include the work content of refrigerated container electrical control system maintenance; their power supply is listed as the second priority trip level, meaning that when the generator is overloaded this load will be cut off before the loads after the first level.

Setting of reverse power protection The reverse power relay is used to detect and protect against reverse power and is one of the commonly used control and protection devices on the ship's main switchboard. The setting value for the diesel engine prime mover is 8% to 15% of rated power, with a delay of 3 to 10 s before operation. For the GG-21 induction-type relay, the starting value of the moving contact differs from the actual contact value; adjustment should be based on the actual contact value. Electronic relays have an operation indicator lamp and a delayed output trip indication function, and the indicator lamp can be used to judge the operating state. One cause of reverse power relay failure is incorrect wiring as required; another cause is a burnt-out voltage coil or current coil, in which case the relay does not function.

Therefore, before setting, check whether the wiring is correct and confirm whether the voltage coil and current coil are intact.

Coordination of measuring instruments and transformers Voltage is a measurable performance, and its measuring tool is a multimeter or voltmeter. Current is likewise a measurable performance, and its measuring tool is a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. A clamp-on ammeter contains a current transformer and can measure current without breaking the circuit. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA; its function is to transform the current ratio, the secondary current is 5 A, and its types include the coil type, busbar type and through-type; the through-type current transformer is one type of current transformer, characterized by one end of the secondary side being earthed. The primary terminals of the current transformer are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary terminals by K1 and K2; in operation it is equivalent to a short-circuited transformer, and the secondary winding must never be open-circuited during operation.

The wattmeter, also called the power meter, consists of a current coil and a voltage coil, and its function is to measure electric power. The wattmeter contains a current coil and also contains a voltage coil. The current coil is connected in series between the power supply and the load to detect the circuit current, and the voltage coil is connected in parallel across the circuit under test to detect the voltage, with an additional resistor connected in series in its branch. The function of the voltage coil is to detect voltage, and its connection mode is parallel. The current coil and voltage coil are marked with corresponding terminals, and during measurement the currents of the two coils must flow in or out from these terminals at the same time. The voltage range of the wattmeter is achieved by connecting additional resistors of different resistance values in series with the voltage coil. In the on-site adjustment of generator protection parameters, it is often necessary to use the above instruments to check the voltage and current readings to judge whether the setting values are appropriate.

Basic steps of fault diagnosis and circuit breaker maintenance The conventional fault diagnosis method uses observation. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part condition, conductor condition and equipment operating parameters; specifically, check whether parts are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt out. This step belongs to the sub-link of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site unchanged".

Circuit breaker maintenance applies to circuit breakers. A circuit breaker is a switching device used in the ship's power system to protect circuits; it belongs to low-voltage distribution devices, is divided into the frame type and the device type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. Air circuit breakers are mostly used as generator main switches and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breakers may suffer faults such as the contacts of a manually operated circuit breaker failing to close, the contacts of an electrically operated circuit breaker failing to close, one phase's contacts failing to close, and the shunt trip unit failing to trip the circuit breaker. The trip unit is the electrical component in a circuit breaker used to realize protection functions such as overload, short circuit and undervoltage and to drive the contacts to open; there is a close coordination relationship between the circuit breaker and the trip unit.

Inspection of related components: the contactor contains a coil. The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC. A fault in the KM coil is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked.

A potentiometer is also called a potentiometer; the volume potentiometer on electronic equipment is this type of component, and it is generally considered manually adjustable. A potentiometer has three pins, among which the resistance between two pins is fixed, and the resistance between the third pin and either pin changes as the shaft rotates. In automatic boiler combustion regulation, the potentiometer R1 driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R10 form a bridge balance; the automatic oil-fired boiler contains a potentiometer, whose purpose is for bridge balance; when the boiler steam pressure changes, the bridge formed by the potentiometer R driven by the pressure regulator YBD and the feedback potentiometer R' driven by the motor M is balanced.

The ship's power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system; the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks, and its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. The ship's power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase-compound voltage regulation system, controlled phase-compound voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 type circuit breaker, ship's power network and shore power box. The main switchboard contains the main switch, and the main switch belongs to the undervoltage release, shunt release, overcurrent protection device, arc extinguishing device, auxiliary contact and control and signal indication circuit. The ship's power network belongs to the ship's power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the ship's power station.

When a DC motor is overloaded, the current per unit area of the brush is large, causing difficulty in commutation and resulting in excessive sparking under brush, that is, motor overload leads to excessive sparking under brush. During standalone operation, starting a large load such as an air compressor, or starting a large load without observing the power, can easily cause the generator to trip due to overload. In the AC three-speed electric windlass, when the rated current of the high-speed winding reaches 110%, the current relay picks up. These phenomena are interrelated with the verification of the setting values, and when adjusting protection parameters, the instrument readings and component states should be checked together.

Signal input and command output of the automatic control system of the main diesel generator set: the automatic control system of the main diesel generator set takes the controller as its core, and on its exterior are provided input terminals numbered 1 to 17 and output terminals numbered 18 to 32; these wiring terminals are metal contact components that connect wires to equipment or circuit nodes, and are commonly found in PLC interfaces, instruments and control circuits. The electric engine telegraph system contains wiring terminals; in the engine telegraph system, poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals is one of the common faults of electrical components, so inspection of this type of terminal should be a fixed item of daily maintenance. The diesel generator set controller receives fault signals through specifically numbered input terminals, among which the overspeed fault signal is input from terminal 10 of the controller to execute immediate shutdown, the low lubricating oil pressure and high cooling water temperature faults correspond to input terminals 13 and 14 respectively, and the automatic start command is input from controller terminal 2, with the contact closed to connect to the negative power supply.

The input terminal is an electrical connection component in PLCs and controllers used to receive external signals or power input; in the PLC equivalent circuit, the input terminal cooperates with the COM terminal to form the input circuit interface.

As for the output terminal, in the automatic control of the diesel generator set, output terminal 20 energizes and actuates the coil of the running signal intermediate relay K₂, and during automatic start, output terminal 18 outputs the start command to energize the coil of the start output intermediate relay K₃. The output terminal is an electrical interface component in PLCs and controllers used to connect external loads or receive input signals; in the PLC equivalent circuit it is located between COM and the load, corresponding to the external contacts of output coils such as Y31-Y32. The harsh environment on board is likewise likely to cause rusting of wiring heads and terminals, resulting in poor contact, which must be cleaned promptly. To determine whether the output terminal is normal, measure the continuity between the terminal and COM after the corresponding command is issued; if the command has been issued but the load does not operate, the terminal contact problem should be ruled out first, and then the load itself should be checked.

The intermediate relay is used for control or protection in the ship's power system and is a type of electromagnetic relay. Its construction is similar to that of the contactor, and it is used to expand contact capacity and the number of contact pairs and for control logic conversion. Its fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the maintenance method of the contactor. In the automatic control of the diesel generator set, the K3 coil is energized and actuates to connect the starting solenoid valve, and the K4 coil is energized and actuates to connect the stopping solenoid valve. When checking the intermediate relay, confirm whether there is the specified voltage across the coil and whether the contacts can close and open reliably; burning of the coil or erosion of the contacts will prevent the start and stop commands from being transmitted to the solenoid valve. The solenoid valve is used to control the on-off of fuel; at ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation circuit and fuel enters the nozzle for injection. The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve, and its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the coil to prevent high voltage from being generated when the power is cut off and to accelerate discharge; when servicing the solenoid valve, in addition to checking the coil, also check whether the freewheeling diode is broken down or open-circuited, and whether the valve core moves flexibly.

Measuring instruments and fault detection: in the troubleshooting process, the multimeter is a commonly used tool; the multimeter contains a changeover switch and uses resistance and current for measurement. The changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts; on the main switchboard it is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands, and its functions include selecting the measurement object and selecting the range. A changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited; during operation it must not be left in the intermediate position, nor may the range be changed arbitrarily under load. The AC ammeter internally is a low-resistance current element and leads out two non-polarized terminals externally; the connections may be interchanged, so polarity need not be distinguished when wiring, but reliable contact should be ensured.

The sensor is the information acquisition device of the ship's monitoring and control system and is divided into two major categories: analog and switching-value sensors. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control the compensating motion when the ship pitches and rolls; the control platform contains sensors. The analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously varying electrical signals and are suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. The inspection of sensors should be carried out in conjunction with their output signals; for analog sensors, focus on verifying whether the output electrical signal corresponds to the measured parameter, and for switching-value sensors, focus on verifying whether the actuation value is within the specified range.

Monitoring and handling of power supply faults: the overspeed controller is powered by the battery, and when K6 detects a power failure it sends a power supply fault signal to the system. A power supply fault will cause the RUN lamp to go out, and correspondingly check the power supply. A power supply fault is an electrical supply abnormality that causes motor overheating, PLC control system faults and main engine remote control failure; in AC electric drive systems, a power supply fault is one of the direct causes of motor overcurrent and hence overheating; in the PLC control system, because the switching inverter power supply is prone to faults and difficult to repair, the ship usually adopts the strategy of overall replacement. When handling a power supply fault, first confirm whether the battery voltage and the supply circuit are normal, then check K6 and the related monitoring links; when the RUN lamp goes out, switch to checking the power supply, and avoid repeatedly starting the generator set under abnormal supply conditions.

Composition of the ship's power station and precautions for connecting shore power. The ship's power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system; the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks, and its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. The ship's power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, controlled phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14-type circuit breaker, ship's power network and shore power box, among which the ship's power network belongs to the ship's power station. The precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the relevant requirements of the ship's power station; when switching between the shore power box and the ship's power network, the voltage, frequency and phase sequence should be checked, and it should be confirmed that the DW14-type circuit breaker and the relevant protection links are in normal state before operation, so as to prevent the safe operation of the various voltage regulation systems and generators in the ship's power station from being affected by inconsistent power supply parameters.

The ship's power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system; the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks. From the perspective of basic responsibilities, the ship's power station must ensure reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur, and therefore it includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, controlled phase-compound excitation voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14-type circuit breaker, ship's power network and shore power box and other constituent parts. Among these, the ship's power network belongs to the ship's power station in terms of attribution, that is to say, the ship's power network is a constituent part inside the ship's power station, undertaking the tasks of power transmission and distribution. The precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the ship's power station, that is, in the operational step of connecting shore power, what needs to be attended to and noted is precisely the ship's power station itself, including its voltage, frequency, phase sequence and the connection relationship between the shore power box and the ship's power network; only by focusing the points of attention on the ship's power station can it be ensured that no abnormality occurs on the power station side during the shore power connection process.

The main switchboard is the control center for the concentration and distribution of electrical energy in the power station; it includes subsystems such as the busbar system, generator measurement and monitoring unit, paralleling circuit and load transfer circuit, and the main switchboard also includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter. In terms of function, the main switchboard can connect or disconnect circuits, issue alarms when protection devices operate, detect and display various electrical parameters, and can regulate the voltage and frequency of the power station as well as the active and reactive power of generator sets operating in parallel. The main switchboard occupies a core position in the composition of the ship's power station; the ship's power station includes the main switchboard, and the main switchboard in turn includes the main switch and the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter, forming a clearly layered control and protection system.

When reading drawings, the main switch is the component in the main switchboard that undertakes the making and breaking and protection of the generator main circuit, while the switchboard-type insulation resistance meter is used to directly monitor the insulation condition of the power network on the switchboard; the two respectively correspond to the making and breaking control of electrical energy and the detection of insulation state, and are the two types of components that must first be located when reading the circuit diagrams of the main switchboard.

In terms of protective electrical apparatus, RS is the electrical equipment used for overload and short circuit protection in the ship's electrical power system; specifically, RS is a fuse series used for short circuit and overload protection of devices such as semiconductor rectifiers or thyristor rectifiers, among which the RS_0 type has a rated voltage of 250 to 900V and current specifications of 30 to 480A, and the RS_0 type is used for short circuit protection of semiconductor rectifiers or their complete sets. The generator paralleling circuit of the main switchboard includes the protective element FU;

In the AC voltage measuring circuit, the voltmeter is connected directly across two phases of the line through FU.

Voltage is one of the measurable quantities; its measuring tools include the multimeter and the voltmeter, and the multimeter uses voltage as the quantity to be measured. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments and is used to understand equipment status; measuring current requires an ammeter, connected in series after breaking the circuit; motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems.

The multimeter contains a measuring circuit, whose function is to convert different electrical quantities and to convert different ranges. The measuring circuit is the part inside the multimeter used to convert different electrical quantities and ranges into signals measurable by the meter head, and it is also one of the three basic components of the MF-30 and MF-47 analog multimeters. Since the magnetoelectric meter head can only pass microampere-level current, a conversion circuit is needed to measure different electrical quantities and ranges, and this is precisely the significance of the measuring circuit. When reading multimeter-related circuits, the measuring circuit should be regarded as the intermediate link connecting the meter head and the measured quantity; its conversion objects include both the type of electrical quantity and the range position.

The contactor is an electrical device used to control the motor in the ship's power system, belongs to ship low-voltage control apparatus, is mainly used to control the motor in electric drive systems, and has the characteristics of high operating frequency and long life, while also being accurate and reliable in operation, high in operating frequency, long in life and small in size. Contactors are used in large quantities on ships, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. The contactor includes the arc chute, main contact, core and coil, and contactor maintenance applies to the contactor as the object. The circuit breaker is a switching apparatus used to protect the circuit in the ship's power system, belongs to ship distribution apparatus, is divided into frame type (air type) and molded-case type, and has both switching and protection functions; the circuit breaker belongs to low-voltage distribution apparatus and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during a short circuit fault; the air circuit breaker is mostly used as the generator main switch and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker as the object. In the switchboard circuit diagram, the contactor's arc chute, main contact, core and coil correspond respectively to different graphic symbols and wiring terminals; the main contact is connected in series in the motor main circuit, the coil is connected in the control circuit, and the core and arc chute are structural components; the circuit breaker appears in the generator main circuit or distribution branch in its different forms as frame type or molded-case type, and when reading the diagram, its operating function as a switch and its tripping function as a protective apparatus should be distinguished.

A wiring terminal is a metal contact component used in an electrical system to connect wires to equipment or circuit nodes, and is commonly found in PLC interfaces, instruments and control circuits. In the synchronizing and paralleling panel of the main switchboard, the SYNS module contains multiple wiring terminals used to connect synchronizing, control and feedback signals. The electric-type main engine remote control system contains wiring terminals; in the main engine remote control system, poor contact or corrosion of wiring terminals is one of the common faults of electrical components. The AC ammeter internally is a low-resistance current element and leads out two non-polarized wiring terminals externally, so the connections can be exchanged. When reading diagrams, wiring terminals often appear in the form of numbers or a terminal block; the synchronizing, control and feedback signals of the SYNS module all enter and leave through these terminals, so the correspondence of the terminals is an important basis for checking whether the circuit connections are correct.

The circuit breaker may exhibit various fault symptoms during operation. The circuit breaker may exhibit the symptom that when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contact cannot close; this symptom occurs on occasions when the circuit breaker is operated manually, and in diagnosis it should first be confirmed whether the operating mechanism is in place, and then the contact and related transmission parts should be checked. The circuit breaker may exhibit the symptom that when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contact cannot close; this symptom occurs on occasions when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, and in diagnosis it should first be confirmed whether the operating power supply and the control circuit are normal, and then the electric operating mechanism and the contact should be checked.
