In addition, the circuit breaker may also exhibit the following: one phase contact cannot close; the shunt trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open; the undervoltage trip unit cannot make the circuit breaker open; the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor; the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1 h after closing; the undervoltage trip unit has noise; the circuit breaker temperature rise is too high; the auxiliary switch fails;

The semiconductor overcurrent trip unit malfunctions, causing the circuit breaker to open. These fault symptoms cover the abnormal manifestations of the circuit breaker in multiple aspects such as manual and electric operation, single-phase contact, shunt trip, undervoltage trip, motor starting, delayed opening after closing, noise, temperature rise, auxiliary switch, and semiconductor overcurrent trip unit, and are content that needs to be identified in combination with the circuit structure during the circuit diagram reading training of the actual ship switchboard. When reading the circuits related to the circuit breaker, the shunt trip unit, undervoltage trip unit, auxiliary switch, and semiconductor overcurrent trip unit should be respectively mapped to the control circuit, protection circuit, and signal circuit in the diagram, so that when the above phenomena occur, the order of inspection and the components involved can be determined according to the circuit routing.

The circuit diagram reading training of the actual ship switchboard must ultimately land on the identification of specific circuits and components. The SYNS module in the synchronizing and paralleling panel of the main switchboard is provided with multiple terminals inside, and the synchronizing signals, control signals, and feedback signals are all connected in or led out through these terminals.

When reading the current measuring circuit, the current transformer is inevitably encountered. The text symbol corresponding to the current transformer is TA, and its function is to transform the current ratio; the standard current on the secondary side is 5A, the primary side terminals are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary side by K1 and K2. Distinguished by structure, current transformers include the coil type, busbar type, and through type, and the through-type current transformer is one type of current transformer. The current transformer has the nature of a current source and, when working, is equivalent to a short-circuit transformer; one end of the secondary side is earthed, and the secondary winding must strictly not be open-circuited during operation. The clamp-on ammeter contains a current transformer inside; the clamp-on ammeter is used to measure current, and the circuit need not be disconnected during measurement.

Resistance, voltage, and current are the three electrical quantities most frequently read in switchboard commissioning and fault finding. The multimeter is used to measure resistance and can measure the resistance value; the multimeter is also used to measure voltage and can measure the voltage value, and the voltmeter can likewise measure voltage; the multimeter is also used to measure current and can measure the current value, and the ammeter and clamp-on ammeter are also tools for measuring current.

When measuring the resistance in the measuring circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring the resistance, and never measure with the power on.

Insulation detection occupies an independent position in the switchboard circuit diagram. Measuring the insulation resistance is used to check the insulation performance of electrical equipment, and is often carried out after major overhaul of the equipment or after shutdown during operation, and is also one of the mandatory inspection and test items for acceptance after the motor is newly installed or overhauled. In the maintenance of the contactor, it is necessary to measure the insulation resistance between the contacts, between the coil and the core, and between the live parts and earth. The E23 type ohmmeter is connected to F440 PNL and F220 PNL through wiring to realize insulation detection of systems of different voltage levels.

The ship power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 type circuit breaker, ship power grid, and shore power box, among which the ship power grid is a component of the ship power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the relevant states of the ship power station.

When reading the diagram, several faults and treatment measures related to the generator and circuit breaker will also be encountered. Corrosion and blackening of the generator slip ring causing non-conduction is one of the common fault causes; the generator slip ring is used to transfer current, the brush braid is the conductor connecting the brush, and the linear reactor is used to regulate current. For the above situations, the coil can be checked and repaired or replaced with a new one; for the trip mechanism, the tripping mechanism can be checked, and the corresponding bolt adjusted or replaced; for the wiring, the wiring and connections can be checked, and the screws connected or tightened; for the spring and electromagnetic mechanism, the spring tension can be checked and reduced, or the electromagnetic attraction increased or the spring reaction force reduced.

Maintenance personnel are the personnel responsible for fault diagnosis and repair of marine electrical equipment; they must be very familiar with the ship-wide electrical equipment circuits, operating principles and the locations of all components, and must also be familiar with the structure and operating principles of the electrical equipment as well as the functions and installation positions of the components (assemblies). In traditional fault diagnosis, maintenance personnel need to understand the fault symptom and make a preliminary judgment through the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling; this method requires maintenance personnel to have sufficient perceptual knowledge of the normal state and abnormal state of the equipment. As commonly used living equipment on ships, the elevator consists of the traction machine, car, landing door and electrical control system, and its regular maintenance is a necessary condition for ensuring safe operation. Maintenance personnel should check the main safety facilities and electrical control part of the elevator every week, and technical inspection should be organized after the elevator has been in use for one year; generally a comprehensive disassembly, cleaning and inspection should be carried out once every 3 to 5 years, with the specific period depending on how new or old the equipment is.

the switch at the corresponding position should be disconnected; when working in the machine room, the main power switch should be disconnected; when working on the car top, the inspection switch should be closed; when working in the pit, the emergency stop switch of the pit inspection button box should be disconnected, or the safety switch of the speed governor tensioning device should be disconnected at the same time; the operation should be carried out jointly by the person in charge and the assistant, and the cooperating personnel must strictly obey instructions; it is strictly prohibited to stand outside the hoistway and lean into the hoistway, or to stand with one foot inside and one foot outside the car sill for a long time during repair. These regulations are aimed at the safety protection of personnel and equipment during repair and maintenance operations, and their applicable objects include both the person in charge of the operation and the assistant cooperating in the operation; the two must act in coordination, and neither party may change the operating steps without authorization. The purpose of hanging the inspection/out-of-service indication sign is to make users at each landing clearly know that the elevator is in a non-use state, so as to avoid mistaken entry or misoperation;

The regulations on the use of the insulation resistance tester during elevator repair and maintenance clearly stipulate: the hand-cranked insulation resistance tester is prohibited, and a battery-type high-voltage insulation resistance tester should be used, with a voltage of 500V and an internal resistance of more than 200kΩ. The insulation resistance tester, also called the megohmmeter, consists of a hand-cranked generator and a moving-coil ratio meter, is provided with three terminal posts L, E and G, and is divided according to the highest voltage emitted by the hand-cranked generator into specifications such as 100V, 200V, 500V, 1000V and 2500V, and is used to measure the insulation resistance of electrical equipment, circuits and cables. In elevator repair and maintenance, the battery-type high-voltage insulation resistance tester is selected to avoid the inconvenience and safety hazards brought by hand-cranked instruments during operation. During measurement, the three terminal posts L, E and G are connected respectively according to the measurement object, among which the G terminal post is used to eliminate the influence of surface leakage current; the specified 500V voltage level and internal resistance of more than 200kΩ are the basic conditions for ensuring that the measurement results can reflect the insulation condition of the elevator electrical part, and instruments with an internal resistance lower than this or non-battery-type instruments do not meet the specified requirements.

The gap between the wedge block of the safety gear and the working surface of the guide rail is generally 3mm, and all gaps should be similar. The fitting rotating parts of the safety gear actuating rod should be coated with mechanical lubricating oil once every two months, and the rolling or sliding parts of the clamp jaw need to be coated with lithium-based grease for lubrication and rust prevention. After stopping the machine, the actuating rod must be manually toggled to check whether the action is normal. When the elevator is out of control and the safety gear has not yet taken effect, passengers must not attempt to jump out of the car. Misoperation of the safety gear is a fault that requires immediately notifying maintenance personnel and stopping for inspection and repair. When inspecting the safety gear, the gap between the wedge block and the working surface of the guide rail is the key value for judging whether it can normally clamp the guide rail; 3mm is the general value, and all gaps should be similar, which requires the gaps on the left and right sides and at different positions to remain consistent, avoiding one side contacting first and asynchronous action due to uneven gaps. Once misoperation of the safety gear occurs, maintenance personnel must be notified immediately and it must be stopped for inspection and repair, and operation must not continue.

The action of the speed governor should be flexible and reliable, and its movement should be observed to be good. The rolling bearing of the speed governor should be inspected annually, and the wear of the speed governor wheel, wheel groove, shaft sleeve and shaft should be checked, and whether the centrifugal throwing head can rotate freely should be checked. When the rope wheel elongates beyond the specified range and cuts off the control circuit, the rope wheel should be shortened; when the speed governor wire rope is severely worn, it should be replaced, with the same requirements as the traction wire rope. The inspection cycle and items of the speed governor have different emphases: the rolling bearing is inspected once a year, and the inspection content includes the wear of the speed governor wheel, wheel groove, shaft sleeve and shaft, as well as whether the centrifugal throwing head can rotate freely; these parts respectively undertake the functions of supporting the rope wheel, guiding the wire rope, rotating fit and overspeed triggering, and wear or jamming at any one place will affect the flexible and reliable action of the speed governor.

In electrical measurement, the multimeter can be used to measure resistance and voltage. When measuring resistance in a measuring circuit, at least one end of the measured resistor must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply must be cut off; if capacitance exists in the circuit, it should be discharged before measuring resistance, and never measure with power on. In the fault of generator no-load voltage high, an open shunt resistor will cause the voltage corrector to have no main regulating effect.

Ship power station is the heart of the ship's power system, and the reliability and vitality of its work are important signs of the effectiveness of the system in achieving specified tasks. Its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination after faults. The ship power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrollable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, controllable phase compound excitation voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 type circuit breaker, ship power grid and shore power box. The ship power grid is a component of the ship power station, and the precautions for connecting shore power need to pay attention to the relevant requirements of the ship power station.

Traction machine maintenance work must be carried out by professional, trained personnel, and some inspection items need to be carried out while the elevator is running, so maintenance personnel must pay attention to personal safety. The outer surface of the traction machine should be kept clean to prevent dust and dirt accumulation, and the working surfaces of the brake wheel and traction wheel should be regularly wiped with clean cotton waste. The brake should be inspected regularly, adjusted and replaced in time if necessary, and note that the temperature rise of the electromagnetic coil must not exceed 90K. The wear of the traction wheel should also be inspected regularly; when the height difference of the wire rope due to uneven wear of the grooves of the traction wheel is greater than 1/10 of the diameter, the rope grooves need to be repaired to a consistent depth; when the groove wear makes the gap between the wire rope and the groove bottom less than 1mm, the traction wheel should be re-machined or replaced. When re-machining the traction wheel, note that the rim thickness below the cut must not be less than the wire rope diameter. The traction wheel is a component of the traction machine, and its working surface needs to be regularly wiped with clean cotton waste to prevent dust and dirt.

For traction machine lubrication, it is recommended to use Shell Omala 460 or Lanzhou Refining and Chemical Kunlun 34# (460) and other elevator-specific gear oils of corresponding viscosity.

When adding lubricating oil, fill to the center of the oil sight glass; too little will cause lubrication difficulty, while too much will cause oil leakage. When using mineral oil, perform the first oil change after the new machine has accumulated about 400 h of operation; when using synthetic oil, perform the first oil change after the new machine has accumulated about 700 h of operation. For mineral oil, subsequently change it every 2000–3000 h, and no longer than 12–18 months; for synthetic oil, subsequently change it every 3000–4000 h, and no longer than 24–36 months.

The surface roughness of the brake wheel must be no less than 3.2, and it must be protected from oil contamination, rain, and ice and snow. The steady-state working temperature of the brake wheel should be less than 180°C, but in actual operation the surface temperature may exceed 100°C. The opening and closing gap between the brake wheel and the arc surface of the brake shoe should be maintained at 0.1–0.3 mm to avoid friction.

The daily inspection criterion is that the surface has no oil contamination or other debris; if it does not meet this, the adhered matter must be removed. When measuring the brake lining thickness, hold the steel ruler perpendicular to the arc surface of the brake wheel; the distance is the brake lining thickness.

Uneven height at guide rail joints will cause running vibration, which is easily confused with electrical system faults. Add lubricating oil to the automatic lubrication device once a week, using No. 100 refined mineral oil. When the working surface wear of the sliding guide rail liner reaches 1 mm, it should be replaced. When the guide rail surface is rough or the surface is damaged by safety gear braking, it must be smoothed before use. Check the guide rails annually for deformation and looseness, and tighten the pressure plate, joint, and bracket bolts. Interviewing the operator is the step preceding observation, and observation is the step preceding checking the monitoring and indicating device. A multimeter can be used to measure resistance and current; an ammeter or clamp-on ammeter can also be used to measure current. A contactor includes the coil as one of its components.

Bearing fault, lubrication fault, and installation fault all cause bearing overheating. Bearing overheating corresponds to three troubleshooting directions: checking for bearing fault, checking the lubrication condition, and checking the installation condition; checking for bearing fault and checking the lubrication condition both require the bearing. Bearing damage will cause low speed under load, abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, and bearing overheating. Insufficient lubricating oil and impurities can also cause bearing overheating. If the bearing is damaged or the lubricating oil contains impurities, the measure of replacing the bearing is usually taken. Generator bearing overheating corresponds to replacing the bearing. When the traction motor has abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, bearing damage is a possible cause, and the damaged bearing must be replaced. Disappearance of noise during no-load operation indicates poor coupling installation; if the noise persists and is accompanied by vibration, it points to a shaft or bearing fault. When an upper bearing fault causes motor overheating, it is usually accompanied by very loud uneven noise and overheating of the bearing end cover.

Poor earthing will cause the motor casing to become live; damp windings, damaged insulation, or dirt on the terminal board will also cause the motor casing to become live; worn insulation on the lead-out wires will likewise cause the motor casing to become live. For the fault of the motor casing becoming live, the handling direction is to find the cause and take corresponding measures to correct it; it also corresponds to the maintenance procedure group of drying the stator winding, repairing when the insulation is damaged, and cleaning dirt from the terminal board. For damp windings, dry the stator winding; for damaged insulation, repair it; for dirt on the terminal board, clean the dirt from the terminal board. When handling a fault caused by damaged insulation adhesive on the motor lead-out wires, repair or replace the lead-out wires. The ship's power grid is part of the ship's power station. The precautions for shore connection power supply must pay attention to the relevant requirements of the ship's power station.

In ship power station equipment, bearing replacement is used to address overheating caused by bearing damage or impurities in the lubricating oil. The measurable property of a resistor is resistance, and the measuring tool is a multimeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools include a multimeter, an ammeter and a clamp-on ammeter. To measure current, an ammeter must be used, connected in series after the circuit is disconnected. Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems. The insulation resistance tester internally contains two measuring coils, a voltage circuit and a current circuit, and the accuracy of their relative positions must be checked. The terminal screws of an electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact; if the external terminal screws of a thermal relay are not tightened, the main circuit will not be connected. A KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start.

Welding is a process in which solder is melted by heating, atomic diffusion occurs between the workpiece and the solder, and after solidification an alloy bonding layer with good electrical conductivity and mechanical strength is formed; welding quality directly affects the performance of electronic products.

The brake wheel is the friction pair component in the elevator traction machine brake; when the brake shoe presses tightly against its circumferential surface, braking torque is generated. In the electromagnet brake-shoe type brake, when power is cut off, spring tension forces the brake shoe to press tightly against the brake wheel to brake.

The brake shoe is the component in the brake that achieves braking or release by friction against the brake wheel, and its wear amount must be less than 2mm. For all models of traction machines, the tightness wear amount of the brake shoe should be less than 2mm; if it exceeds the standard, the brake shoe or brake arm must be replaced. In the brake-released state, the gap between the two arc surfaces of the brake shoe and the brake wheel should be maintained at 0.1～0.3mm.

The surface of the brake shoe must not have oil stains or other debris; otherwise the contamination must be removed or the brake shoe replaced. When adjusting the brake shoe, adjust the lower screw so that it just presses against the flat surface of the brake shoe, then turn it counterclockwise 30° to leave a gap. Before measuring the brake lining thickness, the main power supply must be cut off and it must be confirmed that the brake has been de-energized and engaged, to prevent a runaway car accident. The brake lining is a component of the brake shoe.

Brake system maintenance includes several specific items. When checking the brake-release gap, the gap should be less than 0.5mm; when checking the brake wheel, the surface of the brake wheel must not have any oil stains or other debris; when checking the brake shoe, the surface of the brake lining must not have any oil stains or other debris; when checking the brake shoe, the cumulative wear amount of the brake lining for all models of traction machines should be less than 2mm; when checking the brake, the specified state of the brake should be ensured when the brake is closed. The daily maintenance items of the brake are required to be carried out by the customer, and all friction surfaces of the brake must not be contaminated with oil stains.

Before adjusting the brake system, the corresponding safety measures must be implemented. The elevator must be driven at slow speed to the upper terminal station and be in an empty-load state, and the car must be placed symmetrically on the buffers and be in an empty-load state; after completing the above operations, the main power supply must be cut off. If this measure is not implemented, a runaway car accident may occur.

Safety measures during inspection and maintenance include: all maintenance work must be carried out with the elevator powered off, and it must be ensured that the elevator cannot start unexpectedly; during the brake system adjustment process, it must be ensured that no load torque is applied to the brake wheel or the motor; after maintenance is completed, it is necessary to check whether the interconnected locking components are locked, and operation may be resumed only after adjusting to sufficient braking torque; because the surface temperature of the brake may exceed 100℃, temperature-sensitive devices must not be routed through or fixed on the brake device.

The buffer is a safety component of the elevator, used to absorb the impact energy of the car or counterweight, including oil-pressure buffers and hydraulic buffers. The oil level of the oil-pressure buffer should be below 10℃, and the oil level height should be kept above the minimum oil level. Check the oil level and leakage of the oil-pressure buffer every two months, replenish the oil and tighten all bolts. The exposed surface of the plunger outer circle should be cleaned with gasoline and coated with anti-rust oil or buffer oil. Perform a plunger reset test once a year; the time required from release to returning to the free height should be less than 90s. Before adjusting the braking system, the empty elevator must be driven at slow speed to the upper terminal station and symmetrically placed on the buffers; before measuring the thickness of the brake shoe, the empty elevator must be symmetrically placed on the buffers and the main power supply cut off.

The rolling bearings of the speed governor should be inspected annually. This maintenance item of speed governor inspection requires: the action of the speed governor should be flexible and reliable, and its rolling bearings need to be inspected annually; the tensioning device of the speed governor must be kept working normally, and the reliability of the rope-break safety switch must be checked; check whether the rope-clamping brake iron is located exactly in the center.

The maintenance content of the inspection and adjustment of the car door and automatic door mechanism includes: regularly apply lithium-based grease to bearings such as the swing rod part, and clean once a year; adjustment of the transmission belt tension—if the transmission belt elongates during use, causing the tension to decrease and slip, the base adjusting screw of the motor can be adjusted to bring the belt to proper tension; the action of the safety touch panel and light curtain should be sensitive and reliable, and the collision force of the safety touch panel should not be greater than 5N.

When disassembling the brake, first remove the screws on the junction box, then remove the power line and microswitch line. The junction box is a component used in marine electrical systems to connect cables, protect wiring points and accommodate electrical elements. The general alarm device consists of a shutter, alarm bell, alarm lamp and junction box, etc. The solenoid valve of the paint room zone is not connected to the external junction box, but directly connected to the local control box.

The conventional fault diagnosis method uses the step of observation. The content of observation includes abnormal phenomena, part status, wire status, and equipment operating parameters. Observation belongs to the sub-link of the first step of conventional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while maintaining the site", and its content includes whether parts are stuck or damaged, and whether wires are loose, broken, scratched or burnt.

The contactor contains a core. The core is a component of marine electrical equipment and a magnetic conductive part in electromagnetic equipment, used to form the magnetic circuit, support the coil and serve as a reference point for insulation measurement. When measuring the insulation resistance of the coil of electrical equipment to ground, terminal post E of the insulation resistance tester can be connected to the core. In the through-type current transformer, the large current conductor under test is directly interlinked with the core to replace the primary winding.

The marine motor contains a bearing. The bearing is a mechanical component of the motor, used to support the rotation of the rotor; its fault will cause the motor to overheat, vibrate and produce abnormal noise. Bearing fault is one of the direct causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems, belonging to the branch of excessive mechanical resistance. The bearing is used when checking the bearing fault itself, and the bearing is also used when checking the lubrication condition. The ship power grid belongs to the ship power station. Precautions for shore power connection require attention to the ship power station.

Elevator maintenance work has clear periodic requirements. The regulations to be observed during elevator repair and maintenance cover weekly inspection, annual technical inspection, the cycle of complete disassembly, cleaning and inspection, and the inspection and trial run before re-commissioning after being out of service.

Guide rail and guide shoe inspection is an annual maintenance item. The guide rail device should be inspected once a year, mainly checking for deformation and looseness. Inspectors need to stand on the car top and proceed from top to bottom at slow speed. During inspection, all pressure plates, joints and bracket bolts must be tightened in sequence, and the welding parts must be checked for weld separation. Check whether all moving parts are loose; after stopping the machine, turn the actuating lever by hand to check whether the action is normal; after inspection, all structures should be restored to normal and the clearances at all parts measured.

Buffer inspection is carried out for the oil-hydraulic buffer.

The inspection of the mechanical and electrical interlock device of the landing door is carried out once a month, checking whether the conductive plate and contact have poor or false connection, whether the contact spring pressure can reset automatically, whether the riveting, welding and glued joints are loose, and whether the lock hook, arm and all rollers can rotate flexibly; lithium-based grease is applied to the bearing, and it should be cleaned once a year. The door suspension rollers are inspected once a month, and if wear and damage are found they should be replaced immediately; when the outer diameter of the door suspension roller is seriously worn, it should be replaced. Clean the electrical contacts to ensure good contact, and check and adjust the door ball, rotating parts and lock catch positioning. It is strictly forbidden to pry the landing door open by hand from the outside.

The traction wire rope inspection requires frequent checking and adjustment so that the tension of each traction rope is uniform, with an error less than 0.5% of the average value.

The traction rope should be replaced when any of the following conditions occurs: when broken wires are evenly distributed among the rope strands, the maximum number of broken wires in one lay exceeds 32; when broken wires are concentrated in one or two rope strands, the maximum number of broken wires in one lay exceeds 16; when the wires on the surface of the traction rope are significantly worn or corroded; when the diameter of the seriously worn traction rope is less than 90% of the original diameter. In addition, the length of the traction wire rope must be checked; the distance from the bottom of the counterweight beam to the surface of the hydraulic buffer must not be less than 150mm.

The inspection of the traveling cable includes: checking whether there are foreign objects in the hoistway in contact with the cable and whether the cable sheath is worn; checking whether the cable is twisted or biased to one side, and whether there is swaying or dragging on the ground during movement; when the car stops at the lowest floor, the cable is required to be more than 60mm above the hoistway floor.

The counterweight device inspection requires cleaning the counterweight device and checking whether the bolts at all parts are loose, checking the wear of the counterweight wheel rope grooves and adding an appropriate amount of lubricating grease, confirming whether the counterweight pressure plate fixing buckles are fastened, and checking whether the bolts of the adjusting blocks at the bottom of the counterweight frame are fastened. Hoistway cleaning requires removing garbage on the door head cover, garbage at the bottom of the hoistway, oil stains and accumulated water and other garbage at all parts that affect the machine's operating performance, and removing protruding obstacles in the hoistway that may collide with the car and counterweight.

The inspection of various conduits, trunking and junction boxes and wiring includes: checking whether the wiring of the car button box, car cable junction box, intermediate junction box and various control box wiring bases is loose, confirming the contact tightness of the power line, power switch contacts and motor wiring, and cleaning the wiring bases, checking whether each wiring base is corroded and missing wire number tags; checking whether the conduits, trunking and boxes in the equipment room, car top, car bottom and hoistway are loose or missing covers.

The transmission belt also needs attention in elevator maintenance; when the transmission belt elongates and causes tension reduction and slipping, the motor base screws need to be adjusted to tighten it.

Maintenance personnel should be familiar with the structure of electrical equipment, working principles, functions of components (assemblies) and their locations, master the methods of asking, looking, touching, listening and smelling, and must be very familiar with the whole ship's electrical equipment circuits, working principles and the locations of all components.

Elevator repair and maintenance work is carried out in layers by cycle.

From the perspective of equipment composition, the elevator includes components such as the traction sheave, brake wheel, brake shoe, speed governor, safety gear, guide rail, buffer, traction steel wire rope, traveling cable and counterweight device, and the condition of these components directly determines operational safety. During work, the elevator requires attention to the regulations that must be observed during elevator repair and maintenance; whenever entering the hoistway, car top or pit for work, power cut-off, tagging and the stationing of a supervisor shall be confirmed according to the specified procedures, and after the work is completed, restoration shall be carried out item by item. The elevator requires attention to the regulations on the use of the insulation resistance tester during elevator repair and maintenance; for measuring insulation resistance, a battery-type high-voltage insulation resistance tester shall be selected, with a range of 500V and an internal resistance of 200kΩ or more, and the hand-cranked type is prohibited, so as to avoid unstable output voltage affecting the judgment of readings. The elevator requires attention to the safety measures before adjusting the braking system; before adjustment, the car shall be placed in the specified position and reliably braked, to prevent the car from slipping during adjustment. The elevator requires attention to the safety measures before measuring the thickness of the brake lining; before measurement, braking and anti-slip measures shall likewise be implemented first, and then the brake shoe area shall be measured. The elevator requires attention to the safety measures during inspection and repair; the entire process of inspection and repair shall comply with the sequence requirements of power cut-off, voltage verification, supervision and restoration of power supply.

The specific maintenance items cover multiple aspects. The elevator includes traction machine maintenance and traction machine lubrication; the traction machine shall be inspected by cycle and lubrication shall be ensured in place; the elevator includes braking system maintenance, involving the matching condition of the brake wheel and brake shoe; the elevator includes speed governor inspection and safety gear inspection, and the two shall be confirmed in linkage for reliable action; the elevator includes car door and automatic door mechanism inspection and adjustment, to ensure smooth opening and closing of the doors; the elevator includes guide rail and guide shoe inspection, as well as buffer inspection, so that operational guidance and terminal protection are effective; the elevator includes landing door mechanical and electrical interlock device inspection, to prevent the car from running when the landing door is not closed; the elevator includes traction steel wire rope inspection and traveling cable inspection, with attention to wear and connection conditions; the elevator includes counterweight device inspection, to confirm its balance relationship with the car; the elevator also includes hoistway cleaning as well as inspection of various conduits, trunking and junction boxes and wiring conditions, to keep the hoistway tidy and the line connections reliable.

The traction motor fails to start, which is a fault symptom requiring item-by-item troubleshooting in control system maintenance of the elevator.

There are many causes of this phenomenon, and troubleshooting shall be carried out in order from simple to complex. The power supply not being connected is one of the possible causes; for the phenomenon of failure to start, the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts shall be checked to find the fault point, and the specific electrical connection fault point shall be located through the above inspection means. Incorrect wiring of the control equipment will likewise cause failure to start; for the phenomenon of failure to start, the wiring diagram shall be checked and corrections made. Undervoltage will also cause failure to start; the power supply voltage shall be checked, and if it is indeed too low, it shall be appropriately raised. Electrical faults such as stator winding short circuit to earth between phases, incorrect wiring and stator winding short circuit will also make the motor unable to start; for the phenomenon of failure to start, the short circuit and open circuit locations shall be found and repaired, and if the wiring is incorrect, the wiring shall be corrected. Excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer, are likewise causes of failure to start; during troubleshooting, reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer, and if the motor can run normally, the reducer part shall be checked. In addition, excessive load or the brake not being released can cause this fault; when the traction motor fails to start, if the load is excessive or the brake is not released, it belongs to this category; a stator winding short circuit in the traction motor will cause the motor to fail to start; incorrect wiring of the traction motor control equipment will cause the motor to fail to start; incorrect wiring of the stator winding is a possible cause of the traction motor failing to start, and the wiring diagram shall be checked and corrections made.

When the traction motor operates under load, various abnormalities may also occur. When the load is excessive, it will cause abnormal stator current, and at this time the operation of reducing the load shall be performed. Undervoltage or excessively low power supply voltage will cause abnormalities and overheating or smoking of the traction motor during load operation; the troubleshooting method is to directly check the power supply voltage and, after confirmation, appropriately raise it. If the power supply voltage is too low when the traction motor operates under load, troubleshooting shall be carried out through the step of checking the power supply voltage. If an abnormality occurs when the traction motor operates under load and the cause is excessively low power supply voltage, the voltage needs to be checked. Open welding of the guide bars and end rings of the traction motor will also cause faults during load operation; the end ring is the annular conductive component at the end of the cage rotor, which together with the cage bars forms the short circuit winding; a broken ring means that one or several places in the end ring are cracked, and cracking of the end ring of a cast aluminum rotor can generally be found by visual inspection. Undervoltage will also cause low speed during load operation; excessive load or the brake not being released, or a fault in the reducer, will likewise cause low speed during load operation.

When the traction motor operates with abnormal noise or excessive vibration, the causes and treatments differ. Mechanical friction is one possible cause; for the phenomenon of abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation, the air gap between rotor and stator and the clearance between brake wheel and brake band should be checked, the cause of rubbing found, and correction carried out. Two-phase operation can also cause this phenomenon; in this case the power should be cut off and then switched on again, and if the motor fails to start, one phase may be open-circuited, so check the power supply and the motor and repair them. Bearing damage is another cause, and the treatment is to replace the damaged bearing. A bent shaft extension can also cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration, and the treatment is to replace the shaft. Loose coupling connection likewise leads to this phenomenon, so the loose points must be checked and the coupling tightened. Excessive load may also cause abnormal noise or excessive vibration, so the stator current must be checked and the load reduced when overload is found. When abnormal noise or excessive vibration during operation is caused by excessive load, the load must be reduced; after reducing the load, the motor and the reduction gearbox can be separated to determine whether the fault originates from the reduction gearbox.

Excessive temperature rise or smoking of the traction motor may be caused by several reasons. Undervoltage leads to this result; short circuit to earth between phases of the stator winding, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit lead to this result; mechanical friction also leads to this result. In the traction motor, stator winding short circuit causes excessive temperature rise or smoking of the motor, and the treatment is to locate the short-circuited part and repair it. If excessive temperature rise or smoking of the traction motor is caused by undervoltage, the voltage must be checked and appropriately raised; when the temperature rise of the traction motor is too high or it smokes, if the cause is undervoltage, the maintenance procedure of checking the power supply voltage should be carried out.

In the measurement and inspection stage, voltage is a measurable performance, and its voltage value can be measured with a multimeter or voltmeter; current is likewise a measurable performance, and its current value can be measured with a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter. For the maintenance procedure of checking the power supply voltage, care must be taken to mark the circuit terminals before disassembly. Motor fails to start corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, motor speed low after starting corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, high temperature rise of the motor corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, and excessive sparking under brush also corresponds to checking the power supply voltage.

A winding is a coil component wound from enameled wire in a motor or transformer, used to produce a magnetic field or induce an electromotive force; the shaft is a mechanical transmission component used to transmit torque and rotary motion. Incorrect wiring causes the generator voltage to fail to build up normally.

In the braking device of an elevator, the brake wheel and the brake shoe form a friction pair, and the brake shoe gripping the circumferential surface of the brake wheel produces the braking torque.

When the release clearance of the brake does not meet the requirement, for example reaching 0.5 mm or more, the clearance must be readjusted. Readjustment is a maintenance operation for parameter deviation or abnormal mechanical state of electrical components such as circuit breakers and relays, restoring them to the specified values by adjusting springs, settings or travel. Cases such as excessive reaction spring force, failure of the motor-operated positioning switch, too large re-closing contact surface, incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, and excessive reaction spring force are all handled by readjustment. Among these, readjustment can be used to handle the automatic breaking fault of the circuit breaker caused by incorrect long-time delay setting of the overcurrent trip unit, and can also be used to eliminate the noise of the undervoltage trip unit caused by excessive reaction spring force. An elevator contains a brake wheel and also contains a brake shoe, and the two cooperate to complete the braking and release actions.

In the electrical control circuits of ship refrigeration and air-conditioning installations, the driven object is the refrigeration compressor motor, and the starting and stopping of the motor depend on the pressure change sensed by the pressure relay at the suction end. The electrical circuit of refrigeration equipment is relatively simple, and the starting and stopping of the refrigeration compressor motor is directly controlled by the pressure relay at the suction end; air-conditioning equipment is generally used on ocean-going ships, adopts centralized refrigeration or centralized heating, is equipped with two refrigeration compressor units and fans, and the motor driving the refrigeration compressor is likewise controlled in starting and stopping by the pressure relay at the compressor suction end, stopping when the suction-end pressure is low and starting to run when the suction-end pressure is high. The air-conditioning compressor also has a reduced-load starting function and can automatically unload or load up with changes in the external heat load, that is, adapt to the load by cutting in or out cylinders. Whether refrigeration equipment or air-conditioning equipment, its control system should be provided with protection against insufficient cooling water pressure, excessively low lubricating oil pressure, low refrigerant suction pressure, etc., and be equipped with corresponding audible and visual alarms. For high-power compressors, the load should be reduced first at starting to avoid a large starting current impacting the ship's power network; at the same time, unloading or loading-up control should be possible according to the heat load, both achieving energy saving and avoiding the impact of a large starting current on the power network.

In the specific circuit, for the RKS10F-type food refrigeration unit in automatic mode, when the compartment temperature rises and causes the suction-end pressure to rise, the contactor is energized and the compressor runs accordingly. In the cold-storage defrost control, the defrost timer DT₁ is used to control the automatic changeover of the defrost cycle; when the defrost time ends, its two sets of switches automatically return to the non-defrost state. When the cold-storage selector switch is placed in the "REF" position for manual refrigeration, the defrost timer motor is cut off, so that defrost heating does not operate. One of the fault causes of the cold storage failing to self-defrost is that the two sets of switches of the defrost timer cannot change over automatically. In the control circuit of the refrigeration unit, the defrost timer (code 2DX) is energized when the frost ice on the evaporator thickens and actuates the defrost start switch and the defrost termination thermostat closes, and its normally open contact closes and self-locks. In the cold-storage defrost control, de-energization of the intermediate relay causes the fan contactor and the liquid supply solenoid valve circuit to open. In the cold-storage system, the drain pipe is located below the drain pan and is used to discharge the water produced by defrosting; when the cold-storage control is placed in the "DRAIN" position, the heating element heats the drain pipe to assist drainage. When manual defrosting fails, it is necessary to check the operation of the defrost contactors MC31 and MC32; if their operation is normal, then check the heater and fuse.

When multiple cold storages and compressors are controlled in combination, the circuit is complicated, and it is necessary to be familiar with the unit to which each relay and contactor belongs and the lead numbers, so as to quickly troubleshoot. In the air-conditioning unit, the operation of the 4/2 intermediate relay is a prerequisite interlock condition for compressor starting. Important contactors and solenoid valves should have indicator lights when working, so that operators can understand the system operating condition. A contactor is an electrical device used in the ship's power system to control the motor; it belongs to low-voltage control apparatus and is mainly used to control the motor in electric drive systems, featuring high operating frequency, long life, accurate and reliable operation, and small size. The amount of contactors used on ships is very large, because the power of various auxiliary machinery is almost all driven by motors, and the motors are controlled by contactors. A contactor includes parts such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil; contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself. The intermediate relay is a type of electromagnetic relay, similar in construction to the contactor, and is used to expand contact capacity and number as well as to perform control logic conversion; its function is to expand contact capacity and number, and fault analysis and handling can be carried out by referring to the contactor maintenance method.

A pressure relay is a non-electrical-quantity relay with pressure as the input signal, whose sensing element is an air bag and whose actuating part is a contact; it is used for automatic control and protection of ship boilers, air compressors and pump sets, and in auxiliary boilers it is used as a control apparatus for automatically controlling steam pressure. A thermal relay is a protective relay with a bimetallic strip as the sensing element, mainly used for overload protection of small ship motors; it belongs to thermal relays classified by sensing element, its sensing part is a bimetallic strip, and it is used in large quantities on ships, with overload protection of general small motors being accomplished by it. A solenoid valve is a valve controlled by an electrical signal, used to control the on-off of fuel oil; during ignition it cuts off the fuel circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle and is injected; it can also be used to release residual air from the air compressor or to control a water mist fire-extinguishing zone. In the burner ignition program, the solenoid valve is energized, cutting off the fuel circulation circuit so that oil enters the nozzle and is injected; its drive circuit has a freewheeling diode connected in parallel across the two ends of the coil, to prevent high voltage from being generated when power is cut off and to accelerate discharge. The automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve.

A timer is a digital logic circuit application component used in household appliances, and in ship living equipment it is often used to control the start and stop of electric fans, the washing and spinning programs of washing machines, and the defrost cycle of cold storage; the electric fan includes a timer. In troubleshooting the electric fan, if it sometimes rotates and sometimes does not, one possible cause is timer failure, and the handling method is to replace the timer. In troubleshooting the washing machine not working after power-on, it is necessary to check whether the timer wiring is loose or disconnected, whether the timer knob slips, and whether the contact is in good contact. The drain pipe is the drainage component in the washing machine and the cold-storage defrost system, used to discharge washing wastewater or defrost water; in the washing machine, if it is folded into a dead corner or has creases, it is easily blocked by debris and causes poor drainage; aging and cracking of the washing machine drain pipe will cause water leakage, and it needs to be replaced and the pipe mouth firmly glued with glue.

The ship power station is the heart of the ship's electrical power system; the reliability and survivability of its operation are important indicators of the effectiveness of the system in achieving its specified tasks, and its basic responsibilities include ensuring reliable power supply, safe operation, and rapid elimination of faults after they occur. The ship power station includes the main switchboard, brushed synchronous generator, brushless synchronous generator, uncontrolled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, controlled phase-compounding voltage regulation system, thyristor excitation voltage regulation system, brushless excitation generator voltage regulation system, DW14 circuit breaker, ship power network and shore power box. The ship power network belongs to the ship power station and usually adopts a three-phase three-wire insulated system; single-phase earthing at any point is an abnormal state, and if another phase is earthed, a short circuit is formed; an insulation detection device for the power network is installed on the lighting distribution panel of the main switchboard. Precautions for connecting shore power require attention to the ship power station. The multimeter is used for current measurement, and the clamp-on ammeter is used for current measurement. Measuring current requires the use of an ammeter, connected in series after disconnecting the circuit.

Motor overcurrent is the direct cause of overheating in AC electric drive systems. When the motor is overloaded, the motor overload protection transistor relay converts power into voltage, satisfying the relationship U=KP; the fuse can only serve as short circuit protection for the motor and should not be used as overload protection for the motor; excessive refrigerant charged into the refrigeration system causing excessively high pressure and excessive load will cause motor overload.

When compressor control fails, in automatic operation the start and stop of the compressor is controlled by the suction-side low-pressure switch 63HL(L); if it can start normally after switching to manual, it is determined that the low-pressure switch 63HL(L) is damaged or its contact is not closed; if manual operation is also abnormal, check the high-pressure protection switch 63HL(H) and the oil pressure switch 63QL. Troubleshooting involves the motor overload protection thermal relay 51-1 and the auxiliary relay AX12; if all components of the protection interlock circuit are normal and 88-1 operates, the fault originates from the compressor motor itself failing to start. When compressor control fails, it is also necessary to check whether the motor overload protection thermal relay 51-1 is normal. Before starting the refrigeration unit, it is necessary to confirm that motor overload has not occurred and that the relevant contact 51C is closed.

Failure to start is a fault symptom in which the motor or drive system cannot establish rotational motion after being energized, and is often used as the top event of fault tree analysis; when constructing a fault tree, it is often selected as the top event of electrical equipment, such as motor fails to start, and the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as normal power supply and normal control circuit. Failure to connect the power supply will cause failure to start, incorrect wiring of control equipment will cause failure to start, undervoltage will cause failure to start, stator winding phase-to-phase short circuit to earth, incorrect wiring, and stator winding short circuit will cause failure to start; excessive load or brakes not released, and faults in the reducer, will likewise cause failure to start. For failure to start, the corresponding handling is: check the switch, fuse, and each pair of contacts to find the fault point; check against the wiring diagram and correct it; check the power supply voltage, and if it is indeed too low, raise it appropriately; find the short circuit or open circuit location and repair it, and if the wiring is incorrect, correct the wiring; reduce the load and separate the motor from the reducer, and if the motor can run normally, the reducer part should be checked.

Refrigeration equipment includes refrigeration and air-conditioning control system maintenance. Excessive temperature deviation in the cold storage is a fault symptom requiring attention in refrigeration and air-conditioning control circuits.

The content of observation covers abnormal phenomena, component status, conductor status and equipment operating parameters, specifically including whether components are jammed or damaged, and whether conductors are loose, broken, abraded or burnt. High-power compressors should be able to perform unloading or loading control according to the thermal load, so as to save energy and avoid large starting current impacting the power network. Taking the RKS10F type provision refrigeration unit as an example, in automatic mode, when the storage temperature is high and the suction-side pressure is high, the contactor is energized to make the compressor run.

The temperature relay is used as a regulating switch in the cold storage system; deviation of its setting value will cause the storage temperature to deviate seriously; if the contact cannot close or open, it will cause abnormality of the liquid supply solenoid valve, resulting in refrigeration failure or excessive cooling.

The temperature relay is a non-electrical quantity relay, used in large quantities on ships, and has both control and protection functions; it can be used for cooling water temperature alarm as a protective device, and can also be used in scenarios such as auxiliary boilers as a control device. The contactor includes components such as the arc chute, main contact, core and coil. The main contact is used to make or break the main circuit current, and its closed state directly controls the operation of the motor; discoloration of the copper main contact or a burnt smell indicates poor contact and overheating, and the gap and overtravel need to be adjusted and the oxide film removed; when the main contact is overheated for a long time or welded together, a contactor with a rated current one grade larger should be selected for replacement. The auxiliary contact is a component of the main switch and the contactor, used for control circuit self-locking, signal indication and interlock protection, and is also one of the main components of the generator main switch; in the motor forward rotation control, the normally open auxiliary contact is used to realize the self-locking of the contactor coil. The normally open auxiliary contact of the compressor contactor is used to connect the oil pressure switch power supply and the unloading solenoid valve.

The coil is made by winding a certain number of turns of insulated wire on an insulating bobbin, and has the characteristic of passing DC and blocking AC; a KM coil fault is one of the direct causes of the contactor armature failing to close and the motor fails to start. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself, and its fault analysis and handling can refer to the contactor repair method.

The fuse is a circuit protection component made of protective conductive material, with characteristics such as a low melting point and certain mechanical strength; its material is aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy, etc., and it is one of the commonly used components in electronic circuits, alongside the resistor and capacitance. In the main engine remote control system, fuse blowing is one of the common faults of electrical components. Alarm code AL20 indicates control circuit fuse open circuit (24V), and AL21 indicates computer controller fuse open circuit (18V). The electric main engine remote control system includes fuses.

In the starting control of multi-cylinder high-power compressors, when timing cylinder sealing is adopted to limit the starting current and starting time, the cylinder loading solenoid is controlled by the timer.

The changeover switch is used to set the working state, select measurement points or issue operating commands, and has many selection positions and contacts. On the main switchboard, the changeover switch is mainly used to select indication and measurement points, set the working state and issue operating commands. The changeover switch used for current measurement has a transition state when switching circuits, so as to ensure that the secondary side of the transformer is not open-circuited. The multimeter includes a changeover switch and uses voltage and current for measurement; the clamp-on ammeter also uses current. Voltage is one of the instrument readings to be checked in ship electrical fault diagnosis; the generator failing to build up voltage is an optional top event when constructing a fault tree, and overvoltage is one of the causes of motor overheating in AC electric drive systems.

Regarding fan faults, the fan operating state is controlled by the defrost timer relay; the fan should run when not defrosting; if in the defrost state, the fan stopping is a normal phenomenon rather than a fault; the fan stopping in the non-defrost state is judged as a fault and requires repair. To troubleshoot, first check the selector switch position and the action of intermediate relay AX31; if contactor MC33 does not operate normally, check the coil circuit for an open circuit according to the schematic diagram; if both AX31 and MC33 operate normally, the fan motor itself is judged to be faulty.

For troubleshooting the failure to self-defrost, first place CS in the "DEFROST" position for manual defrosting to determine the fault scope. If manual defrosting succeeds, it indicates that the two sets of switches of the defrost timer cannot switch automatically, or it may be that the selector switch CS is not properly closed in the automatic position; on aged changeover switches, poor contact of CS in the automatic position often causes this fault. If MC31 and MC32 operate normally but there is no heat, check the defrost heater and fuse.

For troubleshooting of compressor failure to start, if the condenser fan does not turn, priority should be given to eliminating fan faults or checking power supply circuit breakers 52C1/52C2 and operation switch 3-88. If the fan turns but the compressor does not start, it is necessary to measure whether there is voltage on the compressor control circuit to determine the closed condition of 88/F. When there is voltage on the control circuit, check whether intermediate relay 4/2 operates; if it does not operate, measure the voltage across its coil. If relay 4/2 operates, further check relay 4/1 and the closed state of its normally open contact and the 52C auxiliary contact. If relay 88/CX does not operate, check start button 3C/C, the 4/1 normally open contact and temperature regulating relay 23LH. In the defrost control logic, if contact 88C is not closed, the compressor may have no power and thus fail to start.

The technical requirements of the refrigerated container electrical control system include: the temperature regulation range inside the container is generally within ±30°C, and the regulation accuracy needs to be improved by controlling intermittent operation of the compressor, hot gas bypass of refrigerant, refrigerant flow and evaporator fan speed. When the temperature inside the container is lower than the set value, the refrigerated container electrical control system can perform electric heating; it can also automatically perform unloading operation according to the size of the heat load, and automatically control the number of condenser fans according to the external environment and condenser pressure. Refrigerated container electrical control system maintenance is usually carried out before loading. The maintenance contents include checking whether the evaporator fan motor assembly bolts are secured and tightened, checking whether there is dirt or oil sludge on the fan frame and cleaning it if necessary; checking whether the bolts of each panel of the refrigerating machine are tightened and whether the panel positions are correct, and checking whether each pressure and temperature sensor or relay is intact; checking the temperature recorder, and if it is a mechanical clockwork recorder, leaving the key on the recorder; and checking the circuit connection points and contactors in the control system box.

The defrost control of the LAKEN5BD refrigerated container evaporator is actuated by the frost thickness microswitch 63DA on the evaporator; if the fault of failure to defrost automatically occurs, the microswitch should be checked first, followed by the defrost termination thermostat 23D, the defrost control intermediate relay 2DX and the overtemperature protector 26AH. The CPE14-2BAⅢA refrigerated container is produced by Mitsubishi Corporation of Japan and adopts microcomputer control. There are five indicator lights on the display panel indicating the system operating conditions: the ALARM lamp flashing indicates fault alarm, the DEF red lamp on indicates defrost, the IR orange lamp on indicates holding, the COOL green lamp on indicates cooling, and the HUM lamp on indicates dehumidification. The operation method for setting the temperature of the CPE14-2BAⅢA refrigerated container is: press the mode selection key MODE, press the enter key ENTER to make the mode code flat, then use the up/down keys to adjust to the required temperature, and finally press the ENTER key to confirm; the microcomputer then accepts the new setting and controls as required. The power supply of refrigerated containers is usually listed as the second-stage load to be cut off in the preferential tripping load shedding stages of container ships; the first stage is non-important loads such as machine repair tools and galley equipment.

Refrigeration equipment includes refrigeration and air-conditioning control system maintenance.

According to the requirements of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, fault analysis should be carried out while keeping the site intact; observation is exactly a sub-step of this link. For the microcomputer-controlled electrical system of refrigerated containers, the maintenance of its peripheral equipment also follows this approach. Contactor maintenance applies to the contactor itself; in the microcomputer-controlled electrical system of refrigerated containers, the maintenance objects include the contactors of the compressor, fan and electric heater. Because containers are highly mobile, this maintenance is generally arranged before loading; it is necessary to check the control system box for loose connection points, open circuits and damaged components, and to carry out specific maintenance operations on the compressor and fan contactors. Circuit breaker maintenance applies to the circuit breaker; the circuit breaker is a switching device used in ship power systems to protect circuits, belongs to low-voltage distribution devices, is divided into frame type (air type) and molded-case type, has both switching and protection functions, and can maintain thermal stability and electrodynamic stability during short circuit faults. Air circuit breakers are mostly used as generator main switches and can automatically disconnect the generator to protect the power grid.

A sensor is an information acquisition device of the ship monitoring and control system, divided into two major categories: analog and switching. In the ship station antenna control platform, sensors are placed in the X-axis and Y-axis directions respectively, used to send error signals to control compensation motion when the ship pitches and rolls; that is, the control platform includes sensors, and the sensors send error signals in the X-axis and Y-axis directions. Analog sensors in the engine room monitoring and alarm system convert parameters into continuously changing electrical signals, suitable for scenarios where both equipment status is monitored and parameter values are displayed. Recording paper is the medium used for marine weather facsimile receivers and refrigerated container temperature recorders, recording weather charts or temperature curves; recording paper is a consumable of the weather facsimile receiver, and when its remaining length is less than 1 m there will be an obvious mark reminding the user that it is about to run out; when paper jamming occurs, the equipment power supply should be turned off and the recording paper reinstalled. When replacing the recording paper of the electronic temperature recorder of a refrigerated container, the recording pen must first be lifted and then put back. The electrical control system of refrigerated containers has developed from the relay type to the microcomputer control type, featuring a wide temperature adjustment range, high constant-temperature precision, electric heating, automatic unloading and automatic control of the number of condenser fans.

Tightening is one of the maintenance procedures of the PLC control system; in electrical maintenance it is used to ensure good contact of wiring terminals, screws and fastening mechanisms or to prevent loosening. The wiring screws of the electromagnetic relay should be tightened to ensure good contact; if the external wiring screws of the thermal relay are not tightened, the main circuit will be disconnected. The step of check the power supply voltage must be carried out before the refrigeration compressor is energized; it is necessary to check whether the power supply voltage matches the position of the voltage selection switch; for motor starting, operation and electrical component faults, it is used to verify the matching of the power supply state with the rated value. When a three-phase asynchronous motor fails to start, according to the principle of from simple to complex, first check whether there is a power supply; when the motor speed low after starting, first check whether the voltage is undervoltage and whether the power supply has phase failure; when the AC electromagnet has loud noise, the power supply voltage needs to be adjusted to 0.85~

1.10 times the rated value. Before the refrigeration compressor is energized and started, confirm that the power supply voltage matches the position of the voltage selection switch; when the electric fan starts slowly and the speed decreases and the cause is undervoltage of the power supply, carry out this check; when the electric drive motor fails to start due to undervoltage, check the power supply voltage and raise it appropriately. Before the refrigeration unit is energized and started, check whether the power supply voltage matches the position of the voltage selection switch; for faults such as slow starting of the electric fan, motor fails to start or excessive temperature rise, verify whether the supply voltage is within the allowable range; in the general inspection of the PLC, if the POWER lamp off, carry out the step of check the power supply fault; when the electric fan starts slowly, the maintenance method includes checking whether the power supply voltage is undervoltage; when the electric drill fails to start and there is no voltage at the power supply, check the power supply line. There is another point to note in the step of check the power supply voltage: before disassembly, the circuit ends should be marked clearly one by one, so that when restoring the wiring the positions will not be connected incorrectly.

The structure of the fault tree is a logic tree, including the top event, intermediate event and basic event, and the logic relationships are AND and OR; fault tree analysis uses a fault tree, and the fault tree is a connected logic tree that does not contain closed loops, using graphical symbols to represent the logical combinations among various events that cause an undesirable event of the system, developing downward from the tree root of the top event, with branches representing accident events and nodes representing logic relationships, among which the most commonly used logic relationships are the "AND" and "OR" relationships. Motor failure to start is a common fault symptom of marine asynchronous motors and DC motors, referring to the state in which the motor cannot produce rotating torque or the speed is zero after power-on; the main causes of failure to start of three-phase cage asynchronous motors include no power supply, motor internal fault and mechanical fault, and when checking this fault the principle of from simple to complex is followed: first check the power supply, then check for a seized shaft or excessive load, and finally check the interior of the motor. Power supply problems, mechanical problems, excessive load and motor internal fault will all cause the motor to fail to start; motor failure to start corresponds to checking the power supply voltage, and also corresponds to checking the motor internal fault; motor speed low after starting, motor temperature rise high, and excessive sparking under brush all correspond to checking the power supply voltage.

In the maintenance of the electrical control circuit of refrigeration equipment, the first thing to solve is the question of where to start with the fault. This step belongs to a sub-link of the first step of traditional fault diagnosis, "carry out fault analysis while keeping the site intact", and its value lies in providing first-hand basis for subsequent judgment.

Unlike traditional methods that rely on experience, fault tree analysis uses the tool of the fault tree to sort out the ins and outs of the fault. The fault tree includes three levels: top event, intermediate event and basic event, among which the most commonly used logic relationships are the AND relationship and the OR relationship. In the maintenance of the electrical control circuit of refrigeration equipment, phenomena such as motor failure to start and compressor failure to start are often selected as the top event, and the boundary conditions for analyzing this fault are usually set as normal power supply and normal control circuit.

During diagnosis, instruments are needed to read voltage and current. The measurable property of voltage is the voltage value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter and voltmeter; the measurable property of current is the current value, and the measuring tools are the multimeter, ammeter and clamp-on ammeter. The current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA, has the nature of a current source, and has an extremely large internal resistance; the standard current on the secondary side is 5A or 1A, and the load current I flowing through the primary side is transformed into a secondary current connected to an AC ammeter or other series current elements; its secondary side must strictly not be open-circuited, the terminals of the externally connected ammeter need to have a short-circuit connecting piece, and it can only be disconnected after the wiring has been checked.

When the compressor unit fails to start and the condenser fan does not turn, check the power supply and the state of the circuit breaker. The possible cause of the compressor unit's failure to start is that the compressor motor itself fails to start or the motor has no power; if the condenser fan turns, it indicates that the compressor motor itself has a failure to start; if the condenser fan does not turn, check whether circuit breakers 52C1, 52C2 and the running switch 3-88 are closed. If there is voltage across the coil of 88C but it does not start, it indicates that the contact of 88C itself is faulty; if there is no voltage across the coil of 88C, check the state of each contact in the coil circuit. When the low-pressure switch 63HL is open, check whether there is voltage across the liquid supply solenoid valve 20S. The automatic fuel oil boiler includes a solenoid valve. During maintenance, first check whether the frost thickness microswitch 63DA is closed;

If 63DA is closed but there is no operation, check the defrost termination thermostat 23D, the defrost control intermediate relay 2DX and the overheating protector 26AH. The main cause of the fault of large temperature variation inside the box is that the electronic temperature controller does not work normally; during maintenance, check whether the temperature sensing element is intact, check whether the lead wires are broken or loose, and check whether the shielded wire is well earthed; if routine checks cannot locate the problem, use the substitution method to replace the spare electronic temperature controller. The relay board is controlled by the alarm processing board and is used to drive external alarm and control equipment; it has two DC 24V/2A power outputs and three DC 24V/2A active signal outputs, four relay signal outputs with a capacity of 2A, and two signal outputs in open-collector form, driving equipment such as the general alarm system, alarm bell and fire door electromagnet.

The display is used to display radar images and is the display terminal of the ship's radar and monitoring system, used to present images, data and alarm information; it belongs to radar equipment, and radar equipment includes the display; the display should be installed in the wheelhouse in a dry place free from strong electromagnetic radiation and away from heat sources, fixed with a hardwood base, with the main radar display oriented so that the observer faces the bow, installed on the starboard side of the bridge; the precautions for radar display installation require attention to the display, radar installation applies to the display, and the display includes two maintenance items: cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface.

The refrigerated container includes the item of refrigerated container electrical control system maintenance. The ship's power grid is a component of the ship's power station. The precautions for shore power connection require attention with respect to the ship's power station.
