The shunt trip unit fails to make the circuit breaker open, and the undervoltage trip unit fails to make the circuit breaker open, indicating that the trip circuit fails to operate normally; the circuit breaker trips immediately when starting the motor, indicating that the circuit breaker trips immediately under the impact of the motor starting current; the circuit breaker automatically opens about 1 h after closing, which is a delayed automatic opening phenomenon; the undervoltage trip unit has noise, reflecting abnormal operation of its electromagnetic mechanism; the temperature rise of the circuit breaker is too high, indicating abnormal heating at the conductive circuit or contact parts; a fault of the auxiliary switch will affect the signal and interlock functions of the circuit breaker; misoperation of the semiconductor overcurrent trip unit will cause the circuit breaker to open before the setting condition is reached. All the above types of faults may occur on the circuit breaker, and troubleshooting should confirm them item by item in accordance with the requirements for circuit breaker maintenance.

Voltage is one of the measurable performance quantities, and its measuring tools include the multimeter and the voltmeter; the multimeter is used to measure voltage. Current is one of the electrical quantities measured by electrical instruments, and is used to understand equipment status;

The automatic fuel oil boiler contains a solenoid valve. In the direct control mode, the alarm lamp is connected to the emergency power supply through the shutter contact and lights up. The sensor is positioned in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, and its function is to send out an error signal.

Maintenance of the refrigeration and air-conditioning control system occupies a fixed place in the daily electrical maintenance of ships, and its control elements and detection elements are both scheduled for inspection at a period of once every 2 months. For the item of control elements, the focus is on confirming whether the interlocks of the cooling pump, fan, solenoid valve, control box, etc. are reliable; during inspection, the action sequence of the interlock circuit should be checked unit by unit, confirming whether the fan can be put into operation at the set delay after the cooling pump starts, whether the on-off of the pipeline after the solenoid valve is energized is consistent with the command, and whether each protection link in the control box can cut off correctly under abnormal working conditions; for the item of detection elements, it is necessary to confirm whether the temperature and pressure switches act flexibly; during inspection, methods such as changing the set value or simulating temperature and pressure changes can be used to observe whether the switch can act reliably and reset near the set value. Daily maintenance also requires regular cleaning of the contacts of each relay to ensure good contact of the contacts, and regular inspection of the setting values of the electrical appliances, which must not deviate too much; once the setting value shifts, it will directly affect the accuracy of the interlock action and the reliability of the protection function.

The automatic fuel oil boiler also contains control system maintenance content; the program actions of its sequence controller should be flexible and reliable; during manual operation, the sound and light alarm safety facilities should be effective and normal; during inspection, the program steps should be verified item by item according to the stages of startup, operation and shutdown, confirming that the alarm sound and light signal are issued synchronously and can be manually acknowledged.

The automatic fuel oil boiler also contains a solenoid valve and a servo motor. The servo motor is used to adjust the opening of the air damper and the oil damper; it rotates according to the output signal of the bridge and drives the feedback potentiometer to adjust, so that the bridge is rebalanced; as the actuator of the temperature recorder, an abnormality of the servo motor will trigger fault code 601; when this code appears, the servo motor winding, transmission mechanism and feedback circuit should be checked first. In boiler combustion regulation, the servo motor is controlled by the differential amplifier and the thyristor to energize the winding, so as to adjust the air-fuel ratio; when rotating, it drives the sliding contact of the feedback potentiometer R10 to move, and stops after the bridge reaches balance again; if the bridge cannot be balanced all the time, the servo motor will continue to rotate or stop at a wrong position, and the air-fuel ratio will be out of adjustment accordingly.

The main radar display should be oriented so that the observer faces the bow, and is installed on the starboard side of the bridge; this arrangement makes it convenient for the observer to take into account both the sea surface ahead and the screen image. The display also contains two maintenance items: cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface; cleaning the air filter can ensure ventilation and heat dissipation inside the unit, and for surface cleaning soft materials should be used to avoid scratching the screen surface or damaging the coating.

The control platform contains sensors. The sensors are arranged in the X-axis and Y-axis directions, and their function is to send out an error signal; the current transformer corresponds to the symbol TA, is used to transform the current ratio, has the nature of a current source, and its secondary standard current is usually 5 A, with one end of the secondary side earthed; its types include the coil type, busbar type and through type, and the through-type current transformer belongs to current transformers. The primary terminals of the current transformer are denoted by L1 and L2, and the secondary terminals by K1 and K2; during operation it is equivalent to a short-circuit transformer, and the secondary winding must never be open-circuited during operation; when open-circuited, a dangerously high voltage will be generated on the secondary side, so the secondary terminals must be short-circuited first during maintenance.

The multimeter uses voltage, current and diode. When using a multimeter to measure voltage, the range shall be set to the voltage range and connected in parallel with the circuit under test; when measuring current, it needs to be connected in series; when measuring a diode, its unidirectional conductivity is used to judge polarity and whether it is good or bad.

Marine electrical equipment uses diodes. A diode has unidirectional conductivity and is commonly denoted by VD in circuits, used for rectification, isolation, voltage stabilization, etc.; under forward voltage it conducts with small resistance, and under reverse voltage its resistance is very large or infinite. According to function, it can be divided into rectifier diodes such as 1N4004, isolation diodes such as 1N4148, Schottky diodes such as BAT85, etc. The performance of a diode that can be measured includes polarity, unidirectional conductivity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance; during measurement, the resistance range of a multimeter can be used to measure the forward and reverse resistances respectively, and an obvious difference in resistance value indicates that the unidirectional conductivity is normal.

Diodes include light-emitting diodes and Zener diodes. A light-emitting diode has unidirectional conductivity, and its emission colors include red, green, yellow, etc.; its external dimensions include diameters of 3mm, 5mm and a 2mm×5mm rectangle; its operating current is generally 1～30mA depending on the model, and its conduction voltage is above 1.7V; its circuit symbol has two more arrows than an ordinary diode, and it is commonly used as a circuit working status indicator or to form a large-screen color electronic display; in actual use, a current-limiting resistor must be connected in series to prevent damage. For light-emitting diodes, attention must be paid to the precautions for use of light-emitting diodes; before connecting to the circuit, confirm that the resistance value of the current-limiting resistor is appropriate and the polarity connection is correct. The diode detection steps are applicable to diodes; during detection, power should first be cut off and discharge performed, and then judgment should be made item by item in the order of polarity, forward voltage drop and reverse resistance.

In the maintenance of the electrical control circuits of refrigeration equipment, checking the electrical parameters at each point of the circuit is the basic means of determining the fault location. Measuring the current value of load circuits such as compressors and fans helps to grasp their operating status. Contactor maintenance is exactly the inspection and upkeep work carried out for the above components. Circuit breaker maintenance is applicable to various circuit breakers, and its common faults have various manifestations. A circuit breaker may have the fault that when the circuit breaker is operated manually, the contact cannot close, that is, when operated manually the contact cannot close normally; a circuit breaker may also have the fault that when the circuit breaker is operated electrically, the contact cannot close, that is, when operated electrically the contact likewise cannot close. The above fault symptoms correspond to different inspection points respectively, and during maintenance, troubleshooting should be carried out item by item in combination with the measurement results of voltage and current.

The temperature controller is an important component of the electrical control of the refrigeration system. Display maintenance includes two items: cleaning the display air filter and cleaning the display surface. Radar installation is applicable to the installation work of the display.

The maintenance of the electrical control circuits of refrigeration equipment is inseparable from the measurement and judgment of electrical quantities. Voltage and current are both electrical quantities to be measured by electrical instruments, and grasping their values helps to understand the state the equipment is in. A multimeter or voltmeter can be used to measure voltage values, and a multimeter, ammeter or clamp-on ammeter can be used to measure current values. When using an ammeter to measure current, the circuit needs to be disconnected and the instrument connected in series; a clamp-on ammeter can directly clamp and measure the current in the conductor without cutting off the circuit. In marine electrical fault diagnosis, voltage is one of the instrument readings that need to be checked.

The alarm codes of the air-conditioning system are directly related to the power supply status. Alarm code LO indicates low supply voltage, which is specifically defined as a voltage deviation exceeding 20%. The fault cause of low supply voltage will cause loud noise of the AC electromagnet, and will also cause welding of contacts, low motor speed and washing machine failure. That is to say, low supply voltage will cause loud noise of the electromagnet (AC); when the supply voltage of the AC electromagnet is on the low side, the noise increases noticeably, and it should be adjusted to 0.85–1.10 times the rated voltage; when the contactor causes welding of contacts due to insufficient holding force, check whether the supply voltage is lower than 85% of the rated voltage. The voltage may also be checked, and if too low it should be raised appropriately; if necessary, replace the power supply or raise the voltage.

The fuse is a component of ship electrical equipment and a commonly used component in electronic circuits, listed alongside the resistor, capacitance, etc. It is made of protective conductive material and has the characteristics of a low melting point and a certain mechanical strength; the commonly used materials are aluminum-tin alloy or aluminum-tin-antimony-bismuth alloy.

During maintenance, check the contacts and fuse of the control device, check the switch, fuse and each pair of contacts, and locate the fault point.

Mechanical faults of refrigeration equipment motors also have their corresponding remedies. Uneven clearance of the friction plates, long-term high-speed friction, and deformation of the friction plates are among the causes of the fault. Low speed during load operation, and excessively high motor temperature or smoking are fault symptoms that need to be identified. During maintenance, check against the wiring diagram and correct it; locate the short circuit and earthing parts and repair them. Check the stator current, reduce the load, check the stator current, and when overload is found, reduce the load. Check the broken bars and unsoldered joints and repair them. Check the air gap between the rotor and stator and the clearance between the brake wheel and the brake band, find the cause of rubbing, and correct it. Cut off the power, then close again; if there is failure to start, one phase may be open-circuited; check the power supply and the motor and repair them.

Replace the damaged bearing. Check the loose points and fasten the coupling. Check whether the bearing and bearing housing are loose, whether the shaft is bent, and whether there is any defect in the stator-rotor assembly, and repair them.

Fracture of the connecting rod of one phase of the circuit breaker is the fault cause leading to circuit breaker failure. For the circuit breaker, the maintenance procedure includes: check the circuit, apply voltage or replace the coil; replace the energy-storing spring; adjust the re-latch contact surface to the specified value; replace the power supply; increase the capacity of the operating power supply; readjust or replace the pull rod; replace the rectifier tube or capacitor; replace the connecting rod;

adjust to the requirements specified in the original technical conditions; replace the power supply or raise the voltage; adjust the energy-storing spring; eliminate the cause of jamming; adjust the instantaneous setting spring of the overcurrent trip unit; replace the thermal element or the semiconductor delay circuit element; remove oil contamination; replace the armature or core; adjust the contact pressure or replace the spring; replace the contact or clean the contact surface; straighten or reinstall the moving contact bridge; replace the transmission rod and roller or replace the entire auxiliary switch.
